variants.name: D2X-G
variants.overview: Gibson Federated BattleMechs built the Gestalt in 3078 under the Word of Blake's Machina Domini program. The neural-interface battlesuit replaces the traditional cockpit entirely — the pilot operates the machine through direct neural link rather than conventional controls. The production facility was destroyed before the design left prototype testing. There are very few of these in existence.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump six on the 315-rated XL engine at forty-five tons. The Divine Spectre-C armour and Void Signature System make it extraordinarily difficult to detect on sensors. An Angel ECM suite degrades enemy electronic systems. The weapons are a heavy PPC and two ER medium lasers — modest for a machine built around this much electronics. The Machina Domini neural interface limits the pilot pool to specially conditioned operators. Pilots who wash out of that conditioning cannot operate this machine at all.
variants.deployment: The Gestalt is an ambush and interdiction platform that relies entirely on not being detected until it fires. The sensor-masking systems are the primary capability; the weapons are secondary. Battlefield losses are almost impossible to replace given how few exist and how limited the qualified pilot pool is. Treat any operational Gestalt as an intelligence asset as much as a combat unit.

variants.name: AGT-1A
variants.overview: Majesty Metals and Manufacturing built the Agrotera on Canopus IV in 3108 for Magistracy operations along the anti-spinward frontier. The partial wing system is the design's unusual feature — it extends both jump range and heat dissipation capacity. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine at fifty tons. The all-energy weapons load was a deliberate choice for units that operate far from supply lines.
variants.capabilities: The AGT-1A carries an ER PPC, a medium VSP laser, a medium pulse laser, two small pulse lasers, and a TAG system. The ER PPC is the primary weapon. The VSP laser adapts its damage profile to range. The TAG designates for artillery and guided munitions. The partial wing adds heat sink capacity that the energy-heavy loadout genuinely needs. The XL engine is the standard side torso concern. No ammunition to manage.
variants.deployment: The 1A was built for extended independent patrols where ammunition resupply is not available. The all-energy loadout suits that role. The TAG system adds force multiplier value when operating with artillery support. The partial wing heat dissipation means this machine can sustain fire at a pace that a standard fifty-ton medium cannot match.

variants.name: AGT-UA 'Ariel'
variants.overview: Majesty Metals and Manufacturing built the Agrotera on Canopus IV in 3108 for Magistracy operations along the anti-spinward frontier. The partial wing system is the design's unusual feature — it extends both jump range and heat dissipation capacity. The Ariel is the aquatic variant, trading the jump capability entirely for underwater operations.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine with no jump jets on the Ariel. Twin ER large lasers and two ER medium lasers replace the 1A's mixed energy suite. The jump jets are gone completely, freeing mass for underwater maneuvering equipment. Clan-grade double heat sinks manage the all-energy thermal load. The TAG system from the 1A is removed. Without the partial wing the heat dissipation profile changes compared to the base configuration.
variants.deployment: The Ariel deploys in aquatic operations on worlds where the 1A's jump capability is irrelevant but underwater mobility matters. The ER large laser output is a meaningful upgrade over the 1A's ER PPC at comparable range. The loss of jump and TAG capability is substantial for units that needed those features. Know which variant you have before the mission.

variants.name: AKU-1X
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Akuma in 3058 as a cost-effective assault platform sharing components with the Atlas. Ninety tons, walk three, run four on the 270-rated standard engine. The design sacrifices some armour compared to the Atlas to hit a lower production cost. The resulting machine fields a capable mixed weapons suite across multiple ranges.
variants.capabilities: The AKU-1X carries an ER PPC, an LB 10-X, an MRM-30, a Streak SRM-4, a Streak SRM-6, a medium laser, and a medium pulse laser. The ER PPC and LB 10-X handle long-range work. The MRM-30 delivers medium-range missile volume. The Streak launchers provide guaranteed close-range hits on lock. Thirteen heat sinks is tight for this weapons density — fire discipline matters. Standard engine survivability is the chassis's reliable quality.
variants.deployment: The 1X established the Akuma's battlefield reputation. The mixed weapons coverage suits units that need an assault platform without Atlas-class procurement costs. The standard engine keeps it alive through hits that kill XL variants. Heat management is the pilot's primary discipline.

variants.name: AKU-1XJ
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Akuma in 3058 as a cost-effective assault platform sharing components with the Atlas. Ninety tons, walk three, run four. The AKU-1XJ adds jump capability, which on a ninety-ton machine is a genuine tactical surprise.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three. The 1XJ carries an LB 20-X, an MRM-40, two medium pulse lasers, an ER large laser, and an ER small laser. The LB 20-X provides heavy ballistic fire with cluster and slug options. The MRM-40 delivers heavy medium-range missile volume. The XL engine is required to accommodate the jump equipment — side torso vulnerability applies. Ten double heat sinks is lean for this weapons load.
variants.deployment: The 1XJ uses jump three to close distance or seize elevated positions unavailable to ground-bound assault machines. The LB 20-X and MRM-40 combination at close range is devastating. The XL engine and limited heat sinks are the tradeoffs. Jump three on a ninety-ton machine surprises opponents who expect this chassis to be stationary.

variants.name: AKU-2X
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Akuma in 3058 as a cost-effective assault platform sharing components with the Atlas. Ninety tons, walk three, run four. The AKU-2X is a 3062 upgrade featuring a heavy PPC and expanded missile capacity.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four on the standard engine. The 2X carries a heavy PPC, an LB 10-X, an MRM-40 with Apollo fire control, and a medium pulse laser with a C3 slave. The heavy PPC hits harder than a standard PPC at medium range but has a minimum range gap. The Apollo fire control improves MRM grouping substantially. The C3 slave integrates targeting data from a network lance. Standard engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The 2X reflects DCMS emphasis on networked lance tactics. The C3 slave and Apollo MRM control together improve the machine's effectiveness in coordinated formations. The heavy PPC minimum range requires the MRM and LB 10-X to handle close threats. The standard engine keeps it alive. This variant is most effective as part of a C3 network rather than in isolated operation.

variants.name: AKU-2XC
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Akuma in 3058 as a cost-effective assault platform sharing components with the Atlas. Ninety tons, walk three, run four. The AKU-2XC is a C3 boosted network variant.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four. The 2XC carries a snub-nose PPC, an LB 10-X, an MRM-40, two medium lasers, and a C3 boosted slave with CASE protection. The snub-nose PPC covers short to medium range without minimum range complications. The C3 boosted slave provides extended network integration range over a standard C3 slave. A coolant pod supplements heat management. Standard engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The 2XC trades the 2X's heavy PPC for a snub-nose that works better at close range, then adds C3 boosted slave capability for extended network coverage. The CASE ammunition protection is appropriate given the MRM and LB 10-X ammunition density. Units that operate in dispersed formations where standard C3 range is insufficient run this variant.

variants.name: AKU-2XK
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Akuma in 3058 as a cost-effective assault platform sharing components with the Atlas. Ninety tons, walk three, run four. The AKU-2XK is the most weapons-diverse variant in the family.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four. The 2XK carries a heavy PPC, a Rotary AC/5, two MML-9 launchers, two medium pulse lasers, an ER medium laser, a Guardian ECM suite, and a C3 slave. The MML-9 flexibility covers both SRM and LRM range bands. The Rotary AC/5 delivers sustained ballistic harassment. The Guardian ECM and C3 slave add electronic warfare and network capability. The compact gyro improves survivability against gyro crits. CASE protects ammunition.
variants.deployment: The 2XK is the most electronically capable Akuma variant. The ECM disrupts enemy targeting while the C3 slave coordinates with lancemates. The combined weapons cover every range band. The ammunition management across Rotary AC, MML-9 SRM, and MML-9 LRM feeds requires pre-mission planning. Lance commanders who want assault firepower with battlefield coordination capability run this variant.

variants.name: ALB-3U
variants.overview: Irian Technologies built the Albatross in 3053 for the Free Worlds League as a generalist ninety-five ton assault platform. Walk four, run six on the 380-rated XL engine. Thirteen tons of standard armour at ninety-five tons is thin, and the XL engine means side torso damage is catastrophic. The design accepts those vulnerabilities in exchange for speed and weapons variety.
variants.capabilities: The ALB-3U carries an LB 10-X, an ER large laser, a large pulse laser, an LRM-15, an SRM-6, and two medium lasers. The weapons cover every range band from a single configuration. The LB 10-X cluster and slug options add flexibility. Heat management across the full suite requires discipline — thirteen heat sinks is modest for this output. CASE protects against ammunition detonation.
variants.deployment: The 3U is the generalist assault platform it was designed to be. It contributes fire at any engagement range without specialising at any one. The thin armour and XL engine mean it cannot absorb the punishment a comparable standard-engine assault survives. Pilots who stay at range and manage heat carefully get good results. Pilots who brawl in this machine find out quickly why thirteen tons of armour is not enough on ninety-five tons.

variants.name: ALB-4U
variants.overview: Irian Technologies built the Albatross in 3053 for the Free Worlds League. The ALB-4U is a 3063 upgrade addressing the armour criticism of the original through ferro-fibrous armour addition and weapons refinement.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the XL engine. The 4U carries a light Gauss rifle, a large pulse laser, two ER medium lasers, an ER small laser, an LRM-15, and a Streak SRM-6. The light Gauss replaces the LB 10-X — more ammunition-efficient at reduced range and damage. The Streak SRM-6 fires only on lock. Over three tons of ferro-fibrous armour added over the 3U. XL engine vulnerability unchanged.
variants.deployment: The 4U improves on the 3U's armour weakness while refining the weapons suite. The light Gauss is more efficient than the LB 10-X for most engagement scenarios. The Streak SRM-6 reliability is an improvement over the standard SRM-6. The armour upgrade addresses the most common criticism of the original without changing the generalist tactical role.

variants.name: ALB-5W
variants.overview: Irian Technologies built the Albatross in 3053 for the Free Worlds League. The ALB-5W is a Jihad-era variant on a light engine, switching to all-energy weapons for line-breaking operations.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 380-rated light engine. The 5W carries an ER PPC, a large VSP laser, two medium pulse lasers, two ER medium lasers, and two ER small lasers. The light engine provides better side torso survivability than the XL variants. The all-energy loadout removes ammunition dependency entirely. The VSP laser adapts to range. Heat management across the full energy suite requires cycling discipline.
variants.deployment: The 5W is built for sustained close assault without ammunition logistics. The light engine survivability improvement is genuine — hits that kill XL variants leave this running. The all-energy suite is less vulnerable to ammunition explosions. Heat management is the discipline requirement. Works well in urban and jungle environments where the range advantage of ballistic weapons matters less.

variants.name: ALB-5W (Dantalion)
variants.overview: Irian Technologies built the Albatross in 3053 for the Free Worlds League. The Dantalion is a named command variant of the ALB-5W that served the 49th Shadow Division during the Jihad.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the light engine. The Dantalion carries an ER PPC with PPC capacitor, a large VSP laser, two medium pulse lasers, two ER medium lasers, an ER small laser, and a laser AMS. The PPC capacitor allows overcharge shots at significant heat cost. The laser AMS provides missile defence without ammunition dependency. Heavy ferro-fibrous armour and a small cockpit are the structural distinctions. The small cockpit is a pilot comfort issue.
variants.deployment: The Dantalion is a personal machine, not a production variant. The PPC capacitor overcharge is a tactical option to use selectively — not a default firing mode. The laser AMS protects the command element from missile attacks. Maintaining this requires the specific configuration documentation from its service history with the 49th Shadow Division.

variants.name: ALB-3Ur
variants.overview: Irian Technologies built the Albatross in 3053 for the Free Worlds League. The ALB-3Ur is a field refit of the 3U that trades the LB 10-X and ER large laser for a Gauss rifle and snub-nose PPC.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the XL engine. The 3Ur carries a Gauss rifle, a snub-nose PPC, an ER large laser (retained), two medium lasers, and an MML-9. The Gauss rifle provides accurate long-range fire. The snub-nose PPC covers short to medium range without minimum range issues. The MML-9 adds SRM/LRM missile flexibility. Three tons of Gauss ammunition requires tracking alongside the MML supply.
variants.deployment: The 3Ur increases direct-fire lethality over the 3U at the cost of the LB 10-X cluster flexibility. The Gauss accuracy and snub-nose PPC close-range capability are the practical improvements. The MML-9 replaces the dedicated LRM-15 and SRM-6 with a single flexible launcher at reduced individual capacity. XL engine vulnerability unchanged.

variants.name: ALB-5U
variants.overview: Irian Technologies built the Albatross in 3053 for the Free Worlds League. The ALB-5U is a survivability-focused variant on a light engine that received disappointing field evaluations for its weapons output.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the light engine. The 5U carries a Rotary AC/2, a large X-pulse laser, two ER medium lasers, an ER small laser, and an MML-7. Fifteen tons of heavy ferro-fibrous armour and a heavy-duty gyro make this genuinely durable. The weapons output per ton is modest — the light engine, heavy armour, and reinforced gyro consume mass that could carry heavier weapons. IrTech reverted to the ALB-4Ur after field evaluation.
variants.deployment: The 5U prioritises survivability over firepower to a degree that field commanders found unacceptable for a ninety-five ton machine. The heavy armour and heavy-duty gyro keep it fighting through damage that stops lighter-armoured variants. The weapons are adequate rather than impressive. Units that need a machine that absorbs punishment more than it dishes it out have a use for the 5U. Most do not.

variants.name: ALB-4Ur
variants.overview: Irian Technologies built the Albatross in 3053 for the Free Worlds League. The ALB-4Ur is the upgraded production standard that replaced the 5U after disappointing evaluations — the Commonwealth's primary Albatross model.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the XL engine. The 4Ur carries an LB 10-X, a large pulse laser, two ER medium lasers, a light PPC, an LRM-15, and an SRM-6. The ER medium laser upgrade over the 3U's standard mediums extends close-range energy capability. The light PPC adds a third direct fire energy weapon. CASE protects ammunition. The XL engine vulnerability remains.
variants.deployment: The 4Ur is the current-production Albatross standard. It builds on the 3U concept with better energy suite and the light PPC addition without changing the generalist tactical role. The ER mediums are a genuine improvement over standard mediums. IrTech recommends this over the 5U for most operational environments. Parts availability as a current-production model is good.

variants.name: ALB-6U
variants.overview: Irian Technologies built the Albatross in 3053 for the Free Worlds League. The ALB-6U is a later production variant carrying a Gauss rifle and variable-speed pulse laser as the primary weapons.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the XL engine. The ALB-6U carries a Gauss rifle, a large VSP laser, three ER medium lasers, a light PPC, an LRM-15, and an SRM-6. The Gauss provides accurate long-range direct fire. The VSP laser adapts to engagement range. The ER mediums provide layered energy fire. The light PPC adds close-range energy output. Gauss and missile ammunition require separate tracking.
variants.deployment: The 6U sees service in Marik heavy fire-support lances where the Gauss accuracy at range anchors the lance's long-range engagement. The VSP and ER medium combination handles closer work. The SRM-6 and LRM-15 provide the missile coverage the family's generalist identity requires. XL engine vulnerability is the persistent concern across XL variants.

variants.name: C 'Sooty Albatross'
variants.overview: Irian Technologies built the Albatross in 3053 for the Free Worlds League. The Sooty Albatross is a Clan Wolf stopgap built after losing access to Night Wolf production lines — an all-Clan weapons suite on the Albatross airframe.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four on an XL engine at ninety-five tons. Jump four on a ninety-five ton machine. The Sooty Albatross carries a Gauss rifle, an ER large pulse laser, twin ER medium lasers, a plasma cannon, an ATM-9, and CASE II on both side torsos. The Clan weapons on an IS chassis create a two-track maintenance requirement. The plasma cannon disrupts enemy heat management while dealing damage. ATM-9 provides three-munition missile flexibility.
variants.deployment: The Sooty Albatross is considered an ill omen within Clan Wolf, built as a stopgap that acknowledges they could not field their preferred design. The jump capability is the tactical surprise on a ninety-five ton chassis. The Clan weapons require Clan-qualified maintenance. CASE II provides ammunition protection on both torsos, which the plasma cannon and ATM ammunition density requires.

variants.name: AL-A1
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Alfar in 2573 for the Lyran Commonwealth Armed Forces as a homegrown alternative to imported medium designs. Fifty-five tons, walk five, run seven, jump three on the 275-rated standard engine. A PPC, three medium lasers, and an SRM-6. Nothing complicated about it.
variants.capabilities: The AL-A1 carries a Magna Hellstar PPC, three Magna Mark II medium lasers, and a Shannon Six-Shooter SRM-6 on the 275-rated standard engine. Walk five, run seven, jump three. The PPC provides the long-range capability. The three mediums and SRM-6 handle closer work. Fifteen heat sinks manage the load adequately under normal cycling — firing everything simultaneously builds heat quickly.
variants.deployment: The Alfar deployed primarily with the LCAF as a medium striker and close-support machine. The combination of PPC range and SRM-6 close punch covers most engagement scenarios a medium faces. Standard engine survivability. Parts availability within Lyran supply chains is good given the long production run.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Wolf Empire introduced the Alpha Wolf as a ninety-ton assault OmniMech combining stealth armour with heavy firepower — an unusual combination at this weight. The Imstar V-Stealth system makes it genuinely difficult to target, and a fixed Gauss rifle backs every configuration. Walk four, run six on the 360-rated Clan XL engine. Production was delayed while the Wolf Empire rebuilt its forces.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety tons. The Clan XL is the standard side torso vulnerability. The fixed Gauss rifle appears across all configurations as the backbone direct fire weapon. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active and creates a consistent thermal management challenge across every configuration. Clan construction quality throughout. Configuration A carries twin ER PPCs, four medium pulse lasers, and two Streak SRM-6 launchers. The ER PPCs provide the approach fire. The medium pulse lasers and Streak SRM-6s close the engagement at range. The Streak launchers fire only on lock, conserving ammunition. Heat from ER PPCs and stealth armour simultaneously requires strict discipline.
variants.deployment: Configuration A uses the ER PPCs to engage during the approach under stealth cover, then closes with the pulse lasers and Streaks. Warriors who understand the stealth heat cost and manage it alongside the PPC heat curve sustain effective output. Warriors who ignore it shut down at inopportune moments.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: The Wolf Empire introduced the Alpha Wolf as a ninety-ton assault OmniMech combining stealth armour with heavy firepower — an unusual combination at this weight. The Imstar V-Stealth system makes it genuinely difficult to target, and a fixed Gauss rifle backs every configuration. Walk four, run six on the 360-rated Clan XL engine. Production was delayed while the Wolf Empire rebuilt its forces.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety tons. The Clan XL is the standard side torso vulnerability. The fixed Gauss rifle appears across all configurations as the backbone direct fire weapon. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active and creates a consistent thermal management challenge across every configuration. Clan construction quality throughout. Configuration B carries a Gauss rifle, two large pulse lasers, and two SRM-6 launchers with Artemis V fire control. The Gauss provides accurate long-range fire alongside the fixed Gauss. The large pulse lasers cover medium engagement. The Artemis V SRM-6s improve missile grouping at close range. Stealth armour heat cost applies.
variants.deployment: Configuration B pairs the fixed Gauss with a pod Gauss for layered long-range ballistic fire, then transitions to pulse lasers and improved SRMs as the range closes. The dual Gauss combination at range is the standout capability. Artemis V on the SRM-6s makes the close-range missile fire more reliable than standard launchers.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: The Wolf Empire introduced the Alpha Wolf as a ninety-ton assault OmniMech combining stealth armour with heavy firepower — an unusual combination at this weight. The Imstar V-Stealth system makes it genuinely difficult to target, and a fixed Gauss rifle backs every configuration. Walk four, run six on the 360-rated Clan XL engine. Production was delayed while the Wolf Empire rebuilt its forces.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety tons. The Clan XL is the standard side torso vulnerability. The fixed Gauss rifle appears across all configurations as the backbone direct fire weapon. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active and creates a consistent thermal management challenge across every configuration. Clan construction quality throughout. Configuration C carries twin ER large lasers, three ER medium lasers, and two Extended LRM-10 launchers. The ELRM-10s reach beyond standard LRM range. The ER large and medium lasers provide layered direct fire. This is the maximum stand-off engagement configuration. Stealth armour heat cost compounds with the energy weapons load.
variants.deployment: Configuration C uses the stealth armour to approach to ELRM-10 range and then maintain that distance while delivering layered energy and missile fire. The ELRM-10 range combined with stealth sensor masking creates a stand-off engagement that opponents struggle to reply to. The heat load requires cycling discipline across both stealth and weapons systems.

variants.name: Prime
variants.overview: The Wolf Empire introduced the Alpha Wolf as a ninety-ton assault OmniMech combining stealth armour with heavy firepower — an unusual combination at this weight. The Imstar V-Stealth system makes it genuinely difficult to target, and a fixed Gauss rifle backs every configuration. Walk four, run six on the 360-rated Clan XL engine. Production was delayed while the Wolf Empire rebuilt its forces.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety tons. The Clan XL is the standard side torso vulnerability. The fixed Gauss rifle appears across all configurations as the backbone direct fire weapon. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active and creates a consistent thermal management challenge across every configuration. Clan construction quality throughout. The Prime carries two Rotary AC/5s and two LRM-15 launchers. The Rotary AC/5s deliver sustained ballistic harassment at medium range. The LRM-15s provide indirect fire capability. No close-range weapons beyond the fixed Gauss. Stealth armour heat applies alongside the weapons heat.
variants.deployment: The Prime uses the stealth approach to get within Rotary AC/5 and LRM-15 effective range, then delivers sustained fire. The Rotary double-tap rate combined with LRM-15 volleys creates consistent pressure at medium range. Rotary AC and LRM ammunition require separate tracking. The stealth armour heat cost means warriors cannot run stealth at maximum weapons output simultaneously.

variants.overview: The Amarok is a hundred-ton Clan assault built on a 400-rated Clan XL engine achieving walk four, run six. Battlefist-equipped arms and inherent chassis stability make it effective in close combat. The design was conceived specifically to counter Death From Above tactics.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at a hundred tons. The Clan XL at this weight carries the standard catastrophic side torso vulnerability. Battlefist arms add physical attack capability that most assault platforms lack. The chassis stability is a genuine engineering feature rather than a marketing claim — this machine holds aim better on rough terrain than comparable designs. Variant 2 carries a Streak LRM-20, an improved heavy large laser, a large pulse laser, three ER medium lasers, and two AP Gauss rifles. MASC provides burst speed capability. The Streak LRM-20 fires only on lock, guaranteeing every salvo hits. The improved heavy large laser delivers hard-hitting medium-range fire. The AP Gauss rifles address infantry and battle armour.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 uses MASC for burst speed when closing distance or breaking contact. The Streak LRM-20 at range transitions to improved heavy laser and pulse laser at medium distance. The AP Gauss rifles handle infantry threats alongside the primary engagement. MASC transmission wear under heavy use is the maintenance concern.

variants.overview: The Amarok is a hundred-ton Clan assault built on a 400-rated Clan XL engine achieving walk four, run six. Battlefist-equipped arms and inherent chassis stability make it effective in close combat. The design was conceived specifically to counter Death From Above tactics.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at a hundred tons. The Clan XL at this weight carries the standard catastrophic side torso vulnerability. Battlefist arms add physical attack capability that most assault platforms lack. The chassis stability is a genuine engineering feature rather than a marketing claim — this machine holds aim better on rough terrain than comparable designs. Variant 3 carries an LRM-20 with Artemis V, a HAG/20, and seven small pulse lasers. The Artemis V improves LRM grouping. The HAG/20 spreads ballistic projectiles across multiple armour locations. Seven small pulse lasers create a point-defence network against fast-moving opponents and physical attack attempts. This is specifically configured to counter Death From Above approaches.
variants.deployment: Variant 3 was designed to discourage jumping attacks. The HAG/20 spread at medium range, the LRM-20 at long range, and seven small pulse lasers tracking close approaches together create a threat profile that makes DFA attempts costly. The small pulse laser volume at close range is the deterrent against pilots who try to jump this machine.

variants.name: ANH-1X
variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Annihilator in 2779 as the most heavily armed BattleMech that could still move under its own power. Walk two, run three at a hundred tons on the 200-rated engine. Everything else went to armour and weapons. I have worked on three of these and the phrase I keep coming back to is 'deliberate' — this machine does not do anything quickly, but what it does, it does thoroughly.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three. The speed is not a limitation so much as a design choice — you position this machine where it needs to be before the battle starts. Maintenance complexity is manageable given the standard components used throughout. The four-weapon variants require four synchronised cleaning schedules. Ammunition management across the multiple ballistic systems is the consistent operational discipline. The ANH-1X is the 2779 original: four LB 10-X ACs, four medium lasers, two small pulse lasers, and a small laser on the 200-rated engine. Walk two, run three. The four LB 10-X ACs provide cluster and slug fire simultaneously. The medium lasers handle anything that closes inside the optimal autocannon range. Four autocannon cleaning schedules run simultaneously.
variants.deployment: The 1X goes to a position with good sightlines and stays there. Walk two means you choose the position before the battle, not during it. Four LB 10-X ACs delivering combined fire is a wall of ballistic rounds that most opponents cannot ignore. The medium lasers handle close threats. The machine does not retreat — it either wins the position or gets destroyed holding it.

variants.name: ANH-1G
variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Annihilator in 2779 as the most heavily armed BattleMech that could still move under its own power. Walk two, run three at a hundred tons on the 200-rated engine. Everything else went to armour and weapons. I have worked on three of these and the phrase I keep coming back to is 'deliberate' — this machine does not do anything quickly, but what it does, it does thoroughly.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three. The speed is not a limitation so much as a design choice — you position this machine where it needs to be before the battle starts. Maintenance complexity is manageable given the standard components used throughout. The four-weapon variants require four synchronised cleaning schedules. Ammunition management across the multiple ballistic systems is the consistent operational discipline. The ANH-1G replaces the four autocannons with three Gauss rifles and an ER PPC. Three Gauss rifles at a hundred tons is a devastating accurate ballistic payload. The ER PPC provides energy backup. Nine tons of Gauss ammunition provides meaningful endurance. Walk two, run three unchanged.
variants.deployment: The 1G has served with Clans Coyote and Star Adder since around 2823. Three Gauss rifles firing simultaneously creates a long-range fire output that heavy fortifications struggle to absorb. The ER PPC provides sustained energy fire between Gauss salvos. The same static positioning doctrine as the 1X applies — walk two does not negotiate with mobility.

variants.name: C 'Gausszilla'
variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Annihilator in 2779 as the most heavily armed BattleMech that could still move under its own power. Walk two, run three at a hundred tons on the 200-rated engine. Everything else went to armour and weapons. I have worked on three of these and the phrase I keep coming back to is 'deliberate' — this machine does not do anything quickly, but what it does, it does thoroughly.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three on the Clan fusion engine. The Gausszilla variant mounts five Gauss rifles with eight tons of ammunition distributed across the chassis. Five Gauss rifles simultaneously is an academic question about what happens when you hit something with that much accurate ballistic fire at once. Fourteen tons of armour. Walk two, run three. Double heat sinks.
variants.deployment: The Gausszilla is what it looks like: five Gauss rifles on a stationary platform. Eight tons of ammunition across five rifles is adequate operational endurance for sustained fire. The name was earned. Walk two, run three means you choose the ground and you hold it. Anything at long range in front of this machine is in a difficult situation.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Annihilator in 2779 as the most heavily armed BattleMech that could still move under its own power. Walk two, run three at a hundred tons on the 200-rated engine. Everything else went to armour and weapons. I have worked on three of these and the phrase I keep coming back to is 'deliberate' — this machine does not do anything quickly, but what it does, it does thoroughly.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four on the Clan engine with endo steel — faster than the base chassis. The Annihilator C carries four Ultra AC/10s and four ER medium lasers. The UAC/10s in double-tap mode deliver a volume of medium-calibre ballistic fire that overwhelms most armour at medium range. The ER mediums provide energy backup. Four UAC mechanisms require synchronised cleaning schedules.
variants.deployment: The C standard, introduced around 2848, is the most mobile Annihilator variant at walk three. The UAC/10 double-tap rate of fire combined with four launchers creates sustained pressure. The ER mediums handle anything inside UAC minimum range. Still a static-position machine by assault standards, just slightly less so than the base chassis.

variants.name: C 2
variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Annihilator in 2779 as the most heavily armed BattleMech that could still move under its own power. Walk two, run three at a hundred tons on the 200-rated engine. Everything else went to armour and weapons. I have worked on three of these and the phrase I keep coming back to is 'deliberate' — this machine does not do anything quickly, but what it does, it does thoroughly.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three. The speed is not a limitation so much as a design choice — you position this machine where it needs to be before the battle starts. Maintenance complexity is manageable given the standard components used throughout. The four-weapon variants require four synchronised cleaning schedules. Ammunition management across the multiple ballistic systems is the consistent operational discipline. The C 2 carries four Gauss rifles, an ER PPC, and an ER small laser. Three tons of armour was removed to mount this weapons load. Four Gauss rifles and an ER PPC on a hundred-ton machine is a long-range fire density that justifies the armour reduction — in theory. Walk two, run three.
variants.deployment: The C 2 prioritises long-range firepower over protection to a degree that the armour reduction makes it more fragile than the base 1X. Four Gauss rifles and an ER PPC deliver impressive output at range. The reduced armour means anything that closes to medium or short range and survives the initial volley has a meaningful chance of ending this machine. A specialist fire position design.

Ammunition management across the multiple ballistic systems is the consistent operational discipline. The ANH-1A is the downgraded version Wolf's Dragoons carried to the Inner Sphere from 3005. Four KaliYama Class 10 standard AC/10s replace the LB 10-X models. Four Martell Model 5 medium lasers. Walk two, run three. Standard autocannons rather than the LB 10-X, which removes the cluster munition option but simplifies ammunition supply.
variants.deployment: The 1A was the Annihilator configuration available when Clan-quality LB 10-X systems could not be sourced in the Inner Sphere. The standard AC/10s perform adequately. The cluster munition option is gone but the fundamental tactics are unchanged. Wolf's Dragoons maintained these machines effectively with Inner Sphere supply chains.

Ammunition management across the multiple ballistic systems is the consistent operational discipline. The ANH-1E is a field-expedient refit from after the Battle of Misery in 3028. With autocannon ammunition critically depleted, Dragoon technicians replaced all four autocannons with standard PPCs and kept the four medium lasers. Walk two, run three. All-energy loadout with no ammunition dependency.
variants.deployment: The 1E was born from necessity, not design philosophy. Replacing four autocannons with four PPCs on a walk-two platform changes the tactical role from a sustained ballistic fire position to an energy fire position. The PPC heat load on twenty heat sinks requires firing discipline the autocannon version did not. The field refit shows in the maintenance documentation.

The LB 10-X upgrade from the 1A restores the cluster munition option. The medium pulse lasers are more accurate than the standard medium lasers of the 1X. Walk two, run three unchanged.
variants.deployment: The 2A is the production standard upgrade. The LB 10-X and pulse laser combination improves on both the original 1X and the Dragoon downgrade 1A. The cluster munition option returns. The pulse laser accuracy is a genuine improvement for engaging fast-moving targets at close range. Same static positioning doctrine throughout.

variants.name: ANH-3A
variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Annihilator in 2779 as the most heavily armed BattleMech that could still move under its own power. Walk two, run three at a hundred tons on the 200-rated engine. Everything else went to armour and weapons. I have worked on three of these and the phrase I keep coming back to is 'deliberate' — this machine does not do anything quickly, but what it does, it does thoroughly.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three on a compact engine. The ANH-3A carries eight Light AC/2s and four ER medium lasers. Light ferro-fibrous armour with CASE covers the ammunition. The compact engine frees internal space for the expanded weapons and armour load. Eight light autocannon feeds require eight cleaning schedules — the maintenance overhead from the 1X's four-weapon cleaning requirement roughly doubled.
variants.deployment: The 3A maximises ballistic rate of fire through eight AC/2s rather than four larger weapons. The volume of fire is higher than any other Annihilator variant at the cost of per-shot damage. The ER mediums provide energy backup. CASE ammunition protection is appropriate given the ammunition density. Compact engine and gyro technology enables the additional armour without sacrificing weapons.

variants.name: ANH-4A
variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Annihilator in 2779 as the most heavily armed BattleMech that could still move under its own power. Walk two, run three at a hundred tons on the 200-rated engine. Everything else went to armour and weapons. I have worked on three of these and the phrase I keep coming back to is 'deliberate' — this machine does not do anything quickly, but what it does, it does thoroughly.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three. The speed is not a limitation so much as a design choice — you position this machine where it needs to be before the battle starts. Maintenance complexity is manageable given the standard components used throughout. The four-weapon variants require four synchronised cleaning schedules. Ammunition management across the multiple ballistic systems is the consistent operational discipline. The ANH-4A carries two heavy PPCs, two LB 10-X ACs, and two Light AC/2s. The heavy PPCs hit harder than standard PPCs at medium range. The LB 10-X ACs add cluster and slug ballistic options. The Light AC/2s provide long-range harassment. A compact gyro improves gyro crit survivability. Walk two, run three.
variants.deployment: The 4A covers multiple range bands from the same configuration: heavy PPCs at medium, LB 10-X at medium-short, Light AC/2 harassment at long. The heavy PPC minimum range gap requires the autocannons to handle close engagement. The compact gyro reduces the likelihood of a single gyro crit ending the engagement prematurely.

variants.name: ANH-2AX
variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Annihilator in 2779 as the most heavily armed BattleMech that could still move under its own power. Walk two, run three at a hundred tons on the 200-rated engine. Everything else went to armour and weapons. I have worked on three of these and the phrase I keep coming back to is 'deliberate' — this machine does not do anything quickly, but what it does, it does thoroughly.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three on a compact engine. The ANH-2AX carries two Improved Heavy Gauss Rifles and nineteen tons of Laser Reflective Armour. The IHGauss rifles deliver substantially more damage than standard Gauss rifles per shot. The laser reflective armour reduces incoming energy weapon damage significantly. The ammunition bays are relocated from the torso to the legs — an unusual placement that requires different maintenance procedures.
variants.deployment: The 2AX is the energy weapon counter-variant. Laser reflective armour at nineteen tons makes energy-heavy opponents significantly less effective. The IHGauss rifles provide the offensive output. The leg-mounted ammunition bays require familiarity with the non-standard layout before working on this variant. The compact engine and gyro enable the armour mass.

variants.name: ANH-5W
variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Annihilator in 2779 as the most heavily armed BattleMech that could still move under its own power. Walk two, run three at a hundred tons on the 200-rated engine. Everything else went to armour and weapons.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three. The speed is not a limitation so much as a design choice — you position this machine where it needs to be before the battle starts. Four-weapon variants require four synchronised cleaning schedules. Ammunition management across ballistic systems is the consistent operational discipline. The ANH-5W carries four Gauss rifles and four medium pulse lasers on endo steel with compact gyro and CASE II. Four Gauss rifles simultaneously at range is the entire tactical concept.
variants.deployment: The 5W builds on the four-Gauss concept with modern IS construction improvements. Endo steel reduces structural mass. CASE II provides thorough ammunition explosion protection. The compact gyro reduces gyro crit vulnerability. Medium pulse laser accuracy handles close threats. Gauss ammunition tracking across four rifles is the operational management task.

variants.name: LK-3D
variants.overview: The Antlion is a forty-five ton quadrupedal indirect fire platform built for the AFFS. The quad configuration provides exceptional stability for mortar delivery. Walk five, run seven on the 225-rated XL engine. Two Mech Mortar-4 systems and two light machine guns. This is a specialised support platform, not a combat machine.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven on the 225-rated XL engine at forty-five tons. The Antlion carries two Mech Mortar-4 systems and two light machine guns. The quad configuration provides stability that a biped cannot match when delivering mortar barrages — the rounds group tighter and the platform is less susceptible to concussion from nearby detonations. The light machine guns handle any infantry that approaches. The XL engine vulnerability applies.
variants.deployment: The AFFS deploys the Antlion in defensive and urban warfare roles where terrain provides cover during mortar delivery. It sets up a position, delivers barrages, and relies on infantry or other 'Mechs to screen it from direct engagement. The quad stability makes it accurate at indirect fire. It has no meaningful direct combat capability beyond the machine guns.

variants.name: ABS-3L
variants.overview: Hellespont Industries built the Anubis in 3063 as a thirty-ton stealth light fire support platform for the Capellan Confederation. Walk eight, run twelve on the 240-rated XL engine. Hellespont Lite stealth armour and Guardian ECM make it difficult to detect and target. The design accepts paper-thin armour protection in exchange for the electronics suite.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at thirty tons. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active — a constant consideration for a machine with energy weapons. The Guardian ECM disrupts enemy sensors and targeting systems. The XL engine at thirty tons makes side torso damage fatal. What keeps this machine alive is that stealth and ECM together make it genuinely hard to hit. The ABS-3L is the original production model: four LRM-5 launchers distributed across both side torsos and an ER small laser. Walk eight, run twelve. The LRM-5s provide indirect fire from stand-off range under stealth cover. The ER small laser handles anything that gets close. Stealth armour heat doubles while active.
variants.deployment: The 3L deploys as a stealth indirect fire platform. The four LRM-5s deliver sustained missile fire from positions opponents cannot easily target. The ER small laser deters close approach. Walk eight means it can reposition between volleys to avoid counter-battery fire. The armour is minimal and close engagement is genuinely dangerous.

variants.name: ABS-3R
variants.overview: Hellespont Industries built the Anubis in 3063 as a thirty-ton stealth light fire support platform for the Capellan Confederation. Walk eight, run twelve on the 240-rated XL engine. Hellespont Lite stealth armour and Guardian ECM make it difficult to detect and target. The design accepts paper-thin armour protection in exchange for the electronics suite.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at thirty tons. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active — a constant consideration for a machine with energy weapons. The Guardian ECM disrupts enemy sensors and targeting systems. The XL engine at thirty tons makes side torso damage fatal. What keeps this machine alive is that stealth and ECM together make it genuinely hard to hit. The ABS-3R carries two LRM-5s, a Rocket Launcher-10, and two Rocket Launcher-15s. Walk eight, run twelve. The RL-10 and two RL-15s are one-shot weapons providing a devastating single alpha strike of forty rockets. After that initial volley the machine has two LRM-5s. The stealth approach enables the alpha strike at close range.
variants.deployment: The 3R is an ambush striker. The stealth approach closes range while undetected. The RL-10 and twin RL-15 alpha strike delivers one devastating volley at close range then the machine becomes a two-LRM-5 platform. Warriors who set up the ambush correctly get one exceptional engagement. Warriors who fire early waste the primary capability.

variants.name: ABS-3T
variants.overview: Hellespont Industries built the Anubis in 3063 as a thirty-ton stealth light fire support platform for the Capellan Confederation. Walk eight, run twelve on the 240-rated XL engine. Hellespont Lite stealth armour and Guardian ECM make it difficult to detect and target. The design accepts paper-thin armour protection in exchange for the electronics suite.

The Guardian ECM disrupts enemy sensors and targeting systems. The XL engine at thirty tons makes side torso damage fatal. What keeps this machine alive is that stealth and ECM together make it genuinely hard to hit. The ABS-3T carries an ER large laser, two ER medium lasers, and an ER small laser. Walk eight, run twelve. All energy, no ammunition dependency. The ER large laser provides the longest reach in the Anubis family. The mediums and small laser handle closer engagement. Heat from the full suite under stealth armour active requires strict cycling.
variants.deployment: The 3T is an aggressive energy skirmisher. The ER large laser range combined with stealth makes it difficult to engage effectively at distance. The all-energy loadout suits independent operations without supply. Heat management with stealth active and the ER lasers firing requires understanding the combined heat budget before each engagement.

variants.name: ABS-3MC
variants.overview: Hellespont Industries built the Anubis in 3063 as a thirty-ton stealth light fire support platform for the Capellan Confederation. Walk eight, run twelve on the 240-rated XL engine. Hellespont Lite stealth armour and Guardian ECM make it difficult to detect and target. The design accepts paper-thin armour protection in exchange for the electronics suite.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at thirty tons. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active — a constant consideration for a machine with energy weapons. The Guardian ECM disrupts enemy sensors and targeting systems. The XL engine at thirty tons makes side torso damage fatal. What keeps this machine alive is that stealth and ECM together make it genuinely hard to hit. The ABS-3MC carries two Enhanced LRM-5s and two ER medium lasers. Walk eight, run twelve. Enhanced LRMs have no minimum range limitation — the standard LRM weakness at close range is eliminated. The Angel ECM suite replaces the Guardian on this variant, providing better electronic warfare capability. Two ER mediums provide close backup.
variants.deployment: The 3MC adds Angel ECM to the standard stealth electronics suite, substantially improving electronic warfare capability. The Enhanced LRM-5s address the minimum range gap that limits standard LRM configurations at close engagement. The 3MC operates effectively at ranges where standard LRM designs cannot.

variants.name: ABS-4C
variants.overview: Hellespont Industries built the Anubis in 3063 as a thirty-ton stealth light fire support platform for the Capellan Confederation. Walk eight, run twelve on the 240-rated XL engine. Hellespont Lite stealth armour and Guardian ECM make it difficult to detect and target. variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at thirty tons. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active — a constant consideration for a machine with energy weapons. The Guardian ECM disrupts enemy sensors and targeting systems. The XL engine at thirty tons makes side torso damage fatal. What keeps this machine alive is that stealth and ECM together make it genuinely hard to hit. The ABS-4C carries two MML-5 launchers and two ER small lasers. Walk eight, run twelve. The MML-5s provide SRM or LRM flexibility from the same launchers. A shared two-ton ammunition bay covers both modes. The ER small lasers handle anything at close range. This is the most versatile Anubis variant for engagement range adaptation.
variants.deployment: The 4C adapts to engagement range through the MML-5 mode selection. At distance it fires LRM rounds. Anything that closes gets SRM fire. The ER small lasers cover point-blank threats. The shared ammunition bay simplifies logistics. Pre-loading the correct mode before engagement is the key preparation step.

variants.name: ABS-5Y
variants.overview: Hellespont Industries built the Anubis in 3063 as a thirty-ton stealth light fire support platform for the Capellan Confederation. Walk eight, run twelve on the 240-rated XL engine. Hellespont Lite stealth armour and Guardian ECM make it difficult to detect and target. It carries two light PPCs and two LRM-5s. The light PPCs provide accurate short-to-medium range fire without minimum range complications. The LRM-5s can load Thunder mine munitions for area denial. Walk seven is slightly slower than the base variant.
variants.deployment: The 5Y trades one point of walk speed for the light PPC and Thunder mine capability. The light PPCs are accurate under stealth cover at medium range. Thunder mine-loaded LRM-5s create area denial zones that complement the stealth approach — plant mines from positions opponents cannot target. The trade in speed is modest.

variants.name: ABS-5Z
variants.overview: Hellespont Industries built the Anubis in 3063 as a thirty-ton stealth light fire support platform for the Capellan Confederation. Walk eight, run twelve on the 240-rated XL engine. Hellespont Lite stealth armour and Guardian ECM make it difficult to detect and target. The design accepts paper-thin armour protection in exchange for the electronics suite.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at thirty tons. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active — a constant consideration for a machine with energy weapons. The Guardian ECM disrupts enemy sensors and targeting systems. The XL engine at thirty tons makes side torso damage fatal. What keeps this machine alive is that stealth and ECM together make it genuinely hard to hit. The ABS-5Z uses the 210-rated engine for walk seven, run ten. It carries two ER medium lasers, two Streak SRM-4s, and a TAG system. The Streak SRM-4s fire on lock, guaranteeing missile hits at close range. The TAG designates targets for guided munitions. The ER mediums provide energy backup.
variants.deployment: The 5Z is a designation and close-range support platform. The TAG adds force multiplier value in combined-arms formations with indirect fire assets. The stealth approach allows close designation without being targeted. The Streak SRM-4 reliability makes the close-range missile fire dependable. Units that operate in isolation without artillery support get less value from the 5Z's TAG capability.

variants.name: ANV-3M
variants.overview: The Anvil is a sixty-ton Free Worlds League heavy built in 3055, conceived alongside the Hammer as a paired close-combat platform. Walk five, run seven, jump three on the 300-rated standard engine. Endo steel structure, standard engine for side torso survivability. The design is built for close-range punishment.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump three at sixty tons. The standard engine survives side torso damage that kills XL competitors. Endo steel keeps the mass budget manageable. The jump capability is modest but useful for closing distance over obstacles. Close-range firepower is the design's whole point. The ANV-3M is the original 3055 production model: twin Sutel Precision Line large pulse lasers, two medium lasers, and jump three on the standard engine. Walk five, run seven, jump three. The large pulse lasers are accurate at medium range. The medium lasers cover close work. Standard engine — side torso damage is survivable.
variants.deployment: The 3M established the Anvil's reputation as a close-combat heavy. The large pulse laser accuracy at medium range suits a machine built to close distance and fight at short engagement. Jump three provides obstacle crossing. The standard engine survivability is the chassis's reliable quality in a role that expects to take hits.

variants.name: ANV-5M
variants.overview: The Anvil is a sixty-ton Free Worlds League heavy built in 3055, conceived alongside the Hammer as a paired close-combat platform. Walk five, run seven, jump three on the 300-rated standard engine. Endo steel structure, standard engine for side torso survivability. The design is built for close-range punishment.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump three at sixty tons. The standard engine survives side torso damage that kills XL competitors. Endo steel keeps the mass budget manageable. The jump capability is modest but useful for closing distance over obstacles. Close-range firepower is the design's whole point. The ANV-5M replaces the large pulse lasers with ER large lasers, adds two more medium lasers for four total, and increases jump capability to jump five. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The ER large lasers extend the engagement range beyond the 3M's pulse lasers. Four medium lasers improve close-range energy density. Standard engine.
variants.deployment: The 5M trades the 3M's pulse laser accuracy for ER large laser reach and additional medium lasers. Jump five is a meaningful improvement over jump three for terrain exploitation. The machine now contributes at longer ranges before closing to close work. Standard engine survivability preserved.

variants.name: ANV-6M
variants.overview: The Anvil is a sixty-ton Free Worlds League heavy built in 3055, conceived alongside the Hammer. Walk five, run seven on the 300-rated standard engine. Endo steel structure. Standard engine survivability. The design is built for close-range punishment.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons. The standard engine survives side torso damage that kills XL competitors. Jump capability varies by variant. Close-range firepower is the design's identity. The ANV-6M carries twin large pulse lasers, a medium laser, and a TAG system on the standard 300-rated engine. Walk five, run seven, jump three. The TAG designates for guided munitions. The large pulse lasers provide the direct combat capability. The medium laser handles close backup.
variants.deployment: The 6M is the designation half of the Hammer-Anvil paired concept. Frequently deployed alongside the ANV-8M Arrow IV platform, the 6M tags targets while the 8M delivers artillery. The large pulse lasers keep it from being a passive bystander in direct engagements.

variants.name: ANV-8M
variants.overview: The Anvil is a sixty-ton Free Worlds League heavy built in 3055, conceived alongside the Hammer. Walk five, run seven on the 300-rated standard engine. Endo steel structure. Standard engine survivability. The design is built for close-range punishment.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons. The standard engine survives side torso damage that kills XL competitors. Jump capability varies by variant. Close-range firepower is the design's identity. The ANV-8M uses a 240-rated engine for walk four, run six, and carries an Arrow IV artillery launcher, an ER large laser, and two ER medium lasers. Arrow IV is battlefield artillery in a 'Mech chassis, hitting far harder at greater range than standard LRMs. Walk four is slower than the base 3M.
variants.deployment: The 8M is the artillery half of the Hammer-Anvil concept. The Arrow IV requires homing munitions or conventional artillery rounds and its supply logistics are entirely separate from standard missile supply. Paired with the 6M's TAG designation capability, the 8M delivers guided artillery fire to designated targets. The ER lasers handle direct combat when needed.

variants.name: ANV-3R
variants.overview: The Anvil is a sixty-ton Free Worlds League heavy built in 3055, conceived alongside the Hammer. Walk five, run seven on the 300-rated standard engine. Endo steel structure. Standard engine survivability. The design is built for close-range punishment.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons. The standard engine survives side torso damage that kills XL competitors. Jump capability varies by variant. Close-range firepower is the design's identity. The ANV-3R trades all three jump jets for three additional tons of armour. Walk five, run seven with no jump capability. Twin large pulse lasers and two medium lasers — same weapons as the 3M. The armour upgrade makes this the most protected Anvil variant.
variants.deployment: The 3R is for commanders who want the Anvil's close-range firepower without the jump dependency. The additional armour is meaningful in a design that expects to receive fire. The loss of jump capability is the tradeoff that experienced Anvil pilots notice immediately. It suits operations in open terrain where jump jets would see limited use.

variants.name: ANV-5Q
variants.overview: The Anvil is a sixty-ton Free Worlds League heavy built in 3055, conceived alongside the Hammer. Walk five, run seven on the 300-rated standard engine. Endo steel structure. Standard engine survivability. The design is built for close-range punishment.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons. The standard engine survives side torso damage that kills XL competitors. Jump capability varies by variant. Close-range firepower is the design's identity. The ANV-5Q carries twin large pulse lasers and two medium lasers with jump three, dropping half a ton of armour and the Guardian ECM suite compared to an earlier configuration to gain two additional heat sinks. The extra heat dissipation allows more aggressive firing.
variants.deployment: The 5Q prioritises heat management over electronic warfare and armour. The two additional heat sinks make a tangible difference in sustained close-range engagement. Units that found the earlier ECM-equipped Anvil variant heat-constrained in sustained combat tend to prefer the 5Q. The modest armour reduction is the cost.

variants.name: ZU-G60
variants.overview: The Anzu is a sixty-ton heavy built for the Aurigan Mercenary Auxiliaries in 3098 on an Earthwerks ZU Endo Steel chassis. Walk four, run six, jump four on the 240-rated XL engine. The design is built around an Ultra AC/10 as the primary weapon, supported by a light PPC and an LRM-10.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four on the XL engine. The ZU-G60 carries an Ultra AC/10, a light PPC, an ER medium laser, an LRM-10, and a TAG system. The UAC/10 is the primary weapon — medium-range ballistic fire with double-tap rate capability. The light PPC covers short to medium range. The LRM-10 adds indirect fire. The TAG designates for guided munitions. XL engine vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The baseline Anzu for the AMSC. The UAC/10 double-tap at medium range is the primary combat output. The TAG adds force multiplier value alongside the direct combat role. The XL engine means side torso damage ends the engagement. Produced from 3098, parts availability within Aurigan supply chains is reasonable.

variants.name: ZU-J70
variants.overview: The Anzu is a sixty-ton heavy built for the Aurigan Mercenary Auxiliaries in 3098 on an Earthwerks ZU Endo Steel chassis. Walk four, run six, jump four on the 240-rated XL engine. The design is built around an Ultra AC/10 as the primary weapon, supported by a light PPC and an LRM-10.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four on the XL engine. The ZU-J70 carries a Rotary AC/5, a snub-nose PPC, an MML-7, an ER medium laser, and an ER small laser. The Rotary AC/5 delivers sustained ballistic fire at medium range. The snub-nose PPC covers short range without minimum range complications. The MML-7 adds SRM/LRM flexibility. XL engine vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The ZU-J70 introduced in 3106 replaces the UAC/10's single-target punch with Rotary AC/5 sustained rate of fire. The snub-nose PPC handles close engagement more cleanly than the light PPC of the base model. The MML-7 flexibility is a useful tactical tool. Rotary AC ammunition and MML ammunition require separate tracking.

variants.name: APL-1M
variants.overview: Earthwerks Incorporated built the Apollo in 3054 for the Free Worlds League Military as an affordable medium fire support platform. Fifty-five tons, walk four, run six on the 220-rated standard engine. Twin LRM-15s with Artemis IV are the whole point. Everything else is backup.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the standard engine at fifty-five tons. The standard engine gives survivability the XL variants sacrifice. The Artemis IV fire control on the LRM-15s improves grouping substantially over unguided fire. Two small pulse lasers handle anything that closes inside LRM minimum range, which is not the primary engagement scenario this machine was built for. The APL-1M is the base production model: twin LRM-15s with Artemis IV and two small pulse lasers. Walk four, run six. Artemis IV on both launchers improves grouping substantially. The small pulse lasers are accurate at close range. Standard engine — side torso damage is survivable.
variants.deployment: The 1M is the reference Apollo. Twin Artemis-guided LRM-15s from a fire support position. The small pulse lasers handle anything that gets past the missile screen. Standard engine survivability means it absorbs counter-battery hits that would kill XL variants. Go somewhere useful, stay there, fire missiles.

variants.name: APL-1R
variants.overview: Earthwerks Incorporated built the Apollo in 3054 for the Free Worlds League Military as an affordable medium fire support platform. Fifty-five tons, walk four, run six on the 220-rated standard engine. Twin LRM-15s with Artemis IV are the whole point. Everything else is backup.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the standard engine at fifty-five tons. The standard engine gives survivability the XL variants sacrifice. The Artemis IV fire control on the LRM-15s improves grouping substantially over unguided fire. Two small pulse lasers handle anything that closes inside LRM minimum range, which is not the primary engagement scenario this machine was built for. The APL-1R removes the Artemis IV systems from both launchers and uses the freed tonnage for additional missile ammunition. Walk four, run six. More rounds, less accuracy per salvo. The small pulse lasers remain. Standard engine survivability.

Units that expect sustained fire missions without resupply opportunities tend to prefer the 1R over the 1M.

variants.name: APL-2S
variants.overview: Earthwerks Incorporated built the Apollo in 3054 for the Free Worlds League Military as an affordable medium fire support platform. Fifty-five tons, walk four, run six on the 220-rated standard engine. Twin LRM-15s with Artemis IV are the whole point. Everything else is backup.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the standard engine at fifty-five tons. The standard engine gives survivability the XL variants sacrifice. The Artemis IV fire control on the LRM-15s improves grouping substantially over unguided fire. Two small pulse lasers handle anything that closes inside LRM minimum range, which is not the primary engagement scenario this machine was built for. The APL-2S replaces the small pulse lasers with medium lasers and adds heat sinks. Walk four, run six. Medium lasers provide better close-range anti-armour capability than small pulse lasers. The added heat sinks improve sustained fire management. Standard engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The 2S is the close-range upgrade. The medium lasers make a meaningful difference when something closes inside LRM minimum range compared to the small pulse laser backup. The additional heat sinks handle the medium laser heat more comfortably than the base configuration would.

variants.name: APL-3T
variants.overview: Earthwerks Incorporated built the Apollo in 3054 for the Free Worlds League Military as an affordable medium fire support platform. Fifty-five tons, walk four, run six on the 220-rated standard engine. Twin LRM-15s with Artemis IV are the whole point. Everything else is backup.

Less missile output at range, better direct combat capability at close range. Standard engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The 3T is the mixed-role variant. The LRM-10s provide reduced but still meaningful indirect fire. The medium pulse lasers and medium lasers make it a capable combatant at close range rather than a missile platform with token self-defence. Units that need a medium to pull double duty as fire support and line fighter use the 3T.

variants.name: APL-4M
variants.overview: Earthwerks Incorporated built the Apollo in 3054 for the Free Worlds League Military as an affordable medium fire support platform. Fifty-five tons, walk four, run six on the 220-rated standard engine. Twin LRM-15s with Artemis IV are the whole point. Everything else is backup.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on a 220-rated XL engine with Composite structure. The APL-4M carries twin Extended LRM-15s and an ER medium laser. The Extended LRM-15s reach substantially beyond standard LRM range. The XL engine frees mass for the ELRM system. The ER medium laser handles anything that closes. XL vulnerability applies.
variants.deployment: The 4M is the maximum stand-off variant. The ELRM-15 range combined with the Apollo's traditional fire support role means opponents need to close significantly farther to escape the missile envelope. The XL engine vulnerability is the tradeoff for the ELRM capability. ELRM ammunition supply is distinct from standard LRM logistics.

variants.name: AQS-3
variants.overview: The Aquagladius is a fifty-ton medium built specifically for Solaris VII's Pool arena and underwater combat. Walk six, run nine on the 300-rated light engine. This is a specialist arena machine, not a general-purpose platform.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 300-rated light engine. The AQS-3 carries a BattleMech Taser and a flail. The Taser disrupts enemy electronics rather than destroying armour. The flail is a physical weapon for close combat. Both weapons are designed for underwater arena engagement. The light engine provides side torso survivability. This machine has almost no conventional combat capability.
variants.deployment: The AQS-3 was built for Solaris VII's Pool arena in 3065 and that is its entire operational context. The Taser disabling and flail physical attack suite is tailored for arena rules and audience appeal. Outside an underwater arena environment the weapons are largely useless against armoured opponents. Maintain it to Pool arena specifications.

variants.name: AQS-4
variants.overview: The Aquagladius is a fifty-ton medium built specifically for Solaris VII's Pool arena and underwater combat. Walk six, run nine on the 300-rated light engine. This is a specialist arena machine, not a general-purpose platform.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the light engine. The AQS-4 carries a large X-pulse laser and four ER medium lasers. The X-pulse laser is accurate and effective underwater where beam weapons degrade less than in atmosphere. The ER mediums provide additional energy fire. Additional armour over the 3 variant improves survivability. Light engine side torso survivability.
variants.deployment: The AQS-4 is the combat-capable Aquagladius variant. The large X-pulse and ER medium suite actually functions as a useful weapons loadout rather than arena-specific equipment. The additional armour and light engine make it more durable than the base model. It sees use in both arena and limited operational roles.

variants.name: AQS-5 MAM
variants.overview: The Aquagladius is a fifty-ton medium built specifically for Solaris VII's Pool arena and underwater combat. Walk six, run nine on the 300-rated light engine. This is a specialist arena machine, not a general-purpose platform.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 300-rated Clan XXL engine. The AQS-5 MAM carries a heavy PPC with PPC capacitor, two small VSP lasers, and two ER flamers. The XXL engine is extraordinarily vulnerable to side torso damage. The heavy PPC capacitor allows overcharge shots at severe heat cost. The VSP lasers and ER flamers handle close threats. Composite internal structure reduces weight but lowers structural integrity.
variants.deployment: The Marine Assault variant pushes the Aquagladius concept into operational territory with a heavy PPC as the primary weapon. The XXL engine vulnerability is severe. The heavy PPC capacitor overcharge is a tactical option, not a default — the heat cost requires selective use. Composite structure and XXL engine together mean this machine is fragile in ways that limit where it can deploy.

variants.overview: The Arbalest is a twenty-five ton Clan light built around electronic warfare rather than raw firepower. Walk five, run seven on the 125-rated Clan engine. The ECM suite and sensor capability are the design's primary tools.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at twenty-five tons. The ECM disrupts enemy fire control networks. The weapons load is modest — this machine operates by degrading what opponents can do rather than by outgunning them. Variant 2 carries two ER medium lasers and one LRM-10, with jump capability added by dropping one LRM launcher. The ECM suite remains. Walk five, run seven. The ER mediums provide better close-range energy fire. Jump was the specific gap addressed.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 addresses the original's inability to break contact by adding jump. The trade is one LRM-10 instead of two. Warriors who needed the exit option that the original lacked run variant 2.

variants.overview: The Arbalest is a twenty-five ton Clan light built around electronic warfare rather than raw firepower. Walk five, run seven on the 125-rated Clan engine. The ECM suite and sensor capability are the design's primary tools.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at twenty-five tons. The ECM disrupts enemy fire control networks. The weapons load is modest — this machine operates by degrading what opponents can do rather than by outgunning them. Variant 3 carries two LRM-10s and four ER small lasers with additional armour. Walk five, run seven. No jump capability. Two LRM-10s restore the twin launcher concept. The ECM suite remains.
variants.deployment: Variant 3 prioritises survivability and missile volume over mobility. The additional armour makes it more durable in garrison duty. Two LRM-10s deliver the sustained fire the original was designed for. The ECM provides the electronic warfare capability throughout.

variants.overview: The Arcas is a sixty-five ton Clan heavy built around a 325-rated Clan XL engine for walk five, run seven, jump five. It was designed as a logistics-friendly option for garrison forces far from supply lines — the weapons choices reflect that priority over raw firepower.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at sixty-five tons. The Clan XL carries standard side torso vulnerability. Endo steel structure. The jump capability is the consistent tactical feature across all variants. Clan construction quality. Variant 2 carries twin ER PPCs and two medium pulse lasers. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The ER PPCs replace the base model's extended range large lasers with heavier direct fire capability. The medium pulse lasers cover close range accurately. The all-energy loadout was specifically chosen for garrison forces without reliable ammunition supply.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 is the ammunition-free configuration for remote garrison operations. The ER PPC range combined with jump five provides strong tactical positioning options. The medium pulse lasers handle anything that closes. The Clan XL vulnerability is the standard concern. Warriors assigned to remote postings find the logistics simplicity valuable.

variants.overview: The Arcas is a sixty-five ton Clan heavy built around a 325-rated Clan XL engine for walk five, run seven, jump five. It was designed as a logistics-friendly option for garrison forces far from supply lines — the weapons choices reflect that priority over raw firepower.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at sixty-five tons. The Clan XL carries standard side torso vulnerability. Endo steel structure. The jump capability is the consistent tactical feature across all variants. Clan construction quality. Variant 3 carries a heavy large laser, two medium pulse lasers, and a Streak SRM-4, with seven improved jump jets for jump seven. Walk five, run seven, jump seven. The improved jump jets are the standout feature — jump seven on a sixty-five ton heavy is exceptional. The heavy large laser hits hard at medium range but generates more heat than a standard large laser.
variants.deployment: Variant 3 prioritises jump mobility over weapons reach. Jump seven allows terrain exploitation and flanking angles unavailable to most heavy designs. The heavy large laser delivers the punch once in position. The Streak SRM-4 handles close threats on lock. Warriors who use the jump jets aggressively get more from this variant than warriors who treat it as a ground-bound heavy.

variants.name: C-ANG-O Invictus
variants.overview: The Archangel is a hundred-ton Word of Blake assault OmniMech built around a 300-rated compact engine and compact gyro. I've only had my hands inside one of these twice, both times on captured machines, and the internal layout is unlike anything from a conventional manufacturer. The compact components are crammed into the centre torso deliberately, so the machine can lose both side torsos and keep walking. For a Manei Domini platform that's not a design quirk, it's a design philosophy.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four. It's slow even by assault standards, and the compact engine doesn't give you the output of a standard 300-rated plant. What it does give you is a machine that is extraordinarily hard to kill through the sides. The pod space that arrangement frees up is considerable. The VDNI neural interface means your pilot pool is essentially zero outside of Blakist augmented warriors, which makes battlefield losses a logistics catastrophe you cannot recover from quickly.
variants.deployment: The Invictus carries a plasma rifle and heavy PPC linked to an advanced targeting computer, with a Guardian ECM suite and a retractable blade for close work. This is a command variant, built to stand in the back of a formation and be unmovable while the pilot directs operations. The plasma rifle is nasty against conventional infantry and vehicles. Keep it out of close range and it does exactly what it was designed for.

variants.name: C-ANG-OA Dominus
variants.overview: The Archangel is a hundred-ton Word of Blake assault OmniMech built around a 300-rated compact engine and compact gyro. I have only had my hands inside one of these twice, both times under circumstances I would rather not repeat. The design is intended to intimidate as much as to fight.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four. Slow even by assault standards, and the compact engine does not give you the output of a standard 300-rated plant. What it gives you is a machine that carries an enormous pod space on a chassis designed to last in extended engagements. The compact gyro saves tonnage. Every configuration I have seen prioritises either firepower or electronic warfare, not both.
variants.deployment: The Dominus mounts two heavy PPCs and two ER medium lasers, plus a snub-nose PPC, with four jump jets that let a hundred-ton machine leap ninety metres. That still surprises me. The heavy PPC minimum range is filled by the snub-nose. The jump capability and weapons suite make this the most mobile and direct-combat-capable Archangel configuration.

Nine extra double heat sinks manage the thermal load, barely. This configuration wants to stand at range and sustain fire until the target stops moving. Pilots who understand heat discipline can keep it going indefinitely. Pilots who don't learn that lesson fast.

Ammo management is the primary concern on extended operations.
