It mixes a Thunderbolt-10, twin binary laser cannons, Clan-manufactured ER medium and ER small lasers, and paired ER flamers, with seventeen double heat sinks trying to keep up with all of it. The binary lasers produce enormous heat for their damage output and the Clan weapons require different maintenance protocols to the IS components on the same machine. Whoever built this had access to a very well-stocked salvage yard and very few concerns about standardisation.

variants.name: ARC-1A
variants.overview: Earthwerks Incorporated built the Archer in 2474 for the Terran Hegemony and it has been delivering LRM fire from the back of the line ever since. Seventy tons, twin LRM-20s, and enough armour to survive counter-battery fire. Twenty-five variants. I have worked on more Archers than I can count. The design is not complicated — it goes somewhere with good sightlines and it fires missiles.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 280-rated engine at seventy tons. The twin Doombud LRM-20s are the whole machine. Everything else is backup. Ammunition management across two heavy launchers is the consistent operational concern. The battlefists are actually useful in close combat — oversized and durable, they have ended more than a few ambushes that got inside the LRM minimum range. The ARC-1A is the early production model using the primitive chassis and equipment from 2474. Walk three, run four on the 255-rated engine. Two medium lasers and twin LRM-20s. The primitive components require period-specific maintenance documentation. Walk three is the old engine's limitation, not a design preference.
variants.deployment: The 1A is the early Archer before the 2R refinements. Slower than the production standard and built to primitive specifications. It deploys in the same fire support role but with lower mobility and the maintenance overhead of primitive construction. Parts sourcing for the primitive components is the consistent challenge.

variants.deployment: The 2R is the Archer that most techs and pilots know. Produced across six factories throughout the Inner Sphere and Periphery. Parts are available everywhere. It goes somewhere with sightlines and delivers LRM-20 fire. The four medium lasers handle anything that closes. The battlefists are a last resort that actually works.

The extra ammunition ton compensates for the lost medium laser mass. Pilots who understand missile accuracy improvements prefer the 2Rb over the 2R for sustained engagements.

The Clan ER medium laser upgrade is a genuine performance improvement over the IS medium lasers. The Clan engine requires Clan-qualified maintenance. The fundamental fire support role is unchanged.

variants.deployment: This variant was produced for Clan-era Kurita forces who needed C3 network integration on a platform robust enough to hold a battle line. variants.name: AF1
variants.overview: The Arctic Fox is a reliable 30-ton OmniMech built for Inner Sphere components. Its reverse-engineered design from salvaged Clan Kit Fox chassis fills a niche as an affordable, reconfigurable light OmniMech. We've found it to be a valued asset in mercenary and garrison commands due to its flexibility and ease of maintenance.
variants.capabilities: The Arctic Fox achieves a respectable top speed with its GM 180 XL fusion engine, but this powerplant's vulnerability to side torso destruction is a calculated risk. The chassis provides superior protection for a light OmniMech with six tons of Royal-7 standard plate, partially offsetting the XL engine's fragility. Ten fixed double heat sinks manage thermal loads across most configurations, and pod space is available for additional sinks when needed.
variants.deployment: The base configuration serves as a versatile skirmisher, mounting an extended-range PPC capable of engaging targets at nearly 700 meters alongside two medium lasers and paired SRM-4 launchers with a ton of ammunition. This loadout allows the Arctic Fox to wear down opponents at range before closing for the kill, seeking weak points in damaged armor.

variants.deployment: The B configuration is the ballistic variant. The LB 10-X cluster option against lighter opponents and aircraft is the reason to run this over energy configurations. One ton of ammunition runs out quickly on active operations.

variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the surface. Configuration U carries a light PPC and an LRT-10 torpedo launcher, with five underwater maneuvering units providing subaquatic mobility. The light PPC performs in both environments. The LRT-10 provides torpedo fire support underwater. The UMUs allow the machine to function in environments where surface mobility is irrelevant.
variants.deployment: The U configuration deploys in aquatic operations. The UMUs provide subaquatic movement capability that surface configurations lack. The LRT-10 delivers torpedo fire support underwater. The light PPC handles direct combat in both environments. Torpedo tube seals require inspection after every subaquatic deployment.

variants.overview: The Arctic Wolf 2 is an upgraded version of the original Arctic Wolf, with a focus on improving its OmniPod design and combat capabilities. Built around a fast and agile chassis, it's designed to close quickly with opponents, unleash devastating short-range missile salvos, and withdraw before taking significant damage. The Wolf-in-Exile produced this variant at WC Site 1 on Arc-Royal, using materials from the Kell Hounds.
variants.capabilities: The Arctic Wolf 2 excels in its ability to deliver rapid-fire short-range missiles, with a salvo capacity of over forty rounds. Its speed and agility allow it to quickly reposition itself after firing, making it difficult for opponents to return fire effectively. However, sustained engagements can be problematic due to heat management issues. The OmniPod design also makes maintenance a bit more challenging than its predecessor.
variants.deployment: The sole factory variant replaces some SRM launchers with an Alpha Series large pulse laser, reducing ammunition dependency and providing long-range engagement capability. This modification doesn't address the chassis' heat dissipation concerns, but it does offer a different playstyle compared to the base model.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Arctic Wolf is a forty-ton Clan medium OmniMech used by Clan Wolf as a fast raider and skirmisher. Walk six, run nine on the 240-rated Clan XL. The design is built around speed and weapons flexibility across its configuration set.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at forty tons. The Clan XL at this weight means side torso damage is fatal. Fast enough to engage or disengage on the warrior's terms in most encounters. Pod space is adequate for the weight class. Configuration A carries twin LRM-15s and two SRM-6 launchers plus two small pulse lasers. Walk six, run nine. The LRM-15s provide long-range indirect fire. The SRM-6s deliver close-range missile volume. The small pulse lasers handle point-blank threats. Ammunition management across LRM and SRM feeds requires planning.
variants.deployment: Configuration A shifts the Arctic Wolf from its primary raider role toward combined fire support and close assault. The LRM-15s at range transition to SRM-6s as the engagement closes. The small pulse lasers handle anything that reaches point-blank. Ammunition management across two missile types is the operational overhead.

variants.deployment: The Primary Configuration mounts four Streak SRM-6 launchers with four tons of CASE-protected ammunition, eliminating wasted missiles inherent in standard launchers. Jump jets provide tactical mobility unavailable to the original BattleMech, partially offsetting the reduced ground speed.

It also includes an ECM suite and active probe for electronic warfare and reconnaissance capabilities. While this variant addresses some performance shortcomings, it was ultimately seen as insufficient to address the OmniMech's fundamental speed deficiency.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Arctic Wolf II redesigned the original Arctic Wolf chassis around a 280-rated Clan XL engine for walk seven, run ten with fixed jump jets providing jump seven. The larger engine and fixed jump capability address performance issues from the predecessor. Forty tons with exceptional speed and jump mobility.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty tons. The Clan XL at forty tons means side torso damage is fatal. Walk seven is fast enough to outrun most non-light opponents. Jump seven is exceptional mobility for the weight class. The fixed jump jets cannot be traded away in pod configurations. Configuration A carries four Streak SRM-4 launchers and two small pulse lasers. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The Streak SRM-4s fire only on lock, guaranteeing every missile hits. Four launchers firing simultaneously at close range is substantial missile volume. The small pulse lasers handle anything at point-blank.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is a close-range strike variant using the jump capability to close distance from unexpected angles. Walk seven, jump seven together allow approach from positions opponents do not cover. The Streak SRM-4s deliver guaranteed missile hits at close range. The Clan XL at forty tons means any hit to the side torso ends the mission.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: The Arctic Wolf II redesigned the original Arctic Wolf chassis around a 280-rated Clan XL engine for walk seven, run ten with fixed jump jets providing jump seven. The larger engine and fixed jump capability address performance issues from the predecessor. Forty tons with exceptional speed and jump mobility.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty tons. The Clan XL at forty tons means side torso damage is fatal. Walk seven is fast enough to outrun most non-light opponents. Jump seven is exceptional mobility for the weight class. The fixed jump jets cannot be traded away in pod configurations. Configuration B carries four standard SRM-4 launchers, a large pulse laser, and a small pulse laser. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. Standard SRM-4s fire without the Streak lock requirement. The large pulse laser is the primary direct fire weapon. The small pulse laser adds close backup.
variants.deployment: Configuration B trades the Streak A's guaranteed missile hits for volume fire and a heavier direct fire weapon. The large pulse laser accuracy is the standout capability at medium range. The four SRM-4s deliver close-range missile volume on demand without needing a lock. Jump seven maintains the A configuration's terrain exploitation advantage.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: The Arctic Wolf II is a 40-ton Clan OmniMech that fixes the speed and armour complaints that followed the original design. The 280-rated Clan XL pushes it to walk seven, run ten, with fixed jump jets providing jump seven capability. That is exceptional mobility for a forty-ton platform and the fixed equipment leaves good pod space for weapons.
variants.capabilities: The C configuration mounts twin ER large lasers and two SRM-4 launchers with a ton of ammunition each. At this weight class the ER large lasers are the primary tools and they are excellent, reaching out to ranges where most enemies at this tonnage cannot reply effectively. The SRMs are close-in deterrents. The XL engine is the standard concern at forty tons: a determined flanking attack through a side torso ends the engagement. Warriors in this configuration need to use their speed to avoid that situation, not armour to absorb it.
variants.deployment: The C configuration sees use as a fast harassment element, using jump capability and speed to control engagement range and strike from unexpected angles. The ER large lasers reward warriors who stay disciplined about distance. Getting into SRM range usually means something has already gone wrong.

variants.name: Prime
variants.overview: The Arctic Wolf II redesigned the original Arctic Wolf chassis around a 280-rated Clan XL engine for walk seven, run ten with fixed jump jets providing jump seven. The larger engine and fixed jump capability address performance issues from the predecessor. Forty tons with exceptional speed and jump mobility.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty tons. The Clan XL at forty tons means side torso damage is fatal. Walk seven is fast enough to outrun most non-light opponents. Jump seven is exceptional mobility for the weight class. The fixed jump jets cannot be traded away in pod configurations. The Prime carries twin LRM-15s, two ER medium lasers, and a small pulse laser. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The LRM-15s provide long-range indirect fire. The ER mediums handle direct engagement. The small pulse laser covers close threats. Two tons of LRM ammunition per launcher is the endurance concern.
variants.deployment: The Prime uses walk seven and jump seven to maintain stand-off range while delivering LRM-15 fire. The jump capability keeps fire positions unpredictable. The ER mediums handle direct threats when the range closes. The speed and jump together make this the most mobile fire support variant of its weight class.

variants.name: AGS-2D
variants.overview: The Argus was originally designed as an OmniMech and then retooled as a conventional platform when the costs of full OmniMech production proved too high for what was intended as a general-purpose heavy. The AGS-2D is the fire support version, built around a 300-rated XL engine at sixty tons, giving you walk five, run seven with no jump capability. Achernar and Robinson both produce this one, which makes parts availability reasonable.
variants.capabilities: Two LRM-15 launchers with Artemis IV fire control are the main event. The Artemis tightens the grouping noticeably and I would not want to operate this variant without it. The ER PPC in the right arm provides direct fire when the target gets inside LRM minimum range or when you run dry. The XL engine is the usual tradeoff: the speed and tonnage savings are real but a side torso breach is fatal. For a fire support platform that wants to stay at range, that is an acceptable risk if the pilot respects it.
variants.deployment: The AGS-2D is a dedicated indirect fire platform and it performs that role well. The Artemis systems make the LRMs count at range and the ER PPC covers the gap when ammunition runs low. The lack of close-range weapons is a real gap in urban or broken terrain where enemies can close faster than the pilot expects. It needs escorts in those conditions.

variants.name: AGS-4D
variants.overview: Foundry originally designed the Argus as an OmniMech but it was retooled as a conventional design with modular weapons bays before production. Sixty tons, walk five, run seven on the 300-rated XL engine. Five variants span long-range fire support to close-quarters brawling. The XL engine vulnerability is the consistent concern across all variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons on the XL engine. Side torso damage is fatal on any XL-equipped Argus. The modular weapons bay design makes field refits easier than most conventional designs. Parts availability within Davion and Kurita supply chains is good given the production history. The AGS-4D carries a Rotary AC/5, an LRM-10, two ER medium lasers, and a machine gun. Walk five, run seven on the XL engine. The Rotary AC/5 delivers sustained ballistic harassment. The LRM-10 adds indirect fire. The ER mediums handle direct energy engagement. The machine gun addresses infantry. Rotary AC and LRM ammunition require separate tracking.
variants.deployment: The 4D is the production urban combat variant. The Rotary AC/5 sustained fire combined with LRM-10 indirect capability suits the engagement mix of urban operations. The machine gun handles infantry threats in close terrain. The XL engine means side torso hits are fatal — the modular weapons bay makes field repairs to the outer weapons faster than replacing damaged internal structure.

variants.name: AGS-5D
variants.overview: Foundry originally designed the Argus as an OmniMech but it was retooled as a conventional design with modular weapons bays before production. Sixty tons, walk five, run seven on the 300-rated XL engine. Five variants span long-range fire support to close-quarters brawling. The XL engine vulnerability is the consistent concern across all variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons on the XL engine. Side torso damage is fatal on any XL-equipped Argus. The modular weapons bay design makes field refits easier than most conventional designs. Parts availability within Davion and Kurita supply chains is good given the production history. The AGS-5D carries a heavy PPC, two Streak SRM-6 launchers, two medium lasers, and a targeting computer. Walk five, run seven on the XL engine. The targeting computer improves accuracy across all weapons. The heavy PPC delivers hard-hitting medium-range fire. The Streak SRM-6s add guaranteed close-range missile hits. The heavy PPC minimum range requires the SRM-6s at close distance.
variants.deployment: The 5D is the precision strike variant. The targeting computer makes the heavy PPC and Streak SRM-6 combination more reliable at their respective range bands. The heavy PPC minimum range gap is where the Streak SRM-6s step in. XL engine vulnerability is the standing concern. The TC maintenance overhead is the additional technical task.

The C3 boosted slave provides extended network integration range over a standard slave. The MML-7 delivers SRM or LRM flexibility. The Rotary AC/5 provides sustained ballistic output. The ER mediums handle direct energy fire.
variants.deployment: The 8DX is the network-optimised variant for heavy ECM environments. The C3 boosted slave maintains connectivity at ranges where standard C3 slaves drop out. The MML-7 flexibility covers both fire support and close engagement. The Rotary AC/5 provides sustained ballistic fire between energy weapon cycles. XL engine vulnerability applies.

The AGS-6F uses a 300-rated light engine, carrying an AC/20, an SRM-6, and two ER medium lasers. Walk five, run seven. The AC/20 is the heaviest single-shot ballistic weapon this chassis can mount. The SRM-6 adds close-range missile punch. The light engine provides better side torso survivability than XL variants. Two tons of AC/20 ammunition is the operational limit.
variants.deployment: The 6F is the close-range devastation variant. The AC/20 at medium range followed by SRM-6 at close range creates a sequence that overwhelms most opponents quickly. Two tons of AC/20 ammunition is not generous for sustained combat. The light engine keeps it alive through side torso hits that kill XL Argus variants. Pilots who manage AC/20 ammunition carefully extend operational effectiveness.

variants.name: ASN-21
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Assassin in 2676 as a forty-ton light hunter and harassment platform. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 280-rated engine. Speed and jump capability are the tactical identity — the weapons load has never been the point.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty tons. That speed and jump combination at this weight is the machine's primary capability. The weapons are self-defence tools rather than the reason to put this machine in the field. Standard engine means side torso hits are survivable. The ASN-21 is the original production model: a medium laser, an SRM-2, and an LRM-5 on the 280-rated engine. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The three weapons together provide modest anti-armour coverage at different ranges. The LRM-5 adds some stand-off capability.
variants.deployment: The 21 has served across the Inner Sphere in rear-area security and raiding operations. The speed and jump capability keep it out of engagements it cannot win. The weapons are for when avoiding contact fails. Units that use the 21 correctly treat it as a fast presence machine that forces reactions rather than a combatant.

variants.name: ASN-101
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Assassin in 2676 as a forty-ton light hunter and harassment platform. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 280-rated engine. Speed and jump capability are the tactical identity — the weapons load has never been the point.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty tons. The speed and jump combination at this weight is the machine's primary capability. The weapons are self-defence tools rather than the reason to put this machine in the field. Standard engine means side torso hits are survivable. The ASN-101 is an unofficial Davion Succession Wars run. Three jump jets removed, armour reduced, to mount three Maxell 50 small lasers alongside the standard medium laser, SRM-2, and LRM-5. Walk seven, run ten, jump four.
variants.deployment: The 101 is a Succession Wars field compromise — fewer jump jets and less armour for more laser firepower. The small lasers add close-range energy volume. Jump four is a reduction but still useful for the light hunter role. The design reflects what was available during the Succession Wars rather than what was ideal.

variants.name: ASN-23
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Assassin in 2676 as a forty-ton light hunter and harassment platform. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 280-rated engine. Speed and jump capability are the tactical identity — the weapons load has never been the point.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty tons. The speed and jump combination at this weight is the machine's primary capability. The weapons are self-defence tools rather than the reason to put this machine in the field. Standard engine means side torso hits are survivable. The ASN-23 is a stripped variant carrying only a medium pulse laser and an LRM-5 with Artemis IV fire control. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The Artemis IV guidance improves the LRM-5 grouping. The medium pulse laser is accurate at close range.
variants.deployment: The 23 is the lightest-armed Assassin variant. The Artemis IV LRM accuracy and pulse laser precision make the limited weapons more effective. The speed and jump capability remain the point. This is a reconnaissance and harassment platform with token self-defence, not a combatant.

variants.name: ASN-30
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Assassin in 2676 as a forty-ton light hunter and harassment platform. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 280-rated engine. Speed and jump capability are the tactical identity — the weapons load has never been the point.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty tons. The speed and jump combination at this weight is the machine's primary capability. The weapons are self-defence tools rather than the reason to put this machine in the field. Standard engine means side torso hits are survivable. The ASN-30 uses a 280-rated light engine carrying an ER medium laser and an LB 5-X autocannon. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The light engine provides better side torso survivability than XL variants. The LB 5-X cluster option adds versatility. One ton of LB ammunition is limited.
variants.deployment: The 30 received a poor reception because it tried to make the Assassin into a direct combatant rather than a scout. The light engine is a genuine improvement over XL variants for survivability. The ER medium and LB 5-X are adequate but the chassis was not designed for sustained engagement. Units that understood the 30's limits as a mobile harasser with better survivability got reasonable results.

variants.name: 'Servitor'

variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty tons. The speed and jump combination at this weight is the machine's primary capability. The weapons are self-defence tools rather than the reason to put this machine in the field. Standard engine means side torso hits are survivable. The Servitor uses a 280-rated XL engine and carries a medium X-pulse laser, two small X-pulse lasers, two SRM-2s, and a small laser, with a vibroblade arm for close combat. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The vibroblade adds physical attack capability. The XL engine vulnerability applies.
variants.deployment: The Servitor is a melee-focused Assassin variant. The vibroblade arm deals physical damage that energy weapons cannot match at point-blank range. The X-pulse lasers are accurate against moving targets. The SRM-2s add missile volume. This is an arena-influenced configuration — the melee capability is most useful in close-quarter environments where the Assassin's speed delivers it to range.

variants.name: ASN-30 (Alice)
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Assassin in 2676 as a forty-ton light hunter and harassment platform. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 280-rated engine. Speed and jump capability are the tactical identity — the weapons load has never been the point.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty tons. The speed and jump combination at this weight is the machine's primary capability. The weapons are self-defence tools rather than the reason to put this machine in the field. Standard engine means side torso hits are survivable. The ASN-30 Alice is a custom configuration on the light engine with four ER medium lasers and ferro-fibrous armour. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. All-energy with no ammunition dependency. Four ER mediums at forty tons is aggressive energy output. Heat cycling is required under sustained fire.
variants.deployment: The Alice configuration trades the standard mixed weapons for pure energy firepower. Four ER mediums at forty tons threaten opponents above this weight class. The ferro-fibrous armour improves protection over the standard Assassin. The light engine survivability and no ammunition dependency suit independent operations. Heat management is the pilot's discipline.

The ASN-99 uses a 280-rated XL engine with stealth armour and a Guardian ECM suite, carrying a light PPC, two SRM-2s, and a TAG system. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active. The Guardian ECM disrupts targeting. TAG designates for guided munitions.
variants.deployment: The 99 is a stealth designation variant. The ECM and stealth armour together make it genuinely difficult to target during approach. The TAG designation adds force multiplier value in formations with artillery or aerospace support. The light PPC and SRM-2s provide direct combat capability. Heat management with stealth active requires awareness of the combined load.

variants.name: ASN-109
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Assassin in 2676 as a forty-ton light hunter and harassment platform. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 280-rated engine. Speed and jump capability are the tactical identity — the weapons load has never been the point.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty tons. The speed and jump combination at this weight is the machine's primary capability. The weapons are self-defence tools rather than the reason to put this machine in the field. Standard engine means side torso hits are survivable. The ASN-109 uses a 280-rated XL engine carrying a light PPC, an MML-5, and an improved one-shot SRM-2. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The improved one-shot SRM-2 is typically loaded with specialty warheads. The MML-5 provides SRM/LRM flexibility. The light PPC handles direct engagement.
variants.deployment: The 109 is a classic harasser configuration. The one-shot SRM-2 specialty warhead provides a single special-purpose strike capability — smoke, inferno, or mine rounds depending on the mission. The MML-5 covers standard missile needs. The light PPC snipes at range. The XL engine vulnerability is the standing concern.

variants.name: AS7-D
variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Atlas in 2755 as the Inner Sphere's definitive assault BattleMech, and the design has held that reputation for three centuries. A hundred tons, walk three, run four. Nineteen-plus tons of armour. When I work on an Atlas I am always aware that this machine is meant to end battles, not survive them by running away.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at a hundred tons. The standard engine survivability is fundamental to the design identity — this machine absorbs punishment that kills other assaults. The weapons loadout varies across variants but the core philosophy is consistent: close range, overwhelming fire, nothing escapes. Ammunition management across the heavy weapons systems is the consistent operational planning task. The AS7-D is the original production model: AC/20, LRM-20, SRM-6, and four medium lasers. Walk three, run four. The Defiance AC/20 is the centrepiece. The LRM-20 handles approach fire. The SRM-6 and medium lasers close the engagement. Nineteen tons of armour makes this machine absorb punishment that destroys lighter assaults.
variants.deployment: The D is the Atlas that defined the design's battlefield identity. Every commander who fields an Atlas for the first time sees a D. The AC/20 at close range ends most engagements decisively. The standard engine survivability means this machine holds the line under fire. Parts availability across the Inner Sphere is excellent after three centuries of production.

variants.name: AS7-D-DC
variants.overview: The Atlas needs no introduction. General Mechanics built the first one in 2755 and every variant since has carried the same premise: maximum armour, maximum firepower, walk forward until the enemy stops. The AS7-D-DC is the command console variant of the standard D, swapping one ton of LRM ammunition for a command console that lets a senior officer coordinate the battle from behind the skull-faced faceplate of the Inner Sphere's most recognisable assault 'Mech.
variants.capabilities: The standard D loadout is still here: AC/20, LRM-20, SRM-6, and two medium lasers. The AC/20 is the Defiance Mech Hunter and it is as brutal as the name suggests. Twenty heat sinks run hot when you fire everything at once, which is a conversation I have had with more than one Atlas pilot who thought the heat scale was a suggestion. The command console means two people in the cockpit, which changes the weight distribution slightly and requires recalibrating the gyro.
variants.deployment: This variant exists for senior officers who want to lead from the front and have the battlefield awareness to do it effectively. The command console gives real-time lance coordination capability that a standard cockpit cannot match. The tradeoff is one ton less LRM ammunition, which matters on long engagements. It is not a subtle machine and it was never meant to be.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Atlas in 2755 as the Inner Sphere's definitive assault BattleMech, and the design has held that reputation for three centuries. A hundred tons, walk three, run four. Nineteen-plus tons of armour. When I work on an Atlas I am always aware that this machine is meant to end battles, not survive them by running away.

The weapons loadout varies across variants but the core philosophy is consistent: close range, overwhelming fire, nothing escapes. Ammunition management across the heavy weapons systems is the consistent operational planning task. The Atlas C is a Clan-specification rebuild. Ultra AC/20 replaces the standard AC/20, Streak SRM-6 replaces the standard SRM-6, medium lasers remain. Clan fusion engine. The Ultra AC/20 in double-tap mode at close range is more devastating than the standard version. Streak SRM-6 fires only on lock, conserving ammunition.
variants.deployment: The C variant was configured for Clan second-line units operating captured or salvaged Atlas machines. The Clan weapons upgrades improve the fundamental AC/20 and SRM concept significantly. Clan engine maintenance alongside IS chassis procedures requires a two-track technical approach.

Ammunition management across the heavy weapons systems is the consistent operational planning task. The C 2 uses a Clan engine and carries an LB 20-X, an ER PPC, two ER large lasers, a Streak SRM-6, and two medium pulse lasers. The weapons coverage spans extreme long range through to close assault. The LB 20-X cluster and slug options add tactical flexibility the standard AC/20 lacks.
variants.deployment: The C 2 is the most weapons-diverse Clan Atlas configuration. The ER PPC and ER large lasers handle range work; the LB 20-X takes over at medium-close range; the Streak SRM-6 and pulse lasers close the engagement. Clan engine maintenance requirements apply. The weapons breadth makes this variant useful across more tactical scenarios than the standard C.

variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Atlas in 2755 as the Inner Sphere's definitive assault BattleMech, and the design has held that reputation for three centuries. A hundred tons, walk three, run four. Nineteen-plus tons of armour. When I work on an Atlas I am always aware that this machine is meant to end battles, not survive them by running away.

Ammunition management across the heavy weapons systems is the consistent operational planning task. The C 3 uses a Clan engine and carries an Arrow IV artillery launcher, a Gauss rifle, and two ER large lasers. variants.deployment: The K2 is the fast Atlas. Walk four on a hundred-ton machine is a genuine tactical surprise. The Gauss and ER large laser combination handles range work during the approach. The Streak SRM-6s close the engagement. The XL engine means this machine cannot absorb the punishment the standard-engine variants survive. Pilots who close range fast and keep moving get the most from it.

variants.name: AS7-K2 (Jedra)
variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Atlas in 2755 as the Inner Sphere's definitive assault BattleMech. A hundred tons, walk three, run four. Nineteen-plus tons of armour. The design is meant to end battles, not survive them by running away.

The Jedra is a named configuration on the K2's 400-rated XL engine, carrying two light Gauss rifles, five ER medium lasers, and two SRM-4s. Walk four, run six. Five ER medium lasers at close range is dense energy fire for a hundred-ton machine. The light Gauss rifles are more ammunition-efficient than standard Gauss at reduced range.
variants.deployment: The Jedra is a close-range specialist. The light Gauss rifles and ER medium volume together create a close-range fire density that opponents struggle to absorb. Walk four delivers this suite faster than standard Atlas variants. The XL engine vulnerability means the pilot uses the speed offensively rather than relying on armour absorption.

variants.name: AS7-K3
variants.overview: The Atlas needs no introduction. General Mechanics built the first one in 2755 and every variant since has carried the same premise: maximum armour, maximum firepower, walk forward until the enemy stops. The K3 is a late-era variant built around a 400-rated XL engine, which pushes an Atlas to walk four, run six, with three jump jets added on top. The first time I saw the spec sheet I read it twice.
variants.capabilities: A Gauss rifle, two ER large lasers, and a Streak SRM-4. The XL engine and jump jets together represent a significant departure from Atlas design philosophy, trading the bulletproof standard engine for speed and mobility. The Gauss rifle is accurate and hits hard but requires careful ammunition management. The ER large lasers provide sustained fire after the Gauss rounds are spent. What the K3 loses is the Atlas's traditional ability to take a side torso hit and keep going: the XL engine changes that equation entirely.
variants.deployment: This variant suits aggressive commanders who want an assault 'Mech that can reposition and threaten from unexpected angles. The jump capability lets it crest terrain features that ground-bound assaults cannot reach. The tradeoff is that it rewards skilled pilots who understand the XL vulnerability and punishes those who treat it like a standard Atlas. I have seen both outcomes and the difference is stark.

The Rotary AC/5 delivers sustained ballistic harassment. The SRM-6s close the engagement.
variants.deployment: The K4 is a speed-and-firepower variant that uses walk four to close range under ER PPC fire, then delivers Rotary AC/5 and SRM-6 volume at close quarters. The thick ferro-fibrous armour helps absorb return fire during the approach. XL engine side torso vulnerability is the standing concern.

The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active. The ER PPCs provide primary long-range fire. The X-pulse lasers are accurate against moving targets. Standard engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The S4 is the stealth Atlas. The stealth armour makes it difficult to target during approach — which matters for a walk-three machine that cannot close range quickly. The ER PPCs and Gauss handle long-range engagement under cover. Heat management with stealth active and energy weapons firing requires understanding the combined thermal load.

The ballistic-reinforced armour is a genuine functional improvement against the ballistic weapons that are most common at the assault weight class. The heavy-duty gyro makes gyro crits less likely to end the engagement immediately. The weapons loadout covers all ranges. XL engine is the tradeoff.

variants.name: AS7-D-H
variants.overview: The Atlas II AS7-D-H is a 100-ton assault 'Mech developed for the Royal BattleMech regiments in the late 27th century. It's a refined version of the original AS7-D, with a focus on firepower, protection, and psychological impact. The extreme rarity of this design has made it highly sought after across the Inner Sphere and Clan space.
variants.capabilities: The Atlas II retains its predecessor's missile armament, but swaps out the heavy autocannon for an LB 10-X autocannon. It also gains extended-range large lasers on the left forearm. While it still packs a punch, the trade-off is that it lacks the devastating close-range stopping power of the original AC/20. The ferro-fibrous armor and advanced systems make spare parts difficult to source, leading to maintenance headaches in the field.
variants.deployment: This variant is best deployed as a heavy hitter or anchor 'Mech, using its firepower to soften up enemy formations before closing in. The extended-range lasers are particularly effective against armor-heavy opponents. Be aware that the ferro-fibrous armor can be prone to damage from high-velocity rounds, so prioritize defense and use cover when possible.

This results in devastating alpha strikes at extreme range, though the reduced number of weapons leaves it more vulnerable if individual systems are damaged.

variants.name: AS7-D-HT
variants.overview: The Atlas II AS7-D-H is a 100-ton assault 'Mech developed for the Royal BattleMech regiments in the late 27th century. It's a refined version of the original AS7-D, with a focus on firepower, protection, and psychological impact. The extreme rarity of this design has made it highly sought after across the Inner Sphere and Clan space.
variants.capabilities: The Atlas II retains its predecessor's missile armament, but swaps out the heavy autocannon for an LB 10-X autocannon. It also gains extended-range large lasers on the left forearm. While it still packs a punch, the trade-off is that it lacks the devastating close-range stopping power of the original AC/20. The ferro-fibrous armor and advanced systems make spare parts difficult to source, leading to maintenance headaches in the field.
variants.deployment: This variant is known for its mammoth AC/20 replacing the LB 10-X autocannon, giving it devastating short-range firepower reminiscent of the original AS7-D Atlas. The weapon placement closely resembles standard Atlas models, suggesting the modification aimed to combine the Atlas II's superior electronics and ferro-fibrous armor with the proven close-combat punch of the original design.

An ECM suite and active probe rounded out the electronics package, giving the ilKhan exceptional battlefield awareness.

The XL engine freed tonnage for an MML-9 with Artemis IV fire control, CASE II ammunition protection, an Angel ECM suite, and an anti-missile system. Its distinctive black-and-white skeletal color scheme makes it easily recognizable on the battlefield.

The Inner Sphere CASE II protecting the side torsos provides additional protection. This combination of weapons makes it a formidable opponent on the battlefield. However, be aware that the faster Vlar 400 XL engine can make the 'Mech more prone to overheating in prolonged combat scenarios.

variants.name: AS7-D2
variants.overview: The Atlas III is a late-era development of the classic design, built around Clan-specification components on the classic Atlas airframe. Walk three, run four on the standard engine. The targeting computer and advanced electronics are the defining additions over the standard Atlas family.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at a hundred tons. The standard engine provides the same survivability as the original Atlas line. Clan-specification components require mixed maintenance procedures — the chassis is IS construction, the weapons and sensors are Clan. Targeting computer maintenance and calibration is an additional overhead the standard Atlas line does not have. The AS7-D2 carries a HAG/30, a Streak LRM-20, a Streak SRM-6, and two medium X-pulse lasers, with a targeting computer linking all weapons. Walk three, run four. The HAG/30 spread pattern is devastating at medium range. The Streak launchers guarantee missile hits when locked. The targeting computer improves accuracy across the suite.
variants.deployment: The D2 is the targeting computer HAG Atlas. The HAG/30 at medium range with targeting computer assistance is a primary weapons combination that most opponents cannot absorb efficiently. The Streak LRM-20 and SRM-6 add missile capability at range and close quarters respectively. Advanced Clan components require mixed maintenance procedures.

variants.name: AS7-D3
variants.overview: The Atlas III is a late-era development of the classic design, built around Clan-specification components on the classic Atlas airframe. Walk three, run four on the standard engine. The targeting computer and advanced electronics are the defining additions over the standard Atlas family.

The AS7-D3 carries a Rotary AC/2, a Streak LRM-20, a Streak SRM-6, and four medium X-pulse lasers, with a targeting computer. Walk three, run four. Four medium X-pulse lasers with a targeting computer is accurate and punishing at close range. The Streak launchers guarantee missile hits. The Rotary AC/2 provides sustained long-range harassment.
variants.deployment: The D3 is rare — production numbers stay low because of its dependence on Clan-specification components. Senior commanders requesting it accept the extended procurement timeline. The targeting computer and Streak launcher combination rewards careful fire management. The medium X-pulse laser volume at close range makes this dangerous in urban terrain.

variants.name: AVL-1O
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Avalanche in 3060 as a fifty-ton OmniMech on a Luthien Class M endo steel chassis. Walk five, run seven, jump five from the fixed jets. Standard engine — side torso survivability is preserved across all configurations. The name comes from the white smoke trails of the primary configuration's LRM salvoes.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at fifty tons. Standard engine means side torso hits are survivable. Fixed jump jets across all configurations are the consistent tactical tool. CASE-protected ammunition bays appear across most configurations. Endo steel structure throughout. The primary configuration AVL-1O carries twin LRM-10s in the side torsos and four ER medium lasers across both arms. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The LRM-10s produce the white smoke clouds that gave the design its name. The ER mediums provide direct fire backup. Two tons of LRM ammunition in CASE-protected bays.
variants.deployment: The primary configuration does exactly what the name implies — drops missile fire on targets at range and uses the ER mediums as backup. Two tons of LRM ammunition is not generous for sustained fire support operations. The standard engine and CASE protection keep it operational under return fire that would kill XL competitors.

variants.name: AVL-1OA
variants.overview: The Avalanche is a fifty-ton OmniMech built by Luthien Armor Works on a Luthien Class M endo steel chassis with a 250-rated standard engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five from the Icarus Standard jets. It was designed to be cheap enough for widespread production without sacrificing the flexibility of OmniMech pod systems, and that philosophy shows in every aspect of the design.
variants.capabilities: The A configuration replaces the LRM launchers with paired SRM-6s in the side torsos and SRM-4s mounted in additional hardpoints, backed by the same four ER medium lasers from the primary config. This turns a fire support machine into a short-range brawler. The jump jets become much more important in this configuration because getting into SRM range quickly is the whole point. Heat builds up fast when the SRMs and ER mediums fire together.
variants.deployment: The A configuration suits pilots who want to use the jump capability aggressively, closing range fast and delivering high-volume short-range fire before the opponent can respond. The staggered SRM sizes give some flexibility in targeting across different profiles. Two tons of ammunition total across both SRM types means this variant is not built for extended engagements.

variants.name: AVL-1OB
variants.overview: The Avalanche is a fifty-ton OmniMech built by Luthien Armor Works on a Luthien Class M endo steel chassis with a 250-rated standard engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five from the Icarus Standard jets. It was designed to be cheap enough for widespread production without sacrificing the flexibility of OmniMech pod systems, and that philosophy shows in every aspect of the design.
variants.capabilities: The B configuration pairs a light PPC and ER medium laser in each arm, keeping the energy fire completely ammo-independent, and adds a Thunderbolt-5 launcher in each side torso for guided missile punch. The light PPCs are accurate and consistent across the engagement range where the Avalanche typically fights. The Thunderbolt launchers add meaningful damage output but two tons of ammunition limits sustained operations.
variants.deployment: The B configuration is the longest-range variant in the Avalanche family, using the light PPC reach to engage before slower opponents can respond. The jump jets let it claim terrain features for better firing angles. When the Thunderbolt ammunition runs out the energy weapons carry the fight without any degradation in capability, which makes this a reliable option for operations where resupply is uncertain.

variants.name: AVL-1OC
variants.overview: The Avalanche is a fifty-ton OmniMech built by Luthien Armor Works on a Luthien Class M endo steel chassis with a 250-rated standard engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five from the Icarus Standard jets. It was designed to be cheap enough for widespread production without sacrificing the flexibility of OmniMech pod systems, and that philosophy shows in every aspect of the design.
variants.capabilities: The C configuration mounts a light AC/5 and ER medium laser in each arm, adding small X-pulse lasers in the side torsos for close-range deterrence. The light autocannons are efficient on ammunition and accurate at medium range. The X-pulse lasers are specifically there to discourage lighter machines from closing, and they do that job adequately. Heat is manageable across this loadout.
variants.deployment: The C configuration is the garrison variant. The light AC/5s are economical to operate over long periods and the mixed loadout handles most threat types a garrison unit encounters. It works in patrol and rear-area security roles where you need something that can sustain independent operations without constant resupply runs. Not glamorous work but the C configuration does it reliably.

variants.name: AVL-1ON
variants.overview: The Avalanche is a fifty-ton OmniMech built by Luthien Armor Works on a Luthien Class M endo steel chassis with a 250-rated standard engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five from the Icarus Standard jets. It was designed to be cheap enough for widespread production without sacrificing the flexibility of OmniMech pod systems, and that philosophy shows in every aspect of the design.
variants.capabilities: The N configuration is an experimental variant built around a single Clan ER PPC linked to a targeting computer, with a light AC/5 providing secondary ballistic fire. The Clan PPC on an IS targeting computer integration caused persistent calibration problems throughout this configuration's testing life. The fundamental incompatibility between the Matabushi Stalker targeting system and the Clan weapon was never fully resolved.
variants.deployment: The N configuration was ultimately abandoned because of that targeting system conflict. The concept was sound: precise long-range energy fire from a mobile platform with autocannon backup. The execution proved more difficult than the engineers anticipated. You may encounter surviving examples in second-line or militia service where the targeting quirks have been partially worked around by experienced crews.

variants.name: AVL-1OR

variants.capabilities: The R configuration is a mixed-tech loadout, using Clan LRM-10 and paired ATM-3 launchers alongside Clan ER medium lasers. The ATM-3s offer three different ammunition types for tactical flexibility, which looks impressive on paper. The targeting system alignment issues that plagued mixed Clan and IS integration on this chassis appeared in the R configuration as well, reducing reliability below what the weapons themselves were capable of.
variants.deployment: The R configuration's Clan weapons require Clan-spec maintenance procedures alongside IS procedures for the chassis systems, which creates a two-track maintenance requirement that most field techs find frustrating. The ATM ammunition variety is genuinely useful if you can keep the targeting aligned. In practice, units that can source Clan tech support get reasonable performance from this variant. Those that cannot will have a bad time.

variants.name: AV1-O
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works developed the Avatar in 3055 using captured Mad Dog design data as the foundation for an IS heavy OmniMech. Seventy tons with thirty-four tons of pod space on the 280-rated XL engine. Walk four, run six. The Draconis Combine field it extensively as the backbone of C3 network lances.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at seventy tons on the XL engine. Side torso damage is fatal on all Avatar variants. Thirty-four tons of pod space is generous for a seventy-ton machine. The DCMS uses this platform for C3 network doctrine — multiple configurations include C3 master or slave units. Artemis IV fire control appears across several configurations. The Prime AV1-O carries an LB 10-X, two LRM-10s with Artemis IV, two medium pulse lasers, two standard medium lasers, and two machine guns. Walk four, run six. The Artemis IV LRM accuracy is the standout feature. The LB 10-X provides cluster and slug ballistic options. Machine guns handle infantry. XL engine vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The Prime is the standard deployment configuration. The Artemis IV LRM-10 accuracy combined with LB 10-X ballistic options covers most engagement scenarios a DCMS heavy faces. The machine guns handle infantry threats. The dual medium laser and pulse laser close-range suite provides adequate direct combat capability. XL engine is the consistent concern.

Configuration A carries an AC/20, an ER large laser, two SRM-6 launchers, and two medium lasers, with four jump jets. Walk four, run six, jump four. The AC/20 is the centrepiece close-range weapon. variants.name: AV1-OE
variants.overview: The Avatar is a seventy-ton OmniMech developed by Luthien Armor Works from captured Mad Dog designs, entering production in 3056. The 280-rated XL engine at seventy tons gives walk four, run six, which is modest for a heavy. What the Avatar trades for that modest speed is thirty-four tons of pod space, more than most competing designs at this weight. The StarSlab/4 armour and integrated CASE are solid foundations.
variants.capabilities: The OE configuration carries an ER PPC, an Ultra AC/10, an ER medium laser, and two standard medium lasers, with six extra double heat sinks added to manage the energy load. The Ultra AC/10 in double-tap mode is the best close-range tool this configuration has, hitting hard and fast. The ER PPC handles long range. The improved C3 computer and Guardian ECM suite make this a network warfare platform as much as a direct combatant, and that combination is what the OE was built for.
variants.deployment: This configuration was developed specifically for ComStar and Word of Blake units that needed C3 network coordination with ECM protection in a single chassis. The combat loadout is competent but the electronics are the point. Maintaining both the C3 and ECM systems to spec is more demanding than the weapons, and field techs who neglect the electronics calibration will find both systems degrading faster than the maintenance schedule suggests.

Jump four allows flanking approaches. The LB 20-X cluster option is useful against lighter opponents and aircraft. XL engine vulnerability makes the jump-and-close approach the intended tactic.

Heat management under sustained heavy PPC fire requires attention.

The C3 master computer enables lance-level coordination beneath the surface. Underwater maintenance requirements for the torpedo systems are distinct from the standard pod weapons and require specific technical certification.
variants.deployment: The OU sees deployment on worlds with significant bodies of water where conventional ground operations face terrain obstacles that aquatic movement avoids. The C3 master makes it a natural command element for underwater lance operations. If you are maintaining one of these, the torpedo tube seals require inspection after every subaquatic mission without exception. Salt water and depth pressure accelerate degradation in ways that standard field maintenance schedules do not account for.
