variants.name: AV1-OBLO
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works developed the Avatar in 3055 using captured Mad Dog design data as the foundation for an IS heavy OmniMech. Seventy tons with thirty-four tons of pod space on the 280-rated XL engine. Walk four, run six. The Draconis Combine field it extensively as the backbone of C3 network lances.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at seventy tons on the XL engine. Side torso damage is fatal on all Avatar variants. Thirty-four tons of pod space is generous for a seventy-ton machine. The DCMS uses this platform for C3 network doctrine — multiple configurations include C3 master or slave units. Artemis IV fire control appears across several configurations. Configuration BLO is a custom loadout for the Blessed Order's First Division, carrying an ER PPC, an LB 10-X, and two medium lasers, with jump four. Walk four, run six, jump four. The Blessed Order improved several components over the standard Configuration F that it resembles. The ER PPC and LB 10-X combination covers long and close range.
variants.deployment: Configuration BLO was developed for a specific formation within the Blessed Order. The jump capability closes distance from unexpected angles. The ER PPC fires during the approach; the LB 10-X handles closer work. Maintenance requires the specific configuration documentation from the Blessed Order rather than standard Avatar procedures.

variants.name: AWS-8Q
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: Three PPCs, twenty-eight heat sinks, and a small laser in the head for anything reckless enough to charge in close. The Kreuss PPCs run hot when you fire all three at once, which pilots do anyway, and the heat curve is the defining maintenance and tactical concern on every Awesome variant I have worked on. The armour is excellent. The battlefist on the left arm has ended more close-range encounters than you would expect on a 'Mech that is supposed to stay at range.
variants.deployment: This is the production standard and the most common variant you will encounter. Garrison commands love it for the ammunition independence. It pairs well with lighter direct-fire 'Mechs that can handle anything that closes inside the PPC minimum range. The heat management is the only real discipline required from the pilot.

variants.name: AWS-8R
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: The 8R swaps two of the three PPCs for LRM-15 launchers and replaces the third with a large laser, keeping the small laser in the head. The heat profile drops considerably compared to the 8Q. The LRM-15s extend the engagement range and provide indirect fire capability the standard variant lacks. Ammunition management becomes the primary concern, where on the 8Q it was heat.
variants.deployment: The 8R suits commanders who want indirect fire capability alongside direct fire without stepping into a dedicated missile boat. The large laser provides consistent output when the LRM ammunition runs low. Two tons of LRM ammunition is the critical limitation on sustained engagements. The battlefist remains on the left arm for close work. This variant sees frequent use in mixed lances where the indirect fire fills a gap left by other chassis.

variants.name: AWS-8T
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: The 8T keeps both LRM-15s from the 8R and adds a second large laser in the left arm where the 8R had only one. The result is better sustained energy fire once missiles are expended and a more aggressive heat load when firing everything. The twin large lasers and twin LRMs is a genuinely capable mid-range combination. The standard engine runs cooler under heavy fire than an XL variant would and the chassis is correspondingly more forgiving of damage.
variants.deployment: The 8T is considered an improvement over the 8R by most pilots who have run both because the second large laser removes the feeling of being unarmed once the LRMs are dry. It deploys in the same roles as the 8R but performs better in engagements that run long. Parts commonality with the 8R makes supporting both variants in the same unit straightforward.

variants.name: AWS-8V
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: The 8V is a light variant carrying one PPC, one large laser, one LRM-15, and a small laser. It is the least armed Awesome configuration and the one I see pressed into service most often when a command needs an assault frame quickly and does not have a better option available. The heat load is genuinely manageable. The armour and the chassis are full standard Awesome, which means it can absorb punishment that would destroy a lighter design.
variants.deployment: The 8V works as a second-line support platform or command vehicle. It is not going to win a one-on-one fight against an 8Q but it will hold a position and provide fire support reliably while more capable assets handle the heavy work. I have seen it used as a lance anchor in garrison units that cannot get allocation for better-armed variants.

variants.name: AWS-9M
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: The 9M goes to a 320-rated XL engine, pushing the Awesome to walk four, run six, which feels strange the first time you see an eighty-ton machine move that fast. Three ER PPCs replace the standard Kreuss weapons. A medium pulse laser and small pulse laser handle close defence. Twin Streak SRM-2s provide reliable short-range fire that does not miss. The XL engine changes the damage profile entirely: a side torso breach kills this machine where the standard engine would not.
variants.deployment: The 9M is the mobile Awesome, designed for commanders who need assault firepower but cannot afford to be static. The ER PPC range combined with the increased speed creates a platform that can dictate engagement distance effectively. The pulse lasers and Streaks handle close-range threats that the ER PPCs cannot engage efficiently. The XL vulnerability requires a different tactical mindset than the standard Awesome chassis.

variants.name: AWS-9Ma
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: The 9Ma is a command variant built on the 9M chassis. Three ER PPCs remain, with a small laser replacing the pulse weapons, and twenty double heat sinks keeping the thermal load under control. The weight saved by the simplified weapons package goes into a Guardian ECM suite, a command console, and two tons of advanced communications equipment. This is a platform built for the officer who needs to fight and command simultaneously.
variants.deployment: The 9Ma deploys with command elements that need both ECM protection and direct combat capability in the same hull. The command console allows real-time coordination while the three ER PPCs ensure the machine is not a safe target just because it is acting as the command post. The ECM suite complicates targeting for enemy units attempting to range the command element.

variants.name: AWS-9Q
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: The 9Q adds a fourth PPC and a Guardian ECM suite, dropping two heat sinks from the 8Q total to nineteen to make room. Four PPCs. The heat management on this variant is not for the faint-hearted. Firing all four simultaneously will shut the machine down faster than most pilots expect the first time they try it. The ECM suite adds real utility in networked combat environments. This variant saw action during Operation Guerrero and the fourth PPC proved its worth there.
variants.deployment: The 9Q is an aggressive upgrade for commanders who think three PPCs is not enough. The fourth PPC increases alpha strike damage substantially at the cost of heat discipline becoming non-negotiable. The Guardian ECM adds protection value in engagements where enemy C3 networks are a factor. Pilots who understand heat management treat this as the definitive Awesome variant.

variants.name: AWS-10KM
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: The 10KM is a 3067-vintage variant built around a 240-rated compact engine and two heavy PPCs with a snub-nose PPC for close range. The compact engine concentrates mass and changes the internal layout substantially. Heavy PPCs at eighty tons hit hard but run very hot, and the snub-nose adds close-range punch that the standard Awesome family historically lacked. This is an IBMU and Alshain Weaponry joint production, which shows in the parts standardisation choices.
variants.deployment: The 10KM tends to overheat during prolonged engagements if the pilot fires all three weapons continuously. Heat management is more demanding here than on the standard Awesome because the heavy PPCs generate more waste heat per shot than the Kreuss weapons. Elite units that can source parts from both IBMU and Alshain maintain these without too much difficulty. Second-line units with one supply chain find them harder to keep in the field.

variants.name: AWS-9Q (Klatt)
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: The Klatt variant is a field conversion of the 9Q, swapping the Guardian ECM for a C3 slave unit and replacing the small laser with a small pulse laser. Four PPCs and a C3 slave means this machine shares targeting data with networked lancemates, letting lighter scouts feed it firing solutions at extreme range. The small pulse laser is a marginal improvement over the standard small laser for close defence.
variants.deployment: This is the Crescent Hawks' preferred configuration, built around the premise that four PPCs guided by C3 network data is more devastating than four PPCs firing independently. The C3 slave requires a functioning network to deliver its benefit, which means this variant underperforms as a standalone unit. Paired with fast C3 scouts it performs exactly as designed. The conversion is straightforward and any unit with access to a C3 slave unit and the original 9Q platform can perform it in the field.

variants.name: AWS-10KM (Cameron)
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: The Cameron variant is a named pilot machine, not a production configuration. It mounts two ER PPCs and a snub-nose PPC, with a targeting computer, improved C3, and armoured gyro, cockpit, and engine components. The armoured internals add meaningful protection to the critical systems but also add weight that squeezes the weapons loadout. The Clan-IS mixed tech requires two maintenance tracks on the same machine.
variants.deployment: This is a command platform built for a specific officer's preferences. The improved C3 enables network coordination and the armoured components make the machine harder to kill through critical hits. The snub-nose PPC fills the standard Awesome gap at close range. Maintaining the armoured components to spec requires additional hours per inspection cycle compared to a standard chassis.

variants.name: AWS-8Q (Buck)
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: Buck Tripp's personal machine is a field conversion built for speed above everything else. A 400-rated XL engine and XL gyro push an eighty-ton Awesome to walk five, run seven. The three standard PPCs stay but the heat sink count drops to sixteen upgraded doubles. Twelve heat sinks gone for the engine and gyro swap. Ferro-fibrous replaces the standard armour. The small laser is gone entirely.
variants.deployment: This is not a machine you maintain to a production spec because there is no production spec. It is a one-off conversion and every component choice reflects what one commander wanted from his personal ride. The XL engine and gyro mean side torso or gyro hits are catastrophic in ways a standard Awesome tolerates. Fast, aggressive, and fragile by assault standards.

variants.name: AWS-11M
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: Eight light PPCs. I have worked on exactly one of these and that was enough. The concept is volume of fire, with eight individual weapon systems all needing independent calibration and maintenance cycles. The Clan fusion engine provides the mass savings that make eight weapons possible on this frame. The compact gyro is the weak point: it frees up space but takes a harder hit from gyro crits than a standard unit.
variants.deployment: The 11M is a Dark Age production variant from the Scorpion Empire. Walk three, run four, eight light PPCs. The thermal load across all eight is substantial despite the Clan heat sinks. Field techs maintaining this variant quickly learn to track each PPC's calibration independently because they drift at different rates under heavy fire cycling.

variants.name: AWS-11R
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: The 11R is a 3133-era design built around stealth armour and an Extended LRM-15, which is an unusual combination. The stealth armour requires the Guardian ECM to function and doubles the heat load while active. The ELRM-15 reaches out to extreme range but requires the ECM to be running, which means the stealth armour heat penalty is always present when the missiles are in use. A light Gauss rifle and ER medium laser round out the armament. The supercharger enables short bursts of higher speed.
variants.deployment: The 11R is a long-range ambush platform. The stealth armour makes it hard to detect at range, the ELRM hits targets that cannot reply, and the supercharger provides emergency repositioning speed. Three tons of ELRM ammunition stored in a compact gyro-freed bay is the endurance limit. The coolant pod is a one-use emergency tool, not a regular thermal management option.

variants.name: AWS-11V
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: The 11V carries an ER PPC, a light Gauss rifle, an Extended LRM-15, and an ER medium laser, with an Angel ECM suite for electronic warfare protection. The combination covers three distinct range bands. The Angel ECM is the most sophisticated electronic warfare system I have worked with on an Awesome chassis and it requires specialist calibration that field techs without specific training should not attempt.
variants.deployment: The 11V is a direct-fire and indirect-fire hybrid with ECM protection. It does not do any single role as well as a dedicated platform but it handles three roles adequately from one chassis. The Angel ECM makes enemy targeting less reliable across the entire engagement area, which has value beyond the machine's own survivability. The ER PPC and light Gauss provide the punch, the ELRM extends reach.

variants.name: AWS-11H
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: Three heavy PPCs and an ER small laser, with twenty-three Clan double heat sinks on a standard engine. The heavy PPCs hit harder per shot than the standard Kreuss weapons but generate more heat and have a minimum range limitation. The Clan heat sinks on an IS chassis require careful integration during production and replacement parts sourcing is a persistent headache in the field.
variants.deployment: The 11H is built for sustained heavy fire at range. The Clan endo steel structure and Clan heat sinks combined with IS weapons and engine is a mixed-tech maintenance challenge. Any unit running these needs techs comfortable with Clan component standards. The heavy PPC damage output at range is the payoff. Walk three, run four, twenty-three Clan doubles managing the thermal load from three heavy PPCs firing on cycle.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: I have kept Awesomes running for fifteen years across two different regiments and my honest assessment is that they are exactly what they were designed to be: eighty tons of armour and PPCs that walk three and shoot things very far away. General Mechanics built the AWS-8Q in 2665 around three Kreuss PPCs and twenty-eight single heat sinks, and the formula proved so effective that the basic chassis ran with minimal changes for centuries.
variants.capabilities: The C variant is a Scorpion Empire production model built in 3143 using mostly Clan technology on an endo-composite structure. Four Clan ER PPCs on eighty tons. The endo-composite frees the mass that would otherwise be impossible to fit four ER PPCs with adequate heat management. Walk three, run four. The Clan fusion engine provides the efficiency to make this loadout viable.
variants.deployment: Four ER PPCs is the Awesome concept taken to its logical extreme. The Scorpion Empire produced this for assault formations that needed maximum standoff firepower from a single chassis. The heat load is severe even with Clan heat sinks. Pilots who respect the heat curve can sustain continuous fire on a rotation. Those who alpha strike repeatedly will shut down. The endo-composite structure requires manufacturing tolerances that limit repair options in the field.

variants.name: AXM-1N
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Axman in 3028 around a five-ton hatchet as the primary weapon — a deliberate return to physical combat at a time when BattleMech designers had largely abandoned it. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four on the 260-rated XL engine. The hatchet deals physical damage that weapons fire cannot replicate in the same way.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. The hatchet is not an afterthought — it deals five tons of physical damage per hit that bypasses conventional weapons calculations. The XL engine adds the standard vulnerability. Jump four is genuinely useful for closing distance to hatchet range. The AXM-1N is the original production model: AC/20, large pulse laser, three medium lasers, and the five-ton hatchet. Walk four, run six, jump four. The AC/20 at close range and the hatchet together are the design concept. The large pulse laser handles medium range. The medium lasers fill the close-range energy role.
variants.deployment: The 1N is built for urban combat and any terrain where jump capability delivers the hatchet to point-blank range. The five-ton hatchet combined with the AC/20 at close range is what opponents fear from this machine. The large pulse laser and medium lasers handle anything before the machine closes. XL engine vulnerability is the standard concern.

variants.name: AXM-2N
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Axman in 3028 around a five-ton hatchet as the primary weapon — a deliberate return to physical combat at a time when BattleMech designers had largely abandoned it. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four on the 260-rated XL engine. The hatchet deals physical damage that weapons fire cannot replicate in the same way.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. The hatchet is not an afterthought — it deals five tons of physical damage per hit that bypasses conventional weapons calculations. The XL engine adds the standard vulnerability. Jump four is genuinely useful for closing distance to hatchet range. The AXM-2N replaces the AC/20 with twin LRM-15 launchers, keeping the large pulse laser, three medium lasers, and the hatchet. Walk four, run six, jump four. The LRM-15s add long-range fire support capability that the original lacked. The hatchet remains for close combat.
variants.deployment: The 2N fundamentally changes the Axman's role during the Clan Invasion era. Adding LRM-15s makes it a fire support and close combat hybrid. The hatchet provides the physical attack capability when the machine closes. The LRM launchers do the work at range. This is a more flexible platform than the 1N but less purely devastating at close quarters.

variants.name: AXM-3S
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Axman in 3028 around a five-ton hatchet as the primary weapon — a deliberate return to physical combat at a time when BattleMech designers had largely abandoned it. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four on the 260-rated XL engine. The hatchet deals physical damage that weapons fire cannot replicate in the same way.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. The hatchet is not an afterthought — it deals five tons of physical damage per hit that bypasses conventional weapons calculations. The XL engine adds the standard vulnerability. Jump four is genuinely useful for closing distance to hatchet range. The AXM-3S uses a 260-rated light engine for better side torso survivability and carries an LB 20-X and three ER medium lasers. Walk four, run six, jump four. Light engine — side torso hits are survivable. The LB 20-X replaces the standard AC/20 with cluster and slug options. The hatchet remains.
variants.deployment: The 3S improves survivability over the XL-equipped 1N at the cost of some internal space. The light engine taking a side torso hit that would kill the 1N is the primary improvement. The LB 20-X cluster option adds close-range flexibility the standard AC/20 lacks. The hatchet is unchanged.

variants.name: AXM-3Sr
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Axman in 3028 around a five-ton hatchet as the primary weapon — a deliberate return to physical combat at a time when BattleMech designers had largely abandoned it. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four on the 260-rated XL engine. The hatchet deals physical damage that weapons fire cannot replicate in the same way.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. The hatchet is not an afterthought — it deals five tons of physical damage per hit that bypasses conventional weapons calculations. The XL engine adds the standard vulnerability. Jump four is genuinely useful for closing distance to hatchet range. The AXM-3Sr uses the light engine and carries a Rotary AC/5, three ER medium lasers, a medium pulse laser, and a C3 slave. Walk four, run six, jump four. The Rotary AC/5 delivers sustained ballistic fire at medium range. The C3 slave integrates targeting data. The hatchet remains for close combat.
variants.deployment: The 3Sr adds C3 network integration and sustained ballistic fire to the light engine survivability of the 3S. The Rotary AC/5 maintains pressure at range. The C3 slave improves fire solutions from network targeting data. The hatchet and ER mediums handle close engagement. A solid combined-arms platform for LCAF network lances.

variants.name: AXM-4D
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Axman in 3028 around a five-ton hatchet as the primary weapon — a deliberate return to physical combat at a time when BattleMech designers had largely abandoned it. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four on the 260-rated XL engine. The hatchet deals physical damage that weapons fire cannot replicate in the same way.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. The hatchet is not an afterthought — it deals five tons of physical damage per hit that bypasses conventional weapons calculations. The XL engine adds the standard vulnerability. Jump four is genuinely useful for closing distance to hatchet range. The AXM-4D uses the standard XL engine and carries four Light AC/5s and two medium lasers, with no jump capability. Walk four, run six. Four Light AC/5s replace the single AC/20 with higher rate of fire and ammunition efficiency at reduced close-range impact. The hatchet remains. No jump jets.
variants.deployment: The 4D is the Federated Suns production variant that sacrifices the jump capability and close-range devastation of the AC/20 for sustained Light AC/5 fire. The sustained rate of fire works at range in ways the single AC/20 did not. The loss of jump capability changes the tactical profile substantially — this is a medium-range fire support platform, not the original close-combat concept.

variants.name: AXM-6X
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Axman in 3028 around a five-ton hatchet as the primary weapon — a deliberate return to physical combat at a time when BattleMech designers had largely abandoned it. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four on the 260-rated XL engine. The hatchet deals physical damage that weapons fire cannot replicate in the same way.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. The hatchet is not an afterthought — it deals five tons of physical damage per hit that bypasses conventional weapons calculations. The XL engine adds the standard vulnerability. Jump four is genuinely useful for closing distance to hatchet range. The AXM-6X uses a 325-rated Clan XL engine for walk five, run seven. Four ER medium lasers and two Thunderbolt-15 launchers. Walk five on an Axman. The Clan engine requires Clan maintenance procedures on an IS chassis. The hatchet remains. No jump jets. The Thunderbolt-15 guided missiles hit with better accuracy than standard LRMs.
variants.deployment: The 6X is a technology demonstrator — six prototypes were built and the Clan component expense prevented full production. Walk five is the practical improvement over the standard Axman. The Thunderbolt-15s provide accurate heavy fire support. The Clan engine maintenance requirement is the operational constraint that kept this from wider deployment.

variants.name: AXM-6T
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Axman in 3028 around a five-ton hatchet as the primary weapon — a deliberate return to physical combat at a time when BattleMech designers had largely abandoned it. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four on the 260-rated XL engine. The hatchet deals physical damage that weapons fire cannot replicate in the same way.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. The hatchet is not an afterthought — it deals five tons of physical damage per hit that bypasses conventional weapons calculations. The XL engine adds the standard vulnerability. Jump four is genuinely useful for closing distance to hatchet range. The AXM-6T uses a standard 325-rated IS XL engine for walk five, run seven and carries the same weapons as the 6X: four ER medium lasers and two Thunderbolt-15 launchers. The IS engine removes the Clan maintenance complexity. Walk five. The hatchet remains. No jump jets.
variants.deployment: The 6T is the IS-engine production version of the 6X concept. LCAF regiments on key interior worlds including Tharkad, Donegal, Coventry, and Hesperus II field this variant. Walk five, Thunderbolt-15 accuracy, and ER medium energy fire makes it a capable heavy striker. The absence of jump jets changes how pilots close to hatchet range.

variants.name: AXM-5N
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Axman in 3028 around a five-ton hatchet as the primary weapon. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four on the 260-rated XL engine. The hatchet deals physical damage that weapons fire cannot replicate in the same way.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. The hatchet is not an afterthought — it deals substantial physical damage per hit. The XL engine adds the standard vulnerability. Jump four closes distance to hatchet range. The AXM-5N uses triple-strength myomer and carries an ER PPC, three ER medium lasers, and a HAG/20. Walk four, run six normally — but TSM activates at elevated heat, boosting ground speed and amplifying the hatchet's physical impact. The ER PPC and ER mediums generate the heat that triggers TSM. The HAG/20 adds ballistic spread damage alongside the energy suite.
variants.deployment: The 5N uses its own weapons heat as a tactical tool. The ER PPC and ER mediums heat the machine deliberately to trigger TSM, then deliver the enhanced hatchet strike. The HAG/20 adds ranged ballistic capability before closing. The XL engine means side torso hits are fatal. Pilots need to understand the TSM heat threshold and manage the activation deliberately.

variants.overview: The Baboon, called the Howler in IS circles, is a twenty-ton Clan light BattleMech with a non-OmniMech fixed configuration, created by Clan Fire Mandrill around 2871. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven from the standard fusion engine. It is ubiquitous in Clan second-line formations because it is cheap to produce and straightforward to maintain. The hyperextendable torso is the design's signature feature and the component that causes the most grief.
variants.capabilities: Configuration 4 carries a single LRM-5 with a ton of ammunition and jump jets for the full seven jump capability. That is a light weapons load for a light 'Mech and pilots know it. The torso serves regular inspection intervals. The hyperextension mechanism accumulates wear faster than the maintenance schedule implies and I have seen actuator failures in field conditions that the schedule would not have predicted.
variants.deployment: This is the jump-capable scout configuration, introduced by Clan Jade Falcon in 2877. The jump jets dominate the weight budget and the LRM-5 is almost a secondary concern. It works as a spotter and terrain scout, not a combatant. Warriors assigned to this configuration understand they are gathering intelligence, not winning Trials of combat.

variants.overview: The Baboon, called the Howler in IS circles, is a twenty-ton Clan light BattleMech with a non-OmniMech fixed configuration, created by Clan Fire Mandrill around 2871. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven from the standard fusion engine. It is ubiquitous in Clan second-line formations because it is cheap to produce and straightforward to maintain. The hyperextendable torso is the design's signature feature and the component that causes the most grief.
variants.capabilities: Configuration 5 mounts six ER medium lasers with no ammunition dependency at all. Six ER mediums on a twenty-ton frame is an aggressive heat load. The heat sinks cannot keep up if the warrior fires all six on repeated cycles. This configuration rewards fire discipline: two or three lasers per firing solution is sustainable, six simultaneously is not. The torso inspection interval still applies regardless of configuration.
variants.deployment: Configuration 5 sees use on extended operations where resupply is unavailable. No ammunition to manage, no logistics tail beyond the machine itself. The heat management requirement is the tradeoff. Warriors who understand their heat curve use this effectively. Those who fire all six lasers until shutdown do not last long in this configuration.

variants.capabilities: Configuration 2 uses a smaller 120-rated Clan XL engine and a MASC system, dropping sustained speed slightly but enabling burst acceleration to 130 kilometres per hour. The XL engine at twenty tons means any serious side torso damage ends the fight. Four ATM-3 launchers with two tons of ammunition provide the flexibility of three different munition types. The MASC system requires its own maintenance discipline: accelerated wear on the transmission components if used too aggressively.
variants.deployment: The ATM-3 loadout gives warriors genuine tactical choice in the field. Standard rounds for the general case, extended-range for standoff work, high-explosive for closing. Two tons of mixed ammunition requires careful loading discipline before an operation. The MASC burst speed is for repositioning and breaking contact, not sustained running. Use it for that purpose and the transmission holds. Use it as a routine speed boost and you will be replacing components.

variants.name: 3 'Devil'
variants.overview: The Baboon, called the Howler in IS circles, is a twenty-ton Clan light BattleMech with a non-OmniMech fixed configuration, created by Clan Fire Mandrill around 2871. The ER PPC is the only weapon and it hits well above what you expect from this weight class. The XL engine vulnerability applies and the single weapon means if it goes down the machine is combat-ineffective immediately.
variants.deployment: Production of this configuration began aboard the Eden Rose, a Potemkin-class WarShip at Dante, before moving to surface facilities around 3076. It is a dedicated sniper that uses MASC burst speed to reposition between shots. The concept works if the warrior understands they are a harasser, not a frontline combatant. One weapon, one chance at range, then move before the target can return fire effectively.

variants.capabilities: Configuration 6 mounts twin SRM-6 launchers in a shoulder turret that exploits the hyperextendable torso to engage across a wide arc. Two tons of ammunition in a CASE II-protected bay. The turret configuration is the most mechanically demanding aspect of maintenance on this variant. The turret drive and traverse mechanism wears faster than the torso actuators on other configurations.
variants.deployment: The SRM-6 turret makes this configuration a close-range brawler that can engage targets across angles most light 'Mechs cannot cover. Walk seven, run ten at twenty tons means it can dictate engagement range against heavier opponents. The CASE II protection on the ammunition bay is important because an SRM ammunition explosion at this tonnage is catastrophic. Keep the CASE II seals inspected.

variants.name: BKN-1K
variants.overview: The Bakeneko is a fifty-five ton mixed-tech medium built on the Phoenix Hawk 3K chassis using a Clan XL engine and experimental TurboProp jump jets. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The TurboProp jets provide enhanced aerial control during jump — the pilot can rotate and reorient during the jump arc in ways standard jets cannot match.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 330-rated Clan XL engine at fifty-five tons. The Clan XL adds side torso vulnerability. The TurboProp jump jets are experimental — they require maintenance procedures not covered in standard Phoenix Hawk technical manuals. The 1K carries a large pulse laser, a light PPC, two MML-3 launchers, and an ER medium laser. Mixed IS and Clan components create a two-track maintenance requirement throughout.
variants.deployment: The 1K was produced in large numbers before the Jihad destroyed most production capacity. The TurboProp jump capability is the tactical differentiator — the aerial reorientation during jump allows approach angles that standard jump-capable machines cannot manage. Techs new to this variant need specific TurboProp training before their first maintenance cycle.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Balius is a sixty-five ton Clan quadrupedal OmniMech hand-crafted by elite technicians for Bloodnamed warriors. Walk six, run nine on the 390-rated Clan XL engine. The quad configuration provides exceptional firing stability. Limited numbers are produced — this is not a line unit platform.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at sixty-five tons. The Clan XL carries the standard side torso vulnerability. The quad chassis provides a stable firing platform that bipedal designs cannot match under movement. Endo steel structure and ferro-fibrous armour. Hand-crafted quality means build consistency is very high but replacement parts require Clan sourcing. Configuration A carries a HAG/20, an ER large laser, three ER medium lasers, and a flamer. Walk six, run nine. The HAG/20 spreads ballistic projectiles across multiple armour locations at medium range. The ER large laser extends direct fire reach. The ER mediums cover closer engagement. The flamer handles infantry.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is a medium-range ballistic and energy platform. The HAG/20 spread combined with the ER laser suite creates multi-location damage that concentrated fire cannot replicate. Walk six, run nine keeps the warrior mobile between firing positions. The quad stability makes the HAG/20 particularly accurate at speed.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: The Balius is a 65-ton Clan quadrupedal OmniMech, hand-crafted by elite technicians for Bloodnamed warriors. The 390-rated Clan XL pushes it to walk six, run nine, exceptional mobility for a heavy. The endo steel structure and ferro-fibrous armour keep protection solid within a tight weight budget. The quadrupedal design provides a stable firing platform but limits torso twist capability, which shapes how every configuration needs to be loaded.
variants.capabilities: The B configuration concentrates firepower into a tight engagement window. Twin ER large lasers as the primary weapons, eight heavy small lasers for close work, a large pulse laser in the rear arc, and a flamer for anti-infantry use. Two extra double heat sinks help manage the load but this is a hot configuration when the heavy small lasers and ER large lasers fire simultaneously. The rear large pulse laser is the best rear-arc weapon I have seen on a Clan OmniMech and the quadrupedal platform makes it genuinely useful rather than a token gesture.
variants.deployment: The B configuration is built for warriors who close range and then use the heavy small laser volume to overwhelm opponents at point blank. The ER large lasers open the engagement and the heavy smalls close it. The limited torso traverse means positioning discipline matters more here than on a biped. Flanking attempts on this configuration run into the rear large pulse laser, which is not a comfortable discovery.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: The Balius is a sixty-five ton Clan quadrupedal OmniMech hand-crafted by elite technicians for Bloodnamed warriors. Walk six, run nine on the 390-rated Clan XL engine. Configuration C carries two ATM-9 launchers, two ER medium lasers, two medium pulse lasers, and a flamer. Walk six, run nine. The ATM-9s provide three-munition tactical flexibility. Four tons of ATM ammunition allows meaningful operational endurance across munition types. The energy weapons provide direct fire backup.
variants.deployment: Configuration C deploys as an adaptive fire platform. Pre-loading the correct ATM munition type for the expected engagement substantially improves output. The energy weapons handle direct fire when the ATMs need to conserve rounds. Walk six, run nine maintains range control while delivering ATM fire.

The jump capability on a quad assault platform is the defining tactical feature. The ER PPC handles extreme range. The ER mediums and pulse lasers cover closer work. All energy, no ammunition.
variants.deployment: Configuration D is the jump-capable Balius. Jump six on a sixty-five ton quad is genuinely surprising to opponents. The warrior uses the jump jets to claim elevated positions and flanking angles, then delivers ER PPC and energy fire from the stable quad platform. The all-energy loadout suits independent operations.

The flamer handles infantry.
variants.deployment: The Prime is the ranged direct fire configuration. The ER large laser combined with walk six, run nine on a quad platform creates a consistent long-range threat from a stable firing position. The four medium pulse lasers handle any opponent that closes the range. The all-energy loadout means no ammunition logistics concerns.

variants.deployment: Configuration U deploys in aquatic operations. The five UMUs provide genuine subaquatic mobility. The SRT-6 torpedo launchers deliver heavy fire support underwater. The ER large laser handles direct threats in both environments. Maintaining the UMUs and torpedo systems requires procedures not in the standard Balius manual.

The Streak LRM-15 guarantee of hitting at range combined with the Streak SRM-6 guarantee at close range means every round fired connects. The ER large pulse laser handles direct fire between missile shots. The improved heavy medium laser closes the engagement decisively.

variants.name: BNDR-01A
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Bandersnatch in 3052 as an affordable seventy-five ton heavy for mercenary commands and independent worlds. Walk four, run six on the XL engine. Two LB 10-X autocannons, three LRM-5 launchers, and six medium lasers. Not a sophisticated design. A straightforward one.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the XL engine at seventy-five tons. XL engine — side torso vulnerability applies. The LB 10-X autocannons provide cluster and slug options. The three LRM-5s provide modest indirect fire. Six medium lasers handle close-range energy work. Parts availability is good given Maltex production volumes. The BNDR-01A carries two LB 10-X ACs, six medium lasers, and three LRM-5s on the XL engine. Walk four, run six. The LB 10-X pair provides cluster and slug fire. The six medium lasers handle close-range energy work. The three LRM-5s add modest indirect fire. XL engine vulnerability applies.
variants.deployment: The 01A established the Bandersnatch's reputation when it entered service in 3052. Mercenary commands remain primary operators because the price and maintenance profile suit independent units. The LB 10-X cluster option against lighter opponents is useful. The six medium lasers handle anything that closes. XL engine means side torso damage is fatal.

variants.name: BNDR-01A (Horus)

The Horus is a named configuration carrying two AC/20s, two medium lasers, and an ER large laser on the XL engine. Walk four, run six. Two AC/20s on a seventy-five ton heavy at close range is devastating but generates severe heat. The ER large laser handles approach fire. Two AC/20s require four tons of ammunition combined.
variants.deployment: The Horus transforms the Bandersnatch from a fire support platform into a close-range devastation machine. Two AC/20s simultaneously is an enormous heat and ammunition management challenge. The ER large laser fires during the approach under tolerable heat levels. Warriors who close range and fire both AC/20s accept severe thermal consequences but inflict corresponding damage.

Two LB 10-X autocannons, three LRM-5 launchers, and six medium lasers. Not a sophisticated design. A straightforward one.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 300-rated light engine at seventy-five tons. The BNDR-01B carries an Ultra AC/10, a PPC, four medium lasers, two LRM-5s, and a Streak SRM-2. The light engine provides better side torso survivability than the XL original. The UAC/10 delivers medium-range ballistic fire with double-tap capability. CASE protects the ammunition bay.
variants.deployment: The 01B was designed for clients who wanted better survivability than the original XL engine provides. The light engine substantially improves resilience. The UAC/10 and PPC combination covers long and medium range. The medium lasers and Streak SRM-2 handle close engagement. CASE ammunition protection is appropriate given the ballistic and missile ammunition density.

variants.name: BNDR-01Ar
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Bandersnatch in 3052 as an affordable seventy-five ton heavy for mercenary commands and independent worlds. Walk four, run six on the XL engine. The BNDR-01Ar carries two LB 10-X ACs, four medium lasers, three LRM-5s, and an ER small laser on the XL engine. Walk four, run six. A Guardian ECM suite is the primary addition over the base 01A. Two medium lasers removed to accommodate the ECM and ER small laser.
variants.deployment: The 01Ar was developed during the Jihad as a counter to Word of Blake C3i networking. The Guardian ECM degrades C3i-linked fire coordination. The weapons loadout is slightly lighter than the 01A — two fewer medium lasers. Units facing C3i-equipped opponents ran the 01Ar; units facing conventional opponents preferred the 01A's heavier laser suite.

variants.name: BNC-1E
variants.overview: The Banshee has a reputation for being underarmed and the early variants earned that reputation. Ninety-five tons, walk four, run six on the 380-rated engine — fast for this weight class. The speed is the design's genuine capability. Eighteen variants over the production run have addressed the firepower criticism with varying success.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety-five tons. The 380-rated engine at this weight is genuinely fast for an assault 'Mech and that speed changes what the machine can do tactically. Standard engine survivability on most variants. The Starshield armour at thirteen-plus tons is adequate but not exceptional for the weight. Physical presence and speed are the design's strengths. The BNC-1E is the primitive prototype using a primitive PPC alongside an AC/5, two medium lasers, and a small laser. Walk three, run four on the primitive 345-rated engine — slower than the production standard. Primitive components require period-specific documentation. The early heat management problems I have read about in the maintenance logs are real.
variants.deployment: The 1E is the pre-production Banshee and the criticism of the design started here. The primitive PPC is less capable than the production version. Walk three is slower than the 3E production standard. Maintaining a primitive BattleMech requires documentation that differs from every production variant. Parts are not interchangeable with production components.

variants.overview: The Banshee has a reputation for being underarmed and the early variants earned that reputation. Eighteen variants over the production run have addressed the firepower criticism with varying success.

The BNC-3E is the standard production model from 2475: a PPC, an AC/5, and a small laser on the 380-rated engine. Walk four, run six. That is all the weapons there are. The criticism that the Banshee is underarmed exists specifically because of this variant. The speed and mass are the contributions, not the firepower.
variants.deployment: The 3E was produced in massive numbers and that is part of the legacy problem — many units inherited these and were unhappy about it. The speed is genuinely useful. Walk four on a ninety-five ton assault machine changes engagement dynamics. The PPC and AC/5 are functional weapons that simply lack the weight of fire an assault 'Mech is expected to deliver.

variants.overview: The Banshee has a reputation for being underarmed and the early variants earned that reputation. Ninety-five tons, walk four, run six on the 380-rated engine — fast for this weight class. The speed is the design's genuine capability. The BNC-3M replaces the AC/5 with a second PPC and adds two medium lasers and a small laser. Walk four, run six on the standard 380-rated engine. Dual PPCs on a standard engine at ninety-five tons generate severe heat under simultaneous fire. Sixteen heat sinks is not enough for two PPCs. The medium lasers add close-range capability.
variants.deployment: The 3M addresses the firepower criticism by adding a second PPC. The heat penalty is severe — pilots who fire both PPCs simultaneously heat quickly and cannot sustain it. Fire discipline is required. The medium lasers provide close-range energy fire that the original 3E completely lacked. A genuine improvement over the 3E at the cost of heat management complexity.

variants.overview: The Banshee has a reputation for being underarmed and the early variants earned that reputation. The BNC-3Q replaces the PPC and AC/5 with a single AC/20 and keeps the small laser. Walk four, run six. An AC/20 on a ninety-five ton machine is devastating at close range. The small laser provides minimal backup. Walk four closes distance quickly for the weight class.
variants.deployment: The 3Q is a close-range devastation machine with almost no ranged capability. The AC/20 at close range is the entire combat contribution. Anything at range is ignored. Pilots close distance using the Banshee's speed advantage over slower assaults and deliver the AC/20 when they get there. The small laser handles point-blank threats the AC/20 cannot engage efficiently.

variants.overview: The Banshee has a reputation for being underarmed and the early variants earned that reputation. Ninety-five tons, walk four, run six on the 380-rated engine — fast for this weight class. The speed is the design's genuine capability. Eighteen variants over the production run have addressed the firepower criticism with varying success.

The BNC-3S uses a smaller 285-rated engine for walk three, run four but mounts a dramatically expanded weapons load: two PPCs, an AC/10, an SRM-6, four medium lasers, and two small lasers. Walk three is the speed penalty. The heat management across all weapons is severe — this machine runs hot under sustained fire.
variants.deployment: The 3S is the fully armed Banshee that the design's critics wanted from the beginning. The weapons load is comprehensive across all ranges. Walk three is the tradeoff. Heat management under sustained fire is the pilot's constant discipline. Units that needed assault firepower at any cost ran the 3S and learned to manage its thermal demands.

The Reinesblatt is a named 3S-chassis configuration carrying an AC/10, four medium lasers, two small lasers, an LRM-10, and a large laser. A five-ton hatchet is mounted for physical combat. Walk three, run four. The hatchet adds a physical attack dimension alongside the weapons suite.
variants.deployment: The Reinesblatt mounts a hatchet on a Banshee chassis, which creates a close-range physical threat that the weapons also support. The LRM-10 softens targets at range, then the machine closes for the hatchet and medium laser close engagement. The large laser provides intermediate range fire. A named machine — maintain to the specific build documentation.

The additional armour addresses the protection criticism alongside the firepower upgrade.
variants.deployment: The 3MC is a straightforward improvement over the 3E — better autocannon, more armour, same speed. The additional armour makes a meaningful difference in survivability. The AC/10 delivers more damage per shot than the AC/5. Field maintenance units can perform this upgrade without significant technical overhead.

The XL engine enables the weapons mass. Two rear-firing small lasers discourage pursuit. The ER PPCs and Gauss handle range work. XL engine — side torso vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The 5S is the most extensively armed standard Banshee variant. The ER PPC reach and Gauss accuracy together cover long-range engagement. The SRM-6 and medium lasers handle close work. The rear small lasers are an actual tactical tool — they discourage opponents from pursuing as the Banshee repositions. XL engine means side torso damage ends the machine.

The jump capability on a ninety-five ton machine opens terrain options unavailable to ground-bound assaults. One ER PPC is the weapons reduction.
variants.deployment: The Sawyer uses jump four to claim elevated positions and cross terrain obstacles. Jump four on ninety-five tons is the defining tactical feature. The remaining ER PPC, Gauss, SRM-6, and medium lasers provide capable direct fire. The XL engine vulnerability applies. Pilots who exploit the jump capability aggressively get tactical options the standard 5S cannot access.

Eighteen variants over the production run have addressed the firepower criticism with varying success.

Standard engine survivability on most variants. The Starshield armour at thirteen-plus tons is adequate but not exceptional for the weight. Physical presence and speed are the design's strengths. The Vandergriff is a named 5S-chassis configuration built for Solaris VII in 3062, carrying twin ER PPCs, an LB 10-X, two medium lasers, and an SRM-4 with jump four. Walk four, run six, jump four on the XL engine. The LB 10-X replaces the Gauss with cluster and slug options.
variants.deployment: The Vandergriff is an arena configuration. The jump capability and ER PPC combined with LB 10-X flexibility suited the arena environment where tactical variety matters. The LB 10-X cluster option is useful against lighter opponents. A named machine — maintain to the specific Solaris VII arena build documentation.

variants.deployment: The 6S prioritises survivability over firepower breadth. The light engine survives hits that kill XL Banshees. The heavy Gauss and LB 10-X together provide ranged ballistic coverage at reduced system count. The small laser handles point-blank threats. For units that needed a Banshee that stays alive under fire rather than one that fires back with maximum effect, the 6S works.

variants.deployment: The 7S is the most capable Banshee variant in terms of weapons coverage combined with light engine survivability. The ER PPC and Gauss at range, four ER mediums and SRM-6 at close range, and a light engine that survives side torso damage. Pilots who manage Gauss ammunition carefully maintain effective long-range fire. This is the Banshee that finally answers the firepower criticism without sacrificing survivability.

Maintenance across eight weapon systems is the overhead.

variants.name: BNC-9S
variants.overview: The Banshee has always had a reputation for being underarmed and the early variants earned that reputation fairly. variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four on the 285-rated light engine. The light engine gives better side torso survivability than an XL at the cost of speed. The Gauss rifle is accurate and hits hard. The heavy PPC hits harder than a standard PPC at medium range. The ER PPC handles long-range work. Three ER mediums and an SRM-6 cover close engagement. C3 slave and Beagle active probe are fitted.
variants.deployment: The 9S was built for the Combine's Clan-era heavy line requirements. The C3 slave enables network integration. The Beagle active probe adds sensor capability for forward positioning. Walk three is slow for a Banshee — the speed advantage over heavier assaults is gone on this variant. The comprehensive weapons suite and light engine survivability compensate.

variants.deployment: The 3Mr is the ER upgrade path for existing 3M machines. The ER PPC range improvement is meaningful. The ER mediums extend the backup energy range. The heat management improvement over the 3M is modest — ER PPCs are still hot weapons. Field maintenance units can perform this refit using the relatively accessible 3M as the base.

The Silver Bullet Gauss fires submunitions that spread across multiple locations.
variants.deployment: The 11X is the survivability-maximised variant. The armoured cockpit and actuators significantly reduce the chance of critical component loss from penetrating hits. The modular armour sections allow field replacement rather than full structural repair. The Silver Bullet Gauss spread pattern and Bombast variable output make the weapons more tactically flexible than their count suggests. Clan XL engine maintenance alongside IS construction requires two-track technical support.

The ER medium handles close backup.
variants.deployment: The 9S2 is the pure PPC and Gauss fire platform. Walk three is the speed penalty for the light engine survivability and weapons density. The heavy PPC minimum range gap is covered by the light PPCs at close distance. The Gauss provides long-range precision. Light engine means this machine survives hits that kill the XL variants. A durable, if slow, assault fire platform.

Weapons cover every range band comprehensively.
variants.deployment: The 12S uses Clan components throughout, which requires Clan-qualified maintenance alongside IS chassis procedures. The full Clan weapon suite delivers performance improvements across all weapon types over IS equivalents. The Clan XL engine provides the standard side torso vulnerability but Clan construction quality is consistently higher than IS equivalents. The comprehensive weapons loadout addresses the original Banshee firepower criticism definitively.

variants.name: BNZ-X
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works developed the Banzai during the Jihad as an experimental assault rebuild of the Mauler chassis. Ninety tons, walk four, run six with a MASC-boosted burst to around one hundred kilometres per hour on the 360-rated XL engine. The MASC system is the design's defining feature and its primary maintenance concern.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the XL engine, with MASC providing burst acceleration to around one hundred km/h. The BNZ-X is the sole prototype: two large pulse lasers, two medium pulse lasers, and an ER small laser. The original design called for capacitor-augmented ER PPCs but the lead engineer replaced them with pulse lasers to reduce heat load. The MASC system requires dedicated maintenance attention — transmission wear under heavy use is the consistent concern.
variants.deployment: The BNZ-X is a prototype that reached the testing stage but not full production. The MASC burst speed is the primary tactical capability. The pulse laser suite handles direct engagement across close and medium ranges. The XL engine vulnerability applies. Any unit operating a BNZ-X is working from prototype documentation rather than a production manual.

variants.name: BGS-1T
variants.overview: Pinard Protectorates Limited built the Barghest in 3058 as a seventy-ton quadrupedal heavy. Walk five, run seven on the 350-rated XL engine. The quad chassis provides firing stability that bipedal designs cannot match, which suits the heavy ballistic weapons most variants carry. Six variants cover a range of fire support and direct assault roles.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy tons. XL engine — side torso vulnerability on all XL-equipped variants. The quad stability is the chassis's genuine tactical advantage: this machine holds aim better at speed than comparable bipedal designs. Parts availability through Capellan supply chains is reasonable given Pinard production. The BGS-1T carries two ER large lasers and an LB 20-X on the XL engine. Walk five, run seven. The ER large lasers provide long-range energy fire. The LB 20-X delivers heavy ballistic fire with cluster or slug options at medium range. The quad stability makes the LB 20-X particularly accurate at speed.
variants.deployment: The 1T established the Barghest's production identity. The ER large laser range combined with LB 20-X close-range ballistics and quad stability creates a consistent fire support and direct engagement platform. The XL engine means side torso damage is fatal. The cluster munition option against lighter targets is the LB 20-X's primary flexibility advantage.

variants.deployment: The 2T is the direct assault variant. The ER PPC fires during the approach; the UAC/20 takes over when range closes. The XL engine requires the pilot to close range decisively and not expose the flanks.

Prototype designation means documentation differs from production procedures. The improved heavy Gauss performance advantages were validated on this chassis.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Battle Cobra is a forty-ton Clan OmniMech built around simplicity and low production cost. Walk six, run nine on the 240-rated Clan engine. Limited pod tonnage constrains weapons diversity but makes this chassis easy to maintain and straightforward to operate. Clan second-line and Inner Sphere units operate it widely.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at forty tons. Limited pod space — around twelve tons — means most configurations carry two or three weapons rather than elaborate mixed suites. The chassis is genuinely easy to maintain. Pod swaps are clean. The Clan engine is the consistent maintenance track. Configuration A carries four medium pulse lasers and six small pulse lasers. Walk six, run nine. Ten pulse laser systems for close-quarters combat. The medium pulse lasers provide the primary fire. The six small pulse lasers add volume at point-blank range. All energy, no ammunition.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is for close-quarters combat and formal Trials. The pulse laser volume at close range is the entire design intent. Walk six, run nine delivers the suite to engagement range quickly. No ammunition to manage. Heat from ten pulse lasers simultaneously requires management but the chassis heat sinks are adequate for cycling fire.

Heat from both ER PPCs firing simultaneously is the pilot's primary discipline.
variants.deployment: Configuration B sacrifices weapons flexibility for raw ER PPC output. The threat that two ER PPCs represent at forty tons consistently surprises heavier opponents. Heat management is the tactical constraint — warriors who fire both PPCs every cycle will hit the shutdown threshold. Warriors who alternate maintain sustained effective output.

Heat from the large pulse lasers under sustained fire is manageable on the chassis heat sinks.
variants.deployment: The Prime is the standard deployment configuration. The large pulse laser accuracy at medium range suits the Battle Cobra's engagement style. The small pulse lasers deter close approach. No ammunition dependency means this configuration sustains independent operations without supply concern.

variants.name: F
variants.overview: The Battle Cobra is a 40-ton Clan OmniMech originally produced by Clan Steel Viper. Its straightforward design and low complexity made it attractive beyond its original manufacturer and it spread widely through second-line Clan forces. The 240-rated Clan fusion engine gives walk six, run nine, jump six, which is good mobility for a medium. The ferro-fibrous armour and endo steel structure provide reliable protection within the weight budget.
variants.capabilities: The F configuration carries three ER medium lasers in the left arm and an Ultra AC/5 in the right arm with one ton of ammunition. The UAC/5 in double-tap mode adds meaningful ballistic output that the laser-heavy primary configuration lacks. The jump capability at this weight class is the configuration's best tactical asset. Six jump jets at forty tons open terrain options most opponents cannot match. Heat runs warm when the ER mediums and UAC fire together but manageable.
variants.deployment: The F configuration is a medium-range striker built around mobility. The jump capability lets warriors close angles and take elevated positions that shape the engagement in their favour. The single ton of UAC ammunition is the operational constraint on extended missions. The ER mediums carry the fight when the bin runs dry. Pod swaps on this chassis are clean and the Battle Cobra has good parts availability across most Clan maintenance lines.

Four additional heat sinks manage the combined thermal load.
variants.deployment: Configuration H is the maximum range and close-range damage variant. The ER large lasers at range transition to heavy medium laser volume as the engagement closes. The additional heat sinks enable sustained fire across both weapon types. Warriors who pace the fire cycling correctly get consistent high output.

The pulse laser close-range suite handles direct combat when the ATMs are conserved. Pre-loading the correct ATM munition type before engagement improves effectiveness substantially.

The slower engine frees space for a C3i networking system that appears across all IS configurations as a standard fitting.

Standard engine means side torso hits are survivable. Pod space is modest. The BTL-C-2O carries two IS-grade large pulse lasers — one per arm — with a double heat sink and the C3i network computer. Walk five, run seven. The large pulse lasers provide accurate medium-range fire. The C3i networking integrates targeting data across the formation.
variants.deployment: The 2O is the baseline IS configuration. The C3i networking is the defining feature across all IS Battle Cobra variants. The large pulse lasers provide direct combat capability. Walk five is slower than the Clan engine variants. The standard engine survivability makes this more resilient under fire.

The ECM, Beagle, and TAG make this a comprehensive electronic warfare and designation platform. The laser suite handles direct combat.
variants.deployment: Configuration 2OA is the electronic warfare specialist. The Guardian ECM, Beagle probe, TAG, and C3i together create a machine that multiplies formation effectiveness beyond its direct combat value. The Beagle finds hidden units. The TAG designates for guided munitions. The ECM degrades enemy targeting. The pulse lasers handle direct engagement.

Twin iNarc launchers combined with C3i networking create a force multiplier that makes every missile-armed unit in the formation more effective. Four light PPCs at forty tons is a respectable energy output at the ranges they work best. All-energy with no ammunition.

variants.name: BH-K305
variants.overview: Defiance Industries built the Battle Hawk in 3053 as a thirty-ton defensive light — unusually armoured for the weight class, with AMS protection and a close-range weapons suite. Walk five, run seven, jump five on the 150-rated engine. The heavy armour and AMS distinguish it from the standard light 'Mech design philosophy.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at thirty tons on the XL engine. The BH-K305 carries three medium pulse lasers, a Streak SRM-2, and an anti-missile system. The pulse lasers are accurate at close range. The Streak SRM-2 fires only on lock. The AMS defends against incoming missiles. XL engine — side torso vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The K305 is the original production model from Hesperus II. The heavy armour and AMS make it more survivable than most thirty-ton lights. The pulse laser and Streak combination handles close engagement reliably. The AMS ammunition requires management alongside the Streak rounds. The XL engine is the survivability caveat on an otherwise defensive design.

variants.overview: Defiance Industries built the Battle Hawk in 3053 as a thirty-ton defensive light — unusually armoured for the weight class, with AMS protection and a close-range weapons suite. variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at thirty tons on the light engine. The BH-K306 carries three ER medium lasers, a Streak SRM-4, and an anti-missile system. The light engine provides side torso survivability the XL variant lacks. The ER mediums extend energy fire reach. The Streak SRM-4 is a genuine upgrade over the SRM-2.
variants.deployment: The K306 addresses the XL vulnerability of the K305 with a light engine that survives side torso damage. The ER medium lasers reach farther than the K305's pulse lasers. The Streak SRM-4 delivers more missile volume per lock than the SRM-2. The AMS ammunition management remains. A straightforward survivability and firepower improvement over the original.

variants.name: BKX-1X
variants.overview: Achernar BattleMechs developed the BattleAxe in 2459 as one of the earliest native Federated Suns heavy designs. Seventy tons. The original prototype used primitive components; the definitive 7K production model uses PPCs and jump jets. The design has a troubled early reputation that later variants improved upon.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four on the prototype 255-rated engine. The BKX-1X is the primitive 2459 prototype: two large lasers, two LRM-5s, an SRM-6, and two machine guns. Primitive components require period-specific documentation and are not interchangeable with production parts. The asymmetric arm configuration creates balance issues I have read about in the original development logs.
variants.deployment: The 1X is the prototype — documentation differs from every production variant. The 255-rated engine limits the machine to walk three. The large lasers, LRMs, and SRM provide workable coverage across ranges. This machine received its unexpected second life during the Jihad when Achernar brought old designs back into production from archive materials.

variants.overview: Achernar BattleMechs developed the BattleAxe in 2459 as one of the earliest native Federated Suns heavy designs. Seventy tons. variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four on the production 7K standard engine. The PPCs provide long-range direct fire. The LRM-5s add modest indirect fire. The SRM-6 handles close threats. Standard engine survivability throughout the conventional variants. The BKX-7K is the definitive production model: two Donal PPCs, two LRM-5s, and an SRM-6 on the 280-rated engine with Rawlings jump jets. Walk four, run six, jump four. The PPCs replaced the prototype's large lasers. The jump capability allows the machine to cross terrain the earlier prototype could not.
variants.deployment: The 7K is the BattleAxe that established the design's reputation — better than the troubled prototype. The PPCs provide genuine long-range capability. Jump four is useful for positioning. The LRM-5s provide modest indirect fire support. Standard engine survivability is preserved throughout.

The MML-7 flexibility covers most engagement scenarios. The ER mediums extend energy fire reach. The light engine means this machine outlasts XL competitors under sustained fire.

variants.name: BLR-1G
variants.overview: The BattleMaster BLR-1G is an iconic assault 'Mech known for its reliability, survivability, and combat presence. Originally designed as a powerful frontline command platform, it combines devastating close-range firepower with sophisticated cockpit electronics for coordinating company-level operations.
variants.capabilities: From a maintenance standpoint, the 1G's most notable feature is its generous cockpit space, which allows for extensive command and control equipment. This makes it an excellent choice for unit commanders at every level. For performance, the design excels in close-range combat, with its six Martell medium lasers and Holly SRM-6 providing a potent punch. However, sustained fire can overwhelm the eighteen single heat sinks, making heat management a critical concern.
variants.deployment: The original BattleMaster configuration has defined the assault command 'Mech role for centuries. The BLR-1G's combination of a right-arm Donal PPC, six Martell medium lasers, Holly SRM-6, and twin SperryBrowning machine guns creates a versatile weapons suite capable of engaging targets at all ranges.

variants.name: BLR-1Gb
variants.overview: Hollis Inc built the BattleMaster in 2633 and it became the Inner Sphere's standard assault command platform. Eighty-five tons, walk four, run six on the 340-rated engine. The cockpit is spacious by assault standards — enough room for command consoles without feeling cramped. Thirty variants have come out of that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at eighty-five tons. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The large cockpit is the design's consistent identity, which has made it the default heavy command platform across all five Great Houses. Parts availability is excellent after nearly four centuries of production. The BLR-1Gb carries two ER PPCs and a large pulse laser on the standard 340-rated engine. Walk four, run six. The ER PPCs extend the engagement range over the standard 1G's PPCs. The large pulse laser provides accurate medium-range backup. Single heat sinks — heat management under sustained ER PPC fire requires discipline.
variants.deployment: The 1Gb is the ER PPC upgrade of the command configuration. The single heat sinks limit sustained fire output — pilots need to pace the ER PPCs rather than cycling them continuously. The large pulse laser handles medium-range work without the PPC heat cost. Standard engine survivability is preserved.

variants.name: BLR-2C
variants.overview: The BattleMaster has been a front-line command assault 'Mech since 2633 and the BLR-2C is a mid-era upgrade that adds sensor and network capability without abandoning the close-range firepower the design is known for. Built on a 340-rated standard engine at eighty-five tons, it walks four and runs six. The standard engine is the right choice for a command platform: it survives torso damage that would kill an XL-equipped machine.
variants.capabilities: The 2C carries an ER PPC, SRM-6, four medium lasers, and an anti-missile system, backed by a Beagle active probe and Nirasaki targeting system. The rear-firing medium lasers that define the BattleMaster family are present. The anti-missile system is a genuine defensive asset rather than a token, and the Beagle extends sensor reach beyond standard cockpit capability. Heat management across the ER PPC and four medium lasers requires discipline but the eighteen double heat sinks handle it adequately.
variants.deployment: The BLR-2C is a command platform that fights. The Beagle and targeting system give the commander situational awareness beyond what lighter scouts provide. The rear medium lasers discourage anything that tries to exploit the close-range work. The SRM-6 handles targets that get inside the ER PPC minimum range. This variant is most effective when the commander uses the sensor advantages actively rather than treating it as a standard assault 'Mech.

The extra armor and heat sinks do improve survivability, but be prepared for some compromises.
