variants.name: BLR-3M (Rogers)
variants.overview: The BattleMaster BLR-1G is an iconic assault 'Mech known for its reliability, survivability, and combat presence. Originally designed as a powerful frontline command platform, it combines devastating close-range firepower with sophisticated cockpit electronics for coordinating company-level operations.
variants.capabilities: From a maintenance standpoint, the 1G's most notable feature is its generous cockpit space, which allows for extensive command and control equipment. This makes it an excellent choice for unit commanders at every level. For performance, the design excels in close-range combat, with its six Martell medium lasers and Holly SRM-6 providing a potent punch. However, sustained fire can overwhelm the eighteen single heat sinks, making heat management a critical concern.
variants.deployment: This variant replaces the standard SRM-6 and machine gun with seven Streak SRM-2 launchers, sacrificing some armor plating in the process. The ferro-fibrous armor provides adequate protection, but be prepared for potential maintenance headaches. This configuration prioritizes reliable short-range damage output over mixed engagement capabilities.

variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at eighty-five tons. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The large cockpit is the design's consistent identity, which has made it the default heavy command platform across all five Great Houses. Parts availability is excellent after nearly four centuries of production. The BLR-CM carries two C3 master computers, an ER PPC, an MRM-30, two ER medium lasers, and jump three on a 255-rated standard engine. Walk three, run four, jump three. The dual C3 master capability is the defining feature — coordinating two separate lances is a significant command tool. Walk three is the speed penalty for the smaller engine. The ER PPC, MRM-30, and ER mediums provide adequate direct combat capability alongside the command role.

variants.overview: The Bear Cub is a twenty-five ton Clan light built around simplicity and low cost — Ghost Bear's answer to second-line units that need something inexpensive to maintain. Walk eight, run twelve on the 200-rated Clan XL. Three variants cover modest tactical variation.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at twenty-five tons. The Clan XL at this weight means side torso damage is fatal — speed is the primary survival mechanism. The design is straightforward to maintain by Clan standards. Limited weapon tonnage means most configurations carry three to four weapons. Variant 2 replaces the original LRM-5 launcher with a second SRM-4, carrying two ER medium lasers, two SRM-4s, and an ER small laser. Walk eight, run twelve. The twin SRM-4s significantly increase close-range missile output at the cost of indirect fire capability.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 is the close-range firepower upgrade introduced in 3070. The second SRM-4 makes the Bear Cub more dangerous at close range than the original at the cost of the LRM-5 stand-off capability. Walk eight delivers the close-range suite to engagement range quickly. The XL vulnerability at this weight means the pilot depends on speed rather than armour.

variants.overview: The Stone Rhino, called the Behemoth in IS records, is a hundred-ton Clan assault built by Clan Smoke Jaguar starting in 2847. Walk three, run four on the standard Clan engine. Eight variants show significant tactical philosophy variation. The quad configuration provides firing stability that bipedal designs cannot match.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at a hundred tons. Slow even by assault standards. The quad chassis provides stable firing positions. Clan construction quality throughout. The standard engine variants survive side torso damage that kills XL competitors. Ammunition management across the heavy weapons systems is the consistent operational overhead. Variant 4 uses a Clan XL engine and carries four LRM-10s, two Ultra AC/10s, four ER medium lasers, four machine guns, and jump three. Walk three, run four, jump three. The XL engine enables the jump capability and weapons density. The UAC/10s handle direct ballistic fire. The LRM-10s provide indirect fire support.
variants.deployment: Variant 4 is the test platform that originated around 2846 with Clan Smoke Jaguar. Jump three on a hundred-ton quad is the tactical surprise. The LRM-10 indirect fire combined with UAC/10 direct fire covers the full engagement range. The XL engine adds the side torso vulnerability the standard engine variants avoid.

The large pulse lasers provide accurate medium-range fire. The ATM-9 flexibility covers three munition types. The XL engine enables the jump capability.
variants.deployment: Variant 3 is a Clan Hell's Horses design produced at Tokasha Mechworks from around 3068. Replacing Gauss rifles with ATM-9 launchers removes ammunition dependency for the primary ballistic weapons and adds three-munition missile flexibility. The large pulse lasers provide direct fire. Pre-loading the correct ATM munition type is the key preparation step.

variants.overview: The Stone Rhino, called the Behemoth in IS records, is a hundred-ton Clan assault built by Clan Smoke Jaguar starting in 2847. Walk three, run four on the standard Clan engine. Eight variants show significant tactical philosophy variation. The quad configuration provides firing stability that bipedal designs cannot match.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at a hundred tons. Slow even by assault standards. The quad chassis provides stable firing positions. Clan construction quality throughout. The standard engine variants survive side torso damage that kills XL competitors. Ammunition management across the heavy weapons systems is the consistent operational overhead. Variant 8 uses the standard Clan engine with no jump jets and carries two Gauss rifles, two large pulse lasers, and a small pulse laser, with Actuator Enhancement Systems in both arms. Walk three, run four. The AES provides enhanced physical attack capability and improved aim. The Gauss rifles provide long-range accurate fire.
variants.deployment: Variant 8 removes the jump jets of the standard model and replaces them with AES for enhanced physical combat effectiveness. The AES makes the quad's physical attacks significantly more damaging than a standard chassis. The Gauss rifles deliver accurate long-range fire. The large pulse lasers handle medium-range engagement. Standard engine survivability is preserved.

variants.name: BEL-1X
variants.overview: The Bellerophon is a sixty-ton primitive BattleMech with an unusual history — it holds the distinction of being the second BattleMech ever developed, produced in 2442 as a prototype that never saw widespread adoption. Primitive components throughout. Walk four, run six. One configuration.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 290-rated primitive engine at sixty tons. The BEL-1X carries two large lasers and an SRM-4. Primitive components throughout — primitive cockpit, primitive armour, primitive engine. The asymmetric arm configuration creates handling characteristics that pilots take time to adjust to. Parts are not interchangeable with standard production 'Mechs.
variants.deployment: The BEL-1X saw its unexpected second life during the Jihad when Achernar brought archive materials back into production. Maintaining a primitive BattleMech requires documentation specific to 2442 construction standards. The two large lasers and SRM-4 are adequate weapons on a sixty-ton chassis. The primitive system limitations are the operational constraint, not the weapons.

variants.name: BEO-12
variants.overview: The Beowulf is a 45-ton medium reconnaissance 'Mech built by ComStar as a replacement for the ageing Mongoose, entering service in 3059. The 270-rated XL engine with MASC gives walk six, run nine, and burst capability significantly higher. Six jump jets provide jump six. The design prioritises sensors and electronics over raw firepower, which is exactly right for the role it was built to fill.
variants.capabilities: The BEO-12 carries a Blankenburg large pulse laser and two Diverse Optics ER medium lasers, with a TAG system for designating targets for artillery. The Beagle active probe is the centrepiece, extending detection range to find hidden units before they become a problem. The MASC system is the maintenance item I watch most carefully: it accelerates transmission wear when used regularly and the XL engine means a side torso breach ends the mission immediately.
variants.deployment: The original production model does exactly what ComStar needed: a fast, sensor-capable medium that can tag targets for indirect fire and handle light opposition independently. The TAG and Beagle combination makes this a force multiplier well beyond its direct combat value. Keep the MASC maintenance current and the Beagle calibrated and it does its job reliably.

variants.name: BEO-X-7a
variants.overview: The Beowulf is a 45-ton medium reconnaissance 'Mech built by ComStar as a replacement for the ageing Mongoose, entering service in 3059. The 270-rated XL engine with MASC gives walk six, run nine, and burst capability significantly higher. Six jump jets provide jump six. The design prioritises sensors and electronics over raw firepower, which is exactly right for the role it was built to fill.
variants.capabilities: The X-7a is an experimental variant with seven improved jump jets instead of the standard six, a full-head ejection system, and a simplified weapons package of four ER medium lasers split between both arms. The improved jump jets provide marginally better jump capability but require specialist maintenance procedures not covered in the standard Beowulf technical manual. The full-head ejection system is the pilot safety improvement that drove this variant's development.
variants.deployment: The X-7a is experimental designation and it shows in the field. The non-standard jump jets mean any tech without specific X-7a training should not touch them. The weapons load is lighter than the production 12 but the jump capability and ejection system improvements were the priority. Used by pilots who need the enhanced escape options the standard cockpit does not provide.

variants.name: BEO-14
variants.overview: The Beowulf is a 45-ton medium reconnaissance 'Mech built by ComStar as a replacement for the ageing Mongoose, entering service in 3059. The 270-rated XL engine with MASC gives walk six, run nine, and burst capability significantly higher. Six jump jets provide jump six. The design prioritises sensors and electronics over raw firepower, which is exactly right for the role it was built to fill.
variants.capabilities: The BEO-14 swaps the 12's laser and TAG loadout for two medium VSP lasers, an ER medium laser, two ER small lasers, a small laser, and a 'Mech-scale sword, with triple-strength myomer replacing standard actuators. The TSM activates when the machine runs hot, providing both a speed boost and enhanced melee capability. The heat sink reduction compared to the 12 means TSM threshold is reached quickly in combat, which is intentional.
variants.deployment: The 14 is a close-quarters variant built around the TSM and sword combination. The sensor focus of the standard Beowulf is gone here in favour of combat capability at short range. The TSM speed bonus when hot lets the 14 close distance faster than opponents expect. Heat management requires careful attention to stay near but not over the TSM activation threshold without losing control of the machine.

variants.name: PR
variants.overview: The Beowulf IIC PR is a unique variant that combines Inner Sphere and Clan technologies. It's essentially a Beowulf IIC with an Improved C3 computer slapped in, which changes its capabilities and quirks.
variants.capabilities: From a maintenance standpoint, the Beowulf IIC PR inherits most of the issues from the standard Beowulf IIC, like the electronics glitches due to the retained Dash-2 comms system. The C3i integration adds complexity, making it harder to diagnose and repair. In combat, the 'Mech's mixed tech means it can't fully utilize its Clan-grade sensors or electronics, limiting its scouting capabilities. On the plus side, the C3i does improve targeting accuracy when working with other C3-equipped 'Mechs.
variants.deployment: The PR variant was developed in 3086 as an experimental platform, integrating an Improved C3 computer into the Beowulf IIC chassis. The extended-range large pulse laser was replaced with a standard Clan extended-range large laser and the light TAG removed, while the Watchdog CEWS and extended-range medium pulse lasers were retained. It saw limited deployment alongside Ursus-PR 'Mechs by the First Drakøns.

variants.name: BRZ-A3
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Berserker in 3052 around a five-ton hatchet and a 400-rated XL engine, achieving walk four, run six on a hundred tons. The hatchet and the speed together are the design concept. For a hundred-ton machine, walk four is genuinely fast. The hatchet deals physical damage that weapons cannot replicate.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at a hundred tons. The XL engine is the standard vulnerability concern, but walk four on this weight class provides engagement options that slower assaults do not have. The hatchet deals substantial physical damage per hit. AMS appears across most variants for missile defence. Heat management is the consistent pilot discipline given the energy-heavy weapons choices. The BRZ-A3 carries an ER PPC, two large pulse lasers, an AMS, a flamer, and the five-ton hatchet. Walk four, run six on the XL engine. The ER PPC handles approach fire. The large pulse lasers are accurate at medium range. The AMS defends against missiles. The hatchet delivers physical damage at close range.
variants.deployment: The A3 is the original Berserker. Walk four closes range at assault speed. The large pulse lasers fire during the approach; the hatchet closes the engagement. The AMS protects during the approach. The ER PPC provides genuine reach before closing. XL engine means side torso hits are fatal — the speed is partly there to ensure those hits are not easy to land.

variants.name: BRZ-B3
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Berserker in 3052 around a five-ton hatchet and a 400-rated XL engine, achieving walk four, run six on a hundred tons. The hatchet and the speed together are the design concept. For a hundred-ton machine, walk four is genuinely fast. The hatchet deals physical damage that weapons cannot replicate.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at a hundred tons. The hatchet deals substantial physical damage per hit. AMS appears across most variants for missile defence. Heat management is the consistent pilot discipline given the energy-heavy weapons choices. The BRZ-B3 carries an ER PPC, two LRM-10 launchers, an AMS, a flamer, and the hatchet. Walk four, run six on the XL engine. The LRM-10s replace the A3's large pulse lasers with indirect fire capability. The ER PPC maintains the long-range direct fire role.
variants.deployment: The B3 transforms the Berserker from a pure close-range brawler into a fire support and assault hybrid. The LRM-10s provide indirect fire during the approach. The ER PPC handles direct long-range engagement. The hatchet closes the fight at melee range. Units that needed the Berserker's speed and hatchet capability alongside fire support capability ran the B3.

variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Berserker in 3052 around a five-ton hatchet and a 400-rated XL engine, achieving walk four, run six on a hundred tons. variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 400-rated light engine. The BRZ-C3 carries an ER PPC, six ER medium lasers, an AMS, a flamer, triple-strength myomer, and the hatchet. Light engine — side torso survivability. TSM activates at elevated heat, boosting the hatchet's physical impact and ground speed. The six ER mediums generate the heat that triggers TSM.
variants.deployment: The C3 uses the light engine's survivability and TSM to create a more durable and physically devastating Berserker. The six ER mediums heat the machine deliberately to trigger TSM, enhancing the hatchet strike. The C3 slave adds network integration. The light engine survives hits that end XL variants. Warriors who manage the TSM activation cycle get a significantly more dangerous close-range platform than the standard A3.

variants.name: BRZ-D4
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Berserker in 3052 around a five-ton hatchet and a 400-rated XL engine, achieving walk four, run six on a hundred tons. The hatchet and the speed together are the design concept. For a hundred-ton machine, walk four is genuinely fast. The hatchet deals physical damage that weapons cannot replicate.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four on the 400-rated Clan XL engine. The BRZ-D4 carries a Bombast laser, four ER medium lasers, a flamer, and the hatchet. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump four on a hundred-ton assault. The Bombast laser fires at variable output — higher power at higher heat cost.
variants.deployment: The D4 is the jump-capable Berserker. Jump four on a hundred-ton machine is the tactical surprise that defines this variant. The Clan XL and jump jets together allow approach from above and from angles ground-bound assaults cannot contest. The Bombast laser variable output allows the pilot to choose between sustained moderate fire and high-power single shots. Use the jump offensively.

variants.name: BSN-3K
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Bishamon in 3062 as a forty-five ton quadrupedal scout for the DCMS, designed specifically to fill network lance roles. Walk seven, run ten on the 315-rated XL engine. The quad configuration provides stability at speed. The C3 networking capability is the design's primary strategic value.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at forty-five tons. The XL engine at this weight means side torso damage is fatal. The quad stability is the tactical advantage — this machine holds aim better at walk seven than a bipedal equivalent. C3 master or slave appears across all variants as the design's networking identity. The BSN-3K is the primary production model: two medium pulse lasers, two ER medium lasers, and an MRM-20. Walk seven, run ten on the XL engine. The quad stability makes the MRM-20 effective at speed. The pulse and ER mediums cover close-range energy engagement. XL engine side torso vulnerability applies.
variants.deployment: The 3K operates as a fast striker in DCMS reconnaissance lances. Walk seven uses the quad speed to scout and harass. The MRM-20 at medium range combined with the pulse laser close-range suite handles most engagement scenarios. The C3 slave integrates targeting data. The XL engine means side torso damage is fatal.

variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Bishamon in 3062 as a forty-five ton quadrupedal scout for the DCMS, designed specifically to fill network lance roles. Walk seven, run ten on the 315-rated XL engine. The quad configuration provides stability at speed. The C3 networking capability is the design's primary strategic value.

The quad stability is the tactical advantage — this machine holds aim better at walk seven than a bipedal equivalent. C3 master or slave appears across all variants as the design's networking identity. The BSN-4K carries a C3 master computer, two medium pulse lasers, two ER small lasers, and an MRM-10. Walk seven, run ten on the XL engine. The C3 master coordinates the network lance rather than just participating in it. The MRM-10 is a reduction from the 3K's MRM-20.
variants.deployment: The 4K reconfigures the Bishamon as a network lance command platform. The C3 master makes it the targeting coordination hub. The reduced weapons load — MRM-10 instead of MRM-20, ER small lasers instead of ER mediums — is the tradeoff for the master computer. Lance commanders using the 4K accept reduced direct combat output for coordination capability.

variants.name: BSN-5KC
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Bishamon in 3062 as a forty-five ton quadrupedal scout for the DCMS, designed specifically to fill network lance roles. variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at forty-five tons. The XL engine at this weight means side torso damage is fatal. The quad stability is the tactical advantage — this machine holds aim better at walk seven than a bipedal equivalent. C3 master or slave appears across all variants as the design's networking identity. The BSN-5KC carries a C3 slave in its head, two medium pulse lasers, an ER medium laser, and a snub-nose PPC. Walk seven, run ten on the XL engine. The snub-nose PPC covers short to medium range without minimum range complications. The C3 slave complements the 4K's master in a network lance.
variants.deployment: The 5KC was introduced during the Jihad as the slave counterpart to the 4K command variant. The C3 slave feeds targeting data to the 4K master. The snub-nose PPC replaces the MRM-20 with direct fire capability. The ER medium and medium pulse lasers handle close engagement. The head-mounted C3 slave is an unusual placement that requires specific maintenance access procedures.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Black Hawk, known to Clan warriors as the Nova, is a 50-ton Clan OmniMech with a 250-rated Clan XL engine giving walk five, run seven, and fixed jump five capability. The chassis is notable for twelve fixed double heat sinks built into the torso, which provides a strong thermal foundation for energy-heavy configurations. Clan Blood Spirit developed it and it spread through multiple Clans.
variants.capabilities: The A configuration carries two ER PPCs and a medium pulse laser for direct fire, with two anti-missile systems providing incoming missile defence. The ER PPCs at fifty tons give this configuration a firepower profile that surprises opponents expecting less from a medium. The anti-missile systems are genuinely useful rather than cosmetic. Heat discipline is required when both ER PPCs fire in the same cycle.
variants.deployment: The A configuration is the long-range sniper variant, designed to address the Prime configuration's limited reach. It works best when kept at ER PPC range where the medium pulse laser is not the primary weapon. The AMS pair makes it resilient against missile-heavy opposition. Warriors who use the jump capability to control engagement distance get the most from this configuration.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: The Black Hawk OmniMech, known as the Nova in Clan records, is a fifty-ton Clan medium built around a 250-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The all-energy base weapons philosophy has influenced several configurations even when pod space permits conventional weapons.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at fifty tons. The Clan XL carries the standard side torso vulnerability. The jump capability is the consistent tactical feature across all configurations. Clan construction quality. The base chassis heat sink count is generous for a fifty-ton machine. Configuration B carries a large pulse laser, an Ultra AC/5, two machine guns, and an ER small laser. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The large pulse laser handles medium-range engagement accurately. The UAC/5 adds sustained ballistic fire. The machine guns address infantry. One ton of UAC/5 ammunition is the operational limit.
variants.deployment: Configuration B is the mixed ballistic and energy variant. The large pulse laser accuracy combined with UAC/5 sustained fire covers medium range well. The machine guns handle infantry. Jump five maintains tactical positioning flexibility. One ton of UAC/5 ammunition runs out on extended operations — the large pulse laser carries the fight after that.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: The Black Hawk OmniMech, known as the Nova in Clan records, is a fifty-ton Clan medium built around a 250-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Eighteen configurations make this one of the most varied Clan medium OmniMechs. The all-energy Prime configuration defines its identity, but later configurations range far from that.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at fifty tons. The Clan XL carries the standard side torso vulnerability. The jump capability is the consistent tactical feature across all configurations. Clan construction quality throughout. Sixteen heat sinks on most configurations — adequate for moderate energy loads but the all-energy configurations need careful cycling. Configuration C carries a Gauss rifle, an SRM-4, and a small pulse laser. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The Gauss rifle is the primary weapon — accurate and hitting hard at range. The SRM-4 handles close threats. The small pulse laser provides point-blank backup. Two tons of Gauss ammunition is the operational limit.
variants.deployment: Configuration C is built around the Gauss rifle as the primary weapon. The SRM-4 and small pulse laser handle anything that closes past optimal Gauss range. Two tons of Gauss ammunition tracks quickly on active operations. Jump five maintains positioning options for the Gauss engagement. The Clan XL side torso vulnerability applies.

variants.name: D
variants.overview: The Black Hawk, known to Clan warriors as the Nova, is a 50-ton Clan OmniMech with a 250-rated Clan XL engine giving walk five, run seven, and fixed jump five capability. The chassis is notable for twelve fixed double heat sinks built into the torso, which provides a strong thermal foundation for energy-heavy configurations. Clan Blood Spirit developed it and it spread through multiple Clans.
variants.capabilities: The D configuration carries an LB 5-X autocannon and an LRM-20 with two tons of ammunition each. This is the missile boat configuration and it differs substantially in feel from the energy-heavy variants. The LRM-20 provides sustained indirect fire and the LB 5-X handles direct ballistic work with cluster or slug options. No energy weapons means the fixed heat sinks are doing almost nothing tactically, which is the tradeoff for ammunition flexibility.
variants.deployment: The D configuration is used as a fire support element, keeping range and delivering LRM fire while the LB 5-X handles targets that close. The anti-aircraft capability mentioned in field reports comes from the LB 5-X cluster rounds against low-flying targets. Two tons each of LRM and LB ammunition means endurance management is critical on extended missions. This variant is less common than the energy configurations but fills a genuine fire support gap.

variants.name: Prime
variants.overview: The Black Hawk OmniMech, known as the Nova in Clan records, is a fifty-ton Clan medium built around a 250-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Eighteen configurations make this one of the most varied Clan medium OmniMechs. The all-energy Prime configuration defines its identity, but later configurations range far from that.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at fifty tons. The Clan XL carries the standard side torso vulnerability. The jump capability is the consistent tactical feature across all configurations. Clan construction quality throughout. Sixteen heat sinks on most configurations — adequate for moderate energy loads but the all-energy configurations need careful cycling. The Prime carries twelve ER medium lasers — six per arm. Walk five, run seven, jump five. No ballistic weapons, no missiles, no ammunition. Twelve ER mediums firing simultaneously generates severe heat. Warriors must cycle fire aggressively or the machine shuts down.
variants.deployment: The Prime is the all-energy archetype that defined the Nova's reputation. Twelve ER mediums at close range deliver output that heavier machines cannot easily absorb. The heat load requires disciplined cycling — three or four lasers per firing group rather than all twelve at once. Warriors who master the cycling pattern sustain devastating fire. Warriors who alpha strike shut down.

variants.overview: The Black Hawk OmniMech, known as the Nova in Clan records, is a fifty-ton Clan medium built around a 250-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The jump capability is the consistent tactical feature across all configurations. Clan construction quality throughout. Sixteen heat sinks on most configurations — adequate for moderate energy loads but the all-energy configurations need careful cycling. Configuration S carries six medium pulse lasers, four machine guns, and an AMS. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The medium pulse lasers are accurate at close range. Four machine guns handle infantry and battle armour. The AMS provides missile defence. An active probe is fitted for sensor coverage.
variants.deployment: Configuration S is the urban combat and anti-infantry variant. The active probe finds hidden units in urban terrain. The medium pulse lasers handle armoured opposition. The machine guns deal with infantry. The AMS defends against missile fire in environments where it is prevalent. The combined anti-infantry and probe capability suits MOUT operations.

variants.overview: The Black Hawk OmniMech, known as the Nova in Clan records, is a fifty-ton Clan medium built around a 250-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at fifty tons. The Clan XL carries the standard side torso vulnerability. The jump capability is the consistent tactical feature across all configurations. Clan construction quality throughout. Sixteen heat sinks on most configurations — adequate for moderate energy loads but the all-energy configurations need careful cycling. Configuration E carries an ATM-12 and three ER medium lasers. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The ATM-12 provides three-munition tactical flexibility at heavy missile scale. Three tons of ATM ammunition. The ER mediums handle direct fire backup across close and medium ranges.
variants.deployment: Configuration E is the adaptive missile platform. The ATM-12 munition selection covers extended range, standard, and close-in engagements. Pre-loading the correct type before engagement is the key preparation step. The ER mediums provide reliable direct fire when the ATMs are conserved. Three tons of ammunition manages well across most engagements.

variants.name: H
variants.overview: The Black Hawk OmniMech, known as the Nova in Clan records, is a fifty-ton Clan medium built around a 250-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Sixteen heat sinks on most configurations — adequate for moderate energy loads but the all-energy configurations need careful cycling. Configuration H carries ten heavy medium lasers. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Ten heavy medium lasers hit substantially harder than standard medium lasers at close range. The heat load from ten heavy lasers is extreme — this configuration requires more aggressive cycling than even the Prime.
variants.deployment: Configuration H is the maximum close-range damage variant. Ten heavy medium lasers at point-blank range overwhelms opponents that the Prime's twelve ER mediums would take longer to finish. The heat load is the critical constraint — warriors who fire all ten simultaneously shut down immediately. This configuration rewards pilots who understand their heat curve precisely.

variants.name: F

Walk five, run seven, jump five. The HAG/20 spreads ballistic projectiles across multiple armour locations at medium range. The ER mediums provide direct energy backup. Two tons of HAG ammunition is the operational limit.
variants.deployment: Configuration F delivers HAG/20 spread damage alongside ER medium energy fire. The HAG/20 spread pattern is particularly effective against opponents who have already taken localised damage — the spread finds weak points. The ER mediums handle direct fire between HAG salvos. Two tons of ammunition tracks quickly.

variants.name: U
variants.overview: The Black Hawk OmniMech, known as the Nova in Clan records, is a fifty-ton Clan medium built around a 250-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The jump capability is the consistent tactical feature across all configurations. Clan construction quality throughout. Sixteen heat sinks on most configurations — adequate for moderate energy loads but the all-energy configurations need careful cycling. Configuration U carries three heavy medium lasers, three micro pulse lasers, and eight machine guns. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The heavy medium lasers handle armoured targets. The micro pulse lasers add supplementary close-range fire. Eight machine guns create overwhelming anti-infantry and boarding action coverage.
variants.deployment: Configuration U is built for boarding actions against WarShips and DropShips. The eight machine guns devastate crew and unarmoured personnel. The heavy medium lasers handle armoured bulkheads and security 'Mechs. Jump five provides manoeuvre capability inside large vessels. The micro pulse lasers add close-range precision against individual targets.

variants.name: G
variants.overview: The Black Hawk OmniMech, known as the Nova in Clan records, is a fifty-ton Clan medium built around a 250-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Configuration G carries two improved heavy medium lasers, a ProtoMech AC/8, and seven ER small lasers. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The ProtoMech AC/8 provides ballistic fire from an unusual weapon type. Two tons of AC/8 ammunition. The improved heavy medium lasers add hard-hitting close-range energy fire. Seven ER small lasers cover close-range volume.
variants.deployment: Configuration G is an unusual mixed loadout. The ProtoMech AC/8 provides ballistic capability not found in most Nova configurations. The improved heavy medium lasers add close-range energy punch. Seven ER small lasers create significant close-range volume. The combination is effective against battle armour and lighter 'Mechs.

variants.name: I
variants.overview: The Black Hawk OmniMech, known as the Nova in Clan records, is a fifty-ton Clan medium built around a 250-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Configuration I carries an ER PPC and five improved heavy medium lasers. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The ER PPC handles long-range engagement. The five improved heavy medium lasers deliver close-range firepower. The asymmetric loadout covers both long and close range from separate systems.
variants.deployment: Configuration I uses the ER PPC to engage at range and transitions to the five improved heavy medium lasers as range closes. The heavy medium laser close-range output is substantial. Heat from the full suite at close range requires discipline. Warriors who pace the transition correctly get consistent output across both range bands.

variants.name: J
variants.overview: The Black Hawk, known to Clan warriors as the Nova, is a 50-ton Clan OmniMech with a 250-rated Clan XL engine giving walk five, run seven, and fixed jump five capability. The chassis is notable for twelve fixed double heat sinks built into the torso, which provides a strong thermal foundation for energy-heavy configurations. Clan Blood Spirit developed it and it spread through multiple Clans.
variants.capabilities: The J configuration pairs an ER PPC with a Streak LRM-15 and two tons of missile ammunition. The Streak system only fires when it has a lock, which conserves ammunition but means the warrior cannot fire on uncertain targets. variants.name: BL-6-KNT
variants.overview: The Black Knight BL-6-KNT is a heavy BattleMech with a reputation for being a formidable command platform and front-line combatant. Its advanced communications suite allows it to coordinate company-level operations, while its energy weapons array makes it a force to be reckoned with on the battlefield.
variants.capabilities: The Black Knight's greatest strength lies in its ability to integrate sensor data from its Beagle Active Probe with its energy weapon systems. This allows for exceptional target acquisition and tracking capabilities. However, heat management is a significant concern, as the sheer volume of energy weapons generates heat quickly. MechWarriors must be mindful of their fire discipline to avoid overheating. The design's armor is also noteworthy, providing excellent survivability despite its size.

Introduced in 2578 for the SLDF, this design served as both a devastating front-line combatant and a sophisticated command platform.

The single heat sinks were replaced with sixteen double-strength models, and the targeting computer was upgraded to mate precision fire control to the expanded engagement range.

variants.name: BL-X-KNT 'Red Reaper'
variants.overview: Technicron Manufacturing built the Black Knight in 2578 as a command-capable front-line heavy. Seventy-five tons, walk four, run six. The Beagle active probe and command systems are the design's identity alongside the energy weapons suite. Ten variants have come out of the original formula.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 300-rated XL engine. The BL-X-KNT Red Reaper carries a heavy PPC and five medium X-pulse lasers, with a large vibroblade for close combat. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The heavy PPC handles medium-range direct fire. The X-pulse lasers are accurate at close range. The vibroblade adds physical combat capability.
variants.deployment: The Red Reaper is built for close-range duelling. The vibroblade adds physical attack capability that few seventy-five ton designs can match. The X-pulse lasers are accurate against moving opponents at close range. The heavy PPC handles anything before the machine closes. The XL engine means side torso damage is fatal — the heavy armour compensates somewhat.

variants.name: BLK-NT-2Y
variants.overview: The Black Knight BL-6-KNT is a heavy BattleMech with a reputation for being a formidable command platform and front-line combatant. Its advanced communications suite allows it to coordinate company-level operations, while its energy weapons array makes it a force to be reckoned with on the battlefield.
variants.capabilities: The Black Knight's greatest strength lies in its ability to integrate sensor data from its Beagle Active Probe with its energy weapon systems. This allows for exceptional target acquisition and tracking capabilities. However, heat management is a significant concern, as the sheer volume of energy weapons generates heat quickly. MechWarriors must be mindful of their fire discipline to avoid overheating. The design's armor is also noteworthy, providing excellent survivability despite its size.
variants.deployment: This variant features a Beagle Active Probe, Guardian ECM Suite, and C3 slave unit alongside a targeting computer, emphasizing its traditional command role. A medium shield on the right arm adds protection, while the all-Inner-Sphere weapons suite of PPC, two large lasers, and four medium lasers maintains familiar firepower. Both Kong Interstellar and Robinson Standard BattleWorks produce this variant.

variants.deployment: This variant prioritizes speed over electronic warfare capability, with a larger XL engine pushing its top speed to sixty-four kilometers per hour. Its weapons array features two ER large lasers, four ER medium lasers, two ER small lasers, and a flamer for anti-infantry work. The -3A deliberately omits advanced electronics, relying instead on nineteen double heat sinks and aggressive energy weapon tactics.

Triple-strength myomers compensate for the lighter close-range armament by increasing physical combat capability when heat levels rise. Seventeen double heat sinks manage the thermal output of the dual particle cannons.

It also carries Inner Sphere plasma rifles with three tons of ammunition, providing devastating anti-vehicle and anti-infantry capability. The Angel ECM Suite delivers superior electronic warfare protection, while eighteen double heat sinks manage the considerable heat load.

variants.deployment: The BL-18-KNT mounts an endo-composite frame and Vlar 300 light engine, armed with a full suite of Clan-specification weapons including an ER PPC, two ER large lasers, four ER medium lasers, and a Clan small pulse laser for anti-infantry work. Twenty Clan-built double heat sinks provide improved cooling, and an Inner Sphere targeting computer ties the entire weapons array together for devastating accuracy.

variants.overview: The Black Knight BL-6-KNT is a heavy BattleMech with a reputation for being a formidable command platform and front-line combatant. Its advanced communications suite allows it to coordinate company-level operations, while its energy weapons array makes it a force to be reckoned with on the battlefield.

variants.deployment: The -5H variant mounts a powerful all-Clan weapons suite featuring a Clan ER PPC, two Clan ER large lasers, and multiple smaller energy and pulse lasers. Its Vlar 300 light engine drives the design at fifty-four kilometers per hour, while seventeen double heat sinks struggle to contain the massive thermal output. The Rander Comm-Marshal communications system and Rander Dragonslayer targeting and tracking system with an advanced targeting computer provide exceptional fire control.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Black Lanner is a 55-ton Clan OmniMech built by Clan Jade Falcon around a 385-rated Clan XL engine. Walk seven, run ten, with MASC providing burst speed higher still. That is exceptional for a heavy-medium and it costs: the engine consumes close to half the design's total mass, which compresses pod space severely. The JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armour keep protection reasonable within what remains.
variants.capabilities: The A configuration carries an ER PPC, two medium pulse lasers, and TAG, with an active probe, ECM suite, and the electronics package that defines this variant. Walk seven, run ten at fifty-five tons. The firepower is modest for the weight but the A configuration is an intelligence and designation platform first. The ECM disrupts enemy sensor networks while the active probe finds targets for the TAG to designate.
variants.deployment: The A configuration is built for mixed formations that include artillery or aerospace assets. The TAG designation capability multiplies the value of those assets substantially. Warriors in this configuration need to understand they are not the main effort; they are enabling the main effort. The speed to stay out of trouble and the electronics to do the job are the whole point.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: The Black Lanner is a 55-ton Clan OmniMech built by Clan Jade Falcon around a 385-rated Clan XL engine. Walk seven, run ten, with MASC providing burst speed higher still. That is exceptional for a heavy-medium and it costs: the engine consumes close to half the design's total mass, which compresses pod space severely. The JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armour keep protection reasonable within what remains.
variants.capabilities: The B configuration carries nothing but twin LRM-20s with two tons of ammunition each. No backup weapons. At walk seven, run ten, the speed is the defence. The LRM-20s deliver sustained missile fire from range but when the ammunition runs dry the machine has no combat capability left at all. Falcon commanders pair B variants with faster escorts that can screen them from opponents who close the distance.
variants.deployment: The B configuration is a pure fire support platform. The speed means it can stay at range against most opponents but that is not guaranteed. Two tons each of LRM-20 ammunition is the operational endurance limit, not a generous supply on an active battlefield. Warriors assigned B configuration understand the job: deliver missile fire from range and trust the escorts.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: The Black Lanner is a 55-ton Clan OmniMech built by Clan Jade Falcon around a 385-rated Clan XL engine. Walk seven, run ten, with MASC providing burst speed higher still. That is exceptional for a heavy-medium and it costs: the engine consumes close to half the design's total mass, which compresses pod space severely. The JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armour keep protection reasonable within what remains.
variants.capabilities: The C configuration packs six ER medium lasers and a Streak SRM-6 with one ton of ammunition. Three extra double heat sinks help manage the thermal load from the full laser array. Firing all six ER mediums simultaneously is hot enough to require careful management. The Streak ensures every SRM round finds its target when the lock is established, which conserves the single ammunition ton.
variants.deployment: The C configuration uses Black Lanner speed to run down lighter opponents that cannot match walk seven. The six ER mediums delivered at close range is a significant fire concentration. Against heavier targets, the speed creates engagement opportunities that slower assault 'Mechs cannot prevent. The Streak ammunition is gone fast in sustained close-range work, after which the six lasers carry on independently.

variants.name: D
variants.overview: The Black Lanner is a 55-ton Clan OmniMech built by Clan Jade Falcon around a 385-rated Clan XL engine. Walk seven, run ten, with MASC providing burst speed higher still. That is exceptional for a heavy-medium and it costs: the engine consumes close to half the design's total mass, which compresses pod space severely. The JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armour keep protection reasonable within what remains.
variants.capabilities: The D configuration is an anti-infantry and urban operations loadout: two medium pulse lasers, two ER small lasers, four machine guns, two SRM-6 launchers, and a flamer. It is the most eclectic configuration in the Black Lanner family and the most demanding to maintain because of the weapon type diversity. Four machine guns on a 55-ton machine requires ammunition management for a calibre most Clan techs do not service regularly.
variants.deployment: The D configuration deploys in garrison and security operations where conventional infantry, vehicles, and light armour are the primary threat mix. It is poorly suited to facing other BattleMechs at anything above company weight. Warriors assigned D configuration are doing security work, not front-line combat, and the loadout reflects that. The flamer and machine guns make it genuinely effective in the role it was built for.

variants.name: Prime
variants.overview: The Black Lanner is a 55-ton Clan OmniMech built by Clan Jade Falcon around a 385-rated Clan XL engine. Walk seven, run ten, with MASC providing burst speed higher still. That is exceptional for a heavy-medium and it costs: the engine consumes close to half the design's total mass, which compresses pod space severely. The JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armour keep protection reasonable within what remains.
variants.capabilities: The Prime carries an ER large laser, LRM-10, two ER medium lasers, an SRM-6, and an ECM suite. It covers long range, medium range, and close range from a single configuration. The ECM provides formation protection. The trade-off is that none of the individual weapon systems is exceptional; the Prime is a generalist. One ton each of LRM and SRM ammunition requires careful tracking on extended operations.
variants.deployment: The Prime is the standard deployment configuration and the one most Clan techs will work on most often. It operates ahead of heavier formations, using the ECM to degrade enemy targeting while the ER large laser and LRM-10 engage at range. The SRM-6 handles anything that closes. It is not the most effective configuration for any single scenario but it handles most scenarios adequately.

variants.name: H
variants.overview: The Black Lanner is a 55-ton Clan OmniMech built by Clan Jade Falcon around a 385-rated Clan XL engine. Walk seven, run ten, with MASC providing burst speed higher still. That is exceptional for a heavy-medium and it costs: the engine consumes close to half the design's total mass, which compresses pod space severely. The JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armour keep protection reasonable within what remains.
variants.capabilities: The H configuration carries a heavy large laser and two medium pulse lasers with an ECM suite and four extra double heat sinks. The heavy large laser does substantial damage at medium range but generates heat that the standard configuration's heat sinks struggle with, hence the four additional units. The medium pulse lasers are accurate and effective at closer range.
variants.deployment: The H configuration is a medium-range engagement variant that uses the heavy large laser as its primary tool. The ECM suite maintains the reconnaissance and protection role from the Prime. Four extra heat sinks are an unusual accommodation and they tell you something about how hot this configuration runs under combat conditions. Warriors in H configuration need to respect the heavy laser heat penalty.

variants.name: E
variants.overview: The Black Lanner is a 55-ton Clan OmniMech built by Clan Jade Falcon around a 385-rated Clan XL engine. Walk seven, run ten, with MASC providing burst speed higher still. That is exceptional for a heavy-medium and it costs: the engine consumes close to half the design's total mass, which compresses pod space severely. The JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armour keep protection reasonable within what remains.
variants.capabilities: The E configuration mounts an ATM-12 with three tons of ammunition and three ER medium lasers. The ATM-12 is the largest ATM system in the Lanner family and three tons of ammunition allows genuine tactical flexibility between standard, extended-range, and high-explosive rounds. The three ER mediums provide energy backup when the ATM ammunition is expended.
variants.deployment: The E configuration is an adaptable fire support variant. Pre-loading the correct ATM munition type for the expected mission profile is the key planning task before deployment. Warriors who carry a mixed load of all three types and switch based on engagement range get the most from the ATM system. Three tons is enough for a full engagement if the warrior is not wasteful.

variants.name: X
variants.overview: The Black Lanner is a 55-ton Clan OmniMech built by Clan Jade Falcon around a 385-rated Clan XL engine. Walk seven, run ten, with MASC providing burst speed higher still. That is exceptional for a heavy-medium and it costs: the engine consumes close to half the design's total mass, which compresses pod space severely. The JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armour keep protection reasonable within what remains.
variants.capabilities: The X configuration is an experimental variant carrying a rotary AC/2 in the right arm and two improved heavy medium lasers in the left, with CASE II protecting the ammunition bay in both side torsos. The rotary AC/2 delivers rapid ballistic salvos at medium to long range. The improved heavy medium lasers hit harder than standard mediums but generate more heat. The combination is unusual and the maintenance complexity reflects that.
variants.deployment: The X designation indicates experimental and the logistics reflect it. The rotary AC/2 requires ammunition management and the improved heavy medium laser heat output pushes heat sinks hard. CASE II in both torsos is appropriate given the mixed ammunition and energy weapon thermal loads. Units operating this configuration need techs comfortable with experimental system protocols.

variants.name: F
variants.overview: The Black Lanner is a 55-ton Clan OmniMech built by Clan Jade Falcon around a 385-rated Clan XL engine. Walk seven, run ten, with MASC providing burst speed higher still. The engine consumes close to half the design's total mass, which compresses pod space severely. The JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armour keep protection reasonable within what remains.
variants.capabilities: The F configuration carries five medium pulse lasers in the right arm and two light machine gun arrays each holding three light machine guns in the left arm, with a light active probe rounding out the fit. The pulse lasers provide accurate fire in running engagements at walk seven speeds. The machine gun arrays are devastatingly effective against infantry and battle armour from a single half-ton ammunition bin. The light active probe extends detection range without consuming significant pod space.
variants.deployment: The F configuration is a dedicated scout and anti-infantry variant. The machine gun arrays make it genuinely dangerous to conventional infantry formations in ways that most OmniMech configurations are not. The speed and light active probe make it effective at finding things and reporting back. Warriors assigned F configuration are doing reconnaissance and security work, not heavy combat.

variants.name: G
variants.overview: The Black Lanner is a 55-ton Clan OmniMech built by Clan Jade Falcon around a 385-rated Clan XL engine. Walk seven, run ten, with MASC providing burst speed higher still. The engine consumes close to half the design's total mass, which compresses pod space severely. The JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armour keep protection reasonable within what remains.
variants.capabilities: The G configuration distributes four LRM-5 launchers across both arms and side torsos, fed by two tons of ammunition, with an ER large pulse laser in the right arm for direct fire support. The four LRM-5s can engage multiple targets or concentrate on one. The ER large pulse laser is accurate at range and generates less heat than a standard ER large laser. Two tons of LRM ammunition across four launchers runs dry faster than pilots expect on active operations.
variants.deployment: The G configuration uses Black Lanner speed to maintain range and deliver sustained missile fire. The ER large pulse laser handles direct fire when the missiles are out. Four LRM-5s deliver modest individual salvos but the distributed mounting makes losing any single arm a less catastrophic event than a single large launcher configuration. This is a fire support variant that relies on speed for survival.

variants.name: T
variants.overview: The Black Lanner is a 55-ton Clan OmniMech built by Clan Jade Falcon around a 385-rated Clan XL engine. Walk seven, run ten, with MASC providing burst speed higher still. The engine consumes close to half the design's total mass, which compresses pod space severely. The JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armour keep protection reasonable within what remains.
variants.capabilities: The T configuration carries a plasma cannon with two tons of ammunition, two improved heavy medium lasers, an SRM-6, and an LRM-10. The plasma cannon is the unusual element: it overheats enemy 'Mechs while dealing direct damage, which is a genuine tactical disruption tool against heat-sensitive opponents. The improved heavy medium lasers hit hard at close range but run hot. This is one of the hotter Lanner configurations and the warrior needs to account for that.
variants.deployment: The T configuration proved effective during the fighting on Coventry in 3148, where the plasma cannon's ability to degrade enemy heat management created tactical openings for heavier Clan units following behind. The mixed weapons suite handles multiple engagement ranges. The plasma cannon ammunition requires dedicated supply management separate from the SRM and LRM rounds.

variants.name: I
variants.overview: The Black Lanner is a 55-ton Clan OmniMech built by Clan Jade Falcon around a 385-rated Clan XL engine. Walk seven, run ten, with MASC providing burst speed higher still. The engine consumes close to half the design's total mass, which compresses pod space severely. The JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armour keep protection reasonable within what remains.
variants.capabilities: The I configuration carries a medium VSP laser in the right arm, two ER medium lasers in the left, three heavy machine guns in the right torso, and a Streak SRM-4 in the left torso, with a targeting computer linking all weapons. The VSP laser adapts its damage profile to range, which suits the variable engagement distances that Black Lanner speed creates. The targeting computer improves accuracy across the whole weapons suite. Heavy machine gun ammunition requires its own supply logistics.
variants.deployment: The I configuration is a precision skirmisher built for warriors who prefer calculated engagements over volume of fire. The targeting computer rewards disciplined shooting. The Streak SRM-4 fires only when it has a lock, conserving ammunition but guaranteeing every round hits. Three heavy machine guns provide anti-infantry capability that complements the anti-armour weapons.

variants.name: J
variants.overview: The Black Lanner is a 55-ton Clan OmniMech built by Clan Jade Falcon around a 385-rated Clan XL engine. Walk seven, run ten, with MASC providing burst speed higher still. The engine consumes close to half the design's total mass, which compresses pod space severely. The JF 5 Light Endo Steel chassis and Compound JF Ferro-Fibrous armour keep protection reasonable within what remains.
variants.capabilities: The J configuration carries a ProtoMech AC/8 in the right arm and three ER medium lasers in the left, with an engine supercharger enabling sprint speeds approaching 180 kilometres per hour. The supercharger provides emergency speed capability beyond the already impressive standard pace. The ProtoMech AC/8 delivers reliable ballistic fire with reasonable ammunition efficiency. The ER mediums provide sustained energy backup.
variants.deployment: The J configuration is built around speed as the primary tactical tool. The supercharger allows the warrior to close distance or break contact faster than almost any opponent can anticipate. The weapons suite is capable rather than exceptional, but at those speeds the warrior chooses every engagement on their own terms. The supercharger has its own maintenance requirements and pilots who use it heavily will accelerate wear on the drivetrain.

variants.name: BKW-7R
variants.overview: Cosara Weaponries built the Black Watch in 3061 on Northwind, sharing the Crockett chassis. Eighty-five tons, walk three, run four, jump three on the standard 255-rated engine. Jump three on an eighty-five ton assault with heavy ballistic weapons makes this a genuine terrain exploitation platform.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three at eighty-five tons. Standard engine — side torso survivability. Jump three on this weight class allows positioning options that ground-bound assaults cannot access. The mixed ballistic and missile weapons cover multiple engagement ranges. Originally allocated exclusively to the Northwind Highlanders. The BKW-7R carries a light Gauss rifle, an Ultra AC/10, and an MRM-40. Walk three, run four, jump three. The light Gauss provides long-range accurate fire. The UAC/10 handles medium-range ballistic work. The MRM-40 delivers heavy medium-range missile volume. CASE-protected ammunition throughout.
variants.deployment: The BKW-7R is the original production model exclusively allocated to the Northwind Highlanders. The light Gauss at range, UAC/10 at medium, and MRM-40 for missile saturation cover the full engagement spectrum. Jump three allows terrain exploitation that makes the static fire support role more mobile than comparable assault designs.

variants.name: BKW-9R
variants.overview: Cosara Weaponries built the Black Watch in 3061 on Northwind sharing the Crockett chassis. Eighty-five tons, walk three, run four, jump three on the standard 255-rated engine. Jump three on an eighty-five ton assault is a genuine positioning tool.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three at eighty-five tons. Standard engine — side torso survivability. The BKW-9R carries a Gauss rifle, a heavy PPC, two MML-7s, and a TAG system. The Gauss provides accurate long-range fire. The heavy PPC hits hard at medium range. The MML-7s cover both SRM and LRM ranges. The TAG designates for guided munitions.
variants.deployment: The 9R emerged as a field refit among expatriate Highlanders on Galatea after the Jihad severed supply lines to Northwind. Available components drove the weapons choices. The Gauss and heavy PPC cover direct fire. The TAG adds force multiplier value with artillery support. MML-7 flexibility covers both missile range bands.

variants.name: BJ-1X
variants.overview: GM built the Blackjack in 2757 under SLDF contract as a forty-five ton fire support and anti-insurgency medium. Walk four, run six, jump four on the 180-rated engine. Twenty-one variants emerged from that original contract, many of them OmniMech configurations following the 3050s conversion. The original AC/2 design philosophy — harassment at range — runs through the family.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four across most variants on the standard engine. The conventional variants use a 180-rated engine while the OmniMech conversion uses a 200-rated XL. The jump capability is the consistent tactical feature across all Blackjack configurations. XL engine adds vulnerability on OmniMech variants. The BJ-1X is the prototype, carrying four medium lasers and four flamers on the 225-rated engine. Walk five, run seven — faster than the production model. The prototype used flamers instead of autocannons and a larger engine. No jump capability.
variants.deployment: The 1X is the prototype configuration that preceded the production BJ-1. The flamer loadout was replaced by autocannons in production. Walk five and no jump distinguishes it from the production standard. Prototype documentation applies for maintenance.

variants.name: BJ-1
variants.overview: GM built the Blackjack in 2757 under SLDF contract as a forty-five ton fire support and anti-insurgency medium. Walk four, run six, jump four on the 180-rated engine. Twenty-one variants emerged from that original contract, many of them OmniMech configurations following the 3050s conversion. The original AC/2 design philosophy — harassment at range — runs through the family.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four across most variants on the standard engine. The conventional variants use a 180-rated engine while the OmniMech conversion uses a 200-rated XL. The jump capability is the consistent tactical feature across all Blackjack configurations. XL engine adds vulnerability on OmniMech variants. The BJ-1 is the SLDF production model: twin Whirlwind-L AC/2s, four Intek medium lasers, and jump four on the 180-rated engine. Walk four, run six, jump four. The AC/2s provide long-range harassment fire. The four medium lasers handle closer engagement. Standard engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The BJ-1 entered service in 2757 and established the Blackjack's fire support identity. The AC/2 harassment at range combined with medium laser close-range capability covers the standard medium 'Mech engagement profile. Jump four is genuinely useful for positioning. Parts availability through most supply chains is good given the production run.

variants.name: BJ-1DB
variants.overview: GM built the Blackjack in 2757 under SLDF contract as a forty-five ton fire support and anti-insurgency medium. Walk four, run six, jump four on the 180-rated engine. Twenty-one variants emerged from that original contract, many of them OmniMech configurations following the 3050s conversion. The original AC/2 design philosophy — harassment at range — runs through the family.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four across most variants on the standard engine. The conventional variants use a 180-rated engine while the OmniMech conversion uses a 200-rated XL. The jump capability is the consistent tactical feature across all Blackjack configurations. XL engine adds vulnerability on OmniMech variants. The BJ-1DB replaces the AC/2s with two large lasers and keeps two medium lasers, adding six additional heat sinks. Walk four, run six, jump four. The large lasers extend direct fire range beyond the standard medium lasers. The additional heat sinks manage the increased energy load. One ton of armour traded for the heat sinks.
variants.deployment: The 1DB trades the AC/2 harassment concept for large laser direct fire range. The heat sink addition makes the two large lasers sustainable. The armour reduction is minor. Jump four is preserved. This variant sees use by units that wanted better direct fire range from the Blackjack chassis.

variants.name: BJ-1DC
variants.overview: GM built the Blackjack in 2757 under SLDF contract as a forty-five ton fire support and anti-insurgency medium. Walk four, run six, jump four on the 180-rated engine. Twenty-one variants emerged from that original contract, many of them OmniMech configurations following the 3050s conversion. The original AC/2 design philosophy — harassment at range — runs through the family.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four across most variants on the standard engine. The conventional variants use a 180-rated engine while the OmniMech conversion uses a 200-rated XL. The jump capability is the consistent tactical feature across all Blackjack configurations. XL engine adds vulnerability on OmniMech variants. The BJ-1DC removes the jump jets entirely to mount two additional small lasers and an extra heat sink alongside the standard AC/2s and four medium lasers. Walk four, run six, no jump. Six energy weapons total.
variants.deployment: The 1DC sacrifices jump capability for additional firepower and heat management. The two small lasers add modest close-range volume. No jump jets changes the tactical profile significantly for a chassis built around jump capability. Units in terrain where jump would see limited use found this tradeoff worthwhile.

variants.name: BJ-3
variants.overview: GM built the Blackjack in 2757 under SLDF contract as a forty-five ton fire support and anti-insurgency medium. Walk four, run six, jump four on the 180-rated engine. Twenty-one variants emerged from that original contract, many of them OmniMech configurations following the 3050s conversion. The original AC/2 design philosophy — harassment at range — runs through the family.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four across most variants on the standard engine. The conventional variants use a 180-rated engine while the OmniMech conversion uses a 200-rated XL. The jump capability is the consistent tactical feature across all Blackjack configurations. XL engine adds vulnerability on OmniMech variants. The BJ-3 carries two PPCs and four medium lasers with double heat sinks as standard — the major upgrade of the Clan Invasion era. Walk four, run six, jump four.
