The B3-HND carries two medium pulse lasers, four ER flamers, a fluid gun, and a B-pod. Walk seven, run ten. The ER flamers and fluid gun handle infantry and soft targets. The B-pod provides area-effect anti-battle-armour defence. The medium pulse lasers handle armoured opponents.
variants.deployment: The B3-HND is the dedicated anti-infantry variant. The ER flamers and fluid gun are far more effective against infantry formations than the energy weapons of the B1 and B2. The B-pod deters battle armour that tries to swarm the machine. The medium pulse lasers handle any armoured opposition. Walk seven delivers this suite to contact quickly.

variants.name: BLF-21
variants.overview: The Blue Flame is a forty-five ton quadrupedal BattleMech built for the Word of Blake Militia. Walk five, run seven on the 225-rated light engine. The quad configuration provides firing stability. Light engine — side torso survivability. C3i networking is a fixed fitting across all variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at forty-five tons on the light engine. The light engine survives side torso hits. The quad chassis provides stable firing at walk five. C3i networking integrates targeting data across the formation. Parts availability outside Word of Blake remnant forces is limited. The BLF-21 carries two ER large lasers and three Streak SRM-2s. Walk five, run seven. The ER large lasers provide the primary long-range direct fire. The Streak SRM-2s add guaranteed close-range missile hits on lock. The C3i network integrates targeting data across the formation.
variants.deployment: The base BLF-21 deployed in Word of Blake Militia networked lances. The ER large laser range combined with C3i network targeting made each machine more accurate than it would be in isolation. The Streak SRM-2s handle close engagement. The light engine keeps it alive under fire that would kill XL competitors.

variants.name: BLF-40
variants.overview: The Blue Flame is a forty-five ton quadrupedal BattleMech built for the Word of Blake Militia. Walk five, run seven on the 225-rated light engine. The quad configuration provides firing stability. Light engine — side torso survivability. C3i networking is a fixed fitting across all variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at forty-five tons on the light engine. The light engine survives side torso hits. The quad chassis provides stable firing at walk five. C3i networking integrates targeting data across the formation. Parts availability outside Word of Blake remnant forces is limited. The BLF-40 carries three light PPCs and a medium VSP laser. Walk five, run seven. The light PPCs provide accurate short-to-medium range energy fire. The VSP laser adapts its damage profile to engagement range. All-energy with no ammunition. C3i networking is fixed.
variants.deployment: The BLF-40 was introduced during the Jihad height in 3073. The light PPCs and VSP laser provide consistent energy fire across the engagement ranges the Blue Flame typically fights at. No ammunition dependency simplifies logistics in the Jihad operational environment. The light engine and quad stability are the chassis constants.

variants.name: BMB-010
variants.overview: Pinard Protectorates Limited built the Bombard in 3053 as a fifty-ton Solaris VII arena machine. Walk two, run three on the 100-rated XL engine — deliberately underpowered to put all the weight into firepower. Arena rules favour heavy weapons over mobility. Four variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three at fifty tons. The minimal engine is the defining design choice — everything that could go into speed went into weapons instead. XL engine — side torso vulnerability, though at walk two the risk of being flanked is permanent regardless. Arena combat doctrine applies. The BMB-010 is the original arena configuration: two AC/20s as the sole weapons. Walk two, run three on the XL engine. Two AC/20s simultaneously at close range is the single most devastating weapons combination at this weight class. Six tons of CASE-protected ammunition.
variants.deployment: The BMB-010 was the original concept: two AC/20s on a machine that walks to firing position and stays there. Any opponent within close range takes both AC/20s in the face. The walk-two limitation means opponents dictate whether they close the distance. At Solaris VII where the arena controlled the engagement range, this worked. Six tons of CASE ammunition kept the machine alive when hits landed near the bays.

variants.name: BMB-013
variants.overview: Pinard Protectorates Limited built the Bombard in 3053 as a fifty-ton Solaris VII arena machine. Walk two, run three on the 100-rated XL engine — deliberately underpowered to put all the weight into firepower. Arena rules favour heavy weapons over mobility. Four variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three at fifty tons. The minimal engine is the defining design choice — everything that could go into speed went into weapons instead. XL engine — side torso vulnerability, though at walk two the risk of being flanked is permanent regardless. Arena combat doctrine applies. The BMB-013 is the redesigned production model: two Thunderbolt-15 launchers and two ER medium lasers replacing the autocannons. Walk two, run three. The Thunderbolt-15 guided missiles hit with better accuracy than standard LRMs. Six tons of CASE-protected ammunition. Standard heat sinks replaced the problematic early units.
variants.deployment: The BMB-013 addresses the heat sink problems of the original while switching from short-range AC/20 devastation to medium-range Thunderbolt guided fire. The guided missiles work at ranges the walk-two engine can never close to for the AC/20 concept. The ER mediums handle direct threats at close range.

variants.name: BMB-1X
variants.overview: Pinard Protectorates Limited built the Bombard in 3053 as a fifty-ton Solaris VII arena machine. Walk two, run three on the 100-rated XL engine — deliberately underpowered to put all the weight into firepower. Arena rules favour heavy weapons over mobility. Four variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 200-rated IS XXL engine. The BMB-1X carries two Clan-specification Gauss rifles and three M-pods. The XXL engine enables walk four at fifty tons — substantial improvement over the 100-rated base variants. The Gauss rifles provide accurate long-range fire. M-pods protect against battle armour at close range.
variants.deployment: The BMB-1X is a special commission variant that fundamentally changes the design by using an XXL engine for walk four. This machine actually moves. The Clan Gauss rifles provide accurate fire at ranges the walk-two variants could never operate at. M-pods handle battle armour threats. Mixed Clan and IS components require two-track maintenance.

variants.name: BMB-016
variants.overview: Pinard Protectorates Limited built the Bombard in 3053 as a fifty-ton Solaris VII arena machine. Walk two, run three on the 100-rated XL engine — deliberately underpowered to put all the weight into firepower. Arena rules favour heavy weapons over mobility. Four variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three at fifty tons. The minimal engine is the defining design choice — everything that could go into speed went into weapons instead. XL engine — side torso vulnerability, though at walk two the risk of being flanked is permanent regardless. Arena combat doctrine applies. The BMB-016 is a field refit using salvaged components from Hornet production: two light Gauss rifles and two medium lasers on the 100-rated XL engine. Walk two, run three. The light Gauss rifles are more ammunition-efficient than the Thunderbolt launchers at reduced close-range impact.
variants.deployment: The BMB-016 was assembled from Filtvelt Coalition salvage — Hornet production components fitted into Bombard frames. The light Gauss rifles work at ranges the walk-two engine makes difficult to exploit. The medium lasers handle close-range threats. A field refit born of component availability rather than tactical design.

variants.name: BMB-12D
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Bombardier in 2681 as a sixty-five ton LRM platform for the SLDF. Walk five, run seven on the XL engine. Twin LRM-20s with diverse munition capability are the design identity. Five variants. The standard deployment is fire support from stand-off range.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The twin LRM-20 launchers are the whole point. Ammunition management across two heavy launchers is the consistent operational concern. The diverse munition capability was the design's selling point — the same launcher handles inferno, mine, smoke, and standard rounds. The BMB-12D carries twin LRM-20s, an SRM-4, and an AMS on the 325-rated XL engine. Walk five, run seven. The Delphinius-20 launchers deliver twelve salvos before resupply. The AMS provides missile defence against counter-battery fire. The SRM-4 handles anything that closes inside LRM minimum range.
variants.deployment: The BMB-12D is the full-technology Bombardier with XL engine speed and AMS protection. Walk five allows repositioning between salvos in ways the slower 10D cannot manage. The AMS defends against the counter-battery missile fire that stationary fire support platforms attract. The XL engine is the survivability tradeoff.

variants.name: BMB-10D
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Bombardier in 2681 as a sixty-five ton LRM platform for the SLDF. Walk five, run seven on the XL engine. Twin LRM-20s with diverse munition capability are the design identity. Five variants. The standard deployment is fire support from stand-off range.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The twin LRM-20 launchers are the whole point. Ammunition management across two heavy launchers is the consistent operational concern. The diverse munition capability was the design's selling point — the same launcher handles inferno, mine, smoke, and standard rounds. The BMB-10D carries twin LRM-20s, an SRM-4, and a machine gun on the standard 260-rated engine. Walk four, run six. The slower standard engine compensates with side torso survivability. The machine gun handles infantry threats.
variants.deployment: The 10D saw primary service with FWL and DCMS militia units while the Federated Commonwealth used theirs for training. The standard engine survivability is the practical advantage over the 12D for militia formations that expect to absorb hits. Walk four is slower but the engine survives damage that ends the 12D. The machine gun handles infantry that closes on fire support positions.

variants.name: BMB-14C
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Bombardier in 2681 as a sixty-five ton LRM platform for the SLDF. Walk five, run seven on the XL engine. Twin LRM-20s with diverse munition capability are the design identity. Five variants. The standard deployment is fire support from stand-off range.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The twin LRM-20 launchers are the whole point. Ammunition management across two heavy launchers is the consistent operational concern. The diverse munition capability was the design's selling point — the same launcher handles inferno, mine, smoke, and standard rounds. The BMB-14C uses an XL engine and endo steel chassis upgrade, carrying twin Artemis IV-guided LRM-20s and an ER small laser. Walk five, run seven. The Artemis IV guidance improves LRM grouping substantially. The endo steel frees tonnage for improved ammunition endurance. The ER small laser handles point-blank threats.
variants.deployment: The 14C is the accuracy-focused upgrade. Artemis IV on both LRM-20 launchers makes every salvo count more than unguided fire. The endo steel chassis reduces structural mass for better ammunition endurance. The ER small laser deters anything that closes. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: BMB-05A
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Bombardier in 2681 as a sixty-five ton LRM platform for the SLDF. Walk five, run seven on the XL engine. Twin LRM-20s with diverse munition capability are the design identity. Five variants. The standard deployment is fire support from stand-off range.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The twin LRM-20 launchers are the whole point. The diverse munition capability was the design's selling point — the same launcher handles inferno, mine, smoke, and standard rounds. The BMB-05A uses an XL engine and carries an Arrow IV artillery launcher, three one-shot Rocket Launcher-20s, a small laser, and an AMS. Walk five, run seven. The Arrow IV provides extreme-range artillery capability. The three RL-20s are one-shot weapons providing a single combined forty-round alpha strike. The AMS defends against counter-battery fire.
variants.deployment: The 05A is the artillery Bombardier. The Arrow IV reaches ranges that dwarf standard LRM capability. The three RL-20 one-shot launchers provide a single massive alpha strike opportunity before the machine reverts to Arrow IV only. AMS defends during the approach and fire mission. Arrow IV ammunition supply requires dedicated logistics separate from standard LRM chains.

variants.name: BMB-14K
variants.overview: Johnston Industries built the Bombardier in 2681 as a sixty-five ton LRM platform for the SLDF. Walk five, run seven on the XL engine. Twin LRM-20s with diverse munition capability are the design identity. Five variants. The standard deployment is fire support from stand-off range.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The twin LRM-20 launchers are the whole point. The BMB-14K uses an XL engine and carries four MML-7 launchers, three machine guns, and a machine gun array. Walk five, run seven. The four MML-7s cover both SRM and LRM range bands. The machine guns and array handle infantry threats comprehensively.
variants.deployment: The 14K was introduced by the Draconis Combine, refitting mothballed BMB-10D and BMB-12D frames at Wakazashi Enterprises. The MML-7 flexibility allows the same launcher to cover both fire support and close engagement depending on mode. The machine gun array and individual guns handle infantry that approaches fire support positions. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Boreas is a sixty-ton Clan Hell's Horses experimental OmniQuadVee — the first QuadVee prototype. Walk four, run six on the 240-rated Clan engine. The QuadVee configuration converts between 'Mech and vehicle mode. Five configurations explore the concept's tactical range.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at sixty tons. The QuadVee conversion between 'Mech and wheeled vehicle mode is the chassis's defining capability. Clan engine — standard Clan maintenance requirements. As the first prototype, documentation is thinner than for production designs. Pod space is modest. Configuration A strips the Boreas to a single HAG/20 with two tons of ammunition. Walk four, run six in 'Mech mode; wheeled vehicle mode for road movement. The HAG/20 delivers ballistic spread damage across multiple armour locations. Two tons of ammunition is the operational limit in this configuration.
variants.deployment: Configuration A concentrates all available mass on the HAG/20. The QuadVee conversion provides tactical mobility variety between combat positions. The single weapon makes ammunition management straightforward. Two tons runs out — the vehicle mode allows withdrawal to resupply efficiently.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: The Boreas is a sixty-ton Clan Hell's Horses experimental OmniQuadVee — the first QuadVee prototype. Walk four, run six on the 240-rated Clan engine. The QuadVee configuration converts between 'Mech and vehicle mode. Five configurations explore the concept's tactical range.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at sixty tons. The QuadVee conversion between 'Mech and wheeled vehicle mode is the chassis's defining capability. Clan engine — standard Clan maintenance requirements. As the first prototype, documentation is thinner than for production designs. Pod space is modest. Configuration B carries a Streak LRM-20 as its sole weapon. Walk four, run six. The Streak LRM-20 fires only on lock, guaranteeing every salvo hits. Two tons of Streak ammunition. The QuadVee conversion provides movement mode flexibility.
variants.deployment: Configuration B is the fire support Boreas. The Streak LRM-20 guarantee of hitting makes every round count. Two tons of Streak ammunition is limited for sustained fire support missions. The vehicle mode allows road-speed movement between fire positions. As with Configuration A, the single-weapon design simplifies but constrains tactical options.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: The Boreas is a sixty-ton Clan Hell's Horses experimental OmniQuadVee — the first QuadVee prototype. Walk four, run six on the 240-rated Clan engine. The QuadVee configuration converts between 'Mech and vehicle mode. Five configurations explore the concept's tactical range.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at sixty tons. The QuadVee conversion between 'Mech and wheeled vehicle mode is the chassis's defining capability. Clan engine — standard Clan maintenance requirements. As the first prototype, documentation is thinner than for production designs. Pod space is modest. Configuration C carries an ATM-12 and two ER medium lasers. Walk four, run six. The ATM-12 provides three-munition tactical flexibility. Three tons of ATM ammunition. The ER mediums provide direct energy fire backup.
variants.deployment: Configuration C is the flexible engagement platform. ATM-12 munition selection covers three range bands from the same launcher. Pre-loading the correct munition type before engagement improves effectiveness. The ER mediums handle direct combat between ATM salvos. The QuadVee conversion provides movement flexibility.

variants.name: D
variants.overview: The Boreas is a sixty-ton Clan Hell's Horses experimental OmniQuadVee — the first QuadVee prototype. Walk four, run six on the 240-rated Clan engine. The QuadVee configuration converts between 'Mech and vehicle mode. Five configurations explore the concept's tactical range.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at sixty tons. The QuadVee conversion between 'Mech and wheeled vehicle mode is the chassis's defining capability. Clan engine — standard Clan maintenance requirements. As the first prototype, documentation is thinner than for production designs. Pod space is modest. Configuration D carries two heavy large lasers. Walk four, run six. No ammunition dependency. The heavy large lasers hit harder than standard large lasers at medium range. Additional laser heat sinks manage the considerable heat. The QuadVee conversion provides movement mode options.
variants.deployment: Configuration D is the all-energy sustained fire platform. The heavy large lasers deliver consistent output without ammunition concern. The additional heat sinks allow sustained firing at a rate standard heavy large laser configurations cannot maintain. The vehicle mode allows rapid repositioning between energy fire positions.

variants.name: Prime
variants.overview: The Boreas is a sixty-ton Clan Hell's Horses experimental OmniQuadVee — the first QuadVee prototype. Walk four, run six on the 240-rated Clan engine. The QuadVee configuration converts between 'Mech and vehicle mode. Five configurations explore the concept's tactical range.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at sixty tons. The QuadVee conversion between 'Mech and wheeled vehicle mode is the chassis's defining capability. Clan engine — standard Clan maintenance requirements. As the first prototype, documentation is thinner than for production designs. Pod space is modest. The Prime carries an ER PPC, a medium pulse laser, and a Streak SRM-6. Walk four, run six. The ER PPC handles long-range direct fire. The medium pulse laser covers medium-range engagement accurately. The Streak SRM-6 adds guaranteed close-range missile hits on lock.
variants.deployment: The Prime is the baseline combat configuration. The ER PPC and pulse laser combination covers long and medium range. The Streak SRM-6 closes the engagement at short range. The QuadVee conversion allows road movement between combat positions. The Clan standard engine provides survivability.

variants.overview: The Bowman is a seventy-ton Clan heavy designed as an artillery platform, built around Arrow IV systems on a 350-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. The Arrow IV concept was controversial within the Clans because the direct-fire tradition disfavoured artillery. Three variants emerged as the design evolved.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy tons. The Clan XL carries the standard side torso vulnerability. Endo steel structure. The Arrow IV is battlefield artillery — range and impact that direct fire weapons cannot match. Arrow IV ammunition requires dedicated supply separate from standard weapon logistics. Variant 4 is the original 2923 configuration: two Arrow IV artillery systems as the only weapons. Walk five, run seven on the XL engine. Two Arrow IV launchers provide extreme-range artillery capability. Anti-personnel pods in the feet handle anything that closes. Arrow IV ammunition is the primary logistics requirement.
variants.deployment: Variant 4 is the purest expression of the Bowman concept. Two Arrow IV systems at seventy tons of mobility delivers battlefield artillery that moves with the advance. The AP pods handle infantry that approaches the artillery position. Warriors inside the Clans found this artillery doctrine uncomfortable given Clan tradition around direct combat — the design's chequered history reflects that.

variants.overview: The Bowman is a seventy-ton Clan heavy designed as an artillery platform, built around Arrow IV systems on a 350-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. The Arrow IV concept was controversial within the Clans because the direct-fire tradition disfavoured artillery. Three variants emerged as the design evolved.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy tons. The Clan XL carries the standard side torso vulnerability. Endo steel structure. The Arrow IV is battlefield artillery — range and impact that direct fire weapons cannot match. Arrow IV ammunition requires dedicated supply separate from standard weapon logistics. Variant 2 removes the Arrow IV systems and carries two LRM-20s, three ER medium lasers, and an ER large laser. Walk five, run seven. The LRM-20s provide conventional long-range indirect fire. The ER large laser and ER mediums handle direct engagement. Double heat sinks improve thermal management.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 replaces the controversial Arrow IV concept with conventional LRM fire support. The Clan warriors who found artillery disreputable preferred this variant. The LRM-20s deliver sustained indirect fire without the cultural baggage. The ER laser suite provides direct fire capability. Double heat sinks allow more aggressive firing cycles.

variants.overview: The Bowman is a seventy-ton Clan heavy designed as an artillery platform, built around Arrow IV systems on a 350-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. The Arrow IV concept was controversial within the Clans because the direct-fire tradition disfavoured artillery. Three variants emerged as the design evolved.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy tons. The Clan XL carries the standard side torso vulnerability. Endo steel structure. The Arrow IV is battlefield artillery — range and impact that direct fire weapons cannot match. Arrow IV ammunition requires dedicated supply separate from standard weapon logistics. Variant 3 carries a HAG/20, an ATM-9, four ER medium lasers, and two B-pods, with a targeting computer. Walk five, run seven. The targeting computer improves accuracy across all weapons. The HAG/20 delivers spread ballistic damage. The ATM-9 adds three-munition missile flexibility. The B-pods handle battle armour threats. The ER mediums provide direct fire.
variants.deployment: Variant 3 converts the Bowman from a long-range support platform into a direct combat heavy with battle armour protection. The targeting computer combined with HAG/20 and ATM-9 creates a precise multi-role combatant. B-pods actively deter battle armour swarming. The ER medium suite handles direct engagement at multiple ranges.

variants.name: BRM-5A
variants.overview: Taurus Territorial Industries built the Brahma in 3080 as a sixty-ton heavy for the Taurian Defense Force, designed to rebuild front-line formations after the Jihad. Walk five, run seven, jump three on the 300-rated XL engine. Ferro-fibrous armour, endo steel structure. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump three at sixty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Jump three provides terrain exploitation capability. The design was built to handle the varied threat environments of the post-Jihad Periphery. The BRM-5A carries three ER medium lasers, a Streak SRM-6, a Light AC/5, an AMS, and a flamer. Walk five, run seven, jump three. The ER mediums handle the primary direct fire. The Streak SRM-6 adds guaranteed close-range missile hits. The Light AC/5 provides ballistic harassment. The AMS defends against missiles. The flamer handles infantry.
variants.deployment: The 5A is the original Brahma that the TDF rebuilt its front-line formations around. The mixed weapons cover most threat types a Periphery command encounters. Walk five, run seven, jump three is good mobility for a sixty-ton heavy. The AMS is worth maintaining given the missile-heavy environments the TDF operates in. XL engine vulnerability is the standing concern.

variants.name: BRM-5B
variants.overview: Taurus Territorial Industries built the Brahma in 3080 as a sixty-ton heavy for the Taurian Defense Force, designed to rebuild front-line formations after the Jihad. Walk five, run seven, jump three on the 300-rated XL engine. Ferro-fibrous armour, endo steel structure. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump three at sixty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Jump three provides terrain exploitation capability. The design was built to handle the varied threat environments of the post-Jihad Periphery. The BRM-5B carries three ER medium lasers, a standard SRM-6, a large X-pulse laser, and an ER small laser. Walk five, run seven, jump three. The large X-pulse laser is the standout weapon — accurate and effective at medium range. The ER mediums add energy volume. The SRM-6 handles close threats.
variants.deployment: The BRM-5B centres on the experimental large X-pulse laser. The X-pulse accuracy is the primary close-range advantage. The ER mediums and SRM-6 round out the weapons suite. The AMS is absent on this variant — units that run the 5B in missile-heavy environments miss it. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: BRM-6T
variants.overview: Taurus Territorial Industries built the Brahma in 3080 as a sixty-ton heavy for the Taurian Defense Force. Walk five, run seven, jump three on the 300-rated XL engine. Ferro-fibrous armour, endo steel structure. Three variants address different tactical requirements.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Jump three provides terrain exploitation capability. Built for the post-Jihad Periphery threat environment. The BRM-6T was introduced in 3148 and removes the jump jets in favour of a conventional ground-based design. It carries three ER medium lasers, a Streak SRM-6, a standard PPC, and an AMS. Walk five, run seven, no jump. The PPC provides long-range direct fire. The ER mediums and Streak SRM-6 cover closer engagement. The AMS defends against missiles.
variants.deployment: The 6T trades the original's jump capability for a PPC as the primary weapon. The PPC range extends the engagement envelope beyond what the ER mediums alone provide. The AMS is a consistent defensive asset in the post-Dark Age threat environment. No jump means the pilot relies on ground speed rather than terrain exploitation.

variants.name: LDT-1
variants.overview: Vengeance Incorporated built the Brigand as a twenty-five ton raiding platform — a pirate organisation's answer to having no legitimate access to military procurement. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 150-rated standard engine. Eleven variants span from the original to later Dark Age-era refinements.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at twenty-five tons. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. XL engine adds vulnerability on variants that upgrade. The contraband jump jets are one maintenance headache I have seen in the field: provenance is uncertain and calibration specs vary. The all-energy loadout on most variants suits raiders operating without supply lines. The LDT-1 is the original production model: two ER medium lasers and two medium pulse lasers. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the standard 150-rated engine. All-energy. The ER mediums handle medium range; the pulse lasers close range. Standard engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The LDT-1 established the Brigand's raiding identity. The all-energy loadout suits operations without supply lines. Jump six combined with walk six makes this machine agile across broken terrain. Standard engine means side torso hits are survivable. Despite its pirate origins, the design is competent.

variants.name: LDT-X1
variants.overview: Vengeance Incorporated built the Brigand as a twenty-five ton raiding platform — a pirate organisation's answer to having no legitimate access to military procurement. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 150-rated standard engine. Eleven variants span from the original to later Dark Age-era refinements.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at twenty-five tons. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. XL engine adds vulnerability on variants that upgrade. The all-energy loadout on most variants suits raiders operating without supply lines. The LDT-X1 replaces the medium pulse lasers with four standard medium lasers, adding two to the original two. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the standard engine. Six medium lasers total. More close-range volume at the cost of pulse laser accuracy. Standard engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The X1 increases close-range energy volume at the expense of the pulse laser accuracy advantage. The four standard medium lasers and two ER mediums deliver more simultaneous fire than the original. Standard engine survives side torso damage. For pilots who preferred volume over precision, the X1 over the LDT-1.

The all-energy loadout on most variants suits raiders operating without supply lines. The LDT-X2 swaps the medium pulse lasers for four Rocket Launcher-15s, keeping the two ER mediums. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the standard engine. The four RL-15s are one-shot weapons — a single sixty-round alpha strike followed by ER medium fire only. Standard engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The X2 is the ambush striker. Jump to a close position, fire all four RL-15s simultaneously, then fight on with the ER mediums. The alpha strike can overwhelm opponents above this weight class. Once fired, the rockets are gone. The ER mediums carry every engagement after that initial salvo.

variants.overview: Vengeance Incorporated built the Brigand as a twenty-five ton raiding platform — a pirate organisation's answer to having no legitimate access to military procurement. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 150-rated standard engine. Eleven variants span from the original to later Dark Age-era refinements.

Walk six, run nine, jump six on the XL engine. The light PPCs handle short to medium range without minimum range complications. The flamers handle infantry and area denial. XL engine — side torso vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The X3 uses illicitly acquired Moscovia light PPCs alongside flamers. The light PPCs are accurate at close range. The flamers handle infantry and force heat problems on opposing 'Mechs at close distance. The XL engine adds the standard vulnerability that the standard-engine Brigands avoid.

variants.name: LDT-XPR1

variants.deployment: The XPR5 trades ground speed for jump capability. Walk five is a real reduction from the standard Brigand's walk six. Jump eight compensates with exceptional vertical mobility — the pilot can approach from angles and elevations that standard jump six cannot reach. Four medium lasers are the weapons. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.deployment: The X4 uses the light engine's survivability alongside TSM for a heat-activated close-combat boost. The ER mediums heat the machine deliberately to trigger TSM, then the physical attack capability and speed become the primary tools. The light engine survives hits that would end XL Brigands. The TSM activation threshold must be managed deliberately.

variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 175-rated XL engine. The LDT-5 carries three medium lasers. Walk seven is faster than all earlier Brigand variants. The weapons are modest — three medium lasers — but the speed and jump capability are the point. XL engine — side torso vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The LDT-5 was first encountered on Lackland in 3083, distilling the best features from five prototype Brigands the Filtvelt Coalition recovered. Walk seven, jump seven on a twenty-five ton machine creates approach options that few opponents can counter. The three medium lasers handle direct engagement. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.overview: The Ghost Bear Dominion developed the Bruin as an eighty-ton assault platform in the late Dark Age era. Walk four, run six, jump four on the 320-rated Clan XL engine. Jump four at eighty tons is the design's tactical surprise. Two variants cover the production run.

variants.deployment: Variant 2 was designed to handle the heavily armoured and infantry-rich opponents of the final Word of Blake campaigns. The large pulse laser accuracy and UAC/5 sustained fire handle armoured opponents. Six machine guns handle infantry formations. Jump four provides positioning options. XL engine side torso vulnerability is the standing concern.

variants.name: BCN-3R
variants.overview: Gibson Federated BattleMechs built the Buccaneer in 3055 as a fifty-five ton close-combat medium with a four-ton hatchet as the primary offensive tool. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated XL engine. Four variants. The hatchet combined with walk six speed delivers physical damage that most opponents at this weight class cannot efficiently absorb.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at fifty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The four-ton hatchet delivers substantial physical damage per hit at close range. Walk six closes the distance to hatchet range faster than many opponents expect from a medium. The BCN-3R carries an ER large laser, four medium lasers, a medium pulse laser, an SRM-6, and the four-ton hatchet. Walk six, run nine on the XL engine. The ER large laser handles approach fire. The medium lasers and pulse laser cover direct energy engagement. The SRM-6 adds close-range missile punch. The hatchet closes the fight.
variants.deployment: The BCN-3R established the Buccaneer's reputation and served exclusively with Word of Blake Militia formations. The hatchet combined with walk six delivers physical damage at close range that the weapons cannot replicate. The ER large laser fires during the approach. The SRM-6 and mediums support the close-range engagement. XL engine vulnerability applies.

Sustained engagement is not viable; this is built for a single decisive close-range strike.

variants.overview: The Burrock is a Clan heavy that absorbed significant damage from the destruction of Clan Burrock by Clan Star Adder and Cloud Cobra in 2912. variants.overview: Clan Jade Falcon built the Butcherbird as a twenty-ton OmniMech partial wing technology test bed — originally for training, eventually fielded in combat after earning a battlefield reputation. Walk eight, run twelve, jump eight on the 160-rated Clan XL. The partial wing provides heat dissipation that changes the thermal performance of every configuration.

The partial wing is the defining chassis feature — it improves heat dissipation beyond what the base heat sink count suggests. Pod space is minimal at twenty tons: four tons across most configurations. Configuration A carries eight machine guns — four per arm — plus a machine gun array and an active probe. Walk eight, run twelve, jump eight. The active probe detects hidden units. Machine gun arrays coordinate multiple feeds for simultaneous fire. Eight machine guns against infantry is thorough.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is the anti-infantry scout. The active probe finds hidden units. The machine gun volume destroys infantry. Jump eight combined with walk eight delivers the machine to contact from unexpected positions. Ammunition management across eight machine gun feeds is the maintenance overhead after every mission.

The XL vulnerability at twenty tons means not getting hit is survival.

The partial wing allows more aggressive cycling than the chassis heat sinks alone would permit.
variants.deployment: Configuration C is the all-energy striker. Walk eight and jump eight deliver the ER small laser suite from any angle. No ammunition dependency suits independent raiding. The ER mediums threaten opponents at ranges where the machine can use walk eight to maintain distance. The pulse laser accuracy suits the close-range engagement when the range closes. Four weapons across anti-armour and anti-infantry roles.
variants.deployment: The Prime balances anti-BattleMech and anti-infantry capability within four tons of pod space. The improved heavy medium lasers deliver meaningful close-range damage against armoured opponents. The AP Gauss rifles handle infantry alongside the 'Mech combat. variants.name: CVR-A1
variants.overview: An unnamed manufacturer built the Cadaver as a thirty-ton Periphery raider with Guardian ECM and a Lynx-Shur communications suite as core equipment. Walk eight, run twelve on the 240-rated XL engine. Two variants. The electronic warfare capability is the design's primary tactical contribution.

The weapons handle threats that get close. Commanders who use the ECM actively rather than treating it as passive protection get the most from this platform.

The ER PPC covers medium-to-long range. The pulse lasers handle close engagement. Two pulse lasers are rear-facing.
variants.deployment: The CES-3R established the Caesar's reputation. The Gauss and ER PPC combination at range is difficult for comparable-weight opponents to answer effectively. The rear-facing pulse lasers deter pursuit. XL engine vulnerability applies. Gauss ammunition is the primary supply task.

variants.name: CTF-5D
variants.overview: Earthwerks Incorporated built the Cataphract in 3025 for the Capellan Confederation, assembled from existing component lines rather than original designs. Seventy tons, walk four, run six. The mixed-heritage construction is both a logistical advantage — parts source from multiple production lines — and a maintenance challenge. Twelve variants emerged from that original design.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump six on the 280-rated light engine. The CTF-5D carries a light AC/5, two ER medium lasers, and a plasma rifle. Light engine — side torso survivability. Jump six at seventy tons. The plasma rifle adds thermal disruption. The light AC/5 provides ballistic harassment. The ER mediums cover energy fire.
variants.deployment: The 5D emerged from the Jihad using salvaged components at New Syrtis. Jump six at seventy tons is the surprise capability. The light engine survivability is the consistent advantage. The plasma rifle disrupts opponents while the light AC/5 and ER mediums handle direct engagement. A field-built configuration that works within the chaos of Jihad-era supply constraints.

variants.name: CTF-5L
variants.overview: Earthwerks Incorporated built the Cataphract in 3025 for the Capellan Confederation, assembled from existing component lines. Seventy tons, walk four, run six. The mixed-heritage construction is both a logistical advantage and a maintenance challenge. Twelve variants emerged from that original design.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at seventy tons. Mixed component heritage means replacement parts come from different manufacturers with varying tolerances. Standard engine on most conventional variants — side torso survivability. XL engine on upgrade variants. The assembly-from-existing-parts philosophy is visible in every maintenance cycle. The CTF-5L carries a Gauss rifle, an ER PPC, two medium lasers, and two small VSP lasers on the standard engine, with reflective armour. Walk four, run six. The reflective armour reduces incoming energy weapon damage. The VSP lasers adapt to engagement range. The Gauss and ER PPC maintain the long-range precision role.
variants.deployment: The 5L replaces the 4L's stealth armour with reflective armour for energy weapon resistance. The reflective protection is passive rather than active, which removes the heat doubling penalty of stealth armour. The Gauss and ER PPC maintain the long-range fire role. The VSP lasers add flexible close-range coverage. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: CTF-5LL
variants.overview: Earthwerks Incorporated built the Cataphract in 3025 for the Capellan Confederation, assembled from existing component lines. Seventy tons, walk four, run six. The mixed-heritage construction is both a logistical advantage and a maintenance challenge. Twelve variants emerged from that original design.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at seventy tons. Mixed component heritage means replacement parts come from different manufacturers with varying tolerances. Standard engine on most conventional variants — side torso survivability. XL engine on upgrade variants. The assembly-from-existing-parts philosophy is visible in every maintenance cycle. The CTF-5LL carries a Gauss rifle, an ER PPC, and four medium lasers, with jump four on the standard engine. Walk four, run six, jump four. Jump capability on a Cataphract at standard engine survivability. The Gauss and ER PPC maintain long-range precision. Four medium lasers handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: The 5LL adds jump four to the standard Cataphract fire support concept without sacrificing the standard engine survivability. Jump four opens terrain exploitation options the standard walk-four Cataphract lacks. The Gauss and ER PPC cover range. Four medium lasers handle close combat. The jump capability makes this variant more mobile than most Cataphract configurations.

variants.name: CPLT-C1
variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four. The distinctive pod-mounted LRM launchers and armless profile make it the most recognisable fire support 'Mech in existence. The lack of arms changes how I approach maintenance — everything accessible from the torso. Nineteen variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons. The pod-mounted launchers are the design's defining feature — maintenance access to the LRM systems is through the top of the torso pods, which I approach differently to arm-mounted weapons. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-C1 is the original 2561 production model: twin Holly LRM-15s and four Martell medium lasers on the standard 260-rated engine. Walk four, run six, jump four. The LRM-15s provide the primary fire support. The four medium lasers handle anything that closes inside minimum range. Standard engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The C1 was produced in record numbers and defined the Catapult's battlefield role for five centuries. It goes somewhere with good firing lanes, stays there, and delivers LRM fire. The medium lasers handle close threats. Jump four is more useful than fire support pilots often acknowledge — repositioning between salvos matters in terrain.

variants.name: CPLT-A1
variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four. The distinctive pod-mounted LRM launchers and armless profile make it the most recognisable fire support 'Mech in existence. The lack of arms changes how I approach maintenance — everything accessible from the torso. Nineteen variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons. The pod-mounted launchers are the design's defining feature — maintenance access to the LRM systems is through the top of the torso pods, which I approach differently to arm-mounted weapons. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-A1 stripped all four medium lasers to double the LRM-15 ammunition — two extra tons per launcher — and added heat sinks. Walk four, run six, jump four. Pure missile fire with no close-range capability. The additional ammunition extends fire support endurance substantially.
variants.deployment: The A1 is a fire support platform that accepted complete close-range helplessness in exchange for ammunition endurance. Anything that closes inside LRM minimum range is a fatal threat. It needs continuous escort. In exchange it sustains fire support for significantly longer than the C1. Know which one you have before the mission.

variants.name: CPLT-C4
variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four. variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons. The pod-mounted launchers are the design's defining feature — maintenance access to the LRM systems is through the top of the torso pods, which I approach differently to arm-mounted weapons. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-C4 swaps both LRM-15 launchers for LRM-20s and replaces the four medium lasers with two small lasers. Walk four, run six, jump four. The LRM-20 upgrade increases the per-salvo missile volume. The small lasers provide token close-range defence.
variants.deployment: The C4 trades the C1's close-range capability for heavier LRM output. The LRM-20 per-salvo damage increase is real. The small lasers are essentially symbolic self-defence — anything that closes stays in range indefinitely. The C4 needs the same escorting the A1 requires, just for different reasons.

variants.name: CPLT-K2
variants.overview: The Catapult CPLT-C1 is a 65-ton fire support 'Mech whose distinctive pod-mounted LRM launchers and armless profile have made it a recognisable piece of Inner Sphere indirect fire doctrine since 2561. I have worked on the chassis in several variants and the K2 is the one that surprises people the most. It abandons the LRM heritage entirely and mounts twin PPCs, turning a fire support frame into a direct fire heavy.
variants.capabilities: Two PPCs, two medium lasers, and two machine guns on a 260-rated standard engine. Walk four, run six. The PPC heat load on an Awesome-weight indirect fire chassis means the K2 runs hot fast and the pilots know it. The machine guns handle infantry and light vehicles. The medium lasers fill the close range gap inside PPC minimum. The standard engine is a survivability asset: this variant can take side torso damage that would kill an XL-equipped 'Mech.
variants.deployment: The K2 is used by commanders who need direct fire capability in a chassis that would otherwise be filling an indirect fire role. It works as a line fighter rather than a support element. The PPC heat management is the pilot's primary discipline. Limited ammunition for the machine guns is rarely a concern given the engagements this variant typically fights.

variants.name: CPLT-C1b
variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four. The distinctive pod-mounted LRM launchers and armless profile make it the most recognisable fire support 'Mech in existence. variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons. The pod-mounted launchers are the design's defining feature — maintenance access to the LRM systems is through the top of the torso pods, which I approach differently to arm-mounted weapons. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-C1b is an upgrade kit doubling ammunition capacity, replacing standard armour with ferro-fibrous, adding CASE to both torsos, and replacing single heat sinks with doubles. Walk four, run six, jump four. The twin LRM-15s and four medium lasers are unchanged. Double heat sinks and ferro-fibrous are the substantive improvements.
variants.deployment: The C1b is the sensible upgrade path for C1 operators. Double heat sinks allow more aggressive firing. Ferro-fibrous improves protection. CASE protects the ammunition bays. The weapons are identical to the C1 — this is a durability and endurance improvement, not a tactical philosophy change.

variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four. variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons. The pod-mounted launchers are the design's defining feature — maintenance access to the LRM systems is through the top of the torso pods, which I approach differently to arm-mounted weapons. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The Butterbee replaces both LRM-15 pod launchers with SRM-6 launchers — two per arm, four total — keeping the four medium lasers. Walk four, run six, jump four. Four SRM-6s at close range on a Catapult chassis. The fire support identity is abandoned entirely for close-range missile saturation.
variants.deployment: The Butterbee is a named configuration that fundamentally changes what the Catapult is. The pod launchers now fire SRM-6s rather than LRMs. Four SRM-6s simultaneously at close range combined with four medium lasers is substantial firepower for a sixty-five ton chassis. Jump four delivers the close-range suite from unexpected angles. Not a fire support machine at all.

Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-K3 is a prototype from after the War of 3039: twin ER PPCs, two medium lasers, and two machine guns on the standard engine. Walk four, run six, no jump. The LRM launchers are gone entirely. Twin ER PPCs make this a direct fire platform rather than a fire support design. No jump jets.
variants.deployment: The K3 prototype was a limited-service attempt to leverage rediscovered Star League technology by converting the Catapult into a direct fire platform. The twin ER PPCs provide real long-range punch. The machine guns handle infantry. No jump jets is a tactical reduction. The prototype saw limited use after the War of 3039.

variants.name: CPLT-C3
variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four. The distinctive pod-mounted LRM launchers and armless profile make it the most recognisable fire support 'Mech in existence. variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons. The pod-mounted launchers are the design's defining feature — maintenance access to the LRM systems is through the top of the torso pods, which I approach differently to arm-mounted weapons. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-C3 replaces both LRM launchers with a single Luxor Mobile Battery Arrow IV artillery system and keeps four medium lasers. Walk four, run six, jump four. The Arrow IV provides extreme-range artillery capability that dwarfs standard LRM fire. Arrow IV ammunition supply is entirely separate from standard LRM logistics.
variants.deployment: The C3 pioneered BattleMech-mounted artillery on the Catapult chassis. The Arrow IV range advantage over LRMs is substantial. Arrow IV ammunition supply chains require separate planning. The four medium lasers handle close defence. The Arrow IV heat was problematic on the C3 — the C5 subsequently addressed this.

Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The Kasigi is a named wartime improvisation: twin ER PPCs and two medium lasers with jump four on the standard engine. Walk four, run six, jump four. New and old components combined into a patchwork configuration. The ER PPCs provide increased range over standard PPCs. Jump four is preserved.
variants.deployment: The Kasigi emerged from wartime component constraints. The ER PPC upgrade from standard PPCs is a genuine improvement. Jump four is maintained. The medium lasers handle close engagement. Named machine — maintain to the specific field-build documentation rather than standard Catapult procedures.

variants.name: CPLT-C4C
variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-C4C uses an XL engine to carry twin LRM-20s, a large laser, a small pulse laser, and a Beagle active probe. Walk four, run six, jump four. The XL engine enables the larger weapons load over the standard engine. The Beagle extends sensor coverage. The large laser and small pulse laser provide direct fire capability.
variants.deployment: The C4C upgrades the C4's standard engine to XL for additional capability mass. The Beagle active probe adds sensor coverage useful for fire support coordination. The large laser provides direct fire that the C4's small lasers could not. XL engine adds the side torso vulnerability the standard engine variants avoid.

Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-K2K uses a 325-rated XL engine for walk five, run seven — the fastest Catapult variant. Twin ER PPCs and two ER medium lasers. No jump jets. Walk five on a Catapult. The ER PPCs provide extended-range direct fire. The ER mediums handle closer engagement.
variants.deployment: The K2K boosts the Catapult to walk five using a larger XL engine. The twin ER PPCs maintain the K-series direct fire identity. Walk five allows repositioning that standard Catapults cannot manage. No jump jets is the tradeoff. XL engine vulnerability applies.

The CPLT-K5 uses a 260-rated XL engine and carries twin MRM-30 launchers and two medium pulse lasers. Walk four, run six, jump four. The MRM-30s deliver heavy medium-range missile volume. The pulse lasers handle close engagement accurately. XL engine vulnerability applies.
variants.deployment: The K5 uses medium-range missiles rather than the long-range LRM or direct-fire PPC concepts of earlier Catapult variants. The MRM-30 output at medium range is substantial. The pulse lasers add accurate close-range capability. XL engine adds vulnerability that standard engine Catapults avoid.

variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four. The distinctive pod-mounted LRM launchers and armless profile make it the most recognisable fire support 'Mech in existence. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-C5 is the corrected Arrow IV Catapult: endo steel chassis, double heat sinks, one Arrow IV system, and four ER medium lasers. Walk four, run six, jump four. The endo steel and double heat sinks address the heat and weight problems of the C3. The ER mediums replace the standard mediums with extended-range energy backup.
variants.deployment: The C5 fixed what was wrong with the C3. The endo steel construction and double heat sinks resolve the heat issues that plagued the original Arrow IV Catapult. The ER mediums provide better close-range coverage than the C3's standard mediums. Arrow IV ammunition logistics remain the dedicated supply requirement.

variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four. The distinctive pod-mounted LRM launchers and armless profile make it the most recognisable fire support 'Mech in existence. The pod-mounted launchers are the design's defining feature — maintenance access to the LRM systems is through the top of the torso pods, which I approach differently to arm-mounted weapons. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-C2 uses a 260-rated XL engine and carries twin Artemis IV-guided LRM-15s and two LB 2-X ACs. Walk four, run six, jump four. The Artemis IV guidance improves LRM grouping. The LB 2-X ACs provide long-range ballistic harassment. XL engine vulnerability applies.
variants.deployment: The C2 upgrades the standard LRM-15s with Artemis guidance and adds LB 2-X ballistic harassment. The Artemis accuracy improvement makes each LRM round count more. The LB 2-X ACs provide additional long-range pressure. XL engine adds the standard vulnerability. The combined long-range output from guided LRMs and LB 2-X fire is the design intent.

variants.name: CPLT-H2
variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four. The distinctive pod-mounted LRM launchers and armless profile make it the most recognisable fire support 'Mech in existence. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-H2 carries a PPC, eight Rocket Launcher-20s, and two medium lasers on the standard engine. Walk four, run six, jump four. The eight RL-20s are one-shot weapons — a single one-hundred-and-sixty round alpha strike. After that the machine has a PPC and two medium lasers.
variants.deployment: The H2 is the one-shot devastation Catapult. Eight RL-20s simultaneously delivers a missile volume that almost nothing survives at close range. Once fired, the rockets are spent and the machine becomes a standard PPC platform. The tactic is straightforward: jump to position, fire all eight RL-20s, fight on with what remains. Choose the moment carefully.

variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-C5A returns to standard LRM fire support: twin LRM-15s and four ER medium lasers on the standard engine, endo steel chassis. Walk four, run six, jump four. The ER mediums replace the Arrow IV systems of the C5 with conventional extended-range energy backup.
variants.deployment: The C5A abandons the Arrow IV concept entirely and returns the Catapult to its LRM heritage. The ER medium upgrade over standard mediums improves close-range energy capability. The endo steel chassis is preserved from the C5. This is the conventional fire support Catapult for commanders who found the Arrow IV logistics burdensome.

variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-K4 uses a smaller 195-rated engine for walk three, run four, jump three — slower than the standard Catapult — carrying twin heavy PPCs, two ER medium lasers, and a C3 slave. The heavy PPCs hit harder than standard PPCs at medium range but have a minimum range gap. Walk three. C3 slave for network integration.
variants.deployment: The K4 traded ground and jump speed for heavy PPC firepower and C3 network integration. Walk three is a significant reduction from the standard Catapult's walk four. The heavy PPC minimum range requires the ER mediums at close distance. The C3 slave adds network coordination value. A deliberate tradeoff for units with heavy C3 network doctrine.

variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four.
