The pod-mounted launchers are the design's defining feature — maintenance access to the LRM systems is through the top of the torso pods, which I approach differently to arm-mounted weapons. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-C6 removes the Arrow IV systems and two ER mediums to mount paired plasma rifles with three tons of ammunition, adding three double heat sinks. Walk four, run six, jump four. The plasma rifles superheat targets while dealing damage. The remaining two ER mediums handle direct energy backup.
variants.deployment: The C6 replaces fire support capability with thermal disruption. The paired plasma rifles force heat management problems on opponents. The ER mediums handle direct combat between plasma salvos. Three tons of plasma ammunition provides reasonable operational endurance. A departure from the Catapult's traditional fire support role.

variants.name: CPLT-K6
variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated built the Catapult in 2561 for the Terran Hegemony. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six, jump four. The distinctive pod-mounted LRM launchers and armless profile make it the most recognisable fire support 'Mech in existence. The lack of arms changes how I approach maintenance — everything accessible from the torso. Nineteen variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at sixty-five tons. The pod-mounted launchers are the design's defining feature — maintenance access to the LRM systems is through the top of the torso pods, which I approach differently to arm-mounted weapons. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability is more useful than many fire support pilots think. The CPLT-K6 uses a 195-rated XL engine for walk three, run four, jump three, carrying twin Extended LRM-15s and four ER small lasers. Walk three. The ELRM-15s reach substantially beyond standard LRM range — opponents at standard LRM maximum range cannot reply effectively. The ER small lasers handle close threats.
variants.deployment: The K6 maximises stand-off range at the cost of ground speed. Walk three is slow even for a fire support platform. The ELRM-15 engagement envelope extends the safe firing range substantially. The ER small lasers are token self-defence. Units that positioned this machine before the battle and held it there got the most from the extreme range advantage.

variants.name: CPLT-L7
variants.overview: The Capellan Confederation built the Catapult II in 3135 as a seventy-ton upscaled version of the original, adding TSEMP cannon technology alongside the LRM heritage. Walk four, run six, jump four on the 280-rated XL engine. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at seventy tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The TSEMP cannon is the technology addition the original Catapult lacked. Capellan Confederation production quality. The CPLT-L7 carries twin LRM-20 launchers and twin TSEMP cannons with two ER medium lasers. Walk four, run six, jump four on the XL engine. The LRM-20s provide heavy indirect fire. The TSEMP cannons deliver electromagnetic pulses that disrupt enemy 'Mech systems without destroying armour. The ER mediums handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: The L7 entered Capellan production in 3135. The TSEMP disabling capability alongside LRM-20 fire support creates a combined threat profile opponents cannot easily manage — shut down or missile-suppressed. TSEMP maintenance requires specialist procedures. XL engine vulnerability is the standing concern.

variants.name: CPLT-L7L
variants.overview: The Capellan Confederation built the Catapult II in 3135 as a seventy-ton upscaled version of the original, adding TSEMP cannon technology alongside the LRM heritage. Walk four, run six, jump four on the 280-rated XL engine. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at seventy tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The TSEMP cannon is the technology addition the original Catapult lacked. Capellan Confederation production quality. The CPLT-L7L carries twin MML-9 launchers and twin plasma rifles. Walk four, run six, jump four on the XL engine. The MML-9s cover SRM and LRM range bands from the same launchers. The plasma rifles superheat targets while dealing damage. This variant trades the experimental TSEMP systems for proven weapons.
variants.deployment: The L7L replaces the experimental TSEMP technology with plasma rifles and MML flexibility. The plasma rifle thermal disruption creates tactical problems for opponents while the MML-9 flexibility covers both fire support and close engagement depending on mode selection. Less experimental than the L7 and correspondingly easier to maintain.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Cauldron-Born, called the Ebon Jaguar in IS records, is a 65-ton Clan OmniMech built on an endo steel chassis with a 325-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Thirty tons of pod space is generous for a heavy OmniMech and the design has been configured into a wider variety of roles than most chassis in its class. No jump jets on any configuration, which shapes how every variant has to be deployed.
variants.capabilities: The A configuration is the most demanding I maintain. An Ultra AC/20 in the right arm, two ER large lasers, a medium pulse laser, three ER medium lasers including two rear-facing, a flamer, and twin machine guns. The Ultra AC/20 in double-tap mode delivers enormous close-range damage. The base thirteen heat sinks handle the energy weapons adequately in isolation but the full weapons combination generates heat fast. The rear-mounted ER mediums are a genuine deterrent against flanking attempts.
variants.deployment: The A configuration is a close-range assault variant. The ER large lasers bring the enemy to close range and the Ultra AC/20 finishes the engagement there. Warriors in A configuration need to manage the AC ammunition carefully: two tons is the operational limit on sustained combat. The rear mediums provide real protection against anything that tries to exploit the approach. No extra heat sinks means heat discipline matters from the first exchange.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: The Cauldron-Born, called the Ebon Jaguar in IS records, is a 65-ton Clan OmniMech built on an endo steel chassis with a 325-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Thirty tons of pod space is generous for a heavy OmniMech and the design has been configured into a wider variety of roles than most chassis in its class. No jump jets on any configuration, which shapes how every variant has to be deployed.
variants.capabilities: The B configuration is an all-energy heavy fire platform: two ER PPCs, two large pulse lasers, two medium pulse lasers, and TAG for target designation. The ER PPCs and large pulse lasers together represent an enormous energy output and firing all four in the same cycle builds heat rapidly. Volley fire discipline is required to sustain this configuration in combat. The TAG system makes this a valuable designation asset for units with indirect fire support.
variants.deployment: The B configuration deploys as a long-range fire support element that can also designate targets for artillery. The TAG capability is most useful when operated with Clan artillery or aerospace assets that can exploit the designations. Warriors who understand volley fire timing can maintain sustained output from the B configuration effectively. Those who alpha strike repeatedly will shut down.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: The Cauldron-Born, called the Ebon Jaguar in IS records, is a 65-ton Clan OmniMech built on an endo steel chassis with a 325-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Thirty tons of pod space is generous for a heavy OmniMech and the design has been configured into a wider variety of roles than most chassis in its class. No jump jets on any configuration, which shapes how every variant has to be deployed.
variants.capabilities: The C configuration is the coolest-running Cauldron-Born in the family. Twin LRM-15s in the side torsos, twin Ultra AC/2s in the arms, and two SRM-6 launchers for close range, with generous ammunition across all systems. The combination runs cool enough that heat is almost irrelevant as a tactical constraint, which is unusual for this chassis. The SRM-6s handle anything that closes while the LRMs and UAC/2s work at range.
variants.deployment: The C configuration suits extended operations where ammunition management matters more than heat management. The generous ammunition supply means this variant can fight through engagements that would exhaust lighter-loaded configurations. The cool running nature makes it forgiving to pilot compared to the energy-heavy variants. Pod swaps from C to other configurations are clean on this chassis.

variants.name: Prime
variants.overview: The Cauldron-Born, called the Ebon Jaguar in IS records, is a 65-ton Clan OmniMech built on an endo steel chassis with a 325-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Thirty tons of pod space is generous for a heavy OmniMech and the design has been configured into a wider variety of roles than most chassis in its class. No jump jets on any configuration, which shapes how every variant has to be deployed.
variants.capabilities: The Prime carries a Gauss rifle in the right arm, an LB 5-X in the left, an LRM-10 in the right torso, and an ER medium laser with an SRM-2 for close defence. The Gauss rifle is the standout weapon: accurate, hard-hitting, and the primary reason to run this configuration. Three tons of Gauss ammunition is adequate for most engagements. The LB 5-X cluster option handles lighter targets the Gauss would be wasted on.
variants.deployment: The Prime is the standard deployment configuration across most Clan units operating this chassis. The Gauss rifle accuracy at range, LB 5-X flexibility, and LRM-10 indirect fire give it genuine multi-role capability without excelling at any single task. Warriors who understand how to sequence the weapons across engagement distances get consistent results from the Prime. It is a reliable workhorse rather than a specialist.

variants.name: (Samantha)
variants.overview: The Cauldron-Born, called the Ebon Jaguar in IS records, is a 65-ton Clan OmniMech built on an endo steel chassis with a 325-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Thirty tons of pod space is generous for a heavy OmniMech and the design has been configured into a wider variety of roles than most chassis in its class. No jump jets on any configuration, which shapes how every variant has to be deployed.
variants.capabilities: The Samantha configuration is a named pilot variant used by a Star Captain during Operation Bulldog on Luzerne. It pairs an ER PPC in the left arm with an Ultra AC/20 in the right, three LRM-10 launchers in the right torso, and an ER small laser. The Ultra AC/20 and ER PPC combination covers close and long range simultaneously. The three LRM-10s provide a substantial indirect fire capability for a named pilot configuration.
variants.deployment: This is a personal configuration tailored for a specific warrior's tactics. The close-range devastation of the Ultra AC/20 combined with ER PPC reach and LRM-10 indirect fire gives considerable flexibility. The Samantha configuration is documented from the Luzerne engagement and may appear in other hands in later service. Maintaining the three LRM launchers alongside the AC/20 requires careful ammunition bay management.

variants.name: D
variants.overview: The Cauldron-Born, called the Ebon Jaguar in IS records, is a 65-ton Clan OmniMech built on an endo steel chassis with a 325-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Thirty tons of pod space is generous for a heavy OmniMech and the design has been configured into a wider variety of roles than most chassis in its class. No jump jets on any configuration, which shapes how every variant has to be deployed.
variants.capabilities: The D configuration carries twin Ultra AC/10s in the arms, an ER large laser in the right torso, and two ER medium lasers. The Ultra AC/10s in double-tap mode deliver high-volume fire at medium range. Two tons of AC/10 ammunition each means endurance management is the primary concern on extended operations. The ER large laser provides sustained energy output when the autocannon bins run low.
variants.deployment: The D configuration is a medium-range brawler built around autocannon volume of fire. The rate of fire from two Ultra AC/10s on double-tap is impressive but burns through ammunition quickly. Warriors in D configuration need a clear plan for when the bins empty: the ER large laser and ER mediums carry the fight at that point. The configuration works best in engagements where ammunition resupply is available between contacts.

variants.name: H
variants.overview: The Cauldron-Born, called the Ebon Jaguar in IS records, is a 65-ton Clan OmniMech built on an endo steel chassis with a 325-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Thirty tons of pod space is generous for a heavy OmniMech and the design has been configured into a wider variety of roles than most chassis in its class. No jump jets on any configuration, which shapes how every variant has to be deployed.
variants.capabilities: The H configuration is a close-range energy and autocannon assault loadout: a heavy large laser, two heavy medium lasers, a medium pulse laser, and an Ultra AC/20. The heavy lasers hit hard but generate more heat than standard equivalents, and the Ultra AC/20 adds to the thermal load. This is one of the hottest Cauldron-Born configurations. Warriors who push all weapons simultaneously will shut down. Warriors who sequence carefully will devastate targets at close range.
variants.deployment: The H configuration is an in-fighter variant for warriors who close range and stay there. The heavy large laser opens the engagement and the heavy mediums and Ultra AC/20 finish it at close quarters. The heat management requirement means this configuration rewards experienced pilots who understand their heat curve well enough to keep the weapons cycling without hitting the shutdown threshold.

variants.name: E
variants.overview: The Cauldron-Born, called the Ebon Jaguar in IS records, is a 65-ton Clan OmniMech built on an endo steel chassis with a 325-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Thirty tons of pod space is generous for a heavy OmniMech and the design has been configured into a wider variety of roles than most chassis in its class. No jump jets on any configuration, which shapes how every variant has to be deployed.
variants.capabilities: The E configuration carries a HAG/20, a large pulse laser, an ER medium laser, and an ATM-12. The HAG/20 is the centrepiece: it delivers a spread of ballistic damage across multiple locations that concentrated fire cannot match for disrupting armour. The ATM-12 with three tons of ammunition provides three munition types for tactical flexibility. The large pulse laser and ER medium handle close and mid-range energy fire respectively.
variants.deployment: The E configuration is genuinely difficult for opponents to defend against because the HAG/20 spread and ATM munition variety attack different armour profiles simultaneously. Pre-loading the correct ATM munition type before engagement is the key preparation step. The HAG/20 ammunition needs dedicated storage and the ATM three-munition logistics require careful bay organisation. Warriors who master the weapons selection get excellent results.

variants.name: X
variants.overview: The Cauldron-Born, called the Ebon Jaguar in IS records, is a 65-ton Clan OmniMech built on an endo steel chassis with a 325-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Thirty tons of pod space is generous for a heavy OmniMech and the design has been configured into a wider variety of roles than most chassis in its class. No jump jets on any configuration, which shapes how every variant has to be deployed.
variants.capabilities: The X configuration carries three ER medium pulse lasers, a Rotary AC/5, and an ER small pulse laser. The Rotary AC/5 delivers rapid ballistic salvos at medium to long range. The ER medium pulse lasers provide accurate energy fire at multiple range bands. This is an experimental configuration and the ER pulse laser technology requires specialist maintenance procedures. The combination runs warm but manageable under combat conditions.
variants.deployment: The X configuration is an experimental designation and units operating it need techs qualified on ER pulse laser systems. The Rotary AC/5 ammunition management is the standard concern for rotating autocannon configurations. The precision of the pulse laser suite combined with the Rotary's volume of fire makes this effective in combined-arms roles where accuracy matters.

variants.name: U
variants.overview: The Cauldron-Born, called the Ebon Jaguar in IS records, is a 65-ton Clan OmniMech built on an endo steel chassis with a 325-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Thirty tons of pod space is generous for a heavy OmniMech and the design has been configured into a wider variety of roles than most chassis in its class. No jump jets on any configuration, which shapes how every variant has to be deployed.
variants.capabilities: The U configuration is the underwater operations variant: twin large pulse lasers, two ER small lasers, and two LRT-15 torpedo launchers. The pulse lasers perform effectively underwater where beam weapons lose efficiency at range. The LRT-15s provide heavy torpedo fire support against submerged targets. This is a specialised configuration and the torpedo tube seals and launcher mechanisms require inspection after every subaquatic deployment.
variants.deployment: The U configuration deploys in aquatic assault operations on worlds with significant bodies of water. The large pulse lasers and torpedo launchers provide genuine heavy fire support capability in environments where most 'Mech configurations are severely degraded. Maintaining this variant requires familiarity with torpedo system procedures that most Clan techs do not encounter on standard deployments.

variants.name: F
variants.overview: The Cauldron-Born, called the Ebon Jaguar in IS records, is a 65-ton Clan OmniMech built on an endo steel chassis with a 325-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Thirty tons of pod space is generous for a heavy OmniMech and the design has been configured into a wider variety of roles than most chassis in its class. No jump jets on any configuration, which shapes how every variant has to be deployed.
variants.capabilities: The F configuration carries two ER PPCs, one in each arm, and two ATM-6 launchers in the side torsos, with eighteen double heat sinks to manage the energy load. The twin ER PPCs deliver consistent long-range fire and the eighteen heat sinks make this one of the more thermally manageable energy configurations in the Cauldron-Born family. The ATM-6 launchers add missile flexibility across three munition types.
variants.deployment: The F configuration is a long-range engagement platform that balances energy and missile fire effectively. The heat sink count means warriors can sustain ER PPC fire at a reasonable cycle rate without compromising the ATM munition choices. Two tons of ATM ammunition manages well across most engagements. This is one of the more straightforward Cauldron-Born configurations to operate and maintain.

variants.name: G
variants.overview: The Cauldron-Born, called the Ebon Jaguar in IS records, is a 65-ton Clan OmniMech built on an endo steel chassis with a 325-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Thirty tons of pod space is generous for a heavy OmniMech and the design has been configured into a wider variety of roles than most chassis in its class. No jump jets on any configuration, which shapes how every variant has to be deployed.
variants.capabilities: The G configuration commits almost all pod tonnage to two weapons: a HAG/40 and an improved heavy large laser. The HAG/40 is among the most destructive ballistic weapons available at this tonnage and the spread of projectiles across multiple armour locations is difficult to absorb. The improved heavy large laser hits hard at medium range but generates considerable heat. This is not a configuration that forgives poor target selection.
variants.deployment: The G configuration is a maximum-damage specialist. The HAG/40 and improved heavy large laser together can overwhelm most opponents in a single engagement cycle if the warrior positions correctly. The weapon load leaves almost nothing else in the pod space, so this configuration lives or dies by those two systems. Warriors assigned G configuration choose their targets carefully and fire decisively.

variants.name: T
variants.overview: The Cauldron-Born, called the Ebon Jaguar in IS records, is a 65-ton Clan OmniMech built on an endo steel chassis with a 325-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Thirty tons of pod space is generous for a heavy OmniMech and the design has been configured into a wider variety of roles than most chassis in its class. No jump jets on any configuration, which shapes how every variant has to be deployed.
variants.capabilities: The T configuration is a mixed-tech loadout: Clan ER PPC in the right arm, Clan Ultra AC/5 in the left, a Streak LRM-10 and improved heavy medium laser in the left torso, and twin Thunderbolt-5 launchers in the right torso, with CASE II protecting both side torsos. The mixed weapons cover every range band. The Streak LRM-10 fires only on lock, which conserves ammunition. CASE II protection on both torsos is appropriate given the ammunition density.
variants.deployment: The T configuration's mixed Clan and IS weapon systems create a two-track maintenance requirement that any tech assigned to this variant needs to be prepared for. The Thunderbolt-5 launchers are less common in Clan maintenance inventories than standard LRM or SRM systems. The CASE II torso protection is not optional on this configuration given the ammunition layout. The overall loadout handles most engagement types adequately.

variants.name: CLR-02-X-D
variants.overview: ComStar's advanced research division developed the Celerity as a fifteen-ton drone ultralight quad in 3052, built around a 240-rated XXL engine for walk sixteen, run twenty-four. That speed is the entire design philosophy. The XXL engine at fifteen tons means any significant hit is likely fatal, but at walk sixteen almost nothing can hit it. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk sixteen, run twenty-four at fifteen tons. The XXL engine at this weight means side torso damage is catastrophic. What keeps this machine alive is that at walk sixteen nothing in the field can reliably hit it. The quad configuration provides stability. Pod space is minimal at two tons across the OmniMech variants. The CLR-02-X-D is the original prototype: no weapons, no sensors — just the chassis and engine. Walk sixteen, run twenty-four. The prototype was built to prove the XXL engine performance at this weight class. Endo steel frame. The drone operates on autonomous programming when fielded.
variants.deployment: The CLR-02-X-D is the unarmed proof-of-concept prototype. There is no combat application without weapons. Field the OmniMech variants for operational use. The prototype exists to document what the chassis and engine combination can achieve before any mission equipment is loaded.

variants.name: CLR-03-O
variants.overview: ComStar's advanced research division developed the Celerity as a fifteen-ton drone ultralight quad in 3052, built around a 240-rated XXL engine for walk sixteen, run twenty-four. That speed is the entire design philosophy. The XXL engine at fifteen tons means any significant hit is likely fatal, but at walk sixteen almost nothing can hit it. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk sixteen, run twenty-four at fifteen tons. The XXL engine at this weight means side torso damage is catastrophic. What keeps this machine alive is that at walk sixteen nothing in the field can reliably hit it. The quad configuration provides stability. Pod space is minimal at two tons across the OmniMech variants. The CLR-03-O Prime carries a TAG system in two tons of pod space. Walk sixteen, run twenty-four. TAG designation at walk sixteen speed. The drone can penetrate forward positions and designate targets before any conventional unit can intercept it.
variants.deployment: The Prime is the forward designation variant. Walk sixteen delivers TAG designation to positions no conventional scout can reach quickly enough to intercept. The drone designates and withdraws. The XXL vulnerability means if anything does hit it the mission ends, but at walk sixteen that requires either luck or extraordinary positioning from the opponent.

variants.name: CLR-03-OA
variants.overview: ComStar's advanced research division developed the Celerity as a fifteen-ton drone ultralight quad in 3052, built around a 240-rated XXL engine for walk sixteen, run twenty-four. That speed is the entire design philosophy. The XXL engine at fifteen tons means any significant hit is likely fatal, but at walk sixteen almost nothing can hit it. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk sixteen, run twenty-four at fifteen tons. The XXL engine at this weight means side torso damage is catastrophic. What keeps this machine alive is that at walk sixteen nothing in the field can reliably hit it. The quad configuration provides stability. Pod space is minimal at two tons across the OmniMech variants. Configuration A carries two one-shot SRM-6 launchers. Walk sixteen, run twenty-four. Two one-shot SRM-6s deliver a single close-range missile salvo then are spent. The walk sixteen delivery speed is the design concept — the drone closes to point-blank range before anything can react.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is an autonomous suicide strike variant. Walk sixteen closes to SRM-6 range before opponents can respond. Two one-shot launchers fire once and are gone. The drone continues as an unarmed target afterward. The tactical value is the single guaranteed close-range strike delivered faster than conventional defences can react.

variants.name: CLR-03-OB
variants.overview: ComStar's advanced research division developed the Celerity as a fifteen-ton drone ultralight quad in 3052, built around a 240-rated XXL engine for walk sixteen, run twenty-four. variants.capabilities: Walk sixteen, run twenty-four at fifteen tons. The XXL engine at this weight means side torso damage is catastrophic. What keeps this machine alive is that at walk sixteen nothing in the field can reliably hit it. The quad configuration provides stability. Pod space is minimal at two tons across the OmniMech variants. Configuration B carries an Angel ECM suite with no weapons. Walk sixteen, run twenty-four. The Angel ECM is the most sophisticated electronic warfare system available, mounted on the fastest chassis in existence. The drone delivers ECM disruption to wherever the network needs it.
variants.deployment: Configuration B deploys Angel ECM at walk sixteen. The disruption effect can be delivered to positions far forward of any conventional ECM carrier. No weapons means the drone operates as pure electronic warfare. Walk sixteen keeps it alive against attempts to destroy it. The combination of Angel ECM quality and Celerity speed is difficult to counter.

variants.overview: ComStar's advanced research division developed the Celerity as a fifteen-ton drone ultralight quad in 3052, built around a 240-rated XXL engine for walk sixteen, run twenty-four. variants.capabilities: Walk sixteen, run twenty-four at fifteen tons. The XXL engine at this weight means side torso damage is catastrophic. What keeps this machine alive is that at walk sixteen nothing in the field can reliably hit it. The quad configuration provides stability. Pod space is minimal at two tons across the OmniMech variants. Configuration C carries a remote sensor dispenser and Beagle active probe. Walk sixteen, run twenty-four. The remote sensor dispenser drops sensors across terrain at high speed. The Beagle active probe extends detection range. No weapons.
variants.deployment: Configuration C is the intelligence gathering variant. Walk sixteen allows sensor coverage of an area before opponents can position to intercept. The Beagle probe detects hidden units during the pass. The remote sensor dispenser leaves surveillance equipment in place after the drone withdraws. A reconnaissance platform that operates at speeds making interception nearly impossible.

variants.name: CLR-03-OD
variants.overview: ComStar's advanced research division developed the Celerity as a fifteen-ton drone ultralight quad in 3052, built around a 240-rated XXL engine for walk sixteen, run twenty-four. That speed is the entire design philosophy. The XXL engine at fifteen tons means any significant hit is likely fatal, but at walk sixteen almost nothing can hit it. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk sixteen, run twenty-four at fifteen tons. The XXL engine at this weight means side torso damage is catastrophic. What keeps this machine alive is that at walk sixteen nothing in the field can reliably hit it. The quad configuration provides stability. Pod space is minimal at two tons across the OmniMech variants. Configuration D carries two ER flamers. Walk sixteen, run twenty-four. ER flamers at walk sixteen speed against infantry. The drone reaches infantry positions before defensive responses can be organised and delivers flamer fire at close range.
variants.deployment: Configuration D is the anti-infantry variant. Walk sixteen delivers ER flamer fire to infantry positions faster than screening forces can respond. Against unarmoured formations this is highly effective. Against armoured opposition the ER flamers provide minimal threat. The drone's primary value is the speed of delivery, not the weapons output per se.

variants.name: CLR-03-OE
variants.overview: ComStar's advanced research division developed the Celerity as a fifteen-ton drone ultralight quad in 3052, built around a 240-rated XXL engine for walk sixteen, run twenty-four. Pod space is minimal at two tons across the OmniMech variants. Configuration E carries a Clan ER medium laser and an improved heavy medium laser. Walk sixteen, run twenty-four. Two weapons providing close-range direct fire. The Clan ER medium laser requires Clan maintenance procedures on an IS chassis. The improved heavy medium laser hits harder than a standard equivalent.
variants.deployment: Configuration E is the close-range direct combat variant. Walk sixteen closes distance before defensive fire can be adjusted. The improved heavy medium laser delivers meaningful close-range damage. Clan ER medium maintenance requires procedures beyond standard IS documentation. The XXL vulnerability means a single penetrating hit likely ends the mission.

variants.name: CLR-03OMM 'Rajah'
variants.overview: ComStar's advanced research division developed the Celerity as a fifteen-ton drone ultralight quad in 3052, built around a 240-rated XXL engine for walk sixteen, run twenty-four. That speed is the entire design philosophy. The XXL engine at fifteen tons means any significant hit is likely fatal, but at walk sixteen almost nothing can hit it. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve on the 120-rated standard engine. The Rajah is an arena conversion of the Celerity chassis using a much smaller standard engine. Two ER small lasers. Walk eight is fast by arena standards but a significant reduction from the standard Celerity's walk sixteen.
variants.deployment: The Rajah is an arena machine. The standard engine replacement of the XXL reduces the speed from walk sixteen to walk eight but eliminates the XXL vulnerability that makes the standard Celerity impractical in the closed arenas of Solaris VII where distances are short and evasion is limited. The ER small lasers handle the harassment role the arena configuration requires.

variants.name: CLR-04-R
variants.overview: ComStar's advanced research division developed the Celerity as a fifteen-ton drone ultralight quad in 3052, built around a 240-rated XXL engine for walk sixteen, run twenty-four. That speed is the entire design philosophy. Seven variants including the OmniMech conversion.
variants.capabilities: Walk fifteen, run twenty-two on the 225-rated XXL engine. The CLR-04-R carries a one-shot TSEMP cannon. The smaller engine reduces speed slightly from walk sixteen. The TSEMP fires once and delivers an electromagnetic pulse that disrupts enemy systems. One shot, then the weapon is spent.
variants.deployment: The CLR-04-R is a single-use TSEMP delivery platform. Walk fifteen closes to TSEMP range before conventional defences can respond. The TSEMP fires once — plan accordingly. After the shot the drone carries no weapons. A quick-hit interdiction tool built around a single disruption strike.

variants.name: CLR-05-X
variants.overview: ComStar's advanced research division developed the Celerity as a fifteen-ton drone ultralight quad in 3052, built around a 240-rated XXL engine for walk sixteen, run twenty-four. That speed is the entire design philosophy. Seven variants including the OmniMech conversion.
variants.capabilities: Walk sixteen, run twenty-four on the 240-rated XXL engine, with MASC and an engine supercharger providing even higher burst speed. The CLR-05-X carries no weapons — it is a pure speed platform. Impact-resistant armour and foreleg-mounted spikes for ramming attacks. The spikes deal physical damage on collision.
variants.deployment: The CLR-05-X is built to ram. The impact-resistant armour and foreleg spikes turn the chassis into a weapon itself. MASC and supercharger together achieve speeds that no conventional 'Mech can escape. The ramming attack delivers physical damage at speeds that amplify the force. A single-purpose tool for pilots who understand what it is.

variants.name: CN9-A
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Centurion in 2801 as a fifty-ton medium that balanced ballistic, missile, and energy weapons at a weight class that could afford to carry all three. Walk four, run six on the standard engine. Twenty-five variants have come from that foundation. I have worked on the Centurion across several postings and the parts availability is consistently reliable.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on most variants. The AC/10 — or whatever autocannon appears in a given variant — is the primary weapon. The LRM-10 provides the fire support element. The medium lasers handle close engagement. Standard engine on the conventional variants gives the survivability the design needs in a medium fire support role. The CN9-A is the production standard from 2801: a Luxor D-Series AC/10, a Luxor 3R LRM-10, and two Photech medium lasers. Walk four, run six. The AC/10 arm mount is the design's most recognisable feature. The LRM-10 adds fire support. The mediums handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: The CN9-A has served across the Inner Sphere since 2801 and parts are available from practically every supply chain. It advances steadily, fires the AC/10, and uses the LRM-10 for fire support and the mediums for close defence. Nothing complicated about it.

variants.name: CN9-AH
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Centurion in 2801 as a fifty-ton medium that balanced ballistic, missile, and energy weapons at a weight class that could afford to carry all three. Walk four, run six on the standard engine. Twenty-five variants have come from that foundation. I have worked on the Centurion across several postings and the parts availability is consistently reliable.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on most variants. The AC/10 — or whatever autocannon appears in a given variant — is the primary weapon. The LRM-10 provides the fire support element. The medium lasers handle close engagement. Standard engine on the conventional variants gives the survivability the design needs in a medium fire support role. The CN9-AH replaces the AC/10 and medium lasers with a single AC/20, keeping the LRM-10. Walk four, run six. An AC/20 on a fifty-ton medium delivers devastating close-range hits. Two tons of ammunition is the operational limit — that runs out fast.
variants.deployment: The CN9-AH was introduced in 2874. The AC/20 at close range is the entire combat concept. Two tons of ammunition means ten shots before the Centurion is fighting on LRM-10 fire alone. Pilots who manage that count carefully can achieve results far beyond what the weight class normally delivers.

The medium lasers handle close engagement. Standard engine on the conventional variants gives the survivability the design needs in a medium fire support role. The CN9-AL replaces the AC/10 with a large laser and adds a small laser, keeping the LRM-10 and two medium lasers. Walk four, run six. All-energy direct fire alongside the LRM-10. No ammunition dependency for the direct fire weapons.
variants.deployment: The CN9-AL was fielded in 2915 and found favour with Lyran Commonwealth guerrilla forces who operated without reliable supply lines. No ammunition for the direct fire weapons simplifies logistics significantly. The large laser reach over the standard medium lasers is the weapons improvement. The LRM-10 still requires ammunition management.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Cephalus is a twenty-five ton Word of Blake OmniMech built around a 250-rated Clan XXL engine for walk ten, run fifteen. The ferro-lamellor armour, Chameleon Light Polarization Shield, and Null-Signature System are the design's core. Five configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk ten, run fifteen at twenty-five tons. The Clan XXL at this weight means any significant side torso hit ends the mission. The CLPS and Null-Signature System make it genuinely difficult to detect or target. Specialist maintenance procedures required for the stealth systems. Configuration A carries a TAG and a laser AMS, with seven jump jets. Walk ten, run fifteen, jump seven. The TAG designates for guided munitions. The laser AMS provides missile defence without ammunition. Jump seven extends mobility in rough terrain where ground speed is reduced.
variants.deployment: Configuration A addresses the Prime's terrain dependency with seven jump jets. The TAG and laser AMS combination makes it a force multiplier in formations with guided munitions support. Walk ten, jump seven on a twenty-five ton stealth machine creates extraordinary mobility.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: The Cephalus is a 25-ton Word of Blake OmniMech built around a 250-rated Clan XXL engine that pushes it to walk ten, run fifteen. The defensive electronics suite is the design's core: ferro-lamellor armour, Chameleon Light Polarization Shield, and Null-Signature system make it extraordinarily difficult to detect and target. The trade-off is that offensive capability is minimal on most configurations.
variants.capabilities: The B configuration carries a BattleMech Taser and a light TAG. The Taser delivers an electrical surge that disrupts enemy 'Mech systems rather than destroying armour. The light TAG designates targets for guided munitions. Neither weapon destroys opponents directly. This configuration is built to disable and designate for other units to finish. The XXL engine at twenty-five tons is extraordinarily vulnerable to side torso damage.
variants.deployment: The B configuration is a support and disruption tool, not a combat machine. Warriors assigned B configuration operate in conjunction with heavier units that can exploit the Taser disruption or follow designated targets. The defensive electronics keep it alive in environments where it would otherwise be easy prey. Maintaining the Null-Signature and CLPS systems requires specific technical certification.

variants.deployment: Configuration C is the thermal disruption platform. The plasma cannon and flamer combined with the stealth systems allow thermal attacks from positions opponents cannot locate. Walk ten keeps it out of direct engagement range after firing.

The Nova CEWS enhances targeting across the suite. Heat management at this weight class with heavy laser systems requires careful cycling.

The speed and defensive electronics keep it alive long enough to deliver the heavy laser firepower at close range. Warriors in D configuration use the XXL speed to close distance and fire the heavy lasers, then break contact before the heat builds to dangerous levels. The CASE in both side torsos provides some protection against the ammunition and energy weapon systems.

variants.overview: Ceres Metals Industries built the Cerberus in 3052 as a ninety-five ton assault platform around twin Gauss rifles and a 380-rated XL engine. Walk four, run six. Eleven tons of armour is thin for the weight class and every pilot who works in one knows it. Five variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety-five tons on the XL engine. Eleven tons of armour is the persistent complaint — the design accepts that in exchange for the twin Gauss rifles. The MR-V2 is the original production model: twin Grizzard Model 200 Gauss rifles, four medium pulse lasers, two rear-mounted machine guns, and an AMS. Walk four, run six. The rear machine guns are the problematic feature — volatile ammunition in the back of an already thin-armoured machine.
variants.deployment: The MR-V2 established the Cerberus concept. The twin Gauss rifles at range are the entire tactical identity. The pulse lasers handle close engagement. The rear machine guns are the design weakness that the MR-V3 subsequently addressed. Eleven tons of armour at ninety-five tons is consistently the pilot complaint.

variants.name: MR-5M
variants.overview: Ceres Metals Industries built the Cerberus in 3052 as a ninety-five ton assault platform around twin Gauss rifles and a 380-rated XL engine. Walk four, run six. Eleven tons of armour is thin for the weight class and every pilot who works in one knows it. Five variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety-five tons on the XL engine. Eleven tons of armour is the persistent complaint — the design accepts that in exchange for the twin Gauss rifles. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Gauss rifles provide accurate long-range fire. The medium pulse lasers handle close engagement. The MR-5M replaces the right-arm Gauss rifle with an ER PPC, adds six medium pulse lasers, and keeps the rear machine guns and AMS. Walk four, run six. The ER PPC extends the engagement range over the second Gauss rifle. Six pulse lasers improve close-range capability.
variants.deployment: The MR-5M trades one Gauss rifle for an ER PPC and two additional pulse lasers. The ER PPC range advantage is real. The six pulse lasers make close-range self-defence more capable. The rear machine guns with their ammunition proximity to engine components remain the same concern as the MR-V2.

variants.name: MR-V3
variants.overview: The Cerberus is a 95-ton assault 'Mech built around a 380-rated XL engine, which at this tonnage gives you walk four, run six. The original MR-V2 had rear-mounted machine guns and volatile ammunition in the back of an already lightly armoured assault 'Mech. The MR-V3 addresses that by removing the machine guns and their ammunition entirely and replacing the weight with a ton and a half of additional armour. Simple upgrade, obvious improvement.
variants.capabilities: Twin Grizzard Model 200 Gauss rifles in the arms are the primary weapons, backed by four Blankenburg medium pulse lasers and a McArthur anti-missile system. The Gauss rifles are accurate and hit hard at range. The pulse lasers handle close work and anti-infantry duty. The AMS earns its keep in missile-heavy environments. Eleven tons of armour is still modest for ninety-five tons, which means this machine cannot absorb punishment the way a comparably armed Atlas can.
variants.deployment: The MR-V3 is the preferred Cerberus variant by most commanders who operate the design because removing the rear machine gun ammunition hazard is a straightforward safety improvement with no tactical downside. The Gauss rifles reward pilots who hold range. Closing to pulse laser distance is viable but the armour limitation means it does not survive the same exchanges that heavier-armoured assault designs can afford.

variants.name: MR-6B
variants.overview: Ceres Metals Industries built the Cerberus in 3052 as a ninety-five ton assault platform around twin Gauss rifles and a 380-rated XL engine. Walk four, run six. Eleven tons of armour is thin for the weight class and every pilot who works in one knows it. Five variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety-five tons on the XL engine. Eleven tons of armour is the persistent complaint — the design accepts that in exchange for the twin Gauss rifles. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Gauss rifles provide accurate long-range fire. The medium pulse lasers handle close engagement. The MR-6B removes the machine guns and their ammunition, replaces two pulse lasers with two ER medium lasers, and adds an ER PPC alongside the remaining Gauss rifle. Walk four, run six. Four medium pulse lasers and two ER mediums. No rear machine gun ammunition hazard.
variants.deployment: The MR-6B is the Word of Blake improvement on the MR-5M concept. Removing the machine guns and their ammunition from the rear eliminates the ammunition proximity hazard. The ER mediums add range to the pulse laser close-range suite. A cleaner, less dangerous machine to operate.

variants.name: MR-7K
variants.overview: Ceres Metals Industries built the Cerberus in 3052 as a ninety-five ton assault platform around twin Gauss rifles and a 380-rated XL engine. Walk four, run six. Eleven tons of armour is thin for the weight class and every pilot who works in one knows it. Five variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety-five tons on the XL engine. Eleven tons of armour is the persistent complaint — the design accepts that in exchange for the twin Gauss rifles. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Gauss rifles provide accurate long-range fire. The medium pulse lasers handle close engagement. The MR-7K carries the original twin Gauss rifles alongside four medium X-pulse lasers, replacing the pulse lasers and machine guns. Walk four, run six. The X-pulse lasers are accurate against moving targets at close range. No rear ammunition hazard.
variants.deployment: The MR-7K is the post-Jihad restoration configuration after LexaTech Industries reopened the Hun Ho facility. The twin Gauss rifles are preserved. The X-pulse upgrade over the standard pulse lasers improves close-range accuracy. No machine guns means no rear ammunition concerns. A cleaner configuration than the original.

variants.name: CTS-6X
variants.overview: General Motors built the Cestus in 2550 but the original all-energy design had crippling heat problems that killed the production run. The 6Y rework that fixed it became the production standard. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six on the 260-rated XL engine. Five variants emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The heat problems of the 6X original were addressed in the 6Y, and subsequent variants built from the fixed design. Thirteen and a half tons of armour is good protection for the weight class. The CTS-6X is the original prototype: two PPCs, two large lasers, and two medium pulse lasers on the XL engine. Walk four, run six. The all-energy loadout generated heat the thirteen heat sinks could not manage. The heat management failure was why the design needed a complete rework.
variants.deployment: The CTS-6X is the prototype that demonstrated the original design was not viable in its all-energy configuration. The PPCs and large lasers together created heat levels that made sustained combat impossible. The 6Y rework replaced the PPCs with a Gauss rifle and fixed the problem. The 6X exists in documentation as the cautionary tale.

variants.name: CTS-6Y
variants.overview: General Motors built the Cestus in 2550 but the original all-energy design had crippling heat problems that killed the production run. The 6Y rework that fixed it became the production standard. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six on the 260-rated XL engine. Five variants emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The heat problems of the 6X original were addressed in the 6Y, and subsequent variants built from the fixed design. Thirteen and a half tons of armour is good protection for the weight class. The CTS-6Y is the definitive production model: a Poland Gauss rifle, two large lasers, and two medium lasers. Walk four, run six. The Gauss rifle replaces the PPCs that caused the 6X's heat problems. The heat issue is resolved. Thirteen and a half tons of armour.
variants.deployment: The 6Y fixed what was wrong with the 6X and became the production standard. The Gauss and laser combination handles multiple engagement ranges. The heat management is workable. Good armour for the weight class. Units that got Cestuses after 3040 generally received the 6Y or later variants.

variants.name: CTS-6Y-EC
variants.overview: General Motors built the Cestus in 2550 but the original all-energy design had crippling heat problems that killed the production run. The 6Y rework that fixed it became the production standard. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six on the 260-rated XL engine. Five variants emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The heat problems of the 6X original were addressed in the 6Y, and subsequent variants built from the fixed design. Thirteen and a half tons of armour is good protection for the weight class. The CTS-6Y-EC carries Clan-acquired weapons: an improved Gauss rifle, two improved large lasers, and two prototype ER medium lasers. Walk four, run six. The Clan weapons provide performance improvements over the 6Y. Mixed Clan and IS construction creates a two-track maintenance requirement.
variants.deployment: The EC variant incorporates weapons from Clan Jade Falcon. The improved Gauss and improved large lasers deliver better performance than their IS equivalents. Prototype ER medium lasers require documentation specific to the prototype systems. Mixed Clan and IS maintenance requires techs comfortable with both standards.

variants.name: CTS-6Z
variants.overview: General Motors built the Cestus in 2550 but the original all-energy design had crippling heat problems that killed the production run. The 6Y rework that fixed it became the production standard. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six on the 260-rated XL engine. Five variants emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The heat problems of the 6X original were addressed in the 6Y, and subsequent variants built from the fixed design. Thirteen and a half tons of armour is good protection for the weight class. The CTS-6Z replaces the Gauss rifle with twin PPCs, keeping two large lasers and two medium lasers. Walk four, run six. All-energy across six weapons. The PPCs and large lasers together generate heat the heat sinks must manage carefully.
variants.deployment: The 6Z was developed for commands in the Periphery or regions with unreliable resupply. All-energy means no ammunition logistics. The heat management is tighter than the 6Y — pilots need to pace fire more carefully. Units that found Gauss rifle ammunition impossible to source ran the 6Z.

variants.name: CTS-7A
variants.overview: General Motors built the Cestus in 2550 but the original all-energy design had crippling heat problems that killed the production run. The 6Y rework that fixed it became the production standard. Sixty-five tons, walk four, run six on the 260-rated XL engine. Five variants emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The heat problems of the 6X original were addressed in the 6Y, and subsequent variants built from the fixed design. Thirteen and a half tons of armour is good protection for the weight class. The CTS-7A carries an LB 20-X, two Streak SRM-4s, two ER medium lasers, and two medium pulse lasers. Walk four, run six. The LB 20-X delivers heavy close-range ballistic fire with cluster and slug options. The Streak SRM-4s add guaranteed missile hits.
variants.deployment: The 7A is a close-range brawler variant that departed completely from the original Gauss/laser fire support concept. The LB 20-X at close range combined with Streak SRM-4 and pulse laser saturation overwhelms most opponents. Used in gladiatorial arenas and by mercenary commands with aggressive doctrine. Heat management under sustained close combat requires attention.

variants.name: TRC-4B
variants.overview: Defiance Industries built the Chameleon in the 2500s as a dedicated training platform, deliberately engineering a challenging weapons-to-heat-sink ratio to force cadet pilots to develop heat management discipline. Fifty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six. Eight variants. The design's sensor manipulation capability was an unusual addition for a training machine.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at fifty tons. The deliberately punishing thermal profile is the design intent — the Chameleon teaches heat management by necessity. The sensor manipulation systems require specific calibration that training techs need to understand. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The TRC-4B is the original 2500s design: a large laser, two medium lasers, four small lasers, and two machine guns on the standard 300-rated engine. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The punishing heat balance forces cadets to learn thermal discipline. The sensor manipulation systems provide additional training complexity.
variants.deployment: The TRC-4B has been produced on Hesperus II since the 2500s as the primary SLDF and later IS training platform. The deliberately demanding thermal profile teaches the skills that matter under fire. The machine guns add anti-infantry training scenarios. Parts availability is excellent given the production run.

variants.name: TRC-4C
variants.overview: Defiance Industries built the Chameleon in the 2500s as a dedicated training platform, deliberately engineering a challenging weapons-to-heat-sink ratio to force cadet pilots to develop heat management discipline. Fifty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six. Eight variants. The design's sensor manipulation capability was an unusual addition for a training machine.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at fifty tons. The deliberately punishing thermal profile is the design intent — the Chameleon teaches heat management by necessity. The sensor manipulation systems require specific calibration that training techs need to understand. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The TRC-4C is the Clan-produced copy of the TRC-4B with identical systems and loadout. Walk six, run nine, jump six. Clan-specification comms suites and ejection seats replace the IS equivalents. The training profile is otherwise identical.
variants.deployment: The 4C was produced by Clans to train their own cadets on the Chameleon's demanding thermal profile. The Clan comms and ejection systems are the only meaningful differences from the IS original. Clan warriors who trained on this machine faced the same heat management demands as IS cadets.

variants.name: CLN-7V
variants.overview: Defiance Industries built the Chameleon in the 2500s as a dedicated training platform, deliberately engineering a challenging weapons-to-heat-sink ratio to force cadet pilots to develop heat management discipline. Fifty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six. Eight variants. The design's sensor manipulation capability was an unusual addition for a training machine.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at fifty tons. The deliberately punishing thermal profile is the design intent — the Chameleon teaches heat management by necessity. The sensor manipulation systems require specific calibration that training techs need to understand. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The CLN-7V carries a large laser, two medium lasers, three small lasers, and two machine guns on the standard engine. Walk six, run nine, jump six. One small laser is removed compared to the TRC-4B. The sensor manipulation systems are carried over.
variants.deployment: The 7V is J.B. BattleMechs Incorporated's continuation of the Chameleon line after purchasing the design rights in 3053. Produced on Storfors from 3055 onward. The modest weapons reduction over the TRC-4B is not tactically significant. The machine remains a training platform first.

variants.name: CLN-7W
variants.overview: Defiance Industries built the Chameleon in the 2500s as a dedicated training platform, deliberately engineering a challenging weapons-to-heat-sink ratio to force cadet pilots to develop heat management discipline. Fifty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six. Eight variants. The design's sensor manipulation capability was an unusual addition for a training machine.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at fifty tons. The deliberately punishing thermal profile is the design intent — the Chameleon teaches heat management by necessity. The sensor manipulation systems require specific calibration that training techs need to understand. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The CLN-7W upgrades the large laser to an ER large laser and replaces smaller lasers with a medium pulse laser, adding double heat sinks. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The ER large laser extends engagement range. Double heat sinks improve the thermal balance somewhat.
variants.deployment: The 7W is a performance upgrade of the training design. The ER large laser and medium pulse laser improve combat capability while maintaining the training platform identity. Double heat sinks reduce the deliberately punishing thermal challenge of earlier variants. A more capable machine that still teaches the fundamentals.

variants.name: CLN-7Z
variants.overview: Defiance Industries built the Chameleon in the 2500s as a dedicated training platform, deliberately engineering a challenging weapons-to-heat-sink ratio to force cadet pilots to develop heat management discipline. Fifty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six. Eight variants. The design's sensor manipulation capability was an unusual addition for a training machine.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine. The CLN-7Z carries an ER large laser and two large lasers with twelve double heat sinks. Three large-class energy weapons with twelve heat sinks. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The weapons output is heavier than any previous Chameleon variant.
variants.deployment: The 7Z upgrades the chassis from a training machine to a capable combat platform. Three large-class lasers at walk six is genuine firepower. The XL engine is the vulnerability. Twelve double heat sinks manage the weapons adequately under sustained fire. The sensor manipulation systems are retained.

variants.name: CLN-7VQ 'Q-'Mech'
variants.overview: Defiance Industries built the Chameleon in the 2500s as a dedicated training platform, deliberately engineering a challenging weapons-to-heat-sink ratio to force cadet pilots to develop heat management discipline. Fifty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six. Eight variants. The design's sensor manipulation capability was an unusual addition for a training machine.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine. The Q-Mech carries a heavy PPC with a PPC capacitor, three improved heavy medium lasers, an Angel ECM suite, and a Clan-specification targeting computer. XL engine. The targeting computer improves accuracy across all weapons.
variants.deployment: The Q-Mech was configured to ambush Clan warriors using the Angel ECM to conceal approach and the targeting computer combined with heavy weapons to deliver maximum damage. The heavy PPC capacitor allows overcharge shots at higher heat cost. The improved heavy medium lasers hit hard at close range. A deliberate anti-Clan trap configuration.

variants.name: CLN-8V
variants.overview: Defiance Industries built the Chameleon in the 2500s as a dedicated training platform, deliberately engineering a challenging weapons-to-heat-sink ratio to force cadet pilots to develop heat management discipline. Fifty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six. Eight variants. The design's sensor manipulation capability was an unusual addition for a training machine.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine. The CLN-8V carries an ER large laser, three medium X-pulse lasers, two medium lasers, and two machine guns. CASE II protects ammunition in the centre torso. XL engine vulnerability. The X-pulse lasers are accurate against moving targets.
variants.deployment: The 8V is a post-Jihad combat upgrade. The X-pulse lasers improve accuracy at the ranges a walk-six machine engages at. The ER large laser extends range. CASE II ammunition protection is appropriate given the machine gun rounds in the centre torso. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: CLN-9V
variants.overview: Defiance Industries built the Chameleon in the 2500s as a dedicated training platform, deliberately engineering a challenging weapons-to-heat-sink ratio to force cadet pilots to develop heat management discipline. Fifty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six. Eight variants. The design's sensor manipulation capability was an unusual addition for a training machine.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated light engine. The CLN-9V carries a light PPC, two ER medium lasers, three small X-pulse lasers, and two machine guns. Reinforced internal structure and six tons of heavy ferro-fibrous armour. Light engine — side torso survivability.
variants.deployment: The 9V combines reinforced structure, heavy armour, and a light engine for the most survivable Chameleon variant. The light engine survives hits that kill XL competitors. The reinforced internal structure resists critical component damage. The weapons suite is modest but the survivability improvement over XL variants is substantial.

variants.name: CHP-1N
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Champion in 2602 as a sixty-ton fast striker. Walk five, run seven. Seven variants. The heat management issues of the original design are the consistent criticism across the family.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons. Heat management varies significantly — the 1N's thermal balance is genuinely problematic. Standard engine on conventional variants — side torso survivability. The CHP-1N carries an LB 10-X, an Artemis IV SRM-6, two medium lasers, and two small lasers. Walk five, run seven. Ferro-fibrous armour. The heat balance on the 1N is the known problem — the weapons generate more heat than the heat sinks manage comfortably under sustained fire.
variants.deployment: The 1N established the Champion's battlefield identity. Walk five for a heavy was the speed selling point. The LB 10-X cluster option and Artemis SRM accuracy are the weapons highlights. The heat management problem is real and pilots pace their fire accordingly.

variants.name: CHP-1N2
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Champion in 2602 as a sixty-ton fast striker. Walk five, run seven on the 300-rated standard engine. The speed was the selling point — fast for a heavy 'Mech at the time. Seven variants built on that foundation. The heat management issues of the original design are the consistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons. The 300-rated engine gives it speed unusual for the weight class. Heat management varies significantly across variants — the original 1N's thermal balance is genuinely problematic and most techs who know the design well will tell you so. Standard engine on conventional variants — side torso survivability. The CHP-1N2 is a field modification around 2667 replacing single heat sinks with doubles to address the 1N's thermal problems. Same weapons: LB 10-X, Artemis SRM-6, two medium lasers, two small lasers. Walk five, run seven. The heat problem that plagued the 1N is the driver of this modification.
variants.deployment: The 1N2 is the field fix. Double heat sinks resolve the 1N's chronic heat management problem without changing the weapons. Many 1N machines in service were field-upgraded to this standard because the thermal improvement was worth the work. The weapons profile is identical to the 1N.

variants.name: CHP-1Nb
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Champion in 2602 as a sixty-ton fast striker. Walk five, run seven on the 300-rated standard engine. The speed was the selling point — fast for a heavy 'Mech at the time. Seven variants built on that foundation. The heat management issues of the original design are the consistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons. The 300-rated engine gives it speed unusual for the weight class. Heat management varies significantly across variants — the original 1N's thermal balance is genuinely problematic and most techs who know the design well will tell you so. Standard engine on conventional variants — side torso survivability. The CHP-1Nb upgrades to endo steel construction and double heat sinks, then replaces all the original weapons with a Gauss rifle and an ER PPC. Walk five, run seven. Two weapons — maximum firepower at range, minimal close-range capability.
variants.deployment: The 1Nb transforms the Champion from a balanced striker into a dedicated long-range fire platform. The Gauss and ER PPC combination covers long and medium range effectively. Two weapons means anything that closes to close range faces the Champion without an effective answer. Endo steel and double heat sinks are the structural improvements.

variants.name: CHP-2N
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Champion in 2602 as a sixty-ton fast striker. Walk five, run seven on the 300-rated standard engine. The speed was the selling point — fast for a heavy 'Mech at the time. Seven variants built on that foundation. The heat management issues of the original design are the consistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons. The 300-rated engine gives it speed unusual for the weight class. Heat management varies significantly across variants — the original 1N's thermal balance is genuinely problematic and most techs who know the design well will tell you so. Standard engine on conventional variants — side torso survivability. The CHP-2N uses a Mydron Model B AC/10 instead of the LB 10-X, with standard plating rather than ferro-fibrous armour. Same SRM-6, two medium lasers, two small lasers. Walk five, run seven. Standard armour provides less protection than the ferro-fibrous 1N.
variants.deployment: The CHP-2N is an inferior production variant. Standard plating reduces protection below the 1N standard. The AC/10 versus LB 10-X difference removes the cluster munition option. The heat problems remain from the original design. Units that ran the 2N did so because the 1N was unavailable.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Champion in 2602 as a sixty-ton fast striker. Walk five, run seven on the 300-rated standard engine. The speed was the selling point — fast for a heavy 'Mech at the time. Seven variants built on that foundation. The heat management issues of the original design are the consistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five on the Clan XL engine. The Champion C carries an LB 10-X, an Artemis IV SRM-6, two medium pulse lasers, two ER medium lasers, and two small pulse lasers. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. The pulse and ER medium upgrade improves accuracy and range over the standard mediums.
variants.deployment: The Champion C is the Clan engine upgrade with jump capability added. Jump five on a sixty-ton heavy opens terrain exploitation options the ground-bound variants lack. The weapons upgrade improves accuracy and range coverage. The Clan XL engine requires Clan maintenance procedures alongside IS chassis procedures.

variants.name: CHP-3N
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Champion in 2602 as a sixty-ton fast striker. Walk five, run seven on the 300-rated standard engine. The speed was the selling point — fast for a heavy 'Mech at the time. Seven variants built on that foundation. The heat management issues of the original design are the consistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons. The 300-rated engine gives it speed unusual for the weight class. Heat management varies significantly across variants — the original 1N's thermal balance is genuinely problematic and most techs who know the design well will tell you so. Standard engine on conventional variants — side torso survivability. The CHP-3N uses an XL engine and carries two large lasers alongside the standard LB 10-X, SRM-6, two medium lasers, and two small lasers. Walk five, run seven. The large lasers add direct fire range that the standard champion lacks. XL engine — side torso vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The CHP-3N extends the Champion's direct fire reach with two large lasers. The heat generation under sustained fire from the large lasers and autocannon together is aggressive. The XL engine enables the additional weapons. The LB 10-X and missile systems are preserved from the original concept.

variants.name: CHP-3P
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Champion in 2602 as a sixty-ton fast striker. Walk five, run seven on the 300-rated standard engine. The speed was the selling point — fast for a heavy 'Mech at the time. Seven variants built on that foundation. The heat management issues of the original design are the consistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons. The 300-rated engine gives it speed unusual for the weight class. Heat management varies significantly across variants — the original 1N's thermal balance is genuinely problematic and most techs who know the design well will tell you so. Standard engine on conventional variants — side torso survivability. The CHP-3P uses an XL engine and carries an Ultra AC/10, four ER medium lasers, and an iNarc launcher. Walk five, run seven. The iNarc plants homing beacons on targets for guided munitions. The UAC/10 provides sustained ballistic fire. The ER mediums cover direct energy engagement.
variants.deployment: The CHP-3P is the designation and precision fire variant. The iNarc multiplies the effectiveness of every missile-armed unit in the formation. The UAC/10 double-tap rate maintains ballistic pressure. The ER mediums cover direct energy engagement. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: CGR-1A1
variants.overview: Chargers were originally built as ultra-heavy recon machines for the Star League, and the five-small-laser weapons fit on the 400-rated engine in an eighty-ton chassis is one of the most discussed compromises in BattleMech design history. Walk five, run seven. The design has evolved significantly across ten-plus variants — later models are far more capable than the original.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at eighty tons on the 400-rated engine. The standard engine provides side torso survivability. The original CGR-1A1's five small lasers are token firepower — the design's primary weapon was always its mass and speed. Later variants replaced the small lasers with weapons appropriate for the weight class. The CGR-1A1 is the 2665 production model carrying five small lasers and nothing else. Walk five, run seven on the 400-rated standard engine. The small lasers are there to show something on the weapons loadout. The actual combat capability at this size and speed is the eighty-ton mass moving at walk five.
variants.deployment: The CGR-1A1 is what happens when a design prioritises speed over firepower at assault weight. Walk five on eighty tons was exceptional in 2665. The five small lasers are practically symbolic. Opponents at the time would close range hoping for easy kills and encounter an eighty-ton machine that could physically bat them aside. Over a thousand units produced despite the obvious armament problem.

variants.name: CGR-1L
variants.overview: Chargers were built as ultra-heavy recon machines for the Star League, and the five-small-laser weapons fit on the 400-rated engine in an eighty-ton chassis remains one of the most discussed compromises in BattleMech design history. Walk five, run seven. The design has evolved significantly — later models are far more capable than the original.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at eighty tons. The standard engine provides side torso survivability. The original CGR-1A1's five small lasers are token firepower — later variants replaced them with weapons appropriate for the weight class. The CGR-1L replaces the five small lasers with two medium lasers and a large laser, at the cost of nearly half the armour. Walk five, run seven. The weapons are a genuine improvement. The armour reduction is severe.
variants.deployment: The 1L improved firepower substantially over the original while stripping the armour. The large laser and medium lasers give the machine actual combat capability rather than the token small lasers. The armour reduction means pilots cannot absorb the fire that walk five allows opponents to deliver. A tradeoff that varies in wisdom based on the tactical environment.

variants.name: CGR-1A5
variants.overview: Chargers were built as ultra-heavy recon machines for the Star League, and the five-small-laser weapons fit on the 400-rated engine in an eighty-ton chassis remains one of the most discussed compromises in BattleMech design history. Walk five, run seven. The design has evolved significantly — later models are far more capable than the original.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at eighty tons. The standard engine provides side torso survivability. The original CGR-1A1's five small lasers are token firepower — later variants replaced them with weapons appropriate for the weight class. The CGR-1A5 uses a 320-rated engine for walk four, run six, and carries an AC/20, two SRM-6 launchers, a medium laser, and a small laser. Walk four — slower than the standard Charger. The smaller engine freed mass for the AC/20 and SRM-6s. Two tons of AC/20 ammunition.
variants.deployment: The 1A5 was reworked at Grand Base and Tikonov by Earthwerks Ltd. The trade of speed for an AC/20 changes the machine completely — from a fast scout to a close-range assault platform. Walk four is a significant reduction. The AC/20 and SRM-6 combination at close range is devastating. Two tons of AC/20 ammunition runs out fast.

variants.name: CGR-SB 'Challenger'
variants.overview: Chargers were built as ultra-heavy recon machines for the Star League, and the five-small-laser weapons fit on the 400-rated engine in an eighty-ton chassis remains one of the most discussed compromises in BattleMech design history. Walk five, run seven. The design has evolved significantly — later models are far more capable than the original.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four on the 240-rated engine. The Challenger carries four large lasers and a medium laser. Walk three is the severe speed penalty for the smaller engine. Four large lasers is substantial energy firepower for the weight class. All-energy with no ammunition dependency.
variants.deployment: The Challenger drops speed dramatically for firepower. Walk three on an eighty-ton machine is essentially a stationary fire position. Four large lasers without ammunition concerns suit units operating without reliable supply. The heat from four large lasers under sustained fire requires management. Named machine — maintain to the specific configuration documentation.

variants.name: CGR-1A9

variants.deployment: The CGR-3K debuted in 3049 as the primary Clan Invasion era upgrade. Jump five at eighty tons opens terrain exploitation options no other assault design of the period could match. The LRM-20 adds fire support. The pulse laser accuracy is a genuine upgrade from the small lasers of the original. XL engine vulnerability is the tradeoff.

variants.deployment: The CGR-C emerged around 3052 as the DCMS adopted C3 networking doctrine. The C3 slave adds network targeting data to the 3K's weapons. One pulse laser is the trade. The extra LRM ammunition extends fire support endurance. XL engine vulnerability applies.

The LB 20-X and Streak SRM-6 combination at close range is overwhelming. The ER mediums handle longer engagement. Urban combat and dense terrain where the armour advantage matters most suits this variant.

The five RL-10s provide a single fifty-round alpha strike then are spent. The medium laser carries the rest of the engagement.
variants.deployment: The 2A2 appeared around 3064. The five RL-10 alpha strike is the design concept. After firing, the machine has only a medium laser. The ferro-fibrous armour was added to keep it alive long enough to close range for the alpha strike. Walk five delivers the RL-10 volley fast.

variants.deployment: The Kamikaze uses improved jump jets for exceptional jump mobility at eighty tons. Jump six creates approach angles opponents cannot predict. The heavy PPC and light PPC combination covers medium and close range. The MML-9 adds SRM/LRM missile flexibility. XL engine vulnerability applies. The jump capability is the design's primary tactical tool.

variants.deployment: The 1X1 is a single-unit technology demonstrator from StarCorps Industries' Son Hoa facility. The dual laser AMS and TAG make it a designation and missile defence platform. Experimental designation means prototype documentation applies. Not a production variant.
