TSM activates at elevated heat, boosting physical attack strength. The sword delivers melee damage.
variants.deployment: The 3Kr is a TSM melee variant. The combined energy weapons generate heat to trigger TSM, enhancing the sword strikes and ground speed. The sword on an eighty-ton machine delivers devastating melee damage. Jump five delivers the sword to range from unexpected angles. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: Chargers were built as ultra-heavy recon machines for the Star League, and the five-small-laser weapons fit on the 400-rated engine in an eighty-ton chassis remains one of the most discussed compromises in BattleMech design history. Walk five, run seven. The design has evolved significantly — later models are far more capable than the original.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven on the 400-rated Clan XL engine. The Charger C carries four improved heavy medium lasers and an ER medium laser, with ferro-lamellor armour, an Angel ECM suite, and a Bloodhound Active Probe. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. The improved heavy medium lasers hit harder than standard equivalents. The Bloodhound extends sensor range.
variants.deployment: The Charger C replaces IS systems with Clan components, converting the chassis into a close-range direct fire and electronic warfare platform. The Angel ECM degrades enemy targeting. The Bloodhound active probe detects hidden units. The improved heavy medium lasers are the primary weapons. Clan engine maintenance alongside IS chassis procedures creates a two-track requirement.

variants.name: CMA-1S
variants.overview: The Draconis Combine, Federated Commonwealth, Free Worlds League, and Lyran Commonwealth jointly developed the Chimera in 3053. Forty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six on the 240-rated XL engine. The design resulted from political compromise as much as tactical planning. Three variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The endo steel chassis provides structural efficiency. The jump capability and speed combination is the design's tactical strength. The CMA-1S carries an ER large laser, an ER medium laser, an MRM-20, and a machine gun. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The ER large laser handles long-range direct fire. The MRM-20 delivers medium-range missile volume. The ER medium covers closer engagement. The machine gun handles infantry.
variants.deployment: The CMA-1S is the base production model that emerged from the inter-House collaboration. Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty tons is genuine tactical mobility. The MRM-20 at medium range and ER large laser at long range cover most engagement scenarios. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: CMA-C
variants.overview: The Draconis Combine, Federated Commonwealth, Free Worlds League, and Lyran Commonwealth jointly developed the Chimera in 3053. Forty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six on the 240-rated XL engine. The design resulted from political compromise as much as tactical planning. Three variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The endo steel chassis provides structural efficiency. The jump capability and speed combination is the design's tactical strength. The CMA-C removes the machine gun to fit a C3 slave unit, keeping the ER large laser, ER medium, and MRM-20. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The C3 slave integrates targeting data from a network lance. The MRM-20 accuracy benefits from C3 network targeting solutions.
variants.deployment: The CMA-C is the network-integrated Chimera. The C3 slave adds targeting coordination with lancemates. The weapons loadout is otherwise identical to the 1S. XL engine vulnerability applies. DCMS network lance doctrine drives the majority of CMA-C deployments.

variants.name: CMA-2K

Forty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six on the 240-rated XL engine. The design resulted from political compromise as much as tactical planning. Three variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 280-rated XL engine. The CMA-2K carries a snub-nose PPC, four medium lasers, a small pulse laser, and a small laser, with a sword in the right arm and a C3 slave. Walk seven. The sword delivers melee damage. The snub-nose PPC covers medium range.
variants.deployment: The CMA-2K is the close-combat Chimera variant with walk seven speed and a sword. The sword combined with walk seven and jump seven delivers melee damage from unexpected angles. The C3 slave adds network coordination alongside the close-range weapons suite. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: CDA-2A
variants.overview: Bergan Industries built the Cicada in 2740 as a forty-ton scout designed around a 320-rated engine. Walk eight, run twelve. The speed is the entire identity — this machine exists to go places quickly, not to fight. Nine variants have emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at forty tons. The 320-rated engine at forty tons is the design's defining feature. Limited firing arcs from the side-torso weapon placements are the consistent tactical constraint. The machine was never meant to stand and fight — it was meant to be fast and hard to hit. The CDA-2A is the original 2740 production model: two medium lasers and a small laser on the 320-rated engine. Walk eight, run twelve. Side-torso mounted medium lasers with limited arc. The small laser is in the centre torso. The Sloane 220 targeting system improves accuracy across the weapons.
variants.deployment: The 2A is the original and the most common Cicada in service. Walk eight keeps it out of trouble. The two medium lasers and small laser handle contacts that cannot be avoided. The side-torso mounting limits firing arcs — the pilot cannot engage targets directly to the rear without turning. Scouts learn to use the targeting system to compensate.

variants.name: CDA-2B
variants.overview: Bergan Industries built the Cicada in 2740 as a forty-ton scout designed around a 320-rated engine. Walk eight, run twelve. The speed is the entire identity — this machine exists to go places quickly, not to fight. Nine variants have emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at forty tons. The 320-rated engine at forty tons is the design's defining feature. Limited firing arcs from the side-torso weapon placements are the consistent tactical constraint. The machine was never meant to stand and fight — it was meant to be fast and hard to hit. The CDA-2B replaces the small laser with a flamer. Walk eight, run twelve. The flamer handles infantry and creates area denial. The two medium lasers remain the primary weapons. Half a ton of armour is traded for the flamer.
variants.deployment: The 2B is the anti-infantry variant. The flamer handles infantry formations the medium lasers would waste shots on. The armour reduction is minor but the machine was already lightly armoured — in practice scouts running the 2B accept slightly less protection in exchange for infantry capability.

variants.name: CDA-3C
variants.overview: Bergan Industries built the Cicada in 2740 as a forty-ton scout designed around a 320-rated engine. Walk eight, run twelve. The speed is the entire identity — this machine exists to go places quickly, not to fight. Nine variants have emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at forty tons. The 320-rated engine at forty tons is the design's defining feature. Limited firing arcs from the side-torso weapon placements are the consistent tactical constraint. The machine was never meant to stand and fight — it was meant to be fast and hard to hit. The CDA-3C uses a 280-rated engine for walk seven, run ten and carries a PPC and two machine guns. Walk seven — reduced from the standard walk eight. The PPC provides genuine long-range punch. The machine guns handle infantry from leg-mounted positions.
variants.deployment: The 3C trades one point of walk speed for a PPC that makes it genuinely threatening at long range. The leg-mounted machine guns handle infantry while the PPC fires. Walk seven is still fast. The PPC heat requires management. The Sloane targeting system makes the PPC more accurate than it would be on other chassis.

variants.name: CDA-3M
variants.overview: Bergan Industries built the Cicada in 2740 as a forty-ton scout designed around a 320-rated engine. Walk eight, run twelve. The speed is the entire identity — this machine exists to go places quickly, not to fight. Nine variants have emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve on the 320-rated XL engine. The CDA-3M carries a UAC/5, two medium lasers, and a small pulse laser. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The UAC/5 adds sustained ballistic fire alongside the energy weapons. The small pulse laser improves close-range accuracy.
variants.deployment: The 3M introduced in 3049 adds the UAC/5 to the standard medium laser complement. The sustained ballistic fire at walk eight speed creates consistent harassment pressure. XL engine adds the standard vulnerability. One ton of UAC/5 ammunition manages adequately for a scout that is not meant to be in sustained combat.

variants.name: CDA-3F
variants.overview: Bergan Industries built the Cicada in 2740 as a forty-ton scout designed around a 320-rated engine. Walk eight, run twelve. The speed is the entire identity — this machine exists to go places quickly, not to fight. Nine variants have emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve, jump eight on the 320-rated XL engine. The CDA-3F carries an ER PPC and two medium lasers. XL engine. Jump eight at forty tons. The ER PPC provides significant long-range punch. The medium lasers handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: The 3F debuted in 3052 based on Clan Invasion combat reports. Walk eight and jump eight make this the most mobile Cicada variant. The ER PPC threatens opponents well above this weight class. XL engine vulnerability means getting hit is dangerous. The Sloane targeting system makes the ER PPC highly accurate.

variants.name: CDA-3G
variants.overview: Bergan Industries built the Cicada in 2740 as a forty-ton scout designed around a 320-rated engine. Walk eight, run twelve. The speed is the entire identity — this machine exists to go places quickly, not to fight. Nine variants have emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve, jump eight on the 320-rated XL engine. The CDA-3G carries an ER large laser, two medium lasers, and a Beagle active probe. XL engine. The ER large laser replaces the ER PPC with a cooler but shorter-range weapon. The Beagle extends sensor coverage for reconnaissance.
variants.deployment: The 3G trades ER PPC punch for ER large laser heat efficiency and Beagle sensor capability. The Beagle adds detection range beyond the Sloane targeting system's combat role. Walk eight, jump eight maintains the 3F's mobility. The ER large laser is less threatening at range but more sustainable under sustained scout operations.

variants.name: CDA-3MA
variants.overview: Bergan Industries built the Cicada in 2740 as a forty-ton scout designed around a 320-rated engine. Walk eight, run twelve. The speed is the entire identity — this machine exists to go places quickly, not to fight. Nine variants have emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve on the 320-rated XL engine. The CDA-3MA carries a snub-nose PPC, two medium lasers, and a small pulse laser. XL engine. The snub-nose PPC replaces the UAC/5 with a weapon that works at short to medium range without minimum range complications. No jump jets.
variants.deployment: The 3MA replaces the 3M's UAC/5 with a snub-nose PPC and improves armour. No jump capability. The snub-nose avoids the minimum range gap of standard PPC designs. The weapons loadout is simpler than the UAC/5 variant. The armour improvement over the 3M is meaningful for a machine that gets into close terrain.

variants.name: CDA-3P
variants.overview: Bergan Industries built the Cicada in 2740 as a forty-ton scout designed around a 320-rated engine. Walk eight, run twelve. The speed is the entire identity — this machine exists to go places quickly, not to fight. Nine variants have emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten on the 280-rated XL engine. The CDA-3P carries a heavy PPC and four ER medium lasers. Walk seven — reduced. The heavy PPC hits harder than a standard PPC at medium range. Four ER mediums provide substantial close-range energy output. XL engine.
variants.deployment: The 3P is the firepower Cicada, trading walk speed for heavier weapons. Walk seven is still fast by most standards. The heavy PPC and four ER mediums together create significant energy output for forty tons. The heavy PPC minimum range gap is covered by the ER mediums. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: CDA-4A
variants.overview: Bergan Industries built the Cicada in 2740 as a forty-ton scout designed around a 320-rated engine. Walk eight, run twelve. The speed is the entire identity — this machine exists to go places quickly, not to fight. Nine variants have emerged from that foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve on the 320-rated XL engine. The CDA-4A carries two medium VSP lasers and a medium re-engineered laser. XL engine. The VSP lasers adapt damage to range. The re-engineered laser disrupts multiple heat sinks on target 'Mechs simultaneously. Three weapons at walk eight.
variants.deployment: The 4A is the most technically advanced Cicada variant. The re-engineered laser's heat degradation effect combined with VSP adaptability creates a different threat profile than standard energy weapons. Walk eight and the Sloane targeting system make all three weapons more effective. Re-engineered laser maintenance requires specific procedures beyond standard laser calibration.

variants.name: CLNT-1-2R
variants.overview: Andoran Industries built the Clint in 2607 for the SLDF as a recon 'Mech with the Sloane 220 targeting system giving it exceptional sensor capability. Forty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six on the 240-rated engine. Six variants. The targeting system is the feature that distinguishes it from comparable weight class competitors.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty tons. The Sloane 220 targeting system is the chassis identity — it improves accuracy across the whole weapons suite. The jump six capability suits the recon role. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. Ammunition management for the autocannon variants is the consistent operational concern. The CLNT-1-2R is the original SLDF prototype: an Armstrong Buster AC/10 and a single medium laser. Walk six, run nine, no jump. The AC/10 provides direct ballistic fire. The medium laser handles close backup. No jump jets on the prototype.
variants.deployment: The 1-2R is the prototype configuration before the production jump jets and second medium laser were added. The AC/10 and single medium laser are functional but limited for a forty-ton design. The Sloane 220 targeting system's accuracy benefits are present from the start.

variants.name: CLNT-2-3T
variants.overview: Andoran Industries built the Clint in 2607 for the SLDF as a recon 'Mech with the Sloane 220 targeting system giving it exceptional sensor capability. Forty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six on the 240-rated engine. Six variants. The targeting system is the feature that distinguishes it from comparable weight class competitors.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty tons. The Sloane 220 targeting system is the chassis identity — it improves accuracy across the whole weapons suite. The jump six capability suits the recon role. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. Ammunition management for the autocannon variants is the consistent operational concern. The CLNT-2-3T is the production standard: an Armstrong J11 AC/5, two medium lasers, and jump six. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The AC/5 provides ballistic harassment at range. The medium lasers handle close engagement. The Sloane 220 targeting system improves accuracy across the suite.
variants.deployment: The 2-3T is the Clint that most pilots and techs know. The AC/5 and two medium lasers with jump six and the Sloane accuracy system makes this an effective recon and harassment platform. Parts availability is good through most supply chains.

variants.name: CLNT-2-4T
variants.overview: Andoran Industries built the Clint in 2607 for the SLDF as a recon 'Mech with the Sloane 220 targeting system giving it exceptional sensor capability. Forty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six on the 240-rated engine. Six variants. The targeting system is the feature that distinguishes it from comparable weight class competitors.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty tons. The Sloane 220 targeting system is the chassis identity — it improves accuracy across the whole weapons suite. The jump six capability suits the recon role. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. Ammunition management for the autocannon variants is the consistent operational concern. The CLNT-2-4T carries twin AC/2s and a medium laser on the standard engine. Walk six, run nine, no jump. The AC/2 pair provides long-range harassment fire. The medium laser handles close backup. No jump jets. More ammunition for longer fire missions.
variants.deployment: The 2-4T trades jump capability for twin AC/2 long-range harassment. No jump jets is the significant reduction for a design built around mobility. The AC/2 pair provides consistent long-range pressure. Pilots who valued range over terrain exploitation preferred this variant.

variants.name: CLNT-2-3T (Denton)
variants.overview: Andoran Industries built the Clint in 2607 for the SLDF as a recon 'Mech with the Sloane 220 targeting system giving it exceptional sensor capability. Forty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six on the 240-rated engine. Six variants. The targeting system is the feature that distinguishes it from comparable weight class competitors.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty tons. The Sloane 220 targeting system is the chassis identity — it improves accuracy across the whole weapons suite. The jump six capability suits the recon role. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. Ammunition management for the autocannon variants is the consistent operational concern. The Denton is a named variant replacing the autocannon with a large laser and adding four heat sinks, keeping two medium lasers and jump six. Walk six, run nine, jump six. All-energy with no ammunition dependency. The large laser extends direct fire range over the standard medium lasers.
variants.deployment: The Denton emerged from a Federated Suns field modification. The large laser and no autocannon removes ammunition dependency entirely. The Sloane targeting system makes the large laser more accurate. Jump six combined with the larger energy suite suits the recon harassment role without supply concern.

variants.name: CLNT-2-3U
variants.overview: Andoran Industries built the Clint in 2607 for the SLDF as a recon 'Mech with the Sloane 220 targeting system giving it exceptional sensor capability. Forty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six on the 240-rated engine. Six variants. The targeting system is the feature that distinguishes it from comparable weight class competitors.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty tons. The Sloane 220 targeting system is the chassis identity — it improves accuracy across the whole weapons suite. The jump six capability suits the recon role. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. Ammunition management for the autocannon variants is the consistent operational concern. The CLNT-2-3U carries an ER PPC and two medium pulse lasers with double heat sinks on the standard engine. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The ER PPC extends threat range significantly. The medium pulse lasers improve close-range accuracy. Double heat sinks manage the increased energy load.
variants.deployment: The 2-3U is the ER PPC upgrade variant. The ER PPC range combined with the Sloane 220 targeting system accuracy creates a genuine long-range threat from a forty-ton scout. The pulse lasers handle close engagement accurately. Double heat sinks allow sustained ER PPC fire at a pace single heat sinks could not support.

variants.name: CLNT-5U
variants.overview: The Clint has been around since 2607 and the various variants span a significant technology range. The CLNT-5U is a modern upgrade built on a light engine, giving walk six, run nine, jump six at forty tons. The light engine trades some speed potential for better side torso survivability compared to an XL. It carries an ER large laser, three ER medium lasers, and a TAG system on an endo steel chassis.
variants.capabilities: The ER large laser is the primary weapon and it gives the 5U genuine reach for a medium 'Mech. Three ER mediums provide backup fire and are the weapons I keep calibrated most carefully: they drift under heavy firing cycles and the Sloane targeting system that has always been the Clint's strength amplifies both accurate and inaccurate shots equally. The TAG system and C3 slave make this a force multiplier well beyond its direct combat value. Light engine survivability is real: side torso hits that would kill an XL-equipped competitor leave this running.
variants.deployment: The 5U works as a scout-striker with C3 network integration. The TAG designates targets for artillery and guided munitions, the C3 slave feeds targeting data to lancemates, and the ER lasers handle anything that needs to be dealt with directly. The endo steel chassis reduces maintenance complexity compared to earlier Clint variants. This is one of the cleaner modern Clint configurations to keep in the field.

variants.name: CLNT-2-3UL
variants.overview: Andoran Industries built the Clint in 2607 for the SLDF as a forty-ton recon 'Mech built around the Sloane 220 targeting system. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the standard 240-rated engine. Ten variants. The targeting system improves accuracy across the entire weapons suite.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty tons. The Sloane 220 targeting system is the chassis identity. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. Jump six suits the recon role. The CLNT-2-3UL carries a plasma rifle and two ER medium lasers on the standard engine. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The plasma rifle superheats targets while dealing damage. Three tons of plasma rifle ammunition. The ER mediums provide energy backup. Double heat sinks manage the thermal load.
variants.deployment: The 2-3UL adds thermal disruption capability to the Clint's recon profile. The plasma rifle forces heat problems on opposing 'Mechs while the Sloane 220 makes both weapons accurate. Standard engine survivability. Plasma rifle ammunition requires separate supply management.

variants.name: CLNT-3-3T
variants.overview: Andoran Industries built the Clint in 2607 for the SLDF as a forty-ton recon 'Mech built around the Sloane 220 targeting system. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the standard 240-rated engine. Ten variants. The targeting system improves accuracy across the entire weapons suite.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty tons. The Sloane 220 targeting system is the chassis identity. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. Jump six suits the recon role. The CLNT-3-3T carries a light AC/5 and two medium lasers on the standard engine, with ferro-fibrous armour. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The light AC/5 is more ammunition-efficient than a standard AC/5. Ferro-fibrous armour improves protection. Taurian Concordat production.
variants.deployment: The 3-3T was produced by Pinard Protectorates Limited in the Taurian Concordat during the Jihad. The ferro-fibrous armour and lighter AC/5 addressed the original Clint's vulnerability while preserving the design's tactical role. Taurian supply chains support this variant without difficulty.

variants.name: CLNT-6S
variants.overview: Andoran Industries built the Clint in 2607 for the SLDF as a forty-ton recon 'Mech built around the Sloane 220 targeting system. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the standard 240-rated engine. Ten variants. The targeting system improves accuracy across the entire weapons suite.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten on the 280-rated light engine. The CLNT-6S carries two ER large lasers, two ER medium lasers, and an ER small laser. Light engine — side torso survivability. Walk seven is faster than the standard Clint. All-energy, no ammunition dependency. Heat from the full suite simultaneously requires cycling discipline.
variants.deployment: The 6S is the direct combatant Clint — more firepower at the cost of the standard jump capability. The light engine survivability advantage over XL variants is real. Walk seven closes range faster than the standard engine Clints. The all-energy loadout suits independent operations. No jump jets changes the tactical profile significantly.

variants.name: CLNT-3-4T
variants.overview: Andoran Industries built the Clint in 2607 for the SLDF as a forty-ton recon 'Mech built around the Sloane 220 targeting system. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the standard 240-rated engine. Ten variants. The targeting system improves accuracy across the entire weapons suite.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 240-rated XL engine. The CLNT-3-4T carries an LB 5-X and two medium X-pulse lasers. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The LB 5-X provides cluster and slug ballistic options. The X-pulse lasers are accurate against moving targets. Taurian Concordat production incorporating Brahma technology.
variants.deployment: The 3-4T is the follow-on to the 3-3T, incorporating X-pulse lasers from concurrent Brahma development and an LB 5-X. The X-pulse accuracy combined with the Sloane 220 targeting system is the standout capability. XL engine adds the standard vulnerability the 3-3T avoided.

variants.overview: Clan Snow Raven developed the Clint IIC in 2849 to address structural problems in the original prototype frame. Forty tons, walk six, run nine, jump eight on the 240-rated Clan XL. Two variants. The improved jump jets provide exceptional aerial mobility.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump eight at forty tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump eight is exceptional mobility for a forty-ton design. Clan construction quality. Ten double heat sinks are the chassis constant. Variant 2 carries five medium pulse lasers across the centre torso, left torso, and right arm. Walk six, run nine, jump eight. All-energy with no ammunition dependency. Five pulse lasers at close range on a forty-ton machine with jump eight is the design concept. Ten heat sinks is lean for five pulse lasers under sustained fire.
variants.deployment: The Clint IIC 2 is built for close-range engagement delivered from unexpected jump angles. Jump eight at forty tons means the warrior arrives at close range before opponents can react. Five medium pulse lasers deliver accurate volume fire. The heat sinks are insufficient for sustained simultaneous fire — cycling is mandatory.

variants.name: 2L 'Leia'
variants.overview: Clan Snow Raven developed the Clint IIC in 2849 to address structural problems in the original prototype frame. Forty tons, walk six, run nine, jump eight on the 240-rated Clan XL. Two variants. The improved jump jets provide exceptional aerial mobility.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump eight at forty tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump eight is exceptional mobility for a forty-ton design. Clan construction quality. Ten double heat sinks are the chassis constant. The Leia is an arena variant carrying a large VSP laser, a medium re-engineered laser, and two ER medium lasers, linked to a Clan targeting computer. Walk six, run nine, no jump. Ballistic-reinforced armour. The targeting computer improves accuracy across the weapons. The re-engineered laser disrupts multiple heat sinks on targets.
variants.deployment: The Leia is configured for Solaris VII arena combat. No jump jets changes the tactical profile from the jump-mobile Variant 2. The targeting computer combined with VSP and re-engineered laser technology creates accurate and disruptive fire. The ballistic-reinforced armour suits arena environments where ballistic fire is prevalent.

variants.name: CBR-02
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Cobra in 3016 as a forty-five ton fire support platform. Walk five, run seven on the 225-rated engine. The distinctive hood-like targeting array and dual LRM-15 launchers define the design. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at forty-five tons. The twin LRM-15 launchers are the whole point. The medium lasers handle anything that closes inside minimum range. Standard or light engine depending on variant. The CBR-02 is the original: twin Coventry Star Fire LRM-15s, two Defiance medium lasers, on a 225-rated standard engine with endo steel chassis. Walk five, run seven. The LRM-15s provide the primary fire support. The mediums handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: The CBR-02 is straightforward fire support — twin LRM-15s from a stand-off position with medium lasers for self-defence. The endo steel chassis keeps the mass manageable. Standard engine survivability. The hood-like targeting array improves LRM accuracy. Parts available through most supply chains.

variants.name: CBR-03
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Cobra in 3016 as a forty-five ton fire support platform. Walk five, run seven on the 225-rated engine. The distinctive hood-like targeting array and dual LRM-15 launchers define the design. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven on the 225-rated light engine. The CBR-03 carries twin Artemis IV-guided LRM-15s and two ER medium lasers, with an extra-light gyro and endo steel. Light engine — side torso survivability. Artemis guidance improves LRM accuracy. The ER mediums extend the backup energy range.
variants.deployment: The CBR-03 addresses the original's most criticised weaknesses. The light engine improves side torso survivability over the standard engine without adding XL vulnerability. Artemis IV guidance makes each LRM round count more. The ER mediums extend the defensive energy envelope. A well-rounded upgrade of the original concept.

variants.name: CL-P3
variants.overview: The Colossus was built in 3053 as an arena combat 'Mech around a 285-rated engine, walk three, run four, jump three on a ninety-five ton chassis. Three variants. The arm-mounted shields and arena-oriented design distinguish it from conventional assault platforms.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three at ninety-five tons. The 285-rated engine at this weight leaves room for heavy weapons and shields. The jump capability at assault weight is the tactical differentiator. Arm shields provide passive damage reduction. The CL-P3 is the original 3053 prototype: a standard AC/20, two large pulse lasers, and two medium pulse lasers with coolant pods. Walk three, run four, jump three. Six coolant pods manage the heavy weapons heat load. The arm shields were not yet fitted on the prototype.
variants.deployment: The CL-P3 is the prototype that suffered reliability problems before the production 4S fixed them. Coolant pods rather than armoured shields. The AC/20 and pulse laser combination is the arena combat concept. Prototype documentation applies for maintenance.

variants.name: CLS-4S
variants.overview: The Colossus was built in 3053 as an arena combat 'Mech around a 285-rated engine, walk three, run four, jump three on a ninety-five ton chassis. Three variants. The arm-mounted shields and arena-oriented design distinguish it from conventional assault platforms.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three at ninety-five tons. The 285-rated engine at this weight leaves room for heavy weapons and shields. The jump capability at assault weight is the tactical differentiator. Arm shields provide passive damage reduction. The CLS-4S is the production model: an LB 20-X, two large X-pulse lasers, and two medium X-pulse lasers, with armoured arm shields replacing the coolant pods. Walk three, run four, jump three. The armoured shields provide passive damage reduction. The X-pulse lasers are accurate against moving targets.
variants.deployment: The 4S fixed the CL-P3 reliability problems with armoured shields and upgraded X-pulse weapons. The LB 20-X provides cluster and slug ballistic options over the standard AC/20. The X-pulse accuracy is the weapons upgrade. Armoured shields provide real protection for the arm weapon systems in arena combat.

variants.name: CLS-5S
variants.overview: The Colossus was built in 3053 as an arena combat 'Mech around a 285-rated engine, walk three, run four, jump three on a ninety-five ton chassis. Three variants. The arm-mounted shields and arena-oriented design distinguish it from conventional assault platforms.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three at ninety-five tons. The 285-rated engine at this weight leaves room for heavy weapons and shields. The jump capability at assault weight is the tactical differentiator. Arm shields provide passive damage reduction. The CLS-5S carries a Gauss rifle, two PPCs, and two ER medium lasers. Walk three, run four, jump three. The Gauss provides accurate long-range ballistic fire. The PPCs cover medium to long range. The ER mediums handle close engagement. All different range bands covered.
variants.deployment: The 5S is the most diverse Colossus configuration in terms of engagement range coverage. The Gauss and PPCs cover long and medium range; the ER mediums handle close work. Walk three still constrains mobility. The jump capability provides the terrain exploitation the low ground speed cannot.

variants.name: COM-1A
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Eighteen variants have come from that foundation. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The COM-1A is the 2463 primitive prototype: a single large laser on the primitive 150-rated engine. Walk five, run seven — slower than the production standard. One weapon. Primitive components throughout.
variants.deployment: The 1A is the primitive prototype. One large laser on a twenty-five ton machine. Primitive construction documentation applies and standard replacement parts do not fit. Walk five is slower than the 150-rated engine's production potential. The design is historically significant but not tactically impressive.

variants.name: COM-1D
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Eighteen variants have come from that foundation. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The COM-1D carries a large laser and an SRM-6 on the standard 150-rated engine. Walk six, run nine. Three tons of armour is thin even by Commando standards. The large laser handles longer range; the SRM-6 closes the engagement.
variants.deployment: The 1D mounts a large laser and SRM-6 at the cost of thin armour. The three tons of armour means this machine cannot absorb hits. The speed and CASE-free ammunition are the vulnerabilities. It maintained production through the Commando's history because the weapons combination works despite the armour concern.

variants.name: COM-2D
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Eighteen variants have come from that foundation. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The COM-2D is the definitive production model from 2486: a medium laser, an SRM-4, and an SRM-6. Walk six, run nine. The SRM-4 and SRM-6 together deliver close-range missile volume. The medium laser provides direct energy backup.
variants.deployment: The 2D established the Commando's reputation across six centuries of production. The SRM-4 and SRM-6 combination at close range is the design's entire combat concept. Walk six delivers it there fast. The ammunition explosion vulnerability before CASE was added is the consistent operational concern.

variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Eighteen variants have come from that foundation. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The COM-1B carries a large laser, a medium laser, and an SRM-2 on the standard engine. Walk six, run nine. The large laser adds range to the standard Commando weapons concept. The SRM-2 is a small close-range supplement.
variants.deployment: The 1B attempted to revive the original large laser concept with the medium laser added. The SRM-2 is essentially a token close-range weapon. The large laser gives it genuine range capability the SRM-focused variants lack. Used through the Succession Wars period as an alternative to the SRM-heavy standard.

variants.name: COM-7X

variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The COM-7X carries three medium lasers and an SRM-6 with expanded ammunition. Walk six, run nine. Three medium lasers replace the SRM-4 with additional energy weapons. The SRM-6 and expanded ammunition remain.
variants.deployment: The 7X trades the SRM-4 for two more medium lasers. Three medium lasers at close range is solid energy volume for twenty-five tons. The SRM-6 with expanded ammunition handles close-range missile work. The tradeoff is reduced missile volume in exchange for more energy weapons.

variants.name: COM-1C
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Eighteen variants have come from that foundation. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The COM-1C carries a medium laser and an AC/2 on the standard engine. Walk six, run nine. The AC/2 provides long-range harassment fire. The medium laser handles close backup. One ton of AC/2 ammunition.
variants.deployment: The 1C attempts to provide longer-range fire support through an AC/2. The AC/2 harassment at walk six range is modest. One ton of ammunition is limited. The medium laser handles close-range threats the AC/2 cannot engage efficiently. Not widely favoured compared to the SRM-focused variants.

variants.name: COM-7Y
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Eighteen variants have come from that foundation. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The COM-7Y carries three medium lasers and an SRM-6 with increased armour, on the standard engine. Walk six, run nine. The additional armour improves survivability over the 7X at the cost of some other capability.
variants.deployment: The 7Y trades some capability for better armour protection. Three medium lasers and an SRM-6 is the same weapons concept as the 7X but with more armour to absorb the hits a close-range machine inevitably takes. Pilots who valued survivability in close engagement over additional firepower preferred the 7Y.

variants.name: COM-3A
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Eighteen variants have come from that foundation. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The COM-3A carries twin SRM-6 launchers, a medium laser, and a flamer, at the cost of one ton of armour. Walk six, run nine. Twin SRM-6 launchers deliver substantial close-range missile volume. The flamer handles infantry.
variants.deployment: The 3A appeared in 3025. Twin SRM-6s at close range is devastating missile volume for twenty-five tons. The armour reduction is the tradeoff. The flamer adds anti-infantry capability. The most common Commando variant encountered by ComStar ROM census data — the close-range concept resonated with operators.

variants.name: COM-7Y2 'Blazing Inferno'
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Eighteen variants have come from that foundation. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The Blazing Inferno carries four medium lasers and six small lasers on the standard engine. Walk six, run nine. Ten laser weapons on a twenty-five ton machine. All-energy with complete ammunition independence.
variants.deployment: The Blazing Inferno sacrifices SRM launchers entirely for laser volume. Ten lasers at close range is the concept. No ammunition dependency means no CASE concern and no resupply logistics. The heat from ten lasers simultaneously is aggressive on a twenty-five ton chassis. Pilots who cycle fire rather than firing everything at once sustain output.

variants.name: COM-5S
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Eighteen variants have come from that foundation. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The COM-5S carries a medium laser, a Streak SRM-2, and an SRM-6, with CASE protecting the ammunition. Walk six, run nine. CASE is the defining addition — it protects against ammunition explosion in the machine that earned its vulnerability reputation early. The Streak SRM-2 fires on lock only.
variants.deployment: The 5S added CASE to the Commando for the first time. The CASE protection addresses the primary operational concern that plagued earlier variants. The Streak SRM-2 guarantees missile hits when locked. Standard weapons otherwise. The CASE addition made the 5S the preferred variant for many operators who understood the ammunition risk.

variants.name: COM-7Z
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Eighteen variants have come from that foundation. variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The COM-7Z carries two medium lasers and an SRM-6, with CASE protecting the SRM ammunition. Walk six, run nine. Simpler weapons than the 2D but with the CASE protection the original lacked. An active probe is fitted for enhanced detection.
variants.deployment: The 7Z's CASE protection and active probe represent the two key upgrades that early Commandos lacked. The active probe extends detection range for the recon role. CASE protects against the ammunition explosion risk. The weapons are reduced from the 2D but the survivability improvements are the point.

variants.name: COM-7Z2
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Eighteen variants have come from that foundation. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The COM-7Z2 carries two small lasers and an SRM-6, with a Beagle active probe. Walk six, run nine. The Beagle extends detection range substantially beyond the standard active probe. Two small lasers are token direct fire weapons. The SRM-6 remains.
variants.deployment: The 7Z2 is the sensor-focused Commando. The Beagle active probe is the most capable detection system available at this weight class. The small lasers are essentially self-defence only. The SRM-6 provides the close-range combat capability. For recon work where detection matters more than firepower, the 7Z2 is the choice.

variants.name: COM-7A
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Eighteen variants have come from that foundation. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The COM-7A carries a medium laser and two SRM-4 launchers. Walk six, run nine. Twin SRM-4s combined with the medium laser provide balanced close-range capability at slightly less missile volume than the SRM-6 variants.
variants.deployment: The 7A performed well in Operation Serpent, prompting Coventry Metal Works to dedicate formal production. Twin SRM-4s with a medium laser is the balanced concept. The SRM-4 ammunition is more compact than the SRM-6, allowing more shots per ton. A sensible close-range striker.

The SRM launchers are the primary weapons — close-range missile volume on a fast light 'Mech. The ammunition vulnerability is the design's known issue until CASE was added. The COM-7J carries a medium laser, two SRM-4s, and five jump jets. Walk six, run nine, jump five. Jump capability added to the 7A loadout at the cost of some equipment elsewhere.
variants.deployment: The 7J saw action during the fighting on Huntress, where jump five proved useful for quick repositioning in close terrain. The same weapons as the 7A plus jump capability. Armour is reduced to accommodate the jump jets. Pilots who valued terrain exploitation over extra armour ran the 7J.

The COM-7W carries two medium lasers, a Streak SRM-2, and an SRM-4 on the standard engine. Walk six, run nine. The Streak SRM-2 fires on lock only. More ammunition than some variants for sustained operations.
variants.deployment: The 7W emphasises operational endurance. The Streak SRM-2 guarantees missile hits when locked. The additional ammunition extends the combat capability before resupply. Two medium lasers provide direct energy fire alongside the missile systems. A balanced configuration for sustained operations.

variants.name: COM-7S
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Eighteen variants have come from that foundation. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 150-rated light engine. The COM-7S carries two ER medium lasers, two Streak SRM-2s, and an Artemis IV SRM-4. Light engine — side torso survivability. The Streak and Artemis systems improve missile accuracy. ER mediums extend energy range.
variants.deployment: The 7S is the most capable standard-production Commando. The light engine provides genuine side torso survivability the standard engine variants rely on luck to achieve. The Streak and Artemis guided missiles are more accurate than unguided fire. ER mediums extend combat range. The combination makes it the most tactically versatile Commando.

The Blazing Inferno II carries four ER medium lasers, five ER small lasers, and a small laser, with triple-strength myomer and double heat sinks. Walk six, run nine. TSM activates at elevated heat, boosting physical combat strength. The weapons generate the heat to trigger TSM.
variants.deployment: The Blazing Inferno II uses the laser heat output to deliberately trigger TSM for enhanced melee capability. Ten energy weapons on twenty-five tons generates significant heat. TSM activation makes the physical attacks the primary weapon alongside the lasers. Double heat sinks help but the heat load is aggressive by design.

variants.name: COM-4H

The COM-4H carries two medium lasers and six one-shot Rocket Launcher-15s from the Marian Hegemony. Walk six, run nine. The six RL-15s provide a single ninety-round alpha strike. After that, two medium lasers carry the engagement.
variants.deployment: The Marian Hegemony's Commando contribution is a one-shot devastation platform. Six RL-15s at close range is a devastating single volley for twenty-five tons. Two medium lasers fight on after. The Hegemony production reflects their preference for concentrated firepower over sustained engagement capability.

variants.name: COM-7B
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Twenty-four variants. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump four on the 150-rated light engine. The COM-7B carries two flamers, an ER medium laser, and two SRM-4 launchers, with CASE. Light engine — side torso survivability. The two flamers handle infantry. The ER medium extends energy fire range. CASE protects the SRM-4 ammunition.
variants.deployment: The 7B is the anti-infantry and light-engine survivability variant. The two flamers in the left arm are the design's unusual feature. The ER medium laser handles direct engagement. The SRM-4s add missile punch. Jump four provides terrain exploitation. The light engine survives hits that kill the XL and standard variants.

variants.name: COM-7S2 (Freyr)
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Twenty-four variants. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six on the Clan XL engine. The Freyr carries Clan ER medium lasers and Streak SRM-4 launchers on an endo steel frame with a salvaged Clan XL. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability at this weight means any significant hit is fatal. Clan ER mediums are superior to IS equivalents. Streak SRM-4s fire on lock.
variants.deployment: The Freyr is built around salvaged Clan components. The Clan XL at twenty-five tons is even more dangerous than IS XL at this weight. The Clan ER mediums and Streak SRM-4s deliver better performance than IS equivalents. Named machine — maintain to specific build documentation with awareness that Clan components require Clan maintenance procedures.

variants.name: COM-1AK

variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons. The ammunition vulnerability is the known issue until CASE was added. The COM-1AK replaces the original 1A large laser with two arm-mounted medium lasers and a head-mounted small laser on the primitive 150-rated engine. Walk five, run seven. The medium lasers address the 1A's heat and accuracy problems.
variants.deployment: The 1AK fixed the 1A's large laser cooling problem. Two medium lasers generate less heat and are more reliable than the original large laser. Walk five remains from the primitive engine. Primitive construction documentation still applies. A field improvement on a fundamentally limited platform.

variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Twenty-four variants. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty-five tons on the standard 150-rated engine. Side torso survivability throughout the conventional variants. The SRM launchers are the primary weapons. The ammunition vulnerability is the known issue until CASE was added. The COM-2Dr carries an ER medium laser and an MML-7, with CASE. Walk six, run nine. The MML-7 provides SRM or LRM flexibility from a single launcher. The ER medium extends energy range. CASE protects the ammunition.
variants.deployment: The 2Dr is the reconnaissance and rapid response configuration. The MML-7 flexibility covers multiple threat ranges — LRM mode for stand-off harassment, SRM mode for close engagement. The ER medium provides energy backup. CASE is fitted. Straightforward and flexible for the scout role.

variants.name: COM-8S
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Twenty-four variants. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten on the 175-rated XL engine. The COM-8S carries two ER medium lasers and two Streak SRM-2s, with a TAG system. Walk seven — faster than standard. Endo steel chassis. The TAG designates for guided munitions. Streak SRM-2s fire on lock. XL engine vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The 8S is the fast dedicated spotter variant. Walk seven combined with TAG designation makes it a forward observer that moves too fast for most opponents to intercept. The Streak SRM-2s handle close defence reliably. The ER mediums provide direct fire. XL engine adds the standard vulnerability.

variants.name: COM-9S
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Commando in 2463 as a twenty-five ton Lyran recon and raider. Walk six, run nine. Twenty-four variants. The ammunition explosion history is the design's consistent liability — CASE protection was added late and many early machines lack it.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten on the 175-rated XL engine. The COM-9S carries a light PPC, two one-shot SRM-2 launchers, and two MML-3 launchers. Walk seven. The one-shot SRM-2s are single-use close-range missiles. The MML-3s cover SRM/LRM flexibility at modest scale. The light PPC handles direct engagement.
variants.deployment: The 9S is the ranged harassment and reconnaissance variant. Walk seven at twenty-five tons maintains speed advantage. The light PPC provides direct fire without minimum range complications. The MML-3s add missile flexibility. The one-shot SRM-2s are a close-range emergency option. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: CPR-HD-002
variants.overview: Omnitech Industries built the Copperhead as a thirty-ton arena fighter for Solaris VII in 3054, designed around a 180-rated XL engine and close-range precision weapons. Walk six, run nine. Three variants, all arena-focused.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at thirty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Arena-optimised construction with ferro-fibrous or reflective armour depending on variant. The X-pulse lasers provide the accuracy that arena combat rewards. Jump capability varies by variant. The CPR-HD-002 carries three medium lasers, a medium pulse laser, a small pulse laser, an SRM-4, and a one-shot Streak SRM-2. Walk six, run nine, jump two. Ferro-fibrous armour. Twelve double heat sinks. The first-production model before the 003 upgrades.
variants.deployment: The CPR-HD-002 was the foundation variant from 3054, produced before the Silver Dragons stable commissioned the 003 upgrade. The weapons suite is well-rounded for arena combat at close range. Jump two is limited — mostly useful for crossing obstacles. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: CPR-HD-003
variants.overview: Omnitech Industries built the Copperhead as a thirty-ton arena fighter for Solaris VII in 3054, designed around a 180-rated XL engine and close-range precision weapons. Walk six, run nine. Three variants, all arena-focused.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at thirty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Arena-optimised construction with ferro-fibrous or reflective armour depending on variant. The X-pulse lasers provide the accuracy that arena combat rewards. Jump capability varies by variant. The CPR-HD-003 carries a medium X-pulse laser, three ER medium lasers, a Streak SRM-4, and a Magshot Gauss rifle, with reflective armour. Walk six, run nine, jump two. The reflective armour reduces incoming energy weapon damage. The X-pulse laser provides accuracy. The Magshot adds Gauss precision.
variants.deployment: The 003 is a comprehensive upgrade commissioned by the Silver Dragons Stable in 3065. Reflective plating provides passive energy weapon protection that the standard ferro-fibrous lacks. The Magshot Gauss accuracy and X-pulse precision make this more accurate than the base model. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: CPR-HD-004
variants.overview: Omnitech Industries built the Copperhead as a thirty-ton arena fighter for Solaris VII in 3054, designed around a 180-rated XL engine and close-range precision weapons. Walk six, run nine. Three variants, all arena-focused.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at thirty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Arena-optimised construction with ferro-fibrous or reflective armour depending on variant. The X-pulse lasers provide the accuracy that arena combat rewards. Jump capability varies by variant. The CPR-HD-004 carries the same weapons as the 003 — X-pulse medium laser, three ER mediums, Streak SRM-4, Magshot — but removes the jump jets and adds a ton of reflective armour. Walk six, run nine, no jump. Heavier reflective armour protection.
variants.deployment: The 004 trades the 003's limited jump capability for extra armour. The additional ton of reflective armour addresses one of the design's most cited weaknesses. No jump is the tradeoff. The same weapons precision as the 003. For arena environments where the jump two of earlier variants provided minimal value, the armour improvement is the better trade.

variants.overview: The Corvis 2 is a forty-ton Clan medium introduced in 3075 as a refit, built on a 160-rated Clan engine with jump four. Walk four, run six, jump four. The HAG/20 and targeting computer combination is the design's fire support identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at forty tons. Clan engine — standard Clan maintenance requirements. The targeting computer links to all weapons for improved accuracy. Jump four provides terrain exploitation options. Variant 2 carries a HAG/20, two heavy medium lasers, and a targeting computer, with jump four. Walk four, run six, jump four. The targeting computer links all weapons for improved accuracy. The HAG/20 spreads ballistic projectiles across multiple armour locations. The heavy medium lasers hit harder than standard equivalents.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 was introduced in 3075 replacing the UAC/10 with a HAG/20. The targeting computer makes the HAG spread more accurate and the heavy mediums more reliable. Jump four provides positioning options. Clan engine maintenance requirements apply.

variants.name: C-SK1
variants.overview: Ceres Metals Industries built the Cossack in 3060 on Warlock as a twenty-ton light trooper rather than a pure scout. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 120-rated XL engine. Two variants. The endo steel chassis keeps production costs manageable.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at twenty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. Jump six provides terrain exploitation. The design is for light trooper duties — it engages rather than purely scouts. The C-SK1 carries a medium laser, two small lasers, and an SRM-6. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The SRM-6 provides the primary close-range missile capability. The lasers handle direct energy engagement. Endo steel chassis. XL engine — side torso vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The C-SK1 entered service in 3060 with Khorsakov's Cossacks and St. Ives militia. Walk six, run nine, jump six at twenty tons is good tactical mobility for light trooper work. The SRM-6 at close range is effective for the engagement types this machine was built for. XL engine vulnerability is severe at this weight.

variants.name: C-1FC
variants.overview: Ceres Metals Industries built the Cossack in 3060 on Warlock as a twenty-ton light trooper rather than a pure scout. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 120-rated XL engine. Two variants. The endo steel chassis keeps production costs manageable.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at twenty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. Jump six provides terrain exploitation. The design is for light trooper duties — it engages rather than purely scouts. The C-1FC carries a medium VSP laser and three one-shot Rocket Launcher-10s. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The three RL-10s provide a single thirty-round alpha strike. After that the machine has only the VSP laser. A Jihad-era field modification.
variants.deployment: The C-1FC emerged as a Federated Suns Capellan March field modification during the Jihad. Three RL-10s deliver a single devastating alpha strike at close range. The VSP laser carries the engagement after. The one-shot concept suits the light trooper hit-and-run doctrine. Jump six enables approach from unexpected angles for the alpha strike.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Jade Falcon developed the Cougar after the Refusal War of 3057 specifically to get more pod space than the Adder offered, and they achieved that by dropping to a lighter engine. The result is a 35-ton light OmniMech with more flexibility than its predecessor. Fifteen configurations over its service life reflects the Falcons getting good use out of the design.
variants.capabilities: The lighter engine trade-off for pod space is a sound engineering decision and the numbers bear it out. The OmniMech flexibility is the real asset here. Clan Jade Falcon construction quality is consistent and high. The Artemis IV-equipped missile configurations are the ones that require the most maintenance attention due to the fire control calibration requirements.
variants.deployment: Fifteen configurations covering the tactical spectrum from dedicated missile platform to direct fire support to electronic warfare. The twin LRM-20 with Artemis configuration is the most popular alternate and the most maintenance-demanding due to the Artemis calibration requirements. Keep those fire control systems in spec and the configuration delivers what's advertised. Falcon parts support is reliable.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Coyotl holds the distinction of being the first OmniMech ever built, developed by Clan Coyote with Sea Fox assistance, and working on one feels like handling history. The Pitban 280 XL at 119 kph for a 35-tonner is impressive even by modern standards. The Golden Century construction shows in the quality of the original hulls.
variants.capabilities: 119 kph for a 35-ton chassis is genuinely fast and the OmniMech concept was revolutionary when this was built. By modern standards it's showing its age in some component areas but the fundamental engineering is sound. The XL concern applies as always. Clan Coyote construction quality on the original hulls is excellent — these were built to demonstrate a concept and they were built well.
variants.deployment: Five configurations developed over the Golden Century production period. Working on a Coyotl means working with some of the oldest OmniMech documentation in existence — thorough in some areas, sparse in others where the original techs considered things self-evident. The historic value doesn't change the maintenance requirements but it does mean you handle every component carefully.

variants.name: CRB-27
variants.overview: Cosara Weaponries introduced the Crab in 2719 as one of the last Star League SLDF designs before the Amaris Civil War, and the all-energy weapons loadout reflects the operational philosophy of extended operations without logistical support. It's a clean design built to high standards and the construction quality shows in how well old hulls hold up.
variants.capabilities: The twin RAMTech 1200 large lasers are the heart of this machine and they're reliable systems with good documentation. All-energy means no ammunition concerns, which suits the independent raider role the design was built for. Heat management is the pilot's discipline — not unmanageable but requires attention. Star League construction quality throughout. The chassis is well-balanced and access for maintenance is good.
variants.deployment: Seven variants from the 2719 original through post-Star League adaptations. The original CRB-27 with full Star League technology is the reference and the most capable. Later variants substitute available components for harder-to-source Star League hardware. The all-energy philosophy carries across all variants. Cosara parts support is reliable through Commonwealth logistics.

variants.name: CRB-20
variants.overview: Cosara Weaponries introduced the Crab in 2719 as one of the last Star League SLDF designs before the Amaris Civil War, and the all-energy weapons loadout reflects the operational philosophy of extended operations without logistical support. It's a clean design built to high standards and the construction quality shows in how well old hulls hold up.
variants.capabilities: The twin RAMTech 1200 large lasers are the heart of this machine and they're reliable systems with good documentation. All-energy means no ammunition concerns, which suits the independent raider role the design was built for. Heat management is the pilot's discipline — not unmanageable but requires attention. Star League construction quality throughout. The chassis is well-balanced and access for maintenance is good.

variants.name: RWN-01
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Cricket in 3132 for the DCMS as a light 'Mech pushing weight-saving technology to limits that most frontline designs avoid. The performance numbers are impressive; the durability trade-offs are real and documented. Initial delivery batches had quality issues that LAW addressed in later production.
variants.capabilities: The aggressive use of weight-saving technologies creates a light that punches above its class in performance and requires more careful handling than a conventionally constructed chassis. The initial quality concerns with early production runs are worth noting — older hulls need closer inspection than newer ones. The performance envelope is genuinely good when the machine is in spec.
variants.deployment: Two variants. The original production model is the more common. The early delivery quality issues are the main historical concern — if you're receiving older hulls, do a thorough inspection before trusting maintenance records. Later production corrected those issues. DCMS parts support through Luthien channels is reliable for current production variants.

variants.overview: Clan Blood Spirit conceived the Crimson Hawk on York in 3069 during a dark period for the Spirit Cats, and the deceptive design philosophy reflects their situation — a machine built to look heavier than it is and survive through misdirection. At 25 tons the extended-range large lasers are an unusual primary armament choice that enables engagement at ranges where the light chassis isn't an obvious liability.
variants.capabilities: Two ER large lasers on a 25-ton chassis is an aggressive choice that makes heat management a real concern at small size. The deception aspect — looking larger than it is — has genuine tactical value at range but breaks down in close combat. Blood Spirit construction quality is solid. The light weight means any significant damage creates proportionally serious problems.
variants.deployment: Three variants with the second replacing the ER large lasers with Streak SRM launchers for a completely different engagement philosophy. The maintenance profiles differ significantly between variants — know which one you're working on. Blood Spirit parts support is limited by their strategic situation; sourcing outside their supply channels requires creativity.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The joint Blood Spirit and Fire Mandrill development produced the Crimson Langur in 3077, and the collaboration shows in the design — fast for a 50-ton OmniMech, well-armed, reflecting both Clans' combat priorities. The 350 XL pushing 120 kph for the weight class is the headline capability.
variants.capabilities: Nearly 120 kph at 50 tons is genuinely impressive and the XL enabling that speed is the primary maintenance focus. The XL vulnerability concern applies with extra weight here — at this speed, a side torso breach creates a mobility crisis very quickly. The OmniMech pod system is well-implemented. Six configurations from the joint development give reasonable tactical flexibility.
variants.deployment: Six configurations with Configuration A's long-range fire support focus being common among Blood Spirit units. The XL advisory is the consistent briefing across all configurations — the speed advantage is the machine's identity but the vulnerability that enables it needs clear pilot communication. Parts support through either Blood Spirit or Fire Mandrill channels depending on the operational area.

variants.name: CRK-5003-1
variants.overview: Blankenburg Technologies designed the Crockett in 3085 tons as a training assault platform for the SLDF, and the diverse weapons array reflects that training mission — cadets needed exposure to multiple weapon types simultaneously. The Norse Heavy XT2-1A chassis is shared with the Black Watch, which gives useful commonality between the two designs.
variants.capabilities: The training origin explains the weapons diversity that might otherwise seem unfocused on an 85-ton assault design. In practice the diverse loadout makes the Crockett a capable all-around combatant. The shared chassis with the Black Watch creates maintenance commonality that's genuinely useful. Star League construction quality throughout the original variants. The extended-range large lasers are the components requiring the most maintenance attention.
variants.deployment: Six variants from the Star League original through later adaptations. The original production model with full Star League technology is the reference and the most demanding to support with modern parts. Later variants substitute available equipment. The Black Watch chassis commonality is a practical logistics advantage worth exploiting when both designs are in the same unit.

variants.name: CNS-3M
variants.overview: Retired FWLM MechWarrior Angus Gilmour designed the Cronus on Talitha, which makes it unusual — a private citizen producing a medium BattleMech. The Earthwerks SHD II endo steel chassis and VOX 330 XL give it solid performance and the design reflects practical field experience rather than theoretical requirements.
variants.capabilities: The VOX 330 XL gives good speed for the weight class and brings the familiar XL vulnerability concern. The endo steel structure requires trained techs for structural repairs. The weapons fit reflects practical combat experience in its layout choices. Three variants show ongoing refinement. Earthwerks construction quality is solid and consistent.
variants.deployment: Three variants, with the original 3031 design using standard technologies that were readily available at the time. The later variants upgrade to more advanced equipment improving capability and adding complexity. The private design origin means documentation standards are different from military procurement designs — thorough in the areas Gilmour prioritized, less comprehensive elsewhere.

variants.name: CRS-X
variants.overview: Arcturan Arms built the Crossbow in 2468 as their first BattleMech production, and the simplified arm assemblies are the design signature — they function as fixed mounts rather than articulated weapons platforms, which simplifies manufacturing and maintenance while limiting the tactical flexibility of the weapons placement.
variants.capabilities: The simplified arm design is both a maintenance advantage and an operational limitation. Less complex actuator systems mean fewer failure points and simpler repairs; fixed weapon arcs mean pilots need to orient the whole chassis to bring weapons to bear in ways that articulated designs don't. Seventeen variants over the production run show the design finding its audience despite that constraint.
variants.deployment: Seventeen configurations from the 2468 prototype through decades of development. The original prototype's LRM-focused loadout established the design as a missile platform, which most subsequent variants maintained. The fixed arm design is the consistent maintenance consideration — understand the arc limitations and communicate them to pilots who haven't worked with this design before.

variants.overview: Earthwerks-FWL built the Crucible in 3149 for the Wolf Empire, explicitly inspired by the Annihilator's Gauss rifle philosophy but with Clan construction quality and modern Wolf engineering. Four Series II Gauss rifles on a 100-ton chassis — the concept is straightforward and the execution reflects the Wolf Empire's need for reliable heavy firepower from available production capacity.
variants.capabilities: Four Gauss rifles distributed across the chassis require synchronized capacitor maintenance that multiplies the inspection workload compared to a single or dual Gauss design. The capacitor failure cascade risk when maintenance is deferred on a quad-Gauss design is significant — keep all four systems on identical schedules. The Clan construction quality throughout helps manage the complexity. The second variant's shift to ER PPCs changes the maintenance profile completely.
variants.deployment: Two variants with fundamentally different weapons philosophies. The original four-Gauss configuration is impressive firepower with demanding maintenance requirements. The second variant's ER PPC loadout is more maintenance-friendly but different tactically. The quad-Gauss capacitor advisory applies only to the original — ensure the right briefing reaches the right pilots.
