variants.name: CRD-2R
variants.overview: The Crusader entered service in 2596 and has been in continuous production somewhere for over five centuries. The balanced LRM-SRM-laser combination that defines the original concept proved so effective that most subsequent variants maintained the same basic philosophy. Twenty-eight variants tells the story of a design that kept finding new users who wanted to improve it without changing what worked.
variants.capabilities: The LRM-SRM combination across multiple ranges is the enduring strength — no single engagement distance where the Crusader has nothing useful to contribute. The ammunition management across multiple launcher types is the operational complexity, and it's a real consideration. The basic chassis is simple and well-documented. Parts are available essentially everywhere given five centuries of production.
variants.deployment: Twenty-eight variants from the advanced Star League original through modern adaptations. The Star League variants with full advanced technology are the most capable and most demanding to support. Later variants substitute available equipment progressively. Whatever variant you're maintaining, the multi-ammunition management advisory applies to any configuration carrying both LRM and SRM systems.

variants.name: CDG-1B
variants.overview: Innovative Design Concepts built the Cudgel for Solaris VII arena combat and the mace-and-battle-claw design makes it immediately recognizable. Engineer Bertrum Moss designed this machine to dominate close-quarters arena combat, and within those parameters it does exactly that. The physical weapons are actually among the simpler maintenance items on the chassis.
variants.capabilities: The mace and battle claw are mechanically straightforward — well-made physical weapons with predictable wear patterns and relatively simple repair procedures compared to most energy or ballistic systems. The secondary weapons supporting the physical assault are the more complex maintenance items. Arena-optimized construction means it's built for dramatic close-range combat, not extended campaigns.
variants.deployment: Three variants with the original relying on a different tactical approach than the mace-focused successors. The machine gun and small pulse laser original is the more conventional weapons fit. The later mace-centered variants are the ones that established the Cudgel's reputation. For arena use the design excels; for field deployment the close-range-only optimization is a significant limitation.

variants.name: CDR-1X
variants.overview: Robinson Standard BattleWorks released the Cuirass in 3086 as a continuation of the Watchman chassis family lineage, and the Dorwinion Hyperactive 3 endo steel chassis shared with the Sentry gives it a proven foundation. The GM 240 XL and rotary AC/5 combination makes it an aggressive medium with sustained fire capability.
variants.capabilities: The Mydron Model RC Rotary AC/5 is the defining weapon and rotary autocannons require more maintenance attention than standard — the mechanism is more complex and more sensitive to contamination. Keep the cleaning cycles current. The GM 240 XL gives good speed for the weight class with the familiar XL vulnerability concern. The shared Sentry chassis creates useful parts commonality.
variants.deployment: Three variants on the same Watchman-lineage chassis. The baseline Cuirass is the most common. The rotary AC maintenance requirement is the consistent advisory — don't let cleaning cycles slip. The XL concern applies across all configurations. Robinson Standard parts support is reliable through Federated Suns logistics and the Sentry chassis commonality is a practical advantage.

variants.name: CP-10-Z
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Cyclops in 2710 as an assault-weight command platform, and the lavish command and control electronics are the defining feature rather than the weapons fit. The Hermes 360 engine giving 64 kph to an 85-ton assault design is impressive, and the command suite made it the preferred headquarters 'Mech for Star League battalion commanders.
variants.capabilities: The command electronics are what distinguishes the Cyclops from a conventional assault 'Mech and they require specialist maintenance that general techs aren't trained for. The Zeus-36 Mark III and backup weapons are solid hardware but secondary to the C3 and command systems. The speed is genuine and useful for a command 'Mech that needs to keep up with a mobile battle line.
variants.deployment: Thirteen variants from the 2710 original through modern developments. The command electronics maintenance requirement is consistent across all command-configured variants — budget for qualified specialist time. Later variants that downplay the command role in favor of direct firepower have different maintenance profiles. The Star League construction quality on original hulls is excellent.

variants.overview: Clan Hell's Horses introduced the Cygnus in 3075 through a joint program with the exiled Arc-Royal Wolves, drawing inspiration from the Annihilator for a 95-ton assault design with Clan construction efficiency. The GM 380 XL is the performance foundation and the ballistic-heavy weapons philosophy reflects both Clans' preferences.
variants.capabilities: The Annihilator-inspired design philosophy of overwhelming ballistic firepower with Clan technology quality is a sound concept and the execution delivers on it. The GM 380 XL at 95 tons creates the familiar XL vulnerability concern at assault weight — side torso damage is a serious event and pilots need clear briefing on that. The Clan construction quality throughout manages the complexity well.
variants.deployment: Three variants, with the second still in development at the time of the original introduction. The ballistic weapon ammunition management is the consistent operational consideration. The XL vulnerability advisory applies to all configurations. Joint Hell's Horses and Wolf parts support through their respective logistics channels depending on the operating unit.

variants.name: DCMS-MX90-D
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Daboku in 3038 for the DCMS as a long-range gunnery platform, and the dual Tronel large laser and LRM rack combination delivers on that mission. Single configuration only, which simplifies everything from training to parts stocking. The numerous firing arcs the design provides give pilots meaningful tactical flexibility.
variants.capabilities: The Tronel large lasers and Holly LRM racks in combination cover multiple engagement ranges effectively. variants.deployment: Single configuration, no factory variants. The DCMS-MX90-D is the only configuration you'll see and the documentation covers it thoroughly. variants.name: DAD-3C
variants.overview: Innovative Design Concepts built the Daedalus in the mid-3050s for Solaris VII from a modified Phoenix Hawk chassis, and the arena origin shows in the mixed-technology weapons approach that prioritizes variety and spectacle alongside effectiveness. variants.capabilities: The Earthwerks PXH II endo steel frame and Hermes 270 XL from the Phoenix Hawk give it 97 kph at 45 tons — good performance that carries over cleanly from the ancestor design. For arena combat the design excels; field deployment benefits from the Phoenix Hawk structural reliability.

variants.name: DAI-01
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Daikyu in 3055 for the DCMS, named after the traditional Japanese longbow, and the long-range fire support role is embodied in everything about the design. The Magna 350 XL gives it better speed than most dedicated fire support heavies and the weapons complement that mobility effectively.
variants.capabilities: The Magna 350 XL pushing 70 tons to 86 kph is the performance advantage and the XL vulnerability concern that comes with it is the consistent advisory. The long-range weapons focus means the design works best when it can stay at range and exploit the mobility to maintain that position. LAW construction quality is solid and consistent throughout.
variants.deployment: Five variants, all maintaining the long-range fire support concept. The base DAI-01 is the reference. The XL advisory applies consistently across all five. Luthien Armor Works parts support through Combine channels is reliable. Brief pilots on the design philosophy — this machine rewards staying at range and punishes commanders who try to use it as a brawler.

variants.name: DMO-1K
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works brought the Daimyo into service in February 3053 as a versatile medium that could engage effectively across all range brackets, and the Lord's Light 2 ER PPC anchored by SRM backup delivers on that concept. At 40 tons it provides more capability than the weight class usually offers.
variants.capabilities: The ER PPC and SRM combination covers both long-range engagement and close-range backup effectively. Heat management on the ER PPC requires pilot discipline — not extreme but consistent attention needed. The chassis is straightforward and the LAW construction quality means the documentation is thorough and parts are available through Combine logistics. Five variants show steady refinement.
variants.deployment: Five variants building on the same versatile medium concept. The base production model is the reference. The multi-range capability is the design strength and the briefing point — this is a chassis that rewards pilots who use all its capabilities rather than defaulting to one engagement distance. LAW parts support is reliable.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Wolf introduced the Dire Wolf in 3010 as their concept of the ultimate assault OmniMech, and the Inner Sphere name Daishi reflects the same gravitas. The Starfire 300 XL accepts slow speed as the trade-off for maximum pod space and weapons payload, and that trade-off has defined assault OmniMech doctrine for generations. Fifteen configurations embody that design philosophy across every tactical application.
variants.capabilities: The explicit speed sacrifice for firepower is the whole design philosophy and the Dire Wolf delivers on it completely. The Starfire 300 XL in a 100-ton chassis is a significant maintenance item but it's well-documented after decades of Clan service. The OmniMech pod system gives exceptional flexibility at the cost of pod maintenance overhead. The XL vulnerability concern at 100 tons is as serious as it gets — a side torso breach on this chassis is catastrophic.
variants.deployment: Fifteen configurations covering the full tactical spectrum for an assault OmniMech. Configuration A's Gauss and precision fire combination is one of the more common. The XL advisory at this weight class needs to be the loudest briefing you give to any pilot assigned a Dire Wolf. Pod maintenance overhead across 15 configurations is substantial — ensure your support infrastructure can handle the inventory.

variants.overview: Clan Snow Raven produced the Dark Crow in 3084 at their Dante facility, and the low-mounted arm design is the physically distinctive feature. At 55 tons it fills a medium-heavy role with a weapons layout that creates specific engagement geometry pilots need to understand. Three variants show adaptation to different tactical requirements.
variants.capabilities: The low-mounted arms create an unusual weapons arc profile compared to conventional designs — techs and pilots both need to understand how this affects targeting geometry. The Snow Raven construction quality is high throughout. The anti-aircraft and sniper variant represents a significant tactical departure from the base model with a different weapons maintenance profile.
variants.deployment: Three variants with meaningfully different tactical applications. The base model and the AA-sniper variant require different pilot skill sets. The arm geometry is the consistent briefing point — both techs and pilots working with a Dark Crow for the first time need specific orientation on how the arm placement affects maintenance access and weapons performance.

variants.deployment: Three variants with meaningfully different tactical applications. The base model and the AA-sniper variant require different pilot skill sets. The arm geometry is the consistent briefing point — both techs and pilots working with a Dark Crow for the first time need specific orientation on how the arm placement affects maintenance access and weapons performance.

variants.name: DRT-3S
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Dart in 3051 for the Federated Commonwealth as a purely energy-weapon light — no ammunition dependency was the explicit design requirement. The VOX 225 engine at 25 tons gives 100 kph and the all-laser loadout delivers on the independence from supply chain that the brief called for.
variants.capabilities: 100 kph for a 25-ton all-energy light is a clean operational concept — fast enough to avoid most trouble, independent of ammunition supply, simple enough to maintain in austere conditions. Heat management is the pilot's main discipline given the all-energy loadout. The chassis is straightforward and Coventry construction quality is consistent. Parts are available through Lyran and Federated Suns supply channels.
variants.deployment: Four variants, all maintaining the all-energy philosophy. The base DRT-3S is the reference. The all-laser maintenance requirement is uncomplicated — no ammunition feeds, no ballistic mechanisms, clean failure modes. The heat management advisory applies across all variants. For reconnaissance and raiding roles where supply independence matters, this chassis delivers what it promises.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Cloud Cobra developed the Fire Moth in 2874 as the fastest BattleMech ever built, and the Inner Sphere codename Dasher captures the essence of what this machine is. At 20 tons with a 200-rated XL achieving 162 kph, the performance numbers are still remarkable by any era's standards. Seventeen configurations show how extensively this chassis has been exploited.
variants.capabilities: 162 kph top speed is extraordinary and it's the whole point. At 20 tons there is almost nothing left in the chassis after the engine takes its share, which means damage tolerance is minimal. The XL vulnerability concern at this size is different than on heavier designs — side torso damage often ends the mission rather than the machine, but the speed that enables survival in the first place is the protection. Clan construction quality throughout is excellent.
variants.deployment: Seventeen configurations covering every possible application of a 20-ton ultralight OmniMech. Configuration A's scout and artillery spotter role is one of the more common. The universal advisory for all Dasher variants: the speed is the armor. Pilots who try to tank hits in one of these have misunderstood their assignment. Pod space is extremely limited; configuration selection matters more here than on heavier OmniMechs.

variants.overview: Clan Diamond Shark introduced the Dasher II in 3077 as a heavier non-OmniMech successor to the Fire Moth, and the Type 79 400-rated XL engine defines the performance identity. At 40 tons this is not a Fire Moth replacement — it's a different machine with the same speed philosophy applied to a heavier chassis.
variants.capabilities: The Type 79 400-rated XL consuming two-thirds of available mass is an extreme example of the speed-first design philosophy. What remains after the engine is limited, and the weapons fit reflects that constraint. The experimental Model 53b XXL engine on the second variant is even more extreme — XXL systems require specialist maintenance that standard XL expertise doesn't cover. Both configurations are fragile in ways that their speed is supposed to compensate for.
variants.deployment: Three variants with the second using experimental XXL technology. The XXL variant requires personnel specifically qualified on XXL engine systems — do not attempt to work on it with standard XL training. The original Type 79 variant is more supportable with standard Clan tech qualified staff. The speed philosophy advisory applies to both: this machine survives by not getting hit.

variants.name: DFN-3C
variants.overview: Defiance Industries prototyped their namesake heavy in 3057 on Hesperus II as an internal product, and the Warhammer resemblance is noted and intentional — they were building on proven PPC-heavy design philosophy with modern improvements. At 75 tons it sits between the Warhammer's 70 and an assault-class threshold.
variants.capabilities: The Warhammer comparison is apt and useful for techs who know that chassis — similar design logic, more modern construction. The original prototype's compact gyro is the unusual component that requires specific maintenance knowledge different from standard gyro procedures. Later production variants that moved to more conventional components are more straightforward to support. PPC maintenance philosophy carries from Warhammer experience.
variants.deployment: Three variants from the experimental prototype through production configurations. The original DFN-3C prototype's compact gyro requires specialist knowledge — confirm your techs have specific training on compact gyro systems before working on prototype hulls. Production variants with conventional equipment are the practical choice for sustained operations. Defiance Industries parts support is excellent through Lyran logistics.

variants.overview: Clan Snow Raven spent over two decades developing the Deimos before it reached service, which tells you something about how seriously they took the design. The broad-shouldered digitigrade frame is distinctive and the OmniMech configuration gives it flexibility that the long development period was used to fully exploit. Nine configurations reflect that thorough development process.
variants.capabilities: The Clan 320 XL gives solid assault-class performance and the OmniMech pod system is well-implemented after the long development cycle. The broad chassis actually improves maintenance access compared to some more compact assault designs. The pre-OmniMech variant the AFFS has identified represents a different maintenance profile from the standard OmniMech configurations. Snow Raven construction quality is consistently high.
variants.deployment: Nine configurations including the non-OmniMech variant. The non-Omni version identified by AFFS intelligence is based on pre-OmniMech technology and has a simpler maintenance profile than the standard configurations. For the OmniMech variants, Snow Raven parts support through their logistics channels is reliable. The long development period means the documentation is thorough — one of the better-documented assault OmniMechs to come out of the Clan homeworlds.

variants.name: DV-1S
variants.overview: Coventry Defense Conglomerate designed the Dervish in 2520 deliberately for the militia market — simple, affordable, effective enough. The twin Federated 10-Shot LRM-10 launchers deeply embedded in the torso are the design signature and they've been lobbing missiles reliably for five centuries. Eight variants show ongoing refinement without losing the original simplicity.
variants.capabilities: The torso-mounted LRM launchers are the whole story and they're workhorses — well-documented, parts everywhere, simple to maintain. Ammunition management is the operational consideration. The design's explicit simplicity is a genuine virtue in the field where complexity costs lives and time. Jump jet capability on some variants adds maintenance overhead but the base structure is uncomplicated.
variants.deployment: Eight variants from the 2520 original through modern upgrades. The original is the simplest and most maintenance-friendly. Later variants add jump jets and upgraded electronics that improve capability and increase complexity proportionally. For militia units or any formation that needs reliable fire support without exotic maintenance requirements, the Dervish remains a sound choice after five centuries.

variants.name: C-DVA-O Invictus
variants.overview: The Deva is the heavier close-combat Celestial OmniMech at 70 tons, and the Word of Blake's design philosophy is evident throughout — the Inspiration 280 light fusion engine rather than XL is an unusual choice that reflects specific engineering priorities. The Celestial series exotic components are the consistent maintenance challenge across this family.
variants.capabilities: The light fusion engine rather than XL changes the damage profile compared to most heavies — different vulnerability considerations, different repair procedures. The Celestial Series DV1E endo steel chassis is well-made but requires Blakist-spec documentation and tooling for structural work. The OmniMech pod system uses non-standard interfaces that complicate cross-configuration work. Nine configurations require extensive parts inventory.
variants.deployment: Nine configurations including the Invictus close-combat variant. The Gauss rifle configuration requires capacitor maintenance on top of the Celestial-specific component considerations. Outside Word of Blake supply chains, parts sourcing for Celestial-series specific components is difficult. Assign dedicated Celestial-qualified techs rather than rotating general staff through these machines.

variants.name: DVS-2-EC
variants.overview: General Kerensky personally designed the Devastator to correct what he saw as flaws in the Titan prototype, which gives it a provenance that ensures it gets taken seriously. Development halted and the design reached the Clans, where Clan technicians built the first operational examples. The twin Poland Main Model A Gauss rifles are the heart of it and they're excellent hardware.
variants.capabilities: Dual Gauss rifles for long-range dominance is the explicit design philosophy and it works. The synchronized dual capacitor maintenance is the primary technical focus — two Gauss capacitor systems require coordinated inspection schedules and the cascade failure risk from deferred maintenance is significant. The slow speed is the design trade-off accepted for the weapons payload and protection level.
variants.deployment: Seven variants from Clan-built originals through Inner Sphere recovered and modernized versions. The earliest Clan-built variants are the most historically interesting and the most challenging to support with modern IS parts. Later recovered and refitted variants substitute available components. The dual Gauss capacitor advisory applies to all Gauss-equipped configurations — synchronized maintenance schedules are non-negotiable.

The twin Poland Main Model A Gauss rifles are the heart of it and they're excellent hardware.
variants.capabilities: Dual Gauss rifles for long-range dominance is the explicit design philosophy and it works. The synchronized dual capacitor maintenance is the primary technical focus — two Gauss capacitor systems require coordinated inspection schedules and the cascade failure risk from deferred maintenance is significant. The slow speed is the design trade-off accepted for the weapons payload and protection level.
variants.deployment: Seven variants from Clan-built originals through Inner Sphere recovered and modernized versions. The earliest Clan-built variants are the most historically interesting and the most challenging to support with modern IS parts. Later recovered and refitted variants substitute available components. The dual Gauss capacitor advisory applies to all Gauss-equipped configurations — synchronized maintenance schedules are non-negotiable.

variants.name: DOL-1A
variants.overview: Shengli Arms introduced the Dola from Victoria in the early 3080s as a fast Capellan light, and 129 kph from a Ceres Motors 240 XL at 30 tons delivers on the speed promise. The experimental prototype origin of the first hulls means early production documentation has some gaps that later production filled in.
variants.capabilities: The Ceres Motors 240 XL pushing 30 tons to 129 kph is impressive speed for the weight class and the XL concern at this velocity is the standard advisory. The advanced composite internal structure on the original prototype is a non-standard component requiring specific repair knowledge — confirm documentation before working on prototype hulls. Production variants use more conventional construction throughout.
variants.deployment: Three variants from the experimental prototype through production configurations. The original prototype's advanced composite structure is the component most likely to create maintenance challenges outside Shengli Arms support channels. Production variants are more straightforward. Shengli parts support through Capellan Confederation logistics is reliable for production models.

variants.name: DLR-O
variants.overview: StarCorps produced the Doloire in 3121 as the flagship Republic Armed Forces assault OmniMech. Eighty tons, walk four, run six on the 320-rated Clan XL engine. Six configurations. The Clan engine in an IS chassis creates a two-track maintenance requirement that every tech on this platform needs to understand from the first day.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at eighty tons. The Clan XL engine requires Clan-spec tooling while the rest of the chassis uses IS-standard procedures. Side torso vulnerability standard to all Clan XL installations. Thirty-three tons of pod space is generous for an assault OmniMech. IS construction quality on the chassis components. The Prime carries a Gauss rifle, two large pulse lasers, and two ER medium lasers. Walk four, run six. The Gauss provides accurate long-range fire. The large pulse lasers cover medium range accurately. The ER mediums handle close engagement. The Prime configuration includes a command console for two-crew operation.
variants.deployment: The Prime is the command platform configuration. The command console enables coordinated operations. The Gauss and pulse laser combination provides consistent fire across multiple ranges. Clan engine maintenance is required alongside IS chassis procedures. Thirty-three tons of remaining pod space allows significant configuration variety.

variants.overview: Clan Wolf introduced the Dominator from their W-12 Facilities on Zosma in 3148 as a versatile heavy, and the field refit origin of the second variant tells you something about how pilots responded to the original — they wanted changes and the factory eventually agreed. The Starfire 325 XL in a Type W4 Endo Steel frame is reliable Wolf construction.
variants.capabilities: The Starfire 325 XL gives meaningful speed for a heavy and the Type W4 frame is well-made Wolf hardware. The XL vulnerability concern applies as always. The field refit that became the factory second variant is interesting from a maintenance standpoint — components that started as improvised solutions have varying documentation quality depending on how systematically the factory formalized them.
variants.deployment: Two variants with the second originating as a popular field modification before factory adoption. The field-origin second variant may have documentation variations compared to factory-designed configurations — verify documentation completeness before committing to a maintenance program. Wolf parts support through their Zosma facility is reliable for both variants.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Hell's Horses introduced the Doom Courser in 3147 from their Csesztreg Industriplex, and the quad heavy OmniMech at 70 tons reflects Hell's Horses' enduring commitment to quad chassis designs. The endo-composite chassis is the unusual construction choice that sets it apart from most quads I've worked on.
variants.capabilities: The Csesztreg Quad 70.1 Endo-Composite chassis combines endo steel weight savings with composite structure reinforcement in a way that requires specific repair knowledge different from standard endo steel or standard composite procedures. The standard 280-rated fusion engine rather than XL is a deliberate choice that improves the chassis damage tolerance profile. Quad maintenance overhead applies — more leg systems, longer inspection cycles. Five OmniMech configurations multiply the pod maintenance.
variants.deployment: Five configurations with Configuration A's ATM focus being a common choice. The endo-composite structure is the consistent maintenance advisory — ensure your techs have specific training on composite repair procedures before working on structural battle damage. The standard engine choice makes the chassis more forgiving of side torso hits than XL-equipped quads. Hell's Horses logistics support is reliable.

variants.name: DRG-1C
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Dragon in 2754 as an advanced close assault 'Mech for the DCMS, and the original prototype's different autocannon choice compared to production is a detail worth knowing when working on early hulls. The combination of respectable firepower, genuine speed, and durability made it a DCMS staple that's remained in service for centuries.
variants.capabilities: The Dragon delivers on the close assault brief through a weapons mix that's effective at multiple ranges while the speed keeps it relevant. The chassis durability is genuine — these machines take hits and stay operational. Six variants over the production run show ongoing refinement. LAW construction quality is consistent and parts are available throughout Combine supply networks.
variants.deployment: Six variants from the 2754 prototype through modern configurations. The original prototype with its AC/2 rather than the production AC/5 is the historical outlier — know which variant you have before working from the standard manual. Production variants are the common case. LAW parts support through Combine channels is reliable and the long production history means most techs have seen a Dragon before their first assignment.

variants.name: DGR-3F
variants.overview: The Dragon Fire traces its origin to the same development project that produced the Marauder, emerging from JBBMI's Storfors facility in 3058 after a development history that stretched back to the twenty-eighth century. The Pitban 300 XL and Royalstar endo steel frame are the modern engineering foundation for a concept that waited a long time to reach production.
variants.capabilities: The Pitban 300 XL gives good heavy performance and the endo steel structure requires trained techs for structural repairs. The weapons balance across ranges is the design strength — this is not a single-engagement-distance machine. Four variants over the production run show steady refinement. The long development history means the concept was well-proven before the production design was finalized.
variants.deployment: Four variants from the initial 3058 production through subsequent developments. The original production model is the reference and the one most commonly encountered. The XL concern applies consistently. JBBMI parts support varies by political situation; the design has been adopted widely enough that supply chains exist outside the original manufacturer's territory.

variants.name: DRG-11K
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works developed the Dragon II post-Jihad as a modernization using technologies developed during the conflict, and the Arrow IV artillery integration is the defining departure from the original Dragon line. This is a fundamentally different machine than the Dragon despite the naming — fire support rather than close assault.
variants.capabilities: The Shigunga Arrow IV system is the centerpiece and the primary maintenance focus. Arrow IV artillery systems require specific maintenance knowledge and the specialized munitions need careful storage and handling protocols different from standard missile systems. The fire support role means the Dragon II operates differently from the close assault design it's nominally descended from — brief pilots accordingly.
variants.deployment: Two variants, both centered on the Arrow IV capability. The Arrow IV ammunition supply chain is the critical logistics factor — specialized munitions, careful storage requirements, limited availability compared to standard missiles. Establish the supply chain before deploying these machines. LAW parts support through Combine channels is reliable for the non-artillery components.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Fire Mandrill produced the Viper — Inner Sphere designation Dragonfly — in 2940 on Shadow, and the 130 kph at 40 tons is the performance headline that defined Clan light OmniMech design philosophy for decades. Eighteen configurations over the production run reflect extensive exploitation of the speed and pod space combination.
variants.capabilities: The Type W2 Endo-steel chassis and 320-rated XL achieving 130 kph at 40 tons is genuinely impressive and the XL concern at this speed is the standard advisory. The OmniMech pod system gives excellent flexibility for the weight class. Eighteen configurations mean significant parts inventory requirements. Clan Fire Mandrill construction quality is consistent. The speed is the armor — that briefing applies to pilots of any configuration.
variants.deployment: Eighteen configurations from close harassment to long-range fire support. Configuration A's close-range focus with ER medium lasers and Artemis SRM is the most common encountered. The Artemis calibration requirement applies to the SRM configuration. variants.name: AEM-01
variants.overview: Stefan Amaris commissioned the Dragoon as part of his vision for modular standardised military equipment. Seventy tons, walk four, run six, jump three on the 280-rated XL engine. Two variants. The documentation gap from the Amaris period is the primary maintenance challenge.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump three at seventy tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Jump three provides terrain exploitation options. The multi-mission modular design concept is visible in the weapons layout. The AEM-01 carries two LB 10-X ACs and an ER PPC. Walk four, run six, jump three. The LB 10-X pair provides cluster and slug ballistic options. The ER PPC extends direct fire reach. The two autocannons and a PPC together cover multiple engagement ranges.
variants.deployment: The AEM-01 is the frontline configuration and the more commonly encountered variant. The documentation gap from the Amaris period means some maintenance procedures require reverse-engineering from the hardware rather than consulting original records. The LB 10-X cluster option against lighter opponents is the primary flexibility advantage.

variants.name: AEM-05C
variants.overview: Stefan Amaris commissioned the Dragoon as part of his vision for modular standardised military equipment. Seventy tons, walk four, run six, jump three on the 280-rated XL engine. Two variants. The documentation gap from the Amaris period is the primary maintenance challenge.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump three at seventy tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Jump three provides terrain exploitation options. The multi-mission modular design concept is visible in the weapons layout. The AEM-05C carries a plasma rifle, two medium X-pulse lasers, and an LB 10-X. Walk four, run six, jump three. The plasma rifle superheats targets while dealing damage. The X-pulse lasers are accurate at close range. The LB 10-X provides ballistic flexibility.
variants.deployment: The AEM-05C is the thermal disruption variant. The plasma rifle forces heat problems on opponents. The X-pulse accuracy suits close-range engagement. The LB 10-X handles ballistic fire. The Amaris documentation gap applies to this variant as to the AEM-01. XL engine vulnerability.

variants.name: D9-G9
variants.overview: Shengli Arms built the Duan Gung in 3058 for the Capellan Confederation as a light fire support platform that can approach 120 kph, and that speed is what makes the fire support concept work at 25 tons. The Chilton system gives it genuine indirect fire capability at a weight class that usually can't support artillery-type weapons.
variants.capabilities: Approaching 120 kph at 25 tons while carrying meaningful fire support weapons is the design achievement. The Chilton system requires specific maintenance knowledge different from standard missile systems. The light armor is the expected trade-off for speed and weapons payload at this weight. Three variants cover different tactical refinements. Shengli construction quality is solid.
variants.deployment: Three variants with the base D9-G9 being the most widely fielded in CCAF service. The fire support role at this speed and weight creates specific operational requirements that pilots need to understand — this is not a conventional light 'Mech assignment. The Chilton system maintenance advisory is consistent across variants. Shengli parts support through Capellan channels is reliable.

variants.name: EGL-1M
variants.overview: Curtiss Militech introduced the Eagle in 3058 as a follow-up to the Wraith, aiming for a light 'Mech with extended-range punch that the Wraith's speed-focused design didn't deliver. The Diverse Optics Type 10 ER large laser is the primary weapon and it punches above the weight class at range.
variants.capabilities: Not as fast as many lights in the class, which is the acknowledged trade-off for the extended-range firepower. The Diverse Optics ER large laser is a quality system with good documentation. The TAG system added to later variants changes the tactical role significantly — from direct engagement to target designation for indirect fire, which is a different operational concept requiring different pilot training.
variants.deployment: Three variants, with the original lacking the TAG system that became the design's signature on later configurations. The TAG-equipped variants are the more tactically versatile for units with artillery support. The original without TAG is the simpler maintenance case. Curtiss Militech parts support through their distribution channels is adequate.

variants.name: MEB-10
variants.overview: The Magistracy of Canopus and Capellan Confederation jointly produced the Ebony in 3081 as a covert operations light, and the design reflects that mission — fast, stealthy, and armed for the specific requirements of clandestine work rather than conventional combat. The Magna 250 XL at 25 tons gives 108 kph to support the covert mission.
variants.capabilities: The stealth systems are the primary maintenance focus — calibration requirements are ongoing and any armor damage degrades stealth performance in ways that aren't always immediately visible. The Magna 250 XL gives genuine speed for the covert role. Five variants cover different covert mission profiles. The joint development means parts support exists through both Magistracy and Capellan channels.
variants.deployment: Five variants adapted for different covert operation requirements. The stealth system maintenance advisory is consistent across all configurations — keep the calibration current. The ER large laser versus snub-nose PPC distinction between variants changes the engagement range profile significantly. Parts support through both joint-development partner channels provides reasonable supply options.

variants.name: C-EID-001
variants.overview: The Eidolon was assembled during the final Jihad years from surplus Celestial OmniMech components, which tells you everything about its origin — improvised, limited production, built to fill a specific gap with available materials. The improved jump jets giving 210 meters of capability are the defining feature for its broken terrain and urban spotter role.
variants.capabilities: The 210-meter jump capability is exceptional and the whole tactical concept depends on it. Celestial-component origin means some parts are non-standard and documentation varies. The improved C3 computer requires specialist calibration. The snub-nose PPCs are effective for the short-range work the role demands. Extreme production limitations mean each hull is somewhat individual in its specific component fit.
variants.deployment: Single production variant, extremely limited numbers. The Celestial-component origin is the primary maintenance challenge — parts sourcing requires Blakist-era supply channels that don't exist cleanly post-Jihad. Build detailed records for each individual hull since batch consistency is lower than in normal production. The jump capability is what makes this chassis valuable; protect the jump jet systems as the priority maintenance focus.

variants.name: EFT-2
variants.overview: The Eisenfaust reached production during the Jihad, fulfilling a 2469 LCAF commission that went through a very long development history. The plasma rifle focus is the defining modern characteristic, though the original 2469 design called for conventional autocannon armament. variants.name: END-6J-EC
variants.overview: The Enfield's origins go back to the Star League era as an urban combat design, and the Blackstone MD2E endo steel chassis with Magna 250 XL gives it 86 kph at 50 tons for the medium-heavy bracket. The Golden Century Clan Mongoose adaptation and subsequent Inner Sphere variants show a design that crossed factional lines.
variants.capabilities: The Magna 250 XL gives good speed for a 50-ton design and the XL vulnerability concern applies. The endo steel structure requires trained techs for structural repairs. The Golden Century Clan Mongoose adaptation changed the weapons fit substantially from the IS original — know which version you have. Five variants cover the factional diversity of the design's production history.
variants.deployment: Five variants spanning the design's complicated production history across multiple factions. The Clan Mongoose Cudahy Assembly variant is the most historically unusual. The IS production variants are the more commonly encountered. Parts availability varies by variant lineage — IS-origin components through IS channels, Clan-adapted components through Clan channels. Confirm the specific variant's heritage before planning parts sourcing.

variants.name: ENF-4R
variants.overview: Achernar BattleMechs built the Enforcer in 2777 from recovered Star League schematics, and the design reflects that careful reconstruction from historical documentation. The Federated Autocannon/10's cooling jacket doubling as arm protection is one of the more elegant engineering details on this chassis. Five variants show ongoing development of the basic concept.
variants.capabilities: The autocannon and large laser combination is straightforward and proven. The cooling jacket arm protection detail means arm actuator work needs to account for the thermal systems integrated into that structure — not complex but different from a standard arm. The Federated Suns association means parts availability is excellent through FedSuns logistics. The chassis is well-documented and most techs know it.
variants.deployment: Five variants from the 2777 original through modern configurations. The original is the simplest and most maintenance-friendly. Later variants add advanced electronics and upgraded weapons. The cooling jacket arm detail is the consistent briefing point for techs new to the design. Achernar parts support through Federated Suns channels is reliable and the design is well-supported throughout the Suns.

variants.name: ENF-6M
variants.overview: First Prince Victor Steiner-Davion commissioned the Enforcer III as part of his Redesign for Davion Pride initiative following the Lyran secession, and the design reflects that political context — an explicitly Davion machine built around Davion technology and traditions. The Dorwinion Standard-Alpha endo steel chassis and Magna 250 XL are the engineering foundation.
variants.capabilities: The Mydron Excel Ultra AC/10 is a quality weapon but ultra-class autocannons require more maintenance attention than standard — the dual-rate mechanism is more complex and more sensitive to wear. The XL gives good speed for 50 tons with the familiar vulnerability concern. The BlazeFire ER large laser backup is reliable. Ten variants show extensive development of the basic Davion design.
variants.deployment: Ten variants developed over the production run. The baseline Enforcer III is the reference. The Ultra AC/10 maintenance advisory applies to all Ultra-equipped variants — keep the mechanism clean and replace wearing components on schedule rather than waiting for performance degradation. XL advisory applies consistently. Davion parts support is excellent throughout Federated Suns territory.

The Dorwinion Standard-Alpha endo steel chassis and Magna 250 XL are the engineering foundation.
variants.capabilities: The Mydron Excel Ultra AC/10 is a quality weapon but ultra-class autocannons require more maintenance attention than standard — the dual-rate mechanism is more complex and more sensitive to wear. The XL gives good speed for 50 tons with the familiar vulnerability concern. The BlazeFire ER large laser backup is reliable. Ten variants show extensive development of the basic Davion design.
variants.deployment: Ten variants developed over the production run. The baseline Enforcer III is the reference. The Ultra AC/10 maintenance advisory applies to all Ultra-equipped variants — keep the mechanism clean and replace wearing components on schedule rather than waiting for performance degradation. XL advisory applies consistently. Davion parts support is excellent throughout Federated Suns territory.

variants.name: Prime
variants.overview: The Epimetheus was built in 3053 as a technology demonstrator integrating Clan technology into an Inner Sphere chassis, and it served on Solaris VII as an arena combatant. Single prototype status means each element of working on this machine involves more research than standard production designs.
variants.capabilities: The mixed IS-Clan technology integration is impressive engineering that creates specific maintenance challenges. IS and Clan components don't always share documentation standards, tooling requirements, or parts interfaces. The arena combatant history means it's been repaired under varying conditions by various hands — build your own technical record for this hull from current examination rather than trusting inherited documentation.
variants.deployment: Single prototype, arena combat history. Treat every maintenance session as an opportunity to document what's actually in the machine versus what the original specification called for — arena machines accumulate changes. The Clan component portions require Clan-spec tooling. The IS portions use standard tools. Keep the two clearly separated in your work procedures to avoid cross-contamination of techniques.

variants.name: ERS-2H
variants.overview: Kallon Weapons built the Eris when component supply problems blocked the original Hel design, adapting the proven N&D HLBM endo steel frame and Hermes 250 XL into a different weapons configuration. The supply disruption origin means the Eris and Hel share structural maintenance procedures while differing in weapons systems.
variants.capabilities: The shared Hel chassis means structural maintenance knowledge transfers directly between the two designs. The weapons configuration is where they diverge — the Eris mounts significantly different armament reflecting what was available and what the mission required after the Hel's supply chain problems. The Hermes 250 XL gives 86 kph at 50 tons with the familiar XL concern. Three variants show adaptation to supply and mission requirements.
variants.deployment: Three variants, with the supply disruption context explaining some of the weapons variation. The original Hel configuration resurgence noted in the deployment history reflects availability dynamics — whichever variant you're maintaining depends on what components are in supply. The structural commonality with the Hel is the practical maintenance advantage. Kallon parts support through their distribution channels is reliable.

variants.name: EXC-B1
variants.overview: Yankee Weapons Systems built the Excalibur in 2620 for the Star League Defense Force as a devastating fire platform, and the Ford 350 XL giving 86 kph at 70 tons makes it one of the faster heavies in its class. Star League construction quality throughout the original variants. Eight configurations show extensive development of the base concept.
variants.capabilities: The Ford 350 XL's speed advantage for a heavy is real and tactically significant. The XL vulnerability concern applies and at 70 tons a side torso breach is serious. The Star League construction quality on original hulls is excellent. The original prototype's small pulse laser in place of CASE is the variant detail worth knowing before working on early hulls — confirm the specific configuration before applying the standard manual.
variants.deployment: Eight variants from the Star League prototype through subsequent developments. The prototype differs from production in the CASE detail — know which hull you have. Production variants are the common operational case. The speed advantage is the consistent tactical asset across the family. Star League parts sourcing for original-spec components is variable; later variants substituting available components are more supportable.

variants.name: EXR-2X
variants.overview: Independence Weaponry built the Exhumer during the Republic's waning years for the Benjamin District Regulars as a fast fifty-five ton raider. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated XL engine. Two variants. The speed is the design's core asset.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at fifty-five tons. Walk six, run nine is genuinely useful speed for the raiding role. XL engine — side torso vulnerability is the consistent concern at this speed. Independence Weaponry parts availability within Combine territory. The EXR-2X carries two ER large lasers, two LRM-5s, and an MRM-10. Walk six, run nine on the XL engine. The ER large lasers provide extended-range direct fire. The MRM-10 delivers medium-range missile volume. The LRM-5s add modest indirect fire.
variants.deployment: The EXR-2X is the original raiding configuration. Walk six, run nine enables aggressive repositioning during raid operations. The ER large laser range combined with MRM-10 medium-range pressure creates a versatile threat profile. XL engine vulnerability is the standing concern at this speed.

variants.name: EXR-3P
variants.overview: Independence Weaponry built the Exhumer during the Republic's waning years for the Benjamin District Regulars as a fast fifty-five ton raider. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated XL engine. Two variants. The speed is the design's core asset.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at fifty-five tons. Walk six, run nine is genuinely useful speed for the raiding role. XL engine — side torso vulnerability is the consistent concern at this speed. Independence Weaponry parts availability within Combine territory. The EXR-3P carries two large pulse lasers, three SRM-2 launchers, and an ER small laser. Walk six, run nine. The large pulse lasers are accurate at medium range. The SRM-2s add close-range missile volume. The ER small laser handles point-blank threats.
variants.deployment: The EXR-3P is the close-range variant. The large pulse laser accuracy at medium range and SRM-2 volume at close range creates a layered close-combat capability. The ER small laser handles anything at point-blank. XL engine vulnerability applies throughout.

variants.name: EXT-4C
variants.overview: General Systems designed the Exterminator in 2630 specifically to kill enemy command personnel, and the Null-Signature System is the whole point. The electronic warfare suite matters more than the weapons on this chassis. Working on the stealth systems is the primary technical challenge and the primary maintenance priority.
variants.capabilities: The Null-Signature System and related electronic warfare components are what make this machine relevant and they require specialist maintenance that general techs aren't trained for. Any armor damage that compromises the stealth systems changes the tactical calculus completely — the Exterminator without its stealth is a mediocre medium 'Mech. The weapons are adequate for the headhunter mission rather than line combat. Ten variants over the production run.
variants.deployment: Ten variants from the 2630 Star League original through subsequent adaptations. The full stealth package variants are the authentic Exterminator configuration. Later variants that omit some stealth components are more maintainable but miss the design's core purpose. The electronic warfare specialist requirement is non-negotiable on properly configured variants. Know which specific stealth systems your variant carries before planning the maintenance program.

variants.name: EYL-4A
variants.overview: The Trinity Alliance collaborative effort produced the Eyleuka in the late 3060s as a special operations medium, and the Canopian prototype origin of the first dozen units means early hull documentation is sparse. The stealth technology and jump capability combination defines the special operations mission this chassis was built for.
variants.capabilities: Impressive jump capability combined with stealth systems creates a medium that can go places conventional 'Mechs can't reach undetected. The ground speed trade-off for the aerial mobility is deliberate and explicit. The stealth calibration requirement is the ongoing maintenance focus — any armor damage degrades stealth performance. Four variants cover different Trinity Alliance member state adaptations.
variants.deployment: Four variants with the original Canopian prototype being the rarest and most challenging to document. The Trinity Alliance production variants are the more commonly encountered. The stealth system maintenance advisory is consistent — keep calibration current and treat armor integrity as a stealth performance issue, not just a protection issue. Parts support through the joint Alliance channels.

The ground speed trade-off for the aerial mobility is deliberate and explicit. The stealth calibration requirement is the ongoing maintenance focus — any armor damage degrades stealth performance. Four variants cover different Trinity Alliance member state adaptations.
variants.deployment: Four variants with the original Canopian prototype being the rarest and most challenging to document. The Trinity Alliance production variants are the more commonly encountered. The stealth system maintenance advisory is consistent — keep calibration current and treat armor integrity as a stealth performance issue, not just a protection issue. Parts support through the joint Alliance channels.

variants.name: FNR-5
variants.overview: Defiance Industries built the Fafnir in 3063 on Hesperus II, borrowing heavily from Atlas production experience, and the result is a hundred-ton assault that embodies Lyran design philosophy — maximum protection, maximum firepower, minimum concern for speed. The dual Heavy Gauss rifles are the design identity and they are impressive hardware.
variants.capabilities: The twin Heavy Gauss rifles on the base FNR-5 are the most powerful direct fire ballistic weapons I've worked on at any weight class. The capacitor maintenance requirement for two Heavy Gauss systems simultaneously is substantial — synchronized inspection schedules are essential and the consequence of capacitor failure at the wrong moment is severe. The Atlas production commonality is useful for structural and chassis maintenance.
variants.deployment: Six variants from the 3061 prototype through production and modernized configurations. The Heavy Gauss capacitor advisory applies to all Gauss-equipped variants — this is not the system where you defer maintenance. The Atlas chassis commonality means Hesperus II-trained techs adapt quickly. Defiance Industries parts support through Lyran logistics is excellent.

variants.name: FLC-4N
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Falcon in 2582 for the Star League Defence Force, and the design emphasis on protection over speed makes it unusual for a 30-tonner. The StarGuard Type II armour is the design signature: six tons on a 30-ton chassis is substantially more than comparable lights and it changes how the machine fights and survives. Walk six, run nine, jump six from the 180-rated fusion engine.
variants.capabilities: The 4N carries two small lasers, one medium laser, and two machine guns. The weapons fit is modest but the armour is the point. Pilots in a Falcon can afford to take hits that would force lighter-armoured competitors to break off. The machine guns handle infantry effectively. The medium laser is the primary anti-'Mech tool at this tonnage. Maintenance on Star League construction standards is more documentation-intensive than later production runs.
variants.deployment: The 4N is the original production model, the reference configuration for the family. It deploys as a scout and skirmisher that can hold its ground when cornered rather than depending entirely on avoiding contact. The armour advantage is most valuable in urban and broken terrain where light 'Mechs frequently take hits they cannot avoid. Parts sourcing for Star League original components is the consistent challenge.

variants.name: FLC-4Nb
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Falcon in 2582 for the Star League Defence Force, and the design emphasis on protection over speed makes it unusual for a 30-tonner. The StarGuard Type II armour is the design signature: six tons on a 30-ton chassis is substantially more than comparable lights and it changes how the machine fights and survives. Walk six, run nine, jump six from the 180-rated fusion engine.
variants.capabilities: The 4Nb carries two medium lasers and a snub-nose PPC. The snub-nose PPC is the upgrade over the original weapons fit, providing meaningful punch at short to medium range that the machine guns of the 4N lack against armoured targets. The snub-nose trades extended reach for a cleaner engagement profile at the ranges a 30-ton machine typically fights. Heat is manageable across this loadout.
variants.deployment: The 4Nb is an upgraded striker variant of the original. The snub-nose PPC makes it more capable against light to medium armoured targets than the 4N. The armour protection remains the chassis constant: this variant can survive contact that would force lighter designs to withdraw. It deploys in the same scout and skirmisher roles as the original with better anti-armour capability.

variants.name: FLC-4Nb-PP
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Falcon in 2582 for the Star League Defence Force, and the design emphasis on protection over speed makes it unusual for a 30-tonner. The StarGuard Type II armour is the design signature: six tons on a 30-ton chassis is substantially more than comparable lights and it changes how the machine fights and survives. Walk six, run nine, jump six from the 180-rated fusion engine.
variants.capabilities: The 4Nb-PP carries a single medium laser and a standard PPC. A PPC on a 30-ton chassis is an aggressive weapons choice and the heat load is significant relative to the size of the machine. The medium laser provides backup when the PPC heat curve demands a pause. The armour protection cushions the vulnerability that comes from a light 'Mech that needs to hold range for the PPC to work effectively.
variants.deployment: The 4Nb-PP is a sniper variant built around the PPC's range. The jump capability lets it claim elevated positions where the PPC reach advantage is maximised. The heat management requirement means the pilot fires the PPC and steps back, allowing heat to dissipate before the next shot. Against opponents who can close range faster than the pilot can manage heat, the armour becomes critical.

variants.name: FLC-4Nb-PP2
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Falcon in 2582 for the Star League Defence Force, and the design emphasis on protection over speed makes it unusual for a 30-tonner. The StarGuard Type II armour is the design signature: six tons on a 30-ton chassis is substantially more than comparable lights and it changes how the machine fights and survives. Walk six, run nine, jump six from the 180-rated fusion engine.
variants.capabilities: The 4Nb-PP2 carries an ER large laser, a medium pulse laser, and a medium laser. This is the most weapons-capable Falcon configuration by range and damage output. The ER large laser reaches further than the standard PPC variant and runs cooler. The medium pulse laser and medium laser provide close-range backup. Heat across all three weapons simultaneously is aggressive for a 30-ton frame but manageable on cycle.
variants.deployment: The 4Nb-PP2 is the long-range engagement variant of the Falcon family. The ER large laser combined with jump capability allows the pilot to threaten opponents from positions that deny close-range retaliation. The armour allows it to absorb return fire that would force lighter competitors to withdraw. This is the Falcon variant that most rewards pilots who understand how to use terrain.

variants.name: FLC-4Nb (Saho)
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Falcon in 2582 for the Star League Defence Force, and the design emphasis on protection over speed makes it unusual for a 30-tonner. The StarGuard Type II armour is the design signature: six tons on a 30-ton chassis is substantially more than comparable lights and it changes how the machine fights and survives. Walk six, run nine, jump six from the 180-rated fusion engine.
variants.capabilities: The Saho is a named pilot configuration carrying a medium laser and a large pulse laser. The large pulse laser is accurate at medium range and generates less heat than comparable energy weapons at this output level. The medium laser provides backup at close range. This is a personalised loadout built around a specific warrior's preferences rather than a general design philosophy.
variants.deployment: The Saho configuration uses the large pulse laser's accuracy and the Falcon's armour to stay in engagements longer than most light 'Mechs. The named pilot designation means this is not a production variant and maintaining it to exact spec requires knowing the original configuration documentation. The chassis itself is standard Falcon and presents no unusual maintenance requirements.

variants.name: FLC-4P
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Falcon in 2582 for the Star League Defence Force, and the design emphasis on protection over speed makes it unusual for a 30-tonner. The StarGuard Type II armour is the design signature: six tons on a 30-ton chassis is substantially more than comparable lights and it changes how the machine fights and survives. Walk six, run nine, jump five from the 180-rated fusion engine on this variant.
variants.capabilities: The 4P carries two small lasers, a medium pulse laser, and an anti-missile system. The AMS replaces one jump jet compared to the standard configuration, dropping jump capability from six to five. The medium pulse laser is more accurate than the standard medium laser at close range. The AMS provides real defensive value in missile-heavy environments. The small lasers handle infantry and very light targets.
variants.deployment: The 4P is a scout configuration with AMS protection added for operations in environments where missile fire is a consistent threat. The reduced jump capability is the trade-off. It deploys in the same scout and security roles as the 4N with better anti-missile survivability. The AMS ammunition requires its own supply management alongside the machine's other logistics needs.

variants.name: FLC-5P
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Falcon in 2582 for the Star League Defence Force. The 5P is a later production variant built on a light engine rather than the original standard fusion, which improves side torso survivability at the cost of some mass efficiency.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump five on the 180-rated light engine at thirty tons. The light engine provides better side torso survivability than earlier variants. The all-energy loadout removes ammunition dependency entirely. The 5P carries two ER medium lasers and a medium pulse laser. The light engine is the significant change from earlier variants: side torso hits that would be immediately fatal to an XL-equipped design leave this running. The weapons loadout is clean and energy-only, requiring no ammunition management.
variants.deployment: The 5P is a later-era upgrade preserving the Falcon's protection-focused identity while improving resilience to torso damage. The all-energy loadout suits independent operations without resupply support. Jump five is one less than the standard six, a minor compromise for the weapons and engine package.

variants.name: FLC-6C
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Falcon in 2582 for the Star League Defence Force. The 6C is a mixed-tech variant using a Clan fusion engine on an IS chassis, a combination that produces maintenance complexity but genuine performance benefits. Walk six, run nine, jump five at thirty tons.
variants.capabilities: The 6C carries an ER large laser, two ER small lasers, and an anti-missile system. The Clan engine requires Clan-spec maintenance procedures alongside IS chassis procedures. The ER large laser provides reach that earlier Falcon variants lack. The AMS is a genuine defensive asset rather than a token. The jump capability drops to five compared to the standard six, a minor compromise for the weapons and AMS package.
variants.deployment: The 6C is the most capable Falcon variant at range, with the ER large laser threatening opponents that earlier configurations could not effectively engage. The AMS provides protection in missile-heavy environments. Maintaining the Clan engine alongside IS components requires a tech comfortable with both maintenance standards. Parts sourcing for the mixed-tech components is the persistent logistics challenge.

variants.name: FNHK-9K
variants.overview: Kallon Industries designed the Falcon Hawk in 2794 but didn't actually produce it until 3057, which is an unusually long gap between design and production. The concept — long-range firepower from a light chassis — waited 263 years to reach service. At 35 tons with extended-range weapons emphasis it delivers on that original concept.
variants.capabilities: Long-range engagement from a light chassis works when the pilot uses terrain and distance effectively, and the Falcon Hawk's weapons support that approach. The design doesn't win straight-up engagements against heavier opponents but it doesn't need to. Three variants cover different weapons emphases on the same base chassis. Kallon construction quality is solid and consistent.
variants.deployment: Three variants from the 3057 production through subsequent configurations. The base FNHK-9K is the reference. The long-range engagement philosophy requires pilots who understand range management — this isn't a close-range brawler. Kallon parts support through their distribution channels is reliable. The 263-year design-to-production gap means the design has modern construction standards despite the older concept.

variants.name: FLC-8R
variants.overview: First Prince Hanse Davion personally directed the creation of the Falconer shortly before his death in 3052, wanting a design that could match Clan weapon ranges while maintaining Inner Sphere durability. The GM 375 XL gives it 86 kph at 75 tons — fast for the weight class — and the design philosophy reflects Hanse's direct combat experience against the Clans.
variants.capabilities: The GM 375 XL pushing 75 tons to 86 kph is the performance foundation and the XL vulnerability concern is the standard advisory. The extended-range weapons emphasis addresses the range disadvantage that Inner Sphere units experienced against Clan opponents. Two variants with meaningfully different weapons configurations. The Prince's personal direction shows in the quality of the original design brief.
variants.deployment: Two variants. The original Falconer saw its first combat with elite Davion units — the Heavy Guards, Deneb Light Cavalry, and Arcturan Guards. The XL advisory is consistent across both variants. The extended-range weapons focus means heat management discipline is essential — brief pilots on managing the higher heat loads of the ER weapons compared to standard alternatives. Federated Suns parts support is reliable.

variants.name: FEC-1CM
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Fennec in 3080 to address a specific AFFS gap in medium strike capability, sharing the Corean Model AG47 endo steel chassis and VOX 330 XL with the Legionnaire. That chassis commonality is genuinely useful for any unit operating both designs. The Davion Guards were the initial recipients.
variants.capabilities: The shared Legionnaire chassis means structural maintenance experience transfers directly — if your techs know the Legionnaire, the Fennec's structural work will be familiar. The VOX 330 XL gives good speed for 55 tons with the familiar XL vulnerability. The weapons complement is designed for the medium strike role that drove the procurement requirement. Three variants show refinement.
variants.deployment: Three variants on the same Legionnaire-shared chassis. The original production model entered service with the Davion Guards' medium strike companies. The chassis commonality with the Legionnaire is the maintenance advantage worth exploiting in any unit operating both designs — shared parts, shared structural procedures, shared tech training. Corean Enterprises parts support through Federated Suns channels is reliable.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Ice Hellion produced the Ice Ferret — Inner Sphere designation Fenris — in 2948 at their W-7 facility, and the 360-rated XL achieving 129 kph at 45 tons is the performance headline. That speed defines everything about how this machine is used and maintained. Fifteen configurations over the production history show extensive exploitation of the fast medium OmniMech concept.
variants.capabilities: 129 kph for a 45-ton OmniMech is fast even by Clan standards and the XL enabling that speed carries its usual vulnerability concern. At this speed a side torso breach is a serious tactical problem very quickly. The OmniMech pod system is well-implemented. Fifteen configurations means substantial pod inventory requirements. Ice Hellion construction quality is consistent.
variants.deployment: Fifteen configurations covering the tactical spectrum. Configuration A's LB 2-X long-range sniping role is an unusual choice for a fast medium. The XL advisory applies universally. Parts support varies by which Clan faction is currently operating the design following Ice Hellion's dissolution. The speed is the armor — pilots who forget that and try to absorb hits in a Fenris don't last long.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Jade Falcon introduced the Fire Falcon in the early 3050s as a replacement for the aging Mist Lynx, and the JF 200 XL achieving 129 kph at 25 tons delivers on the fast ultralight OmniMech concept. Thirteen configurations reflect extensive Falcon use of this chassis across a wide range of tactical roles.
variants.capabilities: 129 kph at 25 tons is genuinely fast and the OmniMech flexibility adds versatility that fixed ultralight designs can't match. At 25 tons the pod space is extremely limited and configuration selection matters more than on heavier OmniMechs — there's simply not much room to work with. The XL vulnerability at this weight class is different from heavier designs; at 25 tons a side torso breach is usually mission-ending.
variants.deployment: Thirteen configurations from long-range harassment to close-range attack. Configuration A's Ultra AC/2 and LRM-10 harassment loadout is common in Falcon service. The ultralight weight means pod maintenance, while following standard procedures, has less physical workspace than heavier OmniMechs. Jade Falcon parts support is reliable. Brief pilots clearly — this machine lives by its speed and dies quickly when it doesn't.

variants.overview: Clan Goliath Scorpion designed the Fire Scorpion as their totem 'Mech in 2852, and the quad chassis at 65 tons reflects their approach to combining stability with firepower. The Space limitations inherent in quad construction concentrated the weapons into two primary systems rather than a broader array. The 3060 rework reflects combat experience feedback.
variants.capabilities: The quad chassis provides genuine stability advantages for the primary weapons systems and the two-main-weapon concentration creates impressive focused firepower. Quad maintenance overhead applies — more leg systems, longer inspection cycles, more complex battle damage assessment. Two variants represent meaningfully different weapons philosophies. Clan Goliath Scorpion construction quality is solid.
variants.deployment: Two variants with the 3060 replacement of the entire weapon suite representing a significant tactical philosophy shift. Know which variant you have before working from either manual. The quad maintenance overhead is the consistent advisory across both. Goliath Scorpion parts support through their logistics channels. The stability advantage of the quad chassis is most apparent in direct fire weapons roles — that's what both variants exploit.

variants.name: ALM-7D
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Fireball in 3053 as a direct response to Clan Elemental battle armour effectiveness during Operation Revival. Twenty tons on a 220-rated XL engine. Walk eleven, run sixteen. Five variants, all built around the same core principle: outrun everything and close on Elementals before they can react.
variants.capabilities: Walk eleven, run sixteen at twenty tons on the XL engine. The XL at twenty tons means any side torso hit is likely catastrophic. What keeps this machine alive is walk eleven — at that speed most opponents cannot reliably hit it and Elementals cannot keep up. The XXL variant pushes even further. Anti-Elemental doctrine drives all weapons choices. The ALM-7D carries a Streak SRM-2 and a machine gun. Walk eleven, run sixteen. Anti-Elemental doctrine drove the weapons choice — a machine gun handles Elementals in powered armour at close range and the Streak SRM-2 fires on lock against any target. Two weapons, maximum speed.
variants.deployment: The ALM-7D entered service with the Crucis Lancers specifically for Elemental engagement. Walk eleven closes to machine gun range before Elementals can respond effectively. The Streak SRM-2 handles anything that requires missile fire. The XXL engine specialist maintenance requirement means standard XL technicians need retraining before their first service cycle.

variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Fireball in 3053 as a direct response to Clan Elemental battle armour effectiveness during Operation Revival. Twenty tons on a 220-rated XL engine. Anti-Elemental doctrine drives all weapons choices. The ALM-8D carries two medium lasers and a machine gun. Walk eleven, run sixteen. The medium lasers provide better anti-armour capability than the 7D's Streak SRM-2 against conventional opponents. The machine gun handles Elementals and infantry.
variants.deployment: The 8D broadens the Fireball's anti-armour capability over the base 7D. Two medium lasers deal with conventional 'Mechs and vehicles more effectively than the Streak SRM-2. The machine gun retains the anti-Elemental mission. Walk eleven remains the primary survival mechanism.

variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Fireball in 3053 as a direct response to Clan Elemental battle armour effectiveness during Operation Revival. Twenty tons on a 220-rated XL engine. variants.name: FFL-3A

Not the fastest 30-tonner and not the most heavily armed, but solid and reliable — the qualities that keep designs in production for decades.
variants.capabilities: Too slow to serve as a dedicated scout against modern designs but compensating with better durability and firepower than lighter contemporaries. The original 2679 production model is the most capable single configuration in the family.
variants.deployment: Twelve variants from the 2679 Star League original through decades of adaptations. The XL-equipped original is the reference for maximum capability. Later non-XL variants are more supportable with commonly available parts. The twelve-variant family means extensive documentation exists for the chassis family even if specific variant documentation varies. Parts availability is generally good given the production history.

variants.name: FS9-A
variants.overview: Argile Technologies of Skye built the Firestarter in 2550 as a specialized incendiary platform, and the FS9-H that defined the design's reputation emerged as the iconic variant. Twenty-eight variants over production history reflects a chassis that found enormous tactical utility beyond the original incendiary mission. The company-and-regimental-level deployment doctrine reflects the specialized role.
variants.capabilities: The flamer and incendiary systems are the chassis identity and they require specific maintenance knowledge — thermal management, fuel systems for conventional flamers, the specific hazards of storing and handling incendiary materials. The jump capability on most variants is tactically important and the jump jet systems need regular inspection. The fire suppression in the cockpit is not optional maintenance — inspect it every cycle.
variants.deployment: Twenty-eight variants spanning the incendiary specialist through conventional light configurations. The FS9-H is the iconic reference but the family now covers roles far beyond incendiary warfare. Whatever variant you're maintaining, the fire suppression cockpit systems are the non-negotiable maintenance priority — pilots fighting in flamer-equipped machines need functioning fire suppression. Argile and successor manufacturer parts support is widespread.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Jade Falcon developed the Flamberge in 3077 from a repurposed experimental testbed, and the JF 7 Light Endo Steel frame is the unusual construction choice that defines its maintenance profile. At 70 tons with a 280-rated XL the performance is deliberately moderate — durability and firepower over speed.
variants.capabilities: The Light Endo Steel construction is less common than standard endo steel and requires specific repair knowledge — the structural properties and repair procedures differ from standard endo in ways that matter during battle damage assessment and repair. The XL concern applies as always. Seven configurations give the Jade Falcons tactical flexibility. The Falcon construction quality is consistently high.
variants.deployment: Seven configurations with Configuration A's precision ER PPC and large pulse laser combination being a common choice. The Light Endo Steel maintenance advisory is the consistent structural note — confirm your techs have specific training on this material before structural work. The XL advisory applies throughout. Jade Falcon parts support is reliable within their logistics network.
