variants.name: FLS-P2
variants.overview: Omnitech Industries built the Flashfire in 3054 for the Solaris VII arena circuit. Thirty tons, walk six, run nine on the 180-rated XL engine. Three variants. The flamer and close-range weapons focus makes this a machine designed for the spectacle of arena combat rather than conventional battlefield service.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at thirty tons on the XL engine. Arena-optimised construction. The close-range weapons focus limits effectiveness beyond close engagement distances. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The endo steel frame is well-made for the construction standards the arena environment requires. The FLS-P2 carries two medium pulse lasers, four flamers, and two SRM-6 launchers. Walk six, run nine. The four flamers handle infantry and area denial in arena settings. The pulse lasers and SRM-6s cover armoured opponents. All close-range weapons.
variants.deployment: The FLS-P2 established the Flashfire's arena reputation in 3054. The flamer and SRM-6 combination at close range is the spectacle that arena audiences appreciated. The design has almost no effective capability at ranges beyond close. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: FLS-P4
variants.overview: Omnitech Industries built the Flashfire in 3054 for the Solaris VII arena circuit. Thirty tons, walk six, run nine on the 180-rated XL engine. Three variants. The FLS-P4 carries two medium pulse lasers, four flamers, and one SRM-6, with six jump jets. Walk six, run nine, jump six. One SRM-6 instead of two, and jump capability added. Jump six opens approach angles for the close-range weapons delivery.
variants.deployment: The FLS-P4 adds jump six to the arena concept. The jump capability delivers the flamer and SRM-6 combination from unexpected angles in the enclosed arena environments. One SRM-6 is the weapons reduction for the jump jets. Still entirely close-range focused. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: FLS-P5
variants.overview: Omnitech Industries built the Flashfire in 3054 for the Solaris VII arena circuit. Thirty tons, walk six, run nine on the 180-rated XL engine. Three variants. Built for close-range spectacle, not battlefield service.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at thirty tons on the XL engine. Arena-optimised construction with endo steel. Close-range weapons only — limited effectiveness beyond engagement distances measured in hexes. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The FLS-P5 carries two fluid guns, four ER small lasers, and an SRM-6, with jump four. Walk six, run nine, jump four. The fluid guns spray an ignitable or adhesive substance. The ER small lasers and SRM-6 handle armoured targets. The fluid guns are the arena novelty element.
variants.deployment: The FLS-P5 adds fluid guns and jump capability to the Flashfire concept. The fluid guns create environmental effects suited to arena spectacle. Jump four adds theatrical approach angles. The ER small lasers and SRM-6 handle actual combat. Still an arena machine with almost no effective capability at range.

variants.name: FLS-8K
variants.overview: The Flashman FLS-8K entered SLDF production in 2701 as a sustained-energy-combat heavy designed to operate without logistical support, and the three Selitex Radonic large lasers on the original are the design identity. All-energy loadout means no ammunition concerns but requires heat discipline. Seven variants over the production run.
variants.capabilities: Three large lasers on a 75-ton heavy chassis generate real heat and pilot discipline is essential — undisciplined use of the full weapons array will shut this machine down. The design was explicitly built for independent operations without supply lines, which the all-energy loadout enables. Star League construction quality on the original variants is excellent. The later variants add additional energy weapons that only intensify the heat management requirement.
variants.deployment: Seven variants from the 2701 Star League original through later configurations. The original FLS-8K is the reference. All subsequent variants maintain or intensify the all-energy philosophy. The heat management advisory applies to every configuration in the family — brief pilots thoroughly before their first deployment in a Flashman. Star League parts availability varies; IS-production equivalent components are more common than original-spec hardware.

variants.deployment: Seven variants from the 2701 Star League original through later configurations. The original FLS-8K is the reference. All subsequent variants maintain or intensify the all-energy philosophy. The heat management advisory applies to every configuration in the family — brief pilots thoroughly before their first deployment in a Flashman. Star League parts availability varies; IS-production equivalent components are more common than original-spec hardware.

variants.name: FLE-4
variants.overview: Toddlette Industries designed the Flea — originally called the Trooper — for the Free Worlds League and it's been in continuous production since 2501 under various manufacturers. The Earthwerk Trooper II endo steel chassis on the modern variants is solid construction and the design has evolved considerably from the original light machine. Nine variants cover the full production history.
variants.capabilities: The post-Helm Memory Core FLE-17 is the modern standard and significantly more capable than the original configurations. The endo steel structure on modern variants requires trained techs for structural repairs — the original primitive construction is a different case entirely. The small size of the chassis means tight access for maintenance on some internal components; patience helps more than forcing it.
variants.deployment: Nine variants from the 2501 original through modern upgraded configurations. The original primitive variant is historically interesting and requires specific knowledge for maintenance — it is not maintained from the modern manual. The FLE-17 post-Helm standard is the common operational case. Parts availability is generally good given the long production history and multiple manufacturers.

variants.name: CS-1
variants.overview: Clan Sea Fox built their first original BattleMech design in 2824 during the early Golden Century, and the result reflects the transitional period — mixed Star League and early Clan technology in a 50-ton chassis. Working on a Fox means working with some of the oldest Clan-origin design work in existence.
variants.capabilities: The Vlar 300 XL gives 97 kph at 50 tons — good performance for the era and still respectable by modern standards. The mixed-technology construction creates maintenance complexity: Star League components with early Clan modifications don't always share documentation standards. The Golden Century construction quality is generally solid but pre-dates some modern Clan manufacturing refinements.
variants.deployment: Single configuration, which simplifies logistics considerably. The mixed-technology maintenance requirement is the primary challenge — ensure your techs understand both the IS components and the Clan modifications before working on this machine. Sea Fox parts support through their trade network channels is reliable but specialized components may require direct contact with Sea Fox suppliers.

variants.name: RJN-301-F
variants.overview: The Fujin represents the DCMS rebranding and modernization of the Raijin lineage after the seizure of Independence Weaponry's Quentin facilities. Using the Tessen TSN Light endo steel frame and retaining the Vlar 300 XL, it's a known quantity structurally while the weapons reflect Combine adaptation priorities.
variants.capabilities: The Tessen Light endo steel frame is the unusual structural element requiring specific repair knowledge — Light endo steel has different properties than standard endo that matter during structural repair work. The Vlar 300 XL and Rawlings jump jets carry over from the Raijin lineage providing familiar performance characteristics. Single variant with complete DCMS rework of the weapons fit.
variants.deployment: Single configuration following the Quentin facility seizure. The Light endo steel structure advisory is the consistent technical note — confirm tech qualification before structural work. The DCMS weapons rework means the Fujin and Raijin/Tessen share structural maintenance procedures but differ in weapons systems maintenance. Luthien Armor Works support through Combine channels is reliable.

variants.name: GLH-1D
variants.overview: Mitchell Vehicles designed the Galahad as a replacement for the Rifleman in Terran Hegemony service, and the dual M-7 Gauss rifles in fully articulated arms are the definitive feature. First unveiled as a 50-ton medium with Star League V endo steel, the production model evolved into the 60-ton heavy that defined the design. Seven variants cover the full production history.
variants.capabilities: The dual M-7 Gauss rifles are excellent direct-fire ballistic weapons and the articulated arm mounts give them tracking capability that fixed-torso weapons lack. The dual capacitor maintenance is the primary technical focus — synchronized inspection schedules for two Gauss systems, and the cascade failure risk from deferred maintenance. The original 50-ton medium versus the 60-ton production heavy are significantly different maintenance cases.
variants.deployment: Seven variants from the original 50-ton medium prototype through the 60-ton production heavy and subsequent developments. Know which weight class and variant you have before applying a manual. The dual Gauss capacitor advisory applies to all Gauss-equipped configurations. Mitchell Vehicles parts support through Hegemony successor supply channels varies considerably by operational area.

variants.name: GLT-7-0
variants.overview: The Gallant emerged from the final stages of the Jihad when the Coalition captured Skobel MechWorks' Moscow facility, inheriting a design conceived as a cavalry platform for broken terrain. The jump capability optimization over straight-line speed is the defining characteristic and the whole tactical concept depends on it.
variants.capabilities: Exceptional jump mobility in broken terrain rather than straight-line speed is the explicit design trade-off and pilots who understand that fight it well. The Skobel Moscow construction quality inherited from the Word of Blake facility is solid. Three variants cover different weapons emphases on the same jump-capable base. The post-capture documentation situation means some original design details required reconstruction from examination.
variants.deployment: Three variants with the base production model following Coalition capture being the most commonly encountered. The jump jet systems are the priority maintenance item — this machine's tactical value depends entirely on that mobility. Regular and thorough jump jet inspection is more important here than on designs where jumping is secondary capability. Post-Jihad parts sourcing through former Blakist channels is variable.

variants.name: GAL-1GLS
variants.overview: Blackwell Heavy Industries built the Gallowglas in 3054 on Outreach specifically for Wolf's Dragoons, and the GLKWL-52gls endo steel chassis with all-energy weapons reflects Blackwell's design philosophy and the Dragoons' operational requirements. The Sunglow large lasers and ER PPC combination is the weapons identity.
variants.capabilities: All-energy loadout means no ammunition concerns in extended operations, which suits the mercenary operational context that drove the design. The Tiegart Magnum ER PPC is a quality weapon and the Sunglow lasers are reliable. Heat management across the full array requires pilot discipline. Seven variants show ongoing development. Blackwell construction quality is excellent — they were building for the Dragoons and those standards show.
variants.deployment: Seven variants from the original 3054 all-energy design through subsequent configurations. The base GAL-1GLS is the reference. Heat management advisory applies across all high-energy configurations. Blackwell parts support through Outreach channels was excellent pre-Jihad; post-Jihad availability requires verification of current supply chain status. The all-energy philosophy makes field maintenance simpler when supply chains are disrupted.

variants.name: GBT-1G
variants.overview: Adam Tech Industries built the Gambit in 3136 on Abadan as a twenty-five ton light emphasising maintainability and wide component availability over peak performance. Walk seven, run ten on the 175-rated light engine. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at twenty-five tons on the light engine. Light engine — side torso survivability. The maintainability emphasis is genuine — Adam Tech designed this for operators without deep supply chains. The light PPC pair is the consistent weapons identity across both variants. The GBT-1G carries two Fusigon Shorttooth light PPCs and an MML-3. Walk seven, run ten. The light PPCs provide consistent short-to-medium range energy fire. The MML-3 adds modest SRM or LRM missile flexibility. Light engine — side torso survivability.
variants.deployment: The GBT-1G is the standard production model. The light PPCs are accurate and reliable. The MML-3 adds missile flexibility at modest scale. The design is straightforward to maintain using widely available parts, which is the point. Operators without deep supply chains can keep this running.

variants.name: GBT-1L
variants.overview: Adam Tech Industries built the Gambit in 3136 on Abadan as a twenty-five ton light emphasising maintainability and wide component availability over peak performance. Walk seven, run ten on the 175-rated light engine. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at twenty-five tons on the light engine. Light engine — side torso survivability. The maintainability emphasis is genuine — Adam Tech designed this for operators without deep supply chains. The light PPC pair is the consistent weapons identity across both variants. The GBT-1L replaces the MML-3 with a TAG system, keeping the two Fusigon Shorttooth light PPCs. Walk seven, run ten. The TAG designates for guided munitions. No missile capability, but the designation role adds force multiplier value in combined-arms operations.
variants.deployment: The GBT-1L trades the GBT-1G's missile flexibility for designation capability. The TAG combined with light PPC direct fire makes it useful as a forward observer alongside its standard combat role. Light engine survivability preserved. The design's maintainability advantage applies equally to this variant.

variants.name: GRM-01A
variants.overview: The Garm was introduced in 3058 as a light fire support platform, and the Johnston Biped L-25-a2 endo steel chassis with Omni 175 engine gives it 86 kph at 25 tons — reasonable speed for a dedicated fire support light. The design trades the extreme speed of pure scouts for a more balanced fire support capability.
variants.capabilities: 86 kph is slower than most lights but the weapons payload for the weight class is the trade-off that justifies it. The Mydron LB 5-X autocannon requires attention to the variable munitions feed system — switching between standard and cluster ammunition mid-engagement requires a reliable mechanism that needs regular cleaning. The LRM-10 is straightforward. Four variants cover different fire support approaches.
variants.deployment: Four variants on the same base chassis. The original configuration's balanced direct-and-indirect fire capability is the most versatile. The LB 5-X ammunition selection mechanism is the consistent maintenance note — keep it clean and test the feed switch regularly. For a unit needing fire support at light weight, the Garm delivers consistent capability without exotic maintenance requirements.

variants.name: GTL-1O
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Gauntlet for the Lyran Alliance as a fifty-five ton OmniMech in 3106, choosing a light engine over XL as a deliberate survivability decision. Walk five, run seven. Four configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty-five tons on the 275-rated light engine. Light engine — side torso survivability that XL designs sacrifice. The tradeoff is internal volume reduction. Lyran doctrine values the damage resilience. IS components throughout. The primary configuration carries a heavy PPC and a Thunderbolt-10. Walk five, run seven. The heavy PPC hits hard at medium range. The Thunderbolt-10 delivers accurate guided missile fire. Light engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The Primary is the Lyran open terrain baseline — heavy PPC for longer engagement ranges, Thunderbolt-10 for accurate missile fire. The light engine damage resilience suits the Lyran preference for machines that stay functional under fire. Thunderbolt ammunition supply logistics are distinct from standard LRM chains.

variants.name: GTL-1OA
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Gauntlet for the Lyran Alliance as a fifty-five ton OmniMech in 3106, choosing a light engine over XL as a deliberate survivability decision. Walk five, run seven. Four configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty-five tons on the 275-rated light engine. Light engine — side torso survivability that XL designs sacrifice. The tradeoff is internal volume reduction. Lyran doctrine values the damage resilience. IS components throughout. Configuration A carries two light PPCs and two MML-7 launchers. Walk five, run seven. The light PPCs provide accurate short-to-medium range energy fire. The MML-7s cover both SRM and LRM ranges. Light engine survivability.
variants.deployment: Configuration A provides more missile flexibility and lighter weapons than the Primary. The MML-7 mode switching covers both fire support and close-range missile engagement. The light PPCs handle direct energy fire. Light engine resilience is preserved.

variants.name: GTL-1OB
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Gauntlet for the Lyran Alliance as a fifty-five ton OmniMech in 3106, choosing a light engine over XL as a deliberate survivability decision. Walk five, run seven. Four configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty-five tons on the 275-rated light engine. Light engine — side torso survivability that XL designs sacrifice. The tradeoff is internal volume reduction. Lyran doctrine values the damage resilience. IS components throughout. Configuration B carries ten medium lasers and a medium pulse laser, with jump five. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Eleven energy weapons at close range on a fifty-five ton chassis. No ammunition dependency. Heat from ten-plus lasers simultaneously requires cycling discipline.
variants.deployment: Configuration B is the close-range energy saturation variant. Eleven lasers at close range with jump five delivery is the concept. No ammunition makes logistics simple. Heat management under sustained fire from ten-plus weapons is the pilot's primary discipline. Light engine survivability preserved.

variants.name: GTL-1OC
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Gauntlet for the Lyran Alliance as a fifty-five ton OmniMech in 3106, choosing a light engine over XL as a deliberate survivability decision. Walk five, run seven. Four configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty-five tons on the 275-rated light engine. Light engine — side torso survivability that XL designs sacrifice. The tradeoff is internal volume reduction. Lyran doctrine values the damage resilience. IS components throughout. Configuration C carries a TSEMP cannon, a snub-nose PPC, and a light AC/5. Walk five, run seven. The TSEMP disrupts enemy 'Mech systems. The snub-nose PPC covers short to medium range. The light AC/5 adds ballistic harassment. TSEMP requires specialist maintenance.
variants.deployment: Configuration C is the electronic disruption variant. The TSEMP disables opponents non-lethally for capture or restraint. The snub-nose PPC and light AC/5 handle conventional combat. TSEMP maintenance requires specialist procedures. Light engine survivability makes this platform more durable than the disable-then-withdraw doctrine might suggest it needs to be.

variants.name: GST-10
variants.overview: The Ghost emerged from the electronic warfare revolution that Clan technology forced on Inner Sphere designers, building on stealth systems pioneered in the Mongoose II. The Starshield stealth armor is the whole point and everything else in the design supports that capability. If the stealth systems aren't in spec, you don't have a Ghost — you have a mediocre medium.
variants.capabilities: Ten and a half tons of stealth armor requires ongoing calibration attention that conventional armor doesn't need. The Guardian ECM and Beagle active probe add electronic warfare capability that multiplies the stealth value but requires specialist maintenance personnel. Five variants maintain the stealth platform identity across different weapons configurations. The stealth system failure mode is gradual rather than sudden — regular calibration catches drift before it becomes tactical degradation.
variants.deployment: Five variants, all built on the stealth platform. The full electronic warfare base variant is the most capable and the most maintenance-intensive. The stealth calibration advisory is universal — keep the maintenance current and treat armor integrity as a stealth performance issue. Assign personnel with electronic warfare system training specifically; general techs cannot maintain the Ghost's defining systems adequately.

variants.name: GLD-1R
variants.overview: The Gladiator holds the distinction of being the first BattleMech designed and built entirely within the Draconis Combine, developed in secrecy at New Samarkand. Twenty-five variants over the production history reflect a chassis that evolved from primitive origins into a competitive medium design. The primitive original shares almost nothing with modern production variants.
variants.capabilities: The GLD-4R is the definitive production standard and the reference for modern maintenance. The MW240 chassis and CoreTek 275 engine are solid DCMS construction. The primitive original variants are historical artifacts requiring entirely different maintenance approaches — confirm which variant you have before applying any manual. The production variants are well-documented after this many years in DCMS service.
variants.deployment: Twenty-five variants from the primitive original through modern configurations. The primitive GLD-1R is the most challenging to support and requires specific knowledge of primitive construction techniques. The 4R and subsequent variants are the operational standard. LAW and DCMS parts support is reliable through Combine logistics for production-era variants. The long production history means most techs have encountered a Gladiator before their first assignment.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Burrock built the Executioner-B, called the Gladiator-B in IS records, during the Golden Century as a ninety-five ton assault OmniMech on a 285-rated Clan XL. Walk three, run four, jump two. Forty-seven tons of pod space is the defining feature. Four configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump two at ninety-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk three is slow even by assault standards. The forty-seven tons of pod space is the remarkable feature — most ninety-five ton OmniMechs cannot field this variety of configurations. Clan construction quality throughout. Configuration A carries two Ultra AC/10s, two LB 10-X ACs, and two ER small lasers. Walk three, run four, jump two. Four autocannons on a ninety-five ton chassis. The UAC/10s in double-tap and LB 10-X cluster and slug options together create a heavy combined ballistic fire output.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is the Annihilator-inspired quad autocannon approach. Four autocannons firing simultaneously at close range creates output few opponents at any weight class can absorb. The ER small lasers handle point-blank threats. Walk three means this configuration commits to a position and holds it.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: Clan Burrock built the Executioner-B, called the Gladiator-B in IS records, during the Golden Century as a ninety-five ton assault OmniMech on a 285-rated Clan XL. Walk three, run four, jump two. Forty-seven tons of pod space is the defining feature. Four configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump two at ninety-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk three is slow even by assault standards. The forty-seven tons of pod space is the remarkable feature — most ninety-five ton OmniMechs cannot field this variety of configurations. Clan construction quality throughout. Configuration B carries two Gauss rifles, two ER large lasers, and four medium pulse lasers. Walk three, run four, jump two. The Gauss rifles provide accurate long-range fire. The ER large lasers extend direct fire reach. The pulse lasers handle close engagement accurately.
variants.deployment: Configuration B is the long-range precision fire platform. Two Gauss rifles simultaneously at range creates consistent accurate ballistic pressure. The ER large lasers add energy fire at the same range band. The pulse lasers close the engagement. Gauss ammunition management across two rifles is the operational task.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: Clan Burrock built the Executioner-B, called the Gladiator-B in IS records, during the Golden Century as a ninety-five ton assault OmniMech on a 285-rated Clan XL. Walk three, run four, jump two. Forty-seven tons of pod space is the defining feature. Four configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump two at ninety-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk three is slow even by assault standards. The forty-seven tons of pod space is the remarkable feature — most ninety-five ton OmniMechs cannot field this variety of configurations. Clan construction quality throughout. Configuration C carries four ER PPCs, two Ultra AC/5s, and two SRM-2s. Walk three, run four, jump two. Four ER PPCs on a ninety-five ton chassis is an enormous long-range energy output. The UAC/5s add sustained ballistic fire. The SRM-2s handle close threats.
variants.deployment: Configuration C is the maximum long-range energy fire platform. Four ER PPCs simultaneously generates severe heat that requires disciplined cycling. The UAC/5s provide sustained ballistic fire when heat forces a pause on the PPCs. The SRM-2s handle anything that closes. Strict fire discipline required.

variants.name: Prime
variants.overview: Clan Burrock built the Executioner-B, called the Gladiator-B in IS records, during the Golden Century as a ninety-five ton assault OmniMech on a 285-rated Clan XL. Walk three, run four, jump two. Forty-seven tons of pod space is the defining feature. Four configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump two at ninety-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk three is slow even by assault standards. The forty-seven tons of pod space is the remarkable feature — most ninety-five ton OmniMechs cannot field this variety of configurations. Clan construction quality throughout. The Prime carries an Ultra AC/20, two large pulse lasers, an ER PPC, and two Ultra AC/2s. Walk three, run four, jump two. The Ultra AC/20 in double-tap at close range is the centrepiece. The ER PPC handles long approach fire. The large pulse lasers cover medium range. The UAC/2s add long-range harassment.
variants.deployment: The Prime is the combined engagement range platform. The ER PPC fires during the approach, the large pulse lasers engage at medium range, and the UAC/20 closes the engagement at close range. The UAC/2s maintain harassment fire at distance. Ammunition management across AC/20 and AC/2 feeds requires separate tracking.

variants.name: GOL-1H
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation introduced the Goliath in 2652 as a larger successor to their earlier quad designs, and at 80 tons it became the definitive heavy assault quad of the Star League era. The PPC and dual LRM combination gives it fire support capability that complements the quad chassis stability. Fifteen variants over the production run show extensive adaptation of the base concept.
variants.capabilities: The steady fire support role suits the quad chassis well — the stability advantages for sustained accurate fire are genuine. 64 kph keeps it relevant in heavy formations. The quad maintenance overhead is real and consistent: more leg systems to inspect, more complex battle damage assessment, longer repair cycles than comparable bipeds. The weapons systems themselves are uncomplicated.
variants.deployment: Fifteen variants from the 2652 original through decades of development. The original production model is the historical baseline. Quad maintenance qualification is the consistent requirement across all variants — ensure your techs are certified on quad systems before assigning them to Goliath work. Brigadier and successor manufacturer parts support through various supply chains.

variants.overview: The Vapor Eagle — Inner Sphere reporting name Goshawk — appeared in Clan service around the twenty-eighth century, and the 330-rated XL with six jump jets at 55 tons creates a medium that uses three-dimensional space unusually well. Six variants show Clan exploitation of the jump-and-speed combination across different tactical roles.
variants.capabilities: The combination of 97 kph ground speed and 150 meters of jump capability creates a medium that's difficult to pin down. The XL vulnerability concern applies — a fast mobile medium that loses that mobility due to side torso damage is suddenly in a difficult position. The jump jet systems require regular inspection given the frequency of use this chassis is designed for. Clan construction quality throughout.
variants.deployment: Six configurations with the Vapor Eagle 6 retaining the targeting computer while adjusting the weapons mix. The jump jet inspection priority is higher on this chassis than designs where jumping is occasional — frequent use accelerates wear. The XL advisory applies consistently. Clan parts support varies by which faction is currently operating the design. The three-dimensional mobility is the machine's identity and the jump systems are what enable it.

variants.capabilities: The XL engine paired with the Crusader-ES chassis creates a weapons-first assault that accepts mobility trade-offs deliberately. XL advisory applies consistently — at 80 tons a side torso breach is a serious event. Post-Jihad parts sourcing through former Blakist channels is variable; plan for alternative supply chain development for Blake-specific components.

variants.name: GRN-D-03
variants.overview: The Grand Crusader II is a comprehensive redesign that addressed the two primary criticisms of the original: limited long-range capability and XL vulnerability. The Pitban 320 Light Fusion engine replacing the XL is the key structural change, and the triple-strength myomer and jump jets change the mobility profile significantly.
variants.capabilities: The light fusion engine resolves the XL vulnerability that made the original a tactical liability in some engagements — this is a meaningful improvement. Triple-strength myomer creates physical combat capability that requires specific maintenance attention: the myomer system itself needs regular inspection and the physical combat components have wear patterns different from conventional weapons. The jump jets add three-dimensional mobility.
variants.deployment: Two variants on the improved platform. The light engine change is the maintenance-relevant structural difference from the original — different damage vulnerability profile, different repair procedures for engine-adjacent components. The myomer maintenance advisory applies — inspect regularly and replace on schedule. The jump capability adds jet inspection requirements. A genuinely improved design over the original.

variants.name: DRG-1G
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works modernized the Dragon chassis using recovered Star League technology, and the Grand Dragon emerged from those field modifications during the late Third Succession War before reaching factory production. The field-modification origin of the original configuration is worth knowing — the first examples were improvised solutions that the factory subsequently formalized.
variants.capabilities: The Star League technology integration improves on the Dragon's core strengths while maintaining the design identity. Twelve variants over the production run show extensive exploitation of the improved platform. LAW construction quality is consistent and the documentation is thorough after this many years in DCMS service. The field-modification heritage of the original means some early hull documentation required reconstruction from examination.
variants.deployment: Twelve variants from the field-modified original through factory production configurations. The original field-modified hulls may have documentation variations — verify against physical examination on early production. Factory variants are the standard operational case. LAW parts support through Combine channels is reliable and extensive. The Dragon family familiarity most DCMS techs have transfers well to the Grand Dragon.

variants.name: T-IT-N10M
variants.overview: Earthwerks built the Grand Titan in 3054 from Vining Engineering and Salvage Team's design, and the LTV 400 XL in a 100-ton chassis giving 64 kph is the performance foundation for this assault. The Corean Model 101BLP Endo Steel chassis is solid construction and the design reflects serious engineering effort.
variants.capabilities: The LTV 400 XL in a 100-ton chassis is a substantial engine delivering genuine speed for the weight class. At 100 tons the XL vulnerability concern is as serious as it gets — side torso damage on a 100-ton assault is a catastrophic event and pilots need that briefed clearly. The pulse laser and Artemis-guided missile combination on the base model is effective across ranges. Four variants cover different weapons emphases.
variants.deployment: Four variants from the original T-IT-N10M through subsequent configurations. The XL advisory at assault weight is the first and loudest briefing for any Grand Titan pilot. The Artemis calibration requirement applies to missile-equipped configurations — keep the fire control systems in spec. Earthwerks parts support through various channels is reliable.

variants.name: GHR-5H
variants.overview: The Grasshopper entered SLDF service in 2780 as a close-range heavy originally conceived as a stealth design, and the all-energy weapons philosophy and jump capability define the design identity. The VOX 280 engine gives real speed for a heavy and the jump jets enable the terrain exploitation that the original stealth concept required. Eleven variants show sustained utility.
variants.capabilities: The all-energy weapons mean no ammunition concerns in extended operations, which suited the original independent operations concept. Heat management is the pilot's constant consideration — the weapons array can sustain significant heat and discipline is required. The jump jets need regular inspection given the tactical emphasis on three-dimensional mobility this chassis is built for. Star League construction quality on original variants.
variants.deployment: Eleven variants from the 2780 original through adaptations. The original production model with full SLDF technology is the reference and the most demanding to support with modern parts. Later variants substitute available components. Heat management advisory and jump jet inspection priority apply across the full family. The all-energy philosophy is the consistent operational advantage — no supply chain dependency for ammunition.

variants.name: GDR-1C
variants.overview: Odin Manufacturing introduced the Gravedigger in 3102 as their first post-war product, designed explicitly for quick manufacture and ease of maintenance. The Hunchback comparison in design philosophy is apt — protection and firepower over speed, built for practicality. The mixed IS-Clan technology reflects what was available on Orestes in the post-Jihad period.
variants.capabilities: The Kallon Type VII endo steel chassis and conservative design approach make this one of the more straightforward 50-ton heavies to maintain. The mixed IS-Clan technology creates the expected cross-documentation challenge, but the components were chosen for availability rather than exoticism. Two variants with different weapons emphasis cover different tactical requirements.
variants.deployment: Two variants, both built on the maintainability-first philosophy. The original 3102 variant uses IS components throughout which is the simpler case. The mixed-technology variant adds Clan components that require Clan-spec tooling for those specific systems. Odin Manufacturing support through Free Rasalhague and successor state channels. The Hunchback-inspired philosophy means any tech who knows the Hunchback will adapt quickly.

variants.name: GTR-1
variants.overview: Vining Engineering and Salvage Team built the Great Turtle on Solaris VII in 3067 as a defensive assault quad, and the Corean Model 202BLP Endo Steel quad chassis with fortress-mentality armor is as defensive a design as I've worked on. Borrowed from the Grand Titan chassis family, the structural commonality is a maintenance advantage.
variants.capabilities: The defensive philosophy permeates every design choice — maximum armor, quad stability, weapons chosen for sustained defensive fire rather than aggressive offense. The Grand Titan chassis commonality means structural maintenance procedures transfer between the designs. Quad maintenance overhead applies as always. Two variants cover different weapons approaches to the same defensive concept.
variants.deployment: Two variants on the Grand Titan-derived chassis. The original VEST design pairs maximum passive protection with precision energy weapons for sustained defensive engagement. The chassis commonality with the Grand Titan is the practical maintenance advantage — if you have Grand Titan experience, the structural work transfers. Quad maintenance qualification is required. Solaris origins mean VEST parts support is through arena-market channels.

variants.name: (Aemelia)
variants.overview: The Great Wyrm holds the distinction of being among the first unique BattleMech designs developed by the Clans after their exodus, and working on one means working with some of the oldest Clan-original engineering in existence. The Clan Mongoose origin adds historical complexity given that Clan's fate.
variants.capabilities: The weapons suite provides engagement flexibility across ranges while emphasizing the standoff approach that the original Clan Mongoose doctrine favored. The design shows the transitional period between Star League equipment and emerging Clan manufacturing refinements. Two variants include a recovered Smoke Jaguar depot modification, which means that specific hull has a documentation history requiring field reconstruction.
variants.deployment: Two variants including the recovered Jaguar modification. The Jaguar-modified variant was created from necessity rather than design intent — build your own technical record from physical examination rather than trusting inherited documentation. The original Clan Mongoose production variant is the more standard maintenance case. Historical rarity means parts sourcing requires creativity for non-standard components.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: First identified at Tukayyid in 3052, the Mongrel — Inner Sphere designation Grendel — appeared among Clan Diamond Shark forces and surprised analysts with its speed. The Consolidated 315 XL achieving nearly 119 kph at 45 tons is genuinely fast for a medium OmniMech. Thirteen configurations have been developed over its service life.
variants.capabilities: 119 kph for a medium OmniMech is exceptional and the XL enabling that speed brings the standard vulnerability concern — at this speed a side torso breach is a serious tactical problem. Thirteen configurations means substantial pod inventory requirements. Diamond Shark construction quality is consistently high. The LRM-15 fire support Configuration A is one of the more common.
variants.deployment: Thirteen configurations from fire support to direct combat to electronic warfare. The XL advisory applies universally — brief every Grendel pilot on side torso protection. Pod maintenance across 13 configurations requires robust inventory management. Diamond Shark parts support through their trade network is generally reliable. The speed is the tactical identity; configurations that waste that advantage are suboptimal choices for this chassis.

variants.name: GRF-1A
variants.overview: The Griffin has been in service for over six centuries and the twenty-four variants accumulated over that time tell the story of a design that kept proving useful in every era. The PPC and LRM combination at 55 tons with jump capability is a formula that worked in 2465 and still works now. Most techs know this chassis before their first assignment.
variants.capabilities: The standard PPC and LRM-10 combination is straightforward and proven — both systems are well-documented with parts available everywhere. The jump capability adds tactical flexibility that the long service history has demonstrated is genuinely valuable. Heat management across the PPC and LRM combination requires basic pilot discipline. The chassis is simple enough that experienced techs work from memory on most procedures.
variants.deployment: Twenty-four variants over six centuries. The 2465 original is a historical artifact. The GRF-1N production standard is the reference. The original was actually a 60-ton design before weight reduction — know the specific variant before working from a manual. Six centuries of production means parts are available essentially everywhere and documentation is comprehensive across the family.

variants.overview: Clan Nova Cat developed the Griffin IIC in 2852 in response to Khan Philip Drummond's unusual doctrinal challenge, and the design reflects that specific origin. At 40 tons with Clan technology throughout, the NCIS Endo Steel Type M chassis and Clan construction quality deliver meaningfully more capability than the IS original at comparable weight.
variants.capabilities: The Clan construction quality throughout enables impressive capability at 40 tons. The design evolution from the fire support LRM-5 quad configuration to the Streak SRM aggressive alternative represents a complete tactical philosophy shift between variants — know which one you have. Eight variants over the production run show Nova Cat exploiting the chassis across different roles.
variants.deployment: Eight variants covering the tactical range from long-range fire support to close assault. The LRM and Streak SRM variants are essentially different machines tactically despite the shared chassis. Clan Nova Cat and successor faction parts support. The Khan-directed origin means the design documentation reflects specific requirements rather than general procurement — thorough in some areas, specific in others.

variants.name: C-GRG-O Invictus
variants.overview: The Grigori is the lighter of the two heavy Celestial OmniMechs built for the Word of Blake's Manei Domini, named after fallen angels, and the GM 240 light fusion engine rather than XL reflects Blakist engineering priorities. Ten configurations and the Celestial-specific components create the familiar exotic maintenance challenge of the Celestial series.
variants.capabilities: The GM 240 light fusion engine changes the damage profile compared to XL-equipped heavies — different vulnerability considerations, different repair procedures for engine-adjacent components. The Celestial Series GG1 standard chassis requires Blakist-spec tooling for structural work. Ten OmniMech configurations multiply the parts inventory requirements. The exotic Celestial components are the consistent maintenance challenge.
variants.deployment: Ten configurations with the Invictus missile-heavy loadout being notable for its layered fire approach. The Celestial-specific component sourcing challenge is universal across all configurations. Assign dedicated Celestial-qualified personnel rather than rotating general staff through these machines. The light fusion engine damage profile advantage is worth communicating to pilots — different survivability characteristics than comparable XL designs.

variants.name: GRM-R-PR29

The Blankenburg ER large laser and Holly LRM combination gives it genuine multi-range capability.
variants.capabilities: The balanced weapons array is the design strength — effective across multiple range brackets rather than specialized for one engagement distance. The Blankenburg ER large laser is quality hardware and well-documented. Five variants show ongoing refinement of the balanced approach. ComStar construction quality is consistently high. The crash program origin means documentation was more comprehensive than rushed designs sometimes achieve.
variants.deployment: Five variants from the 3052 original through developments. The base variant is the reference with the full balanced loadout. ComStar and successor organization parts support through HPG network-connected supply channels. The multi-range capability requires pilots who use the full weapons array rather than defaulting to a favorite system — brief accordingly.

variants.overview: Clan Ghost Bear developed the Grizzly in the late twenty-ninth century at their Alshain facility, and the design spent most of its early service as a garrison machine before the Combine-Ghost Bear War of 3063 demonstrated what it could actually do. The 280-rated RFUM fusion engine at 70 tons gives 64 kph — adequate rather than impressive.
variants.capabilities: The four Clan SRM launchers and supporting weapons give it genuine urban combat capability that the 3063 war brought to light. The Type 56-45C Modified Endo Steel chassis is the unusual construction feature — the modification means specific repair procedures that differ from standard endo steel. Two variants show the before-and-after of the combat experience rework.
variants.deployment: Two variants with the post-3063 rework reflecting direct urban combat lessons. The Modified Endo Steel structure advisory is the consistent technical note — verify your techs have the specific procedures for this variant of endo steel before structural work. Ghost Bear parts support through Dominion channels is reliable. The urban combat role the 3063 war revealed suits the chassis's firepower profile well.

variants.name: GLT-3N
variants.overview: Newhart Industries designed the Guillotine in 2499 as a heavy shock unit for the Terran Hegemony, and the VOX 280 engine giving 64 kph to a 70-ton heavy creates a machine that can keep pace with fast heavy formations. Nine variants over the production run maintained the shock assault identity across different technology eras.
variants.capabilities: The VOX 280 engine speed advantage for a heavy is genuine and defines the tactical doctrine around this chassis. The weapons fit supports the shock assault role with coverage across ranges. The original Star League construction quality on early variants is excellent. The endo steel chassis on Crucis-I variants requires trained tech qualification for structural repairs. CASE on ammunition variants is an important safety system to keep functional.
variants.deployment: Nine variants from the 2499 original through adaptations. The original Star League variant is the historical reference. Later variants with endo steel and upgraded weapons are the operational standard. The CASE systems on ammunition-carrying variants need regular inspection — this is a safety-critical system. Newhart and successor manufacturer parts support through various supply chains.

variants.overview: Clan Coyote engineers rebuilt the Guillotine with Clan technology during the Golden Century, retaining the armor, speed, and jump profile while substantially upgrading the weapons. The 3070 close-quarters rework shows ongoing adaptation of the platform to specific combat requirements.
variants.capabilities: The Clan technology upgrade retains the original's key performance characteristics while improving weapons efficiency throughout. The large pulse laser configuration is effective and well-maintained. The 3070 close-quarters rework with SRM-6 and ER medium laser replacement represents a complete close-range focus shift — different maintenance profile from the base configuration. Single original variant plus the Jihad-era rework.
variants.deployment: Two configurations with the Jihad-era close-quarters rework being the more recent. Know which configuration you have — the weapons systems and their maintenance requirements differ completely. Clan Coyote and successor parts support. The jump capability is maintained across both configurations and the jump jet inspection priority applies to both.

variants.name: GUN-1ERD
variants.overview: The Gunslinger emerged from a joint Draconis Combine and Federated Commonwealth project in 3053, driven by the Clan Invasion's demonstration of what dual heavy ballistic weapons could accomplish. Twin Poland Main Model A Gauss rifles on an 85-ton assault chassis — the concept is effective and the execution at Defiance Industries' Hesperus II facility delivers on it.
variants.capabilities: The twin Poland Main Gauss rifles are the whole point and they're excellent hardware. The dual capacitor maintenance is the primary technical focus — synchronized inspection schedules for both systems, the cascade failure risk from deferred maintenance, immediate replacement when capacitors reach wear thresholds. Five variants cover different secondary weapons configurations but the Gauss rifles are the constant.
variants.deployment: Five variants from the December 3053 original production through subsequent configurations. The dual Gauss capacitor advisory is the first and most important briefing for any tech assigned to a Gunslinger — this is not a system where you defer maintenance. Defiance Industries parts support through Lyran and Federated Suns channels is excellent. The joint-project origin means documentation quality is high.

variants.name: CH11-NG
variants.overview: Jalastar Aerospace introduced the Gunsmith in 3131 from their Panpour facility as a high-speed pursuit and raiding light. Twenty-five tons with a 250-rated XXL engine for walk ten, run fifteen. Two variants, one retaining the XXL, one switching to a standard XL.
variants.capabilities: Walk ten, run fifteen at twenty-five tons on the XXL engine. The XXL at this weight means side torso damage is catastrophic. Walk ten is the survival mechanism — at that speed most conventional opponents cannot reliably hit it. XXL maintenance requires specialist knowledge beyond standard XL expertise. The CH11-NG carries four medium X-pulse lasers. Walk ten, run fifteen. All-energy with no ammunition dependency. Four X-pulse lasers at close range with walk ten speed. The X-pulse accuracy suits high-speed engagement. XXL vulnerability at this weight means any side torso hit is catastrophic.
variants.deployment: The CH11-NG is the base raiding configuration. Walk ten delivers the X-pulse suite to close range faster than most opponents can respond. The X-pulse accuracy makes hits count. No ammunition dependency simplifies logistics for raiding operations. XXL maintenance specialist requirement applies.

variants.name: CH11-NGC 'Cinderella'
variants.overview: Jalastar Aerospace introduced the Gunsmith in 3131 from their Panpour facility as a high-speed pursuit and raiding light. Twenty-five tons with a 250-rated XXL engine for walk ten, run fifteen. Two variants, one retaining the XXL, one switching to a standard XL.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve on the 200-rated IS XL engine. The Cinderella carries four ER medium pulse lasers and a laser AMS. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk eight is slower than the base CH11-NG but the IS XL is more maintainable than the XXL. The laser AMS provides missile defence. ER medium pulse lasers extend range.
variants.deployment: The Cinderella trades the CH11-NG's walk ten and XXL specialist requirement for walk eight and a standard XL that more technicians can service. The ER medium pulse laser range extension over standard X-pulse lasers is the weapons improvement. The laser AMS adds missile defence. XL vulnerability applies.

variants.name: GUR-2G
variants.overview: Word of Blake designed the Gurkha on Terra in the early 3060s as a fast networked striker, and the Krupp 255 endo steel chassis with Magna 245 XL gives it nearly 119 kph at 35 tons. The C3 network integration is the design's tactical identity alongside the speed.
variants.capabilities: 119 kph for a 35-ton light is genuine speed and the XL concern applies — at this velocity a side torso breach creates a serious problem fast. The C3 equipment requires specialist calibration maintenance beyond standard weapons systems. Four variants cover different weapons configurations on the same fast networked platform. The Fusigon Longtooth ER PPC is quality hardware for a light 'Mech.
variants.deployment: Four variants, all built around the speed and C3 networking concept. The C3 calibration advisory is consistent across all C3-equipped configurations — assign personnel with specific network electronics training. The XL advisory applies universally. Post-Jihad Word of Blake parts sourcing is the logistics challenge for Blake-origin components. The C3 networking value depends entirely on having other C3-equipped units to network with.

variants.overview: Olivetti Weaponry introduced the Gyrfalcon in 3112 on Sudeten as part of Clan Jade Falcon's touman revitalization, and the 275-rated XL with MASC at 55 tons creates a medium that can achieve genuine assault-class sprint speed when needed. The MASC system is the defining and most maintenance-intensive feature.
variants.capabilities: The MASC system requires careful monitoring and regular calibration — pushed too hard too often it degrades faster than the maintenance schedule assumes. variants.deployment: Four variants with the ferro-fibrous replacement variant being the more commonly supportable configuration — reflective armor sourcing outside specialized channels is challenging. The MASC advisory applies to all MASC-equipped configurations — monitor closely and don't defer calibration cycles. Jade Falcon parts support is reliable. Brief pilots on MASC discipline; the capability is there for emergencies, not routine use.

variants.name: GTD-20C
variants.overview: Blackstone BattleMechs introduced the Götterdämmerung in 3138 on Inara for the Lyran Commonwealth, and the heavy ferro-fibrous armor layered over composite internal structure creates exceptional survivability for a 75-ton heavy. The Schachtebich Jägers' performance at the Nineteenth Battle of Hesperus II brought the Tiburon Khan's attention to the design.
variants.capabilities: The combination of heavy ferro-fibrous armor and composite internal structure creates survivability that goes beyond what the tonnage numbers suggest. Composite internal structure has specific repair requirements different from standard — confirm your techs have the specific procedures before structural work. Three variants with different weapons configurations on the same well-protected chassis.
variants.deployment: Three variants, with the base design's performance at Hesperus II driving the Sea Fox interest. The composite structure repair advisory is the consistent technical note — specific procedures apply. Heavy ferro-fibrous repair is more demanding than standard armor due to the material properties. Blackstone BattleMechs parts support through Lyran logistics channels. The survivability focus makes this a good choice for contested defensive positions.

variants.name: GN-2O

The plasma rifle maintenance advisory applies to configured variants — specialist training on this weapon type is needed. OmniMech pod maintenance at 20 tons has less physical workspace than heavier designs. Ceres Metals parts support through Capellan channels is reliable.

variants.name: HKO-1C
variants.overview: Clan Diamond Shark introduced the Ha Otoko in 3060 as a dedicated missile support heavy, and the quartet of missile launchers provides overlapping fire coverage at multiple ranges. The Inner Sphere adaptation for the DCMS came quickly as Jade Falcon merchants predicted — the design found a ready market outside the Clan that built it.
variants.capabilities: Four missile launchers on a 65-ton chassis creates serious sustained fire capability but the ammunition management is complex — four separate ammunition feeds mean more failure points and more supply chain logistics than a simpler design. The overlapping coverage at multiple ranges is the tactical advantage. Four variants cover Clan original and IS adaptation configurations.
variants.deployment: Four variants including the Jade Falcon merchant-facilitated DCMS adaptation. The multi-system ammunition management is the consistent operational challenge — establish robust resupply for all launcher types before deployment. The IS adaptation uses different components from the Clan original; know which variant you have before sourcing parts. Both Diamond Shark and DCMS parts channels exist depending on variant origin.

variants.name: HCA-3T
variants.overview: Silver Wyrm commissioned the Hachiwara for the Solaris VII arena circuit in 3064, and the supercharged Super Magna 350 XL with supercharger is the technical centerpiece of this arena design. The Mithril Wyrm Endo-2 chassis is purpose-built arena construction. The supercharger is what gives pilots their dramatic speed bursts that arena audiences expect.
variants.capabilities: The supercharger mechanism requires more maintenance attention than a standard engine configuration — the stress it places on engine components during activation accelerates wear in ways the base maintenance schedule doesn't fully account for. Track actual supercharger usage per hull and adjust inspection frequency accordingly. The endo-2 chassis is arena-optimized construction with different stress assumptions than field designs.
variants.deployment: Four variants from the 3064 original through arena-evolved configurations. The base HCA-3T established the design's arena reputation quickly. Supercharger inspection frequency should be increased based on actual usage patterns. For arena use the design is well-suited; for field deployment the arena-optimized construction assumptions and supercharger wear patterns need different maintenance planning. Silver Wyrm parts support through arena market channels.

variants.name: HMR-3M
variants.overview: Free Worlds Defense Industries built the Hammer in 3053 as a deliberate LRM fire support light, and the twin Coventry Five-Tube LRM-5 launchers with Artemis IV fire control are the design identity. At 30 tons this is a machine built around a single tactical concept executed consistently.
variants.capabilities: The Artemis IV systems on both launchers improve accuracy significantly but require regular calibration — the fire control improvement disappears when calibration drifts. The twin launcher configuration means two separate Artemis calibration requirements simultaneously. The medium laser backup is solid. Four variants develop different secondary weapons configurations while maintaining the Artemis LRM core.
variants.deployment: Four variants, all maintaining the Artemis LRM fire support concept. The dual Artemis calibration requirement is the consistent maintenance advisory — both systems need synchronized maintenance schedules to ensure consistent accuracy across the weapons pair. FWDI parts support through Free Worlds League channels is reliable. The design is single-mission focused; brief pilots that long-range fire support is the purpose, not direct engagement.

variants.name: HMH-3D
variants.overview: Achernar BattleMechs introduced the Hammerhands in 2475 as the Federated Suns' second exclusive BattleMech design, explicitly designed to correct the BattleAxe's overheating problems by replacing PPCs with autocannons. The solution worked — the twin Mydron autocannons run cooler than what they replaced. Six variants over the production run.
variants.capabilities: The heat problem the BattleAxe suffered is genuinely solved here — the autocannon configuration runs significantly cooler and pilots have more freedom of action than on PPC-heavy designs. The trade-off is ammunition management, which the BattleAxe didn't need. The Mydron autocannons are reliable and well-documented after this many years. Six variants show ongoing refinement of the basic autocannon heavy concept.
variants.deployment: Six variants from the 2475 original through modern configurations. The original production model is the historical reference. The ammunition management advisory is the consistent consideration for all autocannon-equipped variants. Achernar parts support through Federated Suns channels is reliable. The heat improvement over the BattleAxe is the design's enduring selling point — pilots who come from PPC-heavy designs appreciate the thermal headroom.

variants.name: HTM-26T
variants.overview: The Hatamoto-Chi emerged from the Draconis Combine's effort to reverse-engineer Clan technology captured after the Battle of Wolcott, and the crude-but-functional PPCs backed by torso-mounted SRM launchers define the design identity. The shared chassis across the Hatamoto family means structural experience transfers between all variants — a genuine maintenance advantage for DCMS units operating multiple Hatamoto configurations.
variants.capabilities: The PPC and SRM combination is effective and the Hatamoto family's shared endo steel chassis with Pitban 320 engine is well-documented DCMS hardware. Eight variants of the Chi alone, and the broader Hatamoto family adds more configurations on the same base chassis. The crude duplication of older technology means some component tolerances are wider than original specifications — not a problem in practice, but worth noting during precision work.
variants.deployment: Eight variants plus the broader Hatamoto family sharing the same chassis. The family commonality is the maintenance advantage — structural procedures, engine work, and chassis maintenance carry across all Hatamoto variants. LAW, Yori, and Maltex parts support through Combine channels covers the full family. Units operating multiple Hatamoto variants benefit significantly from the shared maintenance knowledge base.

variants.overview: The Hatamoto-Godai is a rare electronics-focused variant produced by Maltex Corporation on Unity, packing dual C3 systems into the standard Hatamoto chassis. The rarity in mainline Combine regiments reflects both the specialized role and the component complexity of the dual C3 integration.
variants.capabilities: Dual C3 suites in a 75-ton chassis is technically ambitious and the integration requires specific calibration expertise that general techs don't have. The standard Hatamoto chassis and engine are familiar maintenance territory; the C3 electronics are where specialist time goes. The weapons are reduced compared to other Hatamoto variants to accommodate the electronics payload.

variants.name: HTM-27V

variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at eighty tons on the standard 320-rated engine. Standard engine — side torso survivability. The Hatamoto chassis is a known quantity in Combine service. Parts support through established Combine channels is reliable. The HTM-27V carries two PPCs and two LRM-5 launchers. Walk four, run six. The PPCs provide the primary long-range direct fire. The LRM-5s add modest indirect fire. Standard engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The 27V is the original Kaze configuration. The PPC pair covers long-range engagement. The LRM-5s add minimal fire support capability alongside the primary weapons. Standard engine survivability. Combine supply chains support this variant reliably.

variants.name: HCT-3F
variants.overview: Defiance Industries introduced the Hatchetman in 3023 as the first completely new BattleMech design produced in the Inner Sphere in over a century, and the hatchet is still the design's defining feature. Fifteen variants over the production run show the urban combat concept finding sustained relevance. The hatchet mechanism is actually one of the simpler maintenance items on the chassis.
variants.capabilities: The hatchet mounting and actuators are mechanically straightforward — well-made physical weapon with predictable wear patterns. The challenge is that the urban assault role means the hatchet sees real use, which means real wear, which means regular inspection of the mounting brackets and actuator systems. The ranged weapons are adequate for the approach to hatchet range. Jump capability on most variants enables the terrain exploitation urban combat requires.

variants.name: HA1-O
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works introduced the Hauptmann in 3060 as the Lyran Alliance's first domestically designed OmniMech, and the Coventry HAI III chassis with Pitban 285 standard engine is a deliberate choice over XL — accepting the speed trade-off for the damage resilience that Lyran doctrine values. Nine configurations reflect extensive Lyran development of the design.
variants.capabilities: The standard fusion engine rather than XL is the design philosophy statement — slower than comparable XL assault OmniMechs but survivable when things go wrong in ways XL designs aren't. At 70 tons the standard engine trade-off is meaningful. Nine configurations give extensive tactical flexibility. Coventry Metal Works construction quality is consistent and reliable. The assault weight means comprehensive pod inventory management.
variants.deployment: Nine configurations with the Prime's paired ER large lasers and LB 20-X combination being the baseline. The standard engine damage resilience advantage is worth communicating clearly to pilots — different survivability characteristics from XL-equipped designs, in a positive direction. Coventry parts support through Lyran logistics is excellent. The first domestic Lyran OmniMech status means political support for the program has kept parts flowing reliably.

variants.name: HVC-P6
variants.overview: Adam Tech Industries built the Havoc on Abadan as a companion to their Gambit light, extending the product line to a faster 35-ton design. The Hermes 280 XL at 35 tons gives 129 kph and the all-energy weapons eliminate the ammunition supply concerns that the raiding role makes relevant.
variants.capabilities: 129 kph for a 35-ton light is fast and the XL concern at this speed is the standard advisory. The all-energy weapons make it supply-independent for ammunition, which suits raiding operations. Single production variant — the simplified logistics of a single configuration is a genuine advantage. The Adam Tech design philosophy of available components and maintenance accessibility carries through from the Gambit.
variants.deployment: Single configuration. The XL advisory is the primary briefing — at 129 kph a side torso breach creates a mobility crisis very quickly. The all-energy supply independence is the operational advantage for raiding. Adam Tech parts through Free Worlds League channels. The same maintainability philosophy that distinguishes the Gambit applies here — designed by a small manufacturer for operators without exotic support infrastructure.

variants.name: HWK-3F
variants.overview: Hope Industrial Works built the HawkWolf on Randis IV for the Brotherhood of Randis, and the primitive technology of the original reflects the Brotherhood's limited industrial capacity. The Advanced HWK chassis with Pitban 320 fusion engine is the production standard, but knowing which generation of hull you're working on is essential before opening any manual.
variants.capabilities: The Pitban 320 gives 64 kph at 80 tons — adequate for assault class. The primitive technology original uses components that predate modern standards and require specific primitive construction maintenance knowledge entirely different from modern procedures. The modern production variants with Advanced HWK chassis are more conventionally maintained. Two variants with a significant technology generation gap between them.
variants.deployment: Two variants with the original primitive-technology HWK-3F being the most historically unusual. The primitive construction advisory on early hulls is serious — do not attempt to maintain a primitive HawkWolf from the modern production manual. They are different machines. Hope Industrial Works parts support through Brotherhood of Randis channels. The religious organization origin means supply chain planning outside the Brotherhood's territory requires creativity.

variants.name: HOR-1B
variants.overview: The Hector entered service in 2471 as the Free Worlds League's second original BattleMech design, and the primitive components throughout define everything about maintaining this machine. The Pitban 340 Primitive engine is the dominant maintenance challenge. If you're assigned to maintain a Hector you're working with sixth-century primitive technology.
variants.capabilities: The primitive components throughout create a maintenance situation entirely different from modern designs. Modern parts are not compatible with primitive systems — you are working from primitive construction documentation with primitive replacement components or field-fabricated equivalents. The performance is limited by the primitive technology but the chassis has survived for centuries in service, which says something about the fundamental construction.
variants.deployment: Two variants, both using primitive technology throughout. Primitive construction documentation and specialist knowledge are prerequisites before working on either variant. Modern manuals do not apply. If you have Hectors in your inventory, establish contact with whatever technical archive covers Free Worlds League primitive construction before attempting any significant work. These are historical artifacts in active service.

variants.name: HL-1
variants.overview: Nashan Diversified introduced the Hel in 3092 from their Furillo facility, transitioning from IndustrialMech manufacturing into BattleMech production. The N&D HLBM endo steel frame and Hermes 250 XL are solid construction for a new manufacturer's first BattleMech, filling the Wolverine tactical role for ambush and interdiction work.
variants.capabilities: The Hermes 250 XL gives 86 kph at 50 tons — good speed for the interdiction role. The XL vulnerability concern applies as always. The endo steel structure requires trained techs for structural repairs. Two variants cover different weapons configurations. The LCAF rejection that drove the design to mercenary and militia markets didn't reflect on the engineering quality — the Hel is a capable machine.
variants.deployment: Two variants, with the supply disruption that created the Eris being the notable production history event. The XL advisory applies consistently. Nashan Diversified parts support through their Furillo facility is reliable for standard components. The endo steel maintenance requirement is the technical advisory — confirm tech qualification before structural work. The mercenary and militia market has received this design well.

variants.deployment: Two variants, with the supply disruption that created the Eris being the notable production history event. The XL advisory applies consistently. variants.name: HEP-1H
variants.overview: Mitchell Vehicles built the Helepolis in 2460 as one of the first BattleMechs designed around dedicated artillery capability, and the Armstrong Industries Sniper Artillery Piece is the entire reason the chassis exists. The primitive original through to modern production variants span five centuries and entirely different maintenance realities.
variants.capabilities: The Armstrong Sniper is the maintenance focus and it requires specific artillery system knowledge different from standard ballistic or energy weapons. The mobility sacrifice for artillery capability is deliberate and explicit — this machine does not move or fight like a conventional BattleMech. Four variants span from the primitive original through modern configurations. The primitive original uses a 180-rated primitive engine with specific maintenance requirements.
variants.deployment: Four variants from the 2460 primitive original through modern configurations. The primitive original requires primitive construction documentation — do not apply modern procedures to primitive hulls. The production modern variants are the operational standard. Artillery ammunition supply is the critical logistics factor — specialized munitions with careful storage requirements and limited availability compared to standard weapons. Establish the supply chain before deployment.

The fire support role requires pilots who stay at range and use the weapons array methodically — brief accordingly for pilots coming from more mobile assignments.

variants.overview: The Conjurer — Inner Sphere designation Hellhound — is effectively a Wolverine IIC, a comprehensive Clan technology rebuild of the classic Inner Sphere design. The Clan construction quality throughout delivers meaningfully more capability than the IS original while maintaining the same basic operational identity. Seven variants show extensive exploitation of the platform.
variants.capabilities: The Clan technology upgrade throughout retains the Wolverine's core performance profile while improving every system's efficiency. The skirmisher and raider role is well-served by the speed and weapons combination. Seven variants cover different tactical approaches. The Wolf Empire connection means later variants reflect specific Wolf operational requirements. Clan construction quality is high throughout.
variants.deployment: Seven variants from the original Clan rebuild through Wolf Empire adaptations. The most recent Wolf Empire variants make conservative modifications to the established design. Clan parts support through Wolf Empire and predecessor Clan channels. The Wolverine heritage means techs familiar with IS Wolverine maintenance will find the structural layout conceptually familiar despite the Clan construction differences.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Ice Hellion introduced their totem OmniMech in 3059 as an embodiment of the Clan's speed-and-aggression philosophy, and the 210-rated XL achieving 118 kph at 30 tons delivers on that concept completely. Ten configurations reflect the Hellion's tactical versatility within the fast light OmniMech role.
variants.capabilities: 118 kph at 30 tons is genuinely fast and the XL enabling it carries the standard vulnerability concern — at this speed a side torso breach is a serious problem very quickly. The OmniMech pod system is well-implemented for the weight class. Ten configurations means significant pod inventory requirements. Ice Hellion construction quality is consistent. The LRM-10 long-range configurations are the most maintenance-intensive due to the multiple launcher feeds.
variants.deployment: Ten configurations with Configuration A's three LRM-10 long-range harassment approach being one of the more common. The XL advisory applies universally. Pod workspace at 30 tons is physically limited; configuration swaps take more time than the procedure suggests due to access constraints. Parts support varies following Ice Hellion's dissolution. The speed is the tactical identity across all configurations — pilots who don't exploit it are misusing the chassis.

variants.capabilities: 97 kph for a 45-ton medium is good speed for the networked striker role. The XL vulnerability concern applies. The C3 equipment requires specialist calibration maintenance. Six variants cover different weapons and electronics configurations. The endo steel structure requires trained tech qualification for structural repairs. The anti-infantry focus on some variants reflects specific operational requirements.
variants.deployment: Six variants from the September 3062 original through developments. The base variant entered service with the Crucis Lancers. C3 calibration advisory applies to all C3-equipped variants — assign personnel with network electronics training. XL advisory applies consistently. General Motors parts support through Federated Suns and Federated Commonwealth channels is reliable.

variants.overview: The Hellstar emerged from the joint Wolf-in-Exile and Hell's Horses production effort, following the Cygnus, as another collaborative assault design. Four Ripper Series A1 ER PPCs on a 95-ton chassis is an aggressive all-energy concept that requires serious heat management discipline from pilots.
variants.capabilities: Four ER PPCs on any chassis generates extreme heat and pilot discipline is not optional — undisciplined firing will shut this machine down at the worst possible moment. The reinforced arm mounts for the PPC array are the structural feature requiring specific maintenance attention. The thirty double heat sinks are the thermal management foundation. Two variants with the second trading heat sinks for a targeting computer.
variants.deployment: Two variants. The heat management advisory applies to both but the second variant's reduced heat sink count makes it even more demanding — that targeting computer accuracy advantage comes at real thermal cost. Joint Wolf-in-Exile and Hell's Horses parts support. Brief every Hellstar pilot thoroughly on heat management before deployment — four ER PPCs fired without discipline will end the engagement badly.

variants.name: HRC-LS-9000
variants.overview: Kali Yama introduced the Hercules in 3054 for the Free Worlds League as a mobile firing platform, and the Magna 350 XL gives 86 kph at 70 tons — fast for a heavy fire support design. The design reflected FWLM doctrine needs at the time of the Clan Invasion's threat assessment.
variants.capabilities: The Magna 350 XL pushing 70 tons to 86 kph is the performance foundation and the XL vulnerability concern is the standard advisory. Five variants cover different weapons configurations. The mobile firing platform concept means the weapons array needs to reach range efficiently — the speed enables that. KALI and ATC construction quality is consistent and parts availability through Free Worlds League channels is good.
variants.deployment: Five variants from the 3054 base production through subsequent configurations. The base HRC-LS-9000 is the standard reference. XL advisory applies consistently. Kali Yama parts support through Free Worlds League logistics is reliable. The mobile fire support role rewards pilots who use the speed to establish advantageous fire positions rather than standing and trading — brief the tactical concept to pilots from less mobile assignments.
