variants.name: HER-1S
variants.overview: The Star League commissioned the Hermes in 2632 as a high-speed reconnaissance platform, and the massive GM 270 fusion engine occupying nearly half the chassis mass is the defining design choice. Eleven variants over the production run show the concept adapting through multiple technology eras. The engine dominance creates tight access for maintenance on surrounding components.
variants.capabilities: The GM 270 is the machine — everything else is secondary to enabling that engine. The tight packaging around the oversized powerplant means maintenance access is more constrained than on conventionally proportioned designs. Speed is the primary defense and the weapons support reconnaissance rather than sustained combat. The primitive original Star League configuration is a completely different maintenance case from production variants.
variants.deployment: Eleven variants from the 2632 Star League original through post-Helm Memory Core upgrades. The original Star League configuration with advanced technology is the most capable and most documentation-intensive. Later downgraded variants are more supportable with commonly available parts. The tight engine-adjacent packaging advisory is consistent across all variants — patience and proper tooling matter more than forcing access.

variants.name: HER-2S
variants.overview: Irian BattleMechs introduced the Hermes II in 2798 as a forty-ton medium designed for urban and forest terrain operations. Walk six, run nine on the standard 240-rated engine. Eleven variants span from the original through the Republic era. The terrain expertise is the consistent tactical identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at forty tons. The design's advantage in restrictive terrain is real — the speed and profile suit city and forest fighting where larger machines struggle to manoeuvre. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The HER-2S is the original 2798 model: an AC/5, a medium laser, and a flamer on the standard 240-rated engine. Walk six, run nine. The AC/5 handles direct ballistic fire. The medium laser covers close energy work. The flamer handles infantry.
variants.deployment: The 2S is the design that established the Hermes II's reputation for effective urban and forest fighting. The AC/5 provides harassment at range. The medium laser and flamer handle close engagement. Eleven variants have come from this foundation.

variants.name: HER-2M 'Mercury'
variants.overview: Irian BattleMechs introduced the Hermes II in 2798 as a forty-ton medium designed for urban and forest terrain operations. Walk six, run nine on the standard 240-rated engine. Eleven variants span from the original through the Republic era. The terrain expertise is the consistent tactical identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at forty tons. The design's advantage in restrictive terrain is real — the speed and profile suit city and forest fighting where larger machines struggle to manoeuvre. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The Mercury carries three medium lasers, a flamer, and two machine guns on a larger 280-rated engine. Walk seven, run ten. The 280-rated engine pushes walk seven. Three medium lasers provide more close-range energy fire than the standard 2S. Machine guns handle infantry.
variants.deployment: The Mercury trades the AC/5 for walk seven speed and more medium lasers. Walk seven is noticeably faster in urban terrain where the Hermes II operates. Three medium lasers at close range in confined environments is the concept. The flamer and machine guns handle infantry.

variants.name: HER-4K 'Hermes III'
variants.overview: Irian BattleMechs introduced the Hermes II in 2798 as a forty-ton medium for urban and forest terrain operations. Walk six, run nine. Eleven variants. The terrain expertise is the consistent tactical identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at forty tons. The speed and profile suit urban and forest fighting. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The HER-4K Hermes III carries two large lasers. Walk six, run nine. All-energy, no ammunition. Two large lasers extend direct fire range over the standard medium lasers of the 2S. Capellan Confederation rebrand following Ceres Metals licence acquisition.
variants.deployment: The 4K was renamed Hermes III by Ceres Metals. Two large lasers provide direct fire range the 2S lacks. No flamer or machine guns removes anti-infantry capability. The all-energy loadout suits Capellan operations without reliable ammunition supply. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: HER-5S
variants.overview: Irian BattleMechs introduced the Hermes II in 2798 as a forty-ton medium designed for urban and forest terrain operations. Walk six, run nine on the standard 240-rated engine. Eleven variants span from the original through the Republic era. The terrain expertise is the consistent tactical identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at forty tons. The design's advantage in restrictive terrain is real — the speed and profile suit city and forest fighting where larger machines struggle to manoeuvre. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The HER-5S carries a UAC/5, a medium pulse laser, and a flamer. Walk six, run nine. The UAC/5 provides sustained double-tap ballistic fire. The medium pulse laser is more accurate than the standard medium. The flamer handles infantry.
variants.deployment: The 5S is the primary upgrade using Clan-era technology. The UAC/5 double-tap rate maintains consistent ballistic pressure. The pulse laser accuracy improvement is real in close urban terrain. The flamer retains anti-infantry capability. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: HER-5ME 'Mercury Elite'
variants.overview: Irian BattleMechs introduced the Hermes II in 2798 as a forty-ton medium designed for urban and forest terrain operations. Walk six, run nine on the standard 240-rated engine. Eleven variants span from the original through the Republic era. The terrain expertise is the consistent tactical identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at forty tons. The design's advantage in restrictive terrain is real — the speed and profile suit city and forest fighting where larger machines struggle to manoeuvre. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The Mercury Elite carries a single light Gauss rifle. Walk six, run nine. One weapon, accurate long-range ballistic fire, with impressive armour and electronic equipment. The light Gauss provides accuracy at extended range.
variants.deployment: The Mercury Elite is the sensor and armour variant with a single light Gauss rifle as the weapon. The armour and electronics are the investment. For reconnaissance operations where sensor capability matters more than firepower, the Mercury Elite's loadout priorities make sense. A light Gauss is adequate self-defence on a fast machine.

variants.name: HER-5C
variants.overview: Irian BattleMechs introduced the Hermes II in 2798 as a forty-ton medium designed for urban and forest terrain operations. Walk six, run nine on the standard 240-rated engine. Eleven variants span from the original through the Republic era. The terrain expertise is the consistent tactical identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 240-rated XL engine. The HER-5C carries an iNarc launcher, three ER medium lasers, and an ER large laser. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The iNarc plants homing beacons. The ER large laser extends direct fire reach. The ER mediums handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: The 5C is the designation and long-range fire variant. The iNarc combined with Hermes II speed makes it an effective forward observer that moves quickly. The ER large laser extends the direct fire envelope over earlier variants. XL engine vulnerability is the tradeoff for the heavier weapons load.

variants.name: HER-6D
variants.overview: Irian BattleMechs introduced the Hermes II in 2798 as a forty-ton medium designed for urban and forest terrain operations. Walk six, run nine on the standard 240-rated engine. variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at forty tons. The design's advantage in restrictive terrain is real — the speed and profile suit city and forest fighting where larger machines struggle to manoeuvre. The Rotary AC/5 delivers sustained ballistic harassment at a high rate of fire. The ER medium handles close energy engagement. The flamer handles infantry.
variants.deployment: The 6D brings Rotary AC/5 sustained fire rate to the Hermes II. The urban terrain the design was built for suits the Rotary AC's sustained pressure capability. The ER medium extends energy range. The flamer retains infantry handling capability. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: HER-5SA
variants.overview: Irian BattleMechs introduced the Hermes II in 2798 as a forty-ton medium designed for urban and forest terrain operations. Walk six, run nine on the standard 240-rated engine. variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 240-rated XL engine. The HER-5SA carries a UAC/5, a large pulse laser, and a flamer. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The large pulse laser is accurate at medium range. The UAC/5 adds sustained ballistic fire. The flamer handles infantry.
variants.deployment: The 5SA upgrades the 5S with a large pulse laser replacing the medium pulse. The large pulse laser accuracy at medium range is the improvement. The UAC/5 sustained fire and flamer anti-infantry capability are retained. XL engine adds the standard vulnerability for the weight class.

variants.overview: Irian BattleMechs introduced the Hermes II in 2798 as a forty-ton medium designed for urban and forest terrain operations. Walk six, run nine on the standard 240-rated engine. variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at forty tons. The design's advantage in restrictive terrain is real — the speed and profile suit city and forest fighting where larger machines struggle to manoeuvre. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The HER-5Sr carries a heavy PPC, a medium pulse laser, and a flamer. Walk six, run nine. The heavy PPC hits harder than a standard PPC at medium range but has a minimum range gap. The pulse laser covers the close-range gap. The flamer handles infantry.
variants.deployment: The 5Sr is the heavy PPC variant. The heavy PPC provides significantly more firepower at medium range than the standard AC/5. The minimum range gap requires the pulse laser at close distances. The flamer handles infantry. Standard engine survivability. Heat from the heavy PPC requires management.

variants.name: HER-7S
variants.overview: Irian BattleMechs introduced the Hermes II in 2798 as a forty-ton medium designed for urban and forest terrain operations. Walk six, run nine on the standard 240-rated engine. Eleven variants span from the original through the Republic era. The terrain expertise is the consistent tactical identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve, jump eight on the 320-rated IS XXL engine. The HER-7S carries a light PPC, a large pulse laser, and an ER flamer. Walk eight. The XXL engine pushes walk eight. The large pulse laser is accurate at medium range. The light PPC covers short range. The ER flamer handles infantry.
variants.deployment: The 7S is the maximum speed and jump Hermes II. Walk eight, jump eight on a forty-ton machine creates exceptional terrain mobility. The XXL engine enables this performance but at severe vulnerability cost — side torso damage is catastrophic. XXL maintenance requires specialist procedures. The ER flamer extends infantry engagement range.

variants.name: HER-7A
variants.overview: Irian BattleMechs introduced the Hermes II in 2798 as a forty-ton medium designed for urban and forest terrain operations. Walk six, run nine on the standard 240-rated engine. Eleven variants span from the original through the Republic era. The terrain expertise is the consistent tactical identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 240-rated light engine. The HER-7A carries a UAC/10, a medium X-pulse laser, and a flamer. Light engine — side torso survivability. The UAC/10 provides medium-range ballistic fire with double-tap capability. The X-pulse laser is accurate at close range.
variants.deployment: The 7A combines light engine survivability with UAC/10 punch. The light engine survives hits that kill XL Hermes II variants. The UAC/10 is a substantially heavier ballistic weapon than the standard AC/5. The X-pulse laser accuracy suits urban close-range engagement. The flamer handles infantry.

variants.name: HER-4K
variants.overview: Ostmann Industries engineers on Kurita recognized the potential in imported Hermes II chassis and created the Hermes III in 3025 as a DCMS adaptation, essentially rebadging and modifying the Hermes II for Combine service. The Hermes II foundation means structural maintenance is identical to that design.
variants.capabilities: The Hermes II chassis maintenance experience transfers completely — structural work, engine procedures, and chassis-level maintenance are the same. The Hermes III differs in the weapons reconfiguration for DCMS tactical requirements. Single variant. The import origin means some components may have different sourcing requirements than domestically produced DCMS hardware.
variants.deployment: Single configuration based on the Hermes II import. Techs familiar with the Hermes II have no structural learning curve on the Hermes III. DCMS and Ostmann parts through Combine channels for domestic components; Irian-origin components follow their own sourcing. The urban terrain capability of the Hermes II foundation transfers completely to the III.

variants.name: HMC-13
variants.overview: StarCorps introduced the Hermit Crab in the early thirty-second century following Son Hoa's planetary infrastructure development, and the Jenner-comparable movement profile reflects the design brief for a fast light with aggressive capability. Three variants cover different tactical approaches on the same StarCorps foundation.
variants.capabilities: The Jenner-comparable speed at somewhat greater weight gives it better sustained combat capability than the ancestor while maintaining the mobility that makes lights useful. The Duralex Standard armor is adequate for the weight class. StarCorps construction quality is consistent. The weapons configuration emphasizes extended-range firepower at light weight. Three variants show the design finding different tactical applications.
variants.deployment: Three variants with the base HMC-13 embodying the simplicity and reliability philosophy. Twin ER medium lasers are the reliable energy weapons baseline. StarCorps parts through their distribution channels. The speed-and-light-armor profile means pilots need to understand this machine lives by mobility — it cannot absorb hits the way heavier designs can and shouldn't be asked to.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Olivetti Weaponry introduced the Hierofalcon in 3148 alongside the Jade Phoenix, designed for striker operations with exceptional speed and agility. The 270-rated XL with MASC at 45 tons creates a medium that can achieve genuine sprint speed when the tactical situation demands it.
variants.capabilities: The MASC system is the defining capability and the most maintenance-intensive feature. Regular calibration and close monitoring of usage frequency are essential — MASC systems pushed too hard too often degrade faster than standard maintenance schedules assume. The base 86 kph without MASC is already good for 45 tons; the MASC sprint capability is the tactical reserve. Five configurations cover different striker applications.
variants.deployment: Five configurations with the close-range Configuration A being designed for situations where the MASC sprint gets the Hierofalcon inside opponents' optimal range. The MASC advisory is consistent — monitor closely, calibrate regularly, don't treat it as routine operation. Jade Falcon parts support through Olivetti and Falcon logistics. Brief pilots on MASC discipline; it's there for tactical advantage, not daily use.

variants.name: HGN-732
variants.overview: The Highlander has been an SLDF and Inner Sphere icon since it entered service, and the M-7 Gauss rifle, Holly LRM-20, and SRM-6 combination that defines the original is still effective after centuries. Thirteen variants show ongoing adaptation of the assault platform concept. The jump capability is the tactical feature that distinguishes it from comparable assault designs.
variants.capabilities: The Gauss rifle is the primary weapon and Gauss capacitor maintenance is the primary technical focus — inspect and replace capacitors on schedule, not when they fail. The LRM and SRM launchers are proven hardware with good documentation. The jump jets add inspection requirements beyond what non-jumping assaults need. Thirteen variants mean extensive documentation exists across the family.
variants.deployment: Thirteen variants from the original HGN-732 through modern configurations. The original is the Star League reference. Gauss capacitor advisory applies to all Gauss-equipped variants. Jump jet inspection priority is higher on this chassis than non-jumping designs — frequent assault-weight jump operations accelerate wear. General Motors and successor manufacturer parts support is reliable through most supply chains.

variants.overview: Clan-built Highlanders from the Exodus were mothballed and eventually rebuilt with Clan technology, and the IIC represents that upgrade program. The fundamental design philosophy carries from the IS original — jump-capable assault with diverse weapons — while Clan construction quality improves every system.
variants.capabilities: The Clan technology rebuild retains the jump capability that defines the Highlander identity while delivering meaningfully improved weapons efficiency. The IIC 2's all-range configuration with anti-infantry capability reflects Jihad-era operational lessons. Three variants cover different tactical approaches. Clan construction quality throughout is high and consistent.
variants.deployment: Three variants including the Jihad-era IIC 2. The LRM-20 and ER PPC combination on the IIC 2 covers range effectively while the anti-infantry systems address specific Jihad threats. Jump jet inspection priority applies as on the IS original. Clan parts support through the manufacturing Clan's logistics channels. The IS Highlander maintenance experience provides useful conceptual foundation despite the Clan construction differences.

variants.name: HM-1
variants.overview: Diplan Mechyards built the Hitman in 3055 for the DCMS as a dedicated artillery spotter and electronic warfare platform, and the GM 210 XL at 30 tons gives 118 kph to support that spotting mission. The TAG and ECM systems are the design identity alongside the speed.
variants.capabilities: 118 kph is fast enough to get in position and get out, which is the whole operational concept for an artillery spotter. The TAG system requires specific calibration and the ECM needs regular maintenance attention beyond what standard weapons systems demand. Three variants cover different electronic warfare configurations. The weapons are secondary to the electronics on this chassis.
variants.deployment: Three variants with the base HM-1 being the original TAG and ECM-focused design. The electronic warfare specialist maintenance requirement applies to all variants. The TAG value depends entirely on having artillery units with compatible systems to designate for — ensure the operational context supports the electronic warfare concept before assigning Hitmans. Diplan parts through Combine channels is reliable.

variants.overview: General Motors reimagined the Hollander concept at their Kathil facility, introducing the Hollander III in 3114 at the original thirty-five-ton weight class but with a fundamentally different approach. The GM Bulldog endo steel chassis and GM Nova-10 Ultra AC/10 depart from the Gauss focus of the original family.
variants.capabilities: The Ultra AC/10 substitution for the Gauss rifle changes the maintenance profile significantly — ultra-class autocannons require more attention than standard due to the dual-rate mechanism, but eliminate the capacitor risk that makes Gauss maintenance so critical. variants.deployment: Three variants from the 3114 base production through subsequent configurations. The Ultra AC/10 mechanism maintenance advisory applies — keep it clean and service on schedule. The endo steel structural advisory applies consistently. General Motors parts through Federated Suns channels is reliable from Kathil. The Hollander name creates name recognition but this is a different machine from the Gauss-focused originals in everything except weight class.

variants.name: HOP-4B
variants.overview: Martinson Armaments built the Hoplite in 2578 for the Star League as an infantry support platform, and the deliberate speed sacrifice for firepower and protection reflects the infantry coordination role. Eight variants over the production run show ongoing adaptation. The design remains relevant specifically in the infantry support role it was built for.
variants.capabilities: The DAV 220 engine gives modest speed that limits the Hoplite's tactical flexibility but the infantry support role doesn't demand speed — it demands firepower and armor presence. The weapons array is designed for sustained fire in support of advancing infantry. The original Star League variants use quality construction throughout. Later variants adapt the chassis for different technology periods.
variants.deployment: Eight variants from the 2578 original through modernized configurations. The 2682 variant attempted to convert the Hoplite to a mainline combatant — Martinson's own documentation notes this was unsuccessful in that specific goal. The original infantry support mission is what the chassis does well. Parts availability varies by variant era. For the infantry support role in the right operational context, the Hoplite remains purpose-fit hardware.

variants.name: HNT-151
variants.overview: Kallon Weapon Industries unveiled the Hornet in 2760 as a twenty-ton urban reconnaissance light, and the design's survival through the Succession Wars in degraded form before returning to full production in 2990 tells you about its fundamental utility. Six variants cover the full production history from the advanced original through downgraded variants back to modern.
variants.capabilities: The urban reconnaissance role is where the Hornet's combination of mobility and relatively heavy twenty-ton armor makes sense. The jump jets are the tactical mobility feature requiring regular inspection. The production history created significant variant variation — the 2760 advanced original, the downgraded Succession Wars variants, and modern rebuilt versions are genuinely different maintenance cases despite the same chassis name.
variants.deployment: Six variants with the 2990 re-entry production model being the common modern baseline. Know which specific variant you have — the original advanced technology, the downgraded interim variants, and modern rebuilds have different maintenance requirements. Kallon parts through various channels depending on variant era. The urban reconnaissance role is consistent across the family; the equipment used to fill it varies significantly.

variants.name: HD-2F
variants.overview: Coalition Armory built the Hound on Filtvelt in 3098 as a fire support heavy for the Periphery operational context, and the Mydron Excel LB 10-X shoulder mount is the visual and tactical signature. Single variant, single purpose — this is a machine built around one role without complications.
variants.capabilities: The shoulder-mounted LB 10-X is the primary weapon and the mounting location is the maintenance detail worth noting — access procedures for the shoulder mount differ from arm or torso-mounted systems. The variable munitions capability of the LB 10-X is useful in the fire support role. The diverse supporting weapons provide fallback capability when the primary ammunition runs low. Filtvelt manufacture means Periphery-accessible construction standards.
variants.deployment: Single configuration with no factory variants. The HD-2F is the only Hound you'll see. Single-configuration simplicity is a genuine logistics advantage — one parts list, one manual, consistent across all hulls. Coalition Armory parts through Periphery channels. The Periphery operational context means the design was built for maintenance with limited support infrastructure — a practical advantage in austere conditions.

variants.name: HBK-4G
variants.overview: Komiyaba/Nissan introduced the Hunchback in 2572 as a dedicated urban combat platform, and the chassis-defining autocannon in the right torso has been intimidating opponents in cities for over five centuries. Twenty-four variants accumulated over that time cover essentially every tactical variation on the theme. Most techs have worked on a Hunchback before their first assignment.
variants.capabilities: The right torso autocannon is the design identity and the primary maintenance focus — whatever variant you're working on, the autocannon installation is where you spend most of your time. The weight of the primary weapon creates an inherent chassis imbalance that the actuator systems compensate for; keep those actuators in calibration. Twenty-four variants means extensive documentation exists and parts are available virtually everywhere.
variants.deployment: Twenty-four variants from the 2572 original through modern configurations. The HBK-4G is the standard reference. The autocannon ammunition supply chain is the consistent operational consideration across all ballistic-equipped variants. The urban combat role is the consistent tactical identity — pilots who use the Hunchback in open terrain are accepting a significant disadvantage. Komiyaba/Nissan and successor manufacturer parts support is available through virtually every major supply network.

variants.overview: Clan Smoke Jaguar developed the Hunchback IIC around 2856 as a heavy rebuild of the classic IS design, replacing the original's single autocannon with twin arm-mounted weapons of increasingly devastating calibre. Walk four, run six, jump four from a 200-rated Clan XL at fifty tons. The result is a machine that hits well above its weight class at close range and has almost no business being at long range.
variants.capabilities: The IIC 2 swaps the standard twin Ultra AC/20s for four heavy large lasers and two medium pulse lasers. This addresses the ammunition dependency that makes the standard IIC difficult to sustain in extended operations, at the cost of heavy laser maintenance complexity. The heavy large lasers hit hard but generate substantial heat. Four of them firing together on a fifty-ton chassis builds heat fast.
variants.deployment: The IIC 2 earned its 'Swaybacked' nickname from the visual profile of the heavy laser mounts. It is the preferred configuration for operations where ammunition resupply is uncertain. Warriors who run the standard AC/20 variant and know what it feels like to run dry appreciate the IIC 2 more than those who have not had that experience. Heavy laser calibration is the primary maintenance overhead.

variants.overview: Clan Smoke Jaguar developed the Hunchback IIC around 2856 as a heavy rebuild of the classic IS design, replacing the original's single autocannon with twin arm-mounted weapons of increasingly devastating calibre. Walk four, run six, jump four from a 200-rated Clan XL at fifty tons. The result is a machine that hits well above its weight class at close range and has almost no business being at long range.
variants.capabilities: The IIC 3 carries three ATM-12 launchers and three ER medium lasers. The ATM-12s provide genuine tactical flexibility across three munition types: standard for general use, extended-range for standoff work, high-explosive for close engagement. Three tons of ATM ammunition allows meaningful operational endurance. The ER mediums provide energy backup when missiles run low.
variants.deployment: The IIC 3 is the most tactically flexible Hunchback IIC configuration. Pre-loading the correct ATM munition mix before an operation is the key preparation decision. Warriors who carry a mixed load and switch intelligently between types get substantially better results than those who fire a single type throughout. The ER mediums are not a consolation prize when the ATMs run dry; they are a real weapon.

variants.overview: Clan Smoke Jaguar developed the Hunchback IIC around 2856 as a heavy rebuild of the classic IS design, replacing the original's single autocannon with twin arm-mounted weapons of increasingly devastating calibre. Walk four, run six, jump four from a 200-rated Clan XL at fifty tons. The result is a machine that hits well above its weight class at close range and has almost no business being at long range.
variants.capabilities: The IIC 4 mounts twin Rotary AC/5s and two ER medium lasers. The Rotary AC/5s deliver a high volume of ballistic fire per cycle, more rate than the AC/20 variants can manage. The trade-off is that the Rotary ACs hit for less damage per projectile and require their own ammunition management. Two tons each of Rotary ammunition is the operational limit on sustained combat.
variants.deployment: The IIC 4 is a sustained fire variant that performs well against multiple lighter targets where rate of fire matters more than per-shot impact. The ER mediums extend the engagement envelope beyond what the Rotary ACs cover comfortably. Warriors who favour attrition tactics over single devastating strikes tend to prefer the IIC 4 over the AC/20 primary configuration.

variants.overview: Clan Smoke Jaguar developed the Hunchback IIC around 2856 as a heavy rebuild of the classic IS design, replacing the original's single autocannon with twin arm-mounted weapons of increasingly devastating calibre. Walk four, run six, jump four from a 200-rated Clan XL at fifty tons. The result is a machine that hits well above its weight class at close range and has almost no business being at long range.
variants.capabilities: The IIC 5 replaces the Ultra AC/20s with twin LB 20-X autocannons and adds two medium pulse lasers. The LB 20-X provides both solid slug and cluster munition options that the Ultra AC/20 lacks. Cluster rounds hit lighter opponents and unarmoured targets hard at close range. Two tons per launcher is the ammunition constraint. The medium pulse lasers provide close-range energy backup.
variants.deployment: The IIC 5 is the most versatile of the autocannon-armed Hunchback IIC variants because the LB 20-X cluster option opens engagement profiles the standard AC/20 cannot handle as efficiently. Warriors who carry mixed slug and cluster loads and select correctly for the target type get the most from this configuration. The medium pulse lasers handle anything the autocannons cannot address at extreme close range.

variants.name: HUR-WO-R4L
variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated designed the Huron Warrior on Corey originally as a Clan OmniMech counter, and the heavy armor and XL engine combination reflects that specific design brief. The Grizzard Gauss Rifle is the primary weapon and the design rebuilt around that choice. Six variants show ongoing development of the counter-Clan heavy concept.
variants.capabilities: The Grizzard Gauss Rifle is quality hardware and Gauss capacitor maintenance is the primary technical focus — keep it in spec, inspect and replace on schedule. The XL engine gives competitive speed for a heavy with the standard vulnerability concern. The heavy armor is the defensive foundation that the Clan counter role demands. Six variants cover different secondary weapons configurations.
variants.deployment: Six variants from the 3055 base production through subsequent configurations. The Gauss capacitor advisory applies to all Gauss-equipped variants. XL advisory is consistent. Hollis parts through Capellan channels is reliable. The Clan counter design origin means this machine is built to survive the engagement long enough to use the Gauss rifle effectively — the heavy armor is not decorative.

variants.name: HSR-200-D
variants.overview: Newhart Industries built the Hussar in 2620 for the SLDF as a fast reconnaissance light, and the turreted center torso laser mount is the distinctive engineering feature that sets it apart from conventional arm-mounted designs. Eight variants over the production run show the concept adapting across technology eras.
variants.capabilities: The turreted center torso mount provides firing arc flexibility that arm-mounted weapons can't match, but the turret mechanism itself requires specific maintenance attention beyond standard weapons servicing. The turret bearing and traverse systems need regular inspection and lubrication — neglect creates the kind of mechanical failure that ruins exactly the engagement where you need to track a fast target. The ER large laser is otherwise straightforward hardware.
variants.deployment: Eight variants from the 2620 SLDF original through subsequent configurations. The turret mechanism maintenance is the consistent advisory across all variants — it's the component that makes the chassis distinctive and the one that fails first when maintenance is deferred. Newhart parts through various channels depending on variant era. The pure reconnaissance role means pilots need to understand engagement is secondary to information gathering.

variants.name: HYN-KTO
variants.overview: VEST built the Hyena on Solaris VII in 3066 as a purpose-built SalvageMech on decommissioned Kintaro chassis, and the salvage equipment suite is the entire point. This is not a combat BattleMech — it's a field recovery vehicle in BattleMech form, and maintaining it requires understanding that distinction.
variants.capabilities: The lift hoists, cutting equipment, and salvage systems are the primary maintenance focus rather than weapons. The ferro-fibrous armor inherited from the Kintaro donor is actually better protection than typical IndustrialMech construction. The salvage equipment sees high operational stress — cutting through battlefield debris and lifting damaged 'Mechs puts strain on systems that conventional combat doesn't. Inspect the salvage equipment systems frequently.
variants.deployment: Single configuration built on Kintaro chassis. The maintenance philosophy for this machine is entirely different from a combat 'Mech — the salvage systems are the primary equipment, the weapons are secondary self-defense tools. VEST parts through Solaris arena channels. The Kintaro structural heritage is useful when sourcing chassis-level components since that design has good parts availability.

variants.name: ICR-1X
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Icarus on Stewart as the Free Worlds League's first attempt at an independent BattleMech design, and the primitive technology throughout reflects the mid-twenty-fifth century limitations. This is not a machine you maintain from modern procedures — it requires primitive construction knowledge from the beginning.
variants.capabilities: Primitive cockpit, engine, and armor throughout — every system predates modern standards and requires primitive construction documentation to work on correctly. The simplicity of the design reflects what was achievable in the 2460s rather than what anyone would choose today. Single configuration, single production run. The primitive components have no modern equivalents and field fabrication from original specifications is the repair approach.
variants.deployment: Single prototype variant. If you have an Icarus in your inventory you have a historical artifact. Establish contact with Free Worlds League primitive construction archives before attempting any significant work. Do not apply modern procedures to primitive systems. The design value is historical and operational only in the most limited sense.

variants.name: ICR-1S
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises followed their first attempt with the Icarus II in 2518, producing the Free Worlds League's first mass-produced BattleMech. The Corean Model 1AA chassis with DAV 160 engine is primitive construction throughout, but considerably more practical than the original prototype. Three variants cover the early production history.
variants.capabilities: Primitive technology throughout means primitive construction documentation applies for all maintenance. The DAV 160 gives modest speed for a 40-tonner but the primitives of the era limited options. The design is historically significant as the FWLM's first production 'Mech but the maintenance reality is that modern parts don't fit primitive systems. Field fabrication from original specifications is the practical approach for anything beyond basic maintenance.
variants.deployment: Three variants from the 2518 original through early production refinements. All use primitive technology — confirm documentation before any work. Corean parts for primitive-era components require specialized sourcing. The mass-production achievement is significant historically; the operational limitations are equally significant practically. For a unit fielding these, plan for the specific support infrastructure that primitive designs require.

variants.overview: Clan Ice Hellion derived the Icestorm around 2830 from the Cameroon, a late Star League design, and the 300-rated XL at 25 tons achieving nearly 200 kph is the extraordinary performance number that defines this chassis. Clan Wolf's Jihad-era modernization created the Icestorm 2 on Weingarten as the first serious update to this ancient design.
variants.capabilities: Nearly 200 kph at 25 tons is a performance figure that still gets attention — this is the fastest 'Mech many techs will ever see. The XL enabling that speed at this weight class creates vulnerability that the speed itself is supposed to compensate for. At 25 tons any significant battle damage is proportionally serious. The Jihad-era Wolf rework addresses some of the original's limitations while retaining the speed identity.
variants.deployment: Two variants separated by the Jihad-era modernization. The original ancient design and the Wolf rework have different maintenance profiles — know which you have. The speed is the entire tactical concept and the armor is minimal. Parts support for the original ancient design requires specialist sourcing; the Wolf rework uses more current components through Wolf channels. Brief pilots clearly: this machine has no business absorbing hits.

variants.name: IMP-1A
variants.overview: Nicholas Kerensky specified the Imp as the exiled SLDF's totem 'Mech in 2793, and the bulbous command platform design reflects that origin. A hundred tons, walk three, run four on the 300-rated engine. Seven variants. The electronics suite is as important as the weapons on any command-configured Imp.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at a hundred tons. The command electronics require specialist maintenance attention separate from the standard weapons and mechanical systems. Standard engine — side torso survivability. The distinctive bulbous silhouette is immediately recognisable and cannot be disguised. The IMP-1A carries two ER PPCs, an LRM-20, five medium pulse lasers, and a small laser. Walk three, run four. The ER PPCs provide extended-range direct fire. The LRM-20 delivers heavy fire support. The pulse lasers handle close engagement. The command electronics add the coordination role.
variants.deployment: The 1A is the original Kerensky-specified Imp. The ER PPCs and LRM-20 together cover long and indirect fire. The pulse lasers close the engagement. The command electronics require specialist maintenance attention that the weapons systems alone do not. Walk three means position selection matters.

variants.name: IMP-1B
variants.overview: Nicholas Kerensky specified the Imp as the exiled SLDF's totem 'Mech in 2793, and the bulbous command platform design reflects that origin. A hundred tons, walk three, run four on the 300-rated engine. Seven variants. The electronics suite is as important as the weapons on any command-configured Imp.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at a hundred tons. The command electronics require specialist maintenance attention separate from the standard weapons and mechanical systems. Standard engine — side torso survivability. The distinctive bulbous silhouette is immediately recognisable and cannot be disguised. The IMP-1B carries two ER PPCs, an LRM-20, five medium lasers, and a medium pulse laser. Walk three, run four. Standard medium lasers replace the pulse lasers of the 1A. The medium pulse laser is the only pulse weapon retained.
variants.deployment: The 1B uses standard medium lasers rather than the pulse laser suite of the 1A. The weapons coverage is comparable at slightly reduced close-range accuracy. The command electronics requirement is unchanged. A configuration variant rather than a tactical philosophy change.

variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at a hundred tons. The command electronics require specialist maintenance attention separate from the standard weapons and mechanical systems. Standard engine — side torso survivability. The distinctive bulbous silhouette is immediately recognisable and cannot be disguised. The IMP-1C carries two ER PPCs, a Gauss rifle, six medium lasers, and a small laser. Walk three, run four. The Gauss rifle replaces the LRM-20 with accurate long-range ballistic fire. Six medium lasers provide close engagement.
variants.deployment: The 1C trades the LRM-20 indirect fire for Gauss accuracy. The Gauss combined with ER PPCs creates layered long-range fire. Six medium lasers provide more close-range energy output than the pulse laser variants. The command electronics maintenance requirement is unchanged.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: Nicholas Kerensky specified the Imp as the exiled SLDF's totem 'Mech in 2793, and the bulbous command platform design reflects that origin. A hundred tons, walk three, run four on the 300-rated engine. Seven variants. The electronics suite is as important as the weapons on any command-configured Imp.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four on the standard 300-rated Clan fusion engine. The Clan C carries two ER PPCs, an LRM-20, and five medium pulse lasers. Clan engine — maintenance procedures differ from IS engine variants. The ER PPCs, LRM-20, and pulse lasers provide the standard Imp weapons coverage.
variants.deployment: The Clan C uses a Clan engine in the standard Imp chassis. The Clan engine requires Clan-qualified maintenance alongside IS chassis procedures. The weapons are otherwise equivalent to the 1A. The command electronics maintenance requirement remains. Two-track maintenance across Clan engine and IS chassis.

variants.name: IMP-2E
variants.overview: Nicholas Kerensky specified the Imp as the exiled SLDF's totem 'Mech in 2793. A hundred tons, walk three, run four. Seven variants. The electronics suite is as important as the weapons on command-configured variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at a hundred tons. Command electronics require specialist maintenance. Standard engine variants — side torso survivability. The IMP-2E carries two PPCs, an LRM-15, and five medium lasers. Walk three, run four. The PPCs provide direct long-range fire. The LRM-15 delivers indirect fire support. Five medium lasers handle close engagement. The weapons fit is less capable than the 1A variants at long range.
variants.deployment: The 2E was produced for Clans that acquired Imp machines. The standard IS PPCs rather than ER PPCs reduce the long-range engagement envelope. The LRM-15 is a reduction from the 1A's LRM-20. The command electronics requirement is unchanged. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: IMP-3E
variants.overview: Nicholas Kerensky specified the Imp as the exiled SLDF's totem 'Mech in 2793. A hundred tons, walk three, run four. Seven variants. The electronics suite is as important as the weapons on command-configured variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four on the 300-rated XL engine. The IMP-3E carries two ER PPCs, an LRM-15, a large pulse laser, two medium lasers, and two medium pulse lasers. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The XL engine enables the additional weapons mass. ER PPCs restore the long-range engagement capability.
variants.deployment: The 3E uses the XL engine to carry a heavier weapons suite. ER PPCs at long range, pulse lasers for accuracy at medium and close range, LRM-15 for fire support. The XL engine adds the standard vulnerability that the standard engine variants avoid. Command electronics maintenance requirement unchanged.

variants.name: IMP-4E
variants.overview: Nicholas Kerensky specified the Imp as the exiled SLDF's totem 'Mech in 2793. A hundred tons, walk three, run four. Seven variants. The electronics suite is as important as the weapons on command-configured variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at a hundred tons. Command electronics require specialist maintenance. Standard engine variants — side torso survivability. The IMP-4E carries two ER PPCs, an LRM-20, three ER medium lasers, two medium pulse lasers, and two ER small lasers. Walk three, run four. The most heavily armed Imp variant. ER PPCs at long range, LRM-20 fire support, ER mediums for direct engagement, pulse lasers for accuracy, ER small lasers at point-blank.
variants.deployment: The 4E is the maximum weapons diversity Imp. The ER PPC, LRM-20, ER medium, pulse laser, and ER small laser combination covers every range band. The command electronics requirement is unchanged. Standard engine survivability. Walk three means position selection matters before the engagement begins.

variants.name: INF-NO
variants.overview: StarCorps rushed the Inferno into production on Crofton following the fall of New Avalon, and the urgency shows in some of the engineering choices — the compact gyro freeing center torso space is clever, the rushed production timeline created some initial quality variations that later batches corrected.
variants.capabilities: The compact gyro is the unusual structural component requiring specific maintenance knowledge — compact gyros have different repair procedures from standard gyros and techs who haven't worked with one before need to read the specific documentation carefully. The Heavy PPC is the primary weapon and heavy PPC maintenance differs from standard PPC procedures. Five OmniMech configurations cover different tactical approaches. The rushed production advisory on early hulls — inspect older examples more carefully.
variants.deployment: Five configurations with the Prime's Heavy PPC center torso placement being the baseline. The compact gyro and heavy PPC maintenance advisories are the consistent technical notes — both require specific knowledge beyond standard procedures. StarCorps parts through Federated Suns channels. Early production quality variations mean pre-3070 hulls warrant closer initial inspection than later production.

variants.name: INI-02
variants.overview: Martinson Armaments built the Initiate as the first BattleMech produced on Terra under Word of Blake occupation following the 3058 conquest, and the Geometric 1000 endo steel chassis is a sound engineering foundation. The Blakist connection creates post-Jihad parts sourcing challenges for specialist components.
variants.capabilities: The endo steel construction requires trained techs for structural repairs. The LTV 160 engine gives modest speed for a 35-ton design but the design prioritizes capability balance over speed extremes. Two variants cover different tactical configurations. Martinson construction quality is solid. The Word of Blake origin creates the expected post-Jihad supply chain complications for Blakist-origin components.
variants.deployment: Two variants from the original general-purpose configuration. The endo steel structural advisory applies consistently. Post-Jihad Martinson and Blakist component sourcing requires planning — standard Terra supply channels have changed significantly. The general-purpose design philosophy means neither variant is as specialized as purpose-built alternatives, but both are capable of operating across a range of tactical situations.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Smoke Jaguar produced the Iron Cheetah at their Phan Industriplex on Huntress starting in 3054, and the 400-rated Clan XL in a 100-ton chassis achieving walk four, run six is the engineering achievement that defines this machine. That is exceptional speed for a hundred-ton assault OmniMech and it shapes every tactical deployment decision made around this chassis.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at a hundred tons. The XL engine vulnerability at this weight class is not a theoretical concern: side torso damage is catastrophic and any pilot or tech who treats it otherwise will not survive a sustained engagement. The Huntress Industriplex construction quality is consistently high. Pod inventory for a full assault OmniMech across six configurations requires substantial support infrastructure. Configuration A carries an Ultra AC/20, two large pulse lasers, six machine guns, and two Streak SRM-6 launchers. The Ultra AC/20 in double-tap mode at close range is the centrepiece. The large pulse lasers and Streak SRM-6s add layered fire across the engagement. Six machine guns make this configuration devastating against infantry and battle armour. The machine gun ammunition requires its own supply management.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is a close-range assault variant that uses the Iron Cheetah's speed to close distance faster than opponents expect from a hundred-ton machine. The Ultra AC/20 and Streak SRM-6 combination at close range overwhelms most targets. Warriors who close the distance and keep it closed do well in A configuration. Those who expose the flanks to get there do not.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: Clan Smoke Jaguar produced the Iron Cheetah at their Phan Industriplex on Huntress starting in 3054, and the 400-rated Clan XL in a 100-ton chassis achieving walk four, run six is the engineering achievement that defines this machine. That is exceptional speed for a hundred-ton assault OmniMech and it shapes every tactical deployment decision made around this chassis.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at a hundred tons. The XL engine vulnerability at this weight class is not a theoretical concern: side torso damage is catastrophic and any pilot or tech who treats it otherwise will not survive a sustained engagement. The Huntress Industriplex construction quality is consistently high. Pod inventory for a full assault OmniMech across six configurations requires substantial support infrastructure. Configuration B is an all-energy loadout: two large pulse lasers, six medium pulse lasers, an ER small laser, and four jump jets. No ammunition dependency at all, which simplifies logistics but puts everything on heat management. The pulse laser suite is accurate at medium range and the jump jets provide repositioning capability unusual in a hundred-ton assault platform.
variants.deployment: Configuration B with four jump jets on a hundred-ton machine is a tactical surprise that opponents frequently fail to account for. The all-pulse loadout rewards warriors who can cycle fire to stay below the shutdown threshold. No ammunition logistics means B configuration can sustain independent operations longer than the autocannon variants. The jump jets earn their weight in terrain where ground movement would be slower.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: Clan Smoke Jaguar produced the Iron Cheetah at their Phan Industriplex on Huntress starting in 3054, and the 400-rated Clan XL in a 100-ton chassis achieving walk four, run six is the engineering achievement that defines this machine. Configuration C carries four ER large lasers, four medium pulse lasers, two Streak SRM-2 launchers, and an LRM-15. This is the longest-range Iron Cheetah configuration. Four ER large lasers at a hundred tons is an enormous energy output and the heat sinks work hard under sustained fire. The LRM-15 provides indirect fire capability the other configurations lack.
variants.deployment: Configuration C is the fire support variant, designed to engage from maximum range rather than closing in the way the A configuration does. The ER large laser reach combined with Iron Cheetah speed means the warrior can choose engagement range against almost any opponent. The LRM-15 provides indirect fire when direct targeting is not feasible. The heat load across all ER large lasers demands strict fire cycling.

variants.name: JLP-BD
variants.overview: Victory Conditions Industries and Eris Enterprises jointly developed the Jackalope in 3134 as a mixed-technology reconnaissance platform, and the combination of speed, electronics, and weapons for the weight class is genuinely capable. Eight variants show the design finding tactical applications beyond pure reconnaissance.
variants.capabilities: Fast, well-armed for a light, and equipped with electronics that multiply its tactical value — the Jackalope delivers on its design brief. The mixed technology creates the expected cross-documentation challenge. The sophisticated electronics require specialist calibration maintenance beyond standard weapons servicing. Eight variants mean significant configuration variety with different maintenance profiles.
variants.deployment: Eight variants from the 3134 base production through subsequent configurations. The electronics maintenance specialist requirement is consistent — assign personnel with sensor and electronics training. The mixed technology component maintenance requires both IS and Clan capable techs depending on the specific systems. Parts support through the joint developer's combined channels. The reconnaissance role is the design foundation; the weapons make it capable of self-defense rather than just observation.

variants.name: JKR-8T
variants.overview: Skobel MechWorks built the Jackrabbit in 2763 to provide infantry formations with organic long-range fire support, and the Armstrong JJ-Lite autocannon with Streak SRM backup is the weapons identity. variants.capabilities: The Armstrong JJ-Lite autocannon is straightforward and well-documented hardware for the infantry support role. variants.deployment: Three variants from the 2763 original through the Blakist modernization. The Blakist-era variant's exotic electronics require specialist maintenance and post-Jihad parts sourcing through former Blakist channels. The original and early production variants are more straightforwardly supported. Skobel parts for original components; Blakist channels for the modernized variant's electronics. Know which variant you have before planning the maintenance program.

variants.name: JHK-03
variants.overview: Clan Jade Falcon's technician caste developed the Jade Hawk in the early 3130s under Galaxy Commander Beckett Malthus' direction, and the Starfire 375 XL pushing 75 tons to 97 kph is the performance achievement that drove the design. Dynamic Ordnance manufactured an Inner Sphere adaptation on Galatea. Four variants cover both Clan and IS production.
variants.capabilities: 97 kph for a 75-ton heavy is genuinely exceptional — most heavies in this class achieve 64-86 kph. The XL enabling that speed carries the standard vulnerability concern and at heavy weight a side torso breach is a serious tactical event. The speed advantage is real and tactically significant. Four variants cover different weapons configurations on the same fast heavy chassis.
variants.deployment: Four variants including the Galatea-manufactured IS adaptation. The IS variant uses mixed Clan and IS components — know which version you're working on before sourcing parts. The XL advisory applies consistently across all variants. Jade Falcon parts for Clan variants; Dynamic Ordnance and IS channels for the Galatea production. Brief pilots that 97 kph at 75 tons requires fundamentally different tactical thinking than standard heavy 'Mech doctrine.

variants.name: A

Jade Falcon parts support through Olivetti and Falcon logistics channels.

variants.name: JM6-S
variants.overview: Kallon Industries introduced the JagerMech in 2774 as a dedicated anti-aircraft and long-range fire support platform, and the battery of four Mydron autocannons is the design identity. Twelve variants accumulated over the production run show the chassis adapting far beyond the original AA role. The multiple autocannon configuration is mechanically demanding.
variants.capabilities: Four autocannons mean four mechanism maintenance requirements simultaneously — cleaning schedules, wear assessment, and ammunition feed inspection all multiply by four. The anti-aircraft role for which the original was designed requires the autocannons to be in top condition; degraded accuracy from deferred maintenance defeats the design purpose. The ammunition management across four systems requires careful supply planning.
variants.deployment: Twelve variants from the 2774 SLDF original through developments. The quad autocannon maintenance multiplication is the consistent advisory — four systems, four maintenance requirements, synchronized schedules. Kallon parts through Lyran and Federated Suns channels is reliable. The twelve-variant family means extensive documentation exists. Know which specific variant you have — later variants that substitute energy weapons for some autocannons have significantly different maintenance profiles.

Twelve variants accumulated over the production run show the chassis adapting far beyond the original AA role. The multiple autocannon configuration is mechanically demanding.
variants.capabilities: Four autocannons mean four mechanism maintenance requirements simultaneously — cleaning schedules, wear assessment, and ammunition feed inspection all multiply by four. The anti-aircraft role for which the original was designed requires the autocannons to be in top condition; degraded accuracy from deferred maintenance defeats the design purpose. The ammunition management across four systems requires careful supply planning.
variants.deployment: Twelve variants from the 2774 SLDF original through developments. The quad autocannon maintenance multiplication is the consistent advisory — four systems, four maintenance requirements, synchronized schedules. Kallon parts through Lyran and Federated Suns channels is reliable. The twelve-variant family means extensive documentation exists. Know which specific variant you have — later variants that substitute energy weapons for some autocannons have significantly different maintenance profiles.

variants.name: JM6-D3
variants.overview: The JagerMech III emerged from Victor Steiner-Davion's Redesign for Davion Pride initiative in 3058, built on the Kallon Type XIV endo steel chassis as a modernized successor to the original. The technological upgrades to every system are genuine improvements over the base design.
variants.capabilities: The endo steel construction requires trained techs for structural repairs beyond standard maintenance. The weapons upgrades from the original JagerMech improve every system's capability and change the maintenance profile from pure autocannon to a more balanced mixed weapons array. Two variants cover the modernized design. Kallon construction quality is consistently solid and the documentation is thorough.
variants.deployment: Two variants from the 3058 base production. The Davion Pride program association means Federated Suns parts support is well-established. The endo steel structural advisory applies consistently. The modernized weapons array is more capable and more varied than the original JagerMech family — techs familiar with the original will find some systems familiar and others require fresh learning.

variants.overview: Assault Tech Industries, a Wolf-in-Exile firm on Dompaire, introduced the Jaguar quad in 3121 as a 35-ton design with impressive speed for the weight class. The quad chassis in the light weight class creates a specific maintenance profile and the Light Force 280 XL is the performance foundation.
variants.capabilities: Approaching 100 kph for a quad light 'Mech is impressive and the XL enabling it carries the standard vulnerability concern. The quad chassis at 35 tons means quad maintenance overhead applies to a relatively small frame — more leg systems than a biped, with less physical access space than a larger quad. Two variants cover different tactical configurations. Wolf-in-Exile construction quality is solid.
variants.deployment: Two variants with the Jaguar 2 reconfiguring for close-range combat and reconnaissance. The quad maintenance overhead advisory applies to both — more leg systems to inspect, more complex battle damage assessment. The XL vulnerability concern is consistent. Assault Tech and Wolf-in-Exile parts support through their Dompaire facility and exile channels. Quad-qualified techs are the consistent requirement.

variants.name: JVN-10N
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies introduced the Javelin in 2751 for export to Star League member states, and the twin Arrowlite SRM-6 launchers are the design identity. Eleven variants show the chassis adapting across multiple technology eras. The SRM-focused armament creates a machine that excels in close combat and struggles at range.
variants.capabilities: The twin SRM-6 launchers provide devastating close-range firepower when the Javelin closes to optimal range. The ammunition management is the operational concern — those launchers consume ammunition quickly and the tactical effectiveness drops sharply when bins run low. The jump jets add the three-dimensional mobility that helps a close-range specialist close to engagement distance. Eleven variants cover different technology periods.
variants.deployment: Eleven variants from the 2751 original through modern configurations. The close-range role and ammunition management advisory are the consistent operational considerations. Jump jet inspection is a maintenance priority given the frequency of use the design's tactics demand. Stormvanger parts through various channels depending on variant era. Brief pilots clearly — this is a close-range machine and trying to engage at medium or long range with it is a losing proposition.

variants.name: JR7-A
variants.overview: Diplan Mechyards built the Jenner in 2784 for House Kurita, and the 30-to-90-meter optimal engagement range that defines the design's combat doctrine is worth communicating clearly to every pilot assigned one. Fourteen variants show sustained relevance across multiple eras. Among the fastest designs of its period, it compensates for light armor with speed and burst damage.
variants.capabilities: The speed is the armor — this is one of those designs where the whole tactical concept depends on not being hit. The four medium laser configuration is effective at close range and heat-neutral enough to sustain. The light armor means any serious hit creates proportional problems at 35 tons. Fourteen variants cover the full development from early Kurita service through modern upgrades. Diplan construction quality is consistent.
variants.deployment: Fourteen variants from the 2784 original through modern configurations. The original early variant with the single large laser is the most historically unusual configuration. The JR7-D production standard is the reference. The close-range doctrine and speed-as-armor advisory applies across the family. Diplan parts through Combine channels is reliable and the long production history means most techs know the design.

variants.overview: The Jenner IIC carries the original Jenner's close-range speed philosophy forward with Clan technology, and the result is fast, hard-hitting, and ill-suited for prolonged engagement — exactly what the IS Jenner was but more so. Four variants cover different tactical applications of the same aggressive fast-light concept.
variants.capabilities: The Clan technology upgrade makes every system more efficient while retaining the original's core identity. Fast and hard-hitting with minimal sustain capability — the Jenner IIC wins engagements quickly or loses them. The support variant with ER large laser and LRM-5 is the tactical outlier that transforms the chassis into a sniper role, requiring completely different pilot skills and different maintenance priorities.
variants.deployment: Four variants with the support sniper configuration being the most tactically distinct from the close-range base concept. Know which variant you have — the sniper configuration and the close-range brawler variants require different pilot briefings and different ammunition planning. Clan parts support through the manufacturing Clan's channels. The speed-is-armor advisory applies to close-range variants; the sniper variant relies on range rather than speed for survivability.

variants.name: JN-G8A
variants.overview: Shengli Arms built the Jinggau on Victoria in 3059 for the Capellan Xin Sheng programme. Sixty-five tons, walk five, run seven, jump five on the 325-rated XL engine. Eight variants. The endo steel chassis requires trained tech qualification for structural repairs.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The endo steel structure requires specific structural repair qualification. The jump capability combined with close-range weapons is the design's tactical identity. The JN-G8A carries a Gauss rifle, four ER medium lasers, and a medium pulse laser. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The Gauss provides accurate long-range fire. The ER mediums and pulse laser cover close engagement. XL engine vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The G8A was the Jinggau that impressed CCAF high command in initial trials. The Gauss accuracy at range combined with jump five and close-range energy density creates a capable offensive platform. The endo steel structure requires specific tech training for structural repairs. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: JG-R9T1
variants.overview: Solaris Arms built the Juggernaut exclusively for the Solaris VII arena circuit, and the arena-only construction context shapes everything about maintaining it. Four variants reflect arena combat feedback. The X-Pulse laser technology on later variants is the notable technical feature requiring specific maintenance knowledge.
variants.capabilities: The GM 270 engine gives 54 kph for a 90-ton machine — adequate for arena combat where movement ranges are limited. X-Pulse lasers on later variants have different maintenance requirements from standard or large pulse lasers — the extended-range pulse technology has specific power cycling characteristics. The arena construction prioritizes durability in regulated combat scenarios. The physical combat systems if present require specific mechanical inspection.
variants.deployment: Four variants from the original conventional pulse laser configuration through X-Pulse upgrades. X-Pulse laser maintenance advisory applies to equipped variants — confirm specific training. Arena construction assumptions differ from field deployment requirements; for field use the design needs more aggressive maintenance scheduling than arena rotation schedules suggest. Solaris Arms parts through arena market channels.

variants.name: JLN-5A

The assault weight makes this a logistics-intensive design to support; plan accordingly.

variants.overview: Clan Jade Falcon developed the Jupiter during the Civil War era as a cost-effective complement to the Turkina. A hundred tons, walk three, run four on the 300-rated Clan XL. Three variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at a hundred tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk three is slow even by assault standards. Clan construction quality throughout. Variant 2 carries two Ultra AC/10s, two ER PPCs, and two LRM-15 launchers. Walk three, run four, jump three. The UAC/10s provide medium-range ballistic fire with double-tap capability. The ER PPCs handle long-range engagement. The LRM-15s add indirect fire.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 brings close-range versatility to the Jupiter through the UAC/10s. The ER PPCs maintain long-range fire superiority. The LRM-15s provide fire support. Jump three adds positioning options. The UAC/10 mechanism cleaning schedules add to the maintenance overhead.

variants.overview: Clan Jade Falcon developed the Jupiter during the Civil War era as a cost-effective complement to the Turkina. A hundred tons, walk three, run four on the 300-rated Clan XL. Three variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at a hundred tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk three is slow even by assault standards. Clan construction quality throughout. Variant 3 carries two Ultra AC/10s, two HAG/30s, and two ER medium lasers. Walk three, run four, no jump. The HAG/30s spread ballistic projectiles across multiple armour locations. The UAC/10s add medium-range ballistic fire. The ER mediums handle direct close engagement.
variants.deployment: Variant 3 removes jump capability and adds HAG/30 devastation. The HAG/30 spread combined with UAC/10 concentrated fire creates multi-location damage. Walk three means this variant commits to a position. The ER mediums handle close-range threats. Clan XL side torso vulnerability applies.

variants.overview: Clan Jade Falcon developed the Jupiter during the Civil War era as a cost-effective complement to the Turkina. A hundred tons, walk three, run four on the 300-rated Clan XL. Three variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 400-rated Clan XL engine. Variant 4 carries two ER PPCs, two LRM-15 launchers, and two Streak SRM-4 launchers. Walk four — the fastest Jupiter configuration. The 400-rated engine provides genuine mobility at this weight. The ER PPCs handle long range. The LRM-15s add fire support. The Streak SRM-4s handle close threats on lock.
variants.deployment: Variant 4 is the mobile Jupiter. Walk four at a hundred tons changes the tactical dynamic — it can reposition and close distance more effectively than walk-three configurations. The ER PPCs maintain long-range capability. Streak SRM-4s provide reliable close-range missile defence. The 400-rated engine maintenance is more complex than the 300-rated variant.

variants.name: KBO-7A
variants.overview: Diplan Mechyards introduced the Kabuto in 3059 on Aix-la-Chapelle for the DCMS, and the Chariot Type 1a endo steel chassis achieving impressive performance at 20 tons is the engineering achievement. The Streak SRM-4 focus on the original is an aggressive choice for a 20-ton design.

variants.name: CRK-5003-2
variants.overview: The Katana emerged from Operation Rosebud, ComStar's transfer of downgraded Crockett chassis to the Draconis Combine, and the shared Geometric 530 Hard Core chassis with the Crockett means structural maintenance knowledge transfers directly. The Combine's weapons reconfiguration creates the distinction between the designs.
variants.capabilities: The Crockett chassis commonality is the maintenance efficiency that DCMS units with both designs appreciate. The Strand 255 engine and base chassis maintenance are identical to the Crockett. The weapons reconfiguration for Combine service changes the weapons maintenance profile while leaving the structural work familiar. Five variants cover different DCMS weapons configurations on the shared platform.
variants.deployment: Five variants on the Crockett-derived chassis. The structural commonality with the Crockett is the practical maintenance advantage — techs who know the Crockett have no structural learning curve. DCMS and LAW parts for weapons-specific components; Crockett parts channels apply to chassis-level hardware. The Operation Rosebud origin means some early hull documentation may reference Crockett designations that were subsequently updated.

variants.name: KHP-7R
variants.overview: The Blessed Order developed the Kheper secretly in the mid-thirty-second century, and the ComStar renegade origin creates significant documentation and parts sourcing challenges. The Core Tek 275 XL in a NETC Kappa endo steel frame gives 86 kph at 55 tons for the First Division.
variants.capabilities: The Core Tek 275 XL is the performance foundation with the standard XL vulnerability concern. The NETC Kappa endo steel requires trained tech qualification for structural repairs. Single variant. The secretive development means documentation quality is variable — some systems are well-documented within Blessed Order technical manuals, others require examination-based reconstruction.
variants.deployment: Single configuration that entered service with the rebuilt First Division. The documentation gap from the secretive development is the primary maintenance challenge on non-standard systems. Build your own technical records from physical examination where documentation is absent. Parts sourcing through Blessed Order and former ComStar channels. The endo steel structural advisory applies consistently.

variants.name: KGC-000
variants.overview: Cosara Weaponries designed the King Crab in 2741 at General Kerensky's direct request for an assault 'Mech that could cripple other heavy designs at close range, and the twin Deathgiver AC/20s are the most direct expression of that mission brief in any assault design. Thirteen variants over the production run show the concept adapting across centuries.
variants.capabilities: Twin AC/20s are the most concentrated short-range ballistic firepower available and ammunition management is the critical operational factor — those cannons consume ammunition rapidly. The doctrine is simple and brutal: close quickly and fire everything. The ammunition bins determine how long the engagement can last. Thirteen variants cover development from the 2743 original through modern configurations.
variants.deployment: Thirteen variants from the 2743 original production through subsequent developments. The twin AC/20 ammunition management advisory is the loudest operational briefing — establish robust resupply or the engagement ends when bins empty. Cosara parts through various channels depending on variant era. The close-range assault doctrine requires pilots who understand that positioning for engagement range matters as much as the weapons themselves.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Snow Raven introduced the Kingfisher in 2887 as one of the pioneering second-generation OmniMechs, and the nine-ton pod space at 90 tons reflects early OmniMech technology limitations. Twelve configurations accumulated over the design's service life show extensive development of the reliable all-around assault platform.
variants.capabilities: The broad tactical spectrum capability rather than single-role specialization is the design's identity, and it delivers consistent performance across scenarios without excelling in any one. Nine tons of pod space is limited for an assault OmniMech but the configurations have been designed to make effective use of what's available. Snow Raven construction quality is consistently high. The 2887 origin means some older hulls have documentation reflecting earlier Clan manufacturing standards.
variants.deployment: Twelve configurations with Configuration A's ER PPC and LB 10-X combination covering long-to-medium range effectively. The limited pod space constrains configuration options more than on heavier pod-space designs — configuration selection matters more. Snow Raven parts support through their logistics network is reliable. The all-around capability makes this a good chassis for commanders who don't know what they'll face.

variants.name: KTO-19
variants.overview: General Dynamics introduced the Kintaro in 2587 as a specialized Narc missile beacon carrier for the SLDF, and the close-range beacon delivery mission defines everything about the design. Seven variants cover development from the original Narc specialist through adaptations that moved beyond that narrow role.
variants.capabilities: The Narc missile beacon system requires the Kintaro to close within short range to deliver the beacon, which means the armor needs to absorb hits during the approach. The beacon system itself requires specific maintenance knowledge different from standard missile launchers — the electromagnetic beacon components have their own calibration requirements. The SRM backup weapons support the close-range mission. Seven variants show the chassis evolving beyond pure Narc work.
variants.deployment: Seven variants from the 2587 Narc-specialist original through configurations that downplayed or abandoned the beacon role. The Narc system maintenance advisory applies to original and Narc-equipped variants — specialist knowledge required. General Dynamics parts through various channels depending on variant era. Later variants that replaced the Narc with conventional weapons are more straightforward to maintain and less operationally specialized.

variants.overview: Clan Ghost Bear introduced the Kodiak in 3001 as a second-line counterpart to the Executioner, and the 400-rated XL in a 100-ton chassis giving 64 kph is the same extraordinary performance foundation as the Iron Cheetah. Ghost Bear construction quality throughout. Six variants cover the design's development including significant field refit configurations.
variants.capabilities: 400-rated XL at 100 tons is genuinely impressive speed for the weight class and the XL vulnerability concern at this weight is the most serious possible — side torso damage on a 100-ton assault is catastrophic. Ghost Bear construction quality is high and consistent. The field refit variants show what Ghost Bear pilots actually wanted from the chassis once they had combat experience with it.
variants.deployment: Six variants including field refits that reflect actual combat feedback. The XL advisory at assault weight is the loudest briefing — it must be delivered to every Kodiak pilot without exception. Field refit variants may have documentation that reflects improvised solutions subsequently formalized — verify documentation completeness on refit hulls. Ghost Bear Dominion logistics support is reliable and well-organized.

variants.overview: The Ghost Bear Dominion developed the Kodiak II based on the fourth Kodiak variant, entering service in the early thirty-second century. The retained 400-rated XL maintains the original's performance identity while new technologies add resilience and lethality. Two variants cover the production and modernized configurations.
variants.capabilities: The 400-rated XL maintaining the original's 64 kph performance at 100 tons is the continuity with the base Kodiak. The advanced technologies on the later variant change specific component maintenance requirements. Alshain BattleWorx and Ghost Bear Dominion construction quality is consistently high.
variants.deployment: Two variants with the later variant's advanced technology improvements adding capability and maintenance complexity in proportion. The XL advisory is the universal constant across both variants. Ghost Bear Dominion logistics support is reliable. Techs familiar with the original Kodiak will find the Kodiak II structurally familiar — the maintenance learning curve is in the upgraded systems, not the chassis.
