variants.name: KIM-2
variants.overview: The Draconis Combine conceived the Komodo in 3051 specifically to hunt Clan Elementals following Operation Revival, and the ten medium lasers that define the design reflect exactly that mission brief. Four variants show the design adapting beyond the initial anti-Elemental focus.
variants.capabilities: Ten medium lasers provide overwhelming short-range firepower against small targets — effective against Elementals and effective against any 'Mech that closes to the same range. The heat management is the constraint; ten medium lasers firing simultaneously generates serious heat and pilots need discipline. The all-energy configuration means no ammunition concerns. Four variants with different laser and electronics configurations.
variants.deployment: Four variants from the pure anti-Elemental original through configurations with expanded tactical roles. The heat management advisory is universal — ten medium lasers require disciplined firing to avoid shutdown. DCMS parts through Combine channels is reliable. The anti-Elemental doctrine is the design identity but the weapons work equally well against any target at short range — brief pilots coming from more range-flexible designs on the engagement philosophy.

variants.name: KSC-3I
variants.overview: The Koschei entered service in 2504 as the Capellan Confederation's second BattleMech and the VOX 325 engine giving 86 kph to a 65-ton heavy is impressive for the era. Eight variants over the production run show the design adapting from the original primitive through post-Helm modern configurations.
variants.capabilities: 86 kph for a 65-ton heavy is genuine speed and the weapons array supports the aggressive strike role that speed enables. The original primitive construction is the historical maintenance challenge — modern procedures don't apply to primitive components. Post-Helm variants with modern technology are the operational standard. Eight variants span a significant technology gap that the specific variant determines.
variants.deployment: Eight variants from the 2504 primitive original through modern configurations. The primitive original requires primitive construction documentation — do not apply modern manuals. The post-Helm variants are the common operational case with full modern documentation. Capellan parts through various channels depending on variant technology era. The long production history means the modern variants are well-documented and supported.

Eight variants over the production run show the design adapting from the original primitive through post-Helm modern configurations.
variants.capabilities: 86 kph for a 65-ton heavy is genuine speed and the weapons array supports the aggressive strike role that speed enables. The original primitive construction is the historical maintenance challenge — modern procedures don't apply to primitive components. Post-Helm variants with modern technology are the operational standard. Eight variants span a significant technology gap that the specific variant determines.
variants.deployment: Eight variants from the 2504 primitive original through modern configurations. The primitive original requires primitive construction documentation — do not apply modern manuals. The post-Helm variants are the common operational case with full modern documentation. Capellan parts through various channels depending on variant technology era. The long production history means the modern variants are well-documented and supported.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Smoke Jaguar designed the Mist Lynx, known in IS records as the Koshi, in 2926 as a fast light scout and raider. The 175-rated Clan XL at twenty-five tons achieves walk seven, run ten with jump six capability. Eighteen OmniMech configurations make this the most extensively varied light OmniMech in Clan service, which is impressive but creates a significant pod inventory management burden.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump six. At twenty-five tons the XL engine vulnerability is proportionally severe: any significant hit to the side torsos ends the mission. Eighteen configurations means the maintenance tech needs familiarity with a wide variety of pod weapon types. The Light Series II endo steel structure requires specific technical qualification for structural repairs. Physical access inside the chassis is constrained by the small frame. Configuration A carries TAG, two anti-missile systems, a flamer, and two machine guns. This is the pure support and anti-infantry configuration. The TAG designates targets for guided munitions. The AMS pair provides missile defence for the warrior and nearby units. The flamer and machine guns handle infantry.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is a designation and anti-infantry platform. The dual AMS provides protection that the small chassis and XL engine cannot absorb on their own. Warriors in A configuration operate in support of heavier units, tagging targets and providing anti-infantry coverage. The combat value is indirect rather than direct.

The Light Series II endo steel structure requires specific technical qualification for structural repairs. Physical access inside the chassis is constrained by the small frame. Configuration B carries two ER medium lasers, two SRM-6 launchers, and an ER small laser. At twenty-five tons this is an aggressive close-range loadout. The SRM-6s deliver volume fire at point-blank range and burn through ammunition quickly. The ER mediums provide range backup. Two tons of SRM ammunition is the operational limit.
variants.deployment: Configuration B is the brawler variant, built to close range fast using walk seven speed and deliver SRM-6 volume fire. Warriors in B configuration accept the XL vulnerability and trust their speed to avoid the worst of it. The ER mediums carry the fight when ammunition runs dry. This configuration suits warriors who prefer close-range decisive engagements.

variants.deployment: Configuration C is the long-range energy sniper variant. The AMS prevents missile spam from being the straightforward counter. One of the cleaner Koshi configurations to maintain.

Warriors must manage heat carefully: firing all seven heavy lasers at once on a twenty-five ton chassis with twelve heat sinks is a rapid path to shutdown. The light TAG adds utility beyond the direct combat role.

Against BattleMechs it has almost no relevant capability. The ER small lasers are the anti-armour backup and they are modest at best. Warriors assigned G configuration are doing anti-infantry work and nothing else. The ammunition management across so many machine gun feeds is the primary maintenance burden.

Warriors in I configuration need to close range to use the Narc, which requires accepting the XL vulnerability the speed is supposed to avoid.

The improved heavy medium laser handles anything that closes while the ER PPC cycles. Warriors who try to fire both systems together regularly will shut down. Warriors who use them in disciplined sequence get genuine punch from a twenty-five ton machine.

This is not a specialist configuration but it handles a broad range of scout and skirmisher scenarios adequately.

variants.overview: Clan Diamond Shark developed the standard non-OmniMech Koshi as a simplified production variant of the Mist Lynx, and the fixed configuration trades OmniMech flexibility for manufacturing and maintenance simplicity. The core performance characteristics of the Mist Lynx carry over completely.
variants.capabilities: The Mist Lynx performance profile — 25-ton fast light — carries over without the OmniMech pod system overhead. The fixed configuration means no pod maintenance but also no reconfiguration capability. Two variants cover different fixed weapons configurations. Diamond Shark construction quality is consistently high. The simplification genuinely makes routine maintenance faster and easier than the OmniMech original.
variants.deployment: Two variants with the 3095 Koshi 2 replacing SRM launchers with Streak SRM-6s for ammunition efficiency improvement. Fixed configuration simplifies logistics planning — one parts list, no pod inventory. Diamond Shark parts through their trade network channels. The simplification trade-off is explicit — if you need OmniMech flexibility, use the Mist Lynx. If you need a maintainable fast light without the pod complexity, the Standard Koshi delivers.

variants.overview: Clan Diamond Shark developed the standard non-OmniMech Koshi as a simplified production variant of the Mist Lynx, and the fixed configuration trades OmniMech flexibility for manufacturing and maintenance simplicity. The core performance characteristics of the Mist Lynx carry over completely.
variants.capabilities: The Mist Lynx performance profile — 25-ton fast light — carries over without the OmniMech pod system overhead. The fixed configuration means no pod maintenance but also no reconfiguration capability. Two variants cover different fixed weapons configurations. Diamond Shark construction quality is consistently high. The simplification genuinely makes routine maintenance faster and easier than the OmniMech original.
variants.deployment: Two variants with the 3095 Koshi 2 replacing SRM launchers with Streak SRM-6s for ammunition efficiency improvement. Fixed configuration simplifies logistics planning — one parts list, no pod inventory. Diamond Shark parts through their trade network channels. The simplification trade-off is explicit — if you need OmniMech flexibility, use the Mist Lynx. If you need a maintainable fast light without the pod complexity, the Standard Koshi delivers.

variants.name: KT-P2
variants.overview: Omnitech Industries built the Koto for the Solaris VII arena circuit around 3052, designed for first-strike decisive blows. Twenty-five tons, walk eight, run twelve on the 200-rated XL engine. Four variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at twenty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. Walk eight is the survival mechanism. Arena construction throughout. The KT-P2 prototype carries a large pulse laser, two machine guns, and a small laser. Walk eight, run twelve. The large pulse laser is the primary weapon. Machine guns handle infantry and targets in the close arena environments. The small laser provides point-blank backup.
variants.deployment: The KT-P2 is the original prototype from 3052. The large pulse laser first-strike concept is the design intent. Arena combat means opponents are always at close range. The machine guns handle any arena obstacle. Prototype documentation applies.

variants.name: KTO-2A
variants.overview: Omnitech Industries built the Koto for the Solaris VII arena circuit around 3052, designed for first-strike decisive blows. Twenty-five tons, walk eight, run twelve on the 200-rated XL engine. Four variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at twenty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. Walk eight is the survival mechanism. Arena construction throughout. The KTO-2A carries a large X-pulse laser, two ER medium lasers, and an ER small laser. Walk eight, run twelve. The large X-pulse laser is accurate at medium range. The ER mediums provide additional energy fire. The ER small laser handles point-blank.
variants.deployment: The 2A upgrades to X-pulse accuracy and extends energy range. The large X-pulse laser at walk eight speed creates a consistent medium-range threat. The ER mediums add energy volume. The ER small laser closes the range bands. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: KTO-3A
variants.overview: Omnitech Industries built the Koto for the Solaris VII arena circuit around 3052, designed for first-strike decisive blows. Twenty-five tons, walk eight, run twelve on the 200-rated XL engine. Four variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at twenty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. Walk eight is the survival mechanism. Arena construction throughout. The KTO-3A carries a large pulse laser, two medium lasers, and a small laser. Walk eight, run twelve. The large pulse laser provides the primary close-range fire. The medium lasers add energy volume. The small laser handles point-blank. An endo steel upgrade over the prototype.
variants.deployment: The 3A is the production upgrade of the prototype concept with endo steel construction. The large pulse laser primary is preserved. The medium lasers supplement the close-range energy output. Endo steel reduces structural mass. Walk eight remains the survival mechanism.

variants.name: KTO-4A
variants.overview: Omnitech Industries built the Koto for the Solaris VII arena circuit around 3052, designed for first-strike decisive blows. Twenty-five tons, walk eight, run twelve on the 200-rated XL engine. Four variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at twenty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. Walk eight is the survival mechanism. Arena construction throughout. The KTO-4A carries an ER PPC, two ER medium lasers, and an ER small laser. Walk eight, run twelve. The ER PPC extends the engagement range substantially beyond the pulse laser variants. The ER mediums add energy volume. The ER small laser handles close threats.
variants.deployment: The 4A is the long-range Koto. The ER PPC at walk eight creates a genuine long-range threat that opponents cannot ignore. The ER mediums handle anything at medium and close range. The arena doctrine changes significantly — this variant operates at different distances than the close-range pulse laser configurations.

variants.overview: The Bane, called the Kraken in IS intelligence reports, was first constructed in 2827 based on plans shared between Clans Wolf and Ghost Bear. The ten Ultra AC/2 base configuration stands as the most unusual weapons array on any assault 'Mech in service. Walk three, run four on a 300-rated Clan XL at a hundred tons. Six variants show substantial tactical philosophy variation across the family.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four. The XL engine at a hundred tons carries the standard catastrophic side torso vulnerability. Variant 2 replaces the ten Ultra AC/2s with four Ultra AC/10s and four machine guns. Four weapons to track instead of ten, with the UC/10s delivering far more damage per shot. Four tons of AC/10 ammunition per gun requires careful management on extended operations. The machine guns handle infantry.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 is the brawler version of the Kraken concept, trading the base configuration's extreme range and ammunition volume for concentrated medium-range firepower. The four UC/10s on double-tap at close range is a significant damage output from a hundred-ton chassis. The machine guns make approaching infantry uncomfortable. Warriors who find the base configuration's ammunition management burdensome find the 2 more workable.

variants.overview: The Bane, called the Kraken in IS intelligence reports, was first constructed in 2827 based on plans shared between Clans Wolf and Ghost Bear. The ten Ultra AC/2 base configuration stands as the most unusual weapons array on any assault 'Mech in service. Walk three, run four on a 300-rated Clan XL at a hundred tons. Six variants show substantial tactical philosophy variation across the family.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four. The XL engine at a hundred tons carries the standard catastrophic side torso vulnerability. Variant 3 carries eight LRM-15 launchers and a one-shot Streak SRM-4. Eight LRM-15s at a hundred tons delivers the most sustained indirect fire output available on any assault platform in the Clan inventory. Sixteen tons of LRM ammunition provides meaningful operational endurance. The Streak SRM-4 is a close-range emergency measure, not a combat weapon.
variants.deployment: Variant 3 is the fire support configuration. Eight LRM-15s delivering simultaneous volleys creates incoming fire that most opponents cannot manage defensively. The range and ammunition supply mean Variant 3 can sustain indirect fire throughout an engagement that would exhaust a smaller platform. It has almost no close-range capability beyond the one-shot SRM. It needs escorts.

The ten Ultra AC/2 base configuration stands as the most unusual weapons array on any assault 'Mech in service. Walk three, run four on a 300-rated Clan XL at a hundred tons. Six variants show substantial tactical philosophy variation across the family.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four. The XL engine at a hundred tons carries the standard catastrophic side torso vulnerability. Variant 4 carries two Ultra AC/20s, three ATM-6 launchers, and an ER large laser. The twin Ultra AC/20s in double-tap mode at close range deliver devastation few opponents can absorb. The ATM-6s add tactical missile flexibility across three munition types. Ammunition management across three different system types requires pre-mission planning.
variants.deployment: Variant 4 is built for close-range assault. The Ultra AC/20s in double-tap mode at assault range is the most direct statement the Kraken family makes. Warriors close range using the ER large laser to suppress return fire, then deliver the AC/20 and ATM combination at close quarters. Ammunition management across three different system types requires pre-mission planning.

variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four. The XL engine at a hundred tons carries the standard catastrophic side torso vulnerability. Variant 5 carries four Rotary AC/2s, two LRM-10s, and an ER large laser. The four Rotary AC/2s provide high-rate sustained ballistic fire. The LRM-10s add indirect fire capability. The ER large laser handles direct fire at extended range. Rotary AC ammunition management across four systems requires careful tracking.
variants.deployment: Variant 5 is a sustained fire platform that uses the Rotary AC/2 volume to maintain constant pressure on opponents. The four Rotaries combined with the LRM-10s create a difficult defensive situation for anything in range. Rotary AC ammunition management across four systems requires careful tracking. The ER large laser engages while the Rotaries are reloading.

The ten Ultra AC/2 base configuration stands as the most unusual weapons array on any assault 'Mech in service. Walk three, run four on a 300-rated Clan XL at a hundred tons. Six variants show substantial tactical philosophy variation across the family.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four. The XL engine at a hundred tons carries the standard catastrophic side torso vulnerability. Variant 6 carries ten ProtoMech AC/2s and four ER medium lasers. The ProtoMech weapons are lighter and more ammunition-efficient than standard AC/2s but deliver less damage per projectile. Ammunition management across ten individual ProtoMech AC feeds is a maintenance challenge comparable to the base configuration.
variants.deployment: Variant 6 updates the original ten-small-weapon concept using ProtoMech-derived autocannons. The ProtoMech AC/2s are more ammunition-efficient than standard AC/2s and the four ER mediums add close-range energy capability the base configuration lacked. The ten-weapon maintenance burden still applies, though the ProtoMech systems are less demanding than standard AC/2 mechanisms. The ER mediums provide genuine backup when the ProtoMech ACs run dry.

variants.overview: The Bane, called the Kraken in IS intelligence reports, was first constructed in 2827 based on plans shared between Clans Wolf and Ghost Bear. The ten Ultra AC/2 base configuration stands as the most unusual weapons array on any assault 'Mech in service. Walk three, run four on a 300-rated Clan XL at a hundred tons. Six variants show substantial tactical philosophy variation across the family.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four. The XL engine at a hundred tons carries the standard catastrophic side torso vulnerability. Variant 7 carries two HAG/40s, a large pulse laser, and four ER medium lasers. Twin HAG/40s on a hundred-ton chassis is an extreme ballistic payload. The HAG/40 spreads projectiles across multiple armour locations simultaneously. The large pulse laser and ER mediums provide energy fire across the engagement. HAG/40 ammunition management is substantial.
variants.deployment: Variant 7 is a maximum-damage ballistic platform. The twin HAG/40s create armour disruption across wide target areas that makes follow-up fire from accompanying units substantially more effective. The large pulse laser and ER medium energy suite provides sustained output between HAG reloads. Warriors who understand HAG spread patterns and use them against heavily armoured targets get the most from this variant.

variants.overview: Alshain BattleWorx introduced the Kuma in 3082 for the Ghost Bear Dominion as potentially the most mobile heavy BattleMech ever produced. The 360 Type II extralight engine — a powerplant more typical of lighter designs — in a 60-ton chassis creates extraordinary speed for the weight class.
variants.capabilities: The 360 Type II extralight engine is the most technically unusual feature. Extralight engines have different maintenance characteristics from standard XL systems — not dramatically different but specific enough that tech familiarity with XL maintenance doesn't fully transfer. The speed is genuinely exceptional for a heavy. Three variants with the Kuma 2 trading some mobility for combat versatility through jump jets.
variants.deployment: Three variants with the 3083 Kuma 2 being the first significant adaptation. The extralight engine maintenance specifics are the technical advisory — confirm your techs have specific extralight engine documentation rather than applying standard XL procedures. Alshain BattleWorx and Ghost Bear Dominion parts support is reliable. Brief pilots that this machine's speed advantage is the primary tactical asset — use it or choose a different chassis.

variants.name: KY2-D-01
variants.overview: Martinson Armaments introduced the Kyudo in 2443 as the Terran Hegemony's second production BattleMech, lighter and faster than the Mackie that preceded it. The primitive technology throughout reflects mid-twenty-third century manufacturing capabilities. Three variants span from the primitive original through modern adaptations.
variants.capabilities: The Conan/20 LRM is the primary weapon and the fire-support mission profile suits the design. The original primitive construction requires primitive documentation and procedures — nothing about the 2443 original is maintained from modern manuals. The three variants span a significant technology gap: primitive original to modern production is a complete maintenance philosophy change depending on which hull you have.
variants.deployment: Three variants from the 2443 primitive original through modern configurations. The primitive advisory on the original KY2-D-01 is absolute — primitive construction documentation, primitive procedures, field fabrication for components. Modern variants are conventionally maintained. Know which variant you have before any maintenance work. Martinson and successor parts support varies significantly by variant era.

variants.name: LMT-2R
variants.overview: Skobel MechWorks built the Lament on Terra for the Republic Armed Forces, presented a few years before the 3130s conflict began, and the twin Magna Supernova Heavy PPCs are the design's centerpiece and most demanding maintenance focus. Six variants show the design adapting to Republic operational requirements.
variants.capabilities: Twin Heavy PPCs are impressive firepower requiring specific maintenance knowledge — heavy PPC systems have different thermal and power characteristics from standard or ER PPC. Two heavy PPC capacitor and power regulation systems running simultaneously multiply the maintenance requirement. The heavy PPC firing characteristics require specific pilot training. Six variants cover different supporting weapons configurations on the same heavy PPC foundation.
variants.deployment: Six variants with the base production model entering RAF service after the 3127 appropriations cycle. The dual heavy PPC maintenance advisory is the consistent technical note across all heavy PPC-equipped variants. Confirm your techs have specific heavy PPC training — this is not a procedure that transfers from standard PPC experience alone. Skobel and former Terra facility parts support through post-Jihad Republic channels.

variants.name: LNC25-01
variants.overview: Krupp Stellar Technologies designed the Lancelot in 2581 for the SLDF as a fast self-sufficient striker, and the Kinslaughter PPC with dual Krupp large lasers creates an all-energy loadout that suits extended independent operations. Eleven variants show the design adapting from Star League through Succession War technology constraints.
variants.capabilities: The all-energy weapons mean no ammunition concerns for independent operations, which suited the original SLDF brief. Heat management across PPC and dual large laser requires consistent pilot discipline. Eleven variants include downgraded versions reflecting Succession War technology loss — know which era's technology your specific hull uses before applying any manual.
variants.deployment: Eleven variants from the 2581 SLDF original through Succession War and modern configurations. The technology era of the specific variant determines the maintenance approach — Star League original, downgraded Succession War, and modern rebuilt variants have meaningfully different maintenance profiles. Krupp and successor manufacturer parts through various channels. The heat management advisory applies across all energy-weapon configurations in the family.

variants.name: LHU-2B
variants.overview: Sun-Tzu Liao's Xin Sheng program produced the Lao Hu in 3062, designed by a Victoria Academy student and built at Shengli Arms. The Chariot Type II Endo Steel chassis with GM 375 XL gives 86 kph at 70 tons, and the LB 20-X autocannon focus reflects aggressive Capellan tactical doctrine.
variants.capabilities: The GM 375 XL gives competitive heavy speed with the standard XL vulnerability concern. The Shengli LB 20-X is quality hardware but the variable munitions feed requires regular cleaning and function testing — the ammunition selection mechanism is a failure point that deferred maintenance accelerates. The Zeus LRM-15 provides range flexibility. Five variants cover different weapons configurations on the Chariot chassis.
variants.deployment: Five variants from the 3062 original through subsequent configurations. The LB 20-X ammunition selection mechanism advisory is the consistent weapons maintenance note. The XL advisory applies consistently. Shengli parts through Capellan channels is reliable. The Xin Sheng program origin gives these machines cultural significance in CCAF service similar to the Jinggau — they're valued beyond their tactical utility.

variants.name: LGC-01
variants.overview: Skobel MechWorks built the Legacy on Terra at Word of Blake Precentor Martial Cameron St. Jamais' direction, and the Skobel Template 8 endo steel frame with Pitban 240 standard engine is a deliberate survivability-first design philosophy — standard engine rather than XL, prioritizing damage tolerance over speed.
variants.capabilities: The standard engine rather than XL changes the damage vulnerability profile significantly — the Legacy is more survivable when things go wrong than comparable XL-equipped assaults. The trade-off is speed performance. The twin Mydron Excel Ultra AC/10s are the primary weapons and ultra autocannon mechanism maintenance is the consistent technical focus. Five variants cover different weapons configurations.
variants.deployment: Five variants with the base LGC-01 as the networked fire-support reference. The ultra AC/10 mechanism maintenance advisory applies to all Ultra-equipped variants — keep the mechanism clean and service on schedule. The standard engine damage resilience advantage is worth communicating to pilots. Skobel and former Blakist parts through post-Jihad channels. The networkded C3 system requires specialist calibration personnel.

variants.name: LGN-1X
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises developed the Legionnaire during the Word of Blake occupation of New Avalon, and the Magna 350 XL in a 2A Type 15 endo steel chassis gives 118 kph at 50 tons — exceptional speed for the weight class. Eight variants show extensive development from the original scout concept through combat configurations.
variants.capabilities: 118 kph at 50 tons is genuinely fast and the XL enabling that speed brings the standard vulnerability concern — at this velocity a side torso breach is a serious problem very quickly. The endo steel structure requires trained tech qualification for structural repairs. The rotary AC/2 on the original prototype is different from the production rotary AC/5 in its mechanism maintenance requirements. Eight variants cover significant tactical variety.
variants.deployment: Eight variants from the 3068 scout prototype through combat configurations. The XL advisory is the universal briefing. The rotary autocannon mechanism maintenance applies to all rotary-equipped variants — more complex than standard, more sensitive to contamination, keep cleaning cycles current. The endo steel structural advisory applies consistently. Corean parts through Federated Suns channels is reliable.

variants.name: UABM-2R
variants.overview: The Word of Blake developed the Lich as a quad drone assault during the final Jihad years, and the Republic of the Sphere subsequently adapted it for production. The Endo-Composite skeleton is the unusual structural choice and the drone control systems add a layer of maintenance complexity beyond standard 'Mech systems.
variants.capabilities: Endo-Composite structure requires specific repair knowledge different from standard endo steel and standard composite separately. The drone control systems need regular calibration and software updates — autonomous operation hardware has maintenance requirements that piloted designs don't have. The 270-rated XL at 90 tons gives 32 kph — deliberately slow for maximum weapons payload. Quad maintenance overhead applies throughout.
variants.deployment: Single configuration that the Republic adapted from the Blakist original for their 3140 production. The drone systems maintenance is the specialist requirement — assign personnel specifically qualified on autonomous control systems, not general electronics techs. The Endo-Composite structural advisory applies. Republic and former Blakist parts through post-Jihad channels. Quad-qualified techs are required throughout.

variants.name: LHN-C5
variants.overview: Ceres Metals designed the Lightning on Capella for the CCAF with two devastating long-range weapons as the design concept, and the Improved Heavy Gauss Rifle and Heavy Particle Cannon combination is the most technically demanding weapons pairing I've seen on a single chassis. Single variant with no factory alternatives.
variants.capabilities: The Improved Heavy Gauss Rifle and Heavy Particle Cannon both require specific maintenance knowledge beyond standard systems — the Improved Heavy Gauss capacitor system differs from standard Gauss, and the Heavy PPC has different thermal characteristics from standard PPC. Two demanding weapons systems on one chassis means two separate specialist maintenance requirements simultaneously. The weapons dominate the maintenance schedule.
variants.deployment: Single configuration. The dual specialist weapons maintenance requirement is the defining advisory — you need personnel specifically trained on Improved Heavy Gauss and Heavy PPC systems, ideally the same tech who knows both. Ceres Metals parts through Capellan channels. The CCAF deploys these primarily against high-value targets where the extreme long-range precision justifies the maintenance overhead.

variants.name: LGH-4Y
variants.overview: Martinson Armaments built the Lightray on Terra for the Word of Blake at Precentor Martial direction, and the LTV 385 XL in a 55-ton chassis achieving extraordinary speed is the performance headline. The targeting computer technology secured through ROM intelligence operations is the electronics distinction.
variants.capabilities: The LTV 385 XL pushing 55 tons to exceptional speed is the design achievement and the XL vulnerability at this velocity is the standard concern. The targeting computer improves weapons accuracy and requires specialist calibration beyond standard weapons systems. Five variants cover different weapons configurations from the pre-targeting computer original through subsequent developments.
variants.deployment: Five variants with the original predating the targeting computer and subsequent variants incorporating it. The targeting computer calibration advisory applies to equipped variants — specialist knowledge required. The XL advisory is universal. Post-Jihad Martinson and Blakist parts sourcing through former Terra channels. The ROM-acquired targeting computer technology on later variants has specific sourcing complications post-Jihad.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Wolf commissioned the Linebacker in 3052 to address a gap in their heavy OmniMech roster, wanting the Timber Wolf's firepower in a faster chassis. The Heavy Force 390-rated XL achieving 97 kph at 65 tons delivers on that brief and the eleven configurations reflect extensive Clan Wolf exploitation of the fast heavy concept.
variants.capabilities: 97 kph at 65 tons is exceptional for a heavy OmniMech and the XL enabling that speed carries the standard vulnerability concern — at this velocity a side torso breach is serious. The OmniMech pod system is well-implemented. Eleven configurations means substantial pod inventory requirements. Clan Wolf construction quality is consistently excellent. The speed advantage is genuine and tactically significant.
variants.deployment: Eleven configurations with Configuration A's paired ER Large Lasers mirroring the Timber Wolf Prime's philosophy. The XL advisory applies universally — every Linebacker pilot needs that briefing. Pod maintenance across eleven configurations requires robust parts inventory management. Clan Wolf parts support is reliable. The speed is what distinguishes this from the Timber Wolf; configurations that don't exploit that advantage are suboptimal for this chassis.

variants.capabilities: 97 kph at 65 tons is exceptional for a heavy OmniMech and the XL enabling that speed carries the standard vulnerability concern — at this velocity a side torso breach is serious. The OmniMech pod system is well-implemented. Eleven configurations means substantial pod inventory requirements. Clan Wolf construction quality is consistently excellent. The speed advantage is genuine and tactically significant.
variants.deployment: Eleven configurations with Configuration A's paired ER Large Lasers mirroring the Timber Wolf Prime's philosophy. The XL advisory applies universally — every Linebacker pilot needs that briefing. Pod maintenance across eleven configurations requires robust parts inventory management. Clan Wolf parts support is reliable. The speed is what distinguishes this from the Timber Wolf; configurations that don't exploit that advantage are suboptimal for this chassis.

variants.name: KW1-LH2
variants.overview: Kressly Warworks introduced the Lineholder in 3058 from their Epsilon Eridani facility using Common Soldier Initiative specifications, and the result is exactly what that program intended — a garrison 'Mech that any reasonably equipped depot can maintain. The Core Tek 275 engine in a standard Kressly chassis is the definition of field-maintainable.
variants.capabilities: The deliberate simplicity is the whole point and it works. Standard construction throughout, well-documented components, nothing exotic anywhere in the design. The weapons mix is adequate for garrison work without trying to be anything it isn't. Five variants show modest development without losing the maintainability philosophy. Parts are available almost everywhere the Chaos March and successor states can reach.
variants.deployment: Five variants, all maintaining the low-cost maintainable philosophy. The base model is genuinely found in almost every garrison — if you haven't worked on one you will. The simplicity means new techs can handle most maintenance after basic training. Kressly Warworks parts through Chaos March and various successor state channels. The design does exactly what it promises and nothing more.

variants.overview: Clan Wolf developed the Lobo around 3059 as a lighter faster companion to the Timber Wolf, and the Type-A endo steel chassis with General Systems 240 XL achieves 97 kph at 40 tons. The Jihad-era anti-infantry variant shows the design adapting to specific operational requirements.
variants.capabilities: 97 kph for a 40-ton medium is fast and the XL concern applies at this velocity. The endo steel structure requires trained tech qualification for structural repairs. Two variants with the Jihad-era configuration being a significant departure from the base concept. Wolf construction quality is consistently solid.
variants.deployment: Two variants with the Jihad-era anti-infantry loadout representing a specific operational adaptation. The XL advisory applies to both configurations. The endo steel structural advisory is consistent. Wolf parts support through their logistics channels. The speed advantage is the tactical identity — brief pilots that this machine wins by maintaining distance and exploiting speed rather than standing and trading.

variants.name: LCT-1V
variants.overview: The Locust has been in continuous production since 2499 and I have lost count of how many I have worked on across the years. Twenty tons, walk eight, run twelve on the 160-rated engine. The design philosophy has not changed in five centuries: fast enough to avoid being hit, armed well enough to sting when it cannot. Twenty-four variants make this the most extensively documented light BattleMech family in existence.
variants.capabilities: Speed is the armour. The Locust's physical protection is minimal and any pilot who forgets that does not last long. The standard engine means side torso hits are survivable, unlike XL-equipped variants. The chin-turret on some configurations provides arc flexibility that arm-mounted weapons cannot match, but the turret mechanism needs regular maintenance attention or it binds under field conditions. Parts are available everywhere for every variant. The 1V is the original production model: a medium laser in the chin turret and two machine guns, on a standard 160-rated engine. The chin turret gives the medium laser a firing arc flexibility that surprised many opponents in the early production years. The machine guns handle infantry. Nothing about the loadout is impressive. Everything about the speed is.
variants.deployment: The 1V is the reference configuration and still the most commonly encountered Locust in militia and garrison service. It does what it was built to do: scouts, harasses, and runs away. Pilots who treat it as a combatant get killed. Pilots who treat it as a fast set of eyes with a modest self-defence capability keep operating it indefinitely.

variants.name: LCT-1S
variants.overview: The Locust has been in continuous production since 2499 and I have lost count of how many I have worked on across the years. Twenty tons, walk eight, run twelve on the 160-rated engine. The design philosophy has not changed in five centuries: fast enough to avoid being hit, armed well enough to sting when it cannot. Twenty-four variants make this the most extensively documented light BattleMech family in existence.
variants.capabilities: Speed is the armour. The Locust's physical protection is minimal and any pilot who forgets that does not last long. The standard engine means side torso hits are survivable, unlike XL-equipped variants. The chin-turret on some configurations provides arc flexibility that arm-mounted weapons cannot match, but the turret mechanism needs regular maintenance attention or it binds under field conditions. Parts are available everywhere for every variant. The 1S replaces the machine guns with two SRM-2 launchers. The SRMs add close-range missile punch that the machine guns lack against armoured targets. One ton of SRM ammunition is the operational limit. The medium laser remains the primary weapon. The SRMs are there for when the machine has to fight rather than run.
variants.deployment: The 1S sees use in roles where infantry engagement is less likely than armoured contact. The SRM-2s give the pilot a response to light 'Mechs and vehicles that the 1V's machine guns could not threaten meaningfully. It remains a scout and skirmisher. The SRM ammunition management adds one more thing to track on a machine that is supposed to be simple.

variants.name: LCT-1M
variants.overview: The Locust has been in continuous production since 2499 and I have lost count of how many I have worked on across the years. Twenty tons, walk eight, run twelve on the 160-rated engine. The design philosophy has not changed in five centuries: fast enough to avoid being hit, armed well enough to sting when it cannot. Twenty-four variants make this the most extensively documented light BattleMech family in existence.
variants.capabilities: Speed is the armour. The Locust's physical protection is minimal and any pilot who forgets that does not last long. The chin-turret on some configurations provides arc flexibility that arm-mounted weapons cannot match, but the turret mechanism needs regular maintenance attention or it binds under field conditions. Parts are available everywhere for every variant. The 1M carries two LRM-5 launchers and a medium laser. LRMs on a twenty-ton scout is a different tactical philosophy: engage at range, deliver indirect fire support, and use speed to stay out of trouble. One ton of LRM ammunition is the operational limit. The medium laser backs up the LRMs at close range. Heat is not a concern with this loadout.
variants.deployment: The 1M is the fire support variant of the Locust family. It contributes LRM fire from stand-off range while moving too fast for most units to effectively target. The medium laser handles anything that closes. One ton of LRM ammunition is not a lot for a fire support mission so pilots manage it carefully.

variants.name: LCT-1Vb
variants.overview: The Locust has been in continuous production since 2499 and I have lost count of how many I have worked on across the years. Twenty tons, walk eight, run twelve on the 160-rated engine. The design philosophy has not changed in five centuries: fast enough to avoid being hit, armed well enough to sting when it cannot. variants.capabilities: Speed is the armour. The Locust's physical protection is minimal and any pilot who forgets that does not last long. Parts are available everywhere for every variant. The 1Vb swaps to a 160-rated XL engine and loads two medium pulse lasers, two small pulse lasers, and a medium laser. The pulse laser accuracy at close range suits the Locust's high-speed engagement style. The XL engine changes the survivability profile: side torso hits that the standard engine shrugs off become fatal. Heat is manageable across the pulse laser loadout.
variants.deployment: The 1Vb is the pulse laser upgrade of the standard configuration. The accuracy improvement at close range is real and the heat management is clean. The XL engine vulnerability is the tradeoff that every pilot in a 1Vb needs to understand before they take a hit. It is faster to lose than the standard engine variant.

variants.overview: The Locust has been in continuous production since 2499 and I have lost count of how many I have worked on across the years. variants.deployment: The 1E is an energy weapons upgrade that removes the machine gun anti-infantry capability in favour of better anti-armour performance. It suits operations where infantry is not the primary threat and ammunition resupply is uncertain. The all-energy loadout simplifies logistics. The dual medium laser punch is more useful against most targets a Locust actually fights than the machine gun alternative.

variants.deployment: The C configuration is straightforward to maintain and operate. The mixed Clan-derived and IS weapons add a small maintenance complexity over a pure IS configuration but nothing demanding. It works as a light striker and harasser, using Locust speed to control engagement range and the pulse laser accuracy to make shots count.

variants.name: LCT-3V
variants.overview: The Locust has been in continuous production since 2499 and I have lost count of how many I have worked on across the years. variants.capabilities: Speed is the armour. The Locust's physical protection is minimal and any pilot who forgets that does not last long. variants.deployment: The 3V is the straightforward improvement over the 1V: one more medium laser, same machine guns, same engine. It deploys in the same scout and skirmisher roles with marginally better direct fire capability. The improved weapons fit over the 1V is useful but not transformative. Still a fast platform that survives by not getting hit.

variants.name: LCT-1L
variants.overview: The Locust has been in continuous production since 2499 and I have lost count of how many I have worked on across the years. The 1L is a licence-produced variant from Luthien Armor Works, functionally identical to the 1V in weapons loadout: two machine guns and a medium laser on a standard 160-rated engine. variants.deployment: The 1L performs identically to the 1V in the field. The manufacturing origin matters for maintenance: LAW and General Mechanics components are not always interchangeable and mixing them creates tolerance issues in critical assemblies. Know which variant you have and stock the correct replacement parts. The tactical role is identical to the 1V.

variants.deployment: The 3D is used as a pure indirect fire support scout. It moves fast, stays out of trouble, and contributes LRM fire from range. Having no backup weapon means any pilot forced into a direct engagement is in serious difficulty. This configuration needs reliable escorts or exceptional terrain awareness from its pilot.

variants.overview: The Locust has been in continuous production since 2499 and I have lost count of how many I have worked on across the years. The Streak systems fire only on lock, which preserves the limited one-ton ammunition supply but means the pilot cannot fire into uncertain target situations. The medium laser is the backup when no lock is available. Heat management is clean across this loadout.
variants.deployment: The 3S is a tracker variant, using the Streak lock requirement to ensure missile ammunition is not wasted on evasive targets. It suits pilots who prefer precision over volume. The Streak lock requirement is a tactical discipline that some pilots find frustrating and others find freeing. The medium laser handles everything the Streaks cannot engage.

Parts are available everywhere for every variant. The 3M carries four small lasers, a medium laser, and an anti-missile system. The AMS provides genuine missile defence for a machine that cannot absorb many hits. Four small lasers add close-range volume alongside the medium. Heat across all five laser weapons simultaneously is aggressive but the AMS ammunition is the more pressing management task.
variants.deployment: The 3M is the AMS-equipped variant, most useful in environments where enemy missile fire is a consistent threat. The AMS ammunition is limited and requires tracking. The four small lasers provide reasonable close-range firepower for a twenty-ton machine. This variant is more survivable against missile-heavy opposition than the standard configuration.

Four RL-10s provide a single large volley of forty rockets, then the machine has only its medium laser remaining. The alpha strike potential from the four RL-10s is high for a twenty-ton machine. After that, it is just a fast platform with a medium laser.
variants.deployment: The 1V2 is a single-use ambush variant. The tactical plan is simple: approach fast, deliver the four RL-10 alpha strike, withdraw. After that volley the combat contribution drops to the medium laser. Pilots who set up the ambush correctly get one very effective engagement. Pilots who fire the rockets at the wrong moment are left with a medium laser for the rest of the battle.

variants.name: LCT-5M
variants.overview: The Locust has been in continuous production since 2499 and I have lost count of how many I have worked on across the years. Twenty tons, walk eight, run twelve on the 160-rated engine. The design philosophy has not changed in five centuries: fast enough to avoid being hit, armed well enough to sting when it cannot. Twenty-four variants make this the most extensively documented light BattleMech family in existence.
variants.capabilities: Speed is the armour. The Locust's physical protection is minimal and any pilot who forgets that does not last long. The standard engine means side torso hits are survivable, unlike XL-equipped variants. The chin-turret on some configurations provides arc flexibility that arm-mounted weapons cannot match, but the turret mechanism needs regular maintenance attention or it binds under field conditions. Parts are available everywhere for every variant. The 5M swaps to a 240-rated XL engine, pushing the Locust to walk twelve, run eighteen. That speed is remarkable on a twenty-ton machine and it changes the tactical calculus entirely. The weapons are four ER small lasers and an ER medium laser. The XL engine vulnerability is severe at this weight: side torso damage is fatal. What keeps this machine alive is that almost nothing can hit it.
variants.deployment: The 5M is the fastest Locust in the production family and one of the fastest BattleMechs ever fielded. Walk twelve, run eighteen means the pilot chooses every engagement on their own terms. The ER weapons extend effective range beyond the standard configuration. The XL engine makes any hit to the side torso fatal, which is a significant vulnerability for a machine that depends entirely on not being hit.

variants.overview: Clan Mongoose introduced the Locust IIC in 2832 as a Clan-technology upgrade of the IS Locust, drawing from dwindling SLDF Royal Locust supplies. The Clan construction quality throughout delivers meaningfully more capability than the IS original. Nine variants show Clan exploitation of the fast ultralight concept across multiple configurations.
variants.capabilities: The Clan technology upgrade makes every system more efficient while retaining the original's speed-as-armor philosophy. At the Locust IIC's weight class any significant battle damage creates proportionally serious problems — there's minimal redundancy. Nine variants cover different tactical approaches from missile focus to laser configurations. The XL enabling the speed carries the standard vulnerability concern amplified by the small chassis.
variants.deployment: Nine variants including Jade Falcon adaptations with Streak SRM launchers. The XL advisory applies universally. At this weight class, the speed is genuinely the armor — pilots who try to absorb hits in a Locust IIC are misunderstanding their assignment. Clan parts support through the manufacturing Clan's channels. The nine-configuration variety means diverse maintenance profiles; know which configuration you're supporting.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Hell's Horses introduced the Hellbringer — Inner Sphere designation Loki — in 2926 after losing Tokasha MechWorks, and the 43% pod space allocation defining the design gives it exceptional OmniMech flexibility. Twelve configurations show extensive exploitation of that pod space across tactical roles.
variants.capabilities: Twenty-eight and a half tons of pod space at 65 tons is extraordinary and the configurations exploit every bit of it. The pod space allocation comes at cost elsewhere in the design — understand the trade-offs before judging performance numbers in isolation. Twelve configurations means substantial pod inventory requirements. Hell's Horses construction quality is consistent. The pod system is well-implemented for the weight class.
variants.deployment: Twelve configurations with Configuration A's twin ER large lasers and Ultra AC/5 covering long-range fire support. The pod inventory management for full configuration flexibility is the logistics challenge. XL advisory applies consistently. Hell's Horses and successor Clan parts support. The exceptional pod space is the design's identity — use it to match configuration to mission rather than defaulting to one configuration for all roles.

variants.name: (Prime)
variants.overview: Clan Jade Falcon introduced the Hel — Inner Sphere designation Loki Mk II — in 3121 as a Hellbringer successor, and the 40 tons of pod space in a 65-ton chassis is the remarkable engineering achievement. The Falcon technician caste made specific trade-offs to achieve that pod allocation that define both the design's strengths and its limitations.
variants.capabilities: 40 tons of pod space at 65 tons is exceptional — more than the Hellbringer achieved with its extraordinary pod percentage. The trade-offs made to reach that figure affect other performance characteristics. Five configurations exploit the pod space in different ways. Jade Falcon construction quality is consistently high. The Gauss rifle primary configuration requires capacitor maintenance on top of standard pod maintenance.
variants.deployment: Five configurations with the Prime's paired Gauss rifles and ER large lasers establishing the long-range fire support identity. Gauss capacitor maintenance applies to Gauss-equipped configurations. The pod space advantage is the design's selling point — configuration flexibility to match any tactical requirement. Jade Falcon parts support through Olivetti and Falcon logistics. The trade-offs made for pod space are worth understanding before deployment.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: The Hel designation covers additional Loki Mk II configurations beyond the primary five, and the ATM-focused Configuration C is among the more tactically interesting. The same engineering foundation as the Loki Mk II with different pod selections reflecting specific Falcon tactical requirements.
variants.capabilities: The ATM launcher configurations require specific ammunition management knowledge — Advanced Tactical Missiles use different munition types that need separate storage and handling. Four ATM-12 launchers consuming 10 tons of ammunition creates serious supply chain planning requirements. The Hel chassis performance characteristics are identical to the Loki Mk II across all configurations.
variants.deployment: Three configurations with the ATM-12 battery being the most supply-intensive. ATM ammunition management is the critical operational factor — establish diverse munition supply for all ATM types before deployment. Jade Falcon parts and logistics support. The ATM tactical flexibility — standard, extended range, high-explosive — is the capability advantage, but only if all munition types are available.

variants.name: LGB-0C
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 0C is the standard production model: twin LRM-20s, two medium lasers, and a small laser on a 310-rated standard engine. Walk three, run four. The LRM-20s produce the missile volume the Longbow is known for. The medium lasers handle anything that closes inside minimum range. Standard engine means side torso damage is survivable, which matters for a machine that sits in the back and attracts counter-battery fire.
variants.deployment: The 0C is the reference configuration that established the Longbow's reputation. It goes somewhere with good lines of sight, sits there, and delivers LRM-20 fire until the target stops moving or the ammunition runs dry. Seven tons of LRM ammunition per launcher is generous. The medium lasers are for self-defence, not aggression. This machine should never be at the front.

variants.name: LGB-0W
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 0W runs a 340-rated engine for walk four, run six, adding twin LRM-5 launchers alongside the LRM-20s for additional missile volume. The small laser stays; the medium lasers do not. Four launcher types to manage means more complex ammunition loading. The lack of a medium laser backup means anything that closes inside LRM minimum range and stays there is a serious problem.
variants.deployment: The 0W trades the 0C's medium laser self-defence for more missile launchers and slightly more speed. The LRM-5s add volume rather than range. Four launcher types to manage means more complex ammunition loading. The lack of a backup weapon means anything that closes inside LRM minimum range is a serious problem.

variants.name: LGB-0W2
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 0W2 strips the small laser entirely: twin LRM-20s and twin LRM-5s with nothing else. Walk four, run six on the 340-rated engine. Pure missile fire with no self-defence whatsoever. The weight saved goes into additional ammunition. This machine needs constant escort and has no business near the front line.
variants.deployment: The 0W2 has no weapon capable of engaging anything that closes inside LRM minimum range. It requires constant escort to survive on any battlefield where light fast opponents are present. The additional ammunition endurance is the benefit. This is a deep fire support variant that never belongs at the front under any circumstances.

variants.name: LGB-7Q
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 7Q uses a 255-rated engine for walk three, run four, carrying twin LRM-20s, twin LRM-5s, and two medium lasers. The 255 engine is smaller than the 0C's 310, freeing mass for the additional launchers while restoring medium laser self-defence. More complete as a self-sufficient unit than the 0W variants.
variants.deployment: The 7Q is the workhorse production variant across most Inner Sphere forces. The twin LRM-20s and twin LRM-5s deliver substantial missile volume and the medium lasers provide real self-defence against anything that closes the distance. It deploys as the standard fire support element in formations of all sizes.

variants.name: LGB-8C
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 8C keeps the 7Q's twin LRM-20s and twin LRM-5s and upgrades to four medium lasers. The 255-rated standard engine. Four medium lasers are a meaningful deterrent against lights rather than the token self-defence of earlier variants. Some ammunition storage is traded for the extra laser weight.
variants.deployment: The 8C is an improved 7Q with better close-range capability. Four medium lasers give the pilot real options when something closes the distance rather than the symbolic resistance of two. The missile loadout is unchanged. This is the preferred configuration for commanders who have learned the hard way that two medium lasers is not enough self-defence.

variants.name: LGB-7V
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 7V uses a 255-rated XL engine to free mass for twin LRM-20s, five medium pulse lasers, and an ER large laser. The five pulse lasers and ER large laser make this configuration genuinely dangerous at close range rather than just defensively capable. The XL means a side torso hit ends the machine.
variants.deployment: The 7V is the most combat-capable Longbow configuration at close range. The five medium pulse lasers and ER large laser give it real fighting ability when the LRMs cannot be used. The XL engine is the tradeoff that makes that weapons package possible. Pilots need to understand they cannot absorb hits the standard engine variants survive.

variants.name: LGB-10C
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 10C runs a 255-rated standard engine with twin LRM-20s, twin LRM-5s, and four ER medium lasers. The ER medium upgrade extends the close-range defence envelope slightly over the 8C. Standard engine survivability. Four ER mediums are a real improvement on a machine that needs every advantage in close quarters.
variants.deployment: The 10C is the ER medium upgrade of the 8C concept. The extended range mediums give the pilot slightly more options against opponents closing the distance. The missile loadout is unchanged from the standard family formula. Standard engine means it survives hits that kill the 7V. A solid incremental improvement over earlier four-laser variants.

variants.name: LGB-12C
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 12C uses a 255-rated XL engine carrying twin LRM-20s, twin LRM-15s, and three ER small lasers. The LRM-15s add substantial additional missile volume. Three ER small lasers is essentially symbolic self-defence for an eighty-five ton machine. This configuration is about maximum missile output. It needs dedicated escorts.
variants.deployment: The 12C is the highest LRM volume configuration in the Longbow family: twin LRM-20s and twin LRM-15s delivering simultaneous volleys. The XL engine makes it more fragile than standard engine variants and the three ER small lasers are essentially symbolic self-defence. This machine needs dedicated escorts. In exchange it saturates target zones with missile fire at a rate that few opponents can withstand.

variants.name: LGB-0H
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 0H carries twenty-six Rocket Launcher 10 packs and two standard PPCs on a 340-rated engine. Rocket launchers are one-shot weapons. Twenty-six RL-10s fire once and deliver an enormous single volley. After that the machine has two PPCs. This is a complete departure from the LRM fire support concept and probably the most dramatic single-strike potential in the Longbow family.
variants.deployment: The 0H is a one-time devastation platform. The twenty-six RL-10s all firing at once creates incoming fire that almost nothing survives. After the alpha strike the machine becomes a slower PPC-armed heavy. Pilots who set up the RL-10 strike correctly get one engagement of extraordinary violence. Units that field the 0H plan around that one moment and accept the PPCs as the follow-up capability.

variants.name: LGB-8V
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 8V uses a 255-rated XL engine with two Arrow IV artillery launchers, two medium pulse lasers, and an ER large laser. Arrow IV is battlefield artillery, not conventional LRMs. Range is substantially greater than LRM-20s and each round hits harder. The medium pulse lasers and ER large laser provide direct fire self-defence. Arrow IV ammunition logistics are entirely separate from standard LRM supply chains.
variants.deployment: The 8V is an artillery platform rather than a missile boat. Arrow IV in a mobile BattleMech chassis gives commanders indirect fire capability that moves with the battle line. The medium pulse lasers and ER large laser provide direct fire self-defence. Arrow IV ammunition supply is distinct from LRM logistics and requires its own supply chain planning. The XL vulnerability requires escort.

variants.name: LGB-13NAIS
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 13NAIS carries six light AC/5s, two ER medium lasers, an ER small laser, and anti-battle armour pods. No LRM launchers. This is an anti-infantry and anti-battle armour specialist that uses the Longbow chassis as an airframe rather than a fire support platform. Six light AC/5 ammunition feeds are the maintenance overhead. Strange use of an eighty-five ton machine but effective in its intended role.
variants.deployment: The NAIS designation indicates this was an experimental development. The 13NAIS takes an eighty-five ton fire support chassis and repurposes it for close-range anti-infantry work, which is a strange choice for the weight and platform. The six light AC/5s and B-pods are effective against their intended targets. The light AC/5 ammunition management across six launchers is the maintenance overhead. It sees use in roles where the Longbow airframe was available but LRM fire support was not the mission.

variants.name: LGB-13C
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 13C uses a 340-rated XL engine carrying six MML-7 launchers and three ER small lasers. The MML-7s fire SRM or LRM rounds from the same launcher, adapting to engagement range. Three tons of ammunition per MML pair. The ER small lasers are token close-range defence. XL vulnerability applies.
variants.deployment: The 13C replaces the dedicated LRM launchers with MML flexibility. Six MML-7s can deliver LRM or SRM fire depending on target range, which broadens the engagement profile. The practical effect is a platform that contributes at more ranges than the standard LRM-only Longbow but with less concentrated output at any single range. The XL engine requires escorts.

variants.name: LGB-14C
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 14C uses a 255-rated XL engine with six MML-9 launchers and three ER medium lasers. The MML-9 is heavier than the 13C's MML-7, delivering more per salvo in both modes. Three ER medium lasers are better self-defence than the 13C's ER small lasers. XL vulnerability applies.
variants.deployment: The 14C is the improved MML variant over the 13C, with heavier launchers and better direct fire backup. Six MML-9s in LRM mode approach the output of dedicated LRM-15 launchers while retaining SRM flexibility for close-range engagements. The ER mediums are real weapons rather than token self-defence. The XL engine remains the survivability tradeoff.

variants.name: LGB-12R
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 12R uses a 255-rated light engine with three jump jets alongside four LRM-15s, an ER large laser, and an ER medium laser. The light engine provides better torso survivability than XL while allowing jump capability the standard variants lack. Four LRM-15s deliver substantial volume. The ER large laser handles direct fire at range.
variants.deployment: The 12R is the mobile fire support variant, using jump jets and light engine technology to reposition in ways standard Longbow variants cannot. Jump three at eighty-five tons is not impressive but it allows the machine to cross obstacles and claim elevated terrain that improves LRM firing lanes. The light engine survives side torso hits. This is the most tactically flexible Longbow configuration.

variants.name: LGB-14C2
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 14C2 uses a 255-rated XL engine with six MML-9 launchers and a single ER medium laser. A stripped version of the 14C, trading two of the three ER medium lasers for additional ammunition storage. The six MML-9s still provide SRM and LRM flexibility across engagement ranges. One ER medium laser is the only direct fire backup. XL vulnerability applies.
variants.deployment: The 14C2 trades direct fire capability for ammunition endurance compared to the 14C. The single ER medium is there for emergencies rather than as a genuine combat option. Six MML-9s with the additional ammunition storage makes this the longer-endurance MML variant. Units that expect extended operations without resupply prefer it over the 14C.

variants.name: LGB-14Q
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 14Q uses a 340-rated XL engine for walk four, run six, carrying twin LRM-20s, twin MML-5s, and four ER medium lasers. The combination of LRM-20s and MML-5s covers long-range indirect fire and shorter-range flexibility simultaneously. Four ER medium lasers provide real close-range defensive capability. The XL engine enables the speed and the expanded weapons fit.
variants.deployment: The 14Q is a more mobile fire support variant with better close-range capability than the standard family. Walk four, run six gives it more repositioning ability than walk three configurations. The MML-5s add short-range flexibility alongside the LRM-20s. Four ER mediums make it genuinely dangerous to anything that closes. XL vulnerability is the standard tradeoff.

variants.name: LGB-14V
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries. I have worked on eight different variants. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 340-rated XL engine. The LGB-14V carries twin MRM-20s, twin LRM-5s, two light PPCs, and two ER medium lasers. The MRM-20s engage at medium range rather than the extended distances the LRM family prefers. The light PPCs and ER mediums handle direct fire. XL engine vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The 14V moves away from standard Longbow doctrine. The MRM-20s work at medium engagement distances where LRM doctrine pushes further back. The light PPCs and ER mediums add direct fire capability most Longbow variants lack. Units that need indirect fire capability closer to the engagement line run the 14V.

variants.name: LGB-10K
variants.overview: The Longbow has been delivering long-range missile fire since 2480 and accumulated eighteen variants over six centuries of production. I have worked on eight different variants of this chassis and every one of them has the same primary maintenance concern: LRM ammunition supply. The design philosophy of overwhelming missile fire from range has never changed.
variants.capabilities: The 10K uses a 255-rated XL engine carrying twin Ultra AC/20s, an ER large laser, and a medium pulse laser. No LRM launchers at all. The Ultra AC/20s in double-tap mode at close range is devastating output for an eighty-five ton machine, comparable to dedicated assault-class brawlers. This is the furthest the Longbow design has ever been pushed from its original purpose.
variants.deployment: The 10K is a field conversion that turns a fire support chassis into an assault brawler. The twin Ultra AC/20s are the entire point. The ER large laser handles range work and the medium pulse laser provides close-range backup when something gets too close for the autocannons. The XL engine is fatal on a side torso hit. Units that ran this variant either did not know what they had or knew exactly what they wanted from it.

variants.name: LNG-1B
variants.overview: Innovative Design Concepts built the Longshot for the Solaris VII arena circuit and the 245-rated XL in an endo steel frame at 35 tons gives nearly 100 kph. The arena origin shapes the construction priorities but the design has found field use beyond Solaris. Six variants cover development from the original dual SRM configuration through subsequent refinements.
variants.capabilities: Nearly 100 kph for a 35-ton light is fast and the XL concern applies. The endo steel structure requires trained tech qualification. The original dual SRM-6 plus Narc configuration is an unusual arena weapons choice reflecting the spectacle requirements of arena combat. Six variants show the design evolving away from the original arena-specific loadout toward more field-practical configurations.
variants.deployment: Six variants from the original arena configuration through field-adapted versions. The XL advisory applies consistently. The endo steel structural advisory is consistent. The Narc beacon system on original variants requires specific maintenance knowledge. IDC parts through Solaris arena channels. For field deployment the later variants are more practical than the arena-optimized original.
