variants.name: LN-4B
variants.overview: Tao Mechworks designed the Lu Wei Bing for the CCAF as an 85-ton assault building on the Victor's proven formula with additional mass. The Mydron Devastator LB 20-X is the primary weapon and the design reflects aggressive Capellan close-range assault doctrine. Single variant with no factory alternatives.
variants.capabilities: The Mydron Devastator LB 20-X is the centerpiece and the variable munitions feed requires regular cleaning and function testing — the ammunition selection mechanism deferred maintenance creates reliability issues at the worst moments. The Victor heritage provides structural familiarity for techs who know that design. The assault weight and close-range focus require pilots who commit to closing engagement distance.
variants.deployment: Single configuration. The LB 20-X ammunition selection mechanism advisory is the primary weapons maintenance note. Tao Mechworks parts through Capellan channels. The Strategios deploys these against high-value targets where the assault-weight LB 20-X firepower is decisive. The Victor conceptual heritage means some maintenance procedures transfer, though the additional five tons changes specific structural calculations.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Lupus was the second OmniMech ever built, following the Coyotl, introduced in 2857 during the Golden Century. At 60 tons with a Vlar 300 standard engine, the design prioritized reliability and pod space over maximum speed. Five configurations show development of the second OmniMech concept.
variants.capabilities: The Vlar 300 standard engine rather than XL is a deliberate choice reflecting early OmniMech design philosophy — reliability and damage tolerance over performance extremes. The pod space is generous relative to the total mass. Standard engine means different damage vulnerability profile from XL-equipped designs — a genuine advantage in sustained operations. Five configurations exploit the pod space in different ways.
variants.deployment: Five configurations with Configuration A's Large Pulse Laser and Ultra AC/10 covering direct fire support effectively. The standard engine damage resilience is worth communicating to pilots — different survivability characteristics from XL designs. The Golden Century construction quality is excellent on original hulls. Parts support through the manufacturing Clan's channels. Working on a Lupus means working with early OmniMech history.

variants.name: LNX-9Q
variants.overview: Blue Shot Weapons of Solaris VII introduced the Lynx in 2761 for the SLDF as one of the first XL engine designs in production, and the Nissan 275 XL gives 97 kph at 55 tons. The design was ahead of its time technically and the XL engine that enables its speed was innovative for the era. Five variants cover development from the SLDF original.
variants.capabilities: 97 kph at 55 tons was exceptional when introduced and remains competitive. The XL engine was new technology at this design's introduction and early XL documentation reflects that learning period — some procedures were refined as the technology matured. The ER PPC and large laser combination is effective and well-documented. Five variants cover different technology periods and weapons configurations.
variants.deployment: Five variants from the 2761 SLDF original through subsequent configurations. The XL advisory applies consistently. The early XL documentation on original hulls may reflect earlier maintenance procedures — cross-reference with current XL standards. Blue Shot and successor manufacturer parts through various channels. The SLDF origin means Star League construction quality on original variants.

variants.name: MSK-5S
variants.overview: The Mackie is the first BattleMech ever built, developed by the Terran Hegemony in 2439 under Director-General Michael Cameron, and working on one means working with the foundation of everything that came after. The primitive technology throughout predates modern construction standards by centuries. Five variants span the original through development.
variants.capabilities: Primitive systems throughout — engine, armor, weapons, cockpit — every component predates modern standards and requires primitive construction documentation. The design's historical significance is unquestioned; its practical maintenance reality is that modern procedures and parts simply do not apply. Field fabrication from original specifications is the repair approach for anything beyond basic maintenance.
variants.deployment: Five variants from the 2439 battlefield prototype through development versions. The primitive construction advisory applies to all variants without exception. These are historical artifacts in whatever operational role they fill. Establish contact with Hegemony primitive construction archives before any significant work. The Mackie's value is historical; treat every maintenance session as careful preservation work on irreplaceable machines.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Wolf introduced the Timber Wolf, called the Mad Cat in IS intelligence reports, in 2945 as the centrepiece of their second-generation OmniMech program. The Type W3 endo steel chassis with a Starfire 375-rated Clan XL at seventy-five tons achieves walk five, run seven. That combination of speed, armour, and weapons capacity at heavy weight is what built the Timber Wolf's reputation across a century of warfare.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy-five tons is exceptional mobility for a heavy OmniMech. The Clan XL carries the standard side torso vulnerability. The endo steel structure requires trained tech qualification for structural repairs. Wolf construction quality is consistently high. Twenty configurations mean the pod inventory management demands are substantial and diversity of weapon types across those configurations is the broadest of any OmniMech family. Configuration A carries twin ER PPCs, three medium pulse lasers, a Streak SRM-6, and an ER small laser. The ER PPCs are the primary weapons at range. The pulse lasers and Streak SRM-6 handle close work with accuracy. The Streak fires only on lock, conserving ammunition. This is the most commonly encountered Timber Wolf configuration.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is the standard deployment configuration that most IS pilots and techs will encounter first. It covers long range with the ER PPCs and transitions to close work with the pulse lasers and Streak. The ER small laser handles anything at extreme close range the larger weapons cannot address efficiently. Streak ammunition management is the operational concern.

variants.overview: Clan Wolf introduced the Timber Wolf, called the Mad Cat in IS intelligence reports, in 2945 as the centrepiece of their second-generation OmniMech program. variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy-five tons is exceptional mobility for a heavy OmniMech. The Clan XL carries the standard side torso vulnerability. Twenty configurations mean the pod inventory management demands are substantial and diversity of weapon types across those configurations is the broadest of any OmniMech family. Configuration B carries a Gauss rifle, an LRM-10, a large pulse laser, a small pulse laser, and an SRM-4. The Gauss rifle is the primary direct fire weapon: accurate and hard-hitting at range. The LRM-10 provides indirect fire capability. The pulse lasers and SRM-4 handle close work. Gauss and LRM ammunition require separate tracking.
variants.deployment: Configuration B is a multi-range platform that covers long, medium, and close engagement distances from a single loadout. The Gauss rifle accuracy at range is the standout capability. Warriors who pace their Gauss ammunition carefully get extended operational endurance. The SRM-4 handles anything that closes past the Gauss minimum range.

The UAC/5 adds reliable ballistic output. The AMS protects against incoming missile salvos. This is a comprehensive loadout that covers most engagement scenarios.
variants.deployment: Configuration C is a long-range dominant variant with missile defence. The AMS adds survivability against missile-heavy opposition that few other configurations match. The twin LRM-15s provide sustained indirect fire. UAC/5 ammunition requires tracking alongside the LRM rounds. Warriors who understand how to layer the ER lasers and LRMs at range get excellent sustained output.

Two tons of Streak ammunition across four launchers tracks fast in sustained close engagement.

variants.name: X
variants.overview: Clan Diamond Shark spent a notoriously troubled development period producing the Mad Cat III before full production in 3086, and the visual resemblance to the Timber Wolf at 55 tons is intentional — marketing advantage in the IS market they were targeting. Eight variants show development from the experimental prototype through production.
variants.capabilities: At 55 tons the Mad Cat III is 20 tons lighter than the ancestor and the performance profile reflects that difference despite the visual similarity. The experimental X variant prototype differs from production variants in ways that require attention before working from any manual — confirm which hull you have. Eight variants including the prototype have different maintenance profiles. Diamond Shark construction quality is consistently high.
variants.deployment: Eight variants from the experimental prototype through production configurations. The prototype-to-production documentation gap is the main caution for early hulls. The troubled development period means some early production variants had quality variations that later batches corrected — inspect older hulls more carefully. Diamond Shark parts through their trade network. The IS market targeting means parts availability through non-Clan channels is better than most Clan designs.

variants.capabilities: The all-energy weapons configuration is clean from a logistics standpoint — no ammunition supply chain for the primary weapons. variants.name: C-MK-O Invictus
variants.overview: The Malak is the lightest Celestial series OmniMech built for the Word of Blake's Manei Domini, and the Celestial Series MK1E endo steel with DefHes 210 light fusion engine at 35 tons creates the design foundation. Eight configurations and the Celestial-specific exotic components create the familiar Celestial maintenance challenge.
variants.capabilities: The light fusion engine rather than XL changes the damage profile — different vulnerability considerations, different repair procedures for engine-adjacent components. The Celestial endo steel requires Blakist-spec tooling for structural work. Eight OmniMech configurations at 35 tons means the pod workspace is physically constrained — configuration swaps take longer than the procedure suggests. Exotic Celestial components are the consistent maintenance challenge.
variants.deployment: Eight configurations with the Invictus supply-independent configuration being notable for its incendiary Inferno capability. Celestial-specific component sourcing outside Word of Blake supply chains is difficult post-Jihad. Assign dedicated Celestial-qualified personnel. The light fusion engine damage resilience advantage is worth communicating to pilots. Build comprehensive records for each hull since Celestial construction has less batch consistency than standard production.

variants.name: MAL-XT
variants.overview: The Malice emerged from an Eris Enterprises and Dynamic Ordnance partnership in 3135, and the LTV 400 XL pushing a 100-ton assault to 64 kph is the performance achievement that defines this chassis. Four variants show development of the fast assault concept.
variants.capabilities: 400-rated XL at 100 tons is impressive speed for the weight class and the XL vulnerability at this weight is the most serious possible — side torso damage on a 100-ton assault is catastrophic. Four LB 5-X autocannons on the base model create four mechanism maintenance requirements simultaneously plus four ammunition feed systems to keep clean. The variable munitions capability requires function testing of the feed mechanisms regularly.
variants.deployment: Four variants with the base model's quad LB 5-X configuration being the most maintenance-intensive. The quad autocannon mechanism maintenance multiplication is the consistent advisory — four systems, four cleaning requirements, synchronized schedules. The XL advisory at 100 tons is the most critical briefing. Eris and Dynamic Ordnance parts through their distribution channels. The fast assault concept is tactically interesting but maintenance-demanding.

variants.name: A

Wolf parts support is reliable. Brief pilots that this is not a conventional assault 'Mech — the speed changes the tactical doctrine entirely.

variants.name: MAD-1R
variants.overview: General Motors designed the Marauder in 2612 and it became the most recognisable heavy BattleMech in history. I have worked on this chassis in more variants than I care to count across my career. Thirty-six variants over four centuries of production. The twin PPCs in armoured gauntlets are the design identity and PPC maintenance is the primary technical concern across the entire family.
variants.capabilities: The distinctive pod-like shoulder assemblies and armoured gauntlet weapon mounts create maintenance access considerations that techs new to the design need to learn before their first inspection cycle. PPC calibration drifts under sustained fire and that drift compounds if not caught early. The shoulder actuator on the right arm is the first thing to go on high-use machines — I keep spares. Parts are available essentially everywhere given four centuries of production. The 1R is the Star League original. Twin Magna Hellstar PPCs, two medium lasers, an AC/5, and a 300-rated standard engine at seventy-five tons. Walk four, run six. Nineteen heat sinks on a machine that fires two PPCs simultaneously. Pilots who respect the heat curve keep this running indefinitely. Pilots who alpha strike every turn give me extra work.
variants.deployment: The 1R is the reference configuration that set the template thirty-five variants followed. The PPCs at range, medium lasers as backup, AC/5 for sustained ballistic harassment. Royal brigade machines get priority maintenance time because they deserve it.

variants.name: MAD-2R
variants.overview: General Motors designed the Marauder in 2612 and it became the most recognisable heavy BattleMech in history. I have worked on this chassis in more variants than I care to count across my career. Thirty-six variants over four centuries of production. The twin PPCs in armoured gauntlets are the design identity and PPC maintenance is the primary technical concern across the entire family.
variants.capabilities: The distinctive pod-like shoulder assemblies and armoured gauntlet weapon mounts create maintenance access considerations that techs new to the design need to learn before their first inspection cycle. PPC calibration drifts under sustained fire and that drift compounds if not caught early. The shoulder actuator on the right arm is the first thing to go on high-use machines — I keep spares. Parts are available essentially everywhere given four centuries of production. The 2R upgrades to ER PPCs, extending engagement range while keeping the AC/5 and medium lasers. The ER PPCs run hotter than the standard Hellstars and nineteen heat sinks feel the difference when both fire together. The range advantage is real and pilots who work at ER PPC distance get more from this variant.
variants.deployment: The 2R deploys in the same fire support role as the 1R with better reach. Heat management is tighter. The ER PPCs and standard AC/5 create some weapons combination awkwardness at medium range where neither is fully optimal.

variants.name: MAD-3R
variants.overview: General Motors designed the Marauder in 2612 and it became the most recognisable heavy BattleMech in history. I have worked on this chassis in more variants than I care to count across my career. Thirty-six variants over four centuries of production. The twin PPCs in armoured gauntlets are the design identity and PPC maintenance is the primary technical concern across the entire family.
variants.capabilities: The distinctive pod-like shoulder assemblies and armoured gauntlet weapon mounts create maintenance access considerations that techs new to the design need to learn before their first inspection cycle. PPC calibration drifts under sustained fire and that drift compounds if not caught early. The shoulder actuator on the right arm is the first thing to go on high-use machines — I keep spares. Parts are available essentially everywhere given four centuries of production. The 3R is the post-Star League rebuild produced when original components degraded and replacements were unavailable. Whatever PPC technology was accessible during production went in, which in practice means a downgraded weapons fit compared to the 1R. Armour is reduced from original specification. This is a chassis making do with what the Succession Wars left available.
variants.deployment: The 3R is the Succession Wars Marauder. It represents what happened to a great design when the supply chain collapsed. Performance is below the 1R and pilots who have run both know it. It deploys wherever a Marauder is needed and a 1R is not available, which describes most of the Inner Sphere through the Succession Wars.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: General Motors designed the Marauder in 2612 and it became the most recognisable heavy BattleMech in history. Parts are available essentially everywhere given four centuries of production. The C is an unusual Marauder variant that replaces the PPCs with twin large pulse lasers and an Ultra AC/5, keeping two medium lasers. The large pulse lasers are accurate at medium range and generate less heat than the PPCs they replace. The UAC/5 adds ballistic output at medium range. This is a more heat-efficient loadout than the standard PPC configuration.
variants.deployment: The C variant removes the traditional PPC identity in favour of pulse laser accuracy and autocannon rate of fire. Pilots who found the PPC heat curve restrictive generally prefer the C. The UAC/5 ammunition requires management. The standard engine preserves survivability. This is a valid fire support configuration that simply prioritises a different engagement style.

The 3D is a Davion-specific variant replacing the standard PPCs with an ER PPC and an AC/10, backed by two medium lasers and a small laser. variants.overview: General Motors designed the Marauder in 2612 and it became the most recognisable heavy BattleMech in history. I have worked on this chassis in more variants than I care to count across my career. Thirty-six variants over four centuries of production. The twin PPCs in armoured gauntlets are the design identity and PPC maintenance is the primary technical concern across the entire family.
variants.capabilities: The distinctive pod-like shoulder assemblies and armoured gauntlet weapon mounts create maintenance access considerations that techs new to the design need to learn before their first inspection cycle. PPC calibration drifts under sustained fire and that drift compounds if not caught early. The shoulder actuator on the right arm is the first thing to go on high-use machines. Parts are available essentially everywhere given four centuries of production. The Douglass SD is a field conversion stripped of PPCs and carrying two large lasers, two medium lasers, and two SRM-4s. This is what a Marauder looks like when the PPCs are too degraded to maintain and the unit uses whatever is available. Walk four, run six on the standard 300-rated engine. The large lasers provide the direct fire role. The SRM-4s add close-range punch.
variants.deployment: The Douglass SD is a named field conversion, not a production variant. Someone stripped a Marauder of its PPCs and rebuilt it with available weapons. The result is capable but a step down from the standard configuration. It deploys in whatever role the original Marauder filled, just with less range and a different heat profile.

variants.name: MAD-4A
variants.overview: Blackwell Industries scaled the Marauder up by 25 tons to create the Marauder II, and the design philosophy of building so closely on an existing production machine is smart engineering — the maintenance knowledge transfers, the parts overlap, and the chassis feels familiar. Eighteen variants show the assault-weight Marauder concept proving as enduring as the original.
variants.capabilities: The Marauder heritage is the maintenance advantage — techs who know the original adapt quickly to the II. The assault weight adds structural considerations that the original heavy doesn't have, and the weapons payload at 85-100 tons is substantially heavier than the parent design. Eighteen variants spanning the production history mean extensive documentation exists. The distinctive pod-like shoulder assemblies carry over at assault scale.
variants.deployment: Eighteen variants from the 3012 original upscaling through modern assault configurations. The original assault-weight Marauder established the design identity that subsequent variants refined. Parts availability through Blackwell and successor manufacturer channels is good. The Marauder chassis knowledge base the broader family enjoys applies to the II in structural and powerplant work. Whatever variant you're maintaining, the PPC-focused weapons philosophy carries through most of the family.

variants.overview: Clan technicians built their own Marauder successor during the Golden Century, introducing the Marauder IIC in 2828. They thought highly enough of the original to expand it to eighty-five tons using advanced Clan technology. The result handles differently from the IS original while being structurally recognisable to anyone who has worked on a Marauder. Nine variants cover extensive tactical variation.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 340-rated Clan fusion engine at eighty-five tons. The standard engine means this chassis survives side torso hits that would kill an XL-equipped competitor, which matters for an assault-weight machine expected to hold a line. Clan construction quality throughout is high. The shoulder pod design from the IS ancestor carries over with Clan precision manufacturing improving the fit and tolerances throughout. Variant 9 is the earliest IIC configuration, dated to 2831. Three ER PPCs and two Streak SRM-4s. The three ER PPCs deliver exceptional long-range energy fire that the IS Marauder could not match. The Streak SRM-4s handle close-range threats on lock. Heat from three ER PPCs firing simultaneously requires strict discipline.
variants.deployment: Variant 9 is the original Marauder IIC deployment configuration. Three ER PPCs at eighty-five tons establishes the fire superiority over IS heavy designs that drove the IIC's development. Warriors who respect the heat curve sustain devastating fire. The Streak SRM-4 ammunition is the only supply concern. This is the reference IIC configuration.

Variant 8 carries twin ER PPCs, four medium pulse lasers, an LRM-10, and an ER small laser. The medium pulse laser suite provides accurate close-range firepower that the ER PPCs cannot address. The LRM-10 adds indirect fire capability. The ER small laser handles point-blank threats.
variants.deployment: Variant 8 is the most versatile Marauder IIC configuration, covering long range with ER PPCs, medium with pulse lasers, and indirect fire with the LRM-10. The pulse laser accuracy is the primary close-range advantage. LRM ammunition is the operational management task. This configuration suits warriors who want flexibility across engagement ranges.

The heavy large lasers hit harder than standard ER large lasers but generate substantially more heat. The jump capability is the unique tactical feature of this variant.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 is the jump-capable Marauder IIC. Jump four at this weight class opens terrain options and flanking approaches unavailable to ground-bound assault designs. The heavy large lasers create a severe heat load under sustained fire. Warriors who use the jump jets to claim elevated firing positions and then manage heat carefully get excellent results. The XL engine adds the standard side torso concern.

variants.name: MHL-X1
variants.overview: The Treaty of Taurus in 3056 created the New Colony Region and with it a requirement for a new BattleMech, and the Marshal entered production in 3059 at Taurus Territorial Industries as the result. The standard Magna 220 engine with four jump jets creates a capable medium that can handle the varied terrain of the New Colonies.
variants.capabilities: The standard engine rather than XL reflects the Periphery operational context — the design was built for maintainability in austere conditions and the standard engine is easier to support without sophisticated infrastructure. The four jump jets add terrain flexibility that the colony environment demands. Five variants cover different weapons configurations. Taurus and Detroit Consolidated construction quality is solid for Periphery manufacture.
variants.deployment: Five variants from the 3059 original through subsequent configurations. The standard engine maintainability advantage is worth communicating — different damage vulnerability profile from XL designs, easier to support in limited logistics environments. Jump jet inspection is a maintenance priority given the terrain-flexible operational context. Taurus Territorial Industries parts through Concordat channels are reliable.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Wolf introduced the Warhawk — Inner Sphere designation Masakari — as an 85-ton assault OmniMech, and the four ER PPCs of the primary configuration are among the most impressive energy weapons arrays in any assault design. The General Systems 340 XL gives 64 kph for the weight class. Twelve configurations show extensive tactical development.
variants.capabilities: Four ER PPCs generate extreme heat and pilot discipline on the primary configuration is not optional — undisciplined firing will shut this machine down. The XL vulnerability at 85 tons is serious. Twelve configurations mean substantial pod inventory requirements. Wolf construction quality is consistently excellent. Configurations that replace some PPCs with other weapons change the heat management situation significantly.
variants.deployment: Twelve configurations with Configuration A's more versatile generalist loadout being a common choice for pilots who want heat management flexibility. The heat management advisory is the most important briefing for any primary configuration Warhawk pilot. The XL advisory applies consistently across all configurations. Wolf parts support is reliable. Brief pilots clearly on the heat profile before their first deployment in a primary configuration Warhawk.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Jotunn BattleWorx introduced the Mastodon in 3148 for the Rasalhague Dominion as a direct response to attrition losses in their assault OmniMech inventory. The heavily reinforced internal structure is unusual for a Clan design — this is explicitly a survivability-first engineering choice.
variants.capabilities: The reinforced internal structure creates exceptional battle damage tolerance that conventional Clan construction doesn't offer at the cost of other performance metrics. This is a machine designed to take hits and keep fighting, which is a different design philosophy from most Clan assault OmniMechs. Five configurations exploit the durable platform differently. Jotunn BattleWorx and Ghost Bear Dominion construction quality is consistently high.
variants.deployment: Five configurations with Configuration A's Gauss and Artemis LRM-15 combination covering multiple ranges effectively. The reinforced structure maintenance procedures differ from standard Clan construction in specific repair scenarios — confirm your techs have the specific documentation. Rasalhague Dominion logistics support is reliable. The survivability-first philosophy makes this a good choice for sustained operations where chassis losses are the primary concern.

variants.overview: Clan Steel Viper developed the Matador around 2846 during the Golden Century as a pre-OmniMech heavy with overwhelming close-range firepower. The Jade Falcon field refit of captured Matadors in 3069 shows the design finding continued service long after its production era ended.
variants.capabilities: The close-range firepower philosophy is embodied throughout the design. Massive angular armor plates provide substantial protection for the approach to optimal range. The Streak missile systems on the original provide ammunition-efficient close-range capability. The Falcon field refit replacing the Streak systems creates a significantly different weapons maintenance profile — know which version you have before servicing weapons systems.
variants.deployment: Single production variant plus the Falcon field refit. The field refit documentation reflects improvised solutions subsequently formalized — verify documentation completeness on refit hulls. Steel Viper original components versus Falcon refit components require different sourcing channels. The close-range assault doctrine requires pilots who understand that closing to engagement range is the tactical prerequisite.

variants.name: MAL-1PT5
variants.overview: The Mauler has a convoluted development history that the MAL-1PT5 designation summarises well enough. Fourteen variants emerged from the Capellan prototype process and the result is a ninety-ton assault 'Mech optimised for long-range sustained fire. The four AC/2 concept that defines the standard configurations is unusual and requires specific maintenance discipline across four synchronised mechanisms.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four. Slow even for a ninety-ton machine, but the Mauler is not built for manoeuvre. The four-autocannon variants require four synchronised cleaning and inspection schedules simultaneously, which is the primary maintenance overhead across the family. Ammunition management across multiple launchers is always the operational concern. The design fights at range and suffers when opponents close. The 1PT5 is the original Capellan prototype carrying four SarLon MaxiCannon AC/2s, two LRM-15s, and two medium lasers on a 270-rated standard engine. The SarLon autocannons are different hardware from the production Imperator weapons and require different maintenance documentation. Two LRM-15s add indirect fire. The medium lasers handle close-range self-defence.

variants.name: MS1-O
variants.overview: Hellespont Industries introduced the Men Shen in 3060 as the first OmniMech produced entirely within the Capellan Confederation, and the achievement is genuine — the endo steel chassis with 330-rated XL gives 97 kph at 55 tons for a capable first Capellan OmniMech. Ten configurations show ongoing CCAF development.
variants.capabilities: 97 kph at 55 tons is fast for a medium-heavy OmniMech and the XL vulnerability concern applies at this speed. The endo steel structure requires trained tech qualification for structural repairs. Ten configurations provide substantial tactical flexibility. The pulse laser and Artemis LRM combination on the primary requires Artemis calibration maintenance on top of standard weapons servicing. Hellespont construction quality reflects the pride in their first OmniMech achievement.
variants.deployment: Ten configurations with the Primary's combined arms approach being the most common. Artemis calibration advisory applies to Artemis-equipped configurations. The XL advisory applies consistently. The endo steel structural advisory is consistent. Capellan parts through Hellespont and CCAF channels. The first Capellan OmniMech status means political support for the program has maintained parts supply reliably.

variants.name: MCY-99
variants.overview: Mitchell Vehicles introduced the Mercury in 2742 as a next-generation SLDF reconnaissance platform, and the MASC system is the design's defining and most maintenance-intensive feature. The combination of the base engine speed and MASC boost creates a light that can achieve genuinely impressive velocity when the tactical situation demands it.
variants.capabilities: The MASC system requires careful monitoring and regular calibration — pushed too hard too often it degrades faster than the maintenance schedule assumes. The base speed without MASC is already competitive; the MASC capability is the tactical reserve. Six variants cover development from the Star League original. The pure reconnaissance role means the electronics are as important as the weapons.
variants.deployment: Six variants from the 2742 SLDF original through subsequent configurations. The MASC advisory is the consistent technical note — monitor closely and calibrate regularly. The reconnaissance electronics require specialist maintenance attention beyond standard weapons servicing. Mitchell Vehicles parts through various channels depending on variant era. The MASC capability should be briefed to pilots as a tactical reserve, not routine operation.

variants.name: MLN-1A
variants.overview: Mountain Wolf BattleMechs introduced the Merlin in 3010 as the first entirely new BattleMech design in the Inner Sphere in over a century, and the explicit design goal of durability, multi-role capability, and field repairability using commonly available parts is evident throughout. Nine variants show the design finding diverse tactical applications.
variants.capabilities: The design goal of field repairability with commonly available parts is genuinely achieved — the Pitban 240 engine and straightforward construction mean parts are available almost everywhere and most maintenance procedures are familiar to techs without specialized training. The multi-role weapons mix is balanced without being exceptional in any direction. Nine variants cover different tactical emphases.
variants.deployment: Nine variants from the 3010 original through subsequent configurations. The original entered service marking the end of a century-long design drought — the Mountain Wolf achievement is real. The field repairability philosophy means parts are available through most supply chains. The multi-role identity means no single engagement type is optimal — brief pilots that flexibility is the strength, not peak performance in any specific role.

variants.capabilities: The XL engine gives arena-competitive speed for a heavy and the XL concern applies — arena combat does produce side torso hits. Omnitech parts through Solaris arena market channels. variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Wolf introduced the Naga in 2869 from the Woodsman chassis, and the paired Arrow IV artillery systems are the entire point of this assault OmniMech. At 80 tons with a 400-rated XL giving 86 kph, the design can reposition between artillery volleys in ways that conventional artillery platforms cannot. Six configurations cover different artillery and self-defense approaches.
variants.capabilities: The Arrow IV systems are the primary maintenance focus and they require specific artillery system knowledge different from standard missile launchers. Arrow IV ammunition — including specialized munitions — needs careful storage and handling protocols. The 400-rated XL at 80 tons is the performance foundation for the repositioning capability that makes mobile artillery work. The XL vulnerability concern applies.
variants.deployment: Six configurations with Configuration A adding ER medium laser self-defense to the Arrow IV artillery core. The Arrow IV ammunition supply chain is the critical logistics factor — specialized munitions with careful storage requirements and limited availability. Establish the supply chain before deployment. The XL advisory applies consistently. Wolf parts support is reliable. The repositioning capability is the tactical advantage over fixed artillery — use it.

Independence Weaponry parts through Combine channels is reliable.

variants.name: NTL-UG
variants.overview: Tactical Advantage LLC built the Neanderthal on Regulus in 3124 as a melee-focused assault, and the large pulse laser with physical combat systems defines the close-range assault concept. The Regulan design philosophy prioritizes getting to melee range quickly and ending the engagement decisively.
variants.capabilities: The melee combat systems are mechanically demanding — high-stress components that see actual combat use require more frequent inspection than the maintenance schedule suggests. The large pulse laser is quality hardware. The speed for an assault 'Mech is the enabling capability for reaching melee range before opponents can withdraw. Two variants on the same physical-combat-focused chassis.

variants.deployment: Two configurations working within the limited pod mounting design. variants.name: A

variants.capabilities: Light Endo Steel has different structural properties from standard endo steel — specific repair procedures apply during battle damage work. The XL vulnerability concern applies. Jade Falcon parts support through Ironhold and Falcon logistics. variants.name: NSR-9J
variants.overview: The SLDF commissioned the Nightstar in 2767 during the Amaris Civil War specifically to counter the campaign of targeted Marauder pilot killings, and the Pitban 285 extralight engine in a design sharing Marauder heritage provides the heavier assault-weight counterpart. Six variants cover the design's development including rare recovered variants.
variants.capabilities: The Marauder design heritage is visible in the chassis concept while the 20-ton weight increase enables the assault-class weapons payload. The Pitban 285 extralight requires specialist maintenance beyond standard XL procedures. The shoulder pod assemblies echo the Marauder design. Marauder maintenance experience provides useful conceptual foundation but the extralight engine and assault-class components require specific additional training.
variants.deployment: Six variants from the 2767 NSR-9J original through development and recovered configurations. The original is the definitive configuration — the recovered variants represent battlefield salvage finds with documentation requiring examination-based reconstruction. The extralight engine specialist advisory is consistent. SLDF and successor parts through various channels. The Marauder family familiarity many techs have transfers to structural work but not to the extralight powerplant.

variants.name: NJT-2
variants.overview: Independence Weaponry introduced the Ninja-To on Quentin in 3062 as a C3 slave platform for the DCMS on a 390-rated XL engine. Walk six, run nine at sixty-five tons. Three variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. Walk six, run nine at this weight is genuinely fast. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The C3 slave system is the tactical identity across all variants — it requires specialist calibration maintenance or the network integration that defines this machine degrades. The NJT-2 carries two ER large lasers, two ER medium lasers, and an MRM-10, with a C3 slave. Walk six, run nine. The ER large lasers provide extended-range direct fire. The ER mediums handle closer engagement. The MRM-10 adds medium-range missile volume.
variants.deployment: The NJT-2 is the most common Ninja-To configuration. The ER large laser and MRM-10 combination covers long and medium range simultaneously. The C3 slave integrates targeting data from lancemates. Walk six, run nine makes this a fast heavy in DCMS network lances. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: NDA-1K
variants.overview: Cosby BattleMech Research introduced the No-Dachi on Vega in 3058 as the DCMS answer to the Clan physical attack 'Mechs, and the seven-meter katana-style sword with Triple Strength Myomer is the defining feature. Six variants show the melee assault concept developing through operational experience.
variants.capabilities: The Triple Strength Myomer system requires specific maintenance knowledge — TSM activation characteristics, the temperature threshold required for activation, and the myomer bundle inspection procedures are different from standard myomer systems. The seven-meter sword is mechanically demanding on the mounting and actuators. The ER PPC and MRM racks provide ranged support for the approach to melee range. Six variants develop different secondary weapons configurations.
variants.deployment: Six variants with the base model's katana and ER PPC combination establishing the melee assault identity. The TSM inspection requirements are the primary technical advisory — the system needs to be in perfect condition before any engagement the pilot intends to close to melee range. The physical weapon mounting and actuator inspection applies consistently. Cosby parts through Combine channels. Brief pilots on TSM activation requirements — effective melee requires heat management to hit the threshold.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Nobori-nin is Clan Wolf's medium OmniMech, originally a Diamond Shark design before Wolf claimed it ahead of production. Fifty tons with a 250-rated Clan XL engine gives walk five, run seven, jump five. Twenty-four tons of pod space at fifty tons is exceptional and twelve configurations reflect that flexibility thoroughly.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at fifty tons. The Clan XL carries standard side torso vulnerability. Twelve configurations means the pod inventory management demands are substantial across a wide variety of weapon types. Wolf and Sea Fox construction quality is consistently high. The jump capability across all configurations is the tactical constant that shapes how every variant is deployed. Configuration A carries twin large pulse lasers, an LRM-10, and an LB 2-X. The large pulse lasers are accurate at medium range. The LRM-10 adds indirect fire capability. The LB 2-X provides long-range harassment fire with cluster or slug options. The weapons cover multiple range bands from a single configuration.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is a versatile multi-range loadout. The large pulse laser accuracy combined with LRM-10 indirect fire handles most engagement scenarios a medium OmniMech faces. The LB 2-X harassment fire supplements the primary weapons. Jump capability lets warriors claim elevated firing positions.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Hell's Horses introduced the Notos in 3145 from their Csesztreg Industriplex as a production OmniQuadVee, and the conversion mechanism between quad 'Mech and wheeled vehicle configurations is the technically demanding feature. Five configurations multiply the maintenance complexity of an already complex platform.
variants.capabilities: The conversion mechanism is the most maintenance-intensive component — inspect before every deployment and don't defer the calibration cycles. The extralight engine provides consistent performance in both configurations. The endo steel structure requires trained tech qualification. Five OmniMech configurations on top of the quad chassis and conversion mechanism creates triple maintenance complexity. HAG-20 Configuration A requires ammunition management on top of everything else.
variants.deployment: Five configurations all subject to the conversion mechanism maintenance requirement. The triple complexity — quad chassis, conversion mechanism, OmniMech pods — requires dedicated experienced techs rather than rotating general staff. Hell's Horses logistics support is reliable. The operational flexibility between 'Mech and vehicle modes is the tactical advantage; maintaining that flexibility requires the maintenance investment to justify it.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Nova Cat commissioned the Nova Cat OmniMech in 3059 following their devastating losses during the Clan Invasion, and Khan Severen Leroux's vision of a pocket assault OmniMech at 70 tons is realized in the Consolidated Fusion 280 XL. Twelve configurations show the Nova Cat Clan's extensive development of their signature design.
variants.capabilities: The 280 XL explicitly sacrifices speed for firepower and protection, and the 64 kph result is slow for the weight class but the weapons payload reflects that trade-off honestly. The XL vulnerability concern applies. Twelve configurations means substantial pod inventory requirements. Nova Cat construction quality is consistently high. The pocket assault identity means configurations that try to use this chassis as a fast medium are misapplying the design.
variants.deployment: Twelve configurations with Configuration A's four ER large lasers and targeting computer being a common accurate long-range sniper choice. The XL advisory applies consistently. The speed limitation is the tactical constraint to communicate clearly — this machine wins by firepower and protection, not mobility. Nova Cat and successor faction parts support. The design holds special significance in Nova Cat culture; their units maintain these machines with notable care.

variants.name: NX-80
variants.overview: Word of Blake engineers conceived the Nyx during the Jihad as an extreme-speed reconnaissance platform, and the Pitban 300 XL pushing a 30-ton chassis to 162 kph is what 'extreme' looks like. Five variants show the design adapting from its Blakist origins through Republic and post-Republic service.
variants.capabilities: 162 kph at 30 tons is exceptional — this is among the fastest designs at this weight class. The XL at this speed creates a vulnerability profile where any significant side torso damage is immediately mission-ending at combat velocity. At 30 tons there is essentially no battle damage tolerance once the speed advantage is lost. The weapons are minimal — this machine's role is information, not combat.
variants.deployment: Five variants from the 3076 baseline through developments. The XL advisory at this speed is the most emphatic possible — the speed is the armor and the armor is the speed. Blakist origin creates post-Jihad parts challenges for Blake-specific components. Republic and successor channels for more common components. Brief pilots that engaging anything is secondary to the reconnaissance mission — this machine cannot absorb the hits a combat role would require.

variants.name: OBK-M10
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the O-Bakemono in 3057 as their reverse-engineering of the Naga's Arrow IV capability, and the significant concessions required to implement dual Shigunga Arrow IV systems on an IS 80-ton chassis tell you something about how demanding that technology is. Three variants cover different artillery and support configurations.
variants.capabilities: The dual Shigunga Arrow IV systems are the primary focus and they require specific artillery maintenance knowledge. LAW's reverse-engineering of the Naga concept means some system documentation was reconstructed from examination rather than original specifications — verify documentation completeness before major work on the Arrow IV systems specifically. The self-defense weapons are secondary to the artillery mission.
variants.deployment: Three variants with the base model's twin Arrow IV and medium laser self-defense being the standard configuration. Arrow IV ammunition supply chain is the critical logistics factor — specialized munitions with careful storage requirements. Establish the supply chain before deployment. LAW parts through Combine channels is reliable for standard components; Arrow IV-specific components may require specialized sourcing. The reverse-engineering origin means some documentation gaps exist.

variants.overview: Clan Snow Raven produced the Omen on Dante in 3087 at their Snow Raven Industrial Complex Alpha, and the CSR Version 84.62 chassis with Type 255 Extra-Light engine at 85 tons accepts slower speed in exchange for a weapons payload and the HarJel III self-repair systems of the later variant. The Extra-Light engine specialist advisory applies to both variants. Snow Raven parts through their Industrial Complex Alpha and logistics network. The self-repair capability is genuinely useful in sustained operations.

Two configurations show different approaches to the OmniMarauder concept.

General Motors Kathil parts support through Federated Suns channels. The Marauder cultural weight means this machine carries expectations that the OmniMech format tries to honor.

variants.overview: Red Devil Industries introduced the Onager on Pandora in 3083 for Clan Jade Falcon, named after the medieval siege engine, and the endo steel frame with 15 tons of ferro-fibrous armor creates an 85-ton assault with genuine staying power. variants.name: SA-OS

variants.name: ON1-C
variants.overview: General Mechanics built the Orion in 2456 for the Terran Hegemony and the design's balanced ballistic-missile-energy weapons philosophy has stayed consistent across eighteen variants and five centuries of production. I have worked on four different Orion variants in my career. It is a machine that does everything competently and nothing spectacularly, which is exactly what a workhorse heavy needs to be.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 360-rated standard engine at seventy-five tons. The balanced weapons mix means maintenance covers multiple weapon types simultaneously, which is the consistent planning overhead across all variants. The standard engine provides survivability that XL-equipped competitors cannot match under fire. Parts availability through most supply chains is excellent given the production history. The ON1-C is the earliest Orion variant, a primitive prototype stripped to two medium lasers and a single AC/5 on the full 360-rated engine. This is the machine before the design was complete. Walk four, run six but with almost no weapons fit. The prototype designation means standard production documentation does not apply.
variants.deployment: The ON1-C is a primitive prototype and not a combat-capable production variant. It represents the design in its early proving stage. Maintaining a primitive prototype requires period documentation rather than production spec sheets. Components are not interchangeable with production variants.

variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 360-rated standard engine at seventy-five tons. variants.name: 'Burton'
variants.overview: Clan Wolf developed the Orion IIC out of respect for General Kerensky's chosen BattleMech, and the endo steel and ferro-fibrous construction with Clan technology creates a heavy that honors the original while substantially improving every system. The Burton named variant is the historically unusual configuration.
variants.capabilities: Clan technology throughout delivers meaningfully better performance than the IS original. The endo steel and ferro-fibrous construction both require specific repair knowledge beyond standard construction. Single standard variant plus the named Burton configuration which uses an XL engine rather than the standard engine — meaningfully different damage vulnerability profile requiring a separate maintenance understanding.
variants.deployment: Single standard variant plus the Burton named variant. The Burton's XL engine creates different vulnerability characteristics from the standard variant — know which hull you have before any structural or engine-adjacent work. Wolf parts through their channels. The Kerensky association gives this design significant cultural weight in Wolf service — these machines receive careful maintenance attention as a matter of clan honor.

variants.name: OR-2I
variants.overview: Victory Industries introduced the Orochi on Marduk in 3084 as a modern successor to the Longbow concept for the DCMS, and the design builds on the fire support legacy while taking a fundamentally different approach to indirect warfare. Two variants cover the initial deployment and development.
variants.capabilities: The Longbow conceptual heritage means the fire support role is familiar, but the Orochi's approach to that role differs from its predecessor. The initial DCMS deployment with the Eighth Sword of Light was part of Operation Fortify. Two variants cover the original and operational experience refinements. Victory Industries construction quality is solid for a post-Jihad manufacturer.
variants.deployment: Two variants with the original 3084 model being the DCMS service baseline. The Longbow conceptual familiarity is useful context but the Orochi's specific systems require their own documentation. Victory Industries parts through Combine channels. The Eighth Sword of Light service history means operational experience feedback has shaped the design's development — the second variant reflects those lessons directly.

variants.name: OSR-3D
variants.overview: Achernar BattleMechs designed the Osiris on New Avalon in 3063 explicitly modeled after the Clan Dragonfly OmniMech, and the result achieves IS-manufactured approximation of that performance at 30 tons. Three variants spread through FedSuns and Lyran service quickly after the February 3063 production start.
variants.capabilities: The Dragonfly concept translated to IS construction means competitive speed at 30 tons with the XL vulnerability concern. IS construction throughout means standard tools and parts work everywhere, a genuine advantage over maintaining captured Clan hardware. Three variants cover different weapons configurations. Achernar construction quality is consistently solid. The Dragonfly inspiration is visible in the performance profile.
variants.deployment: Three variants from the base production through configurations refined by FedSuns and Lyran operational experience. The XL advisory applies consistently. Achernar parts through Federated Suns channels is excellent. The broad FedSuns and Lyran Alliance distribution means this is a well-supported design in those supply chains. The IS construction advantage — standard tools and common parts — is the practical benefit over Dragonfly maintenance.

variants.name: OSP-15
variants.overview: Hollis Incorporated designed the Osprey in 2738 for the SLDF as a dorsally-mounted M-7 Gauss rifle platform, and that dorsal mounting position is the distinctive engineering choice that defines the maintenance approach. Five variants cover development from the Star League original through subsequent configurations.
variants.capabilities: The dorsally-mounted M-7 Gauss rifle is excellent hardware but the dorsal mounting position creates specific maintenance access considerations different from arm or torso-mounted Gauss installations. The Gauss capacitor maintenance is the primary technical focus as always — inspect and replace on schedule. The Holly MML provides range flexibility alongside the primary Gauss. Five variants develop different secondary weapons.
variants.deployment: Five variants from the 2738 SLDF original through subsequent configurations. The dorsal mounting access procedures are the maintenance detail that surprises techs new to the design. The Gauss capacitor advisory applies consistently. Hollis parts through various channels depending on variant era. Star League construction quality on original variants. The Gauss and MML combination covers both long-range precision and flexible short-range fire effectively.

variants.name: (Jaguar)
variants.overview: The Society built the Osteon as their assault-class OmniMech with survivability as the primary design priority — a machine conceived for a faction that couldn't afford to lose what they fielded. Ten configurations reflect the design's versatility. The named Russou Howell variant represents a custom commission rather than standard production.
variants.capabilities: The survivability-first design philosophy shapes everything about the Osteon. Infrastructure bottlenecks during Society production meant the design was more carefully engineered than rushed designs from the period. Ten OmniMech configurations mean substantial pod inventory requirements. The Society construction quality reflects careful engineering under resource constraints.
variants.deployment: Ten configurations including the Russou Howell custom variant — that specific hull was crafted to individual specifications and has documentation that reflects custom rather than production standards. The custom variant's documentation requires examination-based reconstruction. Society parts channels are complicated given the faction's history; build comprehensive technical records for each hull. The survivability focus makes these machines valuable assets to preserve carefully.

variants.name: OSR-2C
variants.overview: Ostmann Industries designed the Ostroc in 2511 as a dedicated urban combat platform for Terran Hegemony garrison forces, and the side-torso twin large laser mounting is the distinctive engineering choice that defines both the tactical approach and the maintenance access. Fifteen variants over the production run show the urban combat platform concept proving enduringly useful.
variants.capabilities: The side-torso twin Fuersturm-C large lasers are the design identity and the primary maintenance focus. Side-torso weapon mounting creates different access requirements from arm or center-torso weapons — maintenance procedures account for the torso structure integration. Fifteen variants span multiple technology eras. The medium-to-long range firepower for an urban combat design is unusual and effective.
variants.deployment: Fifteen variants from the 2511 OSR-2C original through modern configurations. The original established the urban combat reputation that subsequent variants maintained. The side-torso weapon access advisory is the consistent maintenance note. Ostmann and successor manufacturer parts through various channels. The urban combat role is the consistent tactical identity — brief pilots coming from open-terrain assignments on the different engagement requirements.

variants.name: OTT-7J
variants.overview: Ostmann Industries built the Ostscout in 2600 for one purpose — scouting — and the VOX 280 engine in a 35-ton chassis reflects that singular focus. An engine more commonly found on designs twice its size, the VOX 280 consumes a significant portion of the chassis mass and shapes everything else about the design. Nine variants cover development across technology eras.
variants.capabilities: The VOX 280 is the dominant chassis feature and the tight packaging around it creates access constraints for maintenance on surrounding components. Speed is the primary defense and the minimal weapons reflect the design philosophy that the Ostscout should avoid combat rather than win it. Nine variants span Star League through modern configurations. The electronics suite for the scout mission requires specialist calibration maintenance.
variants.deployment: Nine variants from the 2600 original through developments. The original mounted only a single Tronel laser — the weapons were always secondary. The oversized engine access advisory is the consistent structural note — patience and proper tooling matter more than forcing access. Ostmann parts through various channels depending on variant era. Brief pilots that the Ostscout's job is to come back with information, not to win engagements.

variants.name: OW-1
variants.overview: The Owens is an OmniMech evolution of the Jenner concept, designed for cavalry and reconnaissance roles. The modular pod system provides the tactical flexibility the cavalry mission demands and nine configurations show the concept developing across different tactical requirements. The Raptor design lessons are visible in the engineering choices throughout.
variants.capabilities: The cavalry screening and reconnaissance role defines the weapons philosophy — LRM racks for suppressive fire and self-defense lasers rather than primary combat armament. Nine configurations cover different tactical approaches. The OmniMech pod system is well-implemented. The Jenner heritage provides conceptual familiarity for techs who know that design. The light weight means any significant battle damage creates proportionally large problems.
variants.deployment: Nine configurations with the Primary using small and medium lasers plus LRM arms for the cavalry support role. The pod maintenance overhead across nine configurations requires parts inventory planning. The Jenner conceptual familiarity helps structurally. Various manufacturer parts through their respective channels. Brief pilots that the Owens is a cavalry and screening machine — direct combat engagement should be the exception rather than the rule.

variants.overview: Clan Wolf-in-Exile produced their first domestic BattleMech design with the Pack Hunter on Arc-Royal following the Refusal War, and Khan Phelan Kell's directive for impressive speed with sharp bite produced a 30-ton light built around a standard Light Fusion engine. Four variants show significant configuration variation including a radical departure from the original single-weapon philosophy.
variants.capabilities: The Light Fusion engine rather than XL changes the damage profile from comparable XL-equipped lights — different vulnerability considerations. The original single-weapon philosophy is clean from a maintenance perspective — one system to service. The Pack Hunter 2's radical departure to extralight engine and multiple weapons creates a completely different maintenance profile. Wolf-in-Exile construction quality is solid.
variants.deployment: Four variants with the Pack Hunter 2 being a radical departure from the original. Know which variant you have before working from any manual — the engine type alone creates fundamental maintenance differences. The Light Fusion engine advisory applies to original variants. The extralight engine specialist advisory applies to the Pack Hunter 2. Arc-Royal parts through Wolf-in-Exile channels.

variants.name: PAL-1
variants.overview: Innovative Design Concepts designed the Paladin for the Solaris VII arena circuit, and the Super-Lite 360 XXL engine on the PAL-2 is the technically extraordinary feature. Three variants span from the conventional original through the arena-competitive XXL configuration. The PAL-2's XXL engine is among the most unusual powerplants I've worked with.
variants.capabilities: The Super-Lite 360 XXL on the PAL-2 is experimental hardware — experimental designation means documentation was developed during and after production rather than preceding it. XXL maintenance requires specialist knowledge that XL experience doesn't cover. The original PAL-1's standard engine and endo steel is the conventional maintenance baseline. The arena construction assumptions differ from field deployment requirements.
variants.deployment: Three variants from the standard-engine original through the XXL arena variant. The PAL-2 XXL experimental maintenance requirement is the primary advisory — confirm specific training before working on the powerplant. The PAL-1 original is the more conventionally maintained configuration. IDC and Solaris Arms parts through arena market channels. For field deployment, arena inspection frequencies should be increased significantly.

variants.name: LFA-1X
variants.overview: Kali Yama Weapons Industries built the Pandarus on Kendall as a specialized Extended LRM platform, and the triplet of KYWI Type IIIE Extended LRM-10 launchers are the defining feature. Two variants cover the experimental prototype and production configurations. Extended LRM systems are unusual hardware requiring specific maintenance knowledge.
variants.capabilities: Extended LRM systems operate at greater ranges than standard LRM launchers and have different guidance and propulsion requirements that create specific maintenance procedures. Three Extended LRM-10 launchers means three separate calibration and mechanism maintenance requirements simultaneously. The prototype origin of the first hulls means some documentation required reconstruction from examination.
variants.deployment: Two variants with the original experimental prototype being the most documentation-sparse. Extended LRM specialist maintenance is the consistent advisory — these are not standard LRM systems and standard LRM procedures don't apply. Kali Yama parts through their Kendall facility and Free Worlds League channels. The extreme range capability requires pilots who understand how to use that range advantage tactically — conventional medium-range doctrine doesn't apply.

variants.name: PNT-8Z
variants.overview: Alshain Weapons commissioned the Panther in 2739 for SLDF reconnaissance and the Lord's Light PPC has been the chassis identity ever since. A PPC on a thirty-five ton light is unusual and it is the thing that makes the Panther dangerous at ranges where most lights cannot threaten anything. Seventeen variants over the production run. I have kept Panthers running in three different units.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four on the standard 140-rated engine. PPC maintenance is the primary technical concern across the family. The Lord's Light calibration drifts under sustained fire faster than most pilots expect, and it has to be caught early or accuracy degrades noticeably. The SRM-4 that appears on most variants is the close-range backup when the PPC heat curve demands a pause. The 8Z is an early variant replacing the standard PPC with a large laser and keeping an SRM-4. The large laser trades PPC range and damage for reduced heat. Walk four, run six, jump four on the standard 140-rated engine. The heat issue that plagued the prototype Tronel laser is less severe here but the large laser still runs warmer than the PPC under sustained fire.
variants.deployment: The 8Z is an early production variant that predates the Lord's Light PPC becoming standard. The large laser works but pilots who know the 9R prefer the PPC's range and punch. It deploys in the same scout and skirmisher roles as the standard Panther with reduced effectiveness at range.

variants.overview: Alshain Weapons commissioned the Panther in 2739 for SLDF reconnaissance and the Lord's Light PPC has been the chassis identity ever since. variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four on the standard 140-rated engine. PPC maintenance is the primary technical concern across the family. The Lord's Light calibration drifts under sustained fire faster than most pilots expect, and it has to be caught early or accuracy degrades noticeably. The SRM-4 that appears on most variants is the close-range backup when the PPC heat curve demands a pause. The 9R is the production standard: Lord's Light PPC, SRM-4, and four jump jets on the 140-rated engine. Walk four, run six, jump four. The PPC at thirty-five tons is what makes this machine dangerous. The SRM-4 handles anything that closes past PPC minimum range. This is the variant I have spent the most time maintaining.
variants.deployment: The 9R is the reference Panther and the most common variant in Combine service. It scouts, skirmishes, and applies PPC fire at ranges lighter opponents cannot reply to effectively. The jump capability claims terrain features that improve the PPC engagement angle. Parts are available everywhere in Combine supply chains.

variants.overview: Clan Hell's Horses developed the Parash in the early 3080s at their Manufacturing Plant, and the Magna 245 XL with Model KT Booster MASC at 35 tons creates genuine sprint capability. Two variants including an experimental model first observed in a 3086 skirmish on Hermagor.
variants.capabilities: The MASC system requires careful monitoring and regular calibration — pushed too hard too often it degrades faster than the maintenance schedule assumes. The XL vulnerability concern applies. Two variants with the experimental one being the most documentation-sparse — build your own technical records from examination on experimental hulls. Hell's Horses construction quality is consistent.
variants.deployment: Two variants including the enigmatic experimental model from the 3086 Hermagor observation. Experimental hull documentation advisory — verify against physical examination. The MASC advisory applies to both variants. The XL advisory is consistent. Hell's Horses parts through their channels. MASC discipline briefing for pilots — the sprint capability is a tactical reserve, not routine operation.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Septicemia was The Society's utilitarian medium OmniMech, the backbone of their forces, designed for mass production without the exotic systems of the Osteon assault. Fourteen configurations reflect the utilitarian design philosophy. The armor layout specifically geared to resist common Clan weaponry reflects who they expected to fight.
variants.capabilities: The anti-Clan armor optimization and adequate pod space for mission flexibility define the design. Speed and pod space proved more than adequate for the medium OmniMech role. Fourteen configurations means substantial pod inventory. The utilitarian construction philosophy means the documentation is more comprehensive than one might expect from a secretive faction. Society construction quality is practical rather than refined.
variants.deployment: Fourteen configurations with the ATM-12 support variant being the second most common encountered. ATM ammunition management applies to ATM-equipped configurations — diverse munition types with separate storage requirements. Society parts channels have the same complications as the Osteon. Build comprehensive technical records for each hull. The utilitarian mass-production philosophy means more consistent batch quality than the Osteon custom work.

variants.capabilities: The anti-Clan armor optimization and adequate pod space for mission flexibility define the design. Speed and pod space proved more than adequate for the medium OmniMech role. Fourteen configurations means substantial pod inventory. The utilitarian construction philosophy means the documentation is more comprehensive than one might expect from a secretive faction. Society construction quality is practical rather than refined.
variants.deployment: Fourteen configurations with the ATM-12 support variant being the second most common encountered. ATM ammunition management applies to ATM-equipped configurations — diverse munition types with separate storage requirements. Society parts channels have the same complications as the Osteon. Build comprehensive technical records for each hull. The utilitarian mass-production philosophy means more consistent batch quality than the Osteon custom work.

variants.name: PFF-2
variants.overview: Zettle Metals Incorporated introduced the Pathfinder on Rahne in 3075 at the lower end of what Lyran Alliance forces needed, and the primitive construction reflects intentional production simplicity rather than inability. Primitive specifications trading performance for production ease were a deliberate post-Jihad rebuilding choice.
variants.capabilities: Primitive specifications throughout — the 180-rated primitive engine and primitive armor and weapons require primitive construction documentation and procedures. Modern parts don't fit. The Lyran Alliance purchasing the design for garrison use despite the primitive technology reflects the post-Jihad urgency of having something rather than waiting for modern alternatives.
variants.deployment: Single configuration. Primitive construction documentation is required — do not apply modern procedures. Zettle Metals parts for primitive-era components require specialized sourcing. The post-Jihad garrison role and primitive construction combination means the Pathfinder is found in units with limited support infrastructure — plan maintenance appropriately for austere conditions.

variants.name: PKM-2C
variants.overview: Ronin Incorporated built the Patriot on Wallis during the Jihad as a purpose-built command platform, and the Arrow IV missile system paired with TAG and heavy PPC reflects an unusual combination of direct fire, indirect fire, and target designation capability. Three variants cover the experimental prototype through production.
variants.capabilities: The Arrow IV and TAG combination creates a machine capable of both delivering and directing indirect fire — a genuine force multiplier when used correctly. The Arrow IV requires specific artillery maintenance knowledge. The heavy PPC has different thermal characteristics from standard PPC. Three systems with three specialized maintenance requirements make the Patriot more demanding than its designation suggests.
variants.deployment: Three variants from the prototype through production configurations. The Arrow IV ammunition supply chain is the critical logistics factor. Arrow IV specialist maintenance and heavy PPC specialist maintenance both apply. The TAG system requires specific calibration. Ronin Incorporated parts through their channels. The command platform role means pilots need doctrine training beyond standard 'Mech operation — the Arrow IV and TAG coordination requires specific skills.

variants.name: PKP-1A
variants.overview: The Republic of the Sphere and former AFFS developed the Peacekeeper jointly in the post-Jihad period as a heavy garrison assault designed for sustained field operations without regular resupply. The all-energy weapons emphasis that this requirement drove is the design identity. Three variants cover the field trial and production configurations.
variants.capabilities: The sustained operations without resupply requirement drove the all-energy weapons loadout, eliminating ammunition supply dependency. Heat management is the pilot's constant concern across the all-energy array. Three variants including the initial field-trial configuration deployed to five mercenary commands for evaluation. Republic and AFFS construction quality is consistently solid.
variants.deployment: Three variants with the initial field-trial model providing the operational feedback that shaped production. The all-energy supply independence is the operational advantage for garrison and extended operations. Heat management advisory applies universally. Republic and Federated Suns parts through their respective channels. The field-trial mercenary deployment means operational experience from diverse commanders shaped the final production design.

variants.name: PDG-1X MUSE RED
variants.overview: General Motors built the Pendragon at New Valencia for the AFFS as a ninety-five ton extended-range striker designed to operate behind the main battle line. Walk three, run four. Three variants. The ELRM systems are the design's defining feature.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at ninety-five tons. Extended LRM systems reach substantially beyond standard LRM range — opponents at standard LRM maximum range cannot reply effectively. XL engine on most variants — side torso vulnerability. The ELRM and ER PPC combination creates a stand-off engagement envelope that forces opponents to close distance under fire. The MUSE RED is the prototype: two Extended LRM-20s, an ER PPC, and three ER medium lasers on the 285-rated XL engine. Walk three, run four. The ELRM-20s reach substantially beyond standard LRM range. The ER PPC handles direct fire. The ER mediums cover close engagement.
variants.deployment: The MUSE RED is the prototype that preceded full production. Early hulls have documentation that may not match current standards — verify against examination of the specific machine. The ELRM-20 engagement distance forces opponents to close significantly under fire. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: PDG-1R
variants.overview: General Motors built the Pendragon at New Valencia for the AFFS as a ninety-five ton extended-range striker designed to operate behind the main battle line. Walk three, run four. Three variants. The ELRM systems are the design's defining feature.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at ninety-five tons. Extended LRM systems reach substantially beyond standard LRM range — opponents at standard LRM maximum range cannot reply effectively. XL engine on most variants — side torso vulnerability. The ELRM and ER PPC combination creates a stand-off engagement envelope that forces opponents to close distance under fire. The PDG-1R production model uses the larger 380-rated XL engine for walk four, run six. Two Extended LRM-15s replace the prototype's ELRM-20s. An ER PPC and three ER medium lasers are retained. Walk four is a meaningful speed improvement over the prototype's walk three.
variants.deployment: The 1R is the production model. Walk four allows repositioning the prototype could not manage. The ELRM-15s provide the extended stand-off range at slightly less per-salvo volume than the ELRM-20 prototype. The ER PPC maintains direct fire capability. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: PDG-3R
variants.overview: General Motors built the Pendragon at New Valencia for the AFFS as a ninety-five ton extended-range striker designed to operate behind the main battle line. Walk three, run four. Three variants. The ELRM systems are the design's defining feature.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at ninety-five tons. Extended LRM systems reach substantially beyond standard LRM range — opponents at standard LRM maximum range cannot reply effectively. The PDG-3R carries a C3 master computer, two Rotary AC/2s, an ER PPC, and three ER medium lasers on the 380-rated XL engine. Walk four, run six. The C3 master coordinates the network lance. The Rotary AC/2s replace the ELRM launchers with sustained ballistic harassment.
variants.deployment: The 3R converts the Pendragon from an extended-range missile platform into a network command and sustained ballistic fire platform. The C3 master coordinates the AFFS network lance. The Rotary AC/2s provide persistent ballistic pressure at range. The ER PPC and ER mediums handle direct fire. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: PTR-4D
variants.overview: Kallon Industries introduced the Penetrator in 3053 at their Talon facility on Wernke, deliberately choosing standard construction — no endo steel, no XL engine, no ferro-fibrous — as the design philosophy. In an era of advanced construction techniques, the intentional conventionality is a statement about durability and field maintainability. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: The deliberate standard construction philosophy is the maintenance advantage — no endo steel structural specialty training needed, no XL vulnerability concern, standard armor repair. The trade-off is mass efficiency compared to endo steel and XL alternatives. Seven variants maintain the all-energy weapons identity across different configurations. The durability focus means these machines handle deferred maintenance better than more tightly engineered designs.
variants.deployment: Seven variants from the 3053 original through subsequent configurations. The base model's ER large laser focus established the energy-platform identity. The intentional conventional construction means parts are available everywhere and any competent tech can handle the work — genuine field maintainability. Kallon parts through Lyran and Federated Suns channels. The durability philosophy translates to real-world resilience in austere operational conditions.
