variants.name: PEN-2H
variants.overview: The Magistracy of Canopus produced their first indigenous heavy fire support design with the Penthesilea in 3083, and the Dynastic 75-P endo steel frame with twenty tons of ferro-fibrous armor at 75 tons reflects serious design investment. Three variants cover the production and development configurations.
variants.capabilities: The endo steel structure requires trained tech qualification for structural repairs. The ferro-fibrous armor requires specific repair techniques. Twelve tons of armor for a heavy 'Mech is substantial protection. The extended-range weapons combination provides genuine long-range fire support. Three variants show modest development of the base concept. Magistracy construction quality has improved significantly in the post-Jihad period.
variants.deployment: Three variants with the base production model being the Magistracy's first indigenous heavy fire support. Endo steel and ferro-fibrous structural advisories apply consistently. Magistracy and Canopus parts through their channels. The first indigenous heavy design holds cultural significance in Magistracy service — these machines are maintained with the care that distinction warrants.

variants.overview: Clan Cloud Cobra produced the Horned Owl — Inner Sphere designation Peregrine — in 2835 as a 35-ton harassing light platform. Six variants show development from the original all-energy configuration through significant departures like the LRM-5 rack configuration. The harassing platform identity requires pilots who understand they win through efficiency rather than raw firepower.
variants.capabilities: The Kolibri Delta Series large laser is quality Clan hardware. The all-energy philosophy of the original eliminates ammunition concerns. The LRM-5 rack variant represents a complete weapons philosophy departure from the energy-weapon base. Six variants cover meaningfully different maintenance profiles depending on weapons configuration. Cloud Cobra construction quality is consistent.
variants.deployment: Six variants with the Horned Owl 2's LRM-5 radical departure from the base design being the most distinct configuration. The energy variants and missile variants have completely different maintenance profiles — know which you're supporting. Cloud Cobra parts through their channels. The harassing platform role requires pilots who use the efficiency advantage — taking sustained fire in a Peregrine is a losing approach.

variants.name: PX-1R
variants.overview: Krauss-Liemann Incorporated on Wotan built the Phoenix as the Rim Worlds Republic's first jump-capable BattleMech, and the five Gerard Special A jump jets providing 150 meters of jump capability are the design's distinctive tactical feature. Seven variants span from the primitive prototype through production and modernized configurations.
variants.capabilities: The five jump jets are the design identity and require regular inspection given the tactical emphasis on three-dimensional mobility. The primitive original requires primitive construction documentation entirely different from production variant procedures. The Magna 250 engine gives 86 kph at 50 tons — competitive for a medium. Seven variants span significant technology variation.
variants.deployment: Seven variants from the 2474 primitive PX-1R prototype through production and development. The primitive original is not maintained from modern manuals — separate procedures, separate parts sourcing. The jump jet inspection priority applies to all jump-capable variants. Krauss-Liemann and successor parts through various channels. The primitive-to-modern technology arc means the specific variant's era determines the maintenance approach.

variants.name: PXH-1
variants.overview: Orguss Industries built the Phoenix Hawk in 2568 as a private venture and the design became the standard medium recon 'Mech of the Star League era. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 270-rated engine is the performance baseline across the family. The electronics suite is as important as the weapons — that has been true since the first production run. Thirty-one variants have come out of that formula.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty-five tons. The jump capability is the tactical constant across almost every variant. Electronics calibration is the maintenance overhead the standard 'Mech tech is not always prepared for: the comm and sensor systems on Phoenix Hawks require specialist attention or they degrade quietly without obvious symptoms until accuracy or detection range drops noticeably. The PXH-1 is the production standard: large laser, two medium lasers, and two machine guns on the 270-rated engine. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The large laser handles long-range direct fire, the mediums cover closer work, the machine guns manage infantry. This is the configuration that established the Phoenix Hawk's reputation.
variants.deployment: The 1 is the historical reference configuration. It deploys as a scout and skirmisher that uses jump capability and speed to control engagement range and electronics to gather information. Parts availability for the 1 is excellent across all supply chains. The machine guns indicate the original combined-arms operational environment the design was built for.

variants.name: PXH-1D
variants.overview: Orguss Industries built the Phoenix Hawk in 2568 as a private venture and the design became the standard medium recon 'Mech of the Star League era. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 270-rated engine is the performance baseline across the family. The electronics suite is as important as the weapons — that has been true since the first production run. Thirty-one variants have come out of that formula.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty-five tons. The jump capability is the tactical constant across almost every variant. Electronics calibration is the maintenance overhead the standard 'Mech tech is not always prepared for: the comm and sensor systems on Phoenix Hawks require specialist attention or they degrade quietly without obvious symptoms until accuracy or detection range drops noticeably. The electronics suite is as important as the weapons — that has been true since the first production run. Thirty-one variants have come out of that formula.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty-five tons. The jump capability is the tactical constant across almost every variant. Electronics calibration is the maintenance overhead the standard 'Mech tech is not always prepared for: the comm and sensor systems on Phoenix Hawks require specialist attention or they degrade quietly without obvious symptoms until accuracy or detection range drops noticeably. The 4M uses a light engine for the standard walk six, run nine, jump six profile, carrying two light PPCs, two medium X-pulse lasers, and two small X-pulse lasers. The light engine improves side torso survivability over XL variants. The X-pulse lasers are more accurate than standard pulse lasers. The light PPCs engage at short to medium range without minimum range issues.
variants.deployment: The 4M is the X-pulse precision variant with light engine survivability. The X-pulse accuracy is a genuine improvement at the ranges the Phoenix Hawk fights at. The light engine survives hits that kill XL variants. No ammunition dependency across the all-energy loadout simplifies logistics.

variants.name: PXH-7KJ 'Jasmine'
variants.overview: Orguss Industries built the Phoenix Hawk in 2568 as a private venture and the design became the standard medium recon 'Mech of the Star League era. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 270-rated engine is the performance baseline across the family. The electronics suite is as important as the weapons — that has been true since the first production run. Thirty-one variants have come out of that formula.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty-five tons. The jump capability is the tactical constant across almost every variant. The Jasmine uses a light engine carrying a snub-nose PPC, two ER medium lasers, and a Rocket Launcher-10. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The RL-10 is one-shot: a single missile salvo then gone. The snub-nose PPC and ER mediums carry the fight after the rocket is expended. Light engine survivability applies.
variants.deployment: The Jasmine is a named variant with a one-shot ambush element. The RL-10 delivers a single salvo when the opportunity is right and then the loadout becomes snub-nose PPC and dual ER mediums for sustained engagement. The light engine survivability advantage over XL variants is preserved.

variants.name: PXH-99
variants.overview: Orguss Industries built the Phoenix Hawk in 2568 as a private venture and the design became the standard medium recon 'Mech of the Star League era. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 270-rated engine is the performance baseline across the family. The electronics suite is as important as the weapons — that has been true since the first production run. Thirty-one variants have come out of that formula.
variants.capabilities: The PXH-99 is not a combat-capable variant. It uses a 45-rated engine — barely enough to power the systems — at walk one, run one, jump two. It carries a large X-pulse laser, two ER medium lasers, and two ER small lasers. This is a battlefield wreck or a warehouse queen pressed into some unusual service. No combat doctrine applies.
variants.deployment: The PXH-99 is non-standard documentation. Walk one on a 45-ton 'Mech means it cannot function in any tactical role. If you encounter one of these, check it for damage first. The weapons are real but the engine is not capable of moving the chassis to any useful position. Document what you find and escalate.

variants.name: C 2
variants.overview: Orguss Industries built the Phoenix Hawk in 2568 as a private venture and the design became the standard medium recon 'Mech of the Star League era. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 270-rated engine is the performance baseline across the family. The electronics suite is as important as the weapons — that has been true since the first production run. Thirty-one variants have come out of that formula.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty-five tons. The jump capability is the tactical constant across almost every variant. Electronics calibration is the maintenance overhead the standard 'Mech tech is not always prepared for: the comm and sensor systems on Phoenix Hawks require specialist attention or they degrade quietly without obvious symptoms until accuracy or detection range drops noticeably. The C 2 uses a 270-rated XL engine carrying a large pulse laser, two medium pulse lasers, and two AP Gauss rifles. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The AP Gauss rifles are anti-personnel weapons effective against infantry and battle armour. The pulse laser suite provides accurate close-to-medium range fire.
variants.deployment: The C 2 is an anti-infantry and light combat variant. The AP Gauss rifles devastate infantry and battle armour. The pulse laser suite handles armoured targets. The XL engine enables the weapons density. AP Gauss ammunition requires its own supply tracking separate from standard combat supplies.

variants.name: PXH-9
variants.overview: Orguss Industries built the Phoenix Hawk in 2568 as a private venture and the design became the standard medium recon 'Mech of the Star League era. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 270-rated engine is the performance baseline across the family. The electronics suite is as important as the weapons — that has been true since the first production run. Thirty-one variants have come out of that formula.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at forty-five tons. The jump capability is the tactical constant across almost every variant. Electronics calibration is the maintenance overhead the standard 'Mech tech is not always prepared for: the comm and sensor systems on Phoenix Hawks require specialist attention or they degrade quietly without obvious symptoms until accuracy or detection range drops noticeably. The PXH-9 uses a 270-rated XL engine for walk six, run nine, jump eight, carrying a large X-pulse laser, two medium lasers, and two light machine guns. Jump eight is exceptional. The large X-pulse laser provides accurate medium-range fire. The medium lasers and light machine guns handle close threats and infantry.
variants.deployment: The 9 is the jump-mobile precision variant. Jump eight opens approach and withdrawal angles unavailable to any standard Phoenix Hawk. The large X-pulse laser accuracy suits the high-speed engagements jump eight enables. The XL engine is the vulnerability. Light machine gun ammunition requires tracking.

variants.overview: The Phoenix Hawk IIC represents the culmination of the Star League's interest in an assault Striker, taking the Phoenix Hawk concept to 80 tons with the massive Type 70 400 XL engine. The result is an assault 'Mech with speed more typical of medium designs. Nine variants show extensive Clan development of the fast assault concept.
variants.capabilities: The Type 70 400 XL at 80 tons achieves remarkable speed for an assault design and the XL vulnerability at this weight is serious — side torso damage on an assault 'Mech is catastrophic. The endo steel structure requires trained tech qualification. Nine variants cover different weapons configurations. Steel Viper and other Clan construction quality is consistently high.
variants.deployment: Nine variants with the Steel Viper IIC 2 mobile fire support variant swapping the baseline weapons for long-range systems. The XL advisory at assault weight is the loudest briefing for every Phoenix Hawk IIC pilot. The endo steel structural advisory applies consistently. Clan parts through the manufacturing Clan's channels. The fast assault concept requires pilots who think differently from conventional assault doctrine — speed is the tactical tool.

variants.name: PXH-11K
variants.overview: The Phoenix Hawk L, called the Fenikkusu Taka in Combine service, is a 35-ton light OmniMech built on a 210-rated XL engine. Walk six, run nine, jump six. It is a lighter, faster adaptation of the Phoenix Hawk concept for the Combine's reconnaissance needs. The TSEMP cannon is the signature feature on the base configuration.
variants.capabilities: The PXH-11K carries a TSEMP cannon, an ER medium laser, an MML-3, and three heavy machine guns. The TSEMP cannon fires a focused electromagnetic pulse that disrupts enemy 'Mech systems without destroying armour, shutting down opponents non-lethally. The ER medium laser handles direct fire. The heavy machine guns address infantry. The MML-3 provides minimal missile flexibility. TSEMP maintenance requires specialist procedures.
variants.deployment: The 11K is a disruption and capture platform. The TSEMP cannon is most useful for disabling high-value targets for recovery rather than destruction. Warriors and techs need TSEMP-specific training. The XL engine adds the standard vulnerability. Walk six, run nine, jump six gives adequate mobility for the disruption role.

variants.name: PXH-11K2
variants.overview: The Phoenix Hawk L, called the Fenikkusu Taka in Combine service, is a 35-ton light OmniMech built on a 210-rated XL engine. Walk six, run nine, jump six. It is a lighter, faster adaptation of the Phoenix Hawk concept for the Combine's reconnaissance needs. The TSEMP cannon is the signature feature on the base configuration.
variants.capabilities: The PXH-11K2 drops the TSEMP cannon and heavy machine guns, carrying a snub-nose PPC, two ER medium lasers, and an MML-3. This converts the disruption platform into a standard light striker. The snub-nose PPC covers short to medium range without minimum range complications. The ER mediums add energy backup. The MML-3 provides minimal missile flexibility.
variants.deployment: The 11K2 is the conventional combat variant of the Fenikkusu Taka. Without the TSEMP it loses the disruption specialty and becomes a fast light with reasonable direct fire. The snub-nose and ER mediums together cover most engagement ranges a light 'Mech encounters. XL engine vulnerability is the standard concern.

variants.name: PHX-HK2
variants.overview: The Phoenix Hawk LAM is a fifty-ton Land-Air 'Mech built on the Phoenix Hawk chassis with conversion equipment for AirMech and Aerospace Fighter modes. The PHX-HK2 debuted in 2730 as the definitive production model. Three operational modes require fundamentally different maintenance procedures.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five in BattleMech mode on the 250-rated engine. A large laser, two medium lasers, and two machine guns in the right arm. The conversion equipment consumes substantial mass that limits the weapons loadout. The AirMech and Fighter modes provide rapid repositioning across terrain at the cost of complexity and vulnerability during conversion.
variants.deployment: The PHX-HK2 is the largest production LAM and the most demanding to maintain. Three operational modes require technicians familiar with aerospace, 'Mech, and conversion system procedures simultaneously. Most ground-based tech crews need supplementary training before their first LAM assignment. The conversion capability is genuine but the maintenance overhead is substantial.

variants.name: PLG-1N
variants.overview: HildCo Interplanetary built the Pillager during the Reunification War as a hundred-ton assault platform. The PLG-1N is the original production model on a 300-rated standard engine. Walk three, run four, jump two. The design carries twin AC/20s as the primary weapons — close-range devastation at a hundred tons.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump two on the standard engine. The PLG-1N carries two AC/20s, three medium lasers, and an SRM-4. The twin AC/20s at close range is the design's entire combat concept. Six tons of ammunition across both rifles. Standard engine — side torso survivability.
variants.deployment: The PLG-1N established the Pillager as a line-breaking assault platform. Walk three is slow but the jump two allows obstacle crossing. Twin AC/20s at close range overwhelms most opponents. Six tons of ammunition runs out faster than pilots expect on active operations. Standard engine survivability means it can absorb the hits the approach requires.

variants.name: PLG-3Z
variants.overview: HildCo Interplanetary built the Pillager during the Reunification War as a hundred-ton assault platform and the dual Gauss rifle concept defined its tactical identity. The PLG-3Z is a later variant on a 300-rated XL engine with jump jets added, carrying twin Gauss rifles, a large laser, and four medium lasers.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three on the XL engine. The twin Gauss rifles provide accurate long-range fire that most opponents cannot effectively answer at range. The large laser and four medium lasers handle anything that closes. Six tons of Gauss ammunition across both rifles is the operational endurance consideration. The XL engine and jump jets together represent a significant departure from the original standard engine design.
variants.deployment: The PLG-3Z uses jump capability to claim elevated positions that improve Gauss firing lanes. The jump jets on a hundred-ton assault 'Mech surprise opponents who expect the platform to be stationary. The XL engine adds vulnerability to side torso damage that the original Pillager's standard engine did not have. Keep the Gauss ammunition managed and it performs well at long range.

variants.name: PLG-4Z
variants.overview: HildCo Interplanetary built the Pillager during the Reunification War. The PLG-4Z is a stealthy variant with stealth armour and Guardian ECM on a 300-rated standard engine. Walk three, run four, jump three.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three on the standard engine. The PLG-4Z carries twin Gauss rifles and two ER medium lasers with stealth armour and Guardian ECM. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active. The Gauss rifles provide accurate long-range fire. The ECM disrupts enemy targeting. Standard engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The 4Z converts the Pillager from close-range devastation to stealth long-range precision. The stealth armour and ECM make it difficult to detect and target during approach. The Gauss rifles engage at range where the stealthy approach is most effective. Heat management with stealth active and any firing requires awareness of the combined thermal load. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: PLG-5L
variants.overview: HildCo Interplanetary built the Pillager during the Reunification War as a hundred-ton assault platform. Walk three, run four. Seven variants span the original AC/20 concept through stealth, artillery, and melee configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three on the 300-rated XL engine. The PLG-5L carries an Arrow IV artillery launcher, a Gauss rifle, and three ER medium lasers with an ER PPC. The Arrow IV provides extreme-range artillery fire. The Gauss handles accurate direct fire. The ER PPC and ER mediums cover direct engagement at all ranges. XL engine — side torso vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The PLG-5L is the artillery-direct fire hybrid. The Arrow IV range combined with the Gauss and ER PPC direct fire creates a machine that threatens opponents at extreme range on two different delivery systems. Arrow IV ammunition supply requires dedicated logistics. Jump three adds positioning options. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: PLG-5Z
variants.overview: HildCo Interplanetary built the Pillager during the Reunification War as a hundred-ton assault platform. Walk three, run four. Seven variants span the original AC/20 concept through stealth, artillery, and melee configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at a hundred tons. The design accepts slow speed in exchange for weapons mass. Standard or light engine on most variants — side torso survivability. Walk three means you choose your ground before the engagement starts. The PLG-5Z carries twin Gauss rifles, an ER PPC, and two ER medium lasers, with stealth armour, triple-strength myomer, and a Guardian ECM suite. Walk three, run four. TSM activates at elevated heat, boosting melee capability. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active.
variants.deployment: The 5Z builds on the 4Z's stealth concept with TSM for close-combat capability. The stealth and ECM allow quiet approach to close range. The Gauss and ER PPC engage at distance. TSM boosts melee once the machine reaches close quarters. Heat management with stealth active, weapons firing, and TSM activation requires careful planning.

variants.name: PLG-4X 'Anvil'
variants.overview: HildCo Interplanetary built the Pillager during the Reunification War as a hundred-ton assault platform. Walk three, run four. Seven variants span the original AC/20 concept through stealth, artillery, and melee configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four on the 300-rated light engine. The Anvil carries two Long Tom Cannons and a laser AMS. Light engine — side torso survivability. The Long Tom Cannons are battlefield artillery in a BattleMech chassis. The laser AMS provides missile defence without ammunition. No conventional weapons.
variants.deployment: The Anvil is a static artillery platform. Walk three means it goes to a position before the battle and stays there. Two Long Tom Cannons create an artillery threat that few targets can ignore. The laser AMS defends against counter-battery missile fire. Light engine survivability means incoming conventional fire is less immediately fatal. An experimental refit built for perimeter defence.

variants.name: PLG-6Z
variants.overview: HildCo Interplanetary built the Pillager during the Reunification War as a hundred-ton assault platform. Walk three, run four. Seven variants span the original AC/20 concept through stealth, artillery, and melee configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three on the 300-rated light engine. The PLG-6Z carries two LB 20-X ACs, an ER large laser, three ER medium lasers, and a medium pulse laser. Light engine — side torso survivability. Jump three. The LB 20-X pair provides heavy ballistic fire with cluster and slug options. The ER laser suite handles direct fire.
variants.deployment: The 6Z is the close-assault variant that sometimes escorts stealth-equipped Pillager machines. The LB 20-X pair at close range is devastating. The ER laser suite handles engagement at range during approach. Jump three positions it across obstacles. Light engine survivability means it takes hits better than XL variants. The standing order to keep it away from the front line is frequently ignored by pilots who have used it.

variants.overview: The Pinion is a forty-five ton Clan Jade Falcon medium built on a 225-rated Clan standard engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Three variants covering patrol, guard, and refit configurations. All-energy throughout.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at forty-five tons. Clan standard engine — side torso survivability. All-energy across all variants means no ammunition logistics. Jump five provides terrain exploitation for the patrol role. Variant 2 carries a heavy large laser, two medium pulse lasers, and two small pulse lasers. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The heavy large laser is the primary weapon — hits harder than a standard large laser at medium range but generates more heat. The pulse lasers cover close engagement accurately.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 was introduced in 3068 replacing micro pulse lasers with small pulse lasers for better range. The heavy large laser primary delivers more damage than the standard equivalent. Heat management under the heavy laser is the pilot's primary discipline. Standard engine survivability supports the patrol role.

variants.overview: The Pinion is a forty-five ton Clan Jade Falcon medium built on a 225-rated Clan standard engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Three variants covering patrol, guard, and refit configurations. All-energy throughout.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at forty-five tons. Clan standard engine — side torso survivability. All-energy across all variants means no ammunition logistics. Jump five provides terrain exploitation for the patrol role. Variant 3 is a field refit carrying two heavy large lasers and nothing else. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Two heavy large lasers generate severe heat under simultaneous fire. The standard engine heat sinks are not generous enough for sustained firing of both.
variants.deployment: Variant 3 appeared in 3069 as a field refit. Two heavy large lasers at medium range deliver significant damage at the cost of thermal discipline. Warriors cannot fire both simultaneously with any regularity. The alternating fire discipline required becomes a defining feature of how pilots use this variant.

variants.overview: The Piranha is a 20-ton Clan light 'Mech developed by Clan Ice Hellion for deep-raiding operations. Walk nine, run thirteen on the 180-rated Clan XL makes it fast enough to outrun almost anything. The original design packed twelve machine guns on a twenty-ton chassis. The variants take that premise in different directions.
variants.capabilities: Variant 2 replaces the machine gun array with twelve ER micro lasers, two heavy medium lasers, and a heavy small laser. Double heat sinks upgrade from the original single. The ER micro lasers extend the engagement range beyond the machine gun original. The heavy lasers add harder-hitting close-range output. Fifteen individual weapon systems require fifteen independent calibration tracks.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 is Ice Hellion's redesign of the deep-raid concept. The ER micro laser range improvement over machine guns allows harassment at distances the original could not threaten armoured targets. The heavy lasers add genuine anti-armour capability. Fifteen weapons on a twenty-ton machine is a maintenance challenge that keeps techs busy between missions.

variants.overview: The Piranha is a 20-ton Clan light 'Mech developed by Clan Ice Hellion for deep-raiding operations. Walk nine, run thirteen on the 180-rated Clan XL makes it fast enough to outrun almost anything. The original design packed twelve machine guns on a twenty-ton chassis. The variants take that premise in different directions.
variants.capabilities: Variant 3 carries two ER medium lasers, eight ER micro lasers, two micro pulse lasers, and a TAG system. The ER mediums provide the primary anti-armour capability. The micro lasers and pulse lasers add volume at close range. The TAG designates targets for guided munitions. This is a reconnaissance and designation variant alongside a combat platform.
variants.deployment: Variant 3 is the reconnaissance designation configuration. The TAG adds force multiplier value in formations with indirect fire assets. The ER mediums handle direct combat. Walk nine makes it fast enough to operate well forward of the main force and still withdraw safely. The thirteen-weapon maintenance burden persists.

variants.overview: The Piranha is a 20-ton Clan light 'Mech developed by Clan Ice Hellion for deep-raiding operations. Walk nine, run thirteen on the 180-rated Clan XL makes it fast enough to outrun almost anything. The original design packed twelve machine guns on a twenty-ton chassis. The variants take that premise in different directions.
variants.capabilities: Variant 4 returns to the machine gun concept with four standard machine guns, four light machine guns, two machine gun arrays, and two ER medium lasers. The arrays coordinate multiple machine gun feeds into simultaneous fire. The ER mediums provide anti-armour capability the machine guns lack. Combined machine gun and array fire at close range against infantry is devastating.
variants.deployment: Variant 4 is the machine gun volume fire configuration. Against infantry formations this variant is extremely dangerous. Against armoured targets the ER mediums carry the fight. The machine gun arrays require understanding their feed and cleaning requirements, which differ from individual machine gun maintenance. The XL vulnerability at twenty tons is always the standing concern.

variants.overview: The Piranha is a 20-ton Clan light 'Mech developed by Clan Ice Hellion for deep-raiding operations. Walk nine, run thirteen on the 180-rated Clan XL makes it fast enough to outrun almost anything. The original design packed twelve machine guns on a twenty-ton chassis. The variants take that premise in different directions.
variants.capabilities: Variant 5 carries two improved heavy medium lasers, twelve machine guns, and an ER small laser. Twelve machine guns on a twenty-ton machine is the original concept taken to an extreme. The improved heavy medium lasers add serious anti-armour capability beyond machine gun range. Twelve machine gun feeds require twelve cleaning schedules.
variants.deployment: Variant 5 emerged from Solaris VII arena experience and it shows in the close-range devastation focus. The twelve machine gun volume combined with improved heavy medium laser punch at close range is designed to overwhelm opponents quickly. Walk nine means it closes the distance fast. Twelve machine gun maintenance schedules are the tech's burden after every engagement.

variants.name: PRC-1N
variants.overview: Jalastar Aerospace built the Porcupine as a twenty-ton arena machine for Solaris VII Class Two divisions in 3063. Three variants, all built around speed and impact spikes rather than conventional weapons.
variants.capabilities: Walk nine, run thirteen at twenty tons. Arena construction throughout. The reinforced impact spikes on the armour panels are the design's unique feature — ramming attacks are a primary combat tool. Supercharger and MASC on some variants push speed further. The PRC-1N carries four medium lasers with a supercharger boosting burst speed beyond the standard walk nine. Reinforced armour spikes make ramming attacks a primary combat tool alongside the medium lasers. XL engine — side torso vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The PRC-1N is the original 3063 arena design. Walk nine with supercharger burst speed closes range before opponents can react. The spikes deal physical damage on collision. The medium lasers handle any direct weapons combat. Pure arena machine — the spike ramming concept works in enclosed arena environments in ways it does not in open battlefield conditions.

variants.name: PRC-2N

variants.name: PY-SR10
variants.overview: The Prey Seeker is a 15-ton ultralight BattleMech designed for speed, with a Magna 180 XXL engine pushing it to an impressive 194 km/h. Its small cockpit and XL gyro help free up tonnage, but the 'Mech only carries 3.5 tons of StarGuard CIV armor, making it vulnerable to incidental fire.
variants.capabilities: The Prey Seeker's speed is its greatest asset, but it comes at a cost. The 'Mech has minimal armament, with two medium re-engineered lasers providing defensive firepower. Its lack of jump jets, electronic warfare suites, and active probes means it relies entirely on speed to avoid detection. The Prey Seeker's armor is its biggest weakness; even glancing hits from behind can penetrate to internal structure.
variants.deployment: The base PY-SR10 mounts a pair of medium re-engineered lasers as its sole armament, reflecting the design's emphasis on speed and survivability over firepower. The re-engineered lasers offer a niche tactical advantage against opponents using advanced armor types, making the Prey Seeker unexpectedly effective in reconnaissance-by-fire roles against hardened or reflective-armored targets.

This configuration trades anti-special-armor capability for significantly greater raw firepower and improved accuracy, transforming the Prey Seeker from a pure scout into a credible hit-and-run striker capable of inflicting serious damage before disengaging at speed.

variants.name: PY-SR30

variants.capabilities: Walk twelve, run eighteen at fifteen tons on the XXL engine. XXL at fifteen tons means any significant hit is catastrophic. Walk twelve keeps this machine alive. XXL maintenance requires specialist procedures beyond standard XL expertise. The PY-SR30 carries three machine guns, a machine gun array, three light machine guns, and a light machine gun array. Walk twelve, run eighteen. Eight machine gun systems optimised for anti-infantry operations. The arrays coordinate simultaneous fire.
variants.deployment: The PY-SR30 is the 3141 anti-infantry field modification. Walk twelve closes to machine gun range before infantry formations can respond effectively. The machine gun arrays and individual guns together create a volume of fire that infantry cannot survive. Against armoured opponents the PY-SR30 has almost no capability. XXL maintenance specialist requirement applies.

variants.name: PWR-1X
variants.overview: The Prowler is a fifty-five ton arena machine built around a 385-rated IS XXL engine for walk seven, run ten, jump seven. Two variants. Mixed IS/Clan technology throughout.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at fifty-five tons on the XXL engine. The XXL at this weight means side torso damage is catastrophic. Walk seven and jump seven are the survival mechanisms. Mixed IS/Clan components create a two-track maintenance requirement. Supercharger is fitted on the base variant. The PWR-1X carries two ER large pulse lasers, two ER medium pulse lasers, and two ER small pulse lasers, with a supercharger for burst speed. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The Clan pulse laser suite provides accurate fire across all range bands. The supercharger enables burst speed beyond walk seven.
variants.deployment: The PWR-1X is the full-capability arena platform. Walk seven, jump seven, supercharger burst speed combined with accurate Clan pulse lasers makes this genuinely difficult to deal with in the arena environment. The XXL vulnerability means a single penetrating side torso hit ends the match. XXL and mixed-tech maintenance requires specialist procedures.

variants.name: PWR-1X1
variants.overview: The Prowler is a fifty-five ton arena machine built around a 385-rated IS XXL engine for walk seven, run ten, jump seven. Two variants. Mixed IS/Clan technology throughout.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump capability removed on the PWR-1X1. Two ER large lasers and two SRM-4 launchers. The jump jets and supercharger are removed. XXL engine remains. The ER large lasers extend the engagement range over the pulse laser suite of the original. The SRM-4s add close-range missile punch.
variants.deployment: The PWR-1X1 trades jump seven and the supercharger for heavier weapons and a different engagement profile. No jump capability is a significant reduction for a machine built around jump mobility. The ER large laser range is the compensation. SRM-4s handle close threats. XXL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: PUL-2V
variants.overview: The Pulverizer PUL-2V is a 90-ton assault 'Mech with a reputation for extreme durability and long-range striking power. As the signature command platform of Clan Wolverine, it prioritizes survivability over speed, relying on its thick armor and powerful weapons to get the job done.
variants.capabilities: The PUL-2V is a beast when it comes to taking a beating. The ferro-fibrous armor and CASE protection make it incredibly difficult to destroy, and the Shredder-II Enhanced ER PPC provides long-range firepower that's hard to match. The twin large lasers are useful for closer-range work, but the real showstopper is the Type III 'Great Bow' LRM-10 rack – it can rain down sustained indirect fire on enemy positions. Just be aware that the Guardian ECM Suite can be a bit finicky in the field, and the fifteen double heat sinks do get pushed to their limits during prolonged engagements.
variants.deployment: Armed with a Shredder-II Enhanced ER PPC, two standard large lasers, and a Type III 'Great Bow' LRM-10, this variant emphasizes sustained long-range firepower from a heavily protected platform. A Guardian ECM Suite reflects its intended role as a command 'Mech, disrupting enemy sensor networks while coordinating Wolverine forces. Fifteen double heat sinks manage the considerable weapons load.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: The Adder, called the Puma in IS intelligence reports, is a 35-ton Clan OmniMech built on a 210-rated Clan XL engine. Walk six, run nine with no jump capability on the base chassis. Fourteen configurations make it a widely varied light OmniMech. The twin ER PPC Prime configuration is what most Inner Sphere pilots think of when they hear the name.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at thirty-five tons. No jump jets on most configurations, which limits terrain exploitation options compared to jump-capable competitors at this weight. The Clan XL at thirty-five tons carries the standard catastrophic side torso vulnerability. The flamer that appears across most configurations handles infantry threats and is rarely the primary tactical tool. Configuration B carries an LB 5-X, a large pulse laser, two ER medium lasers, and a flamer. The LB 5-X provides cluster or slug ballistic fire at range. The large pulse laser is accurate at medium range. The ER mediums handle closer engagement. One ton of LB ammunition is the operational limit.
variants.deployment: Configuration B is a versatile medium-range configuration. The LB 5-X flexibility between cluster and slug rounds suits varied target types. The large pulse laser accuracy suits the Adder's engagement style. The flamer handles infantry. One ton of LB ammunition runs out quickly on active operations.

Each mode requires different maintenance protocols. LAM conversion equipment requires regular inspection. The S-PW-1LAM carries three ER medium lasers. Walk six, run nine in BattleMech mode. Three ER mediums with ten double heat sinks manage the thermal load effectively for sustained laser fire. No ammunition dependency across any of the three modes.
variants.deployment: The Pwwka operated with Manei Domini combined strike elements. The three operational modes provide flexibility that conventional BattleMechs lack — AirMech mode for rapid repositioning across obstacles, Fighter mode for aerospace operations. The ER mediums provide consistent energy fire without resupply concerns. LAM conversion equipment requires regular inspection that standard BattleMech techs are not trained for.

variants.name: QSM-3D
variants.overview: Kali Yama and Alphard Trading Corporation built the Quasimodo in 3140 as a fifty-five ton close-combat heavy evolved from the Hunchback design. Walk five, run seven, jump five on the 275-rated XL engine. Triple-strength myomer and a focus on melee capability define the design.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at fifty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Triple-strength myomer activates at elevated heat, boosting melee capability and speed. All-energy weapons generate the heat that triggers TSM. Jump five delivers the close-range suite from unexpected angles. The QSM-3D carries two ER medium lasers, three medium VSP lasers, and an ER small laser. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The VSP lasers adapt damage profile to range. The ER mediums extend energy reach. TSM activates at elevated heat. The weapons generate heat deliberately to trigger the TSM activation.
variants.deployment: The QSM-3D entered service with Free Worlds League urban assault formations. The TSM activation from the all-energy heat load makes this machine progressively more dangerous as the engagement continues. Jump five delivers close-range weapons from unexpected angles. XL engine vulnerability is the standing concern. The melee capability from TSM changes how opponents must defend against it.

variants.name: QKD-4G
variants.overview: Technicron Manufacturing built the Quickdraw in 2779 as a sixty-ton medium striker. Walk five, run seven, jump five on the 300-rated engine. Nine variants. The ankle actuators are the design's consistent maintenance concern — they are notoriously fragile and the first component I check on any Quickdraw.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at sixty tons. Ankle actuators are the persistent weak point — check them every inspection cycle. Standard engine on conventional variants — side torso survivability. Heat management has been a criticism of this design since the original 4G's thirteen single heat sinks proved insufficient. The QKD-4G is the original production model: four medium lasers, an LRM-10, and an SRM-4. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Thirteen single heat sinks — insufficient for the weapons load under sustained fire. The ankle actuator fragility is the persistent maintenance concern.
variants.deployment: The 4G established the Quickdraw's battlefield reputation during the Succession Wars. Walk five for a sixty-ton heavy is the speed advantage. The medium lasers, LRM-10, and SRM-4 cover all engagement ranges. The heat management problem and ankle fragility are the known issues. Check the ankles every cycle.

The QKD-4H places all four medium lasers in forward-firing positions and moves the SRM-4 to a rear arc. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The rear SRM-4 discourages pursuit. Forward firepower is increased by removing the rear-facing medium laser arcs.
variants.deployment: The 4H modifies the weapons arcs without changing the loadout. Forward medium laser concentration improves the primary engagement arc. The rear SRM-4 provides deterrence against pursuit. The ankle vulnerability and heat issues are unchanged from the 4G.

The QKD-5A replaces the LRM-10 with two additional medium lasers, giving six total, and keeps the SRM-4. Walk five, run seven, jump five. All ammunition dependency removed except the SRM-4. Six medium lasers at close range is solid energy volume.
variants.deployment: The 5A emerged for units without reliable LRM ammunition resupply. Six medium lasers with no LRM dependency simplifies logistics at the cost of indirect fire capability. The SRM-4 retains close-range missile punch. Heat management with six mediums is still a concern.

Double heat sinks address the 4G's heat management problem. Ferro-fibrous improves protection.
variants.deployment: The 5K was introduced in 3049 and directly addresses the Quickdraw's two most criticised weaknesses. Double heat sinks make the weapons loadout sustainable under sustained fire. Ferro-fibrous adds protection. The ankle vulnerability is unchanged — still check every cycle.

The QKD-5M carries four medium lasers, an LRM-10, and a one-shot SRM-4, with ferro-fibrous armour and CASE protection. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The one-shot SRM-4 fires once then is spent. CASE protects ammunition. Ferro-fibrous improves protection.
variants.deployment: The 5M adds CASE ammunition protection and ferro-fibrous armour to the standard configuration. The one-shot SRM-4 delivers a single close-range missile volley before becoming inert. CASE protects against ammunition explosion risks. The weapons otherwise match the 4G. Ankle vulnerability unchanged.

The QKD-C field modification replaces one rear-facing medium laser with a C3 slave, keeping five medium lasers and an SRM-4. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The C3 slave integrates targeting data from a network lance.
variants.deployment: The QKD-C is the network-integrated Quickdraw. One rear-facing medium laser is traded for C3 network access. The C3 targeting improvements benefit the remaining lasers and SRM. The modification is straightforward. Ankle vulnerability unchanged.

variants.deployment: The 8K is a modern upgrade combining MRM-30 medium-range missile volume with ER medium laser precision. The MRM-30 output at medium range is substantial for a sixty-ton machine. The ER mediums handle direct energy engagement. Endo steel and ferro-fibrous improve the structure and protection.

variants.deployment: The 5Mr reflects Jihad-era preference for precision fire and electronic enhancement over close-range volume. The ER medium laser range extension and Guardian ECM are the upgrades. Close-range firepower is reduced from the 5K variants. Guardian ECM provides electronic warfare protection. Ankle vulnerability unchanged.

variants.name: QKD-8X
variants.overview: Technicron Manufacturing built the Quickdraw in 2779 as a sixty-ton medium striker. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Thirteen variants. The ankle actuators are the design's consistent maintenance concern — fragile and the first component I check on any Quickdraw.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons. Ankle actuators are the persistent weak point — check them every inspection cycle. Standard engine on most conventional variants — side torso survivability. Heat management has been a criticism since the original 4G's thirteen single heat sinks proved insufficient. The QKD-8X carries a PPC, two medium lasers, and a TAG, with stealth armour and Guardian ECM. Walk five, run seven, no jump. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active. The PPC and stealth heat combined creates a thermal challenge. The TAG designates for guided munitions.
variants.deployment: The 8X is the stealth designation variant. The stealth armour and ECM make it difficult to target. The TAG adds force multiplier value. The combined PPC and stealth heat load requires careful management — the design's primary weakness is thermal discipline. No jump jets.

variants.name: QKD-8P
variants.overview: Technicron Manufacturing built the Quickdraw in 2779 as a sixty-ton medium striker. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Thirteen variants. The ankle actuators are the design's consistent maintenance concern — fragile and the first component I check on any Quickdraw.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at sixty tons. Ankle actuators are the persistent weak point — check them every inspection cycle. Standard engine on most conventional variants — side torso survivability. Heat management has been a criticism since the original 4G's thirteen single heat sinks proved insufficient. The QKD-8P carries a PPC, a Streak SRM-4, two medium lasers, and a TAG, with stealth armour, ECM, and a small cockpit. Walk five, run seven, no jump. The Streak SRM-4 adds guaranteed close-range missile hits. Otherwise similar stealth profile to the 8X.
variants.deployment: The 8P refines the 8X with a Streak SRM-4 for more reliable close-range missile capability. The stealth designation role is unchanged. The small cockpit is a pilot discomfort issue. The Streak fires on lock, conserving ammunition while the pilot manages the stealth heat load. No jump jets.

variants.name: QKD-9M
variants.overview: Technicron Manufacturing built the Quickdraw in 2779 as a sixty-ton medium striker. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Thirteen variants. The ankle actuators are the design's consistent maintenance concern — fragile and the first component I check on any Quickdraw.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five on the 300-rated XL engine. The QKD-9M carries two large lasers, an LRM-15, and a TAG. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The large lasers extend direct fire range. The LRM-15 provides heavier fire support than the standard LRM-10. The TAG designates for guided munitions.
variants.deployment: The 9M is the factory-built upgrade combining larger direct fire weapons with designation capability. The large lasers and LRM-15 together cover longer engagement ranges than the standard Quickdraw. The TAG adds force multiplier value. XL engine vulnerability. Ankle actuators still need checking.

variants.name: QKD-9G
variants.overview: Technicron Manufacturing built the Quickdraw in 2779 as a sixty-ton medium striker. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Thirteen variants. The ankle actuators are the design's consistent maintenance concern — fragile and the first component I check on any Quickdraw.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five on the 300-rated light engine. The QKD-9G carries two standard medium lasers, two ER medium lasers, a Streak SRM-6, two Streak SRM-4s, MASC, and a supercharger. Light engine — side torso survivability. MASC and supercharger together achieve burst speeds that make this the fastest Quickdraw variant.
variants.deployment: The 9G is the maximum speed Quickdraw. MASC and supercharger burst speed combined with the light engine create an unusually fast and durable machine. The Streak launchers guarantee missile hits at close range. The combined MASC, supercharger, and light engine maintenance load is substantial. Ankle actuators still need checking.

variants.overview: The Rabid Coyote is a 55-ton Clan heavy OmniMech built on a 275-rated Clan XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Variant 2, introduced in 3071, is likely among the last Coyote-produced OmniMechs given what happened to the Clan. It carries an integrated ECM suite and active probe alongside its weapons, making electronic warfare capability part of its base loadout.
variants.capabilities: Variant 2 carries six ATM-3 launchers, four ER medium lasers, an ECM suite, and an active probe. The six ATM-3s provide substantial missile flexibility across three munition types. The ECM disrupts enemy sensor and targeting systems. The active probe extends detection range. The four ER mediums handle direct fire. ATM ammunition management across six launchers and three munition types requires pre-mission planning.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 is an electronic warfare and adaptive fire platform. The ECM and active probe together provide detection and disruption capability beyond most OmniMech configurations at this weight. The ATM flexibility rewards warriors who understand munition selection. The ER mediums provide consistent direct fire. This is a sophisticated platform that rewards skilled warriors and experienced technical support.

variants.name: JL-1
variants.overview: Bannson Universal Unlimited built the Raider as a fifty-ton medium for the Dark Age with an ICE engine and triple-strength myomer for enhanced melee capability. Walk four, run six. Three variants. The ICE engine creates a very different maintenance profile from fusion-powered machines.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at fifty tons on the ICE engine. ICE maintenance is fundamentally different from fusion engine procedures — fuel, air intakes, exhaust systems. Triple-strength myomer activates at elevated heat to boost melee capability. No fusion reactor means no CASE requirement for ammunition. The JL-1 carries two MRM-10 launchers and a dual saw arm. Walk four, run six. The dual saw delivers devastating physical melee damage. The MRM-10s provide medium-range missile fire to close distance for the melee attack. TSM activates at elevated heat.
variants.deployment: The JL-1 is designed to close distance under MRM-10 fire and deliver saw strikes. Walk four is adequate for the close-combat doctrine. ICE maintenance requires fuel supply and different procedures from fusion machines. The dual saw is the primary combat tool — the MRM-10s get the machine to range.

variants.name: JL-3A
variants.overview: Bannson Universal Unlimited built the Raider as a fifty-ton medium for the Dark Age with an ICE engine and triple-strength myomer. Walk four, run six. Three variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at fifty tons on the ICE engine. ICE maintenance is fundamentally different from fusion engine procedures. Triple-strength myomer activates at elevated heat for melee enhancement. The JL-3A carries two MRM-10 launchers and a dual saw arm, with ferro-fibrous armour added over the JL-1.
variants.deployment: The 3A improves the JL-1 with ferro-fibrous protection. The dual saw and MRM-10s are unchanged. Ferro-fibrous provides better protection for the close-combat role where hits are expected. ICE maintenance applies throughout.

variants.name: JL-3B
variants.overview: Bannson Universal Unlimited built the Raider as a fifty-ton medium for the Dark Age with an ICE engine and triple-strength myomer for enhanced melee capability. Walk four, run six. Three variants. The ICE engine creates a very different maintenance profile from fusion-powered machines.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at fifty tons on the ICE engine. ICE maintenance is fundamentally different from fusion engine procedures — fuel, air intakes, exhaust systems. Triple-strength myomer activates at elevated heat to boost melee capability. No fusion reactor means no CASE requirement for ammunition. The JL-3B replaces the MRM launchers and dual saw with an all-energy suite and a retractable blade. A light PPC, two medium lasers, an ER small laser, and a small laser. Walk four, run six. The retractable blade replaces the dual saw for melee capability.
variants.deployment: The 3B converts the Raider from missile-and-saw to energy-and-blade. The ICE engine with auxiliary power amplifiers drives the energy weapons. The retractable blade is more compact than the dual saw. No ammunition dependency. ICE maintenance profile unchanged.

variants.name: JL-2
variants.overview: The Raider Mk II revised the original Raider design, addressing the lack of ranged firepower with a rotary autocannon while retaining the ICE engine and TSM concept. Fifty tons. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk three or four depending on variant. ICE engine — same non-fusion maintenance profile as the original Raider. TSM activates at elevated heat for melee enhancement. The rotary autocannon is the ranged capability addition over the original. The JL-2 carries a single Rotary AC/2 and nothing else. Walk three, run four on the 150-rated ICE engine. The Rotary AC/2 provides sustained long-range harassment fire. Two tons of ammunition. The retractable blade from the Raider series is retained for melee.
variants.deployment: The JL-2 is the range upgrade concept. The Rotary AC/2 provides sustained fire at distances the original Raider could not engage effectively. Two tons of ammunition manages well for harassment operations. Walk three is slow — this is a position and hold machine rather than a mobile raider. ICE maintenance applies.

variants.name: JL-3C
variants.overview: The Raider Mk II revised the original Raider design, addressing the lack of ranged firepower with a rotary autocannon while retaining the ICE engine and TSM concept. Fifty tons. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk three or four depending on variant. ICE engine — same non-fusion maintenance profile as the original Raider. TSM activates at elevated heat for melee enhancement. The rotary autocannon is the ranged capability addition over the original. The JL-3C carries a single Rotary AC/2 on the larger 200-rated ICE engine. Walk four, run six. The larger engine improves ground speed over the JL-2. The Rotary AC/2 is unchanged. Retractable blade retained.
variants.deployment: The 3C uses the larger ICE engine for better ground speed than the JL-2 while keeping the Rotary AC/2 harassment concept. Walk four versus walk three is a meaningful improvement. ICE maintenance applies. The retractable blade provides melee capability when opponents close range.

variants.name: RJN-101-X
variants.overview: The Raijin was developed for ComStar's rearming efforts after Tukayyid as a fifty-ton close-range striker. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine. Five variants including the experimental prototype.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at fifty tons on the XL engine. Walk six, run nine is fast for a fifty-ton medium. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Jump six provides terrain exploitation. The ER PPC is the primary long-range weapon across most variants. The RJN-101-X prototype carries three medium pulse lasers, an ER PPC, a Streak SRM-2, and a concealed one-shot SRM-6. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The one-shot SRM-6 was intended to surprise opponents at close range.
variants.deployment: The X prototype was rejected in favour of the standard production model, but some examples entered service. The concealed SRM-6 provides a single surprise close-range volley. After that strike the weapons suite is the standard ER PPC, pulse lasers, and Streak SRM-2. Prototype documentation applies for maintenance.

variants.overview: The Raijin was developed for ComStar's rearming efforts after Tukayyid as a fifty-ton close-range striker. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine. Five variants including the experimental prototype.

The RJN-101-A is the production standard: an ER PPC, three medium pulse lasers, an SRM-6, and a Streak SRM-2. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The ER PPC handles long-range engagement. The pulse lasers and SRM launchers close the fight.
variants.deployment: The A is the production Raijin. Walk six and jump six combined with ER PPC reach creates a capable striker. The medium pulse lasers are accurate at close range. The SRM-6 adds close missile volume. The Streak SRM-2 fires only on lock. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: RJN-101-B

The large pulse laser replaces missile systems with a more accurate energy weapon. The flamers handle infantry.
variants.deployment: The B emerged after ComStar lost Mongoose supply during Operation ODYSSEUS. The refit replaced the missile loadout with available energy weapons. The large pulse laser provides accurate medium-range fire. The flamers handle infantry threats. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: RJN-101-C
variants.overview: The Raijin is a fifty-ton medium developed for ComStar after Tukayyid. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine. Five variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at fifty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The RJN-101-C carries a large pulse laser, three ER medium lasers, and a Streak SRM-6, with an improved C3 computer and additional armour. The improved C3 coordinates the network lance rather than just participating in it.
variants.deployment: The C variant is the network command Raijin. The improved C3 makes it the lance coordinator. The weapons are capable enough for direct engagement alongside the coordination role. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: RJN-301-B
variants.overview: The Raijin was developed for ComStar's rearming efforts after Tukayyid as a fifty-ton close-range striker. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine. Five variants including the experimental prototype.

variants.deployment: The 301-B is the artillery spotter variant. The iNarc combined with Raijin speed makes it an effective forward observer that moves fast enough to reposition. The ER mediums and SRM launchers provide direct combat capability alongside the designation role. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: RJN-200-A
variants.overview: The Raijin II significantly upgraded the original design with a new endo steel chassis and improved armour. Fifty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six. Three variants built around the improved structural foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at fifty tons. Endo steel chassis — structural repair requires specific tech qualification. Improved armour over the original Raijin. The XL engine on the A variant and light engine on the B and C variants create different survivability profiles. The RJN-200-A carries an ER PPC, three ER medium lasers, and a Streak SRM-4. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The ER PPC provides long-range engagement. The ER mediums and Streak SRM-4 handle closer work.
variants.deployment: The 200-A is the baseline Raijin II. The ER PPC and ER medium combination covers long and medium range. The Streak SRM-4 fires on lock for reliable close-range missile hits. The endo steel chassis and improved armour are the structural improvements over the original Raijin. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: RJN-200-B
variants.overview: The Raijin II significantly upgraded the original design with a new endo steel chassis and improved armour. Fifty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six. Three variants built around the improved structural foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at fifty tons. Endo steel chassis — structural repair requires specific tech qualification. Improved armour over the original Raijin. The XL engine on the A variant and light engine on the B and C variants create different survivability profiles. The RJN-200-B carries four ER medium lasers, a TAG, and an ER small laser. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated light engine. Light engine — side torso survivability. The TAG designates for guided munitions. All-energy with no ammunition dependency.
variants.deployment: The 200-B is the light engine designation variant. The light engine survivability improvement is the key operational advantage. The TAG and ER medium combination makes it an effective combined-arms platform. The all-energy loadout suits extended operations. Produced at multiple facilities including Krupp on Terra.

variants.name: RJN-200-C
variants.overview: The Raijin II significantly upgraded the original design with a new endo steel chassis and improved armour. Fifty tons, walk six, run nine, jump six. Three variants built around the improved structural foundation.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated light engine. The RJN-200-C carries an ER PPC, two ER medium lasers, stealth armour, Guardian ECM, and a C3 slave. Light engine — side torso survivability. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active.
variants.deployment: The 200-C is the stealth C3 variant. The stealth armour and ECM combined with light engine survivability create a more durable stealth platform than XL stealth designs. The C3 slave integrates network targeting. The ER PPC and stealth heat load requires thermal discipline — active stealth and ER PPC fire together build heat quickly.

variants.name: MDG-1A
variants.overview: General Motors introduced the Rakshasa in 3055 as a seventy-five ton IS attempt to replicate the Clan Timber Wolf concept. Walk five, run seven on the 375-rated XL engine. Four variants. The design was never quite the Timber Wolf equivalent GM advertised it as.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk five for a heavy is the speed advantage. The endo steel chassis keeps the mass budget workable. The weapons loadout has been criticised as less capable than Clan equivalents at comparable tonnage. The MDG-1A carries two ER large lasers, two medium lasers, two LRM-10 launchers, and a medium pulse laser. Walk five, run seven on the XL engine. The ER large lasers provide extended-range direct fire. The LRM-10s add fire support. The pulse laser handles accurate close engagement.
variants.deployment: The MDG-1A is the original production model. Walk five for a heavy is the speed that justified comparing it to the Timber Wolf. The ER large lasers and LRM-10s cover multiple ranges. The Clan comparison is aspirational rather than accurate. XL engine vulnerability is the standing concern.

variants.name: MDG-1B
variants.overview: General Motors introduced the Rakshasa in 3055 as a seventy-five ton IS attempt to replicate the Clan Timber Wolf concept. Walk five, run seven on the 375-rated XL engine. Four variants. The design was never quite the Timber Wolf equivalent GM advertised it as.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk five for a heavy is the speed advantage. The endo steel chassis keeps the mass budget workable. The weapons loadout has been criticised as less capable than Clan equivalents at comparable tonnage. The MDG-1B replaces the ER large lasers with standard large lasers, keeping two medium lasers, two LRM-10s, and a medium pulse laser. Walk five, run seven. Standard large lasers generate less heat than ER equivalents at the cost of range.
variants.deployment: The 1B addresses heat management concerns with standard large lasers. The reduced range over the 1A is the tradeoff for better thermal balance under sustained fire. The LRM-10s and pulse laser are unchanged. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk five for a heavy is the speed advantage. The endo steel chassis keeps the mass budget workable. The weapons loadout has been criticised as less capable than Clan equivalents at comparable tonnage. The MDG-2A carries a Rotary AC/5, a large pulse laser, and four medium pulse lasers. Walk five, run seven. The Rotary AC/5 delivers sustained ballistic fire. The large pulse laser is accurate at medium range. Four medium pulse lasers at close range is the close-combat emphasis.
variants.deployment: The 2A shifts from the 1A's missile support concept to close-range firepower emphasis. The pulse laser suite combined with Rotary AC/5 sustained fire creates consistent pressure at medium and close range. The absence of LRM capability changes the tactical role entirely. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: MDG-1Ar
variants.overview: General Motors introduced the Rakshasa in 3055 as a seventy-five ton IS attempt to replicate the Clan Timber Wolf concept. Walk five, run seven on the 375-rated XL engine. Four variants. The design was never quite the Timber Wolf equivalent GM advertised it as.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk five for a heavy is the speed advantage. The MDG-1Ar is a Jihad-era refit carrying two snub-nose PPCs, two medium lasers, and two MML-7 launchers. Walk five, run seven. The snub-nose PPCs cover short to medium range. The MML-7s provide SRM/LRM flexibility. Standard medium lasers remain.
variants.deployment: The 1Ar is the Jihad refit that replaces the ER large lasers and LRM-10s with snub-nose PPCs and MML flexibility. The snub-nose avoids PPC minimum range complications. The MML-7s cover both fire support and close missile engagement. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: RMP-2G
variants.overview: The Rampage was originally designed for the Rim Worlds Republic in 2735 as an eighty-five ton assault platform. Walk three or four depending on variant. Four variants spanning the original and Clan-era upgrades.
variants.capabilities: Walk three or four at eighty-five tons. The 2G's 255-rated standard engine achieves walk three; the 4G and later variants use a 340-rated XL for walk four. Standard or XL engine depending on variant. The weapons cover multiple ranges without specialising. The RMP-2G carries an AC/10, an LRM-10, a large laser, two medium lasers, a flamer, and a machine gun. Walk three, run four on the 255-rated standard engine. The AC/10 provides direct ballistic fire. The LRM-10 adds indirect fire. The large laser extends direct fire reach. Standard engine survivability.
variants.deployment: The original Rampage from 2735. Walk three is slow but the standard engine keeps it fighting through side torso damage that ends XL designs. The weapons cover multiple ranges without complexity. Rim Worlds Republic production heritage is the historical context. Parts availability depends on supply chain access.

variants.name: RMP-4G
variants.overview: The Rampage was originally designed for the Rim Worlds Republic in 2735 as an eighty-five ton assault platform. Walk three or four depending on variant. Four variants spanning the original and Clan-era upgrades.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 340-rated XL engine. The RMP-4G carries a Gauss rifle, an LB 10-X, a large pulse laser, a medium laser, a flamer, and an AMS. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk four is the speed improvement over the original. The Gauss provides long-range precision. The LB 10-X adds ballistic flexibility. The AMS defends against missiles.
variants.deployment: The 4G is the Clan-era upgrade. Walk four, XL engine, Gauss rifle and LB 10-X ballistic combination, AMS defence. The Gauss accuracy at range is the primary improvement over the 2G. The AMS provides missile defence the original lacked. XL engine vulnerability is the survivability tradeoff.

variants.name: RMP-4G (Benboudaoud)

variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 340-rated XL engine. The Benboudaoud is a named configuration carrying an LRM-20, an SRM-4, an LB 10-X, two medium lasers, a flamer, an AMS, and a large pulse laser. XL engine. The LRM-20 replaces the Gauss with heavy missile fire support.
variants.deployment: The Benboudaoud is a named configuration built for a specific commander. The LRM-20 fire support capability combined with LB 10-X and pulse laser direct fire covers multiple roles. The AMS provides missile defence. XL engine vulnerability applies. Named machine — maintain to specific build documentation.

The three Streak SRM-2s provide guaranteed close-range missile hits. The AMS defends against incoming missiles.
variants.deployment: The 5G was designed for elite Republican Guard formations. The Streak SRM-2 triple mount provides reliable close-range missile fire. The LRM-10 and LB 10-X handle longer range. The AMS defends against counter-fire. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: RTX1-O
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Raptor in 3067 as a twenty-five ton IS OmniMech proof-of-concept to demonstrate Inner Sphere mastery of OmniMech technology. Walk seven, run ten on the 175-rated XL engine. Seven configurations.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at twenty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. Walk seven is fast enough that precise targeting against it is difficult. IS OmniMech technology means pod swaps are possible but less refined than Clan equivalents. The Prime carries two medium lasers, two small lasers, three LRM-5 launchers, and two machine guns. Walk seven, run ten. The LRM-5s provide modest fire support. The medium and small lasers handle direct engagement. Machine guns deal with infantry. XL engine vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The Prime is the most balanced Raptor configuration. The LRM-5s provide stand-off capability while the laser suite handles close engagement. Machine guns address infantry. Walk seven delivers everything fast. The IS OmniMech design proves functional if less refined than Clan equivalents.

Configuration A carries two large lasers and three small lasers. Walk seven, run ten. The large lasers extend direct fire range substantially. The small lasers handle close threats. All-energy with no ammunition dependency. XL engine vulnerability.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is for extended operations without supply. The large lasers provide genuine reach for a twenty-five ton light. No ammunition means no resupply concern. Three small lasers handle anything at close range. Walk seven maintains escape capability.

variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at twenty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. Configuration B carries three SRM-6 launchers and a small laser. Walk seven, run ten. Three SRM-6s at close range is substantial missile volume for twenty-five tons. One ton of ammunition per launcher. The small laser handles point-blank threats.
variants.deployment: Configuration B is the close-range missile saturation variant. Three SRM-6s simultaneously at close range overwhelms opponents above this weight class. One ton per launcher runs out fast on active operations. Walk seven closes distance quickly. XL vulnerability is severe if any of those SRM-6s detonate internally.

variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at twenty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. The AMS defends against missiles. Two additional heat sinks manage the thermal load.
variants.deployment: Configuration C is the energy saturation variant. Six medium lasers at close range creates a fire density that opponents cannot easily absorb. The AMS adds missile defence. Two extra heat sinks enable more aggressive cycling. Walk seven delivers the suite fast.

The Streak SRM-2s and small lasers provide minimal self-defence. Machine guns handle infantry. Walk seven keeps it out of close engagement.

variants.overview: The Raptor is a 25-ton Inner Sphere OmniMech built by Luthien Armor Works as a proof-of-concept for IS OmniMech technology. The 175-rated XL engine provides walk seven, run ten, jump seven across most configurations. Lightweight and fast, it is primarily a reconnaissance and fast strike platform.
variants.capabilities: Configuration F carries five ER medium lasers and three extra double heat sinks. Five ER mediums on a twenty-five ton chassis is an aggressive energy loadout. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The additional heat sinks manage the thermal load from sustained ER medium fire. All energy with no ammunition dependency. Heat cycling is still required under sustained fire.
variants.deployment: Configuration F is the maximum energy firepower variant. Five ER mediums at twenty-five tons threatens opponents well above this weight class at range. The XL engine vulnerability is severe at this tonnage. The jump capability and speed provide escape options when the armour runs thin. Warriors who use the speed and range together effectively exploit this configuration well.

The ER mediums handle direct combat in both environments. Torpedo tube seals and UMU maintenance require specific procedures.

variants.name: RPT-2X
variants.overview: The Raptor II is a forty-ton Word of Blake stealth infiltration machine built around a Void Signature System and 280-rated XL engine. Walk seven, run ten. Five variants. The stealth systems are the design identity and the primary maintenance challenge.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at forty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Void Signature System makes this machine genuinely difficult to detect visually and on sensors. VSS maintenance requires specific procedures not in standard tech manuals. Walk seven is the survival mechanism alongside the stealth. The RPT-2X carries a BattleMech Taser and two medium VSP lasers. Walk seven, run ten. The Taser disrupts enemy 'Mech systems without destroying armour. The VSP lasers adapt their damage profile to range. The Void Signature System makes this machine genuinely difficult to detect.
variants.deployment: The RPT-2X is the original Word of Blake variant from 3073. The VSS and Taser combination is for non-lethal capture operations — disable opponents without destroying them. The VSP lasers handle any direct combat requirement. VSS maintenance procedures are not in standard technical manuals.

variants.overview: The Raptor II is a forty-ton Word of Blake stealth infiltration machine built around a Void Signature System and 280-rated XL engine. Walk seven, run ten. Five variants. The stealth systems are the design identity and the primary maintenance challenge.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at forty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk seven, run ten. The ER lasers provide extended-range engagement under VSS cover. The Bloodhound extends detection range.
variants.deployment: The second Blakist variant shifts to combat capability over non-lethal capture. The ER laser suite engages from VSS-concealed positions at range. The Streak SRM-6 closes the engagement. The prototype Bloodhound probe is an additional maintenance complexity beyond the VSS itself.

Walk seven, run ten with MASC providing additional burst capability. The Streak SRM-6s guarantee close-range missile hits. No CASE, no ejection system — Republic production priorities.
variants.deployment: The 3X is the Republic Armed Forces variant. MASC burst speed combined with VSS makes it extraordinarily difficult to engage effectively. The Streak SRM-6 pair at close range is the primary combat delivery. The absence of CASE and ejection system reflects RAF cost-cutting choices that pilots noted with displeasure.

variants.deployment: The 5X replaces MASC with jump five for better terrain mobility rather than burst speed. Jump five at forty tons opens approach angles the MASC-equipped 3X cannot access. The ER lasers and MML-5s cover multiple engagement ranges. The VSS maintains stealth capability through the jump.
