The TSEMP cannon delivers electromagnetic pulses that shut down enemy 'Mech systems temporarily. The VSP lasers provide direct combat backup.
variants.deployment: The 2X2 upgrades the original's BattleMech Taser to a TSEMP cannon. The TSEMP provides temporary system shutdown capability that is more reliable than the Taser for disabling high-value targets. The VSP lasers handle direct combat. VSS maintenance requirement is unchanged.

variants.name: JR7-31
variants.overview: The Rattlesnake is a hand-built upgrade of the Jenner chassis developed under Project Trapdoor and issued to select ComStar units. The 245-rated XL engine provides walk seven, run ten, jump seven. Ferro-fibrous armour and seven medium lasers define the base configuration. These are individually crafted machines, not production runs.
variants.capabilities: The JR7-31 carries seven medium lasers and a Guardian ECM suite. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at thirty-five tons. Seven medium lasers at close range delivers a fire density that thirty-five tons normally cannot produce. Eleven double heat sinks manage the load but sustained firing of all seven simultaneously will build heat. The ECM provides electronic protection.
variants.deployment: The JR7-31 is an ambush and close-range devastation platform. The Guardian ECM degrades enemy targeting while the machine closes range. Seven medium lasers at close range then overwhelm most opponents of comparable or greater weight. Heat management is the pilot's discipline. The XL engine means any side torso damage is fatal, so getting hit is not in the tactical plan.

variants.name: JR7-31P
variants.overview: The Rattlesnake is a hand-built upgrade of the Jenner chassis developed under Project Trapdoor and issued to select ComStar units. The 245-rated XL engine provides walk seven, run ten, jump seven. Ferro-fibrous armour and seven medium lasers define the base configuration. These are individually crafted machines, not production runs.
variants.capabilities: The JR7-31P carries seven medium lasers, a small laser, and a C3 slave unit replacing the ECM. The C3 slave integrates targeting data from a lance network. The small laser adds a token extra close-range weapon. Losing the ECM removes the electronic protection the base variant carries. The C3 targeting benefit is the exchange.
variants.deployment: The P variant trades ECM protection for C3 network integration. The C3 targeting improvement at close range combined with seven medium lasers creates very accurate close-range fire. The Guardian ECM's absence means enemy targeting is unimpeded. Pilots running the P variant rely on speed and the C3 accuracy advantage rather than ECM disruption.

variants.name: JR7-31R (Gideon)
variants.overview: The Rattlesnake is a hand-built upgrade of the Jenner chassis developed under Project Trapdoor and issued to select ComStar units. The 245-rated XL engine provides walk seven, run ten, jump seven. Ferro-fibrous armour and seven medium lasers define the base configuration. These are individually crafted machines, not production runs.
variants.capabilities: The Gideon variant uses a Clan XL engine and carries three standard medium lasers, two Clan ER medium lasers, an ER small laser, a targeting computer, and an Angel ECM suite. The Clan XL requires Clan maintenance procedures on an IS chassis. The targeting computer improves accuracy across the mixed laser suite. The Angel ECM is the most sophisticated electronic warfare system in the Rattlesnake family.
variants.deployment: The Gideon is a Solaris VII arena build. The Clan XL and mixed weapons create a two-track maintenance requirement. The Angel ECM substantially degrades opponent targeting. The targeting computer combined with ER medium lasers creates accurate medium-range fire. This is a personal machine, not a production variant, and requires individual configuration documentation.

variants.name: RSN-2
variants.overview: The Rattlesnake II is a forty-five ton medium built for the Federated Suns with Clan-specification engine components and a focus on close-range laser firepower. Walk seven, run ten, jump five to seven depending on variant. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at forty-five tons. Clan XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Clan engine requires Clan maintenance procedures alongside IS chassis procedures. The laser suite is the combat identity across both variants. The RSN-2 carries six standard medium lasers and a small laser, with stealth armour. Walk seven, run ten, jump five. The stealth armour makes it difficult to target. Six medium lasers at close range is the combat delivery. Standard lasers rather than the Clan ER medium upgrade of the RSN-1.
variants.deployment: The RSN-2 incorporates stealth armour at the cost of some protection and weapon effectiveness over the RSN-1. The stealth and ECM combined with walk seven makes it difficult to target reliably. Six standard medium lasers at close range handle direct combat. Clan engine maintenance applies alongside IS chassis procedures.

variants.name: RSN-1
variants.overview: The Rattlesnake II is a forty-five ton medium built for the Federated Suns with Clan-specification engine components and a focus on close-range laser firepower. Walk seven, run ten, jump five to seven depending on variant. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at forty-five tons. Clan XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Clan engine requires Clan maintenance procedures alongside IS chassis procedures. The laser suite is the combat identity across both variants. The RSN-1 primary configuration carries four standard medium lasers, two Clan ER medium lasers, and an ER small laser, with Guardian ECM and jump seven. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The Clan ER mediums extend the energy engagement range. Jump seven is exceptional for a forty-five ton machine.
variants.deployment: The RSN-1 is the primary configuration. Jump seven at forty-five tons combined with Guardian ECM creates a machine that is hard to predict and hard to target. The Clan ER mediums reach farther than the standard mediums of the RSN-2. Clan engine maintenance alongside IS chassis procedures requires two-track technical support.

variants.name: RVN-1X
variants.overview: The Raven RVN-1X is a thirty-five ton electronic warfare BattleMech developed by the Capellan Confederation. As the first prototype of its kind, it entered service in 3024 as part of the Confederation's efforts to create force multipliers. The design philosophy of the Raven accepts that direct engagement is a tactical failure and instead focuses on electronic countermeasures, target designation, and sensor operations from standoff range.
variants.capabilities: From a maintenance standpoint, the Raven's electronics-heavy design means reliability can be an issue. We've found that the EW suite is prone to electromagnetic interference, which can disrupt communications and targeting systems. The 'Mech's light armor also makes it vulnerable in direct combat. On the plus side, the Raven's speed and agility make it a formidable opponent when used as intended – from standoff range.
variants.deployment: The original 3024 prototype was built around the massive Ceres Arms Electronic Warfare X-1 equipment, which suffered from reliability problems due to electromagnetic pulses disrupting communications and targeting systems. It carried a pair of medium lasers and an SRM launcher for self-defense, with a top speed of only eighty-six kilometers per hour.

variants.overview: The Raven RVN-1X is a thirty-five ton electronic warfare BattleMech developed by the Capellan Confederation. variants.deployment: This variant features the original prototype Triple Strength Myomer recovered during the raid on Bethel. The Capellan Confederation fitted the myomer to increase its ground speed, reasoning that since the Raven was designed for electronic warfare, the myomer's dangerous flaw of igniting when exposed to a catalyst gas was an acceptable risk. In practice, we've found the benefits outweigh the dangers for this platform.

The large laser makes it effective at medium ranges, but its lack of advanced sensors limits its ability to engage targets effectively. The 2X performs well as a light combatant, but its limitations become apparent when facing heavier opponents.

variants.overview: The Raven RVN-1X is a thirty-five ton electronic warfare BattleMech developed by the Capellan Confederation. As the first prototype of its kind, it entered service in 3024 as part of the Confederation's efforts to create force multipliers. The design philosophy of the Raven accepts that direct engagement is a tactical failure and instead focuses on electronic countermeasures, target designation, and sensor operations from standoff range.
variants.capabilities: From a maintenance standpoint, the Raven's electronics-heavy design means reliability can be an issue. We've found that the EW suite is prone to electromagnetic interference, which can disrupt communications and targeting systems. The 'Mech's light armor also makes it vulnerable in direct combat. On the plus side, the Raven's speed and agility make it a formidable opponent when used as intended – from standoff range.
variants.deployment: In my opinion, the Raven's greatest strength lies in its ability to quickly move around the battlefield and deliver accurate fire from unexpected angles. However, pilots should be aware that the lack of electronic warfare capabilities means this 'Mech is more susceptible to enemy detection and targeting.

variants.name: RVN-3L
variants.overview: The Raven was developed by the Capellan Confederation in 3024 as an electronic warfare platform around the Apple Churchill electronics suite. Thirty-five tons, walk six, run nine on the XL engine. The electronics are the point. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at thirty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Apple Churchill electronics suite is the design identity — it requires specialist calibration that standard 'Mech tech procedures do not cover. The EW suite reliability depends on that maintenance being done correctly. The RVN-3L carries a Narc missile beacon, two medium lasers, an SRM-6, and a TAG. Walk six, run nine. The full Apple Churchill electronics suite: Guardian ECM, Beagle active probe, Narc, and TAG. The Narc tags targets for guided munitions. The TAG designates. The weapons provide direct combat capability.
variants.deployment: The 3L is the most comprehensively equipped Raven for combined-arms designation work. The Narc and TAG together with Beagle sensor capability make it a force multiplier for any formation with missile or artillery support assets. The Guardian ECM protects during the forward operations the designation role requires. XL engine vulnerability applies.

This variant was exported to other powers, reflecting the Confederation's need for foreign currency.

The retained stealth armor gave the 4Lr a significant advantage in ambush engagements, allowing it to close on enemy scouts undetected before engaging with its enhanced weapons array.

variants.name: RVN-5L
variants.overview: The Raven RVN-1X is a thirty-five ton electronic warfare BattleMech developed by the Capellan Confederation. variants.deployment: The 5L variant shares the Raven II's VOX 280 XL engine and experimental Raven X's XL gyro, achieving higher speeds than earlier variants. Its loadout includes two ER medium lasers, an iNarc launcher with three tons of ammunition, TAG for artillery designation, and three Improved One-Shot SRM-2 launchers. Stealth armor powered by an Angel ECM suite ensures the 5L maintains the Raven family's tradition of electronic warfare excellence.

variants.name: RVN-5X
variants.overview: The Raven II is a forty-ton medium 'Mech that's all about electronic warfare. It's got a lightweight skeleton, a fast VOX 280 XL engine, and a bunch of stealth armor to make it hard to detect. The real kicker is the Firmir Hypnos TSEMP cannon, which can shut down enemy 'Mechs entirely.
variants.capabilities: The Raven II does electronic warfare like no other. Its Angel ECM suite and Bloodhound Active Probe make it a ghost on the battlefield. The TSEMP cannon's a game-changer for scout hunting and line-breaking ops. Just be careful not to overuse it, or you might fry your own electronics. The medium lasers are solid backup, but that MML-5 launcher in the left torso is a major weak spot - don't get hit there.
variants.deployment: The Raven II mounts the full suite of next-generation electronic warfare equipment, including Angel ECM and Bloodhound Active Probe, combined with the devastating Firmir Hypnos TSEMP cannon. The Ceres Metals Model 777 communications system integrates seamlessly with Angel ECM, while Apple Churchill 3000 targeting system works in concert with Bloodhound probe for unmatched battlefield awareness.

variants.name: RVN-3X
variants.overview: The Raven X is an experimental prototype developed by Hellespont Industrials on Sian during the Jihad. Thirty-five tons, walk six, run nine on the XL engine. A single configuration. The Angel ECM and Bloodhound active probe are the standout electronics.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at thirty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. All experimental systems — Angel ECM, Bloodhound active probe, Apollo fire control, X-pulse lasers, composite structure. Each requires specialist maintenance procedures. Prototype documentation throughout. The RVN-3X carries two medium X-pulse lasers, an MRM-20 with Apollo fire control, and a laser AMS, with an Angel ECM suite and Bloodhound active probe on a composite internal structure. Walk six, run nine. The composite structure is lighter than standard but has reduced structural integrity.
variants.deployment: The RVN-3X is a single-unit prototype. Every system on it is experimental or advanced beyond standard maintenance documentation. The Angel ECM outperforms Guardian ECM substantially. The Bloodhound detection range exceeds the Beagle. The Apollo MRM-20 accuracy is the combat standout. The composite structure requires specific repair procedures the composite material demands.

variants.name: RWD-R1
variants.overview: The Rawhide is a fifty-five ton medium built around a 275-rated XL engine for walk five, run seven, jump five. One production variant. Standard components throughout is the design philosophy.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at fifty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The standard components philosophy means parts are available from multiple suppliers and maintenance is straightforward compared to advanced-technology designs. The RWD-R1 carries an ER PPC, a medium X-pulse laser, and an MML-9. Walk five, run seven, jump five on the XL engine. The ER PPC provides long-range direct fire. The X-pulse laser is accurate at close range. The MML-9 covers SRM/LRM flexibility.
variants.deployment: The RWD-R1 is the only production Rawhide. The standard component philosophy means parts are available without specialist sourcing. The ER PPC and MML-9 together cover long and missile ranges. The X-pulse laser handles close work. Jump five provides terrain exploitation. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: RZK-9S
variants.overview: Bowie Industries introduced the Razorback in 3063 as a thirty-ton light on a light engine. Walk six, run nine. Four variants. The light engine is the design's consistent survivability advantage.
variants.capabilities: Walk six or seven depending on variant. Light engine on most variants — side torso survivability that XL competitors lack. The Razorback's survivability advantage in a weight class where XL engines are common is the design's selling point. The RZK-9S carries an ER large laser, a Streak SRM-4, and four machine guns on the light engine. Walk six, run nine. The ER large laser provides extended-range direct fire. The Streak SRM-4 fires on lock. The machine guns handle infantry.
variants.deployment: The 9S is the base Razorback from 3063. The light engine survivability advantage is real — side torso hits that end XL competitors leave the 9S fighting. The ER large laser reach combined with Streak accuracy and machine gun anti-infantry capability covers most threat types.

variants.name: RZK-9T
variants.overview: Bowie Industries introduced the Razorback in 3063 as a thirty-ton light on a light engine. Walk six, run nine. Four variants. The light engine is the design's consistent survivability advantage.
variants.capabilities: Walk six or seven depending on variant. Light engine on most variants — side torso survivability that XL competitors lack. The Razorback's survivability advantage in a weight class where XL engines are common is the design's selling point. The RZK-9T carries an ER PPC and four ER medium lasers on the light engine. Walk six, run nine. All-energy, no ammunition dependency. The ER PPC extends direct fire range substantially. Four ER mediums handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: The 9T emerged from supply chain disruptions forcing an all-energy design in 3066. No ammunition concerns simplify operations. The ER PPC range is a genuine improvement over the 9S's ER large laser. Light engine survivability preserved. The four ER mediums provide dense close-range energy coverage.

variants.name: RZK-10T
variants.overview: Bowie Industries introduced the Razorback in 3063 as a thirty-ton light on a light engine. Walk six, run nine. Four variants. The light engine is the design's consistent survivability advantage.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten on the 210-rated XL engine. The RZK-10T carries a heavy PPC and four ER small lasers. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk seven is faster than the standard Razorback. The heavy PPC hits hard at medium range. The ER small lasers handle close threats.
variants.deployment: The 10T gains walk seven at the cost of light engine survivability. The heavy PPC provides more punch per shot than earlier variants. The ER small lasers handle close range. XL engine vulnerability is the tradeoff for the speed and heavy PPC combination. Pilots who use walk seven aggressively to dictate engagement range get the most from the heavy PPC.

variants.name: RZK-10S
variants.overview: Bowie Industries introduced the Razorback in 3063 as a thirty-ton light on a light engine. Walk six, run nine. Four variants. The light engine is the design's consistent survivability advantage.
variants.capabilities: Walk six or seven depending on variant. Light engine on most variants — side torso survivability that XL competitors lack. The RZK-10S carries a snub-nose PPC, an MML-5, and two ER small lasers on the light engine, with an XL gyro and small cockpit freeing mass. Walk six, run nine. The snub-nose covers short to medium range. The MML-5 adds SRM/LRM flexibility.
variants.deployment: The 10S uses the XL gyro and small cockpit mass savings for weapons. The snub-nose PPC and MML-5 together cover both direct fire and missile ranges. The ER small lasers handle point-blank threats. The small cockpit is a pilot comfort issue. Light engine survivability preserved.

variants.name: RDS-2A
variants.overview: The Red Shift is a twenty-ton Word of Blake light built as an artillery spotter for combined-arms formations. Walk nine, run thirteen on the XL engine. Three variants with different electronics priorities.
variants.capabilities: Walk nine, run thirteen at twenty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. Walk nine is the survival mechanism. The TAG designation capability is the tactical identity across the design. The RDS-2A carries two medium pulse lasers and a TAG, with a Guardian ECM suite. Walk nine, run thirteen. The TAG designates for artillery and guided munitions. The medium pulse lasers provide accurate self-defence. The ECM degrades enemy targeting of both the Red Shift and its formation.
variants.deployment: The RDS-2A is the baseline production model from 3062, assigned to Word of Blake Militia units alongside Padilla artillery vehicles. Walk nine reaches forward designation positions quickly. The ECM provides electronic protection during forward operations. XL engine vulnerability is the standing concern.

variants.name: RDS-2B
variants.overview: The Red Shift is a twenty-ton Word of Blake light built as an artillery spotter for combined-arms formations. Walk nine, run thirteen on the XL engine. Three variants with different electronics priorities.
variants.capabilities: Walk nine, run thirteen at twenty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. Walk nine is the survival mechanism. The TAG designation capability is the tactical identity across the design. The RDS-2B carries two medium pulse lasers and a TAG, with a Beagle active probe replacing the ECM suite. Walk nine, run thirteen. The Beagle extends sensor coverage for reconnaissance. The TAG designates for guided munitions. The pulse lasers provide accurate direct defence.
variants.deployment: The 2B shifts from ECM protection to reconnaissance capability. The Beagle active probe finds hidden units and extends detection range. The TAG designation capability is unchanged. The ECM loss removes the electronic warfare protection the 2A provided. Units that need sensor coverage over ECM protection run the 2B.

variants.name: RDS-3A

The improved C3 coordinates the network lance. Four ER mediums provide direct combat capability.
variants.deployment: The 3A converts the Red Shift from artillery spotter to network coordinator during the Jihad era. The improved C3 replaces the TAG and ECM with lance coordination capability. Four ER mediums provide genuine combat capability rather than the token self-defence of earlier variants. Walk nine delivers the C3 coordination node wherever the lance needs it.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Regent is a ninety-ton Clan assault OmniMech on a 270-rated Clan standard engine. Walk three, run four. Five configurations. The standard engine — not XL — is the design's notable survivability choice at this weight class.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at ninety tons. Clan standard engine — side torso survivability. No XL vulnerability. The standard engine enables the Regent to absorb hits that kill most other Clan assault designs. Clan construction quality. Thirty-eight tons of pod space. Configuration A carries three ER PPCs with PPC capacitors, an ER medium laser, and a targeting computer. Walk three, run four. The targeting computer improves accuracy across all weapons. The PPC capacitors allow overcharge shots at higher heat cost. Three ER PPCs with capacitors is a severe heat event when fired simultaneously.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is the long-range fire platform drawing on the Awesome's legacy. The targeting computer makes the ER PPCs highly accurate. The capacitor overcharge option provides maximum damage at maximum thermal risk — use selectively. Three ER PPCs simultaneously is the heat event that shuts pilots down. Standard engine — side torso survivability.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: The Regent is a ninety-ton Clan assault OmniMech on a 270-rated Clan standard engine. Walk three, run four. Five configurations. The standard engine — not XL — is the design's notable survivability choice at this weight class.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at ninety tons. Clan standard engine — side torso survivability. No XL vulnerability. The standard engine enables the Regent to absorb hits that kill most other Clan assault designs. Clan construction quality. Thirty-eight tons of pod space. Configuration B carries two ER PPCs, an Ultra AC/20, two ER medium lasers, and four ER micro lasers. Walk three, run four. The UAC/20 in double-tap mode at close range combined with ER PPCs at range creates layered fire across multiple distances.
variants.deployment: Configuration B is the combined ballistic and energy assault platform. The ER PPCs handle long range, the UAC/20 dominates close range. The ER mediums and micro lasers cover the intermediate and close-range gaps. Standard engine survivability. The UAC/20 ammunition is the operational management task.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: The Regent is a ninety-ton Clan assault OmniMech on a 270-rated Clan standard engine. Walk three, run four. Five configurations. The standard engine — not XL — is the design's notable survivability choice at this weight class.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at ninety tons. Clan standard engine — side torso survivability. No XL vulnerability. The standard engine enables the Regent to absorb hits that kill most other Clan assault designs. Clan construction quality. Thirty-eight tons of pod space. Configuration C carries a HAG/40 and an improved heavy Gauss rifle. Walk three, run four. Two weapons. The HAG/40 spreads ballistic projectiles across multiple armour locations. The improved heavy Gauss delivers concentrated accurate fire. Both weapons are ammunition-dependent.
variants.deployment: Configuration C is the maximum ballistic devastation platform. The HAG/40 spread combined with the improved heavy Gauss concentrated fire creates damage across different armour profiles simultaneously. Ammunition supply for both systems is the critical logistics requirement. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: D
variants.overview: The Regent is a ninety-ton Clan assault OmniMech on a 270-rated Clan standard engine. Walk three, run four. Five configurations. The standard engine — not XL — is the design's notable survivability choice at this weight class.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at ninety tons. Clan standard engine — side torso survivability. No XL vulnerability. The standard engine enables the Regent to absorb hits that kill most other Clan assault designs. Clan construction quality. Thirty-eight tons of pod space. Configuration D carries four improved heavy medium lasers, two LRM-15s, two Ultra AC/2s, two LB 2-X ACs, and a small pulse laser. Walk three, run four. The nickname Maulermann reflects the sustained harassment fire concept. Multiple weapons covering every range band.
variants.deployment: Configuration D is the sustained fire support platform. The UAC/2s and LB 2-X ACs maintain long-range pressure. The LRM-15s add indirect fire. The improved heavy medium lasers handle close engagement. The small pulse laser covers point-blank threats. Multiple ammunition types require comprehensive pre-mission planning.

variants.name: Prime
variants.overview: The Regent is a ninety-ton Clan assault OmniMech on a 270-rated Clan standard engine. Walk three, run four. Five configurations. The standard engine — not XL — is the design's notable survivability choice at this weight class.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at ninety tons. Clan standard engine — side torso survivability. No XL vulnerability. The standard engine enables the Regent to absorb hits that kill most other Clan assault designs. Clan construction quality. Thirty-eight tons of pod space. The Prime carries three ER large lasers, a large pulse laser, two medium pulse lasers, a Streak SRM-4, an LB 20-X, and a micro pulse laser. Walk three, run four. The three ER large lasers cover extended range. The pulse lasers and Streak SRM-4 handle medium and close range. The LB 20-X adds ballistic flexibility.
variants.deployment: The Prime is the generalist multi-range platform. The ER large lasers engage at distance. The pulse laser suite handles medium and close engagement precisely. The LB 20-X cluster and slug options add ballistic flexibility. The Streak SRM-4 fires on lock for reliable close-range missile capability. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: UBM-1A
variants.overview: The Revenant UBM-1A is a 30-ton quadrupedal drone BattleMech designed for autonomous operation. It was originally produced by the Word of Blake during the Jihad as a cheap, expendable sentry to bolster ground defenses against coalition forces. The Republic of the Sphere later refined the design into the UBM-2R series, transforming it into a practical defensive asset.
variants.capabilities: The Revenant's slow speed (97 kph) is compensated by its durability and respectable armor protection for its weight class. Its quad configuration provides stability on uneven ground, but lack of jump jets limits tactical flexibility in rough terrain. The primary loadout consists of four Martell extended range medium lasers paired with four MainFire light machine guns, giving it effective anti-infantry and anti-armor capability at medium range. The laser-heavy loadout eliminates ammunition dependency for its primary weapons.
variants.deployment: In the field, we've found that the Revenant UBM-1A is most effective when used as a defensive asset, utilizing its lasers to pick off targets at medium range. Its armor protection holds up well against small arms and light anti-tank missiles. However, be aware that the robotic cockpit can be prone to erratic behavior if subjected to electronic countermeasures.

variants.name: UBM-2R
variants.overview: The Revenant is a 30-ton quadrupedal drone BattleMech produced by the Word of Blake during the Jihad as a cheap autonomous sentry. The 180-rated standard engine provides walk six, run nine. The quad configuration provides stability on rough terrain. The UBM-2R is the armed combat version.
variants.capabilities: The UBM-2R carries four ER medium lasers and four light machine guns. Walk six, run nine on the standard engine. The ER mediums provide medium-range anti-armour fire. The light machine guns handle infantry and battle armour. The quad stability makes this a steady firing platform. No jump capability. The standard engine survives side torso damage.
variants.deployment: The UBM-2R deploys as an autonomous sentry and area denial platform. The ER mediums provide meaningful engagement range. The light machine guns handle infantry threats. Low cost and stable design make it a reliable if unspectacular defensive asset. The standard engine survivability means individual units persist through engagements that would kill XL-equipped competitors.

variants.deployment: This variant trades the base model's laser-heavy loadout for two LRM-5 launchers backed by a pair of extended range small lasers. This configuration allows the Revenant to provide indirect fire support from behind cover, complementing other drone variants in combined-arms formations. We've found that operating in pairs provides effective suppressive fire during raids.

The simplified weapon loadout reduces maintenance requirements, an advantage for autonomous units operating with limited technical support.

The C3 network integration allows it to share targeting data with other Republic units, dramatically improving the accuracy of the less sophisticated combat variants it accompanies.

variants.name: UBM-2R7
variants.overview: The Revenant is a thirty-ton quadrupedal drone built by the Word of Blake during the Jihad as an inexpensive autonomous platform. Walk six, run nine. The UBM-2R7 is an engineering and recovery variant.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 180-rated standard engine. The UBM-2R7 carries no weapons. Engineering and recovery equipment only. Quad configuration for stability on rough terrain. Standard engine — side torso survivability.
variants.deployment: The UBM-2R7 is a non-combat battlefield support variant. The engineering equipment handles recovery, obstacle clearing, and field construction tasks without exposing human crews. The quad stability suits rough terrain operations. No weapons means it requires constant escort in contested environments.

XL engine vulnerability is particularly severe at this weight class.

variants.name: NH-1A
variants.overview: The Rook NH-1A is a 55-ton medium BattleMech with a reputation for being practical and affordable. It originated from a RetroTech design on New Hessen in 3074, conceived as an energy-weapon complement to ammunition-dependent designs. The NH-1A has undergone modernization, incorporating current technology while retaining its emphasis on firepower over speed.
variants.capabilities: The NH-1A's capabilities are centered around its Tiegart Maximum extended-range PPC and four Hellion-V medium lasers, providing effective intermediate firepower. Its Sutel Precision Line small pulse laser handles anti-infantry duties. The 'Mech has a modest top speed of 64 km/h, but the Rawlings 45i improved jump jets provide an impressive 180-meter jump range. Twelve double heat sinks manage thermal load efficiently, although sustained alpha strikes still generate significant heat.
variants.deployment: The NH-1A makes a solid addition to any lance due to its versatility and moderate firepower. The original design's limitations are largely mitigated by modernization, making it a reliable choice for medium-range engagements.

variants.name: PPR-6T
variants.overview: Vandenberg MilTech built the Salamander as an eighty-ton fire support assault platform around three LRM launchers. Walk four, run six on the XL engine. Six variants. The design is a dedicated long-range bombardment platform.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at eighty tons. XL engine on most variants — side torso vulnerability. Three LRM launchers are the design identity. Ammunition management across three launchers is the consistent operational overhead. The medium lasers are self-defence, not the primary combat tool. The PPR-6T carries two LRM-20s, a large pulse laser, and two medium pulse lasers. Walk four, run six on the XL engine. The large pulse laser replaces the third LRM-20 with accurate direct fire capability. The pulse suite handles close engagement precisely.
variants.deployment: The 6T trades the third LRM-20 for direct fire capability. The large pulse laser and medium pulse lasers provide accurate close-range fire that the base model completely lacks. Two LRM-20s still deliver heavy fire support. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: PPR-7S
variants.overview: Vandenberg MilTech built the Salamander as an eighty-ton fire support assault platform around three LRM launchers. Walk four, run six on the XL engine. Six variants. The design is a dedicated long-range bombardment platform.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four on the 320-rated light engine. The PPR-7S carries three Artemis IV-guided LRM-15s and two ER medium lasers. Light engine — side torso survivability. Jump four. The Artemis IV guidance improves LRM accuracy.
variants.deployment: The 7S addresses the Salamander's mobility limitations that became apparent on Melissia. The light engine provides survivability. Jump four allows terrain exploitation unavailable to earlier variants. The Artemis LRM-15s are accurate. The ER mediums extend the backup energy range.

variants.name: PPR-7T
variants.overview: Vandenberg MilTech built the Salamander as an eighty-ton fire support assault platform around three LRM launchers. Walk four, run six on the XL engine. Six variants. The design is a dedicated long-range bombardment platform.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the XL engine. The PPR-7T carries two Extended LRM-15s and one Extended LRM-10. The ELRM systems reach substantially beyond standard LRM range — opponents at standard LRM maximum range cannot reply effectively. No close-range weapons at all.
variants.deployment: The 7T is the maximum stand-off Salamander. The ELRM engagement distance pushes fire support beyond any opponent's ability to close quickly. No close-range weapons means anything that closes stays in range indefinitely — constant escort is essential. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: SRTH-1O
variants.overview: Ronin Inc built the Sarath for the Principality of Regulus as a fifty-ton quad OmniMech with a turret. Walk five, run seven on the 250-rated XL engine. The 360-degree turret is the distinctive feature — it allows weapon engagement in any direction without turning the chassis.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The quad chassis provides firing stability. The turret allows 360-degree weapon engagement — a tactical advantage that changes how the machine is positioned. Turret control systems require specific maintenance procedures. The Prime carries a heavy PPC, a light PPC, two ER medium lasers, and an ER small laser in the turret, with a Beagle active probe. Walk five, run seven. The turret allows 360-degree weapon engagement without chassis rotation. The Beagle extends sensor coverage.
variants.deployment: The Prime is the baseline Sarath for Principality of Regulus forces. The turret weapon engagement is the tactical advantage — the quad chassis holds aim while the turret tracks independently. The heavy PPC hits hard at medium range. The Beagle active probe adds sensor capability. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: SRTH-1OA
variants.overview: Ronin Inc built the Sarath for the Principality of Regulus as a fifty-ton quad OmniMech with a turret. Walk five, run seven on the 250-rated XL engine. The 360-degree turret allows weapon engagement in any direction without turning the chassis.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The quad chassis provides firing stability. The turret allows 360-degree weapon engagement without chassis rotation — a tactical advantage that changes positioning decisions. Turret control systems require specific maintenance procedures. Configuration A carries two LRM-15s, two MML-3s, and two ER small lasers in the turret, with jump five. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The LRM-15s provide fire support. The MML-3s add SRM/LRM flexibility at modest scale. The ER small lasers handle close threats.
variants.deployment: Configuration A converts the Sarath to a turret-mounted fire support platform with jump five. The LRM-15s fire from the 360-degree turret regardless of chassis orientation. Jump five provides positioning. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: SRTH-1OB
variants.overview: Ronin Inc built the Sarath for the Principality of Regulus as a fifty-ton quad OmniMech with a turret. Walk five, run seven on the 250-rated XL engine. The 360-degree turret allows weapon engagement in any direction without turning the chassis.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The quad chassis provides firing stability. The turret allows 360-degree weapon engagement without chassis rotation — a tactical advantage that changes positioning decisions. Turret control systems require specific maintenance procedures. Configuration B carries a plasma rifle, two medium lasers, four ER flamers, and an ER small laser in the turret. Walk five, run seven. The plasma rifle superheats targets while dealing damage. The ER flamers handle infantry and force heat problems on opponents. No jump capability.
variants.deployment: Configuration B is the thermal disruption and anti-infantry platform. The plasma rifle and ER flamers together create severe heat problems for opponents. The 360-degree turret delivers this suite regardless of threat direction. No jump capability. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: MN1-D
variants.overview: The Sarissa is a fifty-ton primitive medium built in the Free Worlds League era as an affordable militia machine. Walk four, run six. Standard construction throughout. Primitive components require period-specific documentation.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at fifty tons on the primitive standard engine. Primitive components — maintenance documentation differs from standard production variants. Parts are not interchangeable with non-primitive equivalents. The binary laser cannon is the most distinctive weapon. The MN1-D carries a binary laser cannon, a medium laser, a small laser, and a machine gun on the primitive standard engine. Walk four, run six. The binary laser cannon fires two beams simultaneously — substantial energy output for a fifty-ton primitive design.
variants.deployment: The MN1-D was produced at Corean/GM's Futuna facility around 3080 for militia duty ranging from civil unrest to conventional combat. The binary laser cannon is the primary weapon. Primitive construction documentation applies throughout. Standard replacement parts do not fit without modification.

variants.name: SQS-TH-001
variants.overview: The Sasquatch is an eighty-five ton assault built by Word of Blake, powered by an experimental XXL engine on the 002 and 003 variants. Walk four or five depending on variant. Three variants, all carrying the Word of Blake reputation for maintenance complexity.
variants.capabilities: Walk four or five at eighty-five tons. The 001 prototype used an XL engine; the 002 and 003 production models use a large IS XXL engine. The XXL at this weight provides walk five but with extraordinary side torso vulnerability. XXL maintenance requires specialist procedures beyond standard XL expertise. The SQS-TH-001 prototype carries a Gauss rifle, four medium pulse lasers, two machine guns, an SRM-6, an AMS, and a small laser on the 340-rated XL engine. Walk four, run six, jump four. The prototype uses an XL rather than the production XXL.
variants.deployment: The prototype carried a broader weapon loadout than the production model. Walk four, jump four on an eighty-five ton machine. The XL engine adds vulnerability. The Gauss provides long-range accuracy. The prototype was stolen before Blakist forces could prevent it — the production design was changed specifically to complicate reverse-engineering.

variants.name: SQS-TH-002
variants.overview: The Sasquatch is an eighty-five ton assault built by Word of Blake, powered by an experimental XXL engine on the 002 and 003 variants. Walk four or five depending on variant. Three variants, all carrying the Word of Blake reputation for maintenance complexity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven on the 425-rated Large IS XXL engine. The SQS-TH-002 carries a Gauss rifle and three medium X-pulse lasers. The IS XXL provides walk five at this weight but is extraordinarily vulnerable to side torso damage. The X-pulse lasers are accurate at close range. The Gauss provides long-range precision.
variants.deployment: The 002 is the production Sasquatch, redesigned after the prototype theft. Walk five, run seven on the XXL engine changes the tactical profile. The XXL side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe — any penetrating hit on either side torso is likely catastrophic. The X-pulse accuracy is the close-range capability. Specialist XXL maintenance throughout.

variants.name: SQS-TH-003
variants.overview: The Sasquatch is an eighty-five ton assault built by Word of Blake, powered by an experimental XXL engine on the 002 and 003 variants. Walk four or five depending on variant. Three variants, all carrying the Word of Blake reputation for maintenance complexity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump eight on the 425-rated Large IS XXL engine. The SQS-TH-003 trades the Gauss rifle and large shield for improved jump jets and carries two medium X-pulse lasers, a large pulse laser, and a small laser. Jump eight on an eighty-five ton machine. All-energy with no ammunition.
variants.deployment: The 003 is the jump-capable Sasquatch. Jump eight at eighty-five tons is the tactical standout — few opponents can match that jump performance at this weight. The XXL vulnerability at this weight means any significant side torso damage ends the engagement. The pulse laser suite handles combat at multiple range bands.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: Clan Coyote built the Savage Coyote as an eighty-five ton OmniMech showcasing their Advanced Tactical Missile technology. Walk three, run four on the 255-rated Clan XL engine. Seven configurations. Forty-five tons of pod space is the defining feature.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at eighty-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk three is slow for the weight class. The forty-five tons of pod space is the design's tactical strength. Clan construction quality. ATM launchers appear across multiple configurations. Configuration A carries a Gauss rifle, an ER large laser, three ATM-6 launchers, three medium pulse lasers, and an AMS, with jump three. Walk three, run four, jump three. The jump capability at this weight opens terrain options unavailable to ground-bound assault variants. The ATM-6s provide missile flexibility.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is the mobile close-range assault variant. Jump three at eighty-five tons is a tactical surprise. The Gauss handles long-range precision, the ER large laser covers medium range, and the ATM-6 and pulse laser suite closes the engagement. AMS provides missile defence. Clan XL side torso vulnerability applies.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: Clan Coyote built the Savage Coyote as an eighty-five ton OmniMech showcasing their Advanced Tactical Missile technology. Walk three, run four on the 255-rated Clan XL engine. Seven configurations. Forty-five tons of pod space is the defining feature.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at eighty-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk three is slow for the weight class. The forty-five tons of pod space is the design's tactical strength. Clan construction quality. ATM launchers appear across multiple configurations. Configuration B carries two ER large lasers, a large pulse laser, an Ultra AC/5, six small pulse lasers, and four ATM-3 launchers. Walk three, run four. The ER large lasers and large pulse laser cover long and medium range. The UAC/5 adds sustained ballistic fire. The small pulse lasers handle close threats.
variants.deployment: Configuration B is the multi-range sustained fire platform. The ER large lasers engage at range. The large pulse laser and UAC/5 cover medium engagement. The small pulse lasers saturate anything at close range. The ATM-3s add small missile flexibility. Walk three means positioning before the battle starts.

variants.name: Prime
variants.overview: Clan Coyote built the Savage Coyote as an eighty-five ton OmniMech showcasing their Advanced Tactical Missile technology. Walk three, run four on the 255-rated Clan XL engine. Seven configurations. Forty-five tons of pod space is the defining feature.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at eighty-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk three is slow for the weight class. The forty-five tons of pod space is the design's tactical strength. Clan construction quality. ATM launchers appear across multiple configurations. The Prime carries two ATM-12 launchers, an ER PPC, an LB 10-X, three ER medium lasers, and two ER small lasers. Walk three, run four. The ATM-12s provide three-munition tactical flexibility at heavy missile scale. The ER PPC handles long-range direct fire. The LB 10-X adds ballistic flexibility.
variants.deployment: The Prime emphasises multi-range combat capability. The ATM-12 and ER PPC combination covers approach fire at multiple munition types. The LB 10-X adds close-range ballistic options. The ER mediums and ER small lasers close the engagement. Pre-loading the correct ATM munition type is the key preparation step.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: Clan Coyote built the Savage Coyote as an eighty-five ton OmniMech showcasing their Advanced Tactical Missile technology. Walk three, run four on the 255-rated Clan XL engine. Seven configurations. Forty-five tons of pod space is the defining feature.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at eighty-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk three is slow for the weight class. The forty-five tons of pod space is the design's tactical strength. Clan construction quality. ATM launchers appear across multiple configurations. Configuration C carries an ER PPC, two ER large lasers, two ATM-9 launchers, and three ER medium lasers, with jump three and a targeting computer. Walk three, run four, jump three. The targeting computer improves accuracy across all weapons. The ER PPC and ER large lasers handle long range.
variants.deployment: Configuration C is the precision long-range platform with jump capability. The targeting computer makes the ER PPC and ER large laser combination highly accurate. The ATM-9s provide missile flexibility. Jump three adds positioning options. Walk three means the jump capability matters more for positioning than ground speed does.

variants.name: Z
variants.overview: Clan Coyote built the Savage Coyote as an eighty-five ton OmniMech showcasing their Advanced Tactical Missile technology. Walk three, run four on the 255-rated Clan XL engine. Seven configurations. Forty-five tons of pod space is the defining feature.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at eighty-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk three is slow for the weight class. The forty-five tons of pod space is the design's tactical strength. Clan construction quality. ATM launchers appear across multiple configurations. Configuration Z carries two improved ATM-12 launchers, an ER large pulse laser, and two ER medium lasers, with a Nova CEWS system. Walk three, run four. The iATM-12 provides enhanced missile performance over standard ATM-12. The Nova CEWS provides both ECM and active probe capability.
variants.deployment: Configuration Z is The Society's experimental variant. The Nova CEWS provides comprehensive electronic warfare. The iATM-12 improvement over standard ATM is the weapons upgrade. The ER large pulse laser accuracy is the direct fire standout. iATM ammunition supply requires planning.

variants.name: J
variants.overview: Clan Coyote built the Savage Coyote as an eighty-five ton OmniMech showcasing their Advanced Tactical Missile technology. Walk three, run four on the 255-rated Clan XL engine. Seven configurations. Forty-five tons of pod space is the defining feature.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at eighty-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk three is slow for the weight class. The forty-five tons of pod space is the design's tactical strength. Clan construction quality. ATM launchers appear across multiple configurations. Configuration J carries an LB 10-X, two ER large lasers, a large pulse laser, and four small pulse lasers, with five improved jump jets. Walk three, run four, jump five. Jump five on an eighty-five ton machine. Improved jump jets provide enhanced aerial control.
variants.deployment: Configuration J is the maximum jump mobility variant. Jump five at eighty-five tons with improved jets is a tactical advantage few opponents can match at this weight class. The ER large lasers and large pulse laser provide direct fire capability. The LB 10-X adds ballistic flexibility. Small pulse lasers saturate close-range threats.

variants.name: W
variants.overview: Clan Coyote built the Savage Coyote as an eighty-five ton OmniMech showcasing their Advanced Tactical Missile technology. Walk three, run four on the 255-rated Clan XL engine. Seven configurations. Forty-five tons of pod space is the defining feature.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at eighty-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk three is slow for the weight class. The forty-five tons of pod space is the design's tactical strength. Clan construction quality. ATM launchers appear across multiple configurations. Configuration W carries four large pulse lasers, two small pulse lasers, two flamers, an ER medium laser, and a light TAG, with five improved jump jets. Walk three, run four, jump five. The TAG designates for guided munitions. The large pulse laser suite provides accurate medium-range fire.
variants.deployment: Configuration W is the jump reconnaissance and designation variant. Five improved jump jets at eighty-five tons creates approach vectors no opponent expects. The TAG designation adds force multiplier value. Four large pulse lasers deliver accurate fire. The flamers handle infantry. A configuration that contributes through designation as much as direct combat.

variants.name: SCB-9A
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Scarabus in 3053 as a thirty-ton fast scout. Walk ten, run fifteen on the 300-rated XL engine. Two variants. The speed and TAG designation capability are the design's primary contributions.
variants.capabilities: Walk ten, run fifteen at thirty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. Walk ten keeps this machine alive. The TAG and Guardian ECM provide electronic support. Two medium lasers and two small lasers are the self-defence suite. The SCB-9A carries two medium lasers, two small lasers, a TAG, and a Guardian ECM suite. Walk ten, run fifteen. The TAG designates for guided munitions. The ECM degrades enemy targeting. Walk ten is the survival mechanism.
variants.deployment: The 9A is the original 3053 production model. Walk ten forward-bases the TAG and ECM where no conventional scout reaches quickly enough to intercept. The ECM protects the 9A during forward operations. The lasers are self-defence. XL engine vulnerability at this weight is severe.

variants.name: SCB-9T
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Scarabus in 3053 as a thirty-ton fast scout. Walk ten, run fifteen on the 300-rated XL engine. Two variants. The speed and TAG designation capability are the design's primary contributions.
variants.capabilities: Walk ten, run fifteen at thirty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. Walk ten keeps this machine alive. The TAG and Guardian ECM provide electronic support. Two medium lasers and two small lasers are the self-defence suite. The SCB-9T carries the same weapons as the 9A — two medium lasers, two small lasers, TAG, and ECM — with triple-strength myomer. Walk ten, run fifteen with TSM boosting speed further at elevated heat. The weapons generate the heat that triggers TSM.
variants.deployment: The 9T adds TSM to the standard Scarabus concept. Walk ten becomes faster still when TSM activates. The same designation and ECM capability as the 9A. The TSM activation allows physical attacks at boosted speed as an additional option. A specialist modification for pilots who understand the TSM heat threshold.

variants.name: UCU-F4
variants.overview: The Scarecrow is a forty-ton mixed-technology medium built for anti-infantry duty. Walk five, run seven, jump three on the 200-rated XL engine. Two variants. B-pods, machine guns, and flamers are the weapons philosophy.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump three at forty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Mixed IS and Clan components create a two-track maintenance requirement. The anti-infantry weapons suite is the design identity. Chameleon Light Polarization Shield provides sensor masking on the base variant. The UCU-F4 carries three ER medium lasers, two medium pulse lasers, two B-pods, eight light machine guns, two light machine gun arrays, and two ER flamers. Walk five, run seven, jump three. The Chameleon Light Polarization Shield provides sensor masking. The machine gun arrays coordinate simultaneous fire.
variants.deployment: The UCU-F4 deploys ahead of friendly lines to identify and eliminate infantry threats. The machine gun volume handles infantry formations. The B-pods protect against battle armour. The ER mediums and pulse lasers handle any armoured opposition. The CLPS provides some protection during forward operations. Mixed tech maintenance requires two-track procedures.

variants.name: UCU-F4r 'Hobbled Scarecrow'
variants.overview: The Scarecrow is a forty-ton mixed-technology medium built for anti-infantry duty. Walk five, run seven, jump three on the 200-rated XL engine. Two variants. B-pods, machine guns, and flamers are the weapons philosophy.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump three at forty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Mixed IS and Clan components create a two-track maintenance requirement. The anti-infantry weapons suite is the design identity. Chameleon Light Polarization Shield provides sensor masking on the base variant. The Hobbled Scarecrow replaces the machine gun arrays and Chameleon Light Polarization Shield with three standard medium lasers. Walk five, run seven, jump three. The three added medium lasers increase direct combat firepower while removing the CLPS sensor masking and the machine gun anti-infantry volume.
variants.deployment: The Hobbled Scarecrow is typically a field modification where the CLPS and machine gun arrays were unavailable. The additional medium lasers provide more direct combat firepower at the cost of the dedicated anti-infantry and sensor masking capabilities. Units operating the Hobbled Scarecrow accept those tradeoffs given the availability constraints.

variants.name: SCP-1N
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Scorpion in 2570 as a fifty-five ton quadrupedal fire support platform. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated engine. Eleven variants. The quad chassis provides stable firing at speed. The massive engine leaves minimal room for weapons — that's the design's persistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at fifty-five tons. The quad stability is genuine — this machine holds aim better at walk six than bipedal equivalents. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The massive engine at fifty-five tons leaves limited weapons capacity. The SCP-1N is the original 2570 model: a PPC and an SRM-6. Walk six, run nine on the standard 330-rated engine. The quad stability makes the PPC effective at range. The SRM-6 handles close engagement.
variants.deployment: The 1N entered service in 2570 and few genuine originals survive. The quad stability is the tactical advantage over bipedal competitors at walk six. The PPC provides long-range fire. The SRM-6 closes the engagement. Most remaining examples have been through multiple rebuilds.

variants.name: SCP-1N (Wendall)
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Scorpion in 2570 as a fifty-five ton quadrupedal fire support platform. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated engine. Eleven variants. The quad chassis provides stable firing at speed. The massive engine leaves minimal room for weapons — that's the design's persistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at fifty-five tons. The quad stability is genuine — this machine holds aim better at walk six than bipedal equivalents. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The massive engine at fifty-five tons leaves limited weapons capacity. The Wendall is a field variant with a large laser replacing the PPC. Walk six, run nine. The large laser generates less heat than the PPC and provides adequate range. The SRM-6 handles close engagement.
variants.deployment: The Wendall emerged when MechWarrior Wendall Puritan II's PPC failed and no replacement was available. The large laser substitution is a field pragmatic solution. The large laser heat management is more forgiving than the PPC. Named after the pilot who first ran this configuration.

variants.name: SCP-1O
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Scorpion in 2570 as a fifty-five ton quadrupedal fire support platform. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated engine. Eleven variants. The quad chassis provides stable firing at speed. The massive engine leaves minimal room for weapons — that's the design's persistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at fifty-five tons. The quad stability is genuine — this machine holds aim better at walk six than bipedal equivalents. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The massive engine at fifty-five tons leaves limited weapons capacity. The SCP-1O upgrades to an ER PPC and keeps the SRM-6. Walk six, run nine. The ER PPC extends engagement range substantially over the standard PPC. The heat output is severe — the massive engine at fifty-five tons means heat sinks are limited.
variants.deployment: The 1O was introduced in 3049 as Star League technology spread. The ER PPC range advantage over the standard PPC is meaningful. The heat management problem is real — the ER PPC fires hotter and the quad chassis's heat dissipation is limited by the massive engine taking internal space.

variants.name: SCP-12S
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Scorpion in 2570 as a fifty-five ton quadrupedal fire support platform. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated engine. Eleven variants. The quad chassis provides stable firing at speed. The massive engine leaves minimal room for weapons — that's the design's persistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated light engine. The SCP-12S carries an LB 10-X and an SRM-6. Light engine — side torso survivability. The LB 10-X provides cluster and slug ballistic options. The SRM-6 handles close engagement.
variants.deployment: The 12S is a Defiance Industries variant based on recovered Scorpion LAM project data from Hesperus II. The light engine provides survivability improvements the standard engine variants already had, but the LB 10-X adds tactical flexibility the original PPC lacked. Light engine survivability is the consistent quality.

variants.name: SCP-12C
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Scorpion in 2570 as a fifty-five ton quadrupedal fire support platform. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated engine. Eleven variants. The quad chassis provides stable firing at speed. The massive engine leaves minimal room for weapons — that's the design's persistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated XL engine. The SCP-12C carries an ER PPC, an iNarc launcher, an ER small laser, and a C3i network computer. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The iNarc designates targets for guided munitions. The C3i integrates network targeting.
variants.deployment: The 12C deploys as a networked designation platform. The iNarc and C3i together make it a force multiplier in combined-arms formations. The quad stability improves iNarc accuracy at walk six. The ER PPC handles direct combat. XL engine vulnerability is the survivability concern.

variants.name: SCP-12K
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Scorpion in 2570 as a fifty-five ton quadrupedal fire support platform. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated engine. Eleven variants. The quad chassis provides stable firing at speed. The massive engine leaves minimal room for weapons — that's the design's persistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated XL engine. The SCP-12K carries a snub-nose PPC, an MML-9, an ER medium laser, and a C3 master computer. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The C3 master coordinates the network lance. The MML-9 provides SRM/LRM flexibility.
variants.deployment: The 12K is the network command Scorpion. The C3 master makes it the targeting coordination hub. The snub-nose PPC covers close to medium range. The MML-9 provides missile flexibility. Ferro-fibrous armour improves protection. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: SCP-1TB
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Scorpion in 2570 as a fifty-five ton quadrupedal fire support platform. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated engine. Eleven variants. The quad chassis provides stable firing at speed. The massive engine leaves minimal room for weapons — that's the design's persistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated light engine. The SCP-1TB carries two light PPCs and an MML-9. Light engine — side torso survivability. The light PPCs provide accurate short-to-medium range energy fire. The MML-9 adds SRM/LRM flexibility.
variants.deployment: The 1TB features light PPCs and MML flexibility within component availability constraints that prevented improved armour or CASE. The light engine survivability is the consistent quality. The light PPCs avoid minimum range complications. The MML-9 covers both fire support and close engagement.

variants.name: SCP-10M
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Scorpion in 2570 as a fifty-five ton quadrupedal fire support platform. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated engine. Eleven variants. The quad chassis provides stable firing at speed. The massive engine leaves minimal room for weapons — that's the design's persistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten on the 385-rated XL engine. The SCP-10M carries a heavy PPC and an LRM-10. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk seven is faster than standard Scorpion variants. The heavy PPC hits harder than a standard PPC at medium range.
variants.deployment: The 10M is the fast Scorpion. Walk seven combined with quad stability creates a mobile precision fire platform. The heavy PPC range and accuracy at walk seven is the primary capability. The LRM-10 adds indirect fire support. XL engine vulnerability applies. Deployed in cavalry and fire support roles.

variants.name: SCP-1BR
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Scorpion in 2570 as a fifty-five ton quadrupedal fire support platform. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated engine. Eleven variants. The quad chassis provides stable firing at speed. The massive engine leaves minimal room for weapons — that's the design's persistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated light engine with MASC providing burst speed. The SCP-1BR carries an ER PPC and a Streak SRM-6. Light engine survivability. MASC provides burst acceleration for positioning. The Streak SRM-6 fires on lock for guaranteed close-range missile hits.
variants.deployment: The 1BR combines light engine survivability with MASC burst speed and Streak SRM reliability. MASC allows rapid repositioning or closing distance. The Streak SRM-6 guarantees missile hits when fired. The ER PPC handles long-range engagement. MASC transmission wear requires regular maintenance.

variants.name: SCP-2N
variants.overview: Brigadier Corporation built the Scorpion in 2570 as a fifty-five ton quadrupedal fire support platform. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated engine. Eleven variants. The quad chassis provides stable firing at speed. The massive engine leaves minimal room for weapons — that's the design's persistent criticism.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated light engine. The SCP-2N carries a plasma rifle, two MML-3 launchers, and a TAG. Light engine survivability. The plasma rifle superheats targets while dealing damage. The TAG designates for guided munitions. The MML-3s add modest missile flexibility.

variants.name: C

variants.deployment: The Clan C variant is the most advanced Scorpion configuration, using Clan components on the IS quad chassis. The ER PPC range combined with ATM-6 flexibility covers multiple engagement scenarios. Light engine survivability. Pre-loading the correct ATM munition type is the key preparation step.

variants.name: SCG-WD1
variants.overview: The Scourge is a sixty-five ton heavy built for the Republic Armed Forces using standardised technology. Walk five, run seven, jump four on the 325-rated XL engine. Four variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump four at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Jump four provides terrain exploitation. Standardised technology means parts are straightforward to source and maintenance is not demanding by heavy 'Mech standards. The SCG-WD1 carries a Gauss rifle, four ER medium lasers, and a medium pulse laser. Walk five, run seven, jump four. Standard technology throughout for ease of supply. The Gauss provides accurate long-range fire. The ER mediums cover medium engagement. The pulse laser handles close work.
variants.deployment: The WD1 is the original 3131 production Scourge. Standard technology means parts are straightforward to source. The Gauss and ER medium combination covers the full engagement spectrum. Jump four provides terrain exploitation. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: SCR-1X-LAM

One configuration. The prototype was redirected from initial testing back to quick-strike concept before production.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump four in BattleMech mode on the 275-rated standard engine. Three operational modes: BattleMech, AirMech, and Aerospace Fighter. variants.overview: The Scylla is a Clan Hell's Horses hundred-ton assault on the Storm Giant chassis with a 400-rated Clan XL engine. Walk four, run six, jump four on the base variant. Three variants. The jump capability at a hundred tons is the chassis's tactical distinguisher.

variants.deployment: Variant 2 was introduced around 3079 after Clan Steel Viper's annihilation. The HAG/20 arm mounts replace the standard weapons suite with spread ballistic damage. Jump four opens positioning options. Clan XL side torso vulnerability applies.

variants.name: C-SRP-O Invictus
variants.overview: The Seraph C-SRP-O Invictus is an assault OmniMech that's earned its reputation as a formidable frontline unit. Its unique triple-strength myomer system allows it to transform from a plodding assault platform into a surprisingly mobile threat. We've found that this design excels in sustained firepower roles, but its limitations are just as notable.
variants.capabilities: The Invictus configuration prioritizes sustained firepower with an Ultra AC/10, dual MML-5 launchers, and a Streak SRM-6. While it's not the most agile OmniMech, the triple-strength myomer system can still deliver rapid closes when needed. However, we've seen issues with heat generation, which can limit its ability to engage the TSM. The design's heavy ammunition dependency is also a concern.
variants.deployment: The Invictus configuration features an Ultra AC/10, dual MML-5 launchers, a Streak SRM-6, and a snub-nose PPC for layered firepower across all ranges. Paired ER medium lasers and a retractable blade add close-range capability. Three tons of autocannon ammunition and CASE protect the pilot. The primary criticism of the Invictus is its failure to generate sufficient heat to reliably activate the fixed triple-strength myomer, a limitation the ammunition-conservative Streak system only exacerbates.

variants.deployment: The 5M is a significant capability upgrade. The LRM-20 provides genuine fire support output rather than the token LRM-5 of standard variants. The UAC/5 double-tap improves sustained ballistic fire. Jump five is the jump upgrade. XL engine adds vulnerability.

variants.name: SHD-2D2

variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump three across the conventional variants. The balanced weapons loadout — ballistic, missile, and energy — is the design philosophy. The SHD-2D2 carries an AC/5, an LRM-5, two medium lasers, and two Streak SRM-2s. Walk five, run seven, jump three. The Streak SRM-2s replace standard SRM-2s with guaranteed missile hits when locked. An additional medium laser improves close-range energy capability.
variants.deployment: The 2D2 was introduced in 3049 as a refit of 2H chassis purchased by the Federated Commonwealth. The Streak SRM-2 upgrade is the key improvement — reliable missile hits rather than potentially wasted salvoes. The additional medium laser adds close-range energy density.

variants.name: SHD-2Ht
variants.overview: The Shadow Hawk has been a workhorse medium since 2467 and is found in almost every military in the Inner Sphere. The SHD-2Ht is a ComStar variant built around anti-battle armour capability, using five Streak SRM-2 launchers alongside a large laser and two medium lasers on the standard 275-rated engine.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five on the standard engine at fifty-five tons. The five Streak SRM-2s provide guaranteed missile hits against battle armour and light targets when locked. The large laser handles longer-range direct fire. The medium lasers fill the mid-range energy role. Standard engine survivability is fully preserved. The Streak launchers require lock before firing.
variants.deployment: Com Guard commanders grouped SHD-2Ht units into dedicated anti-infantry and anti-battle armour teams. The five Streak SRM-2s create a volume of guaranteed missile hits that battle armour formations cannot easily survive. The large laser and mediums handle any armoured opposition. The Streak lock requirement means the pilot cannot fire missiles on uncertain targets.

variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump seven on the XL engine. The plasma rifle superheats targets while dealing damage. The medium VSP laser adapts its damage profile to range. variants.deployment: The SHD-8L is a disruption striker. Jump seven delivers the plasma rifle to range from unexpected angles. The VSP laser handles what the plasma cannon cannot address efficiently. The MML-5 adds missile flexibility. The XL engine means side torso damage is fatal, so the jump capability is also the primary survival tool.

variants.name: SHD-5R

variants.name: SHY-3B
variants.overview: The Shen Yi is a sixty-five ton Capellan heavy built around stealth armour and a Guardian ECM suite on a 260-rated XL engine. Walk four, run six. Hellespont Lite Stealth armour with thirteen tons of coverage makes it genuinely hard to detect at range, which changes the tactical dynamic entirely for a front-line heavy.
variants.capabilities: The SHY-3B carries two MRM-20s, an ER large laser, and two medium pulse lasers. The MRM-20s provide medium-range missile density. The ER large laser handles longer-range direct fire. The pulse lasers cover close engagement. Stealth armour doubles heat generation while active, which compounds with the weapons heat load and requires careful thermal discipline. The XL engine adds side torso vulnerability.
variants.deployment: The SHY-3B is a front-line heavy that approaches under stealth cover rather than accepting fire on the way in. The ECM disrupts enemy targeting. The MRM-20 density at medium range is the primary offensive tool once in position. Heat management with stealth armour active during combat is demanding and the pilot must understand the thermal budget before committing to an engagement.

variants.name: SHY-5B
variants.overview: Hellespont Industries built the Shen Yi as a sixty-five ton Capellan stealth heavy for extended frontline operations. Walk four, run six on the XL engine. Two variants. The stealth armour and Guardian ECM are the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at sixty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The stealth armour doubles heat generation while active. The Guardian ECM degrades enemy targeting. Stealth and ECM require specialist maintenance beyond standard procedures. The SHY-5B carries two LRM-20s and a large laser. Walk four, run six on the XL engine. The LRM-20 pair delivers heavy indirect fire. The large laser handles direct backup. Stealth armour and ECM are retained from the 3B.
variants.deployment: The 5B is the fire support Shen Yi, trading the stealth operation concept for heavy LRM-20 bombardment while retaining stealth for approach protection. The LRM-20 pair at range under stealth cover creates an unusual fire support platform. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: SH-1V
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Shiro for the DCMS as a seventy-five ton heavy on the 375-rated XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Two variants. The twenty-one tons of hardened armour is the design's defining survivability feature — it reduces incoming damage from all sources.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Twenty-one tons of hardened armour significantly reduces incoming damage. Hardened armour doubles the mass-per-point of protection compared to standard armour, which is why the design can mount so little weapons mass. The SH-1V carries four LRM-10s and an LB 2-X on the XL engine. Walk five, run seven. The LRM-10 quadruple launcher creates substantial missile fire. The LB 2-X adds long-range ballistic harassment. The hardened armour provides exceptional protection during the LRM fire support role.
variants.deployment: The 1V is the primary DCMS production model. Four LRM-10s provide overwhelming missile fire volume. The hardened armour means this machine can sustain fire support positions under return fire better than any comparable design. The XL engine is the vulnerability concern. XL engine side torso damage ends the engagement despite the hardened armour.

variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Twenty-one tons of hardened armour significantly reduces incoming damage. variants.deployment: The 2P replaces the LB 2-X harassment with an ER PPC for genuine long-range direct fire alongside the LRM-10 fire support. The ER PPC range threatens opponents well beyond the LRM-10's normal minimum range. The hardened armour provides the same protection as the 1V. XL engine vulnerability applies.
