The Rotary AC/5 delivers sustained ballistic fire at high rate. The Artemis LRM-10 improves missile accuracy. The ER large laser extends direct fire reach.
variants.deployment: The SKW-2F is the base Shockwave. The Rotary AC/5 sustained fire rate is the design's primary combat capability. The Artemis LRM-10 adds accurate fire support. The ER large laser handles long-range direct engagement. XL engine vulnerability.

variants.name: SKW-4G
variants.overview: The Shockwave is a fifty-ton medium built for front-line combat with heavy armour as a priority. Walk five, run seven on the 250-rated XL engine. Four variants. The design emphasises durability over firepower density.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Eleven tons of standard armour is above average for the weight class. The Rotary AC/5 is the weapons identity across the base variants. The SKW-4G replaces the ER large laser with a large X-pulse laser and removes the Artemis IV. Walk five, run seven. The X-pulse laser is accurate against moving targets at close range. The Rotary AC/5 and LRM-10 remain.
variants.deployment: The 4G trades the ER large laser range and Artemis LRM accuracy for X-pulse close-range precision. The X-pulse laser is effective against fast-moving opponents. The Rotary AC/5 sustained fire remains the primary capability. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: SKW-6H
variants.overview: The Shockwave is a fifty-ton medium built for front-line combat with heavy armour as a priority. Walk five, run seven on the 250-rated XL engine. Four variants. The design emphasises durability over firepower density.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Eleven tons of standard armour is above average for the weight class. The Rotary AC/5 is the weapons identity across the base variants. The SKW-6H replaces the Rotary AC/5 with a UAC/10 and removes the Artemis fire control. Walk five, run seven. The UAC/10 hits harder per shot than the Rotary AC/5. The ER large laser and LRM-10 remain.
variants.deployment: The 6H was introduced in 3102 with heavier ballistic fire replacing the Rotary AC's rate of fire. The UAC/10 per-shot damage is substantially higher than the Rotary AC/5. The LRM-10 retains fire support capability without Artemis guidance. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: SKW-8X
variants.overview: The Shockwave is a fifty-ton medium built for front-line combat with heavy armour as a priority. Walk five, run seven on the 250-rated XL engine. Four variants. The design emphasises durability over firepower density.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Eleven tons of standard armour is above average for the weight class. The Rotary AC/5 is the weapons identity across the base variants. The SKW-8X carries a Thumper Cannon and a UAC/10. Walk five, run seven. The Thumper Cannon fires artillery rounds with battlefield artillery range. The UAC/10 handles direct combat. Two weapons replacing the three-weapon standard suite.
variants.deployment: The 8X is the artillery Shockwave. The Thumper Cannon provides extreme-range indirect fire capability that no standard LRM system can match. The UAC/10 handles any direct engagement. Two weapons is simpler to manage than the three-weapon standard. Thumper ammunition supply requires dedicated logistics.

variants.name: SHG-2H
variants.overview: The Shogun is an eighty-five ton assault platform with a Star League lineage, built around jump jets and heavy missile armament. Walk three, run four, jump three. Four variants. The jump capability at assault weight is the tactical differentiator.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three at eighty-five tons. Standard engine on the IS variants — side torso survivability. The jump capability provides positioning options unavailable to ground-bound assaults. The Kitushi frame requires regular maintenance attention to prevent alignment issues with the jump jets. The SHG-2H carries an ER PPC, two Artemis IV-guided LRM-15s, four Streak SRM-2s, a medium laser, and a medium pulse laser. Walk three, run four, jump three. Ferro-fibrous armour with CASE. The Streak SRM-2s fire on lock for guaranteed hits.
variants.deployment: The 2H is the definitive Shogun. The Artemis LRM-15 accuracy combined with Streak SRM-2 reliability creates consistent fire across multiple ranges. The ER PPC handles long-range direct engagement. Jump three at eighty-five tons provides terrain options. The Kitushi frame jump jet alignment requires regular maintenance.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: The Shogun is an eighty-five ton assault platform with a Star League lineage, built around jump jets and heavy missile armament. Walk three, run four, jump three. Four variants. The jump capability at assault weight is the tactical differentiator.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three on the Clan standard engine. The Shogun C carries an ER PPC, two Artemis IV-guided LRM-20s, and four Streak SRM-6 launchers. Clan engine — requires Clan maintenance procedures alongside IS chassis. The LRM-20 upgrade over the 2H's LRM-15 substantially increases missile volume.
variants.deployment: The C variant uses a Clan engine with upgraded weapons. The LRM-20 and Streak SRM-6 combination at assault weight creates overwhelming missile output at multiple range bands. The Clan engine requires two-track maintenance. The Streak SRM-6 volume at close range is formidable.

variants.name: SHG-2E
variants.overview: The Shogun is an eighty-five ton assault platform with a Star League lineage, built around jump jets and heavy missile armament. Walk three, run four, jump three. Four variants. The jump capability at assault weight is the tactical differentiator.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three at eighty-five tons. Standard engine on the IS variants — side torso survivability. The jump capability provides positioning options unavailable to ground-bound assaults. The Kitushi frame requires regular maintenance attention to prevent alignment issues with the jump jets. The SHG-2E carries a standard PPC, two LRM-15s, and two SRM-6s. Walk three, run four, jump three. Standard PPC instead of ER PPC reduces range at lower heat. The SRM-6s are standard rather than Streak.
variants.deployment: The 2E appeared before the 2H's refit and uses a standard PPC instead of the ER PPC. The standard PPC generates less heat at shorter range. The SRM-6s replace the Streak SRM-2s with less missile precision but more volume. Field maintenance simplification was the driver.

variants.name: SHG-2F
variants.overview: The Shogun is an eighty-five ton assault platform with a Star League lineage, built around jump jets and heavy missile armament. Walk three, run four, jump three. Four variants. The jump capability at assault weight is the tactical differentiator.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three at eighty-five tons. Standard engine on the IS variants — side torso survivability. The jump capability provides positioning options unavailable to ground-bound assaults. The Kitushi frame requires regular maintenance attention to prevent alignment issues with the jump jets. The SHG-2F carries an ER PPC, two LRM-15s, and two SRM-6s. Walk three, run four, jump three. The ER PPC restores long-range direct fire capability. The SRM-6s are standard rather than Streak. Wolf's Dragoons' baseline configuration.
variants.deployment: The 2F is the Wolf's Dragoons baseline Shogun, the configuration associated with them following the Fourth Succession War refit. The ER PPC restoration is the key improvement over the 2E. The LRM-15s and SRM-6s provide combined missile fire. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: SHG-2F (Trisha)
variants.overview: The Shogun is an eighty-five ton assault platform with Star League lineage, built around jump jets and heavy missile armament. Walk three, run four, jump three. Seven variants. The jump capability at assault weight is the tactical differentiator.
variants.capabilities: Walk three or four at eighty-five tons. Standard engine on IS variants — side torso survivability. The Kitushi frame requires regular jump jet alignment to prevent wear-related issues. The Trisha is a named salvage configuration: two LB 5-X ACs, two SRM-6s, and a snub-nose PPC. Walk three, run four, jump three. The LB 5-X cluster option is useful against lighter opponents. The snub-nose PPC covers close to medium range without minimum range complications.
variants.deployment: The Trisha was assembled from damaged equipment on Outreach after the Word of Blake bombardment. Component choices were driven by what survived. Named machine — maintain to specific salvage documentation.

variants.name: SHG-3E
variants.overview: The Shogun is an eighty-five ton assault platform with Star League lineage, built around jump jets and heavy missile armament. Walk three, run four, jump three. Seven variants. The jump capability at assault weight is the tactical differentiator.
variants.capabilities: Walk three or four at eighty-five tons. Standard engine on IS variants — side torso survivability. The Kitushi frame requires regular jump jet alignment to prevent wear-related issues. The SHG-3E carries two LRM-15s, two Streak SRM-6s, and a snub-nose PPC, with CASE II ammunition protection. Walk three, run four, jump three. The Streak SRM-6s provide guaranteed close-range missile volume. The snub-nose PPC avoids minimum range complications.
variants.deployment: The 3E is Clan Sea Fox's mercenary market Shogun using IS technology base rather than Clan components. CASE II ammunition protection is a meaningful safety improvement. The Streak SRM-6 reliability and snub-nose PPC range coverage are the weapons improvements.

variants.name: C 2
variants.overview: The Shogun is an eighty-five ton assault platform with Star League lineage, built around jump jets and heavy missile armament. Walk three, run four, jump three. Seven variants. The jump capability at assault weight is the tactical differentiator.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three on the Clan standard engine. The C 2 carries an ER PPC, two Streak LRM-15s, and two Streak SRM-6s, with ferro-lamellor armour. The Streak LRM-15s guarantee LRM hits when locked. The Streak SRM-6s add guaranteed close-range volume.
variants.deployment: The C 2 upgrades the original Clan C with Streak LRM-15 guaranteed hits and ferro-lamellor armour for cluster munitions resistance. Streak LRM-15s fire only on lock — every missile in the salvo hits. The C 2 is the most capable Shogun variant against missile-focused opponents.

variants.name: C 3
variants.overview: The Shogun is an eighty-five ton assault platform with Star League lineage, built around jump jets and heavy missile armament. Walk three, run four, jump three. Seven variants. The jump capability at assault weight is the tactical differentiator.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four on the 340-rated Clan XL engine. The C 3 carries an ER PPC, two LRM-15s, and two ATM-6 launchers. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Walk four, jump four on an eighty-five ton assault. ATM-6 flexibility adds three-munition missile adaptability.
variants.deployment: The C 3 is the speed Shogun. The Clan XL enables walk four — a significant tactical improvement over the standard walk three. Jump four at eighty-five tons is genuinely useful for positioning. The ATM-6 covers multiple engagement ranges. Clan XL vulnerability is the survivability tradeoff.

variants.name: ST-8A
variants.overview: The Shootist was designed in 2621 as a command platform around twelve tons of ferro-fibrous armour and an AC/20. Seventy tons, walk four, run six. Three variants. ComStar hoarded most surviving examples.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at seventy tons. Standard engine — side torso survivability. Twelve tons of ferro-fibrous armour is exceptional protection. CASE protects the AC/20 ammunition. The ST-8A carries an AC/20, two medium pulse lasers, an ER large laser, and a small laser. Walk four, run six. The AC/20 is the primary weapon. The ER large laser handles long-range engagement. The pulse lasers and small laser cover close threats.
variants.deployment: The 8A is the original 2621 configuration, unchanged since introduction. ComStar deployed these with heavy and command lances. The AC/20 at close range combined with ER large laser reach covers the engagement spectrum. CASE protects the AC/20 ammunition. Ferro-fibrous armour at twelve tons is exceptional protection.

variants.name: ST-8C
variants.overview: The Shootist was designed in 2621 as a command platform around twelve tons of ferro-fibrous armour and an AC/20. Seventy tons, walk four, run six. Three variants. ComStar hoarded most surviving examples.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at seventy tons. Standard engine — side torso survivability. Twelve tons of ferro-fibrous armour is exceptional protection. CASE protects the AC/20 ammunition. The ST-8C upgrades the medium pulse lasers to ER medium lasers and adds a C3i network computer, removing the small laser. Walk four, run six. The C3i integrates network targeting data. The ER mediums extend energy fire range.
variants.deployment: The 8C was introduced around 3062 as a networking upgrade. The C3i adds formation coordination capability. The ER medium upgrade extends energy engagement range over the medium pulse lasers of the 8A.

variants.name: ST-9C
variants.overview: The Shootist was designed in 2621 as a command platform around twelve tons of ferro-fibrous armour and an AC/20. Seventy tons, walk four, run six. Three variants. ComStar hoarded most surviving examples.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at seventy tons. Standard engine — side torso survivability. Twelve tons of ferro-fibrous armour is exceptional protection. CASE protects the AC/20 ammunition. The ST-9C replaces the AC/20 with a Gauss rifle, keeping two ER medium lasers and the ER large laser. Walk four, run six. The Gauss provides accurate long-range fire. Three tons of Gauss ammunition.
variants.deployment: The 9C transforms the Shootist from a close-range brawler to a precision fire support platform. The Gauss rifle provides consistent accurate long-range fire. The ER lasers handle direct engagement at all distances.

variants.overview: The Shrike is a ninety-five ton Clan assault on a 380-rated Clan XL engine. Walk four, run six, jump four. Three variants. Jump capability at ninety-five tons is the tactical standout.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at ninety-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump four at this weight opens positioning options unavailable to most assaults. Variant 2 carries two Ultra AC/10s, two ER medium lasers, and an LRM-10. Walk four, run six, jump four. The UAC/10 upgrade provides double-tap ballistic fire at medium range. The ER mediums handle closer engagement.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 was introduced in 3115. The UAC/10 double-tap rate is the primary improvement. The ER mediums cover shorter ranges. The LRM-10 provides approach fire. Jump four at ninety-five tons remains.

variants.overview: The Shrike is a ninety-five ton Clan assault on a 380-rated Clan XL engine. Walk four, run six, jump four. Three variants. Jump capability at ninety-five tons is the tactical standout.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at ninety-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump four at this weight opens positioning options unavailable to most assaults. Variant 3 carries two ER PPCs, two ER large lasers, and an LRM-10. Walk four, run six, jump four. The ER PPCs and ER large lasers provide substantial long-range energy fire. Firing both ER PPCs and large lasers simultaneously is thermally severe.
variants.deployment: Variant 3 is the maximum long-range energy fire platform. The ER PPCs and ER large lasers create a combined output that opponents cannot ignore. Heat discipline is essential — the full suite simultaneously is not sustainable. The LRM-10 provides approach fire.

variants.name: 'Black Rose'
variants.overview: The Shrike is a ninety-five ton Clan assault on a 380-rated Clan XL engine. Walk four, run six, jump four. Three variants. Jump capability at ninety-five tons is the tactical standout.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at ninety-five tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump four at this weight opens positioning options unavailable to most assaults. The Black Rose is a named configuration carrying two ER PPCs and two ER medium lasers with an LRM-10. Walk four, run six, jump four. All-energy except the LRM-10 — no ammunition concerns beyond the LRM rounds. The ER PPCs handle long-range engagement.
variants.deployment: The Black Rose trades Variant 3's ER large lasers for ER medium lasers, reducing heat load at the cost of medium-range energy output. Heat management is more workable than Variant 3 under sustained fire. Named machine — maintain to specific configuration documentation.

variants.name: SJA-7D
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Shugenja for the DCMS as a seventy-five ton C3 command heavy. Walk four, run six. Two variants. The C3 master computer is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at seventy-five tons. The C3 master requires regular calibration to maintain network integration accuracy. XL engine on the base 7D; light engine on the 8H. The SJA-7D carries an ER PPC, two large lasers, an MRM-30, and a C3 master computer on the XL engine. Walk four, run six. The C3 master coordinates the network lance. The ER PPC handles long-range direct fire. The MRM-30 delivers medium-range missile volume.
variants.deployment: The 7D entered service in 3061 with the Genyosha regiments. The C3 master is the design's purpose — networked lance coordination. The ER PPC and large lasers handle direct combat alongside the command role. The MRM-30 adds medium-range missile capability. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: SJA-8H
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Shugenja for the DCMS as a seventy-five ton C3 command heavy. Walk four, run six. Two variants. The C3 master computer is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 300-rated light engine. The SJA-8H carries an ER PPC, two light PPCs, an MRM-30, B-pods, and a C3 master computer. Light engine — side torso survivability. The light PPCs replace large lasers with close-range weapons that avoid minimum range complications.
variants.deployment: The 8H upgrades to a light engine for survivability with a Guardian ECM suite added. The light PPCs handle close engagement without minimum range gaps. B-pods provide anti-battle armour area defence. The light engine and ECM make this configuration more resilient and electronically capable.

variants.name: SVR-5X
variants.overview: The Silver Fox is a thirty-five ton arena combat light built by IDC for Solaris VII. The SVR-5X uses a 315-rated XXL engine for walk nine, run thirteen — exceptional speed that defines its tactical identity. The XXL engine is extraordinarily vulnerable to side torso damage.
variants.capabilities: Walk nine, run thirteen at thirty-five tons. Five Magshot Gauss rifles, two ER medium lasers, and an ER small laser. The Magshots are lightweight Gauss weapons with good accuracy at the ranges this machine prefers to fight from. The ER mediums extend direct fire reach. The XXL engine at this tonnage means any significant side torso hit ends the mission. What keeps it alive is that almost nothing can hit it.
variants.deployment: The 5X is designed for Solaris VII arena combat and its tactical doctrine is built around the XXL speed advantage. Walk nine, run thirteen means it dictates every engagement on its own terms. The Magshot accuracy at range prevents opponents from simply ignoring it. Arena combat emphasis means survivability under sustained fire was not the design priority.

variants.name: SVR-5Y
variants.overview: The Silver Fox is a thirty-five ton arena combat light built by IDC for Solaris VII. The SVR-5Y is the mass-production variant, replacing the experimental XXL engine of the 5X with a more reliable light engine.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten on the 245-rated light engine. Same weapons package as the 5X: five Magshots, two ER medium lasers, an ER small laser. Walk seven is slower than the 5X's walk nine but still fast for the weight class. The light engine provides substantially better side torso survivability than the XXL. The Magshot accuracy remains the primary combat tool.
variants.deployment: The 5Y trades the 5X's extreme speed for reliability and survivability. Walk seven is fast enough to control most engagements. The light engine survives hits that kill the 5X. The weapons are identical. Units outside Solaris VII that wanted the Silver Fox concept but needed a more field-maintainable platform typically run the 5Y.

variants.name: SRC-3C
variants.overview: The Sirocco is a ninety-five ton quadrupedal assault fire support platform. Walk three, run four. Three variants. The quad chassis provides exceptional firing stability for heavy weapons.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at ninety-five tons. Standard engine — side torso survivability. The quad chassis holds aim at range. Ammunition management across heavy systems is the operational overhead. The SRC-3C carries two Ultra AC/10s, six ER medium lasers, and a medium pulse laser. Walk three, run four. The UAC/10s handle long-range ballistic fire with double-tap capability. The ER mediums provide energy fire across all ranges. Large ammunition bins in the rear legs provide endurance.
variants.deployment: The 3C is the original Sirocco. The UAC/10 pair provides consistent ballistic pressure at range. The ER medium laser suite handles direct energy engagement. The quad stability makes the autocannons effective even when moving. Walk three means it positions before the battle begins.

variants.name: SRC-5C
variants.overview: The Sirocco is a ninety-five ton quadrupedal assault fire support platform. Walk three, run four. Three variants. The quad chassis provides exceptional firing stability for heavy weapons.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at ninety-five tons. Standard engine — side torso survivability. The quad chassis holds aim at range. Ammunition management across heavy systems is the operational overhead. The SRC-5C carries two light Gauss rifles, four ER medium lasers, two SRM-4s, and a medium pulse laser. Walk three, run four. The light Gauss rifles provide accurate long-range fire at lighter mass than standard Gauss. The SRM-4s handle close threats.
variants.deployment: The 5C trades the UAC/10 close-range volume for light Gauss long-range accuracy. The extended engagement distance suits units that need stand-off range. The SRM-4s handle close threats. The ER mediums and pulse laser cover direct energy engagement.

variants.name: SRC-6C
variants.overview: The Sirocco is a ninety-five ton quadrupedal assault fire support platform. Walk three, run four. Three variants. The quad chassis provides exceptional firing stability for heavy weapons.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump five on the standard engine. The SRC-6C carries a light Gauss rifle, four ER medium lasers, and an ER large laser. Jump five. Guardian ECM suite. The ER large laser and ER mediums provide all-energy direct fire. The light Gauss adds long-range ballistic precision.
variants.deployment: The 6C adds jump five mobility and ECM protection to the Sirocco's fire support role. Jump five at ninety-five tons is useful for obstacle crossing and repositioning. The Guardian ECM protects during repositioning. Walk three is unchanged.

variants.name: SLG-X
variants.overview: Arc-Royal MechWorks built only two Slagmaiden prototypes during the Jihad as a technology demonstrator for arena duelling. Fifty-five tons, walk six, run nine on the XL engine with a supercharger.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the XL engine with supercharger burst speed. Composite internal structure saves mass but takes criticals more readily. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Two units exist. The SLG-X carries a heavy large laser, two ER flamers, and two Streak SRM-2s. Walk six, run nine with supercharger burst speed. The heavy large laser hits hard at medium range. The ER flamers handle infantry and force heat on opponents. The Streak SRM-2s fire on lock.
variants.deployment: Two units exist. The composite internal structure is fragile — critical hits penetrate more readily than standard construction. The supercharger provides burst speed. The heavy large laser delivers good per-shot damage. The ER flamers force heat problems on opponents. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: SL-1G
variants.overview: Mountain Wolf BattleMechs built the Sling in 2766 as a dedicated minelayer using Thunder LRM munitions. Twenty-five tons, walk seven, run ten, jump six on the 175-rated XL engine. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump six at twenty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Built around Thunder minelaying rather than conventional direct combat. The SL-1G carries three LRM-5 launchers with Thunder munition capability and a TAG. Walk seven, run ten, jump six. The Thunder-loaded LRM-5s deploy minefields rather than delivering standard damage. The TAG designates for guided munitions.
variants.deployment: The 1G is the original production minelayer. Walk seven delivers Thunder mines to contested positions faster than opponents can contest. The TAG adds designation value when not laying mines. Thunder munition supply requires dedicated logistical planning separate from standard LRM chains.

variants.name: SL-1H
variants.overview: Mountain Wolf BattleMechs built the Sling in 2766 as a dedicated minelayer using Thunder LRM munitions. Twenty-five tons, walk seven, run ten, jump six on the 175-rated XL engine. Two variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump six at twenty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Built around Thunder minelaying rather than conventional direct combat. Walk seven is fast.
variants.deployment: The 1H trades the minelaying capability for direct combat capability. The TAG remains for designation work. Two medium lasers and a pulse laser deliver capable close-range energy fire for a twenty-five ton machine. Walk seven allows rapid repositioning between forward designation tasks.

variants.name: SNK-1V
variants.overview: The Snake is a forty-five ton medium built as a dedicated anti-battle armour platform for the Federated Suns in 3058. Walk five, run seven, jump five on the XL engine. Five variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at forty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The LB 10-X cluster munitions are effective against battle armour. Jump five provides approach flexibility. The SNK-1V carries an LB 10-X and three Streak SRM-2 launchers. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The LB 10-X cluster munitions are effective against battle armour. The Streak SRM-2s provide guaranteed missile hits at close range.
variants.deployment: The 1V entered Federated Suns service targeting Clan Elementals. The LB 10-X cluster mode is the primary anti-battle armour tool. The Streak SRM-2 guarantee ensures missile hits when locked. Jump five enables approach from unexpected angles.

variants.name: SNK-1V (Alexi)
variants.overview: The Snake is a forty-five ton medium built as a dedicated anti-battle armour platform for the Federated Suns in 3058. Walk five, run seven, jump five on the XL engine. Five variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at forty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The LB 10-X cluster munitions are effective against battle armour. Jump five provides approach flexibility. The Alexi is a named configuration replacing the LB 10-X with two ER large lasers, keeping three Streak SRM-2s. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The ER large lasers eliminate ammunition dependency. All-energy plus Streak missiles.
variants.deployment: The Alexi was configured after LB 10-X ammunition supply became unreliable. The ER large laser upgrade removes ammunition logistics. The Streak SRM-2s retain guaranteed close-range missile hits. Named configuration — maintain to specific build documentation.

variants.name: SNK-2B
variants.overview: The Snake is a forty-five ton medium built as a dedicated anti-battle armour platform for the Federated Suns in 3058. Walk five, run seven, jump five on the XL engine. Five variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at forty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The LB 10-X cluster munitions are effective against battle armour. Jump five provides approach flexibility. The SNK-2B carries an LB 10-X and two Streak SRM-2 launchers, with stealth armour. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The stealth armour makes it difficult to target at range. The LB 10-X cluster munitions handle battle armour.
variants.deployment: The 2B adds stealth armour at the cost of one Streak SRM-2 launcher. The stealth combined with jump five creates an anti-battle armour platform that is difficult to engage in return. Stealth armour doubles heat generation while active — energy weapons and stealth together require thermal management.

variants.name: (Arthur)
variants.overview: The Snake is a forty-five ton medium built as a dedicated anti-battle armour platform for the Federated Suns in 3058. Walk five, run seven, jump five on the XL engine. Five variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at forty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The LB 10-X cluster munitions are effective against battle armour. Jump five provides approach flexibility. The Arthur is a named command configuration carrying an ER PPC, an LRM-5, and an AMS, with stealth armour and Guardian ECM. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The ER PPC provides long-range direct fire. The AMS defends against missiles. The ECM degrades enemy targeting.
variants.deployment: The Arthur is built for Arthur Steiner-Davion. The stealth armour and ECM combine for strong survivability. The ER PPC handles direct engagement. The AMS and ECM together provide comprehensive defensive capability. The LRM-5 adds minimal indirect fire.

variants.name: SNK-2Br
variants.overview: The Snake is a forty-five ton medium built as a dedicated anti-battle armour platform for the Federated Suns in 3058. Walk five, run seven, jump five on the XL engine. Five variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at forty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The LB 10-X cluster munitions are effective against battle armour. Jump five provides approach flexibility. The SNK-2Br carries two plasma rifles and two Streak SRM-2s, with stealth armour. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The plasma rifles superheat targets while dealing damage. The stealth armour provides approach cover.
variants.deployment: The 2Br replaces the LB 10-X with plasma rifles for thermal disruption alongside direct damage. The stealth armour provides approach cover. The plasma rifle thermal effect forces heat problems on opponents at close range. The Streak SRM-2s close the engagement reliably.

variants.overview: The Snow Fox 2 is a quad-chassis light 'Mech built around the Hellion Slopeback design. It's fast, agile, and meant to unsettle opponents with its speed and MASC-enhanced bursts. We've seen it used effectively as a cavalry platform and battle armor hunter.
variants.capabilities: This 'Mech is all about speed - 130 km/h without MASC and 172 km/h with it. That makes it hard to track, even for advanced systems. The armament is light, but the minimal heat generation and ten single heat sinks make it manageable. The Compound Alpha ferro-fibrous armor provides reasonable protection for a twenty-ton design, but concentrated fire remains a concern.
variants.deployment: This variant replaces laser weaponry with an LRM-10 launcher and one ton of ammunition, transforming it into a highly mobile fire support platform. The sacrifice of close-range punch for indirect fire capabilities is significant, but the lack of heat generation makes it a viable option. However, dependence on ammunition limits operational endurance compared to energy-armed variants.

variants.overview: The Snow Fox is a twenty-ton Clan quad light. Walk nine, run thirteen with MASC providing burst speed. Two non-OmniMech variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk nine, run thirteen on the standard Clan engine at twenty tons. Variant 3 carries two AP Gauss rifles, an ATM-3, and an ER medium laser. No MASC. The standard engine provides side torso survivability. An ECM suite provides electronic warfare capability.
variants.deployment: Variant 3 is configured for reconnaissance with ECM rather than MASC burst speed. The standard engine removes MASC dependence and adds side torso survivability at the cost of peak speed. The AP Gauss rifles handle infantry. The ATM-3 adds missile flexibility. The ECM protects during forward operations.

variants.name: A

variants.name: SPR-4F
variants.overview: The Spector SPR-4F is a light stealth 'Mech originally designed by Norse Technologies as a command-hunting platform. Its combination of Chameleon Light Polarization Shield and Null-Signature system made it nearly undetectable at range, serving within SLDF formations until the Star League's collapse. The modern SPR-5F reintroduced the design without the original stealth systems, but still offers impressive mobility and electronic warfare capabilities.
variants.capabilities: The Spector is a capable light headhunter with exceptional speed (119 km/h) and mobility thanks to its seven jump jets. Its Guardian ECM suite disrupts enemy targeting and sensor equipment, making it effective at disrupting enemy coordination. While its armament is modest (Nightwind large laser, Defiance B3M/B4S medium/small lasers), the Spector's mission profile emphasizes speed and evasion over raw firepower. MechWarriors appreciate the Spector's ability to pick engagements on favorable terms and withdraw before heavier opposition can respond.
variants.deployment: The original SPR-4F model carried a Chameleon Light Polarization Shield, Null-Signature system, and Guardian ECM suite, making it virtually undetectable at range. Armed with a large laser and twin medium lasers, the design served exclusively within SLDF formations until the collapse of the Star League. Surviving units reportedly ended up in mercenary hands, where they remained rare and unacknowledged for decades.

variants.name: STK-9A
variants.overview: The Stalker II is an eighty-five ton assault 'Mech carrying twenty-seven tons of Riese-675 Hardened Armour. Walk three, run four. Hardened armour reduces incoming damage but doubles the mass of the protection, which is why the weapons loadout is relatively modest for this weight class.
variants.capabilities: The STK-9A carries two Extended LRM-10s and eight medium lasers on a 255-rated standard engine. The hardened armour makes this machine extraordinarily difficult to damage through conventional means — hits that would cripple other assaults leave the Stalker II fighting. The ELRM-10s provide long-range indirect fire. Eight medium lasers deliver close-range fire density. CASE II protects the ammunition bays.
variants.deployment: The STK-9A is a siege unit. It advances into positions that would destroy lighter machines and holds them. The hardened armour means opponents must commit sustained concentrated fire to achieve meaningful damage, which exposes them to return fire. The ELRM-10s keep it relevant at long range during the approach. Eight medium lasers make close engagement uncomfortable for anything that tries to rush it.

variants.overview: The Stalking Spider is a fifty-ton Clan quad OmniMech on a 250-rated Clan standard engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Two variants. The quad chassis provides firing stability.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at fifty tons. Clan standard engine — side torso survivability. The quad chassis holds aim at range. Jump five provides terrain exploitation. Clan construction quality. Variant 2 carries a heavy large laser, two medium pulse lasers, and a TAG. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The heavy large laser hits hard at medium range. The medium pulse lasers handle close engagement. The TAG designates for guided munitions.
variants.deployment: The Stalking Spider 2, introduced in 3060, transforms the design into a dedicated hunter-killer. The heavy large laser paired with the TAG makes it a force multiplier — it can engage directly with the heavy laser and designate for guided munitions. The quad stability improves accuracy at range. Jump five provides positioning.

variants.overview: The Stalking Spider is a fifty-ton Clan quad OmniMech on a 250-rated Clan standard engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Two variants. The quad chassis provides firing stability.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at fifty tons. Clan standard engine — side torso survivability. The quad chassis holds aim at range. Jump five provides terrain exploitation. Clan construction quality. Variant 3 carries two medium pulse lasers, an SRM-6, and two heavy small lasers, with jump eight and additional armour. Walk five, run seven, jump eight. Jump eight at fifty tons is exceptional. The heavy small lasers add close-range punch. The SRM-6 handles close missile volume.
variants.deployment: Variant 3 was first confirmed among Jade Falcon forces during the Harvest Trials. The additional armour enhances survivability. Jump eight at fifty tons is exceptional mobility. The medium pulse lasers and heavy small lasers deliver close-range fire. The SRM-6 adds missile volume. The origin of this modification remains uncertain.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Star Adder's ninety-ton Blood Asp OmniMech was designed as a heavy assault 'Mech, built around the Kingfisher chassis with significant modifications to accommodate a Consolidated 360 XL engine. This choice came at the cost of ferro-fibrous armor, replaced by standard ceramic plate. The result is an offensive powerhouse capable of devastating enemies at virtually any range.
variants.capabilities: The Blood Asp's forty-two tons of pod space provide flexibility for its weight class, enabling configurations ranging from long-range fire support to close-quarters brawlers. The base chassis features sixteen tons of Forging ZZ7 Ceramic Plate armor and fourteen double heat sinks, providing a solid defensive foundation. While the XL engine makes it vulnerable to torso destruction, the sheer firepower available in most configurations ensures few opponents survive long enough to exploit this weakness.
variants.deployment: Alternate Configuration A is a dedicated assault configuration built around maximum precision firepower. Twin ER PPCs and a pair of heavy large lasers are linked to an advanced targeting computer, enabling devastating accuracy at extended ranges. An ECM suite provides electronic warfare protection, and enough jump jets to propel the ninety-ton 'Mech ninety meters give it unexpected tactical mobility. Be aware that this configuration runs extremely hot, particularly when combining jump movement with sustained fire.

variants.deployment: Alternate Configuration B is a dedicated fire-support platform, pairing a Gauss rifle with LRM-20 launchers and Artemis IV fire control systems for enhanced accuracy. The four medium pulse lasers provide close-range defense, while the ECM suite disrupts enemy targeting systems. Two additional double heat sinks ensure this configuration maintains comfortable operating temperatures during sustained bombardment operations.

variants.deployment: The C configuration relies almost exclusively on ammunition-based weapons, mounting twin Ultra Autocannon/10s alongside an LB 20-X autocannon for devastating close-range firepower. A single ER large laser provides the only energy-based weapon for long-range engagements. The heavy reliance on ammunition creates a finite combat endurance that makes this configuration best suited for short and decisive engagements characteristic of Clan Trials.

variants.name: D
variants.overview: The Star Adder is a ninety-ton Clan assault OmniMech on a 360-rated Clan XL engine. Walk four, run six. Fixed and pod-swappable configurations. The design is a mainstay Clan assault platform.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Clan construction quality throughout. Configuration variety covers multiple tactical roles. Configuration D carries a Gauss rifle, two ER large lasers, two heavy medium lasers, and three Ultra AC/2s. Walk four, run six. The Gauss and ER large lasers handle long-range fire. The UAC/2s provide sustained long-range harassment. The heavy medium lasers add close-range punch.
variants.deployment: Configuration D is set up for long-range suppression, pairing a single Gauss rifle with twin ER large lasers and three Ultra AC/2s. The combined long-range fire creates consistent pressure that opponents cannot ignore. The heavy medium lasers handle anything that closes. Ammunition management across the Gauss and three UAC/2s is the operational task.

variants.deployment: The Primary configuration is the most common variant encountered in frontline Star Adder formations, and for good reason. It mounts twin Gauss rifles split between the left and right torsos, with limited ammunition stores that demand disciplined fire from MechWarriors. The four heavy medium lasers and two medium pulse lasers distributed across the arms provide devastating close-range firepower, while a center-torso-mounted Streak SRM-6 adds reliable short-range punch. Just be aware that this configuration runs hot under sustained fire, so keep an eye on your heat levels.

Twin ER PPCs linked to a targeting computer deliver precise long-range fire, while paired medium pulse lasers handle close engagements. Four jump jets give this configuration exceptional mobility for an assault OmniMech, enabling leaps of one hundred twenty meters. Additional heat sinks manage the considerable thermal load, making the E configuration a mobile skirmisher that combines the Blood Asp's raw firepower with tactical agility unusual for its weight class.

The four Streak SRM-6 launchers come with three tons of ammunition, while the medium pulse lasers and AP Gauss rifles handle anti-infantry and anti-battle armor tasks.

Twin ER large lasers split between the right arm and torso provide sustained long-range fire, while paired medium pulse lasers and a heavy medium laser handle closer engagements. A targeting computer enhances the accuracy of all direct-fire weapons.

This mixed-technology design substitutes plasma rifles for Gauss rifles and mounts ER large lasers, twin ER medium lasers, and a standard SRM-6. The weight savings are invested in a supercharger that grants brief bursts of additional speed alongside additional heat sinks. Visually similar to the Primary, this configuration trades raw kinetic damage for sustained energy output and enhanced tactical mobility, reflecting Raven doctrine emphasizing operational flexibility and extended patrol endurance over pure alpha-strike capability.

Each arm mounts a large re-engineered laser of Inner Sphere manufacture, while the right torso houses a massive improved heavy Gauss rifle with four tons of ammunition. Four ER small lasers in the left torso provide point-defense capability.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Star Crusader is an eighty-ton Clan OmniMech on a 320-rated Clan XL engine with jump capability. Walk four, run six. Multiple configurations. The jump jets on some configs open positioning options unusual at assault weight.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at eighty tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump capability varies by configuration. Clan construction quality throughout. Configuration A carries a Gauss rifle, two medium pulse lasers, an ER PPC, and a Streak SRM-6, with six improved jump jets for jump six. Walk four, run six, jump six. The Gauss and ER PPC handle long range. The pulse lasers and Streak SRM-6 close the engagement.
variants.deployment: Configuration A transforms the Star Crusader into an aggressive close-range brawler that leverages exceptional mobility. Six improved jump jets deliver jump six at eighty tons — extraordinary mobility for the weight class. The Gauss and ER PPC engage during approach; the pulse lasers and Streak SRM-6 finish the engagement at close range.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: The Star Crusader is an eighty-ton Clan OmniMech on a 320-rated Clan XL engine with jump capability. Walk four, run six. Multiple configurations. The jump jets on some configs open positioning options unusual at assault weight.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at eighty tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump capability varies by configuration. Clan construction quality throughout. Configuration B carries two large pulse lasers, two HAG/20s, and an ER small laser. Walk four, run six. The HAG/20s spread ballistic projectiles across multiple armour locations. The large pulse lasers are accurate at medium range. Eight tons of Gauss ammunition supports sustained fire.
variants.deployment: Configuration B is set up for sustained direct-fire engagements and anti-aircraft operations. Eight tons of HAG ammunition provides significant endurance. The HAG/20 spread pattern is effective against aircraft and armour that has taken localised damage. The large pulse lasers add accurate medium-range fire.

variants.name: Prime
variants.overview: The Star Crusader is an eighty-ton Clan OmniMech on a 320-rated Clan XL engine with jump capability. Walk four, run six. Multiple configurations. The jump jets on some configs open positioning options unusual at assault weight.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at eighty tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump capability varies by configuration. Clan construction quality throughout. The Prime carries two ER large lasers, two ER medium lasers, two Streak LRM-20s, and an AMS, with jump three and a targeting computer. Walk four, run six, jump three. The targeting computer improves accuracy. The Streak LRM-20s guarantee missile hits when locked.
variants.deployment: The Primary configuration emphasises accurate long-range firepower. Twin ER large lasers are paired with a targeting computer that improves their accuracy. The Streak LRM-20s deliver guaranteed missile hits when locked — no wasted salvoes. The AMS defends against incoming missiles. Jump three adds positioning.

variants.name: STY-2C
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Starslayer in 3049 as a medium raider built around the Thor-4 Endo Steel chassis and a 250-rated engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. It is fast for a fifty-ton medium and the jump capability makes it effective in broken terrain. Six variants span several production generations.
variants.capabilities: The STY-2C is the original production model: two large lasers, two medium lasers, a small laser, and an SRM-4 on a standard engine. The large lasers provide the primary direct fire. The mediums fill the mid-range gap. The SRM-4 handles close threats. Standard engine survivability. The original used a standard internal structure rather than the endo steel of later models.
variants.deployment: The STY-2C deploys as a medium raider and striker. Jump five allows terrain exploitation in broken ground. The standard engine means it survives hits that kill XL competitors. The weapons cover all ranges without specialising. It is the design that established the Starslayer's reputation.

variants.name: STY-2C-EC
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Starslayer in 3049 as a medium raider built around the Thor-4 Endo Steel chassis and a 250-rated engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The STY-2C-EC is an Early Clan prototype configuration using experimental Nova Cat Scientist Caste weapons.
variants.capabilities: The EC variant carries improved large lasers, prototype ER medium lasers, a prototype ER small laser, and a prototype Streak SRM-4, with a Clan fusion engine. The prototype weapons require documentation not covered in standard maintenance manuals. The Clan engine adds a separate maintenance track. This is a research and field test configuration, not a production variant.
variants.deployment: The EC designation indicates this is a prototype. Prototype weapons require specialist procedures and are not directly interchangeable with production equivalents. The Clan engine requires Clan maintenance procedures. This machine should be supported by personnel with specific EC prototype qualification. Field techs without that training should escalate maintenance decisions upward.

variants.name: STY-3C
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Starslayer in 3049 as a medium raider built around the Thor-4 Endo Steel chassis and a 250-rated engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The STY-3C is the endo steel production upgrade of the original.
variants.capabilities: The STY-3C carries the same weapons as the 2C — two large lasers, two medium lasers, a small laser, and an SRM-4 — but on the Thor-4 Endo Steel chassis with upgraded Blaze Fire Zeta laser components. The endo steel frees mass for better armour compared to the original. The weapons are functionally similar but the upgraded laser components improve reliability.
variants.deployment: The 3C is the standard production Starslayer that most units operate. The endo steel structure and upgraded lasers are the practical improvements over the 2C. Deployment role is identical. Parts availability through standard channels is good for this variant.

variants.name: STY-3D
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Starslayer in 3049 as a medium raider built around the Thor-4 Endo Steel chassis and a 250-rated engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The STY-3D removes the SRM-4 launcher entirely and replaces the small laser with an ER PPC.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five. The STY-3D carries an ER PPC, a large laser, and three medium lasers on a standard engine. The ER PPC substantially extends direct fire reach over the standard large laser. The three medium lasers provide close-range energy backup. Standard engine survivability is preserved. No SRM means no close-range missile option.
variants.deployment: The 3D is the long-range variant, trading the SRM-4 close-range punch for ER PPC reach. It suits pilots who want to engage from maximum range and use the jump capability to maintain that distance rather than close it. The three medium lasers handle anything that gets past the ER PPC minimum range.

variants.name: STY-3Dr
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Starslayer in 3049 as a medium raider built around the Thor-4 Endo Steel chassis and a 250-rated engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The STY-3Dr replaces the ER PPC of the 3D with a heavy PPC and carries a Guardian ECM suite.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five on a standard engine. The STY-3Dr carries a heavy PPC, three medium lasers, and a Guardian ECM suite. The heavy PPC hits harder than a standard PPC at medium range but has a minimum range gap. The ECM disrupts enemy targeting systems. Three medium lasers fill the close-range role.
variants.deployment: The 3Dr is the ECM-equipped raider variant. The Guardian ECM makes the Starslayer harder to target during approach and retreat. The heavy PPC provides the primary fire capability. The minimum range gap means the three medium lasers must handle anything that closes past the heavy PPC's effective range. The ECM is the primary reason to choose 3Dr over other Starslayer variants.

variants.name: STY-4C
variants.overview: Stormvanger Assemblies built the Starslayer in 3049 as a medium raider built around the Thor-4 Endo Steel chassis and a 250-rated engine. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The STY-4C is the mixed-tech upgrade using improved heavy large lasers and Clan ER medium lasers.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five on a standard engine. The STY-4C carries two improved heavy large lasers, two Clan ER medium lasers, an improved one-shot SRM-4, and an ER small laser. The improved heavy large lasers hit harder than standard large lasers but generate more heat. The Clan ER mediums require Clan maintenance procedures on an IS chassis.
variants.deployment: The 4C is the mixed-tech upgrade for units with Clan component access. The improved heavy large lasers provide substantially more firepower at medium range than the standard 2C and 3C weapons. The Clan ER mediums are more efficient than IS equivalents. The one-shot SRM-4 provides a single close-range missile salvo before becoming inert. Mixed maintenance requirements need technicians comfortable with both standards.

variants.name: STH-1D
variants.overview: General Motors built the Stealth as a forty-five ton reconnaissance medium built around its proprietary endo steel frame and a Beagle active probe. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 315-rated XL engine. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Beagle active probe extends sensor detection range on most variants. Walk seven and jump seven combine for exceptional mobility. The endo steel frame requires specific structural repair qualification. The STH-1D is the original production model: an SRM-6, two medium lasers, and a Streak SRM-2. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The SRM-6 handles close-range missile volume. The medium lasers provide direct fire. The Streak SRM-2 fires on lock.
variants.deployment: The 1D is the original production Stealth, built around the endo steel frame. The Shannon SH-60 SRM-6 rack and Federated Suns weapons provide close-range capability. The Beagle active probe extends sensor detection. Walk seven and jump seven combine for the reconnaissance mobility the design was built for.

variants.name: STH-2D
variants.overview: General Motors built the Stealth as a forty-five ton reconnaissance medium built around its proprietary endo steel frame and a Beagle active probe. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 315-rated XL engine. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Beagle active probe extends sensor detection range on most variants. Walk seven and jump seven combine for exceptional mobility. The endo steel frame requires specific structural repair qualification. The STH-2D carries a Streak SRM-6 and three ER medium lasers. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The Streak SRM-6 fires on lock for guaranteed missile hits. Three ER mediums provide dense direct energy fire. The Beagle active probe is retained.
variants.deployment: The 2D entered service in 3061, stripping the original weapons loadout while retaining the Beagle active probe. The Streak SRM-6 launcher guarantees close-range missile hits. Three ER medium lasers extend the energy engagement range. The improved weapons make it more combat-capable than the 1D while retaining the sensor role.

variants.name: STH-2D1
variants.overview: General Motors built the Stealth as a forty-five ton reconnaissance medium built around its proprietary endo steel frame and a Beagle active probe. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 315-rated XL engine. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The endo steel frame requires specific structural repair qualification. The STH-2D1 carries a Streak SRM-6 and two ER medium lasers, with a C3 slave replacing one ER medium. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The C3 slave integrates targeting data from a network lance.
variants.deployment: The 2D1 removes one ER medium laser and replaces it with a C3 slave unit, allowing direct targeting data sharing across the network lance. The Streak SRM-6 and two ER mediums provide direct combat capability. The C3 integration multiplies the scout's tactical value. Beagle probe and mobility retained.

variants.name: STH-2D2
variants.overview: General Motors built the Stealth as a forty-five ton reconnaissance medium built around its proprietary endo steel frame and a Beagle active probe. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 315-rated XL engine. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Beagle active probe extends sensor detection range on most variants. Walk seven and jump seven combine for exceptional mobility. The endo steel frame requires specific structural repair qualification. The STH-2D2 carries a Streak SRM-6, two ER medium lasers, and a TAG. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The TAG designates targets for Arrow IV artillery and other guided munitions. The Streak SRM-6 and ER mediums provide direct combat capability.
variants.deployment: The 2D2 replaces one ER medium laser with a TAG target designator, allowing the Stealth to designate targets for Arrow IV artillery and guided munitions. The TAG combined with the Stealth's mobility makes it an effective forward observer. The Streak SRM-6 and ER mediums handle self-defence. Beagle probe retained.

variants.name: STH-1D (Anna)
variants.overview: General Motors built the Stealth as a forty-five ton reconnaissance medium built around its proprietary endo steel frame and a Beagle active probe. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 315-rated XL engine. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Beagle active probe extends sensor detection range on most variants. Walk seven and jump seven combine for exceptional mobility. The endo steel frame requires specific structural repair qualification. The Anna is a custom field variant carrying two medium pulse lasers and four medium lasers. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. Six energy weapons deliver dense close-range fire. No missile capability. All-energy with no ammunition dependency.
variants.deployment: The Anna is a custom field variant that replaced the SRM-6 launcher with medium pulse lasers and additional medium lasers, sacrificing missile capability for dense energy firepower. The pulse lasers add accuracy. Six energy weapons at close range is substantial for a forty-five ton machine. Named field configuration — maintain to specific documentation.

variants.name: STH-3S
variants.overview: General Motors built the Stealth as a forty-five ton reconnaissance medium built around its proprietary endo steel frame and a Beagle active probe. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 315-rated XL engine. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Beagle active probe extends sensor detection range on most variants. Walk seven and jump seven combine for exceptional mobility. The endo steel frame requires specific structural repair qualification. The STH-3S carries a single ER PPC. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. One weapon — a long-range sniper. The advanced sensors and mobility support the sniping role. The ER PPC generates heat that the design's cooling must manage carefully.
variants.deployment: The 3S is a long-range sniper. A single ER PPC combined with advanced sensors makes it an exceptional long-range platform. Walk seven and jump seven let it reposition between shots. The single weapon and heat generation mean the pilot must pace fire and use mobility to avoid return engagement. Be aware of the heat build under sustained ER PPC fire.

variants.name: STH-5X
variants.overview: General Motors built the Stealth as a forty-five ton reconnaissance medium built around its proprietary endo steel frame and a Beagle active probe. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven on the 315-rated XL engine. Seven variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten, jump seven at forty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Beagle active probe extends sensor detection range on most variants. Walk seven and jump seven combine for exceptional mobility. The endo steel frame requires specific structural repair qualification. The STH-5X carries two ER flamers, three ER medium lasers, and a Streak SRM-6, with a functional Chameleon Light Polarization Shield. Walk seven, run ten, jump seven. The CLPS provides stealth capability. The ER flamers force heat problems on opponents. The Streak SRM-6 fires on lock.
variants.deployment: The 5X's notable feature is the functional Chameleon Light Polarization Shield, which provides a degree of stealth capability. The Streak SRM-6 and ER medium lasers handle direct combat. The ER flamers add thermal disruption and anti-infantry capability. The CLPS requires specialist maintenance beyond standard procedures.

variants.name: STO-4A
variants.overview: Coventry Metal Works built the Stiletto in 3061 after studying Clan Jade Falcon's Fire Falcon, developing an IS equivalent using a light engine for survivability rather than the XL approach. The STO-4A uses a 280-rated light engine for walk eight, run twelve at thirty-five tons.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at thirty-five tons. The STO-4A carries two Streak SRM-2s, an LRM-5, and a Beagle active probe with a Guardian ECM suite. No jump jets. The Streak SRM-2s fire only on lock, guaranteeing missile hits. The LRM-5 provides modest indirect fire. The Beagle extends sensor range. The ECM disrupts enemy targeting. Light engine provides side torso survivability.
variants.deployment: The STO-4A is a fast reconnaissance platform. Walk eight is sufficient to outrun most non-light opponents. The ECM and Beagle provide the sensor and electronic warfare capability the role requires. The Streak SRM-2s and LRM-5 are self-defence weapons rather than the primary contribution. The light engine survives hits that would kill a comparable XL design.

The all-energy loadouts on later variants remove ammunition dependency. Speed enables harassment and rapid withdrawal. The STO-4B carries an ER large laser, two ER medium lasers, and a flamer on the 280-rated light engine. Walk eight, run twelve. All-energy with no ammunition. The ER mediums cover medium range. The flamer handles infantry. Light engine survivability. The all-energy loadout removes ammunition logistics for extended operations.

IS OmniMech technology means pod swaps work but less smoothly than Clan equivalents. The SD1-OB carries an LRM-20, an LRM-10, two medium pulse lasers, two medium lasers, and two C3 master computers. Walk four, run six. The twin C3 masters coordinate up to three lances. The LRM-20 and LRM-10 provide fire support.
variants.deployment: Configuration B mounts two C3 master computers, enabling coordination of up to three full lances of networked 'Mechs. The twin C3 masters make it a formation command hub. The LRM-20 and LRM-10 provide fire support alongside the command role. The pulse and medium lasers handle direct engagement. XL engine vulnerability applies.

XL engine vulnerability applies.

The LB 20-X delivers heavy close-range ballistic fire with cluster and slug options. The PPCs handle long-range direct fire. Jump three at ninety tons.
variants.deployment: The SD1-OD was first deployed in Kuritan and Davion cities, mounting an LB 20-X autocannon supported by two PPCs for effective engagement across ranges. The LB 20-X dominates close range. The PPCs cover long range. Jump three provides urban terrain mobility. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Thirty-six tons of pod space is generous for an assault OmniMech. The Samual is a custom anti-infantry configuration carrying six SRM-4 launchers with Inferno munitions, twelve machine guns, an ER PPC, and four flamers. Walk four, run six. The Inferno SRM-4s, machine guns, and flamers create overwhelming anti-infantry capability.
variants.deployment: The Samual is a custom configuration set up for anti-infantry and area denial. Six SRM-4 launchers with Inferno munitions, twelve machine guns, and four flamers deliver overwhelming firepower against infantry and light targets. The ER PPC handles armoured threats. Named custom configuration — maintain to specific documentation.

The snub-nose PPCs cover short to medium range without minimum range complications. The LB 10-X adds ballistic flexibility. The Streak SRM-6s guarantee close hits.
variants.deployment: Configuration E mounts paired snub-nose PPCs and Streak SRM-6 launchers, backed by an ER medium laser and an LB 10-X autocannon. The snub-nose PPCs avoid the minimum range gap of standard PPCs. The Streak SRM-6s handle close engagement reliably. A close-to-medium range brawler. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Thirty-six tons of pod space is generous for an assault OmniMech. The SD1-OX carries eight Enhanced LRM-5 launchers, three ER medium lasers, a medium pulse laser, and two B-pods, with a C3 slave. Walk four, run six. variants.deployment: The X configuration employs experimental technology, mounting eight Enhanced LRM-5 launchers fed by a C3 slave unit for improved targeting data. The eight Enhanced LRM-5s create heavy accurate missile output. The B-pods protect against battle armour. The ER mediums and pulse laser handle direct engagement. Experimental systems require specific maintenance.
