variants.overview: The Sunder is a ninety-ton Inner Sphere assault OmniMech on a 360-rated XL engine with thirty-six tons of pod space. Walk four, run six. Twelve configurations. The generous pod space enables extensive tactical variety.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Thirty-six tons of pod space is generous for an assault OmniMech. IS OmniMech technology means pod swaps work but less smoothly than Clan equivalents. The SD1-OF carries five LRM-5 launchers, six Thunderbolt-5s, and an ER medium laser, with a C3 boosted slave. Walk four, run six. The Clan-built LRM-5s and Thunderbolt-5s deliver combined missile fire. The C3 boosted slave enhances network coordination.
variants.deployment: Configuration F features a C3 boosted slave unit for enhanced network coordination. It combines five Clan-built LRM-5 launchers with six Thunderbolt-5 launchers. The combined missile output covers indirect and guided fire. The C3 boosted slave extends the network range. Two-track maintenance for the Clan missiles.

variants.name: SD1-OG
variants.overview: The Sunder is a ninety-ton Inner Sphere assault OmniMech on a 360-rated XL engine with thirty-six tons of pod space. Walk four, run six. Twelve configurations. The generous pod space enables extensive tactical variety.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at ninety tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Thirty-six tons of pod space is generous for an assault OmniMech. IS OmniMech technology means pod swaps work but less smoothly than Clan equivalents. The SD1-OG carries an LB 20-X, an ER medium laser, an ER PPC, and a TSEMP cannon. Walk four, run six. The TSEMP disrupts enemy 'Mech systems. The LB 20-X delivers heavy close-range ballistic fire. The ER PPC handles long range.
variants.deployment: Configuration G is a significant escalation in the Sunder's combat capability. A Clan-built ER PPC and Clan LB 20-X autocannon provide firepower across ranges. The TSEMP disables opponents for capture or exploitation. The ER medium handles close engagement. TSEMP and Clan weapon maintenance require specialist procedures.

variants.name: GRF-2N-X
variants.overview: The Super-Griffin GRF-2N-X is a 60-ton experimental BattleMech developed in 3020 as part of the New Avalon Institute of Science initiative at Friden Aerospace Park on Hoff. It's a custom design with a focus on revolutionary prototype technologies, including double heat sinks and improved jump jets.
variants.capabilities: The Super-Griffin has some impressive capabilities, but also comes with significant maintenance headaches. The experimental freezer double heat sinks are notoriously short-lived and prone to failure, while the prototype improved jump jets generate extreme heat and can explode violently when damaged. The design's reliance on its jump capability for tactical positioning is a major vulnerability. The Super-Griffin's engine performance is compromised by the experimental systems, reducing ground speed to 64 km/h.
variants.deployment: The sole prototype of this variant Super Griffin was constructed in 3020 at the Friden Aerospace Park on Hoff as part of a paired project with the Super Wasp. It mounted a PPC and LRM-10 in the traditional Griffin configuration, supplemented by a medium laser on the left arm and small laser in the center torso. The experimental systems proved problematic during its only engagement on 13 May 3022, when it was destroyed after return fire struck a prototype jump jet, triggering an explosion that ignited the LRM ammunition.

variants.name: WSP-2A-X
variants.overview: The Super-Wasp is a twenty-five ton experimental upgrade of the Wasp with a supercharger. Walk six, run nine, jump six. One prototype variant. Two units were constructed.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at twenty-five tons on the 150-rated engine. The experimental supercharger provides burst speed. Enhanced armour over the standard Wasp. Two prototypes exist. The WSP-2A-X carries two medium lasers and an SRM-2, with the experimental supercharger and enhanced armour. Walk six, run nine, jump six with supercharger burst speed. The medium lasers provide direct fire. The SRM-2 adds close-range missile capability.
variants.deployment: The WSP-2A-X mounted twin medium lasers, enhanced armour protection, and an experimental supercharger system. Two prototypes were constructed. The supercharger provides burst speed for closing distance or withdrawing. The enhanced armour improves survivability over the standard Wasp. Prototype documentation applies to the experimental supercharger.

variants.overview: The Supernova is a ninety-ton Clan assault built around a heavy energy weapons battery. Walk three, run four, jump three. Multiple variants. The design's energy weapons generate famously severe heat.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three at ninety tons on the 270-rated Clan engine. The energy weapons battery generates severe heat — cycling discipline is essential. Clan construction quality. Jump three provides positioning at assault weight. Variant 2 carries two ER large lasers and four ATM-9 launchers. Walk three, run four, jump three. The four ATM-9s provide three-munition tactical flexibility at heavy scale. The ER large lasers handle long-range direct fire. Six tons of ATM ammunition.
variants.deployment: The Supernova 2 features four ATM-9 launchers fed by six tons of ammunition, replacing some of the original's ER large lasers. The ATM-9 flexibility covers multiple engagement ranges. The ER large lasers handle long range. Pre-loading the correct ATM munition is the key preparation step. The reduced laser count eases the Supernova's notorious heat problems.

variants.overview: The Supernova is a ninety-ton Clan assault built around a heavy energy weapons battery. Walk three, run four, jump three. Multiple variants. The design's energy weapons generate famously severe heat.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three at ninety tons on the 270-rated Clan engine. The energy weapons battery generates severe heat — cycling discipline is essential. Clan construction quality. Jump three provides positioning at assault weight. Variant 3 carries two ER PPCs, two ER large lasers, and two medium pulse lasers. Walk three, run four, jump three. The ER PPCs and ER large lasers handle long-range fire. The pulse lasers cover close engagement. Heat management remains demanding.
variants.deployment: The Supernova 3, introduced in 3064, strips out four ER large lasers, replacing them with two ER PPCs and two medium pulse lasers. The reduced weapon count eases the heat problems somewhat. The ER PPCs and remaining large lasers handle long range. The pulse lasers close the engagement. Heat discipline remains essential.

variants.overview: The Supernova is a ninety-ton Clan assault built around a heavy energy weapons battery. Walk three, run four, jump three. Multiple variants. The design's energy weapons generate famously severe heat.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three at ninety tons on the 270-rated Clan engine. The energy weapons battery generates severe heat — cycling discipline is essential. Clan construction quality. Jump three provides positioning at assault weight. Variant 4 carries four large pulse lasers, two heavy medium lasers, and two ER medium lasers, all guided by a targeting computer. Walk three, run four, jump three. The targeting computer improves accuracy across all weapons. The pulse lasers are accurate at medium range.
variants.deployment: The Supernova 4, produced in 3067, features four pulse lasers, two heavy medium lasers, and two ER medium lasers, all guided by a targeting computer. The targeting computer makes the whole energy battery highly accurate. The heavy medium lasers add close-range punch. Heat management under the full battery requires cycling discipline.

variants.overview: The Supernova is a ninety-ton Clan assault built around a heavy energy weapons battery. Walk three, run four, jump three. Multiple variants. The design's energy weapons generate famously severe heat.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three at ninety tons on the 270-rated Clan engine. The energy weapons battery generates severe heat — cycling discipline is essential. Clan construction quality. Jump three provides positioning at assault weight. Variant 5 carries six ER large lasers and jump jets. Walk three, run four, jump three. Six ER large lasers is a formidable long-range energy battery. The heat from six ER large lasers is severe — this is the classic Supernova heat problem in full.
variants.deployment: The Supernova 5 retains the full complement of six large lasers and jump jets, making it a formidable opponent. The additional heat sinks help but firing all six ER large lasers simultaneously builds heat aggressively. This is the classic Supernova experience — devastating firepower balanced against a severe heat curve. Cycling fire is mandatory.

variants.name: SUR-T1
variants.overview: The Surtur is a fifty-five ton anti-infantry and area-denial medium built under the Hanseatic League. Walk six, run nine on the 330-rated XL engine. One variant. The flamer battery is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at fifty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Seven flamers create overwhelming anti-infantry and area-denial capability. The SRM-6s provide missile punch against armoured targets. The SUR-T1 carries seven flamers and two SRM-6 launchers. Walk six, run nine. Seven flamers create overwhelming anti-infantry and area-denial capability. The SRM-6s provide missile punch against armoured targets.
variants.deployment: The SUR-T1 had no factory variants produced, likely due to its brief production run under the Hanseatic League. The seven-flamer battery devastates infantry and creates area denial through fire. The SRM-6s handle armoured threats. Walk six provides mobility for the anti-infantry role. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: SWD-1
variants.overview: The Swordsman is a forty-ton medium built in 2463 as a general-purpose machine. Walk three or four depending on variant. Two variants. Early variants use primitive technology.
variants.capabilities: Walk three or four at forty tons. Primitive technology on the SWD-1; standard on the SWD-2. The mixed weapons loadout covers multiple ranges. The primitive components on the SWD-1 require period-specific documentation. The SWD-1 carries two medium lasers, an AC/5, and an LRM-5 on primitive technology. Walk three, run four. The AC/5 provides ballistic fire. The LRM-5 adds indirect fire. The medium lasers cover close engagement. Primitive components throughout.
variants.deployment: The SWD-1 was the initial production model fielded beginning in 2463, built entirely with primitive technology. It served as a general-purpose machine. The mixed weapons cover multiple ranges. Primitive construction documentation applies — standard replacement parts do not fit. Walk three reflects the primitive engine.

variants.name: SWD-2
variants.overview: The Swordsman is a forty-ton medium built in 2463 as a general-purpose machine. Walk three or four depending on variant. Two variants. Early variants use primitive technology.
variants.capabilities: Walk three or four at forty tons. Primitive technology on the SWD-1; standard on the SWD-2. The mixed weapons loadout covers multiple ranges. The primitive components on the SWD-1 require period-specific documentation. The SWD-2 carries two medium lasers, an AC/5, an LRM-5, an SRM-4, and a small laser on standard technology. Walk four, run six. The SRM-4 adds close-range missile punch. The AC/5 and LRM-5 handle ballistic and indirect fire.
variants.deployment: The SWD-2's loadout is well-rounded, with a focus on general-purpose engagement. The short-range missile launcher adds significant punch at close range over the SWD-1. The AC/5 and LRM-5 cover ballistic and indirect fire. Walk four improves on the SWD-1's primitive speed. Standard construction throughout.

variants.name: TSH-7S
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Tai-sho as an eighty-five ton C3 command assault for the DCMS. Walk three, run four on the 255-rated engine. Two variants. The C3 command capability is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at eighty-five tons. Standard engine — side torso survivability. The C3 command systems require regular calibration. The ER PPCs and UAC/10 provide direct combat capability alongside the command role. The TSH-7S carries two ER PPCs, a UAC/10, and two C3 master computers. Walk three, run four. The twin C3 masters coordinate networked formations. The ER PPCs handle long-range fire. The UAC/10 provides sustained ballistic fire.
variants.deployment: The first production run of the 7S was assigned to the First Genyosha following their return from operations against Clan remnants. The twin C3 masters make it a formation command hub. The ER PPCs and UAC/10 provide direct combat capability alongside the command role. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: TSH-8S
variants.overview: Luthien Armor Works built the Tai-sho as an eighty-five ton C3 command assault for the DCMS. Walk three, run four on the 255-rated engine. Two variants. The C3 command capability is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four at eighty-five tons. Standard engine — side torso survivability. The C3 command systems require regular calibration. The ER PPCs and UAC/10 provide direct combat capability alongside the command role. The TSH-8S carries two heavy PPCs and a UAC/10, with a single C3 slave replacing the dual masters. Walk three, run four. The heavy PPCs hit harder than standard PPCs at medium range. The UAC/10 provides sustained ballistic fire.
variants.deployment: The 8S was developed in 3073 as a frontline combat unit, replacing the dual C3 masters with a single slave computer. The heavy PPCs deliver more firepower at medium range than the ER PPCs of the 7S. The UAC/10 maintains ballistic pressure. The shift from command hub to frontline combatant is the tactical change.

variants.name: TLN-5V
variants.overview: The Talon is a thirty-five ton fast striker on a 280-rated XL engine. Walk eight, run twelve. Multiple variants. Walk eight is the design's core asset.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at thirty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk eight is genuinely fast. The PPC is the primary weapon across the family. The TLN-5V carries two medium lasers and a standard PPC. Walk eight, run twelve. The standard PPC handles long-range direct fire. The medium lasers cover close engagement. Walk eight provides the mobility.
variants.deployment: The 5V mounts a standard PPC rather than the ER model found on later variants. While lacking the reach of the TLN-5W, the standard PPC still provides genuine long-range threat. Walk eight lets it dictate engagement range. The medium lasers handle close engagement. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: TLN-5W
variants.overview: The Talon is a thirty-five ton fast striker on a 280-rated XL engine. Walk eight, run twelve. Five variants. Walk eight is the design's core asset.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at thirty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk eight is genuinely fast. The PPC-class weapon is the primary armament across the family. The TLN-5W carries two medium lasers and an ER PPC. Walk eight, run twelve. The ER PPC extends the engagement range over the standard PPC of the 5V. The medium lasers cover close engagement. Walk eight provides mobility.
variants.deployment: The 5W is the upgraded Royal model introduced in 2760, featuring an ER Lord's Light-2 PPC that extends its engagement range. Walk eight lets it dictate range with the ER PPC. The medium lasers handle close engagement. XL engine vulnerability applies. The Royal designation reflects the SLDF elite unit assignment.

variants.name: TLN-5W-EC
variants.overview: The Talon is a thirty-five ton fast striker on a 280-rated XL engine. Walk eight, run twelve. Five variants. Walk eight is the design's core asset.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at thirty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk eight is genuinely fast. The PPC-class weapon is the primary armament across the family. The TLN-5W-EC carries two medium lasers and an Enhanced PPC. Walk eight, run twelve. The Enhanced PPC provides ER-range direct fire. The medium lasers cover close engagement. A Clan Ice Hellion refit.
variants.deployment: The 5W-EC was refitted by Clan Ice Hellion around 2823, swapping out the original PPC for an enhanced ER PPC. The rest of the configuration matches the 5W. The Enhanced PPC provides extended-range direct fire. Walk eight lets it control engagement range. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: TLN-5Z
variants.overview: The Talon is a thirty-five ton fast striker on a 280-rated XL engine. Walk eight, run twelve. Five variants. Walk eight is the design's core asset.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten on the 245-rated light engine. The TLN-5Z carries two ER large lasers. Light engine — side torso survivability. Walk seven trades some speed for survivability. Two ER large lasers deliver all-energy long-range fire without ammunition.
variants.deployment: The 5Z features a 245-rated light fusion engine, trading top speed for improved survivability against torso penetration. The light engine survives hits that end XL Talon variants. The two ER large lasers provide long-range energy fire without ammunition concerns. Walk seven is still fast for the weight class.

variants.name: TLN-6W
variants.overview: The Talon is a thirty-five ton fast striker on a 280-rated XL engine. Walk eight, run twelve. Five variants. Walk eight is the design's core asset.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve at thirty-five tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk eight is genuinely fast. The PPC-class weapon is the primary armament across the family. The TLN-6W carries two medium lasers and a heavy PPC. Walk eight, run twelve. The heavy PPC hits harder than the ER PPC at medium range but has a shorter reach. The medium lasers cover close engagement. A Jihad-era redesign.
variants.deployment: The 6W was redesigned during the Jihad era, entering production around 3076. It trades the traditional ER approach for a heavy PPC delivering more per-shot damage at medium range. Walk eight lets it close to heavy PPC range and withdraw. The medium lasers handle close engagement. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: TLS-1B
variants.overview: Vandenberg MilTech built the Talos for the Taurian Defense Force in 2532 and it has served without a factory variant ever being produced. The TLS-1B is a fifty-ton medium carrying an AC/10, an SRM-6, and two LRM-5s on a 200-rated standard engine. Walk four, run six.
variants.capabilities: The AC/10 provides direct ballistic fire at medium range. The SRM-6 handles close threats. The two LRM-5s add modest indirect fire capability. The standard engine provides survivability against side torso hits. Heat management is straightforward across this weapons mix. The design has a strong focus on thermal efficiency that gives pilots considerable firing freedom.
variants.deployment: The TLS-1B is the only production Talos configuration and it has served the Taurian Defense Force for centuries without a formal factory replacement. Widespread field modifications exist across individual machines but no standard variants were ever issued. Maintenance against the original spec is straightforward. Parts availability in Taurian space is reliable given the long production history.

variants.name: ZPH-1
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Tarantula on Stewart in 3054 as the first four-legged BattleMech with jump jets. The ZPH-1 is a twenty-five ton quadrupedal light on a 200-rated XL engine. Walk eight, run twelve, jump eight. The quad layout provides stability on rough terrain that bipedal designs cannot match.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve, jump eight at twenty-five tons. The ZPH-1 carries two medium lasers, a Streak SRM-2, and a Beagle active probe. The Beagle extends sensor range for reconnaissance. The medium lasers provide anti-armour fire. The Streak SRM-2 adds close-range missile punch on lock. The XL engine at twenty-five tons means any side torso damage is fatal.
variants.deployment: The ZPH-1 is a pure reconnaissance platform. The Beagle, speed, and jump capability together make it exceptional at finding things in terrain that would slow conventional designs. The weapons are self-defence tools rather than the primary contribution. The quad stability is particularly valuable in broken terrain where bipedal machines risk falling. XL vulnerability is the constant concern.

variants.name: ZPH-2A
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Tarantula on Stewart in 3054 as the first four-legged BattleMech with jump jets. The ZPH-2A is a 3060 upgrade on a twenty-five ton quadrupedal light on a 200-rated XL engine. Walk eight, run twelve, jump eight.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve, jump eight at twenty-five tons. The ZPH-2A upgrades the standard medium lasers to ER medium lasers, extending engagement range without changing the heat profile. The Streak SRM-2 fires on lock only. The Beagle active probe extends sensor coverage. The XL engine at this weight means side torso damage is fatal.
variants.deployment: The 2A is the ER laser upgrade of the ZPH-1 recon concept. Identical deployment role with better engagement range. The quad stability on rough terrain remains the chassis's tactical advantage. The Beagle and speed are the primary recon tools. Weapons are self-defence.

variants.name: ZPH-3A
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Tarantula on Stewart in 3054 as the first four-legged BattleMech with jump jets. The ZPH-3A is a 3063 variant on a twenty-five ton quadrupedal light on a 200-rated XL engine. Walk eight, run twelve, jump seven.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve, jump seven at twenty-five tons. The ZPH-3A removes the Streak SRM-2 and one jump jet, replacing them with improved armour protection and two medium pulse lasers. The pulse lasers are accurate at close range. Seven jump jets is still exceptional mobility. The XL engine vulnerability at this weight remains.
variants.deployment: The 3A trades the Streak SRM-2 and one jump jet for better armour. The pulse laser accuracy is a modest improvement over the standard medium lasers. The survivability increase from the additional armour is the practical benefit. Same reconnaissance deployment role as the ZPH-1 and 2A.

variants.name: ZPH-4A
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Tarantula on Stewart in 3054 as the first four-legged BattleMech with jump jets. The ZPH-4A is a twenty-five ton quadrupedal light on a 200-rated XL engine with no jump jets.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve. The jump jets are gone entirely on the ZPH-4A, replaced by an ER PPC, a C3 slave unit, and additional heat sinks. The ER PPC provides direct fire at ranges that threaten opponents above this weight class. The C3 slave integrates targeting data from a network lance. No jump capability.
variants.deployment: The 4A is the long-range network variant. The ER PPC gives it genuine offensive reach. The C3 slave multiplies its value in a networked formation. The loss of jump jets removes the terrain exploitation that defines most Tarantula tactics. It deploys as a fast long-range harasser and network node rather than a terrain-mobile scout.

variants.name: ZPH-5A
variants.overview: Corean Enterprises built the Tarantula on Stewart in 3054 as the first four-legged BattleMech with jump jets. The ZPH-5A is a twenty-five ton quadrupedal light on a 200-rated XL engine with no jump jets.
variants.capabilities: Walk eight, run twelve. The ZPH-5A replaces the ER PPC with an ER large laser and upgrades the C3 slave to a C3 boosted slave. The ER large laser delivers similar range to the ER PPC with lower heat. The C3 boosted slave provides better network integration than the standard slave. No jump capability.
variants.deployment: The 5A is the C3 boosted network variant. The boosted slave improves targeting data sharing across the network. The ER large laser handles direct fire at range with better heat management than the 4A's ER PPC. No jump jets limits terrain use. Same fast network harasser deployment as the 4A.

variants.name: TRG-1N
variants.overview: Cosara Weaponries built the Targe as a forty-ton fast medium scout and cavalry 'Mech. Walk seven or eight depending on variant. Three variants. Speed and cavalry harassment are the design focus.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven or eight at forty tons. Light or XL engine depending on variant. Light engine on most variants — side torso survivability. variants.name: TMP-3M
variants.overview: The Tempest TMP-3M is a sixty-five-ton heavy BattleMech designed for versatility and well-rounded performance. Its development was marked by significant changes from its initial concept, resulting in a production model that entered service in 3055. Irian BattleMechs Unlimited produces the Tempest at facilities on both Irian and Angell II.
variants.capabilities: The Tempest's primary armament features a Zeus Slingshot Gauss rifle for long-range firepower without waste heat generation. A Sutel Precision Line large pulse laser supplements this at medium to long ranges, while three Diplan M3 medium lasers and an Irian Weapons Works 60mm SRM-6 rack provide close-range firepower. The Gauss rifle carries two tons of ammunition for sixteen rounds of fire, and the SRM-6 has one ton of ammunition providing fifteen salvos. The Tempest's four Chilton 465 jump jets grant a one hundred twenty meter jump capability, allowing it to keep pace with lighter 'Mechs despite mediocre cruising speed.
variants.deployment: The Tempest TMP-3M works well as part of a mixed lance or company, complementing lighter 'Mechs like the SHD-5M Shadow Hawk. It's not ideal for solo operations due to its mediocre cruising speed, but it can hold its own in close-range combat. Be aware that the Gauss rifle ammo is limited - plan your shots accordingly.

variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at seventy tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump five at seventy tons is exceptional mobility. Clan construction quality. Substantial pod space enables extensive tactical variety. The AA configuration carries a Gauss rifle, an ER large pulse laser, and an SRM-6, with jump five. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The ER large pulse laser replaces the Config A's large pulse laser with extended-range accuracy. The Gauss and SRM-6 handle long and close range.
variants.deployment: The AA configuration retains the proven Gauss rifle and SRM-6 combination, replacing the large pulse laser with an ER large pulse laser for extended-range accuracy. The Gauss delivers heatless long-range fire. The ER large pulse laser adds accurate medium-range fire. The SRM-6 handles close engagement. Jump five provides mobility.

variants.name: T
variants.overview: The Thor (Summoner in Clan records) is a seventy-ton Clan OmniMech on a 350-rated Clan XL engine with jump five. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Seventeen configurations. The jump capability combined with substantial pod space makes it one of the most versatile Clan heavies.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at seventy tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump five at seventy tons is exceptional mobility. Clan construction quality. Substantial pod space enables extensive tactical variety. The T configuration carries a ProtoMech AC/8, an ER PPC, and a Streak LRM-15, with jump five. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The ER PPC handles long-range fire. The ProtoMech AC/8 provides close-range ballistic volume. The Streak LRM-15 guarantees missile hits when locked.
variants.deployment: The T configuration features an ER PPC in the right arm as primary long-range striking power, supplemented by the ProtoMech AC/8 for close-range ballistic fire. The Streak LRM-15 delivers guaranteed missile hits. Jump five provides mobility. An unusual mix of ProtoMech-derived and standard Clan weapons.

variants.name: J
variants.overview: The Thor (Summoner in Clan records) is a seventy-ton Clan OmniMech on a 350-rated Clan XL engine with jump five. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Seventeen configurations. The jump capability combined with substantial pod space makes it one of the most versatile Clan heavies.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at seventy tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump five at seventy tons is exceptional mobility. Clan construction quality. Substantial pod space enables extensive tactical variety. The J configuration carries a HAG/40 and two improved heavy medium lasers, with jump five. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The HAG/40 spreads heavy ballistic fire across multiple armour locations. The improved heavy medium lasers hit hard at close range. A short-to-medium range arsenal.
variants.deployment: The J configuration demands aggressive piloting to bring its short-to-medium range arsenal to bear effectively. The HAG/40 delivers devastating spread damage at moderate range. The improved heavy medium lasers add close-range punch. Jump five closes distance to bring the weapons to bear. Be prepared to get close. Clan XL vulnerability applies.

variants.name: (Prime)
variants.overview: The Thor II (Grand Summoner) is a seventy-ton Clan OmniMech on a 350-rated Clan XL engine with jump five. Walk five, run seven, jump five. Multiple configurations. An upscaled evolution of the Thor concept.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at seventy tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump five is exceptional mobility. The Prime carries two Ultra AC/5s, four ER medium lasers, and an LRM-15. The UAC/5s provide sustained ballistic fire. The ER mediums handle direct fire. The LRM-15 adds fire support.
variants.deployment: The Prime configuration establishes the Grand Summoner as a versatile combined-arms platform capable of engaging effectively across ranges. The twin UAC/5s maintain sustained ballistic pressure. The four ER mediums provide dense direct fire. The LRM-15 adds fire support. Jump five provides mobility. Clan XL vulnerability applies.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Thor II (Grand Summoner) is a seventy-ton Clan OmniMech on a 350-rated Clan XL engine with jump five. Walk five, run seven. Six configurations. An upscaled evolution of the Thor concept.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump capability varies by configuration. Clan construction quality. Substantial pod space. Configuration A carries an ER PPC, an LB 10-X, an LRM-15, and an LRM-5, with jump five. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The ER PPC and LB 10-X handle direct fire. The LRM-15 and LRM-5 provide fire support.
variants.deployment: Configuration A pairs direct-fire weapons with missile support, featuring an ER PPC and LB 10-X autocannon alongside LRM launchers. The ER PPC handles long-range fire. The LB 10-X adds ballistic flexibility. The LRM-15 and LRM-5 provide fire support. Jump five provides mobility. Clan XL vulnerability applies.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: The Thor II (Grand Summoner) is a seventy-ton Clan OmniMech on a 350-rated Clan XL engine with jump five. Walk five, run seven. Six configurations. An upscaled evolution of the Thor concept.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump capability varies by configuration. Clan construction quality. Substantial pod space. Configuration B carries two LRM-15s, an ATM-9, an ATM-6, two LRM-5s, and two ER small lasers. Walk five, run seven, no jump. The LRM launchers deliver heavy fire support. The ATMs add three-munition missile flexibility. A dedicated missile platform.
variants.deployment: The B configuration turns the Thor II into a dedicated missile platform, with two arm-mounted LRM-15 launchers and ATM launchers. The combined LRM and ATM output creates overwhelming missile fire. The ER small lasers provide minimal self-defence. Pre-loading the correct ATM munitions is the key preparation step. Clan XL vulnerability applies.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: The Thor II (Grand Summoner) is a seventy-ton Clan OmniMech on a 350-rated Clan XL engine with jump five. Walk five, run seven. Six configurations. An upscaled evolution of the Thor concept.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump capability varies by configuration. Clan construction quality. Substantial pod space. Configuration C carries an Ultra AC/20, two large pulse lasers, a Streak SRM-4, and a flamer. Walk five, run seven, no jump. The UAC/20 delivers devastating close-range ballistic fire. The large pulse lasers are accurate at medium range. The Streak SRM-4 and flamer handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: Configuration C follows a brawler philosophy, mounting close-range weaponry for quick engagements. The UAC/20 dominates close range. The large pulse lasers add accurate medium-range fire. The Streak SRM-4 guarantees close missile hits. The flamer handles infantry. A dedicated close-range brawler. Clan XL vulnerability applies.

variants.name: D
variants.overview: The Thor II (Grand Summoner) is a seventy-ton Clan OmniMech on a 350-rated Clan XL engine with jump five. Walk five, run seven. Six configurations. An upscaled evolution of the Thor concept.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump capability varies by configuration. Clan construction quality. Substantial pod space. Configuration D carries two ER large lasers, two ER medium lasers, and an LRM-15, with a targeting computer and jump five. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The targeting computer improves accuracy. The ER large lasers handle precision long-range fire. The LRM-15 adds fire support.
variants.deployment: The D configuration focuses on precision energy combat with an integrated targeting computer and paired ER large and medium lasers. The targeting computer makes the ER lasers highly accurate. The LRM-15 provides fire support. Jump five provides positioning. Clan XL vulnerability applies.

variants.name: E
variants.overview: The Thor II (Grand Summoner) is a seventy-ton Clan OmniMech on a 350-rated Clan XL engine with jump five. Walk five, run seven. Six configurations. An upscaled evolution of the Thor concept.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump capability varies by configuration. Clan construction quality. Substantial pod space. Configuration E carries two ER PPCs and an ER small laser, with eight improved jump jets for jump eight. Walk five, run seven, jump eight. Jump eight at seventy tons is a two-hundred-forty-metre jump radius. The ER PPCs deliver long-range direct fire.
variants.deployment: The E configuration mounts eight improved jump jets for a remarkable two-hundred-forty-metre jump radius, paired with twin ER PPCs. Jump eight at seventy tons creates approach vectors no opponent can predict. The ER PPCs deliver strong long-range fire. The ER small laser handles point-blank threats. Maximum mobility for a heavy platform.

variants.name: THE-F
variants.overview: The Thorn is a twenty-ton light scout built for the SLDF. Walk six, run nine on the 120-rated engine. Seven variants. The design combines a laser suite with missile capability at scout weight.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty tons. Standard, endo steel, or XL structure depending on variant. The medium lasers and missile launcher provide the combat capability. Thin armour is the scout tradeoff. The THE-F carries two medium lasers and an LRM-5 on a heavier standard internal structure. Walk six, run nine. The medium lasers provide direct fire. The LRM-5 adds indirect fire. The standard structure sacrifices some payload compared to endo steel variants.
variants.deployment: The THE-F mounts the same weapons as the later THE-S on a heavier standard internal structure, sacrificing payload capacity for structural simplicity. The medium lasers handle direct fire. The LRM-5 provides indirect fire. Walk six suits the scout role. Thin armour means direct combat is avoided.

variants.name: THE-N
variants.overview: The Thorn is a twenty-ton light scout built for the SLDF. Walk six, run nine on the 120-rated engine. Seven variants. The design combines a laser suite with missile capability at scout weight.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty tons. Standard, endo steel, or XL structure depending on variant. The medium lasers and missile launcher provide the combat capability. Thin armour is the scout tradeoff. The THE-N carries two medium lasers and an LRM-5 on a Chariot Type II endo steel chassis. Walk six, run nine. The endo steel structure frees tonnage for additional armour over the THE-F. The medium lasers and LRM-5 provide the combat capability.
variants.deployment: The THE-N's Chariot Type II endo steel chassis provides a significant advantage, freeing up tonnage for additional armour. The improved protection over the THE-F is meaningful for a scout that occasionally takes fire. The medium lasers and LRM-5 handle combat. Walk six suits the scout role.

variants.name: THE-Nb
variants.overview: The Thorn is a twenty-ton light scout built for the SLDF. Walk six, run nine on the 120-rated engine. Seven variants. The design combines a laser suite with missile capability at scout weight.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 120-rated XL engine. The THE-Nb carries an ER large laser, a medium laser, and a small laser. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The ER large laser eliminates ammunition dependency and provides genuine long-range fire. The medium and small lasers handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: The THE-Nb's loadout is centred around its ER large laser in the right arm, which eliminates ammunition dependency. The ER large laser gives the scout a long-range threat unusual for the weight class. The medium and small lasers handle close engagement. XL engine vulnerability applies. All-energy simplifies logistics.

variants.name: THE-S
variants.overview: The Thorn is a twenty-ton light scout built for the SLDF. Walk six, run nine on the 120-rated engine. Seven variants. The design combines a laser suite with missile capability at scout weight.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty tons. Standard, endo steel, or XL structure depending on variant. The medium lasers and missile launcher provide the combat capability. Thin armour is the scout tradeoff. The THE-S carries two medium lasers and an LRM-5 on an endo steel chassis. Walk six, run nine. The medium lasers provide direct fire. The LRM-5 adds indirect fire. A ComStar refit for the Draconis Combine.
variants.deployment: The THE-S was created when ComStar refitted Thorns for delivery to the Draconis Combine as part of Operation Rosebud. The endo steel chassis and weapons match the THE-N. The medium lasers and LRM-5 handle combat. Walk six suits the scout role. Standard weapons for a light scout.

variants.name: THE-T
variants.overview: The Thorn is a twenty-ton light scout built for the SLDF. Walk six, run nine on the 120-rated engine. Seven variants. The design combines a laser suite with missile capability at scout weight.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty tons. Standard, endo steel, or XL structure depending on variant. The medium lasers and missile launcher provide the combat capability. Thin armour is the scout tradeoff. The THE-T carries two medium lasers and an SRM-4. Walk six, run nine. The SRM-4 replaces the LRM-5, trading long-range indirect fire for close-range missile punch. The medium lasers provide direct fire.
variants.deployment: The THE-T was developed by the Draconis Combine in 3038, replacing the Zeus LRM-5 with an SRM-4, trading long-range capability for close-range punch. The SRM-4 delivers more damage at close range than the LRM-5 did at distance. The medium lasers handle direct fire. Walk six suits the scout role.

variants.name: THE-N1
variants.overview: The Thorn is a twenty-ton light scout built for the SLDF. Walk six, run nine on the 120-rated engine. Seven variants. The design combines a laser suite with missile capability at scout weight.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 120-rated XL engine. The THE-N1 carries an ER PPC and a small laser. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The ER PPC provides genuine long-range fire. All-energy with no ammunition dependency. The small laser handles point-blank threats.
variants.deployment: The THE-N1's all-energy loadout simplifies logistics and reduces the risk of ammo-related malfunctions. The ER PPC gives the scout a long-range threat well above its weight class. The small laser handles point-blank. XL engine vulnerability applies. The all-energy loadout suits extended operations without resupply.

variants.name: THE-N2
variants.overview: The Thorn is a twenty-ton light scout built for the SLDF. Walk six, run nine on the 120-rated engine. Seven variants. The design combines a laser suite with missile capability at scout weight.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 120-rated XL engine. The THE-N2 carries an MML-7 and an ER small laser. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The MML-7 fires both LRM and SRM ammunition, adapting to engagement range. The ER small laser handles point-blank threats.
variants.deployment: The THE-N2's loadout is centred around its MML-7 launcher, which offers flexibility in combat scenarios. The MML-7 covers both fire support and close missile engagement depending on mode. The ER small laser handles close threats. Be aware of the ammunition management the MML requires. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.overview: The Thresher is a sixty-ton Clan medium OmniMech on a 300-rated Clan XL engine with jump five. Walk five, run seven. Multiple variants. The jump capability combined with fire support weapons defines the design.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at sixty tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump five provides terrain exploitation. Clan construction quality. Variant 2 carries two ER large lasers, an ER medium laser, an LB 5-X, and two SRM-6 launchers, with jump five. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The ER large lasers handle long range. The LB 5-X adds ballistic flexibility. The SRM-6s handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: The Thresher 2 is best deployed as a fire support platform, using its long-range weapons to soften enemy positions. The ER large lasers and LB 5-X provide the long-range fire. The SRM-6s handle close threats. Jump five provides positioning. Clan XL vulnerability applies.

variants.name: (Edward)
variants.overview: The Thresher is a sixty-ton Clan medium OmniMech on a 300-rated Clan XL engine with jump five. Walk five, run seven. Multiple variants. The jump capability combined with fire support weapons defines the design.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at sixty tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump five provides terrain exploitation. Clan construction quality. The Edward carries three ER medium lasers, an MRM-20, and an Ultra AC/10, mixing Clan and IS technology. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The UAC/10 provides sustained ballistic fire. The MRM-20 adds medium-range missile volume. The ER mediums handle direct fire.
variants.deployment: The Edward variant features a mix of Clan and Inner Sphere technologies. The torso-mounted Clan weapons remain intact, while the IS additions provide the MRM-20 and UAC/10. The combined output covers ballistic, missile, and energy. Two-track maintenance for the mixed technology. Named variant — maintain to specific documentation.

variants.name: THG-11E
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Thug as an eighty-ton assault around twin PPCs and SRM-6 launchers. Walk four, run six on the 320-rated engine. Eight variants. The twin-PPC configuration is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at eighty tons. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The twin PPCs and SRM-6s cover long and close range. Heat management under the PPCs is the consistent consideration. The THG-11E is the original Star League production model: two PPCs and two SRM-6 launchers. Walk four, run six. The twin PPCs handle long-range direct fire. The SRM-6s handle close engagement. The definitive expression of the design philosophy.
variants.deployment: The 11E is the original Star League-era production model and the definitive expression of the Thug's design philosophy. The twin PPCs deliver strong long-range fire. The SRM-6s handle close engagement. Heat management under the twin PPCs is the pilot's primary consideration. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: THG-11Eb
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Thug as an eighty-ton assault around twin PPCs and SRM-6 launchers. Walk four, run six on the 320-rated engine. Eight variants. The twin-PPC configuration is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at eighty tons. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The twin PPCs and SRM-6s cover long and close range. Heat management under the PPCs is the consistent consideration. The THG-11Eb Royal carries two ER PPCs and two SRM-6 launchers. Walk four, run six. The ER PPCs extend the engagement range over the standard PPCs. The SRM-6s handle close engagement. A simple Royal upgrade.
variants.deployment: The Royal variant is a simple upgrade to the standard 11E, replacing the standard Tiegart PPCs with ER models. The ER PPCs extend the long-range engagement envelope. The SRM-6s handle close engagement. The Royal designation reflects the SLDF elite unit assignment. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: THG-11ECX (Jose)
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Thug as an eighty-ton assault around twin PPCs and SRM-6 launchers. Walk four, run six on the 320-rated engine. Eight variants. The twin-PPC configuration is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four on the 320-rated XL engine. The Jose carries two ER large lasers and five SRM-6 launchers. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Jump four. The ER large lasers handle long range. Five SRM-6 launchers deliver overwhelming close-range missile volume.
variants.deployment: The Jose is an experimental custom refit produced at Maltex Corporation's Errai facility in late 2772. The XL engine enables the weapons and jump capability. The ER large lasers handle long range. Five SRM-6 launchers create overwhelming close-range missile output. Jump four provides positioning. Named experimental refit — maintain to specific documentation.

variants.name: THG-10E
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Thug as an eighty-ton assault around twin PPCs and SRM-6 launchers. Walk four, run six on the 320-rated engine. Eight variants. The twin-PPC configuration is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at eighty tons. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The twin PPCs and SRM-6s cover long and close range. Heat management under the PPCs is the consistent consideration. The THG-10E carries two PPCs and two SRM-4 launchers. Walk four, run six. The SRM-4s are a downgrade from the 11E's SRM-6s. A Succession Wars production variant with reduced missile capability.
variants.deployment: The 10E is a downgraded Succession Wars variant produced by Earthwerks Incorporated after Maltex's Errai facility was lost. The SRM-4s replace the 11E's SRM-6s, reducing close-range missile volume. The twin PPCs are retained. A wartime production compromise. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: THG-12E
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Thug as an eighty-ton assault around twin PPCs and SRM-6 launchers. Walk four, run six on the 320-rated engine. Eight variants. The twin-PPC configuration is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at eighty tons. Standard engine on most variants — side torso survivability. The twin PPCs and SRM-6s cover long and close range. Heat management under the PPCs is the consistent consideration. The THG-12E carries two ER PPCs and two SRM-6 launchers, with a C3i battle computer. Walk four, run six. The C3i integrates network targeting. The ER PPCs handle long range. The SRM-6s handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: The 12E was introduced in 3067, featuring ER PPCs and a C3i battle computer for network-centric warfare. The C3i coordinates targeting across the network. The ER PPCs deliver strong long-range fire. The SRM-6s handle close engagement. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: THG-12K
variants.overview: The Thug is an eighty-ton Star League assault 'Mech built around paired PPCs and exceptional armour. The THG-12K is a Kurita variant carrying twin ER PPCs, two SRM-6 launchers, and a Guardian ECM suite on the standard 320-rated engine.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six. Twin ER PPCs provide extended-range direct fire superior to the standard Thug PPCs. Two SRM-6 launchers handle close threats. The Guardian ECM suite disrupts enemy targeting. The standard engine provides the survivability the Thug is known for. Two tons of SRM ammunition requires management.
variants.deployment: The 12K is the Kurita ECM variant. The Guardian ECM makes it harder to target during approach and in formation. The ER PPCs extend the standard Thug engagement range. The SRM-6s handle anything that closes past ER PPC minimum range. Combine supply chains support this variant reliably.

variants.name: THG-13K
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Thug as an eighty-ton assault around twin PPCs and SRM-6 launchers. Walk four, run six on the 320-rated engine. Eight variants. The twin-PPC configuration is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 320-rated XL engine. The THG-13K carries three heavy PPCs and two medium pulse lasers. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Three heavy PPCs deliver devastating long-range fire. The heat from three heavy PPCs requires strict cycling discipline.
variants.deployment: The most notable change from the original Thug design philosophy is the stripping out of missile launchers and replacement with three heavy PPCs. Three heavy PPCs create devastating long-range fire but generate severe heat. The medium pulse lasers handle close engagement. Heat discipline is essential. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: THG-11E (Reich)
variants.overview: Maltex Corporation built the Thug as an eighty-ton assault around twin PPCs and SRM-6 launchers. Walk four, run six on the 320-rated engine. Eight variants. The twin-PPC configuration is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four on the 320-rated fusion engine. The Reich carries two ER PPCs and two Streak SRM-6 launchers, with Clan-specification weapons. Jump four. The Clan ER PPCs and Streak SRM-6s outperform IS equivalents. The Streak SRM-6s guarantee close hits.
variants.deployment: The Reich variant has been refitted with Clan-specification ER PPCs and Streak SRM-6 launchers, providing superior performance. The Clan ER PPCs deliver extended-range fire. The Streak SRM-6s guarantee close-range missile hits. Jump four provides positioning. Two-track maintenance for the Clan weapons. Named variant — maintain to specific documentation.

variants.name: THG-13U
variants.overview: The Thug is an eighty-ton Star League assault 'Mech built around paired PPCs and exceptional armour. The THG-13U is a later variant using snub-nose PPCs and four MML-3 launchers on the standard 320-rated engine.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six. The snub-nose PPCs cover short to medium range without minimum range complications. Four MML-3 launchers provide SRM or LRM flexibility at modest scale. Standard engine survivability is preserved. The MML ammunition management across four launchers with two modes each requires planning.
variants.deployment: The 13U is a close-to-medium range variant. The snub-nose PPCs are more effective than standard PPCs at close distances. The MML-3s add missile volume and flexibility. The Thug armour survives sustained engagements that would force lighter designs to withdraw. This variant suits pilots who want to fight at closer range than the standard long-range Thug concept.

variants.name: THR-1L
variants.overview: The Thunder is a seventy-ton Capellan heavy built around close-range firepower on a 350-rated XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Four variants. The AC/20 or LB 20-X is the close-range centrepiece.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk five is fast for the weight class. The heavy ballistic weapon dominates close range across the family. The THR-1L carries an AC/20, three medium pulse lasers, and an LRM-5. Walk five, run seven. The AC/20 delivers devastating close-range ballistic fire. The medium pulse lasers handle close engagement accurately. The LRM-5 adds indirect fire.
variants.deployment: The THR-1L entered Capellan service in 3055, establishing its reputation as a devastating close-range combatant. The AC/20 dominates close range. The medium pulse lasers add accurate close-range fire. The LRM-5 provides indirect fire. Walk five lets it close distance quickly. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: THR-2L
variants.overview: The Thunder is a seventy-ton Capellan heavy built around close-range firepower on a 350-rated XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Four variants. The AC/20 or LB 20-X is the close-range centrepiece.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk five is fast for the weight class. The heavy ballistic weapon dominates close range across the family. The THR-2L carries an LB 20-X, a Streak SRM-6, two ER medium lasers, and an ER small laser. Walk five, run seven. The LB 20-X delivers heavy close-range ballistic fire with cluster and slug options. The Streak SRM-6 guarantees close hits. The ER mediums handle direct fire.
variants.deployment: Field experience has shown that the THR-2L's advanced technology upgrades make it more reliable in close-range engagements. The LB 20-X dominates close range. The Streak SRM-6 handles close missiles reliably. The ER mediums add direct fire. Walk five closes distance quickly. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: THR-3L
variants.overview: The Thunder is a seventy-ton Capellan heavy built around close-range firepower on a 350-rated XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Four variants. The AC/20 or LB 20-X is the close-range centrepiece.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk five is fast for the weight class. The heavy ballistic weapon dominates close range across the family. The THR-3L carries an Arrow IV artillery launcher, a Streak SRM-6, and two ER medium lasers. Walk five, run seven. The Arrow IV provides extreme-range artillery fire. The Streak SRM-6 handles close engagement. The ER mediums add direct fire.
variants.deployment: The 3L carries a loadout that prioritises range and firepower over close-quarters combat. The Arrow IV delivers extreme-range artillery fire that no standard weapon can match. The Streak SRM-6 and ER mediums handle direct engagement. Arrow IV ammunition requires dedicated logistics. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: THR-C4
variants.overview: The Thunder is a seventy-ton Capellan heavy built around close-range firepower on a 350-rated XL engine. Walk five, run seven. Four variants. The AC/20 or LB 20-X is the close-range centrepiece.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump six on the 280-rated XL engine. The THR-C4 carries a Thunderbolt-20, three ER medium lasers, and a medium X-pulse laser. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Jump six. The Thunderbolt-20 delivers accurate heavy guided missile fire. The ER mediums and X-pulse handle direct fire.
variants.deployment: The C4 was developed jointly by the Capellan Confederation and the Magistracy of Canopus in 3083. The Thunderbolt-20 delivers accurate heavy guided missile fire. The ER mediums and X-pulse laser handle direct engagement. Jump six at seventy tons is exceptional mobility. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: TFT-A9
variants.overview: The Thunder Fox is a fifty-five ton sniping and fire support medium. Walk four or five depending on variant. Four variants. The light Gauss and ballistic weapons provide the sniping capability.
variants.capabilities: Walk four or five at fifty-five tons. Fusion, light, XL, or XXL engine depending on variant. The design combines ballistic precision with support weapons. Jump capability on some variants. The TFT-A9 carries an ER large laser, a light Gauss rifle, a Streak SRM-4, and an ER small laser, with jump three. Walk four, run six, jump three. The light Gauss provides accurate long-range fire. The ER large laser handles direct fire. The Streak SRM-4 handles close threats.
variants.deployment: The base TFT-A9 represents the Thunder Fox as originally conceived, a balanced sniping platform combining long-range ballistic fire with energy weapons. The light Gauss delivers accurate long-range fire. The ER large laser adds direct fire. The Streak SRM-4 handles close engagement. Jump three provides positioning.

variants.name: TFT-L8
variants.overview: The Thunder Fox is a fifty-five ton sniping and fire support medium. Walk four or five depending on variant. Four variants. The light Gauss and ballistic weapons provide the sniping capability.

variants.name: TSG-9H
variants.overview: The Ti Ts'ang TSG-9H is a 60-ton heavy BattleMech designed for aggressive close-quarters combat. Built by Ceres Metals Industries on Capella, it's part of the Xin Sheng national revitalization program. The design incorporates Chinese cultural aesthetics into its armor plating and features a massive hatchet as its primary weapon.
variants.capabilities: From a maintenance standpoint, the Ti Ts'ang is a mixed bag. The XL engine is a significant vulnerability, as a critical hit to either side torso will disable the 'Mech entirely. On the other hand, the SL Special endo steel chassis saves considerable weight and provides near-maximum protection for the chassis weight. We've found that the triple-strength myomer requires elevated temperatures to activate, which can be both a blessing and a curse in combat. The design's heat generation is intentional, but it does mean you'll need to keep an eye on temperature readings during prolonged battles.
variants.deployment: The base production model carries five Diverse Optics extended-range medium lasers, four extended-range small lasers, an Apple Churchill TAG designator, and the signature hatchet. The TAG system provides additional tactical utility by enabling the 'Mech to designate targets for allied artillery and missile support. This configuration is effective at generating heat to activate triple-strength myomer before delivering a devastating melee strike.
