variants.overview: The Tomahawk II is a hundred-ton Clan assault OmniMech built around a 300-rated Clan XL engine. Walk three, run four. The design prioritises firepower over speed. Configuration A is the precision anti-materiel and anti-aircraft variant.
variants.capabilities: Configuration A carries twin LB 10-X ACs, four AP Gauss rifles, two large pulse lasers, two medium pulse lasers, and an ER large laser. The LB 10-X cluster option is effective against aircraft and lighter targets. The AP Gauss rifles devastate infantry and battle armour. The pulse laser suite provides anti-armour direct fire. Ammunition management across LB and AP Gauss systems requires planning.
variants.deployment: Configuration A deploys in combined-arms environments where the threat mix includes aircraft, infantry, battle armour, and armoured opponents simultaneously. The LB 10-X cluster rounds handle aerial targets. The AP Gauss rifles clear infantry. The pulse lasers deal with armoured opponents. It is the most tactically versatile Tomahawk II configuration.

variants.name: B
variants.overview: The Tomahawk II is a hundred-ton Clan assault OmniMech built around a 300-rated Clan XL engine. Walk three, run four. The design prioritises firepower over speed. Configuration B adds three jump jets for repositioning capability unusual in a hundred-ton machine.
variants.capabilities: Configuration B carries twin Streak LRM-15s, twin ER large pulse lasers, two ER large lasers, an ER medium laser, a laser AMS, and three jump jets. Jump three on a hundred-ton assault 'Mech is a tactical surprise. The Streak LRM-15s fire only on lock, conserving ammunition. The laser AMS provides missile defence. The ER pulse laser accuracy is the direct fire standout.
variants.deployment: Configuration B uses jump capability to claim elevated positions and reach urban terrain features that ground-bound assaults cannot access. The laser AMS protects against incoming missiles without ammunition dependency. The Streak LRM-15s provide guaranteed missile hits when locked. ER large pulse laser accuracy makes this an effective precision fire platform.

variants.name: C
variants.overview: The Tomahawk II is a hundred-ton Clan assault OmniMech built around a 300-rated Clan XL engine. Walk three, run four. The design prioritises firepower over speed. Configuration C is the maximum missile fire support variant.
variants.capabilities: Configuration C carries six LRM-15 launchers, three large pulse lasers, and CASE II protection on the side torsos. Six LRM-15s at a hundred tons delivers a missile volume that few platforms in any weight class can match. Five tons of LRM ammunition provides substantial operational endurance. The large pulse lasers provide direct fire capability when LRMs are expended or targets are too close.
variants.deployment: Configuration C goes to the back of the formation and saturates target zones with six simultaneous LRM-15 salvos. The large pulse lasers deter anything that tries to close the distance. CASE II protects against ammunition explosions. Five tons of LRM ammunition allows sustained fire support across extended operations. This configuration needs escorts to protect it from fast flanking threats.

variants.name: TR-A-1
variants.overview: The Toro is a thirty-five ton light built for the Free Worlds League. Walk four to six depending on variant. Four variants. Early variants use primitive technology.
variants.capabilities: Walk four to six at thirty-five tons. Primitive, standard, or XL engine depending on variant. The design combines a primary weapon with missile support. The TR-A-1 carries a large laser and two SRM-2 launchers on a primitive 170-rated engine. Walk four, run six. The large laser handles direct fire. The SRM-2s add close-range missile capability. Primitive components throughout.
variants.deployment: The original Toro prototype mounts a primitive 170-rated engine that limits its top speed to approximately 64 kilometres per hour. The large laser handles direct fire. The SRM-2s add close-range missile capability. Primitive construction documentation applies — standard replacement parts do not fit. A prototype light.

variants.name: TR-A-6
variants.overview: The Toro is a thirty-five ton light built for the Free Worlds League. Walk four to six depending on variant. Four variants. Early variants use primitive technology.
variants.capabilities: Walk four to six at thirty-five tons. Primitive, standard, or XL engine depending on variant. The design combines a primary weapon with missile support. The TR-A-6 carries a PPC and two LRM-5 launchers on a 175-rated engine. Walk five, run seven. The PPC handles long-range direct fire. The LRM-5s provide indirect fire. Improved targeting software over earlier models.
variants.deployment: The TR-A-6 features the same paired LRM-5 racks as earlier models, with the added bonus of improved targeting software. The PPC delivers strong long-range fire. The LRM-5s provide indirect fire support. The improved targeting improves accuracy. Walk five is faster than the primitive prototype. A fire support light.

variants.name: TR-B-9
variants.overview: The Toro is a thirty-five ton light built for the Free Worlds League. Walk four to six depending on variant. Four variants. Early variants use primitive technology.
variants.capabilities: Walk four to six at thirty-five tons. Primitive, standard, or XL engine depending on variant. The design combines a primary weapon with missile support. The TR-B-9 carries a light PPC, a medium laser, and two MML-5 launchers on a 175-rated engine. Walk five, run seven. The MML-5s fire both LRM and SRM ammunition, adapting to range. The light PPC handles direct fire without minimum range complications.
variants.deployment: The TR-B-9's loadout is designed for flexibility rather than specialisation. The twin MML-5 launchers provide flexibility across engagement ranges. The light PPC handles direct fire. The medium laser adds close-range fire. Walk five provides mobility. A flexible fire support light.

variants.name: TR-B-12
variants.overview: The Toro is a thirty-five ton light built for the Free Worlds League. Walk four to six depending on variant. Four variants. Early variants use primitive technology.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 210-rated XL engine. The TR-B-12 carries a light PPC, an ER medium laser, and two MML-5 launchers, with CASE II ammunition protection. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk six is faster than earlier variants. The MML-5s adapt to engagement range.
variants.deployment: The TR-B-12's CASE II ammunition protection and upgraded armour provide capable survivability. The light PPC handles direct fire. The MML-5s cover both LRM and SRM ranges. The ER medium adds close-range fire. Walk six improves mobility over earlier variants. CASE II protects the ammunition. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: TYM-1A
variants.overview: The Toyama is a seventy-five ton Word of Blake heavy fire support platform. Walk four, run six. Three variants. The mixed ballistic, energy, and missile loadout covers multiple ranges.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 300-rated XL engine. The TYM-1A carries two ER large lasers, an LB 10-X, three medium lasers, and an LRM-20. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The ER large lasers and LB 10-X handle long and medium range. The LRM-20 delivers heavy fire support.
variants.deployment: The original TYM-1A was deployed exclusively with the Word of Blake Militia from its introduction in 3057. Its combination of ballistic, energy, and missile weapons covers multiple ranges. The ER large lasers and LB 10-X handle direct fire. The LRM-20 provides heavy fire support. The medium lasers close the engagement. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: TYM-1B
variants.overview: The Toyama is a seventy-five ton Word of Blake heavy fire support platform. Walk four, run six. Three variants. The mixed ballistic, energy, and missile loadout covers multiple ranges.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 300-rated light engine. The TYM-1B carries a heavy PPC, two light PPCs, two ER medium lasers, and an LRM-15. Light engine — side torso survivability. The heavy PPC handles medium range. The light PPCs cover close range. The LRM-15 adds fire support.
variants.deployment: The TYM-1B features a significant redesign driven by combat experience during the Jihad. The Vlar light engine replaces the XL for survivability. The heavy PPC delivers strong medium-range fire. The light PPCs handle close range. The LRM-15 provides fire support. The light engine survives hits that end the XL variants.

variants.name: TYM-1C
variants.overview: The Toyama is a seventy-five ton Word of Blake heavy fire support platform. Walk four, run six. Three variants. The mixed ballistic, energy, and missile loadout covers multiple ranges.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six on the 300-rated XL engine. The TYM-1C carries a Gauss rifle, two medium VSP lasers, and an LRM-20. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Gauss provides accurate long-range fire. The VSP lasers adapt to engagement range. The LRM-20 delivers heavy fire support.
variants.deployment: The TYM-1C emerged in 3072 with significant changes from the original TYM-1A. The M-2 Gauss rifle replaces the LB 10-X for accurate long-range fire. The medium VSP lasers adapt to range. The LRM-20 provides heavy fire support. XL engine vulnerability applies. A Gauss-armed fire support platform.

variants.name: TR-XB
variants.overview: The Trebaruna is a ninety-five ton assault built for the Republic of the Sphere. Walk three, run four, jump four on the 285-rated engine. Multiple variants. The mixed ballistic and energy loadout covers multiple ranges.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump four at ninety-five tons. Standard engine — side torso survivability. Jump four. The TR-XB carries a Gauss rifle, three light PPCs, and an advanced targeting computer. The targeting computer improves accuracy. The Gauss handles long range. The light PPCs cover close to medium range.
variants.deployment: The base TR-XB combines a primary ballistic weapon with energy-based secondary armament and an advanced targeting computer. The targeting computer makes the Gauss and light PPCs highly accurate. The Gauss handles long range. The three light PPCs cover close and medium range. Jump four at ninety-five tons is exceptional mobility. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: TR-XJ
variants.overview: The Trebaruna TR-XB is a 95-ton quad assault 'Mech designed for long-range fire support. Its unique chassis provides exceptional stability for its heavy armament, earning it a reputation as a durable command vehicle.
variants.capabilities: The Trebaruna's greatest strength lies in its survivability. The 16 tons of Durallex Heavy armor and Pitban 285 standard fusion engine make it highly resistant to damage. While firepower is modest for an assault-class machine, the Imperator Dragon's Fire Gauss rifle and Moscovia light particle projection cannons provide reliable and low-maintenance options. The Orion Suretrak XVII targeting computer enhances the value of these armaments. Jump range is impressive at 120 meters, making it a formidable command vehicle.
variants.deployment: This variant was manufactured exclusively at the Earthwerks-FWL facility on Keystone and replaces the Moscovia light particle cannons with snub-nose particle projection cannons for devastating close-range firepower. A double-strength heat sink is added to manage the increased thermal load, and the Spillman Multitrack 8 tracking system takes over from the Orion Suretrak targeting computer.

variants.name: TR-XL
variants.overview: The Trebaruna is a 95-ton quadrupedal assault 'Mech designed for long-range fire support. The quad chassis provides exceptional firing stability for heavy weapons. The TR-XL variant uses a 285-rated light engine with jump jets and carries a plasma rifle pair alongside an LB 20-X.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump four on the 285-rated light engine. Twin plasma rifles deliver thermal disruption and direct damage simultaneously. The LB 20-X provides heavy ballistic fire with cluster or slug options. Jump four on a ninety-five ton machine is genuinely surprising to opponents. The light engine provides better side torso survivability than XL. Plasma rifle ammunition requires dedicated supply.
variants.deployment: The TR-XL uses jump capability to claim firing positions the standard TR-XB cannot reach and delivers plasma disruption combined with LB 20-X fire. The quad stability makes it a steady platform for the heavy weapons under any firing conditions. Plasma rifle supply logistics require separate planning from standard autocannon ammunition chains.

variants.name: TR-XH
variants.overview: The Trebaruna TR-XB is a 95-ton quad assault 'Mech designed for long-range fire support. Its unique chassis provides exceptional stability for its heavy armament, earning it a reputation as a durable command vehicle.
variants.capabilities: The Trebaruna's greatest strength lies in its survivability. The 16 tons of Durallex Heavy armor and Pitban 285 standard fusion engine make it highly resistant to damage. While firepower is modest for an assault-class machine, the Imperator Dragon's Fire Gauss rifle and Moscovia light particle projection cannons provide reliable and low-maintenance options. The Orion Suretrak XVII targeting computer enhances the value of these armaments. Jump range is impressive at 120 meters, making it a formidable command vehicle.
variants.deployment: This variant features more than twenty-five tons of hardened armor, enabling it to shrug off withering volumes of enemy fire that would cripple lighter designs. The primary armament is an improved heavy Gauss rifle, delivering devastating kinetic impacts at extreme range. A turret-mounted extended-range particle projection cannon provides secondary firepower with a wide field of fire, compensating for the quad chassis's limited torso rotation.

variants.name: TBT-3C
variants.overview: The Trebuchet is a fifty-ton fire support medium built for the SLDF in 2780. Walk five, run seven. Thirteen variants. The twin LRM-15 and medium laser combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 300-rated XL engine. The TBT-3C carries two LRM-15s and four medium lasers. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk six is faster than standard. The LRM-15s provide fire support. Four medium lasers deliver dense close-range fire.
variants.deployment: The original Trebuchet produced for the Star League Defence Force mounted a formidable array of advanced technology. The XL engine enables walk six and the four medium lasers. The LRM-15s provide fire support. The medium lasers close the engagement. XL engine vulnerability applies. A capable fire support medium.

variants.name: TBT-5N
variants.overview: The Trebuchet is a fifty-ton fire support medium built for the SLDF in 2780. Walk five, run seven. Thirteen variants. The twin LRM-15 and medium laser combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty tons on most variants. The LRM launchers and medium lasers cover indirect and direct fire. Standard, XL, or light engine depending on variant. The TBT-5N carries two LRM-15s and three medium lasers on a standard 250-rated engine. Walk five, run seven. The LRM-15s provide fire support. Three medium lasers handle close engagement. A straightforward, maintainable design.
variants.deployment: The Trebuchet 5N is a straightforward design that is easy to manufacture and maintain, even with degraded industrial infrastructure. The LRM-15s provide fire support. The medium lasers close the engagement. Standard engine survivability. The maintainability makes it accessible to units without deep supply chains. A definitive workhorse fire support medium.

variants.name: TBT-5J
variants.overview: The Trebuchet is a fifty-ton fire support medium built for the SLDF in 2780. Walk five, run seven. Thirteen variants. The twin LRM-15 and medium laser combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty tons on most variants. The LRM launchers and medium lasers cover indirect and direct fire. Standard, XL, or light engine depending on variant. The TBT-5J carries an LRM-15 and three medium lasers, with jump five. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The reduced missile capacity trades fire support volume for jump mobility. The medium lasers handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: The 5J's loadout is designed to provide a balance between firepower and mobility. The reduced LRM capacity means it will not saturate targets like the 5N, but jump five opens terrain exploitation options. The medium lasers close the engagement. A mobile fire support Trebuchet. Standard engine survivability.

variants.name: TBT-5S
variants.overview: The Trebuchet is a fifty-ton fire support medium built for the SLDF in 2780. Walk five, run seven. Thirteen variants. The twin LRM-15 and medium laser combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty tons on most variants. The LRM launchers and medium lasers cover indirect and direct fire. Standard, XL, or light engine depending on variant. The TBT-5S carries two SRM-6 launchers and three medium lasers. Walk five, run seven. The SRM-6s deliver close-range missile volume. Three medium lasers handle close engagement. A close-range brawler configuration.
variants.deployment: The 5S's brawler configuration is best used in tandem with other 'Mechs or as part of a larger unit. Its close-range focus trades the standard LRM fire support for SRM-6 missile volume. The medium lasers close the engagement. Standard engine survivability. A dedicated close-range Trebuchet.

variants.name: TBT-7K
variants.overview: The Trebuchet has been a medium fire support platform since 2481. The TBT-7K is a Kurita variant that departs entirely from the LRM heritage, carrying a PPC and AC/5 alongside an SRM-2 on the standard 250-rated engine.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven. The PPC provides long-range direct fire. The AC/5 adds sustained ballistic harassment. The SRM-2 handles close threats. Standard engine survivability. The absence of LRM launchers means this machine does not fit the standard Trebuchet fire support role at all. It is a direct fire medium that happens to be on the Trebuchet chassis.
variants.deployment: The 7K is a Kurita refit that turns the Trebuchet into a direct fire platform. Pilots expecting fire support behaviour from this machine will be disappointed. Pilots who treat it as a medium striker will find the PPC and AC/5 combination performs well at medium range. Standard engine survivability is the chassis contribution.

variants.name: TBT-7M
variants.overview: The Trebuchet is a fifty-ton fire support medium built for the SLDF in 2780. Walk five, run seven. Thirteen variants. The twin LRM-15 and medium laser combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five on the 250-rated XL engine. The TBT-7M carries two LRM-15s, three medium lasers, and a Narc missile beacon. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Narc tags targets for guided munitions. The LRM-15s provide fire support.
variants.deployment: The 7M features an Octagon Missile Magnet Narc Missile Beacon with two tons of ammunition, enabling the Trebuchet to share targeting data. The Narc multiplies the effectiveness of the formation's missile-armed units. The LRM-15s provide fire support. The medium lasers close the engagement. Jump five provides positioning. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: TBT-9K
variants.overview: The Trebuchet is a fifty-ton fire support medium built for the SLDF in 2780. Walk five, run seven. Thirteen variants. The twin LRM-15 and medium laser combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five on the 250-rated XL engine. The TBT-9K carries two MRM-20s, a medium laser, and two medium pulse lasers. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The twin MRM-20s deliver devastating medium-range salvos. The pulse lasers handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: The 9K's most notable feature is the twin MRM-20 launchers, which provide devastating medium-range salvos at the cost of accuracy. The MRM-20s create overwhelming medium-range missile fire. The medium and pulse lasers handle close engagement. Jump five provides positioning. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: TBT-8B
variants.overview: The Trebuchet is a fifty-ton fire support medium built for the SLDF in 2780. Walk five, run seven. Thirteen variants. The twin LRM-15 and medium laser combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump five on the 300-rated XL engine. The TBT-8B carries four MML-5 launchers and four ER medium lasers. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk six is faster than standard. The MML-5s fire both LRM and SRM ammunition. Four ER mediums deliver dense close-range fire.
variants.deployment: The 8B's loadout allows for flexible engagement options between long-range missiles and close-in laser firepower. The four MML-5s cover both fire support and close missile engagement. The four ER mediums provide dense direct fire. Jump five provides positioning. Walk six improves mobility. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: TBT-XK7
variants.overview: The Trebuchet is a fifty-ton fire support medium built for the SLDF in 2780. Walk five, run seven. Thirteen variants. The twin LRM-15 and medium laser combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five on the 250-rated XL engine. The TBT-XK7 carries two Streak SRM-6s, an ER medium laser, an ER flamer, and a medium pulse laser. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Streak SRM-6s guarantee close hits. The ER flamer handles infantry.
variants.deployment: The XK7's loadout is centred on close-range combat, suited for urban or jungle environments where grappling range is common. The Streak SRM-6s guarantee close-range missile hits. The ER medium and pulse laser handle direct fire. The ER flamer handles infantry. Jump five provides positioning. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: TBT-K7R
variants.overview: The Trebuchet is a fifty-ton fire support medium built for the SLDF in 2780. Walk five, run seven. Thirteen variants. The twin LRM-15 and medium laser combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five on the 250-rated light engine. The TBT-K7R carries a BattleMech Taser, two ER medium lasers, two ER flamers, and a Streak SRM-6. Light engine — side torso survivability. The Taser disables opponents for capture. The Streak SRM-6 guarantees close hits.
variants.deployment: The K7R's most distinctive feature is the BattleMech Taser mounted in the left arm, which allows it to disable and potentially capture opponents. The Taser shuts down enemy systems. The ER mediums and Streak SRM-6 handle direct combat. The ER flamers handle infantry. Light engine survivability preserved. Jump five provides positioning.

variants.name: TBT-7MM 'Merida'
variants.overview: The Trebuchet is a fifty-ton fire support medium built for the SLDF in 2780. Walk five, run seven. Thirteen variants. The twin LRM-15 and medium laser combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven on the 250-rated XL engine. The Merida carries two Streak LRM-15s and two ER medium lasers. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Streak LRM-15s guarantee missile hits when locked. The ER mediums handle close engagement. An arena configuration.
variants.deployment: The Merida's loadout is designed for arena combat, with the Streak LRM-15 systems and ER medium lasers prioritising long-range accuracy. The Streak LRM-15s deliver guaranteed missile hits. The ER mediums handle close engagement. XL engine vulnerability applies. Named arena configuration — maintain to specific documentation.

variants.name: TBT-9R
variants.overview: The Trebuchet is a fifty-ton fire support medium built for the SLDF in 2780. Walk five, run seven. Thirteen variants. The twin LRM-15 and medium laser combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten on the 350-rated IS XXL engine. The TBT-9R carries three LRM-15s and two medium X-pulse lasers. XXL engine — side torso damage is catastrophic. Walk seven reaches 110 kph. Three LRM-15s deliver heavy fire support. The X-pulse lasers handle close engagement.
variants.deployment: The 9R features an XXL fusion engine that drives the fifty-ton chassis to 110 kilometres per hour with an integrated targeting system. Three LRM-15s deliver heavy fire support. The X-pulse lasers close the engagement. Walk seven makes it a fast fire support platform. The XXL vulnerability at fifty tons is severe — any penetrating side torso hit likely ends the engagement.

variants.name: TBT-9N
variants.overview: The Trebuchet is a fifty-ton fire support medium built for the SLDF in 2780. Walk five, run seven. Thirteen variants. The twin LRM-15 and medium laser combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine on the 300-rated XL engine. The TBT-9N carries two LRM-15s and three medium VSP lasers. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk six is faster than standard. The VSP lasers adapt to engagement range. The LRM-15s provide fire support.
variants.deployment: The 9N delivers comparable capability to the TBT-9R at significantly reduced cost and complexity. The XL engine enables walk six. The LRM-15s provide fire support. The medium VSP lasers adapt to whatever range the engagement settles at. XL engine vulnerability applies. A cost-effective fast fire support Trebuchet.

variants.name: TRK-4V
variants.overview: The Triskelion is a seventy-five ton Inner Sphere heavy hand-built rather than mass-produced. Walk five, run seven on the 375-rated Clan XL engine. One production variant.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at seventy-five tons on the Clan XL engine. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. The TRK-4V carries four ER medium lasers and two LRM-15s. The ER mediums deliver dense direct fire. The LRM-15s provide fire support.
variants.deployment: The TRK-4V is the sole production variant of the Triskelion, built by hand rather than on a production line. The four ER medium lasers provide dense direct fire. The LRM-15s provide fire support. Walk five for a seventy-five ton heavy is the speed advantage. Clan XL vulnerability applies. A hand-built heavy with mixed direct and indirect fire.

variants.name: TP-1R
variants.overview: The Trooper is a twenty-ton Free Worlds League light. Walk six, run nine on the 145-rated engine. One production variant.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at twenty tons. Standard engine — side torso survivability. The TP-1R carries two small lasers, a machine gun, and a flamer. The small lasers provide direct fire. The machine gun and flamer handle infantry.
variants.deployment: The TP-1R is the sole production variant of the Trooper, representing the original prototype that entered Free Worlds League service. The small lasers provide direct fire. The machine gun and flamer handle infantry. Walk six suits the light trooper role. A simple anti-infantry light.

variants.name: TS-P1
variants.overview: The Tsunami is a forty-ton medium BattleMech designed for both arena combat and light battlefield operations. It's a well-designed but unimpressive machine that found a niche among Solaris stables and small mercenary outfits. OmniTech's low production rate limited its distribution, but those who operated it found a reliable and versatile platform.
variants.capabilities: The Tsunami has respectable mobility for its weight class, with an emphasis on jump capability. Its armor protection is adequate, placing it in the middle of its weight class for survivability. It can be configured with different weapons to suit various combat philosophies. Later models traded some jump capability for improved physical combat performance and a conditional speed advantage. However, maintenance can be challenging due to its complex internal layout.
variants.deployment: The original TS-P1 mounts a standard loadout of energy and ballistic armament, plus a light missile launcher for close-range punch. Without myomer upgrades, this variant relies on superior jump mobility, with enough jets to cover 180 meters – giving it an edge in broken terrain like Solaris arenas and battlefields.

variants.name: TS-P1D
variants.overview: The Tsunami is a forty-ton medium BattleMech designed for both arena combat and light battlefield operations. It's a well-designed but unimpressive machine that found a niche among Solaris stables and small mercenary outfits. OmniTech's low production rate limited its distribution, but those who operated it found a reliable and versatile platform.
variants.capabilities: The Tsunami has respectable mobility for its weight class, with an emphasis on jump capability. Its armor protection is adequate, placing it in the middle of its weight class for survivability. It can be configured with different weapons to suit various combat philosophies. Later models traded some jump capability for improved physical combat performance and a conditional speed advantage. However, maintenance can be challenging due to its complex internal layout.
variants.deployment: The TS-P1D has a fundamentally different combat profile than its predecessors, trading two jump jets for dramatically improved melee capability and a conditional speed boost. Its energy-focused weapons suite and precision ballistic armament offer far greater effective range than the original's loadout, while an accurate missile system provides reliable close-range punch.

variants.overview: The Tundra Wolf is a seventy-five ton Clan Wolf heavy BattleMech. Walk four, run six, jump four on the 300-rated Clan XL engine. Five variants. The mixed weapons cover multiple ranges.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at seventy-five tons on the Clan XL engine. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump four provides terrain exploitation. Clan construction quality. Variant 2 carries an ER PPC, an ER large laser, six ER medium lasers, and an LRM-15. Walk four, run six, jump four. The all-energy loadout addresses ammunition dependency. The ER PPC and ER large laser handle long range. The ER mediums deliver dense close-range fire.
variants.deployment: The energy-focused loadout addresses concerns about ammunition dependency, with an ER PPC, six ER medium lasers, and an ER large laser. The ER PPC and ER large laser handle long range. The six ER mediums deliver dense close-range fire. The LRM-15 adds fire support. The heat from the full energy suite requires cycling. Jump four provides positioning.

variants.overview: The Tundra Wolf is a seventy-five ton Clan Wolf heavy BattleMech. Walk four, run six, jump four on the 300-rated Clan XL engine. Five variants. The mixed weapons cover multiple ranges.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at seventy-five tons on the Clan XL engine. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump four provides terrain exploitation. Clan construction quality. Variant 3 carries two ER PPCs, an ER large laser, four ER medium lasers, a Streak SRM-4, and an LRM-15. Walk four, run six, jump four. The twin ER PPCs handle long range. The ER large laser and ER mediums add direct fire. The Streak SRM-4 guarantees close hits.
variants.deployment: The Tundra Wolf 3 was clearly designed with Clan duellists in mind. It sacrifices three tons of armour and two medium lasers for twin ER PPCs. The ER PPCs deliver strong long-range fire. The ER large laser and mediums close the engagement. The Streak SRM-4 handles close threats. Jump four provides positioning. A duellist-focused variant.

variants.overview: The Tundra Wolf is a seventy-five ton Clan Wolf heavy BattleMech. Walk four, run six, jump four on the 300-rated Clan XL engine. Five variants. The mixed weapons cover multiple ranges.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six, jump four at seventy-five tons on the Clan XL engine. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump four provides terrain exploitation. Clan construction quality. Variant 4 carries two large pulse lasers, two ER medium lasers, two AP Gauss rifles, and an ATM-9. Walk four, run six, jump four. The large pulse lasers are accurate at medium range. The AP Gauss rifles handle infantry. The ATM-9 provides missile flexibility.
variants.deployment: The Tundra Wolf 4's loadout is designed for ammo-independent firepower, with a pair of Delta Series large pulse lasers. The large pulse lasers deliver accurate medium-range fire. variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine at thirty tons on the Clan XL engine. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability at this weight is severe. Clan construction quality. The extensive configuration range covers scout, fire support, and direct combat roles. Configuration T carries an ER large laser, an ER medium laser, a Streak SRM-4, and a ProtoMech AC/4. Walk six, run nine. The ER large laser handles long range. The ProtoMech AC/4 provides close-range ballistic fire. The Streak SRM-4 guarantees close hits.
variants.deployment: The left arm carries an ER large laser and ER medium laser for ranged engagements, while the right arm mounts a ProtoMech AC/4. The ER large laser handles long range. The ProtoMech AC/4 adds close-range ballistic volume. The Streak SRM-4 handles close missiles reliably. Walk six positions it. Clan XL vulnerability at this weight is severe.

variants.name: UAE-7R
variants.overview: The Uraeus is a seventy-five ton Inner Sphere heavy. Walk four, run six on the 300-rated fusion engine. Multiple variants. The mixed ballistic and energy loadout covers multiple ranges.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at seventy-five tons. Standard fusion engine — side torso survivability. The UAE-7R carries an Ultra AC/10, a Bombast laser, and a Streak SRM-4. The UAC/10 delivers sustained ballistic fire. The Bombast laser fires at variable power. The Streak SRM-4 guarantees close hits.
variants.deployment: The UAE-7R carries a Mydron Excel Class 10 Ultra Autocannon as its primary ranged weapon, capable of delivering punishing sustained fire. The UAC/10 maintains ballistic pressure. The Bombast laser provides variable-output energy fire. The Streak SRM-4 handles close engagement. Standard engine survivability. A capable ballistic-focused heavy.

variants.name: UM-R60
variants.overview: The UrbanMech is a thirty-ton urban defence 'Mech that has been in service since 2675. Walk two, run three, jump two on the tiny 60-rated engine. Multiple variants. The design is famously slow — built for static ambush from urban cover, not manoeuvre.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three, jump two at thirty tons. The design is extremely slow — this machine ambushes from cover rather than manoeuvring. The heavy autocannon delivers disproportionate firepower for the weight. Jump two provides limited urban terrain mobility. The UM-R60 carries an AC/10 and a small laser. Walk two, run three, jump two. The AC/10 delivers heavy ballistic fire from ambush. The small laser handles close threats. The definitive UrbanMech configuration.
variants.deployment: The original production model introduced in 2675 mounts the Imperator-B autocannon and Harmon small laser that defined the design. The AC/10 delivers heavy ballistic fire from urban ambush. The small laser handles close threats. Jump two provides limited urban terrain mobility. The design is famously slow but hits hard from cover.

variants.name: UM-R60L
variants.overview: The UrbanMech is a thirty-ton urban defence 'Mech that has been in service since 2675. Walk two, run three, jump two on the tiny 60-rated engine. Multiple variants. The design is famously slow — built for static ambush from urban cover, not manoeuvre.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three, jump two at thirty tons. The design is extremely slow — this machine ambushes from cover rather than manoeuvring. The heavy autocannon delivers disproportionate firepower for the weight. Jump two provides limited urban terrain mobility. The UM-R60L carries an AC/20 and a small laser. Walk two, run three, jump two. The AC/20 delivers devastating close-range ballistic fire from ambush. The small laser handles close threats. A close-range ambush configuration.
variants.deployment: The -R60L's loadout is designed for close-range combat, suited for urban ambushes. The AC/20 delivers devastating close-range ballistic fire from cover. Be cautious when engaging targets at range, as the AC/20's reach is limited. The small laser handles close threats. Jump two provides urban terrain mobility. A close-range ambush UrbanMech.

variants.name: UM-R63
variants.overview: The UrbanMech is a thirty-ton urban defence 'Mech that has been in service since 2675. Walk two, run three, jump two on the tiny 60-rated engine. Multiple variants. The design is famously slow — built for static ambush from urban cover, not manoeuvre.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three, jump two at thirty tons. The design is extremely slow — this machine ambushes from cover rather than manoeuvring. The heavy autocannon delivers disproportionate firepower for the weight. Jump two provides limited urban terrain mobility. The UM-R63 carries an LB 10-X, a small pulse laser, and a small laser. Walk two, run three, jump two. The LB 10-X provides cluster and slug options with enhanced range. The pulse laser handles close engagement accurately.
variants.deployment: The -R63 upgrade kit replaces the standard autocannon with a Mydron Excel LB 10-X, providing enhanced range and cluster capability. The LB 10-X cluster option is useful against lighter opponents and aircraft. The small pulse laser handles close engagement. Jump two provides urban terrain mobility. A flexible ballistic UrbanMech.

variants.name: UM-R69
variants.overview: The UrbanMech is a thirty-ton urban defence 'Mech that has been in service since 2675. Walk two, run three, jump two on the tiny 60-rated engine. Multiple variants. The design is famously slow — built for static ambush from urban cover, not manoeuvre.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three, jump two at thirty tons. The design is extremely slow — this machine ambushes from cover rather than manoeuvring. The heavy autocannon delivers disproportionate firepower for the weight. Jump two provides limited urban terrain mobility. The UM-R69 carries an Ultra AC/10, a small pulse laser, and an ER small laser. Walk two, run three, jump two. The UAC/10 delivers sustained double-tap ballistic fire. The pulse and ER small lasers handle close engagement. Five tons of ammunition.
variants.deployment: The upgraded loadout includes a Mydron Excel Ultra Autocannon/10 and an ER small laser. Five tons of ammunition support sustained fire. The UAC/10 maintains double-tap ballistic pressure. The pulse and ER small lasers handle close engagement. Jump two provides urban terrain mobility. A sustained-fire UrbanMech.

variants.name: UM-R68
variants.overview: The UrbanMech is a thirty-ton urban defence 'Mech that has been in service since 2675. Walk two, run three, jump two on the tiny 60-rated engine. Multiple variants. The design is famously slow — built for static ambush from urban cover, not manoeuvre.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three, jump two at thirty tons. The design is extremely slow — this machine ambushes from cover rather than manoeuvring. The heavy autocannon delivers disproportionate firepower for the weight. Jump two provides limited urban terrain mobility. The UM-R68 carries an MRM-30, a small pulse laser, and a small laser. Walk two, run three, jump two. The MRM-30 delivers devastating medium-range missile salvos. The pulse laser handles close engagement.
variants.deployment: The UM-R68 features a Shigunga MRM-30 launcher with two tons of ammunition, replacing the autocannon. The MRM-30 delivers overwhelming medium-range missile fire from urban cover. The pulse and small lasers handle close engagement. Jump two provides urban terrain mobility. A missile-armed UrbanMech.

variants.name: UM-R70
variants.overview: The UrbanMech is a thirty-ton urban defence 'Mech that has been in service since 2675. Walk two, run three, jump two on the tiny 60-rated engine. Multiple variants. The design is famously slow — built for static ambush from urban cover, not manoeuvre.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three, jump two at thirty tons. The design is extremely slow — this machine ambushes from cover rather than manoeuvring. The heavy autocannon delivers disproportionate firepower for the weight. Jump two provides limited urban terrain mobility. The UM-R70 carries a Rotary AC/5, an ER medium laser, and an ER small laser. Walk two, run three, jump two. The Rotary AC/5 delivers sustained ballistic fire at high rate. The ER medium extends the energy range.
variants.deployment: The -R70 is typically deployed in the Federated Suns' Capellan March, replacing the standard autocannon with a Mydron Rotary AC/5. The Rotary AC/5 maintains sustained ballistic pressure from urban cover. The ER medium and small lasers handle direct fire. Ammunition management under the rotary autocannon is critical. Jump two provides urban terrain mobility.

variants.name: UM-AIV
variants.overview: The UrbanMech is a thirty-ton urban defence 'Mech that has been in service since 2675. Walk two, run three, jump two on the tiny 60-rated engine. Multiple variants. The design is famously slow — built for static ambush from urban cover, not manoeuvre.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three, jump two on the 60-rated XL engine. The UM-AIV carries an Arrow IV artillery launcher and an ER medium laser. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The Arrow IV provides extreme-range artillery fire. The ER medium handles self-defence.
variants.deployment: The -AIV's most notable feature is its ability to deliver tactical nuclear warheads via the Arrow IV system. The Arrow IV delivers extreme-range artillery fire. The ER medium provides self-defence. Arrow IV ammunition requires dedicated logistics. Jump two provides urban terrain mobility. XL engine vulnerability applies. An artillery UrbanMech.

variants.name: UM-R80
variants.overview: The UrbanMech has been defending cities since 2675 and the joke about it is that it looks like a trash can with legs. The joke stops being funny when you are inside one of its kill zones. The UM-R80 is an electronic warfare variant trading the standard autocannon for a snub-nose PPC and TAG system.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three, jump three. The UM-R80 carries a snub-nose PPC, a TAG system, a small laser, and a small pulse laser. The snub-nose PPC handles direct combat at short to medium range. The TAG designates for guided munitions. The small weapons handle close threats. Standard UrbanMech armour and the standard slow speed profile.
variants.deployment: The R80 is an urban artillery spotter. The TAG designates targets for guided munitions from supporting assets while the snub-nose PPC handles anything that approaches. Walk two means it goes somewhere useful and stays there. Its urban terrain and building-to-building movement capability is unchanged from the standard UrbanMech.

variants.name: UM-R27
variants.overview: The UrbanMech is a thirty-ton urban defence 'Mech that has been in service since 2675. Walk two, run three, jump two on the tiny 60-rated engine. Multiple variants. The design is famously slow — built for static ambush from urban cover, not manoeuvre.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three, jump two at thirty tons. The design is extremely slow — this machine ambushes from cover rather than manoeuvring. The heavy autocannon delivers disproportionate firepower for the weight. Jump two provides limited urban terrain mobility. The UM-R27 carries three SRM-6 launchers. Walk two, run three, jump two. Three SRM-6 launchers deliver overwhelming close-range missile volume. A dedicated close-range missile ambush configuration.
variants.deployment: The UM-R27's loadout is centred around its three SRM-6 launchers, with a focus on rapid rearming and aggressive tactics. Three SRM-6 launchers create overwhelming close-range missile fire from cover. The design ambushes and rearms rather than manoeuvring. Jump two provides urban terrain mobility. A missile ambush UrbanMech.

variants.name: UM-R93
variants.overview: The UrbanMech is a thirty-ton urban defence 'Mech that has been in service since 2675. Walk two, run three, jump two on the tiny 60-rated engine. Multiple variants. The design is famously slow — built for static ambush from urban cover, not manoeuvre.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three, jump two on the 60-rated engine with twelve tons of hardened armour. The UM-R93 carries a plasma rifle, an ER medium laser, and an ER small laser. Hardened armour makes it nearly indestructible in urban environments. The plasma rifle superheats targets.
variants.deployment: The UM-R93 variant features twelve tons of hardened armour, making it nearly indestructible in urban environments. The hardened armour reduces incoming damage substantially. The plasma rifle forces heat problems on opponents. The ER lasers handle direct fire. Jump two provides urban terrain mobility. An armoured plasma UrbanMech.

variants.name: UM-R96
variants.overview: The UrbanMech is a thirty-ton urban defence 'Mech that has been in service since 2675. Walk two, run three, jump two on the tiny 60-rated engine. Multiple variants. The design is famously slow — built for static ambush from urban cover, not manoeuvre.
variants.capabilities: Walk two, run three, jump three on the 60-rated engine with hardened armour. The UM-R96 carries a snub-nose PPC and a small X-pulse laser. Hardened armour provides exceptional protection. The snub-nose PPC covers close to medium range without minimum range complications.
variants.deployment: The -R96 evolves the -R80's configuration while incorporating the -R93's hardened armour shell. The improved jump jets provide jump three, above the standard UrbanMech. The snub-nose PPC delivers direct fire without the minimum range gap. The X-pulse laser handles close engagement. The hardened armour provides exceptional protection. A durable mobile UrbanMech.

variants.overview: The UrbanMech IIC is the Clan's take on the urban defence concept, built with Clan components on the thirty-ton standard chassis. The IIC 2 is a 3070 upgrade replacing the standard UAC with a HAG/20, a genuinely alarming weapon on a machine this size.
variants.capabilities: Walk three, run four, jump three on a 90-rated Clan engine. The IIC 2 carries a HAG/20 and a flamer. The HAG/20 spreads ballistic projectiles across multiple armour locations at medium range. On a thirty-ton machine in an urban environment, the HAG/20 range and spread creates serious problems for larger opponents who cannot manoeuvre away quickly. The flamer handles infantry. Two tons of HAG ammunition is the operational limit.
variants.deployment: The IIC 2 deploys in urban defence where the HAG/20's spread and the tight engagement distances create a damage profile that opponents above its weight class cannot ignore. The flamer clears infantry from the approaches. Walk three limits tactical mobility but in a prepared urban position that is not the primary concern. HAG/20 ammunition is precious and warriors manage it carefully.

variants.name: URA-2A
variants.overview: The Ursa is a sixty-five ton heavy reconnaissance 'Mech with an exceptional gyroscope system that provides stability at high speeds. Walk five, run seven on the 325-rated XL engine with MASC providing burst acceleration. The URA-2A is the base production model.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven with MASC. The URA-2A carries an ER PPC, four medium X-pulse lasers, and a Rotary AC/2. The X-pulse lasers are accurate against moving targets at close range. The ER PPC handles long-range engagement. The Rotary AC/2 provides sustained ballistic harassment. MASC maintenance requires attention to transmission wear under heavy use.
variants.deployment: The URA-2A is a fast heavy that uses MASC burst speed for aggressive repositioning and the X-pulse accuracy for consistent fire while moving. The ER PPC reaches at range. The Rotary AC/2 maintains harassment fire between energy weapon cycles. The XL engine vulnerability means it relies on speed and positioning rather than armour absorption.

variants.name: URA-2C
variants.overview: The Ursa is a sixty-five ton heavy reconnaissance 'Mech with an exceptional gyroscope system that provides stability at high speeds. Walk five, run seven on the 325-rated Clan XL engine with MASC providing burst acceleration. The URA-2C is the Clan engine upgrade.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven with MASC. The URA-2C carries an ER PPC, four Clan ER medium pulse lasers, and a Rotary AC/2. The Clan ER medium pulse lasers provide better range and performance than the IS X-pulse equivalents. The Clan engine requires Clan maintenance procedures on an IS chassis. MASC transmission wear applies as in the 2A.
variants.deployment: The 2C is the mixed-tech upgrade, replacing IS X-pulse lasers with Clan ER medium pulse lasers for extended range and improved output. The Clan engine maintenance requirement is the tradeoff. Units with Clan tech access get meaningfully better pulse laser performance from the 2C. Units without it run the 2A.

variants.overview: The Ursus is a fifty-ton Clan medium built for the Rasalhague Dominion. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated Clan XL engine. Multiple variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at fifty tons. Clan XL — side torso vulnerability. Jump six provides exceptional mobility. Variant 2 carries a HAG/20, a plasma cannon, two AP Gauss rifles, and an ER medium laser. The HAG/20 spreads ballistic fire across armour locations. The plasma cannon superheats targets. The AP Gauss rifles handle infantry.
variants.deployment: The Ursus 2 suits Inner Sphere combat conditions. The Bergan XIV endo steel structure supports the weapons payload. The HAG/20 delivers spread ballistic damage. The plasma cannon forces heat problems on opponents. The AP Gauss rifles handle infantry. Jump six provides exceptional mobility. Clan XL vulnerability applies.

variants.name: PR
variants.overview: The Ursus is a fifty-ton Clan medium built for the Rasalhague Dominion. Walk four, run six on the 200-rated fusion engine. Multiple variants.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at fifty tons on the fusion engine. Standard fusion engine — side torso survivability. The PR carries three AP Gauss rifles, two ProtoMech AC/8s, two improved heavy medium lasers, and an ER flamer, with an improved C3 computer. The improved C3 shares targeting across the network.
variants.deployment: The most notable feature is the Inner Sphere Improved C3 Computer, which enables up to six Ursus-PRs to share targeting data. The improved C3 coordinates the network. The AP Gauss rifles and ProtoMech AC/8s handle infantry and close ballistic engagement. The improved heavy medium lasers add close-range punch. The fusion engine provides side torso survivability. A networked mixed-tech medium.

variants.overview: The Ursus 3 is a fifty-ton Clan medium built for the Ghost Bear Dominion. Walk four, run six on the 200-rated Clan fusion engine. A counterinsurgency variant of the Ursus line.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at fifty tons on the Clan fusion engine. Standard fusion engine — side torso survivability. The Ursus 3 carries a HAG/20, three AP Gauss rifles, two ProtoMech AC/8s, two improved heavy medium lasers, and an ER flamer. The HAG/20 delivers spread ballistic damage at close range. The AP Gauss rifles and ProtoMech AC/8s handle infantry and hardened positions. The ER flamer forces heat on opponents.
variants.deployment: The Ursus 3 was produced specifically for Watch and Mimir operatives conducting counterinsurgency operations against the Motstand resistance movement. Its weapons array handles hardened positions and suppresses infantry. By 3085, full production supplied every world in the Ghost Bear Dominion with its complement, though few MechWarriors volunteered to pilot one due to its sinister reputation.

variants.name: UZL-2S
variants.overview: The Uziel is a fifty-ton Inner Sphere medium built for the Free Worlds League as a fast fire support and skirmisher. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine. Multiple variants. The PPC-class weapons and jump mobility are the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at fifty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk six with jump six is exceptional mobility. The energy weapons and SRM launcher provide the combat capability. The UZL-2S carries two PPCs, an SRM-6, and two machine guns. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The twin PPCs handle long-range direct fire. The SRM-6 handles close missiles. The machine guns handle infantry. Heat management under twin PPCs requires cycling.
variants.deployment: The 2S replaces the diverse weapon mix of the 3S with a pair of standard PPCs as primary armament, giving it consistent long-range firepower. The twin PPCs deliver strong long-range fire. The SRM-6 and machine guns handle close threats and infantry. Jump six provides positioning. Heat discipline is the pilot's consideration. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: UZL-3S
variants.overview: The Uziel is a fifty-ton Inner Sphere medium built for the Free Worlds League as a fast fire support and skirmisher. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine. Multiple variants. The PPC-class weapons and jump mobility are the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk six, run nine, jump six at fifty tons on the XL engine. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Walk six with jump six is exceptional mobility. The energy weapons and SRM launcher provide the combat capability. The UZL-3S carries a large pulse laser, an LB 2-X, an ER medium laser, two ER small lasers, and an SRM-6. Walk six, run nine, jump six. The large pulse laser is accurate at medium range. The LB 2-X provides long-range harassment. The SRM-6 handles close missiles.
variants.deployment: The 3S is the primary production variant, entering full manufacturing in 3065. It carries the design's signature mixed loadout. The large pulse laser handles accurate medium-range fire. The LB 2-X provides long-range ballistic harassment. The SRM-6 and lasers handle close engagement. Jump six provides positioning. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: UZL-2S (Jacob)
variants.overview: The Uziel is a fifty-ton Inner Sphere medium built for the Free Worlds League as a fast fire support and skirmisher. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine. Multiple variants. The PPC-class weapons and jump mobility are the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty tons on the 250-rated XL engine. The Jacob carries two Rotary AC/5s, two ER small lasers, and an SRM-6. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The twin Rotary AC/5s deliver devastating sustained ballistic fire. The SRM-6 handles close missiles.
variants.deployment: The Jacob features paired rotary autocannons in each arm, providing devastating sustained firepower at the cost of reduced speed. The twin Rotary AC/5s create overwhelming sustained ballistic pressure. The ER small lasers and SRM-6 handle close engagement. Ammunition management across the rotary autocannons is critical. Named variant — maintain to specific documentation.

variants.name: UZL-2S (Jacob II)
variants.overview: The Uziel is a fifty-ton Inner Sphere medium built for the Free Worlds League as a fast fire support and skirmisher. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine. Multiple variants. The PPC-class weapons and jump mobility are the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven at fifty tons on the 250-rated XL engine. The Jacob II carries two light AC/5s, two medium pulse lasers, and a Streak SRM-6. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The light AC/5s provide long-range ballistic fire at reduced weight. The Streak SRM-6 guarantees close hits.
variants.deployment: The Jacob II features experimental technology pushing the Uziel chassis beyond its original design parameters. The light AC/5s deliver long-range ballistic fire at reduced weight. The medium pulse lasers handle close engagement accurately. The Streak SRM-6 handles close missiles reliably. Named custom variant — maintain to specific documentation. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: UZL-8S
variants.overview: The Uziel is a fifty-ton Inner Sphere medium built for the Free Worlds League as a fast fire support and skirmisher. Walk six, run nine, jump six on the 300-rated XL engine. Multiple variants. The PPC-class weapons and jump mobility are the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump eight at fifty tons on the 250-rated XL engine. The UZL-8S carries four medium pulse lasers and a Streak SRM-6. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. Jump eight at fifty tons is exceptional. Four medium pulse lasers deliver dense accurate close-range fire. The Streak SRM-6 guarantees close hits.
variants.deployment: The 8S was introduced in 3075 during the Jihad, replacing the earlier 3S configuration with four medium pulse lasers and improved jump capability. Jump eight at fifty tons creates approach vectors no opponent can predict. The four medium pulse lasers saturate close range accurately. The Streak SRM-6 handles close missiles. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: V4-LNT-K7
variants.overview: The Valiant is a thirty-ton light built during the Solaris resistance to the Word of Blake occupation. Walk seven, run ten on the 210-rated engine. Multiple variants. The triple ER medium laser loadout is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at thirty tons. Fusion, light, or XL engine depending on variant. Walk seven is fast for the weight class. Three ER medium lasers deliver dense direct fire without ammunition dependency. The V4-LNT-K7 carries three ER medium lasers on the fusion engine. Walk seven, run ten. Three ER medium lasers deliver dense direct fire. All-energy with no ammunition. The original production configuration.
variants.deployment: The original production model entered service during the Solaran resistance to the Word of Blake occupation in 3068. Three ER medium lasers deliver dense direct fire for a thirty-ton machine. Walk seven provides the mobility. All-energy removes ammunition concerns. A fast energy-armed light.

variants.name: V4-LNT-J3
variants.overview: The Valiant is a thirty-ton light built during the Solaris resistance to the Word of Blake occupation. Walk seven, run ten on the 210-rated engine. Multiple variants. The triple ER medium laser loadout is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at thirty tons on the 210-rated light engine. The J3 carries two ER medium lasers, three ER small lasers, and a flamer. Light engine — side torso survivability. The ER lasers deliver dense direct fire. The flamer handles infantry. Heavy ferro-fibrous armour.
variants.deployment: The J3 variant features a 210 GM light fusion engine and Terminal heavy ferro-fibrous armour, freeing tonnage for improved protection. The light engine provides survivability. The ER lasers deliver dense direct fire. The flamer handles infantry. The heavy ferro-fibrous armour improves protection. A durable energy-armed light.

variants.name: VLN-3T
variants.overview: The Valiant is a thirty-ton light built during the Solaris resistance to the Word of Blake occupation. Walk seven, run ten on the 210-rated engine. Multiple variants. The triple ER medium laser loadout is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at thirty tons. Fusion, light, or XL engine depending on variant. Walk seven is fast for the weight class. Three ER medium lasers deliver dense direct fire without ammunition dependency. The VLN-3T carries three ER medium lasers with a functional light shield on the right forearm. Walk seven, run ten. The light shield deflects incoming fire at the cost of some weapon capacity. Three ER medium lasers deliver direct fire.
variants.deployment: This variant debuted in Hartford Gardens and features an improved right forearm for a functional light shield at the cost of some capability. The light shield deflects incoming fire from that arc. The three ER medium lasers deliver direct fire. Walk seven provides the mobility. An arena-oriented variant with defensive capability.

variants.name: VAL-NT-JX 'Hot Knife'
variants.overview: The Valiant is a thirty-ton light built during the Solaris resistance to the Word of Blake occupation. Walk seven, run ten on the 210-rated engine. Multiple variants. The triple ER medium laser loadout is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at thirty tons on the 210-rated light engine. The Hot Knife carries three ER medium lasers, with experimental prototype systems. Light engine — side torso survivability. Three ER medium lasers deliver dense direct fire. An experimental prototype.
variants.deployment: This experimental prototype was developed at Johnston Industries' Warehouse 12 Research Facility on Noisiel. The three ER medium lasers deliver dense direct fire. The light engine provides survivability. Prototype documentation applies to the experimental systems. Named prototype — maintain to specific documentation. A fast energy-armed light.

variants.name: VLT-3E
variants.overview: The Valiant is a thirty-ton light built during the Solaris resistance to the Word of Blake occupation. Walk seven, run ten on the 210-rated engine. Multiple variants. The triple ER medium laser loadout is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk seven, run ten at thirty tons on the 210-rated XL engine. The VLT-3E carries a light AC/5, three ER medium lasers, and a fluid gun, with a composite internal structure. XL engine — side torso vulnerability. The light AC/5 provides long-range ballistic fire. The fluid gun sprays chemical agents. The composite structure saves mass but takes criticals more readily.
variants.deployment: The VLT-3E mounts a composite internal structure and 210 XL engine to save weight, protected by five and a half tons of armour. The light AC/5 delivers long-range ballistic fire. The three ER medium lasers provide direct fire. The fluid gun can spray coolant or chemical agents. The composite structure is fragile. XL engine vulnerability applies.

variants.name: VLK-QA
variants.overview: The Valkyrie is a thirty-ton light that has been in service since 2787, a mainstay light 'Mech across the Inner Sphere. Walk five, run seven, jump five on the 150-rated engine. Multiple variants. The medium laser and LRM combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at thirty tons on most variants. The medium laser and LRM launcher cover direct and indirect fire. Standard, light, or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability suits the mobile light role. The VLK-QA carries a medium laser and an LRM-10. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The medium laser handles direct fire. The LRM-10 provides indirect fire. The original production configuration that endured for centuries.
variants.deployment: The original production model entered service in 2787 and remained the sole variant for nearly two centuries. The medium laser handles direct fire. The LRM-10 provides indirect fire support. Jump five suits the mobile light role. A definitive workhorse light 'Mech.

variants.name: VLK-QF
variants.overview: The Valkyrie is a thirty-ton light that has been in service since 2787, a mainstay light 'Mech across the Inner Sphere. Walk five, run seven, jump five on the 150-rated engine. Multiple variants. The medium laser and LRM combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at thirty tons on most variants. The medium laser and LRM launcher cover direct and indirect fire. Standard, light, or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability suits the mobile light role. The VLK-QF carries a flamer and an LRM-10. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The flamer handles infantry and forces heat on opponents. The LRM-10 provides indirect fire. A straightforward anti-infantry modification.
variants.deployment: The VLK-QF was first fielded during the Succession Wars era, with a straightforward modification replacing the medium laser with a flamer. The flamer handles infantry and area denial. The LRM-10 provides indirect fire support. Jump five suits the mobile light role. An anti-infantry Valkyrie.

variants.name: VLK-QD
variants.overview: The Valkyrie is a thirty-ton light that has been in service since 2787, a mainstay light 'Mech across the Inner Sphere. Walk five, run seven, jump five on the 150-rated engine. Multiple variants. The medium laser and LRM combination is the design identity.
variants.capabilities: Walk five, run seven, jump five at thirty tons on most variants. The medium laser and LRM launcher cover direct and indirect fire. Standard, light, or XL engine depending on variant. The jump capability suits the mobile light role. The VLK-QD carries a medium pulse laser and an LRM-10. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The medium pulse laser is accurate at close range. The LRM-10 provides indirect fire. A Helm Memory Core technology upgrade.
variants.deployment: This variant was introduced in 3049 following the recovery of the Helm Memory Core. It features a reengineered chassis using recovered technology. variants.name: VP-5
variants.overview: The Viper VP-1 is a 70-ton heavy BattleMech designed as a collaborative effort between the Free Worlds League and Kallon Industries. Built on an upscaled Crusader chassis, it's intended for rugged reliability and battlefield adaptability. The design focuses on direct-fire energy weapons, eliminating ammunition dependency issues.
variants.capabilities: The Viper's primary armament consists of two Magna Mk III-B binary laser cannons, supported by three Intek medium pulse lasers. This energy-focused loadout provides devastating firepower at medium to long ranges, but demands careful heat management and tactical discipline to avoid thermal shutdown. The design's increased tonnage allows for improved armor protection over the base Crusader, while its upscaled Crucis-B chassis provides a stable firing platform with reasonable mobility.
variants.deployment: The VP-5 saw service primarily with FWLM regular forces and select mercenary units during the Third Succession War. Its enhanced reliability made it particularly valuable during extended campaigns. Combat reports indicate that VP-5 variants demonstrated improved survivability compared to earlier models, likely due to improvements in heat dissipation systems and possibly enhanced armor protection around critical components.

variants.deployment: The Viper 2 is a long-range fire support variant. The ER large laser reach combined with jump five creates strong terrain exploitation capability. The small pulse lasers and machine guns deter close approach. The UAC/2 provides ballistic harassment at range. The Clan XL vulnerability requires range management.

variants.overview: The Vixen is a 30-ton Clan light 'Mech originally built for dueling Trials that evolved into a standard reconnaissance and raiding platform. Walk nine, run thirteen on the 270-rated Clan XL engine makes it fast enough to outrun almost anything it cannot fight. Nine variants cover significant tactical variation from the base concept.
variants.capabilities: Walk nine, run thirteen at thirty-five tons. The Clan XL at this weight means any significant side torso hit ends the mission. What keeps it alive is that at walk nine almost nothing can catch it or reliably hit it. Ferro-fibrous armour provides reasonable protection for the weight class. The speed is the primary survival tool, not the armour. Variant 2 carries an ER PPC, two ER medium lasers, and four machine guns. The ER PPC is the most powerful weapon this chassis mounts — at thirty tons the range and damage it provides is exceptional. The ER mediums cover closer engagement. The machine guns handle infantry. Heat from the ER PPC requires discipline.
variants.deployment: Variant 2 is the long-range sniper configuration. The ER PPC at walk nine can threaten opponents at ranges where their weapons cannot reply effectively. The ER mediums handle anything that closes. The machine guns deal with infantry. Warriors who use the speed to maintain ER PPC range and fire patiently get devastating results.

variants.name: WTC-4M
variants.overview: The Watchman is a forty-ton medium built for the Federated Suns. Walk five, run seven, jump five on the 200-rated engine. Multiple variants. The large laser and support weapons cover multiple ranges.

The WTC-4M carries a large laser, two medium lasers, and two machine guns. Walk five, run seven, jump five. The large laser handles direct fire. The medium lasers close the engagement. The machine guns handle infantry.
variants.deployment: The baseline Watchman mounts a ChisComp 43 Special large laser as primary, supported by two ChisComp medium lasers and machine guns. The large laser handles direct fire. The medium lasers close the engagement. The machine guns handle infantry. Jump five suits the mobile medium role. Standard engine survivability. A general-purpose medium.

variants.overview: The Watchman is a forty-ton garrison 'Mech built on the Enforcer chassis for rapid production and ease of maintenance. The WTC-4DM replaces the standard large laser with a PPC and adds a third medium laser.

variants.deployment: The 4DM is a more capable close-range combatant than the standard Watchman, with three medium lasers and a PPC covering the full range spectrum. Garrison and patrol units that encounter varied threat types benefit from the flexibility. The PPC heat management is the primary pilot adaptation from the standard large laser variants.

The re-engineered laser degrades opponents' heat management. The four ER mediums provide dense direct fire.
variants.deployment: The Belle's advantage lies in its ability to disrupt adversary sensors and heat management. The large re-engineered laser degrades opponents' heat management while dealing damage. The four ER mediums provide dense direct fire. The light engine provides survivability. Re-engineered laser maintenance requires specific procedures. Named variant — maintain to specific documentation. A disruption-focused Watchman.

The four ER mediums close the engagement. The Streak SRM-6 handles close missiles reliably. The LRM-10 adds fire support. Walk six provides mobility. Clan XL vulnerability applies. variants.name: WVR-1R
variants.overview: The Wolverine WVR-1R is a versatile medium BattleMech designed for front-line combat, emphasizing maneuverability and balanced firepower. Its origins date back to 2471 when Norse BattleMech Works of Marduk developed the prototype. The design has undergone significant improvements since then, but this early variant still showcases its core capabilities.
variants.capabilities: The WVR-1R's well-balanced combination of firepower, mobility, and protection makes it effective in various roles. Its primary weapon is an Imperator-A autocannon/5, complemented by a Holly short-range missile six-pack and a single Magna Mk II medium laser. The integrated Garret T11-b communication system and Sync Tracker targeting-tracking system provide above-average command and control capabilities. While its 86.4 km/h ground speed might be criticized for a dedicated reconnaissance platform, it remains adequate for combined-arms skirmishing.
variants.deployment: The original WVR-1R had some quirks, like the primitive engine limiting its top speed. The armor layout was also a bit heavy-handed, with too much emphasis on protection over mobility. That being said, it's still a solid design that has held up well over time. Just be aware of the jump jets – they're not as reliable as modern designs, but they can still get you out of a tight spot.

variants.name: WVR-9K
variants.overview: The Wolverine WVR-1R is a versatile medium BattleMech designed for front-line combat, emphasizing maneuverability and balanced firepower. Its origins date back to 2471 when Norse BattleMech Works of Marduk developed the prototype. The design has undergone significant improvements since then, but this early variant still showcases its core capabilities.
variants.capabilities: The WVR-1R's well-balanced combination of firepower, mobility, and protection makes it effective in various roles. Its primary weapon is an Imperator-A autocannon/5, complemented by a Holly short-range missile six-pack and a single Magna Mk II medium laser. The integrated Garret T11-b communication system and Sync Tracker targeting-tracking system provide above-average command and control capabilities. While its 86.4 km/h ground speed might be criticized for a dedicated reconnaissance platform, it remains adequate for combined-arms skirmishing.
variants.deployment: In the field, we've seen the WVR-9K excel in close-quarters combat, using its PPC and SRM-4 to devastating effect. The machine gun array is useful against infantry, while the sword and triple-strength myomer bundles make it a formidable melee opponent. Be aware that the C3 slave unit can be vulnerable to jamming or disruption, which may impact targeting data sharing with lancemates.

variants.overview: The Wolverine II WVR-7H is a Star League-era design built around the venerable Wolverine chassis. variants.capabilities: The WVR-7H retains the balanced combat philosophy of its standard counterpart while dramatically improving capabilities through the application of Star League Royal-grade technology. The ultra-class autocannon/5 provides superior firepower, while the Artemis IV fire control integration in the SRM-6 launcher improves missile accuracy. The medium pulse laser offers improved close-range performance, and the double heat sinks ensure thermal management is no longer a concern. CASE protection in both side torsos mitigates the risk of catastrophic ammunition explosions.
variants.deployment: The WVR-7H's loadout includes an ultra-class autocannon with additional tonnage for sustained engagements, Artemis IV fire control system on the SRM-6 launcher, and medium pulse laser. The endo steel internal structure and ferro-fibrous armor save critical weight, while double-strength heat sinks and CASE protection in both side torsos improve survivability.

variants.name: A
variants.overview: The Woodsman is a 75-ton Clan heavy OmniMech built on a 300-rated standard Clan fusion engine. Walk four, run six. The standard engine is the design's key survivability feature — it takes hits that kill XL competitors. Five configurations cover a useful range of tactical roles. The conservative design philosophy puts durability ahead of speed.
variants.capabilities: Walk four, run six at seventy-five tons. The standard Clan engine survives side torso damage that would end an XL-equipped competitor's engagement. Pod space is generous. Clan construction quality is high throughout. The slower speed compared to XL-equipped heavies means warriors in Woodsman configurations cannot reposition as quickly, which shapes deployment decisions. Configuration A carries twin ER PPCs, a large pulse laser, two medium pulse lasers, and an ER small laser. The ER PPCs provide the primary long-range direct fire. The pulse laser suite covers medium to close range accurately. Heat from both ER PPCs and the pulse suite simultaneously is aggressive and requires volley fire discipline.
variants.deployment: Configuration A is the long-range energy fire variant. The ER PPCs at range transition to pulse laser volume as the engagement closes. All energy with no ammunition dependency suits extended operations. Warriors who manage fire cycling carefully sustain consistent output. Those who alpha strike repeatedly will hit heat limits quickly.
